b.description: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. (NASDAQ: BLMN) is one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world, headquartered in Tampa, Florida and founded in 1988. It owns and operates four restaurant concepts — Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill, and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar — across the United States and internationally (Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, and China). The company's consumer technology centers on the Web-based Dine Rewards loyalty program, per-brand mobile apps (iOS/Android) for online ordering, curbside takeaway, delivery, table payment, reservations, and waitlist, and corporate supplier portals (BBI Connect). Bloomin' Brands does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; the apis collection below is intentionally empty.
b.name: Bloomin' Brands

b.description: Blooming Health is an AI-powered, omnichannel care-management and community-engagement platform for healthcare and social-services organizations. It lets teams design multilingual care workflows across voice, SMS, and email in minutes — automating screening and needs assessments, service recommendations, outreach, appointment reminders, wellness check-ins, emergency broadcasts, closed-loop referral tracking, and Medicaid/SNAP recertification. The platform integrates with existing EHR/CRM systems and databases via FHIR, HL7, API, and SFTP, and is HIPAA compliant with encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, audit trails, BAAs, and SOC 2 documentation available on request. Blooming Health is a healthcare portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes an enterprise integration surface but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.
b.name: Blooming Health

b.description: Bloomingdale's is an American luxury department store chain and a subsidiary of Macy's, Inc. Bloomingdale's does not publish a public developer portal; partner integration is delivered through the parent Macy's Inc. vendor and trade partner programs, drop-ship and EDI channels with suppliers, the Bloomingdale's affiliate program for marketing partners, and the shared Macy's Inc. technology platform powering Bloomingdale's commerce, loyalty, and fulfillment.
b.name: Bloomingdale's

b.description: BloomNation is a flower-delivery marketplace that connects consumers with independent local florists for same-day and next-day delivery of handcrafted floral arrangements across 40+ U.S. cities and the UK. Customers shop florist-designed bouquets for occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries, sympathy, and get-well, then pay with credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, or Afterpay. Distinctive features include BloomSnap photo delivery confirmation and video message cards. BloomNation also runs a florist-facing SaaS side (point-of-sale, website, and order management, now part of Promenade) that powers member shops. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company; no public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment.
b.name: BloomNation

b.description: Bloomon is a flower and gift delivery service that lets customers order one-off bouquets or sign up for a recurring flower subscription delivered on a chosen cadence. It offers seasonal hand-tied and letterbox arrangements, gifting options, gift vouchers, and add-ons, with delivery across the United Kingdom and other European markets. Bloomon is part of the Bloom & Wild Group (confirmed via its published .well-known/security.txt, which points to bloomandwild.com). The company operates a consumer-facing e-commerce and subscription website rather than a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile therefore captures its web, security, and discovery surface rather than a machine-readable API.
b.name: Bloomon

b.description: Bloomreach is a commerce experience cloud combining an e-commerce search and merchandising engine (Discovery), a marketing automation platform and customer data platform (Engagement, formerly Exponea), and a headless content management system (Content, formerly Hippo/brXM). It publishes REST APIs for product and category search, autosuggest, recommendation widgets, catalog management and indexing, customer tracking and segmentation, email and SMS campaigns, and headless content delivery and management. Its Loomi AI layer adds agentic capabilities, and Loomi Connect exposes the estate to AI agents as an OAuth-protected remote MCP server carrying more than 160 tools across marketing, analytics, search and data hub.
b.name: Bloomreach

b.description: Bloomsbury AI was a London-based natural-language-processing startup, backed by Seedcamp, that built Cape — an API making it easy to build software that answers questions about the contents of documents (machine reading / document question answering). Bloomsbury AI was acquired by Facebook in 2018; the hosted Cape API is terminated and bloomsbury.ai now serves only a farewell page. The team open sourced the Cape stack (web services, document QA, machine reader, and clients) under the bloomsburyai GitHub organization, which remains publicly available as archival source. This API Evangelist profile preserves that identity and the open-source footprint.
b.name: Bloomsbury

b.description: Bloomscape is a direct-to-consumer houseplant company that grows plants in its own greenhouses and ships them fully grown directly to customers' doors, bypassing traditional retail and nursery supply chains. Alongside houseplants, it sells planters, plant-care accessories, and gifting options, and backs every order with its Grow-How team of horticultural experts plus a plant guarantee. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. Bloomscape operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties along with a domain-security probe.
b.name: Bloomscape

b.description: Bloom Institute of Technology (BloomTech) is an online coding bootcamp offering full‑stack web development and AI‑focused courses. Founded to provide low‑risk, high‑impact pathways to tech careers, it boasts over 4,000 graduates since 2017, an 86% job placement rate in 2022, and a tuition‑refund guarantee. The platform combines flexible part‑time and full‑time options, AI‑enhanced learning, and corporate upskilling solutions for diverse learners.
b.name: BloomTech

b.description: BloomThat was an a16z-backed, San Francisco same-day flower and gift delivery startup, surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. It operated a consumer (B2C) mobile and web ordering experience and never published a public developer API. As of this enrichment pass its domain (bloomthat.com) 301-redirects to ftd.com/bloomthat, indicating the brand has been acquired by / absorbed into FTD and no longer operates an independent developer surface.
b.name: BloomThat

b.description: BloomThis is a Malaysian online florist and gifting brand (backed by 500 Global) offering fresh flower boxes, hand-tied bouquets, and weekly fresh-flower subscriptions, with a free personalised card and photo on every order and free same-day delivery across Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Kedah, Penang, Negeri Sembilan, and Johor Bahru. Its Shopify storefront natively exposes an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): a hosted MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp, an OpenID Connect / OAuth Customer Account API, and published /llms.txt and /agents.md instructions that let AI shopping agents search the catalog, build a cart, and run a buyer-approved checkout.
b.name: BloomThis

b.description: Bloomy (bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered adaptive learning platform for K-12 students, founded by Alex Southmayd and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). The product diagnoses each student's knowledge gaps, builds a personalized standards-aligned learning path across English Language Arts, Math, and Writing, and delivers Socratic AI tutoring plus mastery-based practice, requiring 90%+ mastery before a student advances. It integrates third-party diagnostic/assessment data (i-Ready, NWEA MAP) and provides a real-time teacher dashboard. Bloomy serves traditional districts, charter schools, homeschools, and microschools, and sells to families via monthly or annual subscriptions (with ESA/EFA fund eligibility in some states). As of this profile Bloomy publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this record captures its verified public identity and legal/account surface only.
b.name: Bloomy

b.description: Blooom was an independent robo-advisor that provided automated, flat-fee management of employer-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 403(b), 457, and TSP plans — analyzing holdings, rebalancing allocations, and flagging hidden fund fees on accounts it advised but did not directly custody. Founded in 2013 and backed by QED Investors, the Kansas-based company operated a consumer web application rather than a public developer API. The consumer service has since wound down: blooom.com no longer resolves to a website and the domain is now served by Morgan Stanley nameservers with a locked-down, mail-disabled defensive DNS posture (null MX, SPF -all, DMARC p=reject). Retained here as a historical wealth-management profile; no live API or developer surface remains to enrich.
b.name: Blooom

b.description: Bloq is a Web3 infrastructure company offering a suite of decentralized finance, mining, metaverse, and blockchain application tools. Their platform includes BloqCloud, Lumerin hashpower marketplace, Vesper DeFi services, Metronome synthetic assets, and more, targeting enterprises and developers building on decentralized technologies.
b.name: Bloq

b.description: Bloqit is a technology company focused on providing blockchain-based solutions for secure data storage and transaction processing. The company aims to enable enterprises to integrate decentralized ledger technology into their existing workflows, offering APIs for data immutability, smart contract execution, and audit trails. Bloqit’s platform emphasizes scalability, compliance with financial regulations, and developer-friendly SDKs across multiple programming languages. While still emerging, Bloqit positions itself as a bridge between traditional enterprise systems and the decentralized web, targeting sectors such as finance, supply chain, and digital identity.
b.name: Bloqit

b.description: Blossomenergy is a private renewable energy startup listed on secondary‑market platforms such as EquityZen. Public information about the company is limited; attempts to locate an official website or detailed corporate branding have been unsuccessful. The company appears in investment listings but its own domain, documentation, or API endpoints are not publicly discoverable. This entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment when more concrete data becomes available.
b.name: Blossomenergy

b.description: BlossomHill Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2020 by drug designer J. Jean Cui, Ph.D. and biotech operator Y. Peter Li, Ph.D., M.B.A. It develops intelligently designed small-molecule medicines for oncology and autoimmune disease, led by BH-30643, a first-in-class macrocyclic non-covalent mutant-selective OMNI-EGFR inhibitor for EGFR- and HER2-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, and BH-30236, a macrocyclic CLK inhibitor for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia and higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. The company is a drug discovery business, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.
b.name: BlossomHill Therapeutics

b.description: Blotato is an AI content-creation and social-media publishing platform. Its REST API lets automation and AI-agent builders upload media, publish posts to many platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest), generate AI videos and visuals from templates, and track publishing status, with an authenticated MCP server for AI agents.
b.name: Blotato

b.description: Blowfish is a proactive web3 security platform that scans EVM and Solana transactions, EVM messages, and dApp domains before a user signs, returning a recommended action (NONE, WARN, or BLOCK), severity-sorted warnings, and human-readable transaction simulation results. Its Scan API and downloadable domain blocklist help wallets and dApps protect users from scams, malicious token approvals, and phishing across 10+ blockchains. Backed by Paradigm.
b.name: Blowfish

b.description: BLOX is a Bessemer, Alabama design-manufacture-construct (DMC) company that describes itself as the largest manufacturer of healthcare buildings in the United States. Founded in 2010-2011 as a spinoff of Giattina Aycock Architecture Studio by Chris Giattina, BLOX designs, prefabricates and installs modular medical buildings and building components — freestanding emergency departments, acute-care patient-room modules, primary-care clinics and full hospitals — from a former Pullman Standard railcar plant in the Interstate Industrial Park. Customers include HCA Healthcare, Encompass Health, Universal Health Services and Walmart Health. The company is privately held and its shares appear on secondary-market venues such as Forge Global. BLOX publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable specification; its software work is internal tooling for the DMC delivery system rather than a product.
b.name: Blox

b.description: bloXroute operates the Blockchain Distribution Network (BDN), a high-capacity, low-latency global relay network that speeds up transaction and block propagation for blockchain traders, builders, and validators. Its developer surface spans the BDN Gateway and Cloud API, the Solana Trader API (gRPC/HTTP/WebSocket/QUIC) for low-latency transaction submission, bundles, sniping, and DEX routing across Pump.fun, Jupiter, and Raydium, real-time mempool/block/event streams (newTxs, pendingTxs, txReceipts, newBlocks), the Optimized Feed Relay (OFR) shred stream, MEV relay and BackRunMe programs, and Protect/Fast RPC services. Supported chains include Solana, BNB Chain, Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Hyperliquid, Robinhood, Monad, and X Layer. Added to the API Evangelist network as a crypto-infrastructure provider.
b.name: bloXroute

b.description: Bloxroutelabs is a technology company that appears in the API Evangelist harvest backlog. It is currently a stub entry pending full profiling. The company may be listed on secondary-market platforms such as EquityZen, but no direct corporate site was verified.
b.name: Bloxroutelabs

b.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.
b.name: Bloxtel

b.description: Blu Homes, originally a modular home builder, has been acquired by Dvele and now operates under the Dvele brand. The company focuses on sustainable, precision-engineered homes with low environmental impact, offering modern modular designs, advanced manufacturing, and health‑centric living spaces. Through Dvele, Blu Homes continues to provide innovative, energy‑efficient housing solutions for developers and homeowners seeking high‑quality, customizable homes.
b.name: Blu Homes

b.description: BluBØX manufactures and services physical security products, offering the BluSKY platform—a patented, AI‑powered, cloud‑based security solution for residential, SMB and enterprise customers. The company provides hardware such as access control readers, video intercoms, elevator management systems, and related software services.

b.description: Blub Blub Inc. is the company behind Speech Blubs, a speech-therapy and language-development app for children aged 1 to 8. Created by speech-language pathologists and child-development experts, the app uses video modeling, speech exercises, face filters, and play-based activities to help kids with speech delays, autism, Down syndrome, and apraxia learn to talk. Speech Blubs is available on iOS and Android, supports English, Spanish, and German, and has been downloaded by over 10 million families worldwide. Blub Blub is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This is a consumer mobile-app company; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so the entry is limited to verified company identity and published web properties.

The API uses OAuth 2.0 authentication and enables third-party applications to integrate with podcast hosting workflows.
b.name: Blubrry API

b.description: Blue Apron is a direct-to-consumer meal-kit and prepared-food delivery company that ships chef-designed recipes with pre-portioned fresh ingredients on a weekly, no-commitment basis. Its consumer-facing surface spans meal kits, assembly-and-bake meals, ready-to-eat prepared dishes, and family-style options ordered and managed through blueapron.com and its mobile apps. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, Blue Apron operates a consumer e-commerce and subscription platform with no public developer program, API portal, or documented API surface at the time of enrichment.
b.name: Blue Apron

b.description: Blue Bottle Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer founded in 2002 in Oakland, California by James Freeman, known for freshly roasted single-origin beans, seasonal blends, cafes, and a direct-to-consumer subscription service that ships coffee within 48 hours of roasting. A majority stake was acquired by Nestle in 2017. The company operates cafes across the United States and Asia and sells whole-bean coffee, brewing equipment, and gift subscriptions through its e-commerce site. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv, kindred-ventures and true-ventures; no public developer API program has been found. Sector: consumer.

b.description: Blue Cedar provides intelligent mobile app security solutions, enabling enterprises to protect device integrity, prevent data loss, and safeguard intellectual property. Their platform offers self‑defending mobile applications, comprehensive security policies, and compliance tools for a mobile‑first universe.
b.name: Blue Cedar

b.description: Blue Cheetah develops analog and mixed-signal semiconductor intellectual property for connecting chiplets. Acquired by Tenstorrent, its BlueLynx technology provides customizable physical and link interfaces for chip designs using different fabrication processes and packaging configurations. Founded in 2018, the company is based in Sunnyvale, California and focuses on AI accelerator IP and open hardware solutions.
b.name: Blue Cheetah

b.description: Blue Cloud Pediatric Surgery Centers operates accredited ambulatory surgery centers specializing in pediatric and special-needs dental and oral surgery care delivered under general anesthesia. Positioning itself as the largest pediatric surgery center company in the United States, Blue Cloud partners with dentists and payors across multiple U.S. locations with a mission to expand access to care, exemplify safety and quality, and reduce costs to patients and payors. Headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas, the company is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Blue Cloud is a healthcare services provider and does not publish any public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained for network identity and demand-side coverage.
b.name: Blue Cloud Pediatric Surgery Centers

b.description: Blue Cross Canada (bluecross.ca) is the national consumer-facing brand of the Canadian Association of Blue Cross Plans, the association that owns the Blue Cross trademark in Canada and coordinates a federation of independent, largely not-for-profit regional Blue Cross plans — Alberta Blue Cross, Pacific Blue Cross, Manitoba Blue Cross, Saskatchewan Blue Cross, Ontario and Quebec Blue Cross (Canassurance), and Medavie Blue Cross. Operating in Canada since 1938, the federation covers roughly eight million Canadians a year across supplementary health and dental benefits, group and employee benefits, retiree plans, travel medical insurance, and term life and critical illness cover, and several member plans also administer public health programs on behalf of provincial and federal governments. Its API posture is partner-gated and effectively non-existent as a public surface: bluecross.ca is a WordPress marketing and region-routing site with no developer portal, no API reference, and no published OpenAPI, and the developer/developers/docs/api subdomains do not resolve at all. Members, plan sponsors, brokers, and health-care providers integrate through authenticated member portals, mobile apps, group-benefit employer portals, and third-party health-claim rails rather than through any self-serve API. Canada offers no forcing function that would change this — OSFI supervises prudentially, the provinces (FSRA, AMF) regulate market conduct, there is no open-insurance mandate, and Consumer-Driven Banking explicitly excludes insurance.
b.name: Blue Cross Canada

The app is available on iOS and Android, has been featured as an Apple App of the Day, and carries a 4.6 App Store rating. The company builds browser-based and social strategy games, best known for Starfleet Commander — a persistent, multi-universe game of resource management, alliance building, and fleet combat — along with Stardrift Empires (built with Syfy Games) and the sci-fi MMO ShadowRift. Blue Frog Gaming is a consumer game developer rather than an API-first platform: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API description. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is discovered.

b.description: Blue Hexagon is a cybersecurity company that provides an agent‑less, cloud‑native AI security platform. Leveraging deep‑learning models, it offers real‑time threat detection, continuous compliance, and automated hardening across multi‑cloud workloads, networks, and storage. The solution is designed for enterprises seeking advanced threat defense without the overhead of traditional agents, delivering visibility and protection at runtime.
b.name: Blue Hexagon

b.description: Blue J is an AI-powered tax research platform that delivers defensible, source-backed answers to complex tax questions in seconds, drawing on primary law plus Tax Notes and IBFD content. Built for tax professionals, the platform supports advisory, compliance, tax writing, and training workflows, and is trusted by 4,000+ firms including Crowe, RSM, and Larson. Blue J is a SaaS product accessed through its web application at app.askbluej.com; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Blue J's own public website, security, pricing, and trust-center pages.
b.name: Blue J

b.description: Blue Jeans Network (later BlueJeans by Verizon) was a cloud-based video conferencing company founded in 2009 in Mountain View / San Jose, California. It delivered interoperable video meetings across desktop, mobile, and conference-room systems, and offered a developer surface that included the onVideo/Meetings REST API and a WebRTC Embed SDK for embedding live video into applications. Verizon acquired BlueJeans in 2020; Verizon subsequently discontinued the BlueJeans service and the bluejeans.com website and developer portal are no longer reachable. This profile preserves the company's published package artifacts, which persist in public registries even though the hosted service is retired. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Battery Ventures.
b.name: Blue Jeans Network

b.description: Blue Nile is an online retailer of diamonds and fine jewelry, founded in 1999 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington. It pioneered the direct-to-consumer model for engagement rings and loose diamonds, letting shoppers search and compare certified diamonds by cut, color, clarity, and carat and build custom rings, wedding bands, and gifts online. The company is now part of Signet Jewelers. Blue Nile is included in the API Evangelist network as a consumer / e-commerce company profile; it was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Trinity Ventures. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.
b.name: Blue Nile

b.description: Blue Note Therapeutics is a digital therapeutics company focused on developing innovative treatments for cancer patients. Listed as a member of the Digital Therapeutics Alliance, the company aims to address cancer-related distress through digital interventions. While its own website is not publicly reachable, the alliance member page confirms its identity and mission, providing a basis for API profiling.
b.name: Blue Note Therapeutics

b.description: Blue Ocean Barns develops Brominata®, a patented seaweed-based feed supplement that dramatically reduces methane emissions from cattle, improving energy conversion and profitability for farmers. By leveraging Asparagopsis taxiformis, the product can cut enteric methane by up to 80%, contributing to climate-smart agriculture and offering a sustainable solution for the livestock industry.
b.name: Blue Ocean Barns

b.description: Blue Origin is an American private aerospace manufacturer and spaceflight services company founded in 2000 by Jeff Bezos and headquartered in Kent, Washington. It builds and flies the reusable New Shepard suborbital vehicle, the heavy-lift New Glenn orbital launch vehicle, the BE-3 and BE-4 rocket engines, the Blue Moon lunar lander and the Blue Ring orbital transfer vehicle, and it owns Honeybee Robotics. Blue Origin publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API description for any of its space products; customer, payload and supplier relationships run through authenticated portals — payloads.blueorigin.com and bodp.blueorigin.com on Salesforce Experience Cloud, and supplierportal.blueorigin.com on AWS GovCloud. The only genuinely agent-addressable surface on a blueorigin.com host is the Blue Origin Shop, a Shopify storefront that publishes a real llms.txt and agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, and an anonymous MCP server at /api/mcp exposing five tools. The corporate site itself sits behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint that answers HTTP 429 to every non-browser request, including /robots.txt.
b.name: Blue Origin

b.description: Blue Owl Capital Inc. (NYSE: OWL) is a New York-headquartered alternative asset manager formed in 2021 from the merger of Owl Rock and Dyal Capital, with Oak Street joining in 2022. It manages over $319 billion of assets across three platforms — Credit (direct lending), Real Assets (net lease real estate and digital infrastructure) and GP Strategic Capital (minority stakes in alternative asset managers) — plus insurance solutions, serving institutional investors, financial advisors, individual investors and insurance companies, and runs several publicly traded BDCs including Blue Owl Capital Corporation. Blue Owl publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract; its only investor-facing software surfaces are gated third-party portals (iCapital, DST Vision) reached from blueowl.com/portals.
b.name: Blue Owl Capital

b.description: Blue Planet is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, representing a company for which detailed API information has not yet been discovered. The entry serves as a placeholder pending further investigation to identify the company's official website, API offerings, and related documentation. This placeholder will be enriched as more data becomes available through subsequent profiling steps.
b.name: Blue Planet

b.description: SS&C Blue Prism is an enterprise intelligent-automation vendor whose platform combines robotic process automation, business process management and agentic AI. Its products — Blue Prism Enterprise, Blue Prism Cloud, WorkHQ, Chorus, AI Gateway, Decipher IDP and Process Intelligence — coordinate people, AI agents, digital workers and APIs across regulated, mission-critical workflows. Blue Prism Enterprise publishes a REST contract, the Blue Prism API, covering work queues, sessions, schedules, calendars, processes, runtime resources, licensing and webhook subscriptions. The company was acquired by SS&C Technologies in 2022.
b.name: Blue Prism

b.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.
b.name: Blue River Technology

b.description: Blue Square Group Limited is the corporate entity behind GRVT (pronounced "gravity"), a licensed hybrid crypto derivatives exchange headquartered in Singapore and engineered by Gravity Technologies. GRVT pairs a high-performance central limit order book with self-custody settlement on a zkSync-based Layer 2, and exposes a public Market Data API and an authenticated Trading API over both REST and WebSocket. The APIs cover perpetual futures and spot trading, order management (including bulk orders, TP/SL and trigger orders), positions and margin, sub-account and funding-account summaries, transfers, deposits and withdrawals, and on-chain vault investment and redemption. Authentication combines an API-key login with Ethereum-style ECDSA (secp256k1 / EIP-712) request signing and scoped session keys. First-party Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs plus published agent skills round out the developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Blue Square Group Limited

b.description: Blue Studios Labs is a family-focused technology company operating under the tagline "Where Families Flourish." It builds consumer digital products that help couples and families explore, learn, and grow together. Its portfolio includes Wallio, a shared financial-management app for couples and families; Blue Studios EDU, an entertainment-based educational streaming service; and Blue Studios Entertainment, a media-production studio creating family-oriented narratives and content. The company reports more than 400 million digital views, 350,000 game plays, and 4,000+ classes delivered. Blue Studios is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.
b.name: Blue Studios

b.description: Blue Vision Labs was a London-based computer-vision company that built the first city-scale augmented reality cloud — crowdsourcing centimetre-accurate 3D maps of entire cities from images captured by car-mounted smartphone cameras, then letting developers use visual positioning to place shared and persistent AR content that every device sees in the same real-world spot. It emerged from stealth in March 2018 with a $14.5M round led by GV, alongside Accel and Horizons Ventures, and offered invite-only early access to iOS and Android SDKs covering San Francisco, New York City and London. Lyft acquired the company in October 2018 and made it the UK hub of its Level 5 self-driving division. The developer platform is retired: bluevisionlabs.com no longer resolves to a web host, the documentation and SDK downloads are offline, and no public API surface remains.
b.name: Blue Vision Labs

b.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.
b.name: Blue Water Autonomy

b.description: Blue White Robotics Ltd. — operating as Bluewhite — is an Israeli off-road autonomy company founded in 2017 by Ben Alfi, Yair Shahar and Aviram Shmueli, headquartered in Tel Aviv with a US operation in Fresno, California. Bluewhite builds an OEM-agnostic autonomy stack that retrofits conventional vehicles into unmanned ground vehicles: Pathfinder, an aftermarket autonomy kit combining control, intelligence and perception modules over a distributed CAN network, and Compass, a cloud fleet-operations SaaS that lets operators remotely supervise, task and monitor an autonomous fleet. The company began in permanent-crop agriculture — autonomous spraying, mowing and harvest support across roughly 150,000 US acres for 20-plus growers — and has since extended the same GPS-denied navigation and perception stack to defense and homeland-security ground robotics. Elbit Systems' FUSE acquired 100% of Blue White Robotics in 2026. Bluewhite markets a Software SDK and an "API platform" for OEM and system integration, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the Compass operator platform sits behind a Keycloak/OIDC login and integration access runs through a contact-sales form.
b.name: Blue White Robotics

b.description: Blue Wire is a podcast network and monetization platform built for independent sports content creators, positioning itself as "The Monetization Engine for Sports Creators." The company provides sales, marketing, distribution, and operational support so creators can focus on producing content while Blue Wire handles ad sales and sponsorship coordination across a network of 200+ shows and 500+ creators reaching hundreds of millions of listeners. Backed by 500 Global. Blue Wire operates as a media and advertising business and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Blue Wire

b.description: Transforming supply chains through an end-to-end platform for planning, execution, commerce and returns.

b.description: Bluebirds was an AI-powered outbound sales and go-to-market (GTM) prospecting platform, founded in 2022 by Rohan Punamia (CEO) and Kunal Punera (CTO). The product helped sales teams create, test, and scale AI-driven prospecting triggers, combining LinkedIn signals with first-party CRM data and de-anonymized web traffic so representatives could target and personalize outreach in a unified workflow. Bluebirds was seed-funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners (invested 2023). Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Bluebirds in August 2025 and folded the prospecting agent into Sales Cloud and Agentforce, with integration expected complete by the end of Salesforce fiscal Q3 2026. The absorption is now complete: as of August 2026 every path on bluebirds.com — including /pricing, /docs and every /.well-known/ path — answers HTTP 301 to Salesforce's AI prospecting agent page from an AWS redirect service, api./docs./developer./status./trust subdomains do not resolve, and the former application host app.bluebirds.com resolves but resets the TLS handshake. Bluebirds therefore exposes no public developer or API surface of its own; the prospecting capability is now reached through Salesforce, and this profile is identity-only.
b.name: Bluebirds

b.description: Blueboard is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
b.name: Blueboard

b.description: Bluebook is a Stockholm, Sweden based software company building AI agents for accounting firms, accountants, and CFOs. The platform automates accounting workflows — reconciliations, accruals, accounts payable and receivable, month-end close, reporting, and accounting research — with the stated goal of a "zero-day close", and integrates with the general ledgers firms already run on, notably QuickBooks and NetSuite. The product surface is organized around Background Agents, Checklists (tasks, delegation, human-in-the-loop approvals, month-end close), and an Assistant covering FP&A, flux analysis, and accounting research. Founded in 2024 by Philip Andersson (CEO), Jonathan Andersson (COO), and Filip Stål (CTO), Bluebook went through Y Combinator (Winter 2025) and raised a $3M pre-seed led by EQT Ventures with participation from Y Combinator and angel investors from Affirm, OpenAI, and ElevenLabs. Bluebook is a product company, not an API provider: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, or SDKs.
b.name: Bluebook

b.description: Bluebox (Bluebox Security) was an enterprise mobile and application security startup founded around 2012 that let organizations secure corporate data on employee-owned smartphones and tablets without managing the whole device. It raised roughly $27.5M, with Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) leading its Series A and returning for the Series B alongside Tenaya Capital, Andreas Bechtolsheim, and SV Angel. Its technology assets were acquired by Lookout on April 8, 2016, after which Bluebox ceased operating as an independent company. It was a packaged security product vendor, not a public API provider, and it maintains no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface today.
b.name: Bluebox

b.description: BlueCart is an end-to-end eCommerce and procurement platform for the hospitality and food and beverage industries, connecting restaurants and buyers with wholesale distributors and suppliers. It streamlines wholesale ordering, order management, inventory, and payments for both sides of the supply chain. BlueCart exposes a public REST API that lets distributors and partners programmatically manage products, orders, customers, catalogs, and users, returning JSON responses and integrating BlueCart data with external accounting, eCommerce, and logistics systems used across foodservice operations.
b.name: BlueCart

b.description: Bluechipart is an art dealer specializing in sourcing and selling high-value blue-chip artworks for collectors and dealers. They provide discreet, cost-effective transactions, expert consultation, and access to masterpieces by artists such as Picasso, Warhol, and Rothko, operating in the secondary art market.
b.name: Bluechipart

b.description: Blue Coat Systems was a web-security and network-forensics vendor best known for its ProxySG secure web gateway appliances, SSL Visibility, WebPulse/Global Intelligence Network threat intelligence, and cloud web security (the Web Security Service). Bain Capital led a consortium that took Blue Coat private in 2015; Symantec acquired the company in 2016, and Broadcom acquired Symantec's enterprise security business in 2019. Blue Coat's technology now ships inside Broadcom's Symantec Enterprise Cloud portfolio as Cloud Secure Web Gateway (Cloud SWG), Secure Web Gateway (ProxySG/ASG), SSL Visibility, CASB (CloudSOC), and DLP. Product documentation and REST APIs are published on the Broadcom TechDocs portal.
b.name: Bluecoat (Symantec)

b.description: BlueConic is a customer data platform (CDP) with a REST API for managing unified customer profiles, lifecycle stages, segments, connections, and permissions-based data activation. The API provides OAuth 2.0-secured access to visitor profiles, segments, interactions, and audit events via an OpenAPI-compliant interface.
b.name: BlueConic

b.description: Bluecore is a retail marketing technology platform that unifies shopper identity, behavior, and product data into a customer data platform with 20+ predictive AI models, cross-channel experience orchestration (email, SMS, site, paid media), and AI shopping and marketing agents. Its public developer API (developers.bluecore.com) exposes OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication, Customer Profile management, eligibility (consent) management, and Communicate surfaces for transactional and direct-send messaging. Customers include Wayfair, Gap, J.Crew, Lenovo, CVS, and Fender. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Techstars.
b.name: Bluecore

b.description: BlueData Software Inc was a big-data infrastructure company whose EPIC platform ran Hadoop, Spark, and other analytics workloads in Docker containers on-premises and in the cloud. It was a dcvc (Data Collective) portfolio company and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2018; its technology now lives on as the HPE Ezmeral Container Platform. The original www.bluedata.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's container-platform page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.
b.name: Bluedata Software Inc

b.description: Bluefarmkorea is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. It appears to be associated with agricultural technology services in Korea, but no public website or detailed information could be verified.
b.name: Bluefarmkorea

b.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.
b.name: Bluefin Labs

b.description: Bluefish AI is an enterprise AI marketing platform built for Fortune 500 brands to gain visibility and control over how they are represented across AI channels. The platform spans AI monitoring of brand reputation in AI-native experiences, generative engine optimization (GEO) to improve performance across AI search, GEO measurement frameworks, AI brand safety and accuracy verification, and agentic commerce tooling for AI-driven buying journeys. It serves search, content, brand, and PR teams. Founded by martech veterans whose prior advertising technologies are now owned by Microsoft and Meta, and backed by enterprise and AI investors including Bloomberg Beta and Threshold Ventures, with a $43M Series B in 2026. Bluefish publishes no developer documentation, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs, but it does operate a live first-party remote MCP server at platform.bluefishai.com/mcp, protected by OAuth 2.1 with full RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 discovery and offered to customers as a connected app.
b.name: Bluefish AI

b.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.
b.name: blueflite

b.description: Blue Frontier, Inc. specializes in innovative air‑conditioning systems that combine sustainability, comfort, and energy storage. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the company leverages artificial intelligence and data analytics to create energy‑efficient HVAC solutions. It targets commercial and residential markets, aiming to reduce carbon footprints while delivering high performance and smart climate control.
b.name: Bluefrontier

b.description: Blueground is a global proptech company that leases, furnishes and operates move-in-ready apartments for stays of a month or longer, running thousands of units across cities in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America. It operates an end-to-end technology stack: a consumer booking site and iOS/Android guest apps, an internal property, pricing and operations platform, and the Blueground Partner Network — an invite-only marketplace where third-party furnished-rental operators list supply and connect inventory through PMS and channel-manager integrations (Avantio, NextPax, Rentals United, Hostify, Hostfully, SiteMinder, Cloudbeds, Airbnb). Blueground publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable contract: partner connectivity is brokered through channel-manager partners rather than a self-serve API. Its engineering organization does maintain a real open-source footprint on GitHub (bluegroundltd), with libraries released to Maven Central and npm, and the main website publishes an llms.txt.
b.name: Blueground

b.description: Bluejay is the testing, monitoring, and improvement layer for conversational AI agents. Enterprises, startups, and developers use Bluejay to evaluate voice and chat agents, run lifelike simulations with synthetic "digital humans" across voice, chat, SMS, and text channels, load-test and replay production calls, and catch regressions before they reach customers. The platform pairs a simulation engine with production observability - automated evaluation of tone, accuracy, task completion, and custom metrics, plus dashboards and alerts. It exposes a REST API (X-API-Key auth, /v1), a hosted MCP server, event webhooks, a first-party Python SDK, and integrations with Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs, Bland, LiveKit, Google Dialogflow CX / CES, and Kore.ai. Backed by Homebrew.
b.name: Bluejay

b.description: Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc. was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing treatments for viral hepatitis and liver disease. Its lead asset, brelovitug (BJT-778), is an investigational monoclonal antibody targeting the surface antigen shared by the hepatitis D and hepatitis B viruses; it received U.S. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for chronic hepatitis delta and reported a 100% virologic response at week 48 in its Phase 2 monotherapy study before entering the AZURE-2 global Phase 3 trial. The company also advanced a proprietary TLR9 agonist (cavrotolimod), a liver-targeted HBV transcript inhibitor (BJT-628) and a liver-targeted fatty acid synthase inhibitor (BJT-188) toward a combination regimen aimed at functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. Mirum Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire Bluejay Therapeutics in December 2025 and completed the acquisition on 26 January 2026; the corporate site now serves a single acquisition notice redirecting readers to mirumpharma.com. Bluejay Therapeutics never ran a developer program — no product API, no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs, no GitHub organisation and no package-registry presence. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind bluejaytx.com, catalogued here. That surface is notable for outliving the web site it belongs to: the marketing page tree was deleted in the teardown, but the REST API and the post archive still serve all 35 press releases and publication notices from 2021 through 2025 with full text.
b.name: Bluejay Therapeutics

b.description: BlueKai was a data management platform (DMP) and third-party audience data marketplace founded in 2008 that let marketers collect, organize, and activate first- and third-party audience data for programmatic advertising and targeting. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into the Oracle Data Cloud; Oracle wound down its advertising business (including the former BlueKai and Data Cloud assets) in 2024. The company operates no independent developer program today — the bluekai.com domain 301-redirects to Oracle's advertising pages and exposes no live public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.
b.name: BlueKai

b.description: BlueLabs (withbluelabs.ai) is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building toward "emotional intelligence at scale." Its core technology, Blue-JST, is described as a novel dual reward mechanism designed to balance relationships and utility — an approach grounded in reward modeling and reinforcement learning. The company is backed by Forerunner Ventures and is actively hiring research talent. As of this profile it publishes a single marketing site (built on Webflow) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface; this record will be enriched as a developer- or agent-facing surface emerges.
b.name: BlueLabs

b.description: BlueLayer is an operating-system platform for carbon-project developers, providing infrastructure to collect project data, run automated digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV), manage the carbon-credit lifecycle from estimation through retirement, and generate revenue by distributing and selling credits while reducing compliance burden. The product spans project operations, a revenue engine, credit management, a stakeholder DataHub, customizable dashboards, and integrations with registries, CRMs, accounting software, and ERPs. Backed by Point Nine, BlueLayer was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface was found — the platform is accessed via its hosted web application.
b.name: BlueLayer

b.description: Blueleaf is a wealth management software platform for financial advisors and enterprise RIAs that combines a branded client portal, automated investment performance reporting, account aggregation across custodians and institutions, automated billing, and portfolio rebalancing into one system. Its data-access API lets partners pull householded account balances, holdings, and transactions without handling end-user banking credentials, and it operates an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect identity provider at secure.blueleaf.com. Blueleaf is backed by 500 Global and Anthemis and was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public developer, security, and OIDC discovery surfaces.
b.name: BlueLeaf

b.description: Bluemtec Co., Ltd. is a South Korean company providing digital and distribution services for the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors. It operates platforms for big data analysis, online pharmaceutical commerce, marketing, IT development, logistics, and medical staff matching. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Yongin-si, the firm serves both domestic and international pharmaceutical manufacturers and platform operators, aiming to drive digital transformation in the medical industry.
b.name: Bluemtec

b.description: BlueNalu, Inc. is a San Diego, California cellular aquaculture company founded in 2017 by Lou Cooperhouse, Chris Somogyi and Chris Dammann that produces cell-cultivated seafood — real seafood grown directly from fish cells rather than harvested from the ocean. Its lead product is cell-cultivated bluefin tuna toro, marketed as "Seafood Without Compromise", targeted first at premium foodservice operators in the United States and then internationally. The company has raised approximately $84 million to date, including a Series B and a December 2025 insider-led convertible note and preferred stock financing led by Agronomics, Siddhi Capital and Lewis & Clark AgriFood, and was the first cell-cultivated seafood company admitted to the National Fisheries Institute. BlueNalu is a food and biotechnology producer; it publishes a marketing website and no public developer or API surface.
b.name: BlueNalu

b.description: Bluenote is an AI platform for life sciences that automates regulatory and clinical documentation for pharmaceutical, medical device, diagnostic, and CDMO companies. Its AI agents, workflow builder, document generation, dataset search, and translation tooling accelerate regulatory submissions by 50-75% across the pre-clinical, clinical, CMC, regulatory, quality, and commercial stages of the product lifecycle. Bluenote is an enterprise, sales-led company with no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface published as of this profile; it maintains a Vanta-hosted trust center and a public privacy policy. Backed by Electric Capital and Lux Capital, tracked in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare / life-sciences AI company.
b.name: Bluenote

b.description: BlueOcean is a Context AI platform purpose-built for marketing teams. Its agentic AI framework, Spark, combines brand, market, product, and customer context to help marketers unlock creativity, accelerate go-to-market, and deliver measurable impact — automating work from strategy through content creation, competitive intelligence, brand performance analytics, and reporting. The platform surfaces evidence-grounded recommendations across brand, product marketing, and content, and is used by enterprise marketing teams at companies such as SAP, AWS, and Cisco. BlueOcean is backed by Insight Partners. b.description: Blueprint Power was a New York City software company, founded in 2017 by Robyn Beavers, that turned commercial real estate portfolios into virtual power plants. Its cloud platform connected to distributed energy assets in buildings — solar, batteries, cogeneration — and used data-driven and machine-learning models to aggregate, orchestrate and transact that surplus capacity into wholesale energy markets. It raised a $3.5M Series A (Congruent Ventures, MetaProp, Fifth Wall, Fred Wilson, Brad Burnham) and was acquired by bp in October 2021, joining the bp Launchpad portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public surface: www.blueprintpower.com returns a 301 permanent redirect to bp.com/retailenergy, and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public GitHub organization could be found. b.name: Blueprint Title

b.description: Blueqat provides a quantum computing library and SDK that enables developers to simulate and run quantum algorithms on various backends. The platform offers Python and other language support, extensive documentation, and tools for quantum circuit design, making quantum computing accessible to researchers and developers.
b.name: Blueqat

b.description: BlueRock Security is a runtime security, observability, and governance platform for AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Its BRACE (BlueRock Agent Control Environment) provides deep observability and context-powered guardrails across the full agentic action path — from model decision through agent actions, tool calls, and MCP server interactions — with a Trust Context Engine and an MCP Trust Registry for verifying MCP server ownership and capabilities. BlueRock ships a lightweight open-source Python runtime sensor (Apache 2.0) that captures MCP tool calls, session lifecycle, module imports, subprocess execution, and network calls as structured NDJSON with zero code changes, plus a self-hostable runtime daemon, sandbox isolation, policy engine, dashboard, and agent-framework integrations for LangChain and CrewAI. Backed by Wing Venture Capital.
b.name: Bluerock Security

b.description: BlueRock Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative cell therapies for neurodegenerative and ophthalmic diseases. Leveraging advanced stem cell technologies, the company aims to address unmet medical needs in Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and retinal disorders, advancing candidates through preclinical and clinical stages to bring innovative treatments to patients.
b.name: BlueRock Therapeutics

b.description: Blues (formerly Blues Wireless) is an IoT connectivity platform that provides hardware modules called Notecards and a cloud service called Notehub for routing device data from edge devices to cloud applications. The Notehub REST API enables developers to manage fleets of cellular, satellite, LoRa, and Wi-Fi connected devices across 130+ countries. Developers can use the API to retrieve device events, manage projects and fleets, configure routes to downstream cloud services, and monitor device health. Blues follows a consumption-based pricing model with no subscription fees, charging per ingressed event beyond a free monthly allowance bundled with each Notecard hardware purchase.
b.name: Blues

b.description: Blueshift is an AI-powered customer engagement and customer data platform (CDP) that unifies customer profiles, product and content catalogs, and behavioural event streams, then activates them across email, SMS, push, in-app messaging, mobile inbox, iOS Live Activities and on-site live content. Its public surface is a REST API on api.getblueshift.com (US) and api.eu.getblueshift.com (EU) covering customers, events, catalogs, segments, custom user lists, campaigns, templates, shared assets, promotions, external fetches, interest alerts, subscription groups and email validation, documented operation-by-operation with a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0 document behind every reference page. Blueshift also runs an official OAuth 2.0 remote MCP server in public beta, and ships first-party SDKs for iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter and Cordova.
b.name: Blueshift

Founded to provide a flexible alternative to Braze and Iterable, Blueshift serves retailers, financial services, healthcare, and other industries, delivering tools for journey orchestration, AI agents, and real‑time personalization.

b.name: BlueSpace

b.description: Bluespine is an AI‑driven platform that helps self‑insured employers and health‑plan sponsors reduce medical claims overbilling, monitor plan performance, and meet fiduciary duties under ERISA. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, the company leverages machine‑readable price transparency files, carrier billing guidelines, and proprietary data sources to detect policy violations and recover savings for plan participants.
b.name: Bluespine

b.description: BlueStacks is the Android app player and mobile-cloud gaming platform operated by now.gg, Inc. (Campbell, California). The consumer product runs Android apps and games on Windows and macOS, while the now.gg mobile cloud streams the same titles in a browser. The developer-facing surface is published at docs.now.gg and is built around nowStudio (the publisher console) and nowSDK (Unity and native Android modules for Payments, User Account Service, Rewarded Ads, Events and Utility). Two server-side REST surfaces are documented publicly: a User Account Service OAuth 2.0 API on now.gg for token generation, token verification, user info and session info, and a Payments API on payments-api.now.gg for server-side purchase verification, consumption and subscription acknowledgement. now.gg also calls developer-hosted webhooks for subscription and webshop order events, ships an official nowgg CLI on PyPI for uploading app builds, and publishes an embeddable JavaScript module for running cloud games in an iframe. BlueStacks AI is a separate, newer product line that packages a sandboxed local runtime for AI agents.
b.name: Bluestacks

b.description: Bluestem Brands, Inc. is an American multi-brand direct-to-consumer retailer headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minnesota. It is best known for Fingerhut, a credit-based catalog and online retailer that extends revolving credit (via partner WebBank) to underserved consumers so they can purchase brand-name merchandise across home, electronics, apparel, and general merchandise categories. Bluestem historically operated a broader portfolio of catalog and e-commerce brands and reaches shoppers through its websites, mobile apps, and printed catalogs. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found for Bluestem Brands or Fingerhut at the time of enrichment.
b.name: Bluestem Brands

b.description: BlueStone is one of India's largest online retailers of fine jewellery, founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and headquartered in Bangalore. It runs an omnichannel model spanning its e-commerce storefront and 125+ physical stores across India, offering 7,000+ BIS-hallmarked and certified designs in gold, diamond, gemstone, and platinum, plus services such as lifetime exchange, buyback, 30-day returns, and personal video consultations. The company is backed by Accel. BlueStone publishes no public developer portal or API; this profile captures the company's identity and a probed domain-security posture for the network.
b.name: Bluestone

b.description: Bluestone Lane is an Australian‑origin coffee brand operating cafés across the United States. It offers ethically‑sourced, meticulously‑roasted coffee beans, a subscription service, wholesale programs, and a loyalty app that rewards frequent customers. The company emphasizes sustainable packaging, community‑centric café experiences, and corporate coffee solutions for businesses. While it runs a robust retail e‑commerce site and provides corporate coffee services, it does not currently expose a public API for external developers. The brand focuses on quality, sustainability, and a distinctive Australian café culture brought to American neighborhoods.
b.name: Bluestonelane

b.description: BlueStripe Software was an application performance management (APM) vendor headquartered in the Research Triangle Park area of North Carolina. Its flagship product, FactFinder, provided application-aware infrastructure performance monitoring and end-to-end transaction tracing across distributed servers, letting operations teams map and troubleshoot how applications behaved across physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure. The company was backed by Trinity Ventures and other venture investors before being acquired by Microsoft in April 2015, after which its technology was folded into Microsoft System Center and the Operations Management Suite (OMS) and the standalone BlueStripe product and developer surface were discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company no longer operates an independent website, developer portal, or API.
b.name: BlueStripe Software

b.description: BlueTalon was a data-centric security company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, that provided centralized data access control, dynamic data masking, and policy enforcement across big-data and hybrid data environments (Hadoop, Spark, relational databases, and cloud data stores). Its platform let enterprises define and enforce fine-grained authorization, auditing, and data- protection policies from a single control point. BlueTalon was backed by DCVC (Data Collective) among other investors, and was acquired by Microsoft in 2019, with its technology folded into Microsoft's Azure data-governance and security portfolio. The company no longer operates independently: bluetalon.com is no longer resolvable and the GitHub organization retains only archived, deprecated repositories. This profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider; there is no live public API surface to enrich.
b.name: Bluetalon

b.description: BlueTalon Data Systems was a data-centric security company that built dynamic, policy-based access control, data masking, filtering, and auditing for enterprise data platforms such as Hadoop, relational databases, and big-data stores. It let organizations enforce fine-grained authorization and privacy controls at the point of data access. Founded around 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, BlueTalon was acquired by Microsoft in July 2019, after which its team and technology were absorbed into Microsoft's data-governance and security efforts (Azure). BlueTalon no longer operates as an independent company; the bluetalon.com domain is parked on Azure DNS with no active web, developer, or API surface, so this network profile carries identity only and has no live artifacts to enrich.
b.name: BlueTalon Data Systems

b.description: BlueTarp Financial is a B2B trade-credit and accounts-receivable financing company, founded in Portland, Maine, that lets suppliers, distributors, and building-materials dealers extend revolving or net-terms credit to their business customers while BlueTarp pays the supplier upfront and assumes the credit risk and collections. Its SmartView portal manages the purchase-to-payment lifecycle: credit decisioning, invoicing, billing, and receivables. BlueTarp was acquired and is now operated as Capital One Trade Credit; its independent site (bluetarp.com) redirects to capitalone.com/trade-credit/bluetarp. BlueTarp publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.
b.name: BlueTarp Financial

b.description: Blueteamglobal is a stealth-mode cybersecurity company offering advanced cyber threat monitoring services. Listed on LinkedIn, the firm appears affiliated with BlueVoyant and focuses on threat detection, incident response, and security analytics for enterprise clients. While detailed public documentation is limited, the company positions itself as a specialized provider in the cyber defense market, targeting organizations seeking proactive threat intelligence and monitoring solutions.
b.name: Blueteamglobal

b.description: Blue Tech (Bluetechcbdc) is a manufacturer specializing in research, development, and production of core functional components for industrial machine tools, CNC machine tools, and machining centers. Founded in 2010, it operates in software, AI, data and analytics industries, offering advanced components for machining applications.
b.name: Bluetechcbdc

b.description: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters is an Indian specialty coffee company founded in 2013, roasting and selling fresh coffee beans, capsules, and ready‑to‑drink beverages. The company operates an e‑commerce site offering subscriptions, wholesale, and retail sales, and maintains a blog, brewing guides, and community recipes. It provides a developer portal for its e‑commerce APIs, enabling partners to integrate product catalogs, orders, and customer data.
b.name: Bluetokaicoffeeroasters

b.description: BlueTrace provides a cloud‑based platform that streamlines seafood supply‑chain operations, offering tools for inventory management, order processing, pricing, traceability, and compliance. Their solution connects distributors, processors, and retailers, enabling real‑time data sharing, automated invoicing, and analytics to improve efficiency and sustainability across the seafood industry.
b.name: BlueTrace

b.description: Blue Triangle Technologies provides a Revenue Assurance Platform that quantifies website friction in monetary terms, enabling digital teams to prioritize fixes that impact revenue. The platform continuously measures visitor interactions, identifies costly friction points, and validates ROI of improvements, integrating with tools like Jira. It serves enterprises across eCommerce, financial services, travel, and healthcare, offering analytics, remediation plans, and AI‑assisted insights.
b.name: Bluetriangletechnologies

b.description: Bluevine is a small business banking and lending platform offering business checking accounts, lines of credit, bill pay, invoicing, and cash flow management tools for United States small and medium businesses. Bluevine does not publish a first-party public developer API or developer portal; external programmatic connectivity is delivered through the Plaid open-banking aggregator (with Finicity/Mastercard coverage also reported) and through native app integrations to QuickBooks Online, Xero, Wave, Expensify, Stripe, Square, Gusto, Cash App, and Venmo. Deposits are FDIC-insured up to $3 million through a sweep network, with revolving credit up to $250,000 issued by Celtic Bank.
b.name: Bluevine

b.description: BlueVoyant is a cyber defense company that combines managed detection and response (MDR), digital risk protection, and supply-chain (third-party) cyber risk management into a cloud-native platform backed by a global security operations capability. It continuously monitors customers' internal networks, endpoints, and cloud along with their external attack surface and vendor ecosystem, using threat intelligence to detect, investigate, and remediate threats. BlueVoyant serves enterprises and governments across sectors and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead (8vc); this profile is maintained by the enrichment pipeline against public sources.
b.name: Bluevoyant

b.description: Bluewhite is an AI‑powered autonomy company delivering off‑road autonomous solutions for critical defense missions. Their platform automates high‑risk, labor‑intensive operations such as combat logistics, route clearance, and border security, enabling frontline units to operate safely and efficiently. With over 100,000 autonomous operating hours and a modular, interoperable stack, Bluewhite provides scalable, software‑driven autonomy for defense forces worldwide.
b.name: Bluewhite

b.description: BlueWillow Biologics is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company pioneering intranasal vaccine technology. Their NanoVax® platform delivers antigens via an oil‑in‑water emulsion, aiming to transform prevention and treatment of infectious diseases, pandemic preparedness, and food allergies. The company originated from University of Michigan research and now advances human clinical trials of its adjuvant and delivery system.
b.name: BlueWillow Biologics

b.description: Blue World Technologies develops and manufactures high‑temperature PEM methanol fuel cell components and systems for maritime, stationary and heavy‑duty transportation sectors. The company aims to provide green, efficient alternatives to combustion engines and diesel generators, focusing on renewable methanol solutions and advanced fuel cell platforms.
b.name: Blueworldtechnologies

b.description: BlueYard Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2016, operating as a small, equal partnership with offices in Europe and the United States. Managing roughly $500M in AUM, it invests $500K-$5M at pre-seed to Series A as lead or co-lead investor, backing two kinds of technologies: those that move us toward utopia and those that hold the line against oblivion. Its focus areas span computation & intelligence, engineering/aerospace & defense, biology & chemistry, and crypto. Notable portfolio companies and exits include Privy (acquired by Stripe), Groq, IonQ, Filecoin, Castelion, and Marvel Fusion. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio relationship of foundry-group and enriched from BlueYard's public website; it exposes no public developer API.
b.name: BlueYard

b.description: Bluma is a San Francisco-based AI company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) building a short-form AI content engine that lets creators, agencies, and brands produce social media video ads at scale. The platform "de-edits" existing reference videos into their individual scenes, captions, and overlays, then uses AI asset generation and a node-based canvas editor to recreate and remix shots into new ads, UGC, and template-based videos optimized for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. Bluma ships a public developer program: a REST API at api.getbluma.com/api/v1 for asynchronous video generation, templates, credits, API keys, webhooks and usage analytics; Mintlify-hosted documentation at docs.getbluma.com; first-party TypeScript and Python SDKs; a seven-event HMAC-signed webhook surface; published per-tier rate limits; and an undocumented but live hosted MCP server at api.getbluma.com/api/mcp gated by Clerk OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. Founded by Alisa Wu (formerly Zoox/Amazon) and Stephen Ni.
b.name: Bluma

b.description: Blume is a women-owned self-care and skincare brand (blume.com) selling cleansers, serums, oils, gel creams, and sunscreen for acne, dark spots, and sensitive skin, marketed as vegan, certified clean, climate neutral, and plastic neutral. Its direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a genuine agent-native commerce surface: a canonical /agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP 2026-04-08) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a live Model Context Protocol endpoint for agent-driven shopping (search, cart, checkout, fulfillment), and Shopify Customer Account OAuth2/OpenID Connect authentication. Surfaced from the 500 Global and Felicis portfolios and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from live discovery documents.
b.name: Blume

b.description: Blume Global provides a cloud-based supply chain visibility platform that empowers partners across logistics, manufacturing, and distribution to detect risks early, act decisively, and protect performance. Their solutions include real-time visibility, strategic sourcing, part quality management, and carrier integrations, helping enterprises streamline operations and improve decision-making throughout the supply chain.
b.name: Blume Global

b.description: Blumira provides a security operations platform that helps IT teams detect, investigate, and respond to threats across cloud, on‑premise, and hybrid environments. It offers features such as automated alerting, evidence‑rich case management, integrations with major cloud providers, and a developer‑friendly API for ingesting logs, managing detections, and automating response actions. The platform aims to simplify security operations while delivering comprehensive visibility and compliance reporting.
b.name: Blumira

b.description: Blur is a New York-based NFT marketplace and aggregator built for professional traders on Ethereum, founded by the pseudonymous "Pacman" (Tieshun Roquerre) in October 2022 and backed by Paradigm and Standard Crypto. The flagship product, blur.io, offers zero marketplace fees, multi-marketplace sweeping, bulk listing/bidding, real-time mempool reveal sniping, and a portfolio-grade analytics surface that aggregates liquidity from OpenSea, X2Y2, LooksRare, and other Seaport-compatible venues. Blur also operates Blend, a peer-to-peer perpetual NFT lending protocol designed by Paradigm researchers that powers ETH-against-NFT borrowing and Buy-Now-Pay-Later flows without oracles or fixed expiries — Blend has captured the dominant share of NFT lending volume on Ethereum. The BLUR token, distributed via multi-season airdrop campaigns, governs the Blur DAO through the Blur Foundation. The same team launched Blast, an Ethereum L2 with native yield, which now hosts its own NFT activity. Blur does not publish an official public developer API or SDK; on-chain integration happens via the deployed marketplace and Blend smart contracts (Seaport-compatible), and marketplace data is reached through third-party indexers such as Bitquery, SimpleHash, and Alchemy rather than a Blur-operated REST or GraphQL endpoint.
b.name: Blur

b.description: Blurb is an online self-publishing and print-on-demand platform that lets photographers, designers, businesses, and creative storytellers design, print, and distribute their own books, magazines, notebooks, and wall art. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in San Francisco, Blurb provides desktop and web design tools (BookWright, Bookify, and plugins for Adobe InDesign and Lightroom) alongside professional in-house printing, global fulfillment, and distribution through its own bookstore, Amazon, and Ingram. Blurb also offers a RESTful print-on-demand API — powered by its RPI Print fulfillment infrastructure — so businesses can programmatically submit print orders, upload print-ready PDFs, and receive real-time order tracking and fulfillment updates. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Blurb

b.description: BluSmart Mobility was an Indian ride‑sharing company offering all‑electric taxis across major cities. Founded in 2019, it grew to operate a fleet of over 3,000 EVs, providing a surge‑free, environmentally friendly alternative to traditional cabs. The startup faced financial difficulties and entered insolvency proceedings in 2025, marking the end of its operations.
