b.name: Bone

b.description: Bone Health Technologies develops innovative diagnostic and monitoring solutions for bone health, focusing on advanced imaging, biomarkers, and data-driven platforms to help clinicians assess bone density, fracture risk, and treatment efficacy. The company aims to improve patient outcomes through technology integration and research collaborations, offering APIs for data access and integration with healthcare systems.
b.name: Bone Health Technologies

b.description: Bonfire Analytics provides sales intelligence solutions for the healthcare sector, helping commercial leaders and business development teams identify target markets, optimize referral pathways, and evaluate market share. Their platform offers deep provider and organization insights, market segmentation, and referral intelligence to drive growth and improve outreach strategies across the health ecosystem.
b.name: Bonfire Analytics

b.description: Bonfire Interactive is a strategic sourcing and procurement software company serving the public sector, based in the Kitchener-Waterloo region of Ontario, Canada. Its GoBonfire platform digitizes RFP/RFQ sourcing, bid evaluation and scoring, supplier management, and contract workflows for government agencies, education, healthcare, utilities, and nonprofit organizations. Bonfire was acquired by GTY Technology Holdings in 2019, and has since been consolidated — alongside IonWave, EqualLevel, and DemandStar — into Euna Solutions as Euna Procurement, a full-cycle public-sector procurement suite spanning sourcing, contracting, marketplace purchasing, invoicing, and supplier management. The gobonfire.com domain now redirects to eunasolutions.com. Bonfire does not publish a public developer API program or OpenAPI definition; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness and demand tracking.
b.name: Bonfire Interactive

b.description: Bonfire Studios is an independent video game development studio based in Irvine, California, focused on building original interactive entertainment, including its announced title Arkheron. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, Bonfire Studios does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other programmable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich; this profile is maintained as a company record and an ongoing lead should a developer surface emerge.
b.name: Bonfire Studios

b.description: Bonfire Ventures is a Los Angeles-based, seed-stage venture capital firm co-founded by Mark Mullen and Jim Andelman that invests exclusively in business-to-business (B2B) software companies, with a current focus on AI-native B2B founders. The firm runs a low-volume, high-conviction, high-support model — backing roughly 10 to 12 new companies a year, leading approximately 95% of the rounds it participates in and taking board seats — and positions itself as "AI-native too," operating an in-house AI system called Bonnie to source and support founders. Bonfire reports more than $18B in cumulative exit value across its history, with notable outcomes including TaxJar (acquired by Stripe), MNTN (IPO), The Trade Desk, Scopely, Moat (acquired by Oracle), and Comparably (acquired by ZoomInfo). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Foundry Group and enriched from the firm's public site.
b.name: Bonfire Ventures

b.description: Bonfy.AI provides advanced data security solutions for enterprises, protecting against data risks, shadow AI, and ensuring contextual data enforcement across AI agents and platforms. Their offerings include data surface visibility, secure AI systems, and compliance tools for financial services, healthcare, and technology sectors, helping organizations mitigate AI‑driven threats and maintain governance.
b.name: Bonfy.AI

b.description: Bongo Learn provides an assessment and skills development platform for partners and higher education, offering AI role‑play, video assessments, scoring, and coaching tools to certify and measure partner enablement and student learning outcomes.
b.name: Bongo Learn

b.description: Bongobd, operating as Bongo, is Bangladesh’s leading OTT and VOD platform since 2013, offering a vast catalog of Bangla movies, natok, web series, live TV channels, and originals. It streams content in HD, provides subtitles and dubbing in multiple languages, and supports offline downloads via its app. With over 500 YouTube channels, 83+ million subscribers, and a reach of 210 million unique viewers monthly, Bongo serves a South Asian audience across multiple countries, delivering entertainment through state‑of‑the‑art video delivery technology.
b.name: Bongobd

b.description: Bonitasoft is the French open-source company behind Bonita, a business process management and process automation platform used to model BPMN processes, build living applications, and orchestrate work across an organization. Bonita ships as Bonita Studio, Bonita Fabric (Process Designer, BPA Studio, UI Builder), Bonita Work Hub and the Bonita Runtime, in a free Community Edition and a commercial Enterprise Edition, plus a managed Bonita Cloud offering. Every Bonita feature reachable over HTTP is described by a single first-party OpenAPI 3.0.2 document — the Bonita Web REST API, 153 paths and 224 operations across BPM, identity, application, BDM and platform resources — published as an open-source repository, a versioned release asset and a live ReDoc reference. In June 2026 the company rebranded to Ofelia and moved its web, documentation and community properties from bonitasoft.com to ofelia.com, adding a governed agentic AI orchestration line (Ofelia Assistant, Ofelia Workflow, Ofelia Agentic) alongside the Bonita BPM platform.
b.name: Bonitasoft

b.description: Bonjoro is a personal-video customer engagement platform operated by Vimily Pty Ltd of Sydney, Australia. Sales, marketing, customer success and education teams use it to record short one-to-one videos — "Bonjoros" — and deliver them at the moments that decide a relationship: signup, onboarding, first purchase, renewal and churn risk. Alongside the messaging product it runs a video testimonial collection surface. Bonjoro publishes a REST API (API V2, 94 paths and 123 operations) covering greets, recipient profiles, campaigns and workspaces, recordings and media, message templates, engagement results and stats, transmissions and deliverability, replies, teams and users, custom sending domains and verified signatures, and the trigger/action automation engine that wires Bonjoro into CRMs and email platforms. REST API access is published as a Company-tier entitlement; the wider integration surface runs through 18+ native connectors and a first-party Zapier app.
b.name: Bonjoro

b.description: Bonnet is a UK-based electric vehicle (EV) charging app that aggregates multiple charging networks into a single platform, letting drivers find, access, and pay for chargers across Europe through one membership. Headquartered in Bristol and acquired by OVO Energy, it gives consumers real-time charger status, route planning, membership plans with per-charge savings, and weekly charging-credit rewards, while offering charge point operator (CPO) and fleet solutions with white-label integration for businesses. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Bonnet publishes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API at this time.
b.name: Bonnet

b.description: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is a federal agency within the U.S. Department of Energy that markets wholesale electrical power from federal hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest. BPA also operates and maintains about three-quarters of the high-voltage transmission in the Pacific Northwest. The agency provides publicly available GIS data, energy statistics, and operational data through its data hub and web services.
b.name: Bonneville Power Administration

b.description: Bonnier is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: stockholm-trip) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Bonnier

b.description: Bonnus is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
b.name: Bonnus

b.description: Bonobos is a US menswear brand and direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer, founded in 2007 and known for pioneering online-first apparel sales alongside its physical "Guideshop" fitting-room locations. It sells men's clothing including pants, chinos, dress shirts, suits, and casualwear through bonobos.com. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel, Felicis and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer-sector retail company. Bonobos publishes a public retail website but does not operate a public developer API program; this profile captures its real published surface (identity, legal, support, and domain-security posture).
b.name: Bonobos

b.description: Bonpara, Inc is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
b.name: Bonpara

b.description: Bonsai (hellobonsai.com) is an all-in-one business management platform for service businesses -- freelancers, agencies, and firms -- consolidating client management (CRM, pipeline, proposals, contracts, forms, client portal), project management (tasks, Gantt, time tracking, timesheets, resource planning), and financial management (invoicing, payments, expenses, bookkeeping, rate cards, budgeting and profitability) into one system. Used by 500,000+ small businesses globally. Bonsai exposes its programmatic surface through an official hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server at mcp.hellobonsai.com so AI clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Codex) can act on tasks, projects, deals, contacts, time entries and invoices; a public REST API is documented as forthcoming. Backed by Matrix Partners.
b.name: Bonsai

b.description: Bonsai, made by One More Cloud, is a fully managed hosted Elasticsearch and OpenSearch search service (managed or bring-your-own-cloud on AWS and Google Cloud), with vector search, a Heroku add-on and a Terraform provider. Its Bonsai Cloud REST API at https://api.bonsai.io (alpha) manages clusters and lists plans, releases (search engine versions) and spaces (regions), authenticated with Basic or Bearer API tokens.
b.name: Bonsai

b.description: Bonsai Robotics is a full‑stack physical AI company building the intelligence layer for autonomous machines in rugged, off‑road environments. It offers vision‑based automation solutions for agriculture, mining, construction and other sectors, enabling autonomous vehicles and equipment to operate without GPS or cellular connections.
b.name: Bonsai Robotics

b.description: Bonterra (formerly EveryAction) is a social-good technology company whose EveryAction / NGP VAN platform powers fundraising, advocacy, organizing, and supporter engagement for nonprofits, unions, and political campaigns. The EveryAction 8 (EA8) REST API at api.securevan.com/v4 exposes people matching, contributions and recurring commitments, disbursements, events, survey questions, activist codes, canvass responses, bulk import and file-loading jobs, early-vote and voter-registration fields, employers/worksites, scores, printed lists, and MiniVAN exports. It uses HTTP Basic authentication with an application name and an API key scoped to a database mode (My Voters or My Campaign), and is documented on a ReadMe-hosted developer portal with a reference, recipes, changelog, and an llms.txt.
b.name: Bonterra (fka EveryAction)

b.description: Bonum Coaching is an enterprise coaching platform based in Latin America that pairs personalized human coaching with technology to develop talent and improve organizational performance. Its offering spans one-to-one executive coaching, group and team coaching, structured mentoring programs, and CLARA, an AI coach-bot for practicing workplace conversations in a safe environment. The company positions itself around democratizing access to coaching, leadership development, talent retention, building a growth culture, and diversity, equity and inclusion, and counts enterprises such as Uber, Davivienda, Farmatodo, and Mi Banco among its clients. Backed by 500 Global, Bonum Coaching is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.
b.name: Bonum Coaching

b.description: Bonumtherapeutics, operating as Bonum Tx, develops antibody‑controlled therapeutics that deliver potent activity only where needed, aiming to improve safety and efficacy across oncology, autoimmunity, metabolic disorders, and pain management. The company leverages a novel regulated protein platform validated by Roche’s acquisition of its predecessor Good Therapeutics in 2022, and is advancing preclinical programs targeting immune cells and tumor microenvironments.
b.name: Bonumtherapeutics

b.description: Bonus Homes offers a Home Appreciation Partnership (HAP) that lets homeowners unlock cash equity quickly, often within two weeks, while retaining a share of future home appreciation. By converting homes into rental properties and handling mortgage payments, insurance, and maintenance, Bonus Homes provides a faster, less stressful alternative to traditional home sales, targeting homeowners seeking liquidity and long‑term wealth building.
b.name: Bonus Homes

b.description: Bonusly is an employee recognition and rewards platform that lets coworkers give each other small, frequent, public bonuses tied to company values, which recipients redeem for gift cards, custom rewards, donations, and more. The Bonusly REST API (base https://bonus.ly/api/v1) exposes the same surface the product is built on - bonuses, users, the reward catalog, redemptions, awards, company settings, and analytics - authenticated with a Bearer personal access token. API access is available on paid plans; tokens are minted by admins with fine-grained read / write / administer scopes.
b.name: Bonusly

b.description: Boohee (薄荷健康) is a Chinese consumer health-technology company focused on scientific weight management, serving a cumulative 180 million users over its ~17-year history. Its portfolio spans the Boohee Health mobile app (calorie and food tracking, diet and exercise logging, AI weight-management coaching, meal plans, smart body scales, community), Boohee Life nutritional foods and subscription services, the Boohee Life Internet Hospital (Tianjin-based telemedicine for internal and traditional Chinese medicine), and a Boohee weight-loss SaaS platform that helps hospitals stand up weight-management clinics. The company operates as a consumer mobile and content platform and does not publish a public developer API or open platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of DCM Ventures.
b.name: Boohee

b.description: BookMyShow (Bigtree Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.) is India's premier online entertainment ticketing platform, serving as a centralized hub for discovering and booking movies, live music festivals, comedy, theatre, sports, activities, and Video-on-Demand (VOD) streaming. For enterprise partners and event organizers it also provides venue management software, box-office point-of-sale solutions, corporate vouchers, gift cards, and end-to-end event production capabilities. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel; enriched by the enrichment pipeline. No public developer API or portal was found, but BookMyShow publishes an agent-facing llms.txt describing its consumer inventory hubs and B2B services.
b.name: Book My Show

b.description: Bookatable was a European online restaurant reservation platform (bookatable.co.uk / bookatable.com). It was acquired by Michelin and later sold into TripAdvisor's TheFork, after which the Bookatable brand was retired and its booking service merged into TheFork. As of this enrichment pass the domains no longer operate independently — bookatable.co.uk and bookatable.com both redirect to TheFork (thefork.co.uk / thefork.com), and there is no surviving Bookatable developer portal, API, documentation, or package surface. This profile is retained only as a portfolio lead of balderton-capital; the live API surface, if any, lives under thefork.
b.name: bookatable

b.description: BookBub is a book-discovery and ebook-deals platform that connects a membership of over 10 million power readers with limited-time discounted ebooks, new releases, and preorders across major retailers (Kindle, Apple Books, Barnes & Noble, Kobo, Google Play) in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia. For readers it curates personalized daily deal alerts and recommendations; for authors and publishers it operates a partner side offering Featured Deals promotions, BookBub Ads (a self-serve display advertising platform), preorder and new-release alerts, author profiles, and free marketing tools, all managed through the Partner Dashboard. BookBub is backed by Bloomberg Beta. No public developer API is currently published; partner tooling is delivered through the web dashboard rather than a documented API surface.
b.name: Bookbub

b.description: Bookend AI is a healthcare automation company building a Gastroenterology Practice Automation Platform that combines Payer Policy Intelligence with intelligent workflow automation. Its Universal Policy Library aggregates and interprets prior authorization, eligibility, benefits, and reimbursement requirements from hundreds of medical and pharmacy payers, and its Benefits, Coverage, and Authorization Assistants automate eligibility verification, coverage triage, and prior-authorization creation, submission, and tracking to reduce claim denials, accelerate care, and improve practice margins across specialty pharmacy, infusion, procedures, and imaging service lines. Bookend AI is a Seedcamp portfolio company; this API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public website.
b.name: Bookend AI

b.description: Booking Holdings is the world's leading provider of online travel and related services, operating a portfolio of brands including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK, OpenTable, Rentalcars.com, Rocketmiles, FareHarbor, HotelsCombined, Cheapflights, and Momondo. The company connects travelers with accommodations, flights, rental cars, restaurant reservations, and travel experiences worldwide.
b.name: Booking Holdings

b.description: Booking.com is the world's largest online travel agency, part of Booking Holdings, listing more than 28 million accommodation options plus car rentals, flights, attractions and airport transfers in over 60,000 destinations. It runs two distinct API programmes. The Demand API serves affiliate partners who want to search, price and book Booking.com inventory inside their own product; the Connectivity platform serves the supply side - channel managers, property management systems and hotel groups keeping rooms, rates, availability, content, reservations and payouts in sync. Twenty OpenAPI descriptions covering 210 operations are published through the developer portal, and the Connectivity estate additionally speaks OpenTravel Alliance (OTA) and Booking.com's own B.XML message formats. Both programmes are credentialed: keys come from the Affiliate Partner Centre or from a machine account in the Connectivity Portal, and no API host answers an anonymous request.
b.name: Booking.com

b.description: Bookit N Go is an AI‑powered travel technology SaaS platform that provides white‑labeled solutions for OTAs, corporate travel managers, TMCs, distributors and startups. Their suite includes the Zoe AI engine for conversational booking, the Nevo corporate travel platform, Trava consumer portal, and Nexel B2B partner platform, enabling rapid launch of branded travel services with full data control and AI‑driven personalization.
b.name: Bookit N Go

b.description: Bookkeep.com provides accounting automation solutions for Shopify and other ecommerce platforms, offering features such as automated reconciliation, sales tax compliance, multi‑bank settlement, inventory management, and integration with various POS and marketplace systems. It targets merchants, retailers, franchises, and accounting firms, delivering a unified financial workflow across online and offline sales channels.
b.name: Bookkeep.com

b.description: Bookkeeping Express (BKE) provides monthly bookkeeping and financial coaching services for franchise owners and small‑medium businesses. Their platform reconciles books, delivers actionable insights via FinalyzeIQ, and offers fixed‑price plans with senior accountant access. BKE emphasizes security, confidentiality, and U.S.-based accountants, aiming to help clients grow profitably through data‑driven recommendations.
b.name: BookKeeping Express

b.description: Bookmd is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Bookmd

b.description: BookNook is a K-8 high-impact tutoring company that delivers live 1:1 and small-group virtual instruction in reading and math through its own online learning platform. Schools and districts license the platform and either use BookNook's trained tutor corps or run sessions with their own staff; educators work from a district dashboard that reports attendance, session detail, lesson-band progress, and math engagement and understanding scores. Students and staff reach the platform at app.booknooklearning.com and sign in manually or through Clever Instant Login and ClassLink single sign-on, with district rosters provisioned by Clever Secure Sync. BookNook operates a production API service (api.booknooklearning.com, listed as an "API" component on its public status page), but it is the platform's own backend — BookNook publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract, and its integration surface is consumed from partner platforms (Clever, ClassLink, Ed-Fi) rather than published as its own.
b.name: BookNook

b.description: Booko is an Australian book, eBook, audiobook, DVD, music and collectibles price-comparison service operating since 2007. It aggregates new and used prices across many online retailers and regions, calculates shipping, and converts international prices to the shopper's local currency to surface the cheapest place to buy a title. Booko also offers shopping lists with bundled shipping calculations, barcode scanning, reading lists, price alerts and notifications. It is a consumer-facing comparison site rather than a retailer or a public API provider, earning referral fees from partner shops (including Amazon Associates) when shoppers buy through its links. Booko is a solo developer-run product surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company.
b.name: Booko

b.description: Bookpalkorea, operating under the brand Bookpal, is a Korean digital platform offering a wide range of novels and web novels. The service provides users with a library of romance, fantasy, BL, and other genres, along with features such as personal bookshelves, rankings, and community interaction. It includes business details like its Seoul address, registration number, and contact emails, indicating a formal corporate entity. The platform appears to target Korean readers seeking serialized fiction and related content.
b.name: Bookpalkorea

b.description: Booksloth is a community-driven platform that connects readers through personalized book recommendations, book clubs, and a store offering curated selections. Users can join the BookSloth app to track their reading history, discover new titles, and engage with fellow book enthusiasts. The service provides a blog, mobile apps for iPhone and Android, and integrates social media channels to foster a vibrant literary community. Founded in 2018, BookSloth aims to make reading a shared, enjoyable experience for all.
b.name: Booksloth

b.description: BookStack is a free, open-source, self-hosted wiki and documentation platform built with PHP and Laravel. It provides a REST API for managing the full content hierarchy including books, chapters, pages, and shelves, as well as attachments, image galleries, comments, roles, users, audit logs, imports, search, tags, and content permissions across hierarchical knowledge bases.
b.name: BookStack

b.description: Booksy is a beauty, wellness and health services platform that pairs a consumer appointment marketplace (booksy.com) with Booksy Biz, a subscription business-management application for salons, barbershops, spas, nail studios, tattoo artists, massage therapists and other independent service providers. The platform covers online booking, calendar and staff scheduling, client records, inventory, no-show protection, digital loyalty cards, marketing tools such as Boost, reviews, and integrated card payments including a Booksy Card Reader and Tap to Pay. Booksy also operates the Booksy Public API, a partner-facing REST API documented at docs.booksy.com that exposes businesses, business categories and amenities, business and staff schedules, resources (staff and appliances), services, service variants, service categories, service and staff photos, consent forms, customers, appointments and appointment status transitions, appointment consents, reviews and review statistics, plus an appointment webhook. The API is versioned through an Accept header, authenticates with partner-issued RSA key pairs exchanged for short-lived JWT access tokens, and is served per country from https://<country_code>.booksy.com/public-api/<country_code>/.
b.name: Booksy

b.description: Booktrack provides immersive audiobook production services, creating original soundtracks, sound design, and synchronized audio for publishers, authors, and studios. Since 2011, they have delivered over 300 immersive titles, leveraging patented technology to enhance the listening experience with multi‑layered soundscapes and Dolby Atmos. Their services include full‑production, post‑production, narration, quality control, and studio facilities, partnering with global publishers such as Penguin Random House and Simon & Schuster.
b.name: Booktrack

b.description: Boolbc2a is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Boolbc2a

b.description: Boom AI (useboom.ai) is a Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) San Francisco company building "an AI workforce for your customers" — autonomous agents that hold real, multi-turn conversations over SMS, email, WhatsApp, and phone in 50+ languages to run collections and payment recovery, churn recovery, retention monitoring, customer onboarding, sales qualification, and market research for e-commerce and B2B brands. Boom exposes one uniform public REST API — and a hosted MCP server over the same capabilities — covering a customer data platform (people, custom objects, behavioral events, relationships, sources), segments, initiatives and participants, and journey authoring. Authentication is a Bearer organization API key (boom_org_...); the API uses cursor pagination, 1,000 requests/minute rate limits with X-RateLimit-*/Retry-After signaling, and idempotent upsert plus up-to-1000-record batch endpoints.
b.name: Boom Ai

b.description: Boom Supersonic is a Denver-based aerospace company building supersonic commercial aircraft to make the world dramatically more accessible. Its flagship airliner, Overture, is designed to carry passengers at twice the speed of today's jets and has orders and pre-orders from United Airlines, American Airlines, and Japan Airlines. The company develops the Symphony medium-bypass turbofan engine purpose-built for supersonic flight, flew the XB-1 demonstrator past Mach 1, and is applying its propulsion technology to Superpower gas turbines for data-center energy. Boom is a deep-tech, hardware-first manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric Capital, and Homebrew.
b.name: Boom Supersonic

b.description: Boombox.io is an all‑in‑one platform for musicians, offering tools for distribution, AI‑powered mastering, stem splitting, lyric generation, and chord progression creation. It provides apps for macOS, iOS, and Android, along with a web portal for managing releases, collaborations, and monetization. The service aims to simplify music production and distribution for independent artists and producers.
b.name: boombox.io

b.description: Boombox42b0 is a stub company identified in the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. It currently lacks publicly available API documentation or a dedicated website. The profile aims to gather future information about its services, potential API offerings, and related resources as they become discoverable.
b.name: Boombox42b0

b.description: Boomerang, from Baydin Inc, is a productivity software company founded in 2010 that builds email management and meeting scheduling tools. Its products include Boomerang for Gmail and Boomerang for Outlook browser extensions, Boomerang mobile apps for iOS and Android, and GQueues, a task manager for Google Workspace teams. Boomerang lets users schedule email to send later, snooze messages back to the inbox, track responses with read receipts and follow-up reminders, share availability and book meetings without back-and-forth, and use AI writing assistance. With over 2 million active customers, the platform has processed more than 500 million messages. Boomerang is a consumer and team-facing productivity suite delivered as browser extensions and apps rather than a developer API platform; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Boomerang

b.description: BoomerangAI provides an AI‑powered referral agent that helps sales teams get warm introductions. By leveraging conversational AI, it surfaces relevant contacts, tracks champion relationships, and automates pipeline leak assessments, turning cold outreach into data‑driven engagements. The platform offers use‑cases like Path to Power, Champion Tracking, and Buying‑Group Intelligence, delivering measurable revenue impact for B2B sellers.
b.name: BoomerangAI

b.description: Boomerangmedical is a healthcare technology startup identified through the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. No public website or documentation could be located despite web searches, indicating the company may be early‑stage, operating privately, or its online presence is not publicly indexed. This entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment when verifiable resources become available.
b.name: Boomerangmedical

b.description: Boomi is a leading integration platform that allows organizations to connect applications, data, and people across cloud and on-premise environments. By leveraging Boomi's intuitive visual interface and pre-built connectors, businesses can quickly and easily create integrations that streamline processes, improve productivity, and enhance the overall customer experience.
b.name: Boomi

b.description: Boomingtechnologies is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Boomingtechnologies

b.description: Boompop is a corporate event management and planning SaaS platform that helps companies organize offsites, conferences, team gatherings, and other business events. The platform pairs AI-powered planning tools that generate briefs, agendas, and logistics with hotel and vendor sourcing (AI-powered RFPs and rate negotiation), guest and RSVP management, itinerary and event websites, budget and expense tracking, and 24/7 AI messaging. Tiers range from a free Starter plan through a per-event Pro plan to Full Service white-glove planning with a dedicated expert. Boompop was named the 7th fastest-growing software company on the 2025 Inc. 5000 list. It is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant, and offers passwordless login plus Google and Microsoft single sign-on. Boompop is backed by Wing Venture Capital. Boompop does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.
b.name: Boompop

b.description: Boomtechnology is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Boomtechnology

b.description: BoomTrain was a machine-learning marketing technology startup that used AI to power personalized, cross-channel messaging (email, web, and push notifications) for brands, predicting individual content and send-time recommendations for each consumer. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among others, BoomTrain raised roughly $15M before being acquired by Zeta Global in July 2017 (reportedly $35-40M), which folded its machine-learning, decisioning, and personalization technology into the Zeta Marketing Platform. The boomtrain.com domain now redirects to Zeta Global; there is no standalone BoomTrain developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.
b.name: BoomTrain

b.description: Boomy is a consumer-facing generative music platform that lets anyone create original AI songs in a browser or mobile app and release them to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, TikTok, YouTube, and other DSPs with Boomy collecting and paying out streaming royalties. Boomy does not publish a public, self-serve developer API; integrations and partner arrangements (DSP distribution, licensing) are handled directly by the Boomy team rather than through a documented public API surface.
b.name: Boomy

b.description: Boon is an agile referral hiring platform that helps organizations source talent through employee, vendor, customer, and external referral networks. Using AI-driven semantic matching and proactive referral requests, Boon surfaces hidden candidates, manages reward and gamification programs, and syncs with existing HR/ATS tech stacks (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS, Ashby, JazzHR, Slack, Teams, and 50+ others). Founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global and Redpoint Ventures, Boon markets faster time-to-hire and lower cost-per-hire through community-driven recruiting. This profile was seeded from VC portfolio data and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Boon exposes a private integration API (api.goboon.co) but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer portal.
b.name: Boon

b.description: Boonray, also known as Shanghai Bolei Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd, develops autonomous driving and intelligent mining solutions, focusing on unmanned mining vehicles, new energy power systems, and smart car technologies. The company provides integrated charging and swapping solutions for mining equipment, aiming to enhance safety and efficiency in mining operations worldwide.
b.name: Boonray

b.description: Booost Technologies is a Japanese sustainability‑focused enterprise software company offering the Booost Sustainability ERP platform. The platform helps organizations integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) data into their operations, driving scalable growth and net‑zero initiatives across more than 95 countries. With multilingual support and a global client base, Booost delivers a comprehensive suite for sustainability reporting, risk management, and value creation.
b.name: Booosttechnologies

b.description: Booqable is equipment and inventory rental management software for rental businesses - it handles online bookings, product and stock-item inventory, orders, scheduling and availability, documents and invoicing, payments, and a customer-facing online store. Booqable exposes a documented REST API (v4, "Boomerang") that follows the JSON:API specification. Requests are directed to a company-specific host, https://{company}.booqable.com/api/4, and authenticated with an access token (Bearer) or a signed single-use request. A legacy v1 API remains documented. The API lets developers manage orders, products, product groups, customers, stock items, availability and plannings, documents, payments, and webhooks.
b.name: Booqable

b.description: BOOQED is a Hong Kong-based proptech company building flexible workplace technology that turns underutilized real estate into bookable, on-demand workspace. Its flagship product QUBIC is a line of sound-isolating, modular smart booths and work pods (for one to six people) with soundproofing, ventilation, power, and a proprietary access-control system managed through a mobile web app. Alongside the hardware, BOOQED offers space-management SaaS that makes existing meeting rooms and desks bookable and trackable with utilization analytics, plus the BOOQED app for individuals to book hot desks and meeting rooms on demand across Hong Kong, Singapore, and Shenzhen. Founded by David Wong, Charles Oh, and Ken Huang, BOOQED went through the Colliers and Techstars proptech accelerator and raised seed funding in 2019. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; BOOQED does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.
b.name: Booqed

b.description: Boost is a distributed onchain incentives network that lets any team reward any onchain action with any token. Teams define target actions, fund a budget, and deploy campaigns across Base, Optimism, Arbitrum and other EVM chains, then measure ROI and iterate in real time. Boost ships two products — One-Time Actions and Time-Based Incentives (TBI) — plus RewardKit and a Headless SDK for embedding reward primitives, a public read-only Boost V2 REST API, a TypeScript SDK, a CLI, and a published MCP server. Founded by Ido Ben-Natan and Raz Niv and backed by Electric Capital and Greylock.
b.name: Boost

b.description: Boost Biomes leverages the powerful social networks among microbes to provide novel, sustainable solutions that feed and heal people worldwide. Their technology focuses on a causal understanding of microbial interactions, enabling the rational design of functional consortia. Initial products aim to reduce agricultural waste caused by fungal pests, addressing significant needs in crop loss mitigation and post-harvest preservation.
b.name: Boost Biomes

b.description: Boost Insurance is an insurance-as-a-service / embedded-insurance infrastructure platform that packages compliance, capital, and technology into a turnkey, white-labeled program accessible through a modern RESTful API. The Boost Policy Admin System (PAS) lets partners quote, bind, issue, endorse, cancel, and manage claims for admitted and surplus-lines products using JSON over OAuth 2.0.
b.name: Boost Insurance

b.description: Boost Media (formerly BoostCTR) was a digital-advertising creative-optimization SaaS platform that paired machine-learning analysis with a curated marketplace of more than 1,000 human writers and designers to test and improve ad creative across paid search, social, video, and display campaigns. Its technology powered roughly $1 billion in paid-search advertising for around 100 global brands across retail, education, financial services, healthcare and insurance, gaming, auto, and travel. Backed by Battery Ventures (Series C, $19M, 2014), Founder Collective, and 500 Global, the company raised about $42.8M total before being acquired by AdLabs Technology in April 2019. The company is now closed; its former domain (boostmedia.com) has been released and now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, and the acquirer's own domain (adlabs.ai) no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a Battery Ventures portfolio record. No public API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich — the Internet Archive record of boostmedia.com shows a WordPress marketing site and blog only, with no developer, docs, or API path ever published.
b.name: Boost Media

b.description: Boost Payment Solutions provides a comprehensive suite of B2B payment solutions, including commercial card processing, virtual card payments, and AP/AR automation. Founded in 2009, the company serves global enterprises across 180+ countries, offering patented technologies such as Boost 100, Boost Intercept, and Dynamic Boost to optimize payment efficiency, security, and data insights.
b.name: Boost Payment Solutions

b.description: Boostd243 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

b.description: Boosted Commerce is a Los Angeles based consumer brand platform that acquires and operates direct-to-consumer and Amazon FBA businesses in health, wellness, beauty and longevity. Founded by Keith Richman and Charlie Chanaratsopon, the company runs a portfolio of supplement and skincare brands — Prime Labs, Vital Vitamins, Happy Healthy Hippie and Asterwood — and is expanding those brands from marketplace and DTC channels into national retail with EDI-ready vendor operations. Boosted Commerce publishes no first-party developer program of its own, but every brand storefront runs on Shopify and serves a live, anonymous agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, agent instructions at /llms.txt and /agents.md, and a Model Context Protocol endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp exposing 13 catalog, cart, checkout and order tools with published JSON Schema inputs.
b.name: Boosted Commerce

b.description: Boosted.ai is an agentic AI platform purpose-built for the financial services and investment management industry. Its Alfa product gives portfolio managers, analysts, and wealth and institutional platforms conversational financial chat and autonomous investment agents that automate research, market monitoring, idea generation, and reporting over verified, financial-grade data. Boosted.ai exposes these capabilities to developers through an API, SDK, and embeddable UI so platforms can deliver an investing assistant, an insights feed of agent-generated research, and custom compliant agents inside their own products. The company reports serving 300+ global clients managing $5T+ in assets and is headquartered in New York, with offices in Toronto and San Francisco.
b.name: Boosted.ai

b.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.
b.name: Booster Fuels

b.description: Boosters is a Seoul-based global commerce company and brand aggregator, founded in 2019, that acquires and accelerates the growth of emerging Korean direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, with a particular focus on K-Beauty. Boosters takes over small and medium-sized Korean brands that have strong product potential but struggle with marketing, distribution, and inventory management, then scales them across domestic and international commerce channels. Portfolio brands include Eqqualberry and Branden. The company raised a USD 10 million Series A round in 2022 with participation from Partech and other investors. Boosters is a consumer commerce operator rather than a developer platform, and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal.
b.name: Boosters

b.description: Boostertech is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, identified from secondary‑market data. The company’s public presence is not clearly established; no definitive website or API documentation could be verified. This entry records the limited known information and serves as a placeholder for future enrichment when reliable sources become available.
b.name: Boostertech

b.description: Boostly provides a SMS marketing platform for restaurants, enabling them to attract new diners, boost orders, manage reviews, and measure ROI through text message campaigns. The service offers tools for targeted ads, loyalty programs, and detailed analytics, helping restaurant owners increase revenue and customer engagement.
b.name: Boostly

b.description: Boostr is an all‑in‑one ad management platform offering CRM, Order Management System (OMS), and a Proposal Engine. It helps media companies streamline sales, operations, finance, and retail advertising through unified workflows, real‑time forecasting, and AI‑driven recommendations. Founded in 2015 and based in Los Gatos, CA, Boostr serves clients like BuzzFeed and Weatherbug, providing integrations, a developer portal, and extensive resources for ad sales teams.
b.name: Boostr

b.description: Boostrmind is a technology startup focused on providing AI-driven mind‑mapping and knowledge‑management tools for enterprises and individuals. The platform leverages natural language processing to automatically organize thoughts, generate visual maps, and integrate with popular productivity suites. Boostrmind aims to enhance creativity, collaboration, and information retention across teams, offering both web‑based and mobile applications with secure cloud storage and customizable workflows.
b.name: Boostrmind

b.description: Boostup (now operating as Terret, terret.ai) is an AI-powered revenue intelligence platform that connects data across a company's revenue systems to analyze sales performance, forecast pipeline, and translate insights into real-time execution guidance for sales teams. Its products include Terret Nexus (an answer-to-action revenue engine that generates playbooks), Terret Forecast (pipeline forecasting), and Terret Conversation Intelligence (call analysis). For developers, Boostup exposes a public REST data-export API at app.boostup.ai/export that lets customers programmatically pull their Opportunities, Accounts, and Forecast Submissions out of the platform for in-house analysis and reporting. The API is authenticated with API keys passed in the Authorization header, returns JSON paginated in batches of up to 1000 records, and supports date-based filtering on close/create/update times. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.
b.name: Boostup

b.description: BoostUp.ai provides an AI‑driven revenue acceleration platform that combines pipeline forecasting, conversation intelligence, and automated deal‑closing tools. The solution helps sales teams uncover hidden opportunities, prioritize high‑value prospects, and automate follow‑ups, driving higher win rates and faster revenue growth. Powered by advanced machine learning, BoostUp.ai integrates with CRM systems to deliver real‑time insights and actionable recommendations across the sales funnel.
b.name: BoostUp.ai

b.description: Bootc is an open source tool that enables transactional, in-place operating system updates using OCI/Docker container images as the source for OS updates. It applies the container layering model to bootable host systems, using standard OCI containers as a transport and delivery format for base operating system updates. The container image includes a Linux kernel, and when deployed the base userspace runs normally with systemd as PID 1. Bootc is a CNCF Sandbox project with a stable CLI and API.
b.name: Bootc

b.description: Bootic is an e‑commerce platform based in Chile, offering a marketplace where multiple vendors sell products through a unified shopping experience. The site provides a modern storefront, advanced search, and integration options for businesses to reach customers online.
b.name: Bootic

b.description: Booz Allen Hamilton is a leading management and technology consulting firm providing services primarily to U.S. government agencies in defense, intelligence, and civil markets. The firm employs over 2,500 AI specialists and 8,000 cybersecurity professionals, and maintains a significant open source presence on GitHub with projects including the Solutions Delivery Platform, Open Data Platform, and Cognition data fusion platform.
b.name: Booz Allen Hamilton

b.description: Bop.fm was a music-sharing and playlist startup that let people share and play individual songs across streaming services — building a link for a track that would resolve to whichever service (Spotify, Deezer, SoundCloud, YouTube, Rdio) each listener used. Founded out of Y Combinator, it reportedly reached several million monthly listeners and raised roughly $2M before being acquihired by identity-protection company LifeLock in October 2015, at which point the website, mobile apps, and embedded players were shut down. The company is defunct: the bop.fm domain no longer serves the product (it now redirects to an unrelated parked site) and no developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.
b.name: Bop.fm

b.description: Bopixel (Beijing Bopixel Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese provider of high‑performance machine‑vision core components and imaging solutions. The company operates R&D centers in Beijing and Yokohama, offering products such as 3D structured‑light cameras, high‑speed line‑scan cameras, DLP projectors, barcode readers, and optical sensors for industries including automotive, logistics, robotics, food‑pharma, and semiconductor manufacturing. Bopixel focuses on advanced visual detection, segmentation, 3D pose estimation, and intelligent planning for automated inspection and measurement systems.
b.name: Bopixel

b.description: Border0 is an identity-aware Zero Trust network access platform for securing access to infrastructure — SSH and RDP servers, PostgreSQL/MySQL/MSSQL/MongoDB/Elasticsearch databases, Kubernetes clusters, AWS consoles and S3 buckets, and any internal HTTP or TCP service. Instead of VPNs and shared credentials, Border0 publishes each resource as a policy-gated "socket," authenticates users through their existing SSO/identity provider, and records every session for audit. Its REST admin API (api.border0.com/api/v1) manages sockets, access policies, connectors, organizations, identity providers, service accounts, tokens, sessions, and audit logs, and is complemented by an official Go SDK, a Terraform provider, a CLI, and GitHub Actions. Border0 was acquired by Tailscale in March 2026.
b.name: Border0

b.description: BorderX Lab, founded in 2014 by three former Google PhDs, is a Silicon Valley‑based leader in AI‑driven cross‑border e‑commerce. It offers a suite of products—including CloudStore AI, BeyondStyle, and the Bieyang app—to empower brands and merchants worldwide to deliver autonomous shopping experiences. With over 200 employees across the US and China, BorderX Lab combines advanced personalization, logistics, and agentic commerce technology to create a seamless global trade platform.
b.name: BorderX Lab

b.description: Borderxlab is a Silicon Valley‑based AI‑driven cross‑border e‑commerce platform. Founded in 2014 by three former Google PhDs, it offers products such as CloudStore AI, BeyondStyle, and BieYang app to enable brands and merchants to sell globally. The company reports over 5 million successful orders, 20 million SKUs and $1 billion GMV, positioning itself as a leader in agentic commerce.
b.name: Borderxlab

b.description: The Bored API is a free, open-source, no-authentication public API that serves suggestions for things to do when you are bored. The canonical reference implementation is an MEVN (MongoDB / Express / Vue / Node) project maintained by Drew Thoennes at github.com/drewthoennes/Bored-API (MIT licensed). The historically hosted instance at https://www.boredapi.com/ has been intermittently or fully unreachable since June 2024 (originally hosted on Heroku); a community fork maintained by The App Brewery at https://bored-api.appbrewery.com remains actively available for students and consumers. This profile documents the v1 surface (legacy activities-only), the v2 surface (activities + facts + riddles + websites + suggestions), and the App Brewery community mirror, so the API contract is preserved as a historical, self-hostable artifact.
b.name: Bored API

b.description: The Boring Company, founded by Elon Musk, focuses on developing tunneling and infrastructure technologies to reduce traffic congestion and enable rapid point‑to‑point transportation. It designs and manufactures advanced tunnel boring machines, such as Prufrock, and builds large‑scale transportation systems like the Vegas Loop. The company aims to create safe, fast, and low‑cost tunnels for transportation, utilities, and freight, transforming urban mobility and infrastructure.
b.name: Boring Company

b.description: Born (formerly Slay) is a Berlin-based consumer AI company founded in 2022 by Fabian Kamberi (CEO), Jannis Ringwald, and Stefan Quernhorst. Born builds AI characters and companions designed for shared, social experiences rather than isolating one-to-one chatbots. Its flagship product Pengu is a co-parented virtual pet with more than 15 million registered users, and the company is expanding into a multi-character platform called Friends and a photorealistic voice-and-video companion experience called Life. Since 2022 Born has launched five consumer social apps that reached #1 globally on the App Store. It raised a $15M Series A in September 2025 (participants include Accel, Tencent, and Laton Ventures), bringing total funding to roughly $25M. Born is a consumer mobile-app maker and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.
b.name: Born

b.description: Borqs Technologies Inc. is a global Internet of Things (IoT) platform solution provider delivering customizable, differentiated and scalable smart-connected IoT software, hardware and cloud-service platforms. Founded in 2007, Borqs is a Google-licensed Android and Android Wear partner with R&D centers in the U.S., India and China, and debuted publicly on Nasdaq (BRQS) in August 2017. Its BorqsWare platform powers smartphones, tablets, wearables, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), M2M and smart-appliance solutions, and in 2021 it expanded into solar and energy storage systems (ESS) via its Holu Hou Energy acquisition. Borqs is now a Sasken Group company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published; this profile carries company identity and a live domain-security probe.
b.name: Borqs

b.description: BorrowMyDoggy is a UK-based platform that connects dog owners with trusted local borrowers for dog walking, sitting, boarding, and holiday care. Owners who cannot always be with their dog are matched with nearby dog lovers who want to spend time with a dog without the full-time commitment, so dogs get more walks, company, and care. Membership is free to join, with optional Premium tiers for owners and borrowers that unlock messaging, insurance cover, and a 24/7 vet line. The company operates a consumer web and mobile application built on Ruby on Rails; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from public web surfaces.

b.description: Boruspanprecision is a precision engineering subsidiary of Borusan Holding, specializing in high‑accuracy pipe and component manufacturing for industrial and automotive sectors. The company offers advanced machining services, custom‑made precision profiles, and engineering consultancy, leveraging Borusan’s extensive manufacturing network and sustainability initiatives. It serves global clients with a focus on quality, innovation, and environmental responsibility.
b.name: Boruspanprecision

b.description: Borvo is an outsourcing IT company offering custom software development, big data analytics, research & development, and QA testing services. Based on its website, Borvo positions itself as a technology partner for web hosting companies, providing end‑to‑end solutions from specification to delivery. The firm showcases case studies, career opportunities, and a contact portal, indicating an active service‑focused business.

b.description: Boréastechnologies, operating as Boréas Technologies, designs and manufactures ultra‑low power piezoelectric drivers and haptic solutions for smartphones, automotive, and IoT devices. Their product line includes CapDrive® drivers, development kits, and software tools, supported by extensive technical documentation, integration guides, and a developer portal.
b.name: Boréastechnologies

b.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

b.description: Boshihitech (大连博世科技有限公司) is a Chinese technology company specializing in industrial automation, IoT solutions, and smart manufacturing services. Established in 2008, the firm offers a range of products including sensor integration, data analytics platforms, and cloud-based monitoring tools for factories and enterprises. Their website provides detailed information on capabilities, case studies, and partnership opportunities, reflecting a focus on advancing digital transformation in the manufacturing sector.
b.name: Boshihitech

b.description: Bosie Knitwear is a Scottish apparel brand offering handcrafted wool garments, including sweaters, cardigans, and accessories. The company operates an e‑commerce site at bosie.co, shipping internationally and showcasing collections such as Shetland, Chunky Fishermen, and Cashmere. It emphasizes heritage, quality materials, and sustainable production.
b.name: Bosie

b.description: Boson Motors is an electric vehicle and robotics company founded in 2017, building a modular electric off-road utility vehicle (UTV) platform for agriculture, farm automation, and work applications. Its flagship LX40 is a user-serviceable, low-maintenance electric 4WD UTV that charges from a standard 110v outlet and accepts interchangeable work modules for spraying, hauling, and crew transport. The company operates engineering and production out of Tada, Andhra Pradesh, India, with a strategic base in Fremont, California, and maintains a robotics arm (Boson Robotics) focused on autonomous and agricultural automation. Boson Motors is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer marketing and reservation site with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation; its public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of ROS/robotics libraries. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and enrichment target.
b.name: Boson Motors

b.description: Bosonic is a venture and consulting collective based in Sweden, dedicated to bringing great products to life through experimentation, iteration, and autonomy over hierarchy. The team offers software development, product ownership, and consultancy across sectors, emphasizing pragmatism, continuous self‑improvement, and innovative solutions for partners such as Womni, Manwell, and Finanzero.
b.name: Bosonic

b.description: Boss (BOSS Zhipin / BOSS直聘) is the largest online recruitment platform in China by average monthly active users, operated by Kanzhun Limited (NASDAQ: BZ, HKEX: 2076) and founded in 2014 in Beijing. It pioneered the "Direct Recruitment" model, a mobile-native experience that connects employers (bosses) and job seekers through instant direct chat rather than static resume exchange, with candidate and job matching powered by proprietary AI algorithms and big-data insights. The consumer job-search product at zhipin.com does not publish a public developer/job-data API; an authorized enterprise developer surface (BossHi mini-program open platform) exists for partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.
b.name: Boss

b.description: Boss Digital Technology is a digital transformation agency offering web design, mobile app development, performance marketing, and strategic consulting services. It helps brands scale through comprehensive digital solutions, emphasizing user experience, technology integration, and growth-focused strategies.
b.name: Boss Digital Technology

b.description: Bossa Nova Robotics develops autonomous retail robots and AI solutions for inventory management. Their flagship robot, Bossa Nova, scans store aisles in Walmart and other retailers, providing real‑time out‑of‑stock detection and analytics. The company shares its technology and learnings through open documentation and APIs to help other businesses build similar automation solutions.
b.name: Bossa Nova Robotics

b.description: Bossanovaroboticsinc, operating as Bossa Nova Robotics, provides autonomous inventory management robots and AI-driven retail automation solutions. Their platform deploys robots across large retail chains to continuously scan shelves, detect out‑of‑stock items, and feed real‑time data to store associates, improving inventory accuracy and reducing labor costs. The company also shares extensive operational insights, guides, and resources for startups via their public documentation site.
b.name: Bossanovaroboticsinc

b.description: BossTax is a mobile bookkeeping and tax-filing app for 1099 workers, freelancers, and independent contractors. Founded in 2022 and based in Stamford, Connecticut, BossTax lets self-employed users track expenses by photographing receipts, automatically categorize deductions, log expenses hands-free by voice, manage separate business banking, and file federal, state, and local taxes with a licensed tax professional for a single flat fee with no subscriptions. BossTax is an IRS-authorized Electronic Return Originator (ERO) and is backed by Bloomberg Beta and Boyd Street Ventures. The company ships iOS and Android consumer apps; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time, so this profile tracks the company identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.
b.name: BossTax

b.description: Bostaldrugdelivery is a company identified in the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. No public website or official documentation could be located after exhaustive searches, including the listed EquityZen profile which returned access‑denied. Consequently, the company currently appears only as a stub entry without verifiable online presence, and no API endpoints, documentation, or contact details are publicly available.
b.name: Bostaldrugdelivery

b.description: Boston Dynamics, a Hyundai Motor Group subsidiary, designs advanced mobile robots including Spot (agile quadruped for dynamic sensing and industrial inspection), Atlas (electric humanoid for manufacturing), Stretch (warehouse case-handling robot), and the Orbit enterprise fleet management platform. Boston Dynamics publishes a public, open-source Spot SDK (Python and C++) on GitHub built on gRPC and Protocol Buffers for developing applications and payloads for Spot; Atlas and Stretch are enterprise products without public APIs.
b.name: Boston Dynamics

b.description: Boston Heart Diagnostics is a specialty cardiovascular diagnostics laboratory, part of Eurofins Scientific, that has been improving patient outcomes since 2007 through a combination of integrated diagnostics, advanced lipid and metabolic testing, genetic risk evaluation, personalized reporting, and a scientifically designed nutrition and lifestyle program. It serves clinicians and patients through a provider portal and a patient portal (mybostonheart.com) rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the identity and security-posture fields below are captured from the provider's public web presence.
b.name: Boston Heart Diagnostics (Eurofins Scientific)

b.description: Stations and predicted arrivals for MBTA
b.name: Boston MBTA Transit

b.description: Boston Metal is an industrial metals and materials company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts, with a wholly owned subsidiary and commercial plant in Brazil. The company commercializes Molten Oxide Electrolysis (MOE), a one-step electrochemical process that uses clean electricity rather than fossil fuels to reduce iron ore into liquid metal, producing steel with no direct CO2 emissions, and to recover high-value critical metals such as niobium and tantalum from low-grade ore and mining waste. Boston Metal commissioned a multi-inert-anode industrial MOE cell at its Woburn facility and has raised over $500 million from investors including Tata Steel. Boston Metal is a physical process-technology and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind. This profile captures its public web, corporate, and domain-security posture only.
