The Bridge API is versioned at /v0, authenticated with a scoped Api-Key header, and supports idempotent writes plus a webhook event surface. Bridge was acquired by Stripe. Backed by Ribbit Capital.
b.name: Bridge

b.description: Bridge (Bridge Interactive / Bridge Data Output), the Zillow Group MLS data distribution platform. This is a duplicate profile: Bridge Interactive is profiled in the bridge-interactive repository, which is canonical. Consolidated 2026-10-13, approved by Kin Lane.
b.name: Bridge

b.description: Bridge Interactive (a Zillow Group company) is a real-estate data-access platform that normalizes MLS listing data to RESO standards and serves it through the Bridge API. The Bridge Data Output platform exposes a proprietary RESTful Bridge Web API and a RESO-compliant RESO Web API (OData) for properties, members, offices, open houses, and media, all secured with a Bearer server token.
b.name: Bridge Interactive

b.description: BridgeCare (getbridgecare.com) is an integrated, modular software platform for the early care and education (ECE) system. It gives state agencies, cities and counties, child care resource and referral organizations (CCR&Rs), nonprofits, and school districts one system to run Pre-K program administration, family navigation, coordinated eligibility and enrollment, centralized eligibility screening, licensing, workforce development, quality management (QRIS), grants management, subsidy administration, tri-share administration, and program assurance. The platform is used by 500,000+ families, 50,000+ providers, and 500+ counties. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, BridgeCare is backed by Techstars and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. BridgeCare operates an API host but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer documentation, so this profile is identity-only.
b.name: BridgeCare Finance

b.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.
b.name: Bridgeco

b.description: Bridgecrew was a developer-first cloud security company that pioneered infrastructure-as-code (IaC) security by creating Checkov, the open-source static analysis scanner for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, ARM, Serverless, and Dockerfile configurations. Founded in 2019 and backed by Battery Ventures, Bridgecrew shipped a SaaS platform that scanned IaC and connected cloud accounts for misconfigurations, enforced policy guardrails in CI/CD, and remediated findings through automated pull requests. Palo Alto Networks acquired Bridgecrew in March 2021 for roughly $156 million and folded the platform into Prisma Cloud (now the PANW Application Security offering). The standalone Bridgecrew developer API and docs.bridgecrew.io documentation have since been retired, while Checkov remains actively maintained open source under the bridgecrewio GitHub organization and the www.checkov.io docs site.
b.name: Bridgecrew

b.description: Bridgeinternationalacademies is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Bridgeinternationalacademies

b.description: BridGene Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on pioneering the next era of small molecule therapeutics. The company develops innovative platforms to discover and optimize novel drug candidates, aiming to address unmet medical needs across various disease areas.
b.name: Bridgenebiosciences

b.description: BridgeStackAPI provides a lightweight API gateway that enables per‑client usage control, rate‑limiting, and custom routing without rebuilding the gateway. It offers dashboards, real‑time logs, and integration guides for Node.js, cURL, and Python, helping developers quickly enforce policies and monitor API consumption.
b.name: BridgeStackAPI

b.description: Bridgestone Corporation is a Japanese global tire and rubber manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo. Bridgestone produces tires for passenger, commercial, off-road, and aircraft applications, plus diversified rubber and chemical products, and is one of the largest tire makers in the world.
b.name: Bridgestone

b.description: Bridgetown Research is an AI-powered research and analysis platform that helps organizations analyze businesses with speed and precision. Its AI agents conduct expert interviews, gather primary and secondary data at scale, and execute 300+ of the most common analyses to power autonomous market research and commercial due diligence. The platform serves private equity and venture capital firms, professional services firms, and corporate strategy and development teams, who access it either through a SOC 2-compliant SaaS platform with interactive generative-search reporting or via an email-driven workflow that returns PDF reports. Bridgetown Research also exposes a REST API (documented on Apidog at docs.bridgetownresearch.com) for creating research projects and managing experts, expert actions, and scheduled calls. It is backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
b.name: Bridgetown Research

b.description: BridgeU is an education technology company providing a university and careers guidance platform for international schools. Used by more than 1,200 partner schools across 150+ countries, the platform helps students from Grade 9 onward explore careers, research over 26,000 global universities, build shortlists, and manage applications in one connected system, with analytics dashboards for counsellors and AI-assisted guidance. BridgeU is a Seedcamp portfolio company and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface as of this enrichment pass; integration with school systems (for example ManageBac+) is handled via partner single sign-on rather than an openly documented API.
b.name: BridgeU

b.description: Bridgewater Bank is a Canadian Schedule I chartered bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Alberta Motor Association (AMA), headquartered in Calgary, Alberta and established in 1997. It is a member of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) and operates a broker-distributed, deposit-and-lending model rather than a direct-to-consumer retail branch network — residential mortgages, Guaranteed Investment Certificates (GICs), and high-interest savings accounts sold through a select network of trusted mortgage and deposit brokers, with roughly $3.3 billion in mortgages and deposits across approximately 53,000 customer accounts nationwide. Bridgewater Bank exposes NO public first-party developer API or developer portal. Its only dedicated digital surface beyond the corporate site is a partner-gated broker information portal (bwbbrokerinfo.ca). Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated but not yet operational, so any consumer data access from a bank of this size is voluntary and today would be aggregator/screen-scraping based rather than through a documented first-party API. No Interac, Real-Time Rail (RTR), FDX, or consumer-driven-banking API participation is publicly documented by the institution.
b.name: Bridgewater Bank

b.description: Bridgewire connects Telegram and WhatsApp so your messages, photos, and videos flow between them automatically — no manual forwarding, nothing missed. It provides real‑time bi‑directional messaging, enabling seamless communication across platforms for individuals and businesses.
b.name: Bridgewire

b.description: Bridgit is a Kitchener, Ontario-based construction technology company founded in 2012 by Mallorie Brodie and Lauren Lake. Its flagship product is Bridgit Bench, an AI-first workforce planning platform built exclusively for construction general contractors and subcontractors. Bench centralizes project staffing, role assignments, forecasting, utilization, time-off, internal resumes, and certifications, replacing the spreadsheets most contractors still use to plan their people across pursuits and active projects. Bridgit is trusted by nearly 40% of the ENR 400 and serves customers across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand. The company has raised over $35M USD from investors including Autodesk, Salesforce Ventures, Sands Capital, BDC Capital, and Camber Creek. Bridgit Bench exposes a documented REST API (OpenAPI 3.0) for managing accounts, projects, people, roles, allocations, certifications, and groupings, and ships pre-built integrations across CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics, Unanet, Zoho, Pipedrive), HRIS/ERP (Workday, BambooHR, UKG, Oracle, ADP, Namely), project management (Procore, Autodesk Build, CMiC, Trimble), and data warehouses (Snowflake, Office 365).
b.name: Bridgit

b.description: Bridgit6b25 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Bridgit6b25

b.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.
b.name: Briefcase

b.description: Brigad is a French-founded staffing marketplace that connects verified, self-employed hospitality and healthcare professionals with businesses that need short-term cover. Founded in Paris in 2016 by Florent Malbranche, Jean Lebrument and Alexandre Rovetto, the platform pairs a talent app (for freelance chefs, waiters, bartenders, carers and nurses) with a business app (for restaurants, caterers, hotels, clinics, retirement homes and hospitals) and uses a matching algorithm to fill missions, often within hours. Brigad operates in France and the United Kingdom, has supported over 12,000 businesses and 23,000 independent professionals, and completed more than 300,000 missions. It is backed by Balderton Capital, Wendel, Serena and Square, having raised roughly €50 million to date. Brigad publishes no documented public developer API or developer program, but its web app is powered by first-party GraphQL routers on brigad.cloud (talent, business/agent and legacy schemas) whose anonymous introspection is open; those live SDLs are captured here as an undocumented internal contract, alongside the company identity and public web properties tracked for the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Brigad

b.description: Bright is Mexico's leading residential and commercial solar energy provider, founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Jonah Greenberger. Often described as "Sunrun for the developing world," Bright combines financing and software to let homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar and battery energy storage (BESS) at no upfront cost. The company operates a marketplace connecting a network of local installers, distributors, and retail promoters with customers, and offers financing models such as solar PPAs and leasing schemes. Bright's public web presence is a Wix-hosted marketing site (thinkbright.mx) covering its industrial, commercial, and home solutions, success cases, and 24/7 energy monitoring technology. It exposes an agent-facing surface via an llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint, but publishes no first-party developer/REST API.
b.name: Bright

b.description: Bright Data is an Israeli web data platform and operator of the world's largest legitimate residential proxy network (400M+ IPs across 195 countries). The platform combines proxy infrastructure (residential, ISP, datacenter, mobile) with higher-level web-access APIs — Web Unlocker, SERP API, Web Scraper API, Scraping Browser, Deep Lookup, and Web Archive — plus a 350-dataset marketplace and an MCP server that exposes 60+ web-access tools to AI agents. Serves 20,000+ customers across eCommerce, finance, real estate, ad-tech, and AI/ML, and is a primary supplier of training and grounding data for foundation-model providers.
b.name: Bright Data

b.description: Bright Data is a web data platform providing a global proxy network (residential, datacenter, ISP, mobile), pre-built Web Scraper APIs for 100+ sites, a SERP API, the Web Unlocker, ready-made Datasets, and a Scraping Browser (Browser API) that exposes a real Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint over WebSocket for Puppeteer, Playwright, and Selenium automation.
b.name: Bright Data

b.description: Bright Funds is a workplace-giving, corporate grants, and employee volunteering platform (now part of Submittable) that lets employers run donation, matching-gift, and volunteering programs for their employees and route funds to vetted nonprofits. The platform operates a live OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authorization server at www.brightfunds.org for single sign-on and API integrations (authorization_code, client_credentials, and refresh_token grants; RS256 id_tokens; openid/profile/email/write/update scopes). It publishes a PGP-signed security.txt but no standalone developer portal or OpenAPI specification. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its public identity and well-known discovery surface.
b.name: Bright Funds

b.description: Bright Health Group was a Minneapolis-based healthtech and health-insurance company founded in 2016 by former UnitedHealthcare CEO Bob Sheehy, offering individual, family, and Medicare Advantage plans on the ACA exchanges through its Bright HealthCare brand. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and other venture investors, the company went public in 2021, then exited the insurance business, rebranded to NeueHealth in January 2024 to focus on value-based care delivery (NeueCare) and provider enablement (NeueSolutions), and shut down all remaining Bright HealthCare health-plan operations effective December 31, 2024. NeueHealth was subsequently taken private by New Enterprise Associates. Bright Health never published a public developer program, API, or documentation surface; runout operations are handled under the NeueHealth corporate brand.
b.name: Bright Health

b.description: Bright Horizons Family Solutions Inc. (NYSE: BFAM) is the largest provider of employer-sponsored child care in the United States, headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts and founded in 1986 by Linda Mason and Roger Brown. The company operates more than 1,000 early-education and child-care centers across the US, UK, Netherlands, and India, serving roughly 1,450 employer clients through three core lines: Full Service Center-Based Child Care (on-site and near-site centers for employer-sponsored families), Back-Up Care (last-minute child, adult/elder, and pet care via in-home and in-center networks), and Educational Advisory Services. The Educational Advisory segment is anchored by EdAssist by Bright Horizons (tuition assistance, student loan repayment, and workforce education administration covering 257 employer clients, 4.7 million eligible learners, and more than $1 billion in education and loan payments administered annually), College Coach (college admissions coaching delivered as an employee benefit), and Sittercity (consumer caregiver marketplace acquired in 2020 and offered through corporate benefits). Bright Horizons sells exclusively to enterprise HR and benefits buyers — 72 of the Fortune 1000's top 100 companies use EdAssist — and does not publish public APIs, SDKs, a developer portal, status page, or a public GitHub organization. The brighthorizons GitHub org exists but contains zero public repositories. This profile documents the corporate structure, segment portfolio, and employer-benefit positioning of a child-care and family-benefits operator that runs a closed B2B technology stack with no third-party developer surface.
b.name: Bright Horizons Family Solutions

b.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.
b.name: Bright Machines

b.description: Bright MLS is one of the largest multiple listing services in the United States, serving real estate professionals across the Mid-Atlantic. Its developer portal (developer.brightmls.com, a SwaggerHub Portal) documents the RESO Web API (OData, RESO Data Dictionary 1.6 Platinum certified) for licensed listing data and the ShowingHub showing-scheduling interoperability API, and its public SwaggerHub registry publishes OpenAPI contracts for the Data Hub ingestion and DataLake distribution services and the Manifest Services API for media vendors.
b.name: Bright MLS

b.description: Bright Moments is an onchain art organization and decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that produces live, in-person (IRL) generative NFT minting experiences in cities around the world. Its flagship CryptoCitizens collection (10,000 Art Blocks-powered generative portraits by artist Qian Qian) was minted 1,000 at a time across ten cities including Venice CA (CryptoVenetians), New York, Berlin, London, Mexico City, Tokyo, Buenos Aires, Paris, Venice Italy, and the Metaverse. Holding a CryptoCitizen confers membership and governance rights in the Bright Moments DAO, which was founded on-chain in March 2021. Bright Moments also runs artist collaborations/residencies, a Golden Token minting mechanism, and display software for at-home viewing. It is not a traditional API provider: the public technical surface is Ethereum/Base smart contracts, a documentation site, a DAO portal app, and a public GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.
b.name: Bright Moments DAO

b.description: Bright Pattern is a cloud contact center (CCaaS) software company whose omnichannel platform routes voice, IVR, email, chat, SMS/MMS, video and social messenger conversations to agents, with built-in quality management, workforce management, outbound dialing and AI/bot assistance. The platform is multi-tenant: every customer contact center runs on its own tenant hostname, and Bright Pattern exposes nine public REST API families against that tenant — Configuration, SCIM-compliant user provisioning, List Management (v2, v3.0, v3.2), Task Routing, SMS/MMS, Interaction Content (call recordings and metadata), Real-Time Statistics, and the Mobile/Web Messaging APIs (v1 and v2) that back the iOS and Android Mobile SDKs. The public API reference is published as Postman documenter collections linked from the Bright Pattern documentation wiki.
b.name: Bright Pattern

b.description: Bright Peak Therapeutics AG is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and co-located in Allschwil, Switzerland (Switzerland Innovation Park Basel Area) and San Diego / Del Mar, California. The company engineers next-generation multi-functional immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease, using a protein-engineering and site-specific chemical-conjugation platform to build multi-functional PD-1 inhibitors and cytokine immunoconjugates that combine novel and clinically validated mechanisms in a single molecule. Its lead program, BPT567, is a first-in-class PD1-IL18 immunoconjugate that entered a Phase 1/2a clinical trial. The company has raised a USD 90 million Series C led by Johnson & Johnson Innovation (JJDC) alongside Versant Ventures, RA Capital Management, Fidelity, Qatar Investment Authority, Invus, Venrock, KB Investment, Alexandria Venture Investments and Northleaf Capital Partners. Bright Peak is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.
b.name: Bright Peak Therapeutics

b.description: Bright Silicon Technologies is a Pleasanton, California photonics and semiconductor company, founded in 2020 out of work at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, that builds solid-state optical beam control. Its Lightfield Directing Array (LDA) is a chip-scale segmented micromirror array — described by the company as "400 micro-gimbals on a chip" — that steers light with no moving parts, offering a plus-or-minus 30 degree optical field of regard at sub-microradian precision, a 350k degrees/second slew rate and 100ns settling time. The company positions the LDA as a replacement for bulky mechanical gimbals and conventional MEMS mirrors in free-space optical communication terminals, LIDAR, counter-UAS tracking, adaptive optics and metal 3D printing. The product is silicon and optical hardware sold to aerospace, defense and datacenter customers; the company publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.
b.name: Bright Silicon Technologies

b.description: Bright Uro offers innovative bladder function diagnostic technology through its Glean system, providing non‑invasive, real‑life data collection without catheters. The platform improves patient comfort and delivers high‑quality insights for clinicians, aiming to streamline diagnosis and treatment decisions in urology.
b.name: Bright Uro

b.description: BrightView Technologies, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina optical film company specializing in computational optics and the design and manufacture of Micro Lens Array (MLA) solutions that shape, diffuse, and manage light. Founded in 2002 on intellectual property licensed from Duke University, the company engineers precision optical films and micro-optical structures used in automotive displays, head-up displays, and LiDAR; consumer and mini/micro-LED displays (gain enhancement and LED-hiding films); LED and architectural lighting (beam shaping and diffusion); and augmented- and virtual-reality beam-shaping optics. BrightView is a hardware and materials manufacturer serving OEMs and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead of Battery Ventures and enriched from the company's public website.
b.name: Bright View Technologies

b.description: Bright3 is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions in the renewable energy sector. The company aims to accelerate the adoption of clean energy through advanced analytics, data-driven insights, and integration services that help businesses optimize their energy consumption and reduce carbon footprints. Bright3 collaborates with partners across the energy ecosystem to deliver scalable platforms that support sustainable growth and environmental stewardship.
b.name: Bright3

b.description: BrightAI builds Physical AI for essential services — continuous, AI-driven awareness of the real-time state of physical infrastructure for operators of water, power, energy, transportation and industrial systems. Founded in 2019 by SmartThings founder Alex Hawkinson, the company ships a four-layer Stateful platform (Data Acquisition, AI Hub, Stateful OS, Foundation Models) combining peel-and-stick sensors (Stateful Sticker), autonomous drone and quadruped inspection, a voice-interactive field Stateful Wearable, and infrastructure foundation models trained on operational outcomes across millions of industrial assets. BrightAI publishes no conventional developer portal or OpenAPI, but it does operate a public, no-authentication Model Context Protocol server at public.stateful.world/mcp exposing six read-only tools over its Global Observability Database, alongside an llms.txt index, agent-addressed markdown briefs, and two unauthenticated public JSON endpoints.
b.name: BrightAI

b.description: Brightback (now Chargebee Retention) is a churn-prevention and cancellation- experience platform for subscription businesses. When a customer clicks "cancel," Brightback intercepts the flow with a personalized, hosted save experience — targeted offers, surveys, and deflection paths — driven by customer and billing context passed from the merchant. Founded as a standalone SaaS backed by Point Nine and other investors, Brightback was acquired by Chargebee in 2021 and operates as Chargebee Retention. Developers integrate via the brightbackjs client library or a server-side pre-cancel API that returns a unique Cancel Session URL, with HMAC-SHA-512 signed requests for backend calls.
b.name: brightback

b.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.
b.name: BrightBytes

b.description: Brightchamps is an education technology company focused on teaching coding, robotics, financial literacy, and other future‑ready skills to children through online and in‑person programs. Their platform offers a variety of courses, including coding classes, robotics, math, generative AI, and soft‑skill development, aiming to empower the next generation with practical tech knowledge. Brightchamps serves families worldwide, providing flexible learning paths and resources for both kids and educators.
b.name: Brightchamps

b.description: Brightcove is an online video platform providing REST APIs for uploading and managing videos, encoding, CDN delivery, player configuration, analytics, and live streaming management. Its Video Cloud platform serves media companies, broadcasters, marketers, and OTT providers globally.
b.name: Brightcove

b.description: Brighte provides financing solutions for Australian households and businesses to adopt solar panels, green loans, and energy-efficient home improvements. Their platform offers interest‑free payment plans, green loans, personal loans, and various government‑backed schemes to make sustainable energy affordable. By partnering with vendors and offering a portal for customers, Brighte aims to accelerate the transition to renewable energy across Australia, supporting both residential and commercial projects.
b.name: Brighte

b.description: BrightEdge is an enterprise SEO and content performance platform, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Silicon Valley, used by thousands of brands and a majority of the Fortune 100. Its products include the DataCube keyword and content data repository, ContentIQ site auditing, Autopilot, Copilot, and the DataMind AI engine plus AI Catalyst for generative-search visibility. The BrightEdge Platform API (v5.0) is a REST API published at api.brightedge.com that exposes accounts, keywords, keyword groups, competitors, domains, pages, backlinks, the DataCube dataset, recommendations, People-Also-Ask, SERP features, Core Web Vitals, bulk export, and user/organization management, so teams can integrate BrightEdge search and content intelligence into their own reporting, analytics, and data-warehouse workflows.
b.name: BrightEdge

b.description: Brighter is a Santa Monica, California digital health technology company founded in 2010 by internet entrepreneur Jake Winebaum that built a consumer-driven dental benefits platform connecting dentists, patients, and dental insurers. Brighter licensed digital engagement solutions to insurance carriers, including online and mobile provider directories, patient reviews, and its proprietary Brighter Schedule online appointment scheduling feature, along with the Brighter PRO self-insured dental plan launched in 2014. Its platform powered member-engagement tools for major dental insurers including Cigna, Delta Dental, and Aetna. Backed by roughly $49M from General Catalyst, Mayfield, Benchmark, DAG Ventures, and Tenaya Capital, Brighter was acquired by Cigna in December 2017 and its technology folded into Cigna's digital health offerings. The brand persists as a Cigna dental provider experience.
b.name: Brighter

b.description: BrightFarms grows fresh, pesticide‑free greens in indoor farms across the United States, delivering crisp lettuce and salads directly to grocery stores within a day of harvest. The company emphasizes sustainable agriculture, using less water and land while eliminating pesticides, herbicides, and fungicides. Their mission is to create a new generation of farming that benefits the planet and consumers, offering year‑round produce regardless of weather or season.
b.name: BrightFarms

b.description: Brightfield is an extended-workforce intelligence company whose TDX (Talent Data Exchange) and TDX AI platform give enterprises data, automation, and precision over contingent-labor and statement-of-work (SOW) spending across 100+ countries. Products include Rate Intelligence, Rate Card Manager, SOW Rate Insights, SOW Quality and Risk Analytics, Supplier Scorecard, and an ROI Dashboard, built on transaction-level data from 700+ companies and $500B+ of global spend. Founded and led by CEO Jason Ezratty and headquartered in Washington, DC, Brightfield is backed by Sapphire Ventures. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application; no public developer API or documentation surface is published at this time.
b.name: Brightfield

b.description: Brightfield Software, operating under the Distyra brand, provides European bank data APIs that deliver raw transaction information distilled into actionable signals. Their platform offers products for data enrichment, underwriting, and compliance, tailored to European payment formats and regulations. Built in the EU, Distyra ensures data residency and privacy, supporting developers with comprehensive documentation, pricing plans, and a status page. The service aims to simplify access to bank data for fintech applications, offering a free tier and enterprise options.
b.name: Brightfield Software

b.description: Brightflag is an AI-first enterprise legal management (ELM) platform that helps corporate legal teams control legal spend, manage matters, benchmark outside counsel, and automate invoice review. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Dublin with a New York presence, Brightflag combines patented AI for invoice review and spend classification with e-billing, matter management, vendor management, and reporting. For developers Brightflag exposes an OAuth 2.0 secured REST API (OpenAPI 3.1) — including a Reporting API for extracting key datasets and a Matter Budget API — to integrate legal operations data with ERP, payment, and enterprise systems. This profile was enriched from Brightflag's public developer documentation and help center.
b.name: Brightflag

b.description: BrightFunnel was a San Francisco-based B2B marketing analytics company founded in 2012 that built a revenue attribution and forecasting platform. Its Revenue Intelligence Suite gave B2B marketers multi-touch attribution, revenue-funnel analysis, account-based measurement, web analytics, and predictive forecasting so they could quantify marketing's impact on pipeline and revenue and align plans with business priorities. BrightFunnel was acquired by account-based marketing vendor Terminus in January 2018, and its multi-channel analytics were folded into the Terminus platform. It no longer operates as a standalone product: the brightfunnel.com domain now serves only a redirect, and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) to enrich. This profile remains a historical company stub, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.
b.name: BrightFunnel

b.description: BrightGo is an all-in-one janitorial and commercial-cleaning ERP platform for building service contractors. It unifies field operations, workforce management, and back-office finance in one system: scheduling, GPS-verified time and attendance, inspections and quality assurance, real-time job costing, payroll, and accounting, plus operations business-intelligence dashboards and an in-app employee communication portal. Backed by Index Ventures and Costanoa Ventures, BrightGo serves janitorial companies across the U.S. and Canada. No public developer API or documentation surface has been identified; the product is delivered via web (app.brightgo.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps.
b.name: BrightGo

b.description: BrightHire is an interview intelligence platform that helps talent and hiring teams run more consistent, equitable, and effective hiring processes. Its AI copilots and agents support the full interview lifecycle — interview planning, AI-assisted screening interviews, automated interview notes and highlights, structured decision support, and interviewer coaching — with deep integrations into applicant tracking systems, video conferencing, and collaboration tools. BrightHire is a closed SaaS product with no public developer API; it exposes value through partner ATS, calendar, and conferencing integrations rather than a documented API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as an index-ventures portfolio company.
b.name: BrightHire

b.description: Profile for Brighthouse Financial in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F500 (rank 448).
b.name: Brighthouse Financial

b.description: Brightidea provides an innovation management software platform that helps organizations capture ideas, run crowdsourcing challenges, manage hackathons, and drive company‑wide transformation. Their solutions enable collaborative innovation, idea evaluation, and portfolio management for enterprises seeking to foster a culture of continuous improvement and measurable outcomes.
b.name: Brightidea

b.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.
b.name: BrightInsight

b.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.
b.name: Brightline

b.description: BrightLocal is a local SEO platform offering a REST API for managing local business listings, tracking Google rankings, monitoring reviews, auditing citations, and generating local search reports. Used by 15,000+ agencies and businesses to rank higher in local search.
b.name: BrightLocal

b.description: Brightloom is a San Francisco customer data and customer intelligence platform for restaurant and retail brands. It began as Eatsa, the automated quinoa-bowl restaurant chain, and rebranded to Brightloom in 2019 when Starbucks licensed select components of its Digital Flywheel customer engagement software to the company, took an equity stake and a board seat alongside a $30M round. The product unifies point-of-sale, loyalty, ecommerce and marketing data into a single customer view, reports on data health, runs AI-driven hyper-segmentation and anomaly detection over that data, and recommends the next campaign and audience a brand should target. Brightloom was sold as an end-user SaaS with prebuilt connectors to common POS, loyalty and marketing platforms rather than as a developer platform, and it published no public API reference, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification. The company now appears defunct: the last dated item on its own press page is December 2022, the entire operating estate it once held TLS certificates for is gone from DNS — api.brightloom.com, api-prd/api-dev, the cgp.brightloom.com application, its auth0-cgp Auth0 tenant, and the status, support and knowledgebase hosts all NXDOMAIN — brightloom.com publishes no MX record, and only the frozen marketing site remains, with its /about/ page defaced by injected search-spam.
b.name: Brightloom

b.description: Brightly (Brighterly) is an online K‑12 education platform offering personalized math and reading tutoring. It provides 1‑on‑1 lessons, smart practice tools, and a wide range of resources to help students build strong foundations.
b.name: Brightly

b.description: Brightmail was an email anti-spam software company founded in 1998 by Sunil Paul, best known for its network of "spam probe" honeypot email addresses that fed real-time anti-spam filtering rules to enterprise mail servers. Symantec acquired Brightmail in 2004 for roughly $370 million, and the technology shipped for years as Symantec Brightmail AntiSpam and later Symantec Mail Security; Symantec's enterprise security business was subsequently acquired by Broadcom in 2019. Brightmail today is a defunct brand with no independent developer program or public API surface — www.brightmail.com redirects to broadcom.com and the brightmail.com apex domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness rather than active API enrichment.
b.name: Brightmail

b.description: Bright Money (Bright) is a San Francisco-based financial technology company that describes itself as the world's first AI Loan Assistant. Its consumer mobile app helps people pay off credit-card debt faster, build credit history, and access affordable credit through products including Bright Builder (a secured 0% APR credit line reported to the major bureaus), Bright Plan debt-payoff and budgeting, Smart Round-Ups automated savings, rent reporting, personal loans up to $10,000 through network partners, and cash advances up to $750 for all credit scores. Bright is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.
b.name: Brightmoney

b.description: Brightoniximaging is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Brightoniximaging

b.description: Brightpick is a data aggregation platform that provides a marketplace for private market securities, enabling investors to discover, evaluate, and transact in secondary market offerings. The company focuses on delivering comprehensive data, analytics, and tools to facilitate liquidity and transparency in private equity, venture capital, and other alternative asset classes. As part of the API Evangelist network, Brightpick aims to expose its services via APIs for integration with financial platforms and services.
b.name: Brightpick

b.description: BrightPlan is a San Jose, California based financial wellness company that sells a Total Financial Wellness platform to enterprise HR and benefits teams, combining a self-service digital financial planning application, an AI-powered financial wellness coach, and access to human CFP fiduciary advisors. BrightPlan LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and the product is delivered to employees as an employer-sponsored benefit rather than as a self-serve consumer subscription. The employee experience runs at my.brightplan.com and web.brightplan.com with iOS and Android apps; employer value is framed around benefits engagement, retention, and measurable financial wellbeing. BrightPlan markets HRIS and benefits-system integration to employers but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind.
b.name: BrightPlan

b.description: Brightpointoptoelectronics is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Brightpointoptoelectronics

b.description: Brightree is a ResMed company providing cloud-based business management software for post-acute care providers, including home medical equipment (HME), durable medical equipment (DME), home infusion and specialty pharmacy, orthotics and prosthetics, and home health and hospice organizations. Its platform automates the end-to-end operational workflow from intake, documentation and inventory through billing, delivery, resupply, and patient engagement. Brightree does not publish a public, self-service developer API; integrations are delivered through a partner-gated Integrated Vendor program, so this profile is limited to the company's public web presence rather than a developer portal or machine-readable API surface.
b.name: Brightree

b.description: BrightRoll was a programmatic video advertising platform founded in 2006 in San Francisco that ran one of the largest independent real-time bidding marketplaces for digital video ads (RTB/DSP/SSP), connecting brand advertisers and agencies with publisher video inventory across web, mobile, and connected devices. The company was acquired by Yahoo in November 2014 and its technology was folded into Yahoo's advertising stack, later branded under Oath / Verizon Media and now Yahoo Advertising. BrightRoll no longer operates as an independent provider and publishes no standalone developer program or public API. As of this enrichment pass its former domain, brightroll.com, returns an HTTP 301 redirect to Yahoo's advertising platforms page, and the domain is served from Yahoo-owned DNS and mail infrastructure. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired / absorbed company record rather than an active API producer.
b.name: BrightRoll

b.description: Brightseed is a bioactives and AI company founded in 2017 (San Francisco, CA, with operations in Durham, NC) that uses its Forager AI platform to map the compounds in plants to human biological pathways and health benefits. Forager draws on a proprietary dataset the company describes as the world's largest — 21 million bioactive compounds and hundreds of biological receptors spanning 23 health areas — combining high-resolution omics, high-throughput robotics and machine learning to predict which natural compounds confer a benefit and where to source them at commercial scale. Hummingbird, launched in 2026, layers an agentic AI system on top of Forager to carry partners from discovery through development. Brightseed sells discovery services (Bioactive Profiler, Bioactive Ingredient Finder) and market-ready ingredients (Bio Gut Fiber, Bio Meta Control, Bio Gut Core) to food, supplement and health-science companies. Brightseed publishes no product or developer API for Forager or Hummingbird — those are sold as enterprise engagements through a contact form. The single machine-readable surface the company operates is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) behind its corporate site at www.brightseedbio.com, which exposes anonymous read access to posts, pages, categories, tags, users, media, comments, search, taxonomies, types and statuses, plus authenticated write operations via WordPress application passwords. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from that live surface.
b.name: Brightseed

b.description: Brightside (Brightside Benefit, Inc.) is an employer-sponsored financial care benefit that helps working families reduce everyday money stress. Delivered as an employee benefit through employers, Brightside pairs each employee with a human Financial Assistant and a mobile/web app offering emergency cash and loans, debt management and credit-score improvement, savings and early wage access, bill negotiation, crisis support (eviction, utilities, food), and guidance through major life events. The company is backed by a16z, Obvious Ventures, and Trinity Ventures. Brightside is a consumer-facing benefits platform and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.
b.name: Brightside

b.description: Brightside Health is a U.S. national telehealth provider of evidence-based psychiatry (medication management) and therapy for people aged 13 and older, founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Francisco. It treats the full acuity spectrum — depression, anxiety, bipolar and mood disorders, OCD, PTSD, ADHD, insomnia, substance and alcohol use disorder, and behavioral addictions — using measurement-based care (PHQ-9/GAD-7 tracking) and precision prescribing, and runs virtual Intensive Outpatient Programs plus an evidence-based Suicide Prevention Program (Crisis Care) for elevated suicide risk. Care is delivered in all 50 states, in-network with Aetna, Cigna, Optum/UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Ambetter, Medicare and Medicaid, alongside self-pay. The platform is HIPAA compliant and has earned HITRUST Certified status for information security. Brightside sells to health plans, health systems and medical groups with EHR integration, ADT notifications and a patient referral portal, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification — partner integration is arranged through its partnerships team.
b.name: Brightside Health

b.description: Brightsidec784 is currently a stub entry harvested from secondary-market sources. No verifiable public website or detailed corporate information has been located. The company appears in multiple unrelated search results, but none conclusively identify an official domain or API documentation. Further investigation is required to confirm its existence and digital presence.
b.name: Brightsidec784

b.description: BrightSource Energy is a renewable energy technology company founded in 2006, historically known as a pioneer of utility-scale Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) — it designed, developed and built the 377 MW Ivanpah Solar Electric Generating System in California along with CSP projects in Israel, Dubai and South Africa. In 2022 the company transformed into a software business and now commercializes OASES, a cloud-based, AI-powered Energy Management System (EMS) that forecasts, optimizes and dispatches portfolios of photovoltaics, battery energy storage (BESS), wind, microgrids and EV charging. OASES combines physics-based digital twins, big-data analytics and sensor fusion with an on-site SCADA edge controller ("OASES Gateway + IoT") to run asset management, energy-market bidding and arbitrage, PPA management, grid services and frequency regulation. Engineering is based in Jerusalem, Israel, with a UK office in London. BrightSource does not publish a public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026.
b.name: BrightSource Energy

b.description: Brightspec provides advanced molecular rotational resonance (MRR) spectroscopy instruments, consumables, and software solutions for analytical chemistry. Their platform offers high‑resolution spectral analysis for pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, cosmetics, and chemical industries, enabling precise identification, quantitation, and chiral analysis of compounds. Brightspec’s offerings include hardware such as SpectraMRR, IsoMRR, NanoMRR, and software like BrightHub and Edgar, supporting comprehensive analytical workflows.
b.name: Brightspec

b.description: BrightSpring Health Services is a leading Fortune 500 provider of comprehensive home and community-based health services for complex populations. The company operates across three primary service lines: Provider Services (home health, rehabilitation, neurorehabilitation, personal care), Pharmacy Services (specialty infusion, home and community-based pharmacy dispensing over 40 million prescriptions annually), and Managed Care (home-based primary care with demonstrated 44% reduction in hospitalizations). BrightSpring operates multiple clinical brands including Adoration Home Health, Amerita specialty infusion, and All Ways Caring.
b.name: BrightSpring Health Services

b.description: Profile for BrightView Holdings in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 891).
b.name: BrightView Holdings

b.description: Brightwave is an agent infrastructure company building a compliance‑ready foundation for safely connecting AI agents to the systems where work happens. The platform enables secure, auditable interactions between autonomous agents and enterprise tools, providing governance, monitoring, and integration capabilities for modern AI‑driven workflows.
b.name: Brightwave

b.description: Brightwheel (mybrightwheel.com) is an all-in-one childcare and early education management platform used by childcare centers, preschools, and early-learning programs to run daily operations - attendance and check-in, digital daily sheets, tuition billing and payments, enrollment and admissions, staff/timecards, classroom (room) management, learning assessments, and real-time parent messaging and photo/video sharing. As of this catalog entry, Brightwheel does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key signup, OpenAPI specification, or webhook documentation. The only Brightwheel API activity that is publicly acknowledged is bespoke, contract-scoped work built for individual government partners - for example a private API implemented to submit attendance and subsidy data to Iowa's childcare subsidy data system - and inbound integrations where Brightwheel pushes data into third-party products (e.g. staff timecards to Gusto for payroll). None of these expose a documented API surface that outside developers can build against. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.
b.name: Brightwheel

b.description: Brigit is a consumer financial technology company whose mobile app helps people manage everyday money with instant cash advances of up to $500 with no credit check, interest, or late fees, a Credit Builder account, and a Finance Helper for budgeting, spending analysis, bill tracking, and overdraft prediction. The app also bundles identity-theft protection and a deals-and-offers marketplace, and is offered on paid monthly subscription tiers. Brigit reports more than 12 million users. This API Evangelist profile is a company lead surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (Canaan Partners, DCM Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners); Brigit is a direct-to-consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record is enriched at the identity and web-property level.
b.name: Brigit

b.description: Brii BioSciences Limited (stock code: 2137.HK) is a biotechnology company founded in 2018, developing therapies for high unmet medical needs, notably hepatitis B virus infection. Operating in China and the United States, the firm focuses on innovative therapeutic candidates and has a pipeline of unique programs. It employs a visionary leadership team and aims to improve patient health through advanced biotech research.
b.name: Brii BioSciences

b.description: Brik ("[Re]Constructing Construction") is an Indonesian construction-materials company, backed by Accel, that operates concrete batching plants and supplies ready-mix concrete for building and infrastructure projects across the Greater Jakarta region, including Bekasi, Bogor, Karawang, and Bandung. Its product line spans standard ready-mix batches and higher-performance "Super Concrete" variants used for mass-concrete pours. At the time of enrichment Brik publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.
b.name: Brik

b.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.
b.name: Briko Robotics

b.description: Brilent is a private-company investment opportunity listed on EquityZen, a marketplace for accredited investors to buy and sell pre-IPO shares. The company appears in EquityZen’s secondary-market listings, offering details such as valuation, stock price, management information, and funding history. Brilent’s profile includes investor resources, risk factors, and compliance disclosures, reflecting its status as a venture-backed firm seeking liquidity through private placements.
b.name: Brilent

b.description: Brilliant is an online learning platform for interactive STEM education, covering mathematics, computer science, data, and science. Headquartered in San Francisco and used by over ten million learners worldwide, Brilliant pairs guided, problem-first lessons with adaptive practice that blends classic intelligent tutoring systems, machine-learning recommender systems, and natural-language conversations. The platform is delivered through brilliant.org and native iOS and Android apps, with a freemium model and a Brilliant Premium subscription that unlocks the full course catalog, including expanding AI-powered features such as personalized tutoring conversations and on-the-fly generation of interactive content. Brilliant operates as a direct-to-consumer subscription business with an educator program for classroom access; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program, and the `github.com/brilliant` org on GitHub is an unrelated namespace of personal projects rather than an official Brilliant presence.
b.name: Brilliant

b.description: Brilliant Light Power is a privately held energy technology company founded by Dr. Randell L. Mills. It claims to develop a novel method of extracting usable energy from hydrogen atoms, termed the SunCell® technology, which it says can produce clean, non‑polluting power. The company provides detailed information about its theory, validation reports, and commercial applications on its website, including business, technology, and research sections. It positions itself as a potential source of primary energy beyond conventional fossil fuels.
b.name: Brilliant Light Power

b.description: Brilliant Planet is a carbon-removal company that grows microalgae in open-air ponds on otherwise-unproductive coastal desert land, using seawater rather than fresh water, to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide at scale. Harvested algal biomass is dried and stored to lock the captured carbon away durably, while the process also deacidifies the seawater it returns. The company operates research and demonstration facilities in coastal Morocco and is developing measurement, reporting, and verification approaches for its nature-based carbon capture. It is backed by Union Square Ventures and other climate-focused investors. This API Evangelist profile is a company/provider record; Brilliant Planet publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time (its primary web presence is access-restricted).
b.name: Brilliant Planet

b.description: Brilliant.org is an online learning platform that offers interactive problem‑solving courses in mathematics, science, and computer programming. It provides a personal tutor named Koji that adapts to each learner, delivering adaptive lessons, practice sets, and instant feedback. The service targets students, educators, and lifelong learners, aiming to develop critical thinking and STEM skills through engaging, gamified content. With millions of users worldwide, Brilliant.org combines educational research with AI‑enhanced tutoring to help learners master concepts efficiently.
b.name: Brilliantdotorg

b.description: Brim Financial is a Toronto-based Canadian fintech (founded 2017) that operates a fully-integrated, API-first credit-card Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS). It is not a chartered Schedule I or Schedule II bank; it describes itself as the only fintech in North America licensed to issue credit cards, and it delivers Credit-Cards-as-a-Service (CCaaS), loyalty/rewards, BNPL, and money-movement infrastructure to banks, credit unions, fintechs, and large brands (clients include Manulife Bank, Laurentian Bank, Canadian Western Bank, Affinity Credit Union, and Air France-KLM). Brim is registered under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) to Bank of Canada standards and was admitted to Payments Canada as a payment service provider, and has partnered with Mastercard to embed open-banking capabilities. Although Brim markets a comprehensive API-first platform, that API is delivered to enterprise/embedded-finance partners through a commercial onboarding relationship: as of this review there is no public, self-serve first-party developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no operational consumer-driven-banking (open-banking) API, consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-live open-finance framework.
b.name: Brim Financial

b.description: Brimbiotechnology is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Brimbiotechnology

b.description: Brimstone is a materials technology company decarbonizing heavy industry through a single-rock co-production process it calls the Rock Refinery. From ordinary calcium silicate rock it extracts multiple high-value materials at once - carbon-negative Portland cement and supplementary cementitious materials, alumina and aluminum, magnesium, titanium, iron/steel feedstock and critical minerals - aiming to use 100% of the feed rock and eliminate tailings while cutting process emissions. The company uses commercially available equipment for a low-cost, market-ready approach, and has secured commitments including Amazon as a buyer of low-carbon cement from its first commercial plant. Brimstone is a private heavy-industry / climate-tech company backed by DCVC and Fifth Wall; it operates no public developer API.
b.name: Brimstone

b.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.
b.name: BRINC

b.description: Brincdrones is a startup that focuses on providing drone-based solutions for various industries, including aerial surveying, inspection, and delivery services. The company aims to leverage advanced drone technology and data analytics to offer efficient, cost-effective, and scalable solutions for clients ranging from construction firms to logistics providers. While detailed public information is limited, Brincdrones appears to be positioned within the emerging market of commercial drone applications, seeking to address industry-specific challenges through innovative aerial platforms and services.
b.name: Brincdrones

b.description: Brine — now rebranded as tanX — is a cross-chain, self-custodial orderbook decentralized exchange (DEX) built on StarkWare's StarkEx Layer-2 scaling engine. It combines the trustless, non-custodial security of a DEX with the speed and low fees of a centralized exchange: gasless trading, rapid off-chain order execution with on-chain settlement, cross-chain deposits and withdrawals, and simple APIs for programmatic trading. The company is backed by Pantera Capital and is repositioning around "a secure and compliant future for crypto." This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Pantera Capital's portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; as of this pass the public REST API host is no longer reachable and the developer surface is limited to the GitBook documentation.
b.name: Brine (Tanx)

b.description: Bringg is a last-mile delivery and fulfillment orchestration platform headquartered in Tel Aviv (founded 2013, CEO Guy Bloch). The Bringg platform combines modular software (Shopping Experience, Plan, Dispatch, Drive, Delivery Experience, Automation Center, Intelligence, Connect) with the Bringg Carrier Network — 250+ pre-integrated third-party, crowdsourced, and autonomous carriers across 70+ countries — to give enterprise retailers and logistics providers a single integration point for orchestrating own-fleet and partner-fleet deliveries. Bringg's developer surface exposes a REST Delivery Hub API for orders/runs/customers/teams/service areas/service plans/delivery slots/blackouts/inventory/packages, a Drivers & Shifts API for users/shifts/delivery-blocks/vehicles, a Fleet Partners API for self-integrated carriers, 50+ outbound webhook event types, and JavaScript/iOS/Android SDKs powering the Dispatcher and Driver apps. All HTTP APIs use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant against region-specific GCP base URLs (US2/US3/US4, EU2/EU3) — visible on status.bringg.com. Bringg counts 800+ customers including Best Buy, AutoZone, ASDA, Wegmans, FedEx Office, Metro, uBreakiFix, and B&Q, and processes 200 million annual deliveries.
b.name: Bringg

b.description: Bringittechnologies is a stub company identified in the secondary-market harvest. No public website or API documentation could be located after exhaustive searches of common domains, search engines, and known hosting platforms. The company appears in equityzen listings but lacks a verifiable corporate domain, preventing confirmation of its online presence or API offerings.
b.name: Bringittechnologies

b.description: Bringy, Inc. is a digital insurance brokerage operating in Egypt, founded in 2019 and licensed by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA License #100). Through its website and iOS/Android mobile apps, Bringy lets consumers compare, select, purchase, and manage insurance policies online, positioning itself as a digital insurance advisor that guides customers from policy selection through claims and compensation. Coverage lines include car, business, medical, personal-accident, and home insurance, with payment via Visa, Mastercard, Meeza, mobile wallets, and installment providers (ValU, Sympl, Souhoola). Bringy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer marketing site and blog but no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.
b.name: Bringy

b.description: Brink Commerce provides enterprise eCommerce solutions enabling brands to build, scale, and manage online stores with flexible APIs, composable architecture, and AI‑driven tools. Their platform supports high‑traffic, complex pricing, global fulfillment, and integrates with ERP, CRM, and marketing systems, helping CEOs, CFOs, CTOs, and agencies accelerate digital commerce initiatives.
b.name: Brink Commerce

b.description: Brinker International is a leading casual dining restaurant company that owns, operates, and franchises Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Brinker operates over 1,600 Chili's locations across 29 countries and over 50 Maggiano's locations in the United States. The company leverages digital ordering platforms, loyalty programs, mobile apps, in-restaurant kiosks, and point-of-sale integrations for restaurant operations, running a unified open-source e-commerce environment built on Red Hat (RHEL, Satellite, Lightspeed) and using Prismic CMS for digital content management. Brinker runs a real but entirely partner-facing API program on Google Apigee: an Apigee Edge gateway at api.brinker.com and an Apigee Integrated Developer Portal at developer.brinker.com whose API catalog is approval-gated (accounts are approved by the Brinker API Team and API Products assigned by entitlement). The portal's anonymous catalog endpoint returns an empty apiDocs/apiProducts list; its QA sibling names six API product families — LoyaltyEA, Promos, ITSM ServiceNow, GMS, OrderManagement and POS — but exposes no paths, schemas or base URLs. There is no public, self-service developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, agent card, or open GitHub organization. Consumer-facing surfaces are the Chili's and Maggiano's mobile apps and websites and their loyalty programs, with online ordering powered by Olo and site content by Prismic.
b.name: Brinker International

b.description: Brink's is a global leader in secure cash management, armored transport, ATM services, and financial security solutions. The company serves retail, restaurant, financial institutions, and entertainment businesses with its Total Cash Management platform, combining hardware, software, and logistics services. Brink's digital customer portal 24SEVEN ACCESS enables businesses to track cash deposits, order change, and manage operations via mobile and desktop interfaces. Additional products include the Brink's Armored Account payment processing service, Brink's Money paycard for employee payments, and RetailBox point-of-sale cash management.
b.name: Brinks

b.description: Brinqa is an AI-powered vulnerability and exposure management platform that unifies cyber risk data from across an enterprise's security tools into a single trusted data model. It ingests and correlates exposure findings from scanners and connectors, deduplicates them, and applies risk scoring, custom risk factors, and workflow automation to prioritize and drive remediation. The Brinqa Platform exposes a GraphQL API and the Brinqa Query Language (BQL) for traversing an entity-relationship graph of assets, findings, hosts, tickets, and vulnerabilities, plus reporting and dashboards on those datasets. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched from Brinqa's public developer documentation.
b.name: Brinqa

b.description: Briq provides AI-driven orchestration solutions for the construction industry, enabling companies to automate workflows, optimize resource allocation, and integrate data across projects. Their platform leverages machine learning to improve decision‑making and operational efficiency in construction management.
b.name: Briq

b.description: Brisk Health is a Colorado urgent care and primary care provider operating a cash-pay clinic in the Denver metro area plus a fleet of mobile vehicles staffed by acute care clinicians for in-home visits, with same-day visits advertised from $49 and no insurance required. In October 2025 it announced a move from its Lakewood location to a purpose-built facility in Littleton, Colorado. Brisk Health is a healthcare services business rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable specification of any kind. Its patient-facing mobile app has been delisted from both the Apple App Store and Google Play, and both of its brand domains now serve parked-domain error pages.
b.name: Brisk Health

b.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.
b.name: Brisk Teaching

b.description: Bristle (Bristle Health) is a consumer health company that makes the world's first at-home oral microbiome saliva test, helping people measure, understand, and improve their oral health. Customers order a mail-in saliva collection kit, and Bristle sequences the oral microbiome to report on bacteria associated with cavities, gum disease, and bad breath, then pairs the results with guidance and a line of targeted oral-care products including probiotics. Bristle also works with dental professionals who offer microbiome testing to their patients. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted storefront at bristlehealth.com and is backed by Initialized Capital. There is no first-party public developer API; this profile captures Bristle's public web, commercial, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Bristle

b.description: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is a global Fortune 500 biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and delivering innovative medicines for patients with serious diseases. BMS focuses on oncology, immunology, cardiovascular, fibrosis, and cell therapy (CAR T). The company operates BMS Study Connect for clinical trial recruitment, a Medical Information portal for healthcare providers, and the BMS Business Development platform for research partnerships and data sharing. BMS actively pursues technology partnerships in protein degradation, advanced treatment modalities, and digital health.
b.name: Bristol Myers Squibb

b.description: Brit + Co is a lifestyle and entertainment media platform founded by Brit Morin that publishes content and creative education for a primarily women audience. It covers self-care, food, home and DIY, travel, relationships, celebrity and entertainment news, horoscopes, shopping guides, and games, and operates a learning platform (learn.brit.co) offering more than one hundred creative online classes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures. It is a consumer media and e-learning brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.
b.name: Brit + Co

b.description: British Airways Plc is the United Kingdom's flag carrier, headquartered at Waterside near London Heathrow and owned since 2011 by International Consolidated Airlines Group (IAG), which also owns Iberia, Aer Lingus, Vueling and LEVEL. In the distribution chain BA is a supplier of its own seat inventory, reached either through the three legacy GDSs, through IATA NDC connections it operates itself, or direct on ba.com. BA was one of the earliest and most aggressive NDC adopters: from 1 November 2017 IAG applied a per-fare-component Distribution Technology Charge to BA and Iberia marketed fares that are not booked through an NDC based connection or a low-cost channel such as ba.com, explicitly pricing GDS intermediation out of the stack. Its API posture is honest to state plainly - the NDC distribution API is real and is built on the IATA EDIST message set, but there is no public specification, no published base URL, no self-serve signup and no exit path. Access requires registration, a B1 or B2 certification form, acceptance of the British Airways API and Services Trial Use Agreement plus the Travel Agency Addendum for IATA accredited agents, and signed live API contracts. The older public consumer REST APIs (Flight Information, Flight Offers, Lowest Prices, In-Flight Entertainment, Hotel/Car/Flight packages) on the IAG Developer Programs portal are gone: as of 2026-07-28 developer.iairgroup.com returns HTTP 404 and api.ba.com returns HTTP 596 ERR_596_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND for every documented resource.
b.name: British Airways

b.description: Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO) is a Daytona Beach, Florida headquartered insurance brokerage and risk-management intermediary founded in 1939, and one of the largest independent brokers in the United States. Following the 2025 acquisition of Accession Risk Management Group (Risk Strategies and One80 Intermediaries), it reports through two segments: Retail — property and casualty insurance, employee benefits, private client, captive solutions and financial/wealth services — and Specialty Distribution — programs, wholesale brokerage and MGA/binding-authority businesses including Arrowhead. As a distributor rather than a carrier, Brown & Brown places risk with insurers instead of underwriting it, and its US home market has no federal insurance regulator and no open-insurance mandate. Its API posture reflects that honestly: Brown & Brown publishes no public developer portal and no self-serve API. developer.bbrown.com, developers.bbrown.com, docs.bbrown.com and api.bbrown.com do not resolve, and every /developers, /api, /partners and /integrations path returns 404. Every discoverable application subdomain is a login wall — agent, client and vendor portals behind Microsoft Entra ID SSO or third-party sign-in. The only real programmatic surface is partner-gated: the Arrowhead Programs "Enterprise API" (EAPI), a quoting integration distributed through comparative raters and aggregators such as CoverHound, Tarmika, Semsee and DAIS, with no public documentation, base URL or specification. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference is published on any Brown & Brown first-party property; carrier data exchange runs, as it does across US retail brokerage, through the agency management system layer — Brown & Brown is a publicly referenced Vertafore AMS360 agency — and IVANS agency download rather than through any API Brown & Brown itself exposes. In July 2026 the company announced an AI-first transformation with Anthropic, McKinsey and Accenture, deploying Claude across 23,000 teammates and Claude Code across its software engineering organization; that is internal adoption and has so far produced no external API, developer portal or agent-facing surface. The only machine-readable documents Brown & Brown publishes are two RSS feeds — the blog and investor news releases.
