b.description: Burro develops is a robotics company building autonomous, electric workhorse platforms for agriculture and industrial tasks. Founded in 2017, Burro creates collaborative robots that automate repetitive labor, improving productivity in farms, nurseries, vineyards, and warehouses. The company offers modular, plug‑and‑play robots capable of towing, load‑carrying, mowing, spraying, and monitoring, targeting specialty crop operations and heavy‑duty material handling.
b.name: Burro develops

b.description: Burrow provides a client reporting and operations platform for web agencies, offering an event‑driven orchestration layer that ingests data from tools like WordPress, Shopify, Stripe, and many others. It supplies SDKs, plugins, and a JSON‑RPC MCP for AI agents to automate agency workflows, generate reports, and query analytics. The platform is self‑funded, independent, and built for long‑term agency operations.
b.name: Burrow

b.description: Burst Oral Care is a consumer oral‑care brand offering a range of electric toothbrushes, accessories, and oral‑health products. Backed by dental professionals, the company focuses on high‑quality design, innovative technology, and subscription‑based brush‑head replacement. Their e‑commerce site provides detailed product information, customer support, and a blog on oral health.
b.name: Burst Oral Care

b.description: BurstIQ is a health-and-data technology company whose LifeGraph platform pairs a blockchain-secured knowledge graph (GraphChain) with granular consent-and-ownership wallets and configurable data pipelines to give enterprises trusted, agent-ready data. The LifeGraph REST API (OpenAPI 3.1, version 2.42.0) exposes 171 operations across GraphChain Smart Data Objects, user and system wallets, dictionaries, glossaries, edge definitions, data pipelines, job management, and an OData v4 query surface, secured with bearer (JWT) authentication. BurstIQ was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
b.name: BurstIQ

b.description: Burt builds AI teammates (AI coworkers) for logistics, aimed at freight brokers and forwarders. Its agents automate the repetitive, manual work of daily freight operations — track and trace, quoting, scheduling, carrier booking, document processing, proof-of-delivery chasing, and invoice and data entry — so human operators can focus on customer relationships and growing the business. Burt gives full visibility into every AI action with human oversight and approval workflows, rolls out autonomy gradually, and learns from operator corrections and exceptions to build institutional knowledge over time. Burt is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Burt does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.
b.name: Burt

b.description: Bushel provides software solutions for agriculture, offering tools for farm management, agribusiness CRM, commercial grain sales, payments, and digital services. Their platform connects farmers, agribusinesses, and partners to streamline operations, improve data insights, and enable modern agricultural workflows.
b.name: Bushel

b.description: Business Box provides an integrated booking and payment platform tailored for Japanese small businesses. It combines a booking page, calendar synchronization with Google and Outlook, and Stripe‑based pre‑payment handling, all in one service. Users can publish booking pages, automatically sync availability, and receive payments directly into their Stripe accounts without additional fees. The service includes free usage tiers, supports Japanese public holidays, offers bilingual (Japanese/English) interfaces, and is built for the Japanese market.
b.name: Business Box

b.description: Business Insider is a global business and financial news media company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York City, operating as part of Axel Springer. It publishes fast-paced coverage of markets, technology, finance, the economy, retail, media, and careers across its flagship Business Insider brand and verticals such as Markets Insider. The organization was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm IVP. It operates consumer news properties and content syndication feeds rather than a public developer API program, so this profile tracks its public web presence and domain security posture rather than API artifacts.
b.name: Business Insider

b.description: Business Leads World is a US lead-generation and B2B data company serving the alternative business-finance market. Operating since 2016 from Queens, New York, it supplies merchant cash advance (MCA) and business loan leads to lenders, ISOs, funding companies and loan brokers — MCA live-transfer calls, call-back leads, aged MCA leads, business loan leads, digital marketing leads and B2B email data. Leads are sourced through SEO, PPC and email marketing and pre-qualified against published criteria (credit score above 550, no bankruptcies, at least one year in business, and monthly bank deposits above $15,000). The company sells lead lists through a self-service storefront on its own website; it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.
b.name: Business Leads World

b.description: G2 is the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace. More than 90 million people annually use G2 to make smarter software decisions based on authentic peer reviews. Find the right software and services based on real user reviews.
b.name: Business Software and Services Reviews | G2

b.description: Business Canvas is a business development and client acquisition advisory firm helping established B2B service businesses strengthen market positioning, attract better-fit clients, and develop more effective acquisition approaches around buyer behavior. It offers a 4‑Pillar Accelerator Program and strategic consulting to improve revenue growth and client quality for service firms.
b.name: Businesscanvas

b.description: Businesslist2, also known as nobul, is a technology-driven real estate marketplace that enables agents from any brokerage to compete for consumer business. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in West Palm Beach, FL, US, the company leverages software and artificial intelligence to facilitate pre-IPO share investments through platforms like EquityZen. It offers a platform for buying and selling shares of private companies, aiming to democratize access to private market investments.
b.name: Businesslist2

b.description: Businest Pty Ltd provides step‑by‑step monthly advisory training and certification for accountants and bookkeepers, helping them transition into advisory services. Their platform offers various subscription plans, live sessions with accredited experts, and resources aimed at improving client outcomes and business growth.
b.name: Businestptyltd

b.description: Bustle is the flagship lifestyle and culture publication of Bustle Digital Group (BDG), a New York-based digital media company that moves culture forward through premium editorial content, social storytelling, and live experiences. BDG operates a portfolio of eight brands - Bustle, NYLON, Scary Mommy, W Magazine, Inverse, The Zoe Report, Romper, and Elite Daily - spanning lifestyle, fashion, parenting, entertainment, and luxury. The company produces award-winning branded content and campaigns through its BDG Studios and BDGx experiential arm. Bustle is a consumer media publisher rather than an API provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead, and no public developer API or specification has been identified on its properties.
b.name: Bustle

b.description: Bustle Digital Group is a digital media company that operates a portfolio of online brands, including Bustle, Elite Daily, Mic, and others. It creates content across lifestyle, news, entertainment, and culture, reaching millions of readers worldwide. The company leverages data-driven storytelling and social media distribution to engage audiences and offers advertising solutions for brands.
b.name: Bustle Digital Group

b.description: BusUp Technologies provides a cloud‑based platform that enables businesses to digitize and automate their procurement, invoicing, and expense management processes. The solution offers real‑time analytics, integration with ERP and accounting systems, and a mobile app for on‑the‑go approvals. Targeted at mid‑size enterprises, BusUp aims to streamline spend management, improve compliance, and reduce manual effort across the purchase‑to‑pay lifecycle.
b.name: BusUp

b.description: Busy Ming Group (Hunan Mingming Busy Commercial Chain Co., Ltd. / 湖南鸣鸣很忙商业连锁股份有限公司) is a mass-market snack retail chain operator headquartered in Changsha, Hunan, China, and a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). It operates two discount snack store brands — Snacks Are Busy (零食很忙, founded 2017) and Zhao Yiming Snacks (赵一鸣零食, founded 2019) — which combined into a network of more than 21,000 retail locations, heavily concentrated in county-level cities and townships. The group publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, franchising, and investor-relations web presence.
b.name: Busy Ming Group

b.description: Butler Electric is a residential and commercial electrical contractor based in Sandy, Utah, offering services such as panel upgrades, basement wiring, EV charger installations, remodel electrical work, and general electrical repairs. With over 25 years of experience, the licensed team provides reliable, code‑compliant solutions across the Salt Lake City area, emphasizing safety, professionalism, and customer satisfaction.
b.name: Butler Electric Group

b.description: Butlr is an AI platform for privacy-first, heat-based (thermal) occupancy sensing that turns anonymous people-sensing into real-time space-utilization insight for workplaces, senior living, higher education, retail, and smart buildings. Its camera-free thermal sensors capture no personally identifiable information while powering occupancy, traffic, presence-time, and heatmap analytics. Butlr exposes an API-first platform: a GraphQL asset-management API for sites, buildings, floors, rooms, zones, hives, and sensors; a RESTful Reporting API (v3) for historical time-series occupancy; real-time webhooks for detections, traffic, and occupancy events; and an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agent access. The company reports 30,000+ deployed sensors generating a billion data points daily across 100M+ square feet in 22 countries.
b.name: Butlr

b.description: Butlr0e8d is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Butlr0e8d

b.description: Butn is an Australian embedded-finance company that funds business cashflow at the point of transaction, plugging invoice finance, outsourced credit terms, and supplier "pay now, settle later" directly into the platforms its business customers already use. Its funding products — Butn X (invoice finance to draw cash early against receivables), Butn Terms (outsourced buyer credit where Butn carries the risk), and Butn Pay (paying suppliers upfront in exchange for extended repayment) — are designed to be embedded into partner marketplaces, accounting tools, and B2B platforms such as MYOB, Salesforce, and FoodByUs rather than sold as a standalone destination. Butn sits in the spend / accounts payable and accounts receivable financing layer of Australia's payments market, where money movement rides the New Payments Platform and the banks opened by the Consumer Data Right. Its integration and embedding are delivered through private, partner-provisioned APIs: Butn markets "plug and play" embedding for partners but does not operate a public self-serve developer portal, publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger definitions, or expose openly documented API reference material as of this profile.
b.name: Butn

b.description: Butter Systems was a San Francisco restaurant-technology startup founded in 2013 by Sam Brin and Jon Li and backed by Y Combinator (batch S13). The company replaced the paper restaurant menu with a locked-down tablet at the table, letting diners browse an interactive menu, place food and drink orders on demand without waiting for a server, and request the check, while restaurant operators adjusted menu items, pricing, and promotions on the fly through a web back office. Butter Systems raised roughly $120K across two seed rounds in 2013 from Y Combinator and Fenox Venture Capital, and shut down in 2014. Y Combinator lists the company as inactive, and its buttersystems.com domain is now a parked "domain may be for sale" page. Butter Systems published no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and none survives in the Internet Archive record; it is retained in the API Evangelist network as a closed-company reference only.
b.name: Butter Systems

b.description: Butter6f77 is a stub entry created during the API Evangelist harvest process. It represents a company identified from secondary-market sources but currently lacks publicly available documentation, a dedicated website, or known API endpoints. The entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment as more information becomes available, ensuring the company is tracked within the network for potential API discovery and profiling.
b.name: Butter6f77

b.description: Butterball is a leading turkey producer in the United States, offering a wide range of turkey products for holidays and everyday meals. The company provides recipes, cooking guides, and product information through its website, helping consumers prepare delicious turkey dishes. Butterball emphasizes quality, sustainability, and community involvement, with resources for food safety, cooking tips, and charitable initiatives.
b.name: Butterball

b.description: Butterfly is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions in data integration and workflow automation. The company offers APIs to connect systems, automate processes, and build custom integrations, simplifying complex data flows and improving operational efficiency across industries.
b.name: Butterfly

b.description: Butterfly Network develops handheld, portable ultrasound devices and a cloud‑based imaging platform that enable clinicians to capture, store, and share diagnostic images at the point of care. The company offers a suite of products including the iQ series of probes, AI‑assisted image analysis, and a subscription service for data management and tele‑medicine integration, serving hospitals, clinics, and veterinary practices worldwide.
b.name: Butterfly Network

b.description: ButterflyMX is a property-access technology company whose smart video intercoms, keypads, smart locks, elevator controls, vehicle-access readers, package rooms and front-desk stations are installed in more than 20,000 multifamily, commercial, gated-community, student-housing and senior-living buildings. Its public ButterflyMX API (v4) exposes the same access-control core to partners and property-technology platforms: buildings, units, tenants, access points, devices, access groups, permanent access tools (PINs and RFID tags), keychains and virtual keys for visitor passes, door-release requests for programmatic swipe-to-open, and access and video-call logs. Real-time delivery is handled by building- and tenant-scoped webhook integrations, and native iOS and Android SDKs add in-app video-call handling on top of the REST surface. Authorization is OAuth 2.0 authorization-code, issued by an OpenID-Connect-discoverable authorization server at accounts.butterflymx.com, with a full sandbox replica for pre-production testing.
b.name: ButterflyMX

b.description: Butternut Box is a London-headquartered direct-to-consumer pet nutrition company that cooks and delivers fresh, gently-steamed dog food on a personalised subscription. Customers complete an online profiling wizard covering their dog's breed, age, weight, activity level and health needs, and Butternut Box calculates a portioned meal plan from human-quality meat and vegetables, batch-cooks it at low temperature, freezes it, and ships it on a recurring schedule. Founded in 2016 and certified as a B Corporation, the company operates nine locale storefronts covering the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium (Dutch and French), Germany, Italy, Sweden and Denmark, and runs its own production facility alongside a React / React Native / Ruby on Rails engineering stack. Butternut Box publishes no public developer API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its customer-facing surfaces are the marketing site, the subscription web app and the iOS/Android apps.
b.name: Butternut Box

b.description: Butter Payments is a payment recovery and involuntary-churn platform that uses machine learning to recover revenue from failed subscription payments. Its Recover product ingests real-time transaction and payment-method events, optimizes retry timing, and reports outcomes back to merchants via HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks; Dispute (powered by Verifi) intercepts chargebacks and runs Rapid Dispute Resolution; PaymentScore identifies recoverable failed payments; and a PCI DSS Level 2 Card Vault secures card data behind a secure-iframe element. Butter integrates turnkey with Stripe Billing, Braintree, and Recharge, or directly through the Recover Enterprise API.
b.name: Butterpayments

b.description: Button (usebutton.com) is a mobile commerce technology company whose platform connects Publishers and Brands in a two-sided marketplace: publishers deep-link their users into retailer apps and sites with full attribution, and brands acquire and re-engage customers through those optimized journeys. Its server-to-server APIs cover personalized Offers, attributed Link and Shortlink generation (including Amazon creator links), Brand partnership details, Billing/affiliation transaction reporting, and Order reporting, complemented by Publisher SDKs, Merchant Libraries, and HMAC-signed transaction webhooks.
b.name: Button

b.description: Buttondown is an independent, bootstrapped email newsletter platform for writers, creators and developers, offering a Markdown and rich-text editor, subscriber management with tags, segments and metadata, automations, RSS-to-email, surveys, comments, paid subscriptions via Stripe with no revenue share, custom sending and hosting domains, and hosted archives. Its public REST API covers 133 operations across 29 resource areas — subscribers, emails, tags, segments, automations, webhooks, imports, exports, surveys, forms, images, snippets, prices and more — described by a live OpenAPI 3.1 document, backed by an 82-event webhook catalog, a date-based version train, idempotency keys, and a first-party CLI for syncing newsletter content to a local folder.
b.name: Buttondown

b.description: BUX is a European neobroker and mobile-first investing app operated by BUX B.V., a subsidiary of ABN AMRO. It lets retail investors across Europe buy and sell individual stocks and ETFs commission-free starting from as little as EUR 10, build automated BUX Investment Plans (thematic and expert-built portfolios), and earn interest on uninvested cash across BUX Basic, Plus, and Prime account tiers. BUX is authorised and regulated by the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM), with client financial instruments and money held in segregated custody via ABN AMRO Clearing and deposits protected up to EUR 100,000 under the Dutch Deposit Guarantee Scheme. BUX does not publish a public developer API or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, legal, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.
b.name: BUX

b.description: Buxfer is a personal finance and money management platform that consolidates bank, investment and retirement accounts in one place. It connects to 20,000+ banks across 70+ countries, tracks assets in 100+ currencies, and provides budgeting with real-time alerts, expense forecasting, net-worth projection, automatic transaction tagging with custom rules, investment and retirement planning, shared-expense groups, and encrypted cloud backups to Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive. Buxfer exposes a JSON HTTP API for reading accounts, transactions, tags, budgets, reminders, groups, contacts and loans, and for creating, editing and deleting transactions and uploading statements. Authentication uses a login call that returns an ephemeral token passed on every subsequent request. Buxfer is a Y Combinator company.
b.name: Buxfer

b.description: Buy Me a Coffee is a creator-support platform that lets fans tip creators ("buy a coffee"), subscribe to recurring memberships, and buy extras from a creator's shop. Its developer API is a read-only REST interface (base https://developers.buymeacoffee.com/api/v1) authenticated with a personal access Bearer token created self-serve in the Developer Dashboard. The API exposes a creator's own one-time supporters, memberships/subscriptions, and extra purchases, and the platform also delivers server-push webhooks for donation, membership, and shop events. Buy Me a Coffee charges a flat 5% platform fee on transactions with no monthly fee.
b.name: Buy Me a Coffee

b.description: Buyandship is a parcel forwarding and global shopping service based in Hong Kong. It allows users to shop from international retailers, consolidates shipments from over 10 countries, and provides affordable shipping, protection plans, and a user-friendly platform with mobile apps. The service supports major marketplaces like eBay, Mercari, and JDirectItems, offering price monitoring, coupons, and a help center for customers worldwide.
b.name: Buyandship

b.description: Buybox provides an omnichannel gift card solution for brands, enabling B2C and B2B gift card programs across Europe and beyond. Their platform offers integrated tools for distribution, analytics, and compliance, supporting multiple languages, currencies, and regulatory environments. The company emphasizes rapid international deployment, ROI guarantees, and deep integrations with major CMS, PSP, and POS systems, positioning itself as a strategic partner for brands seeking efficient customer acquisition through gift cards.
b.name: Buybox

b.description: BuyBuddy is an AI-powered retail merchandising platform positioned as an "AI Merchandiser that tracks, thinks & acts for you." It automates in-store operations for retailers and brands, including planogram compliance and shelf monitoring via computer vision, stockout prevention, product placement optimization, dynamic pricing and promotions, demand forecasting, store transfers, and shopper-behavior analysis through smart tags. BuyBuddy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; at time of enrichment BuyBuddy publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or specification surface, so this remains a company-level profile.
b.name: BuyBuddy

b.description: BuyerSight provides an AI‑augmented outbound sales pipeline platform that combines automated prospecting, email deliverability management, and human sales expertise. It helps B2B companies increase qualified meetings, improve conversion rates, and reduce customer acquisition costs through AI‑driven recommendations and managed email infrastructure.
b.name: Buyersight

b.description: Buyitmobility is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Buyitmobility

b.description: Buyk was a rapid‑delivery grocery startup that promised 15‑minute door‑step deliveries with no minimum spend or delivery fee. Founded in 2020, it expanded to dozens of US cities before collapsing in 2022 amid financial pressures linked to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The company’s assets were later sold off in a bankruptcy proceeding. This entry records the company’s brief history and its now‑defunct API ecosystem.
b.name: Buyk

b.description: Buymed leverages technology, innovation, and data to build a seamless, intelligent pharmaceutical supply chain that connects manufacturers, distributors, hospitals, pharmacies and patients across Vietnam, Cambodia, and Thailand. Founded in 2018, it aims to provide faster, fairer, and more efficient access to healthcare, empowering better outcomes for millions.
b.name: Buymed

b.description: Buynomics is a Cologne, Germany-based software company providing an AI-powered Revenue Growth Management (RGM) platform for consumer goods, retail, telecom, and consumer software companies. Its proprietary "Virtual Shoppers AI" runs agent-based simulations of consumer purchasing behavior so commercial teams can optimize pricing, promotions, price pack architecture (product mix), and trade terms before going to market — capturing cross- effects, cannibalization, and competitive response. The platform's Decision Guide generates prescriptive recommendations from thousands of evaluated scenarios. Buynomics is used by brands including Unilever, Nestle, L'Oreal, Danone, General Mills, Vodafone, and Ferrero, and is backed by Insight Partners and Seedcamp. The product is delivered as a web application; no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time.
b.name: buynomics

b.description: Buysight, Inc. was a Silicon Valley advertising technology startup founded in 2008 that built intent-based audience targeting, retargeting, and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO) for display advertising, using machine learning to select both the audience for an impression and the creative shown to that user. The company raised approximately $16 million from ONSET Ventures, Rembrandt Venture Partners, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC / Jeff Clavier), Reid Hoffman, and AOL. On December 4, 2012 Buysight was acquired by AOL's Advertising.com Group, with the entire team joining AOL and the DCO and machine-learning technology folded into AOL's AdLearn optimization engine alongside Advertising.com, ADTECH, the AOL On Network, goviral, and Pictela. Buysight no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, documentation, or SDKs. The buysight.com domain is held by MarkMonitor and redirects to a registrar placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical acquisition record in the API Evangelist network.
b.name: Buysight

b.description: Agent-native, MCP-native product catalog and price comparison API for Southeast Asia and US e-commerce. Search 1.5M+ products across Shopee, Lazada, Carousell, FairPrice, Best Denki, Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and 20+ retailers. AI agents and MCP clients discover and route purchases to local merchants through a hosted MCP HTTP endpoint at api.buywhere.ai/mcp or via the @buywhere/mcp-server STDIO package.
b.name: BuyWhere

b.description: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
b.name: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe)

b.description: Buzz360 is an all‑in‑one political campaign software platform based in Minneapolis, United States. Founded in 2011, it provides tools for voter contact, relational organizing, SMS, email, fundraising, event management, and ballot chase, targeting conservative campaigns and small organizations. The platform unifies data, door‑knocking, messaging, and analytics into a single system for fast, high‑stakes election work.
b.name: Buzz360

b.description: Buzzer was a mobile live-sports streaming startup founded in 2020 by Bo Han, formerly director of live content at Twitter. Its consumer app, launched in 2021, sold micropayment access — as low as $0.99 to $1 — to short in-game moments of live sporting events, targeting Gen Z fans who would not buy a full cable or league subscription. Buzzer secured streaming rights covering the NBA, WNBA, NHL, PGA Tour and ATP Tour, and raised roughly $44 million in total, including a $20 million Series A in June 2021 co-led by Sapphire Sport and Canaan Partners alongside a large group of athlete and team-owner investors. On 19 May 2023 the company shut down the direct-to-consumer app and pivoted to a business-to-business model branded "Powered by Buzzer", announced as API licensing, custom development and consulting for leagues, teams and networks streaming direct to fans. That offering never reached public availability: Buzzer ceased all operations on 30 June 2023, citing "recent fundraising developments and market dynamics". No public developer portal, API documentation, specification, SDK or package was ever published. The buzzer.com domain no longer hosts the company and now redirects to an Atom.com domain-for-sale listing. Retained in the network as a historical record of a defunct company; not an active API provider.
b.name: Buzzer

b.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.
b.name: BuzzFeed

b.description: Buzzkill Labs is a technology startup focused on developing innovative solutions for digital content moderation and user engagement analytics. The company aims to provide APIs that enable developers to integrate sentiment analysis, toxicity detection, and real-time moderation tools into their applications, helping platforms maintain healthy online communities. While the company is currently in early stages, it plans to release a suite of RESTful services and SDKs across multiple programming languages.
b.name: Buzzkill Labs

b.description: Buzzkilllabs is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
b.name: Buzzkilllabs

b.description: Buzzni is a Korean AI-driven commerce technology company offering subscription-based AI solutions for e‑commerce, home‑shopping platforms, and digital marketing. It provides large‑scale product and review data, AI recommendation engines, and tools for video and image analysis, serving millions of users and partnering with major retailers.
b.name: Buzzni

b.description: Buzzsprout is a podcast hosting platform that handles hosting, distribution, promotion, and analytics for podcasters - uploading and optimizing audio, publishing an RSS feed, listing shows in directories like Apple Podcasts and Spotify, and reporting on plays. Buzzsprout also exposes a documented public REST API (base https://www.buzzsprout.com/api) so third parties can programmatically read and manage the podcasts and episodes on an account. The API is RESTful, JSON-serialized, SSL-only, and authenticated with a per-account token.
b.name: Buzzsprout

b.description: BVNK is a stablecoin payments infrastructure company that lets businesses move money between fiat and stablecoins over a single API. The platform covers merchant crypto payment collection through payment links and blockchain channels, embedded stablecoin wallets and named virtual accounts (vIBAN) in EUR, GBP and USD, fiat pay-ins and payouts over SWIFT, ACH, Fedwire and local rails, on-ramp and off-ramp conversion, card issuing, treasury and trading, plus customer onboarding, compliance and Travel Rule workflows. Developers integrate over a REST API authenticated with Hawk HMAC-SHA256 request signing, with webhooks for every payment, wallet, card and onboarding lifecycle event, a full sandbox with a payment simulator, and a Postman collection generated from the OpenAPI. BVNK operates as a regulated EMI in the UK (FCA) and Malta (MFSA), is ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certified, and also runs the Layer1 institutional digital-asset platform.

b.description: By Miles is a London-based insurtech that pioneered pay-by-mile motor insurance in the United Kingdom, founded in 2016 for low-mileage drivers who cover under roughly 7,000 miles a year. Its single line of business is UK private motor (personal lines property and casualty), priced as a fixed annual premium covering the parked car plus a per-mile charge for the distance actually driven. Mileage is measured either by the OBD-II "Miles Tracker" telematics dongle or, on its "connect" trackerless policies, by pulling odometer data directly from the manufacturer's connected-car platform after the driver links a Tesla, Ford or Mercedes-Benz account. By Miles was acquired by Direct Line Group in April 2023 and, following Aviva's acquisition of Direct Line Group, has been wound down — it stopped quoting new business and, from 6 January 2026, stopped offering renewal quotes to existing customers. Its API posture is that of a pure API CONSUMER, not a producer: it was the first UK insurtech directly authorised by the FCA as an AISP/PISP to consume Open Banking APIs (January 2020), and it consumes OEM connected-car APIs for mileage, but it publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no reference documentation, no OpenAPI, no Postman collection and no webhook catalogue. The only integration surface is a partnerships email address and a private AWS API Gateway host serving its own mobile app, so this record is a partner-gated stub by design.
b.name: By Miles

The Bytewax Platform layers a self-hostable Kubernetes-based control plane on top, managed with the waxctl CLI and Helm chart, with deployment targets that include AWS, GCP, and the AWS Marketplace.

b.description: Bytez is a unified, serverless model-inference API that gives developers access to 100,000+ open-source and closed-source AI models (from OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Mistral, and the open-source community) through a single API key and one consistent endpoint shape. It covers 30+ task types across text, vision, audio, multimodal, and generation - including chat, embeddings, transcription, image and video generation, translation, and object detection - and offers OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Completions, and Responses endpoints plus a LangChain integration. The platform connected small and medium retailers in the United States and other markets with curated suppliers and manufacturers in India and Southeast Asia, listing thousands of products across home, lifestyle, accessories, apparel, jewelry, cookware, and bakeware verticals, and layering sourcing services such as vendor management, quality control, consolidated logistics, and cross-border payments on top of the catalog. c.description: c/side (cside) is a client-side security platform that detects script attacks, AI agents, account takeover, and fraud at the browser layer. It provides active runtime detection that watches what third-party scripts, users, and agents actually do as they execute in the live browser session, in real time, rather than relying on static scans or block-lists, and it automates PCI DSS 4.0.1 requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 (validated by a VikingCloud QSA). cside deploys as a single JavaScript snippet with no proxy and no DNS changes, and was the first client-side security product with integrated AI analysis. The platform protects websites from malicious third-party scripts, e-skimming, Magecart, and supply chain attacks, and adds device fingerprinting (102+ signals), VPN/bot/AI-agent detection, chargeback evidence, and privacy monitoring for GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA. Founded in 2024 and backed by Uncork Capital, cside integrates via a CLI, Next.js and Vite plugins, a manual script tag, and Salesforce Lightning, and sends security alerts through webhook, S3, and Jira/Linear notification endpoints. cside publishes an llms.txt, a public read-only MCP server, and a Trust Center covering SOC 2 Type II, PCI SAQ-D, and ISO 27001.
c.name: c/side

The ConductorOne platform API is an OAuth2 (client-credentials) HTTP API for managing apps, entitlements, grants, users, access-request tasks, request catalogs, policies, and webhooks, with Go/TypeScript/Python SDKs, the cone and baton CLIs, the open-source Baton connector framework, and a hosted MCP control plane for governed agent access.

It provides information for patients, healthcare providers, investors, and partners through its corporate website and investor relations portal.

c.description: C6 Bank is a Brazilian digital bank offering a full suite of financial products including checking accounts, credit cards, loans, investments, and international banking, all accessible via a mobile app. It emphasizes innovative features such as C6 Carbon, C6 Graphene, and AI-powered assistance, targeting both individuals and businesses with competitive rewards and low fees.
c.name: C6 Bank

c.description: Cerberus Tech, Inc. (C7 Security) is a Central Asian cybersecurity firm combining practical offensive security with research-backed methodology. Its flagship product, Cerberus, is an IDE and programming language purpose-built for ethical hackers to run faster penetration-testing assessments. Services span security assessment (penetration testing, audits, red teaming), secure development (code, design, and architecture reviews), OSINT reconnaissance, R&D grounded in type theory, and consulting. The company also runs C7 Academy, an elite penetration-testing training program, alongside free education and community initiatives. It reports 150+ security audits with a 95%+ penetration rate and 300+ students trained. Backed by 500 Global; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.
c.name: C7 Security

c.description: CA Technologies (originally Computer Associates) was a major enterprise software vendor focused on infrastructure management, DevOps, security, and mainframe software. It was acquired by Broadcom in November 2018 and its products are now part of Broadcom's Enterprise Software Division, including Layer 7 API Management, AppDynamics (later spun out to Cisco), DX Application Performance Management, Rally / Agile Central, Clarity PPM, BlazeMeter, AutoSys workload automation, and mainframe management suites. The primary developer portal is developer.broadcom.com.
c.name: CA Technologies (Broadcom)

c.description: CAA Insurance Company is a Canadian property and casualty carrier that began underwriting in 1974 and is part of CAA Club Group, the CAA South Central Ontario federation, with its head office at 60 Commerce Valley Drive East in Thornhill, Ontario. It underwrites personal-lines auto insurance (including accident benefits, the CAA MyPace pay-as-you-drive product, CAA Connect telematics, and antique and classic vehicle coverage) and personal property insurance (homeowners, condominium, and tenant), plus optional endorsements such as tire coverage, home equipment breakdown, service line, renewable energy equipment, and legal expense coverage. It sells in British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island through a direct-to-consumer channel and through independent brokers. Its API posture is honestly none: as of the July 2026 review there is no public developer portal, no self-serve API program, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no published event or webhook catalog. Every developer-style host and path probed (developer/developers/docs/api subdomains, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners, /integrations on both caainsurancecompany.com and caainsurancecompany.ca) either failed DNS or returned 404. The only integration surface is the CAA Broker Portal at caabrokerportal.ca, which is a Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM) WS-Federation login wall in front of a SharePoint broker workspace, and the broker program microsite at broker.caainsurance.com, which is marketing and business-development content only. The one machine-readable contract anywhere in the estate is platform-provided rather than authored by CAA: the broker portal runs Microsoft SharePoint 16.0.0.5552 and serves twenty SOAP WSDL documents (199 operations, none of them insurance operations) anonymously at /_vti_bin/<service>.asmx?WSDL, with its REST/OData sibling at /_api/web returning 403 to anonymous callers; the CAA Club Group Entra External ID tenant likewise serves standard OpenID Connect discovery. Consumer quoting runs through hosted web applications rather than an exposed quote API. This is a representative record of the Canadian carrier tier, where there is no open-insurance mandate — OSFI supervises prudentially, provincial regulators such as FSRA and the AMF handle market conduct, and Consumer-Driven Banking excludes insurance entirely — so carriers face no forcing function to publish anything.
c.name: CAA Insurance

c.description: CaaMTech is a pharmaceutical drug discovery company in Issaquah, Washington, founded by Dr. Andrew Chadeayne, engineering next-generation psychedelic-inspired small-molecule therapeutics for mental health conditions. It synthesizes and characterizes novel tryptamines, screens natural and synthetic compounds for safety and efficacy, publishes fundamental crystallographic and pharmacological research, and builds a patent portfolio around the results. CaaMTech operates no developer program and publishes no product API; the only machine-readable surface on caam.tech is the standard WordPress REST API that serves the company site, which does make its research updates, pages and media programmatically readable without credentials, alongside an authenticated WordPress MCP adapter endpoint.
c.name: CaaMTech

c.description: CaaStle Inc. was a New York based business-to-business "Clothing-as-a-Service" company that built white-label clothing rental, subscription and resale infrastructure for apparel retailers, operating tenant-branded storefronts and reverse-logistics for partner brands rather than selling directly to consumers. The company collapsed in 2025: its board confirmed financial distress and furloughed staff in April 2025, and it filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 20 June 2025 (case 25-11187), electing liquidation over reorganization. Founder and chief executive Christine Hunsicker resigned amid allegations of fabricated financial disclosures and later pleaded guilty to a fraud scheme prosecutors valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars. CaaStle never operated a public developer program, and the caastle.com domain has since passed out of the company's control.
c.name: CaaStle

c.description: CABA Design Co. is a direct-to-consumer home-furnishings company building the next generation of furniture brands powered by community and technology. It develops sustainable, high-quality furniture and gives customers choice through customization and modularity, selling directly through its Shopify-hosted storefront at cabadesign.co under the tagline "Your Home. Your Way." Caba was surfaced as a portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub; it publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and does not currently expose a first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile captures the identity, storefront, and domain/security posture verified during enrichment.
c.name: Caba

c.description: Cabal is an AI-powered relationship-intelligence and warm-introduction platform that turns an organization's professional relationships into warm introductions. It infers connections across millions of professional records without CSV uploads or calendar syncs, letting teams "ask who's connected to anyone." Cabal serves VC platform / deal-sourcing teams, sales organizations, and investor-relations and partnerships teams, and ships Cabal Mail for bulk personalized outreach (company updates, LP communications, strategic asks). The relationship graph is queryable through in-app chat, Claude and ChatGPT via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a Slack bot, or an API. Backed by Craft Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Cabal's public surface; the company advertises API and MCP access but does not publish a public OpenAPI spec or open developer reference (both are account-gated).
c.name: Cabal

c.description: Caban Systems is a private company listed on the Forge Global marketplace, offering a platform for trading private company shares. The company appears as a tradable entity within Forge’s secondary market, providing liquidity solutions, IPO insights, and investment opportunities for accredited investors and institutions. While no dedicated corporate website is identified, its presence on Forge includes detailed company information, market data, and access to private market tools.
c.name: Caban Systems

c.description: Cabana Pools is a California pool-service company providing recurring maintenance, repair, and equipment installation for residential swimming pools across San Diego, Los Angeles, Orange County, and Sacramento. Services include weekly cleaning, filter maintenance, chemical balancing, algae removal, and repair of pumps, heaters, filters, and automation systems, delivered by CPO-certified technicians with photo documentation and chemical reports after each visit. The company offers an instant online pricing quote tool. No public API or developer surface is currently published; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead.
c.name: Cabana

c.description: Caban Systems designs and manufactures software-enabled modular lithium‑ion energy storage solutions for off‑grid and weak‑grid telecom sites. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Burlingame, CA, the company operates in the software, artificial intelligence, and data analytics industries, offering modular battery systems to improve reliability of telecom infrastructure.
c.name: Cabansystems

c.description: Cabela's is a specialty retailer of hunting, fishing, camping, and outdoor recreation merchandise, operating retail stores and an e-commerce platform. Cabela's is a subsidiary of Bass Pro Shops following the 2017 acquisition, and continues to operate under its own brand with retail locations and a consumer-facing web storefront.
c.name: Cabela's

c.description: Cabify is a Spanish multi-mobility company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Madrid, operating ride-hailing, corporate mobility, and last-mile logistics across Spain and Latin America (6+ countries and 40+ cities). Its public developer platform exposes two authenticated REST APIs: a Ride-Hailing API (v4) for price estimation, journey booking, real-time state tracking, rider and label management, and sales reporting; and a Logistics API (v1) for creating, shipping, tracking, and configuring proof of delivery for parcels, including ecommerce integrations with Shopify, Tiendanube, and VTEX. Both APIs authenticate with OAuth2 client-credentials access tokens (Bearer), publish independent sandbox environments, and deliver asynchronous updates via webhooks.
c.name: Cabify

c.description: Cabinet is a calendar management and scheduling automation platform built for executive assistants and the leaders they support. It brings group scheduling polls, copy-and-paste availability, unique booking links, shadow holds, and a shared meeting log into one all-in-one workspace, and integrates with Outlook and Google Calendar plus Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. Trusted by over 2,000 companies, Cabinet is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and continuously monitored by Secureframe. It was founded by former executive assistant Julia Leibowitz and is backed by Techstars.
c.name: Cabinet

c.description: Cabinet Health is an end-to-end supply chain platform for private-label over-the-counter (OTC) medicines. The company develops, sources, manufactures, and delivers OTC products across 70+ active ingredients in tablet, softgel, capsule, liquid, powder, gummy, and chewable formats to retailers, wholesalers, and online marketplaces, emphasizing sustainable, refillable packaging and quality assurance at scale. Cabinet also produces its own certified B Corp consumer brand sold on Amazon and Target. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer or API surface has been found for this provider.
c.name: Cabinet Health

c.description: Cable is an automated compliance and financial-crime assurance platform for banks, fintechs, and crypto companies. Based on transaction, customer, screening, risk-assessment, and onboarding data you send it, Cable continuously tests 100% of activity against your regulatory frameworks (US Bank Secrecy Act, UK Money Laundering Regulations, Reg E/B/Z, UDAAP, and others) to detect any single instance of control failure or regulatory breach, replacing manual dip-sampling. The Cable API is primarily a data-ingestion surface: a REST entry point for transferring raw data from your systems into Cable's analysis environment, with resource-oriented URLs, JSON request/response bodies, token-based authentication, and standard HTTP verbs and status codes. Cable is backed by Anthemis and CRV.
c.name: Cable

c.description: An agent-native, pay-per-call MCP resource server exposing 168 TensorFlow.js machine-learning analytics tools (image classification, object detection, NLP, forecasting, and social-media analytics for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitter/X, Facebook, Discord, and Twitch). Each tool call is monetized via the x402 payment protocol at $0.05 per call, settled in USDC on Solana devnet. Unpaid requests receive an HTTP 402 challenge.
c.name: Cables

c.description: Cabletron Systems, Inc. was an American manufacturer of networking and network-management equipment, founded in 1983 by Craig Benson and Robert Levine and headquartered in Rochester, New Hampshire. It rose to prominence in the 10BASE5 and Ethernet switching markets, shipped the ST-500 transceiver and the LAN-MD field test set, built the SPECTRUM network-management platform, and passed one billion US dollars in annual sales in 1996 at a peak of roughly 6,600 employees. In 2000 the company announced a split into four businesses: Enterasys Networks (enterprise switching), Riverstone Networks (metro service provider), Aprisma Management Technologies (SPECTRUM software), and GlobalNetwork Technology Services. The Cabletron holding company merged into Enterasys, which went public in 2001, was taken private by The Gores Group in 2006, and was acquired by Extreme Networks in 2013. Riverstone was acquired by Lucent and later liquidated. Cabletron Systems no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, or documentation: the cabletron.com and enterasys.com domains both redirect to extremenetworks.com. This record is retained as a historical company profile only.
c.name: Cabletron Systems

c.description: Cablevision Systems was a U.S. cable television company that provided telecommunications and television services (Optimum TV, Optimum Online, Optimum Voice) in the New York metropolitan area. It was acquired by Altice in 2016 and now operates as part of Altice USA under the Optimum consumer brand.
c.name: Cablevision Systems

c.description: CaboLabs Health Informatics is a Montevideo, Uruguay based health informatics company founded in 2012 by Pablo Pazos Gutierrez, specializing in clinical data standards and interoperability. It builds and licenses Atomik, a standardized openEHR Clinical Data Repository and Demographic Data Repository that implements the openEHR ITS REST API Release 1.0.2 over a JWT-authenticated JSON API, and maintains a family of Apache-2.0 open source openEHR tooling including the EHRServer clinical data repository, the openEHR-SDK for JVM languages, the openEHR-CLI, an openEHR conformance verification framework, and the openEHR Toolkit. Alongside the software it delivers consultancy, audit and training services covering openEHR, HL7 FHIR, HL7 v2.x, CDA, DICOM and SNOMED CT for hospitals, health-tech startups and software vendors worldwide.
c.name: CaboLabs

c.description: Cabot Corporation is a global specialty chemicals and performance materials company serving the transportation, infrastructure, environment, and consumer industries. The company's products include reinforcing carbons, specialty carbons, fumed silica, inkjet colorants, and engineered elastomer composites.
c.name: Cabot

c.description: Cabot Oil & Gas was an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploitation, exploration, production, and marketing of natural gas and oil properties in the United States. In 2021 it merged with Cimarex Energy to form Coterra Energy, which operates across the Permian Basin, Marcellus Shale, and Anadarko Basin.
c.name: Cabot Oil & Gas

c.description: CABRA Sports is a Latino-focused sports fandom platform based in Los Angeles. It aims to capture the true nature of Latino sports fandom by putting fans at the center, offering a vibrant community where culture and sports intersect. The company provides a digital space for fans to engage, share content, and experience sports with a unique cultural flavor.
c.name: CABRA Sports

c.description: Cache provides tax-efficient solutions for diversifying concentrated stock positions, offering exchange funds, long‑short strategies, and collar‑advance financing. It serves individual investors and advisors, delivering tools to manage large stock holdings, reduce tax drag, and access institutional‑grade strategies through a modern digital platform.
c.name: Cache

c.description: Cacheflow was a B2B SaaS billing, CPQ (configure-price-quote), and subscription-management platform that let software companies build interactive deal rooms, automate quote-to-cash, and offer buyers flexible payment and financing options. Founded in 2020 and backed by GGV Capital and GV, Cacheflow was acquired by HubSpot in 2024 and folded into HubSpot Commerce / HubSpot CPQ. The company shipped a substantial REST API — 305 paths and 400 operations across proposals, products, customers, subscriptions, billing schedules, usage, invoices, payments, refunds, approvals, e-signature and CRM/accounting integrations — and that contract is still publicly published: developer.getcacheflow.com serves a live ReadMe developer portal with an llms.txt and an OpenAPI 3.0.1 definition. The runtime is gone. As of 2026-08-13 api.getcacheflow.com, api.sandbox.getcacheflow.com, checkout, status and help all return NXDOMAIN, and getcacheflow.com 301-redirects to HubSpot's Commerce CPQ page. This profile therefore records a rare shape: a fully published, machine-readable API contract that outlived the API it described.
c.name: Cacheflow

c.description: Cachet OÜ is an Estonian InsurTech that provides adaptive, usage-based insurance for digital platforms and their users across new mobility, gig work, and car-sharing. Digital platforms integrate Cachet through three inbound event APIs: the Parking API (car-sharing fleets stream vehicle events so Cachet manages parking), the Verify / Platform API (gig-work platforms register workers and push task events to drive worker protection), and the Partners API (embed a prefilled Cachet onboarding link into a partner app). All three are OpenAPI 3.1 and authenticated with issued x-api-key and x-api-username headers. Cachet is backed by Techstars; notable platform clients include Bolt, Bird, Ryde, and TaskRabbit.
c.name: Cachet

c.description: CACI International provides information technology, professional services, and managed solutions to U.S. federal government agencies in the defense, intelligence, homeland security, and civilian markets. The company delivers expertise and technology across C3I, cyber, digital solutions, enterprise IT, mission support, space, and spectrum superiority domains.
c.name: CACI International

c.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.
c.name: Cactos

c.description: Cactosaa16, operating as Cactos, is a Finnish startup delivering smart battery energy storage systems for commercial and grid‑scale applications. Their platform optimises energy use, shifts consumption to low‑price periods, and enables participation in electricity markets, helping customers reduce costs and increase resilience.
c.name: Cactosaa16

c.description: CAD Solutions, Inc. is a historical Battery Ventures portfolio company that appears in the firm's all-companies list. Research during the API Evangelist enrichment pass found no operating business, no developer surface, and no live web presence behind the name - public records indicate the company was acquired by microCAD Solutions on 1995-05-29, and the closest matching domain, cadsolutions.com, now resolves to a GoDaddy parked "for sale" page rather than a company site. The many unrelated "CAD Solutions" businesses currently trading under similar names (CAD Solutions LLC, CAD Solutions Inc of Dassault partner fame, CADD Solutions, CAD-E Solutions) are separate entities and are not this Battery portfolio record. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead with no API surface to catalog.
c.name: CAD Solutions

c.description: Cadana is a white-label global payment and payroll infrastructure provider for talent platforms, staffing companies, and HR providers. Its APIs let partners onboard and pay employees and contractors in 100+ countries, run multi-currency payroll, provision embedded wallets and virtual accounts, calculate gross-to-net tax across 150+ jurisdictions, and automate statutory filing and government remittance. The platform is delivered as five REST APIs (Workforce Management, Embedded Payments, Embedded Consumer Wallets, Global Tax Engine, and Statutory Compliance) with bearer-token auth, Svix-signed webhooks, a sandbox, and an embeddable white-label UI and salary-calculator widget. Backed by 500 Global.
c.name: Cadana

c.description: Cadasto B.V. is a Dutch health-IT company (Alkmaar, Netherlands) that builds a vendor-neutral Clinical Data Repository on the openEHR standard. The Cadasto CDR stores structured care data as openEHR compositions and exposes the openEHR ITS-REST 1.0.3 API surface — EHR, Query (AQL), Definition, Demographic, Admin and System — plus a Cadasto-specific Additional API for Datamap (a simplified JSON projection of openEHR paths), episodes of care and terminology helpers, a bidirectional FHIR R3 facade, and SMART-on-openEHR app launch. Access is OAuth 2.0 client-credentials per tenant. Cadasto also publishes an unusually strong agent surface for its size: a live anonymous MCP server for openEHR modelling knowledge, eight packaged Agent Skills, a Claude Code plugin marketplace, an llms.txt, and a public openEHR conformance statement naming every specification version it does and does not implement.
c.name: Cadasto

c.description: CADDi is a Tokyo-headquartered manufacturing-technology company that builds an AI Data Platform for industrial manufacturers. Its two products, CADDi Drawer and CADDi Quote, aggregate scattered 2D engineering drawings and supply-chain data into a single searchable asset, offering keyword and drawing-similarity search, automatic extraction of dimensions, text and shapes, and AI-assisted quotation and sourcing. The platform serves procurement, engineering, sales, production, quality, and leadership teams across automotive, robotics, and precision-machinery sectors, and connects to ERP, CAM, CAD, and quality systems via batch and CSV imports. CADDi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK.
c.name: CADDi

c.description: Caddy is a modern, extensible, open-source web server and reverse proxy written in Go that provides automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt, a dynamic JSON-based admin API, a human-friendly Caddyfile configuration format, and a modular architecture with a rich ecosystem of plugins for authentication, observability, and custom behavior.
c.name: Caddy

c.description: Cadea AI is a company identified in the API Evangelist harvest backlog as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. It appears to be associated with financial data services, as indicated by its listing on Forge Global. However, no dedicated corporate website could be located, and attempts to resolve a primary domain (cadea.ai) resulted in a 503 error. The available information suggests the company may operate primarily through market listings rather than a public-facing web presence.
c.name: Cadea AI

c.description: Cadee is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Cadee

c.description: Cadena8ba7 is a stub entry created during the API Evangelist harvest process. The company appears in secondary-market listings but limited public information is available. This placeholder entry enables the profiling pipeline to collect and enrich data about Cadena8ba7 as more resources become discoverable. The entry will be updated with a detailed description, official website, and relevant metadata once verifiable sources are identified.
c.name: Cadena8ba7

c.description: Cadence Bank is a regional U.S. commercial bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi and Houston, Texas, formed in October 2021 when legacy Cadence Bancorporation merged into BancorpSouth Bank (the surviving entity, subsequently renamed Cadence Bank; NYSE ticker CADE). It is a Mississippi state-chartered bank operating roughly 400+ branches across the U.S. South, Midwest, and Texas with about $48-50 billion in assets, offering consumer banking, mortgages, home equity, credit cards, small business and commercial banking, treasury management, and wealth/insurance services. On open finance, Cadence Bank exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), which is the honest, prevailing posture for most U.S. regional banks. No documented direct FDX (Financial Data Exchange) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access API was found as of this profile.
c.name: Cadence Bank

c.description: Cadence Design Systems is a multinational electronic design automation (EDA) software and hardware company. Cadence provides tools for designing integrated circuits, systems on chips, printed circuit boards, and pharmaceutical drugs, with a portfolio that includes Virtuoso, Spectre, Genus, Innovus, JasperGold, Xcelium, Palladium, Allegro, OrCAD, and AI tools such as Cerebrus and ChipGPT.
c.name: Cadence Design Systems

c.description: Cadence Neuroscience, Inc. is a clinical-stage medical device company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, developing a personalized neuromodulation system for pediatric and adult patients with focal drug-resistant epilepsy. Its implantable system, licensed from Mayo Clinic and incubated by a Mayo Clinic Rochester neurology and neurosurgery team, delivers chronic subthreshold cortical stimulation and detects EEG biomarkers of epileptiform activity in order to reduce or eliminate seizures. The company raised a $15M Series A in 2019 and a $26M Series B in 2023 led by the Angelini Lumira Biosciences Fund, with participation from F-Prime Capital, LivaNova USA, Angelini Ventures, Spectrum Financial Services and Mayo Clinic, and is using the proceeds to complete pivotal clinical studies and pursue FDA clearance. It is a regulated medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.
c.name: Cadence Neuroscience

c.description: Cadence Solutions, Inc. — operating as Cadence — is a New York-based clinical AI and remote patient monitoring company founded in 2020 by Chris Altchek. Cadence partners with large health systems and payers to deliver continuous chronic-care management between clinic visits: FDA-cleared connected devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, weight scales) stream daily vitals to a 24/7 clinical care team backed by supervised AI agents that flag out-of-range readings, close care gaps, and escalate to clinicians for medication titration. The platform covers hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and COPD, is integrated two-way into partner EHRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth), and supports Medicare RPM/CCM and the CMS ACCESS model. Cadence serves more than 100,000 patients across systems including Community Health Systems, LifePoint Health, Providence, Rush, MemorialCare, Corewell Health, Ardent Health and Duke Health. It raised a $100M Series C led by Spark Capital in June 2026 ($241M total, ~$1.23B valuation). Cadence publishes no public developer program or API: EHR interoperability is delivered as bilateral health system integrations, not a self-serve API surface.
c.name: Cadence Solutions

c.description: Cadent Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel therapies for neuropsychiatric disorders, particularly schizophrenia. Founded in 2020, the company aims to leverage cutting‑edge neuroscience and clinical research to address unmet medical needs. It was acquired by Novartis in 2021, integrating its pipeline into Novartis’s broader neuroscience portfolio. While its original website is no longer active, the company’s activities are documented through press releases, regulatory filings, and third‑party industry profiles.
c.name: Cadent Therapeutics

c.description: Cado Gifts, Inc. (CADO Gifting) is a luxury and corporate gifting company operating a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at cadogifting.com, serving the UAE and international markets with curated executive, host, and occasion gift collections plus a corporate/bulk gifting program. The business runs on Shopify (customer accounts, checkout, and blog/journal content) rather than a first-party public API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No developer program, OpenAPI, or public API documentation is published; the only machine surface discovered is Shopify's Customer Account OIDC/OAuth well-known documents served under the store's own host.
c.name: Cado Gifts

c.description: Cadre is a New York-based, technology-driven investment platform that gives individual and institutional investors access to private-market alternatives, historically centered on institutional-quality commercial real estate. Founded in 2014 and backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive Capital, and Slow Ventures, Cadre now operates in partnership with Willow Wealth (Willow Wealth Markets LLC, a FINRA/SIPC broker-dealer formerly known as RealCadre LLC, and Willow Asset Management LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser) to offer diversified private-market funds alongside traditional stocks and bonds. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Cadre does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.
c.name: Cadre

c.description: Caer, Inc. is the company behind YUMI (helloyumi.com), a direct-to-consumer children's nutrition brand that makes nutritionally-engineered organic snacks for babies, toddlers, and kids. The product line includes toddler bars, squeezable smoothies-to-go, freeze-dried smoothie melts, super/breakfast bars, and soft-baked cookies, all formulated as function-first, nutrient-dense, organic, dairy-free, gluten-free, and clean-label. YUMI sells through its own WooCommerce storefront, Amazon, and select retail, offering one-time purchases and recurring subscription memberships. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was seeded as a venture-portfolio stub; it is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no first-party public developer API, so most API-artifact scoring dimensions are not applicable.
c.name: Caer

c.description: Caesars Entertainment is the largest U.S. casino-entertainment company, operating over 50 gaming facilities, hotels, restaurants, and entertainment venues across the country and internationally. The company operates the Caesars Rewards loyalty program and offers gaming, hospitality, dining, entertainment, meetings and conventions, and retail experiences.
c.name: Caesars Entertainment

c.description: CafeX Communications, Inc. is a US-headquartered software company (founded 2013) that builds a low-code platform for developing intelligent applications and agentic systems for regulated industries — banking, insurance, healthcare and government. The current CafeX AI platform is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS at app.cafex.com and is organised into App Studio (App Builder, Flow Builder, Rule Builder, Data Tables and API Lab), Data Studio (Data AI, Data Gateway, Data Visualizer) and Agent Studio (Agent Builder, LM Insights). CafeX began life as a WebRTC and embedded-communications vendor (Fusion Client, Live Assist, CafeX Meetings, later the Challo collaboration workspace) and has since repositioned around AI workflow and process automation. Its one publicly documented, publicly callable API is the CafeX Audit Events API, a tenant-scoped REST search endpoint for audit event data secured with OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
c.name: CafeX Communications

c.description: Cafextechnologies is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Cafextechnologies

c.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.
c.name: Caffeine

c.description: Cage Bio Inc. is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company developing localized therapies for dermatology, inflammation, and immunology using its proprietary deep eutectic ionic liquid platform. The company aims to provide high‑efficacy, skin‑targeted treatments that reduce systemic exposure while maintaining therapeutic potency.
c.name: Cage Bio

c.description: Cagent Vascular is a privately held endovascular medical device company based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, that develops and commercializes Serration Remodeling Therapy (SRT). Its flagship product, the Serranator PTA Serration Balloon Catheter, embeds stainless-steel serrated strips into a semi-compliant angioplasty balloon to create linear, interrupted micro-fissures along the artery wall, producing controlled lumen expansion at lower pressures when treating peripheral artery disease (PAD) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). The Serranator is FDA 510(k) cleared and CE marked, and the portfolio has expanded to include Serranator SL-PRO and the Serranator SONIC intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) system. Cagent Vascular is a device manufacturer rather than a software or platform company: it publishes clinical data, case studies, webinars and reimbursement material on its website, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

c.description: Caidya is a full-service, global clinical research organization (CRO) formed from the April 2021 merger of dMed and Clinipace, rebranded to Caidya in October 2022. It runs clinical development programs end to end — pre-IND and regulatory strategy, early phase, Phase II/III delivery, study start-up, trial feasibility, clinical operations, risk-based quality management, medical monitoring, clinical data management, biometrics, medical writing, pharmacovigilance, quality assurance and post-marketing surveillance — across oncology and hematology, cardiovascular-metabolic, rare disease, pediatrics, gastroenterology, nephrology, dermatology, ophthalmology, cell and gene therapy, neurology, immunology and infectious disease. The company took a $165M strategic growth investment from Rubicon Founders and announced a strategic combination with Simbec-Orion. It provides end‑to‑end supply chain services, including domestic and international warehousing, parcel delivery, cross‑border logistics, and smart infrastructure. Leveraging AI, IoT, and a massive network of warehouses and sorting centers across over 200 countries, Cainiao enables merchants to ship efficiently worldwide, offering solutions such as same‑day delivery, automated customs clearance, and a digital parcel tracking ecosystem.
c.name: Cainiao

c.description: Caira Surgical is a pioneering medical technology company focused on advanced joint replacement software, scanning, and precision radar technologies. Their mission is to deliver sub-millimeter precision, intuitive workflows, and affordable solutions for surgeons worldwide. The team comprises experienced surgeons and engineers developing navigation systems for knee replacement, protected by multiple US patents. Caira aims to improve patient outcomes through innovative, reliable, and globally accessible surgical tools.
c.name: Caira Surgical

c.description: CAIS (Capital Integration Systems LLC) is a New York-headquartered fintech company operating the leading alternative investment platform for independent wealth management. Founded in 2009 by Matt Brown, CAIS connects financial advisors with a curated menu of private equity, private credit, hedge fund, real estate, infrastructure, structured note and precious metals strategies from third-party asset managers and bank issuers, and pairs the marketplace with CAIS Solutions (a SaaS trade and post-trade operating layer for RIAs, aggregators and independent broker-dealers), CAIS IQ (advisor education), Compass (portfolio construction) and CAISey (an AI assistant). The platform serves 2,500+ wealth management firms and 65,000+ advisors overseeing roughly $8.5 trillion in end-client assets, with technology integrations into major custodians (Fidelity, BNY Pershing, Schwab Advisor Services, Goldman Sachs Custody Solutions), reporting providers (Addepar, Black Diamond, Envestnet, Orion, Tamarac) and 30+ fund administrators, plus DTCC AIP reporting. In May 2026 CAIS launched a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as part of its "Alts Engine" strategy, exposing fund, holdings, education and identity data to AI agents over OAuth 2.1.
c.name: CAIS

c.description: Cajal Neuroscience, which now operates publicly as Cajal Therapeutics, is a Seattle, Washington biotechnology company founded in 2020 by Alex Vaughan, Andrew Dervan and Ian Peikon, and launched in November 2022 with a $96 million Series A led by The Column Group and Lux Capital with participation from Two Sigma Ventures and Bristol Myers Squibb. The company develops small-molecule and RNA medicines that restore iron homeostasis, built around "iron mobilizers" — small molecules that transport iron across membranes into the compartments where it is required, bypassing disease-driven bottlenecks such as chronic inflammation, altered iron transporter expression and lysosomal dysfunction. Its pipeline spans systemic disease (CTX001, a clinical-stage iron mobilizer for anemia of chronic kidney disease; CTX201 and CTX211, preclinical siRNA programs for inflammatory anemia and myelofibrosis anemia) and CNS disease (a discovery-stage brain-penetrant iron mobilizer for Parkinson's disease). This is a therapeutics company, not a software or data platform company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. Its public GitHub organization contains open-source laboratory hardware and firmware (a drone-motor spin coater, a microfluidic pressure sensor, a flow sensor) plus forks of third-party single-cell and genomics analysis tooling — none of which expose a network API.
c.name: Cajal Neuroscience

c.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.
