c.description: Capchase provides embedded financing and B2B payment infrastructure for software and hardware vendors. Its Capchase Pay API lets vendors offer buyers flexible installment payment terms at checkout while the vendor is paid the full contract value upfront. Vendors create buyer companies, run automated KYB/underwriting qualification, create subscriptions that generate hosted payment links, list and retrieve subscription status, and pull instalment receipts. The v2 REST API is served from universe.capchase.com, uses HTTP Basic authentication (clientId / clientSecret), ships a Playground environment, and is documented on a ReadMe developer portal with an OpenAPI reference and an AI-agent llms.txt index. Sector: fintech; backed by QED Investors.
c.name: Capchase

c.description: Capcon2be2 is a stub entry discovered in the secondary-market harvest. No public website or API documentation could be located despite searches of equityzen.com, Google, and DuckDuckGo. The company appears to have no publicly accessible domain, and its online presence is limited to a listing on equityzen.com which returns a 403 error. Consequently, detailed information about its services, products, or API offerings is unavailable at this time.
c.name: Capcon2be2

c.description: CapConnect+ provides a digital platform that simplifies fixed income primary market issuance, connecting corporate issuers, dealers, and investors. The solution offers live book building, pricing optimization, and automated investor management, aiming to lower funding costs and increase transparency in bond and commercial paper issuance.
c.name: CapConnect

c.description: Cape is a privacy-first U.S. mobile carrier (mobile virtual network operator) that leases physical tower capacity from major operators but builds and runs its own mobile core and SIMs, enabling privacy-enhancing controls that traditional carriers cannot offer. Features include daily identifier rotation (changing SIM ID numbers to disrupt persistent tracking), minimal data collection, disappearing call logs, secondary phone numbers, SIM-swap protection, network lock, and secure global roaming. Founded in 2022 by John Doyle and Nicholas Espinoza and headquartered in Arlington, Cape serves privacy-conscious consumers, enterprises, and U.S. government agencies, and has raised roughly $190M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Bain Capital Ventures, IVP, and Costanoa Ventures. Cape publishes no public developer API; this profile is an API Evangelist network company record enriched from Cape's public web surface.
c.name: Cape

c.description: Cape Analytics (now part of Moody's) is a geospatial property intelligence provider that applies computer vision and machine learning to high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other novel data sources to produce inspection-quality condition and characteristic data for over 100 million residential and commercial structures across the United States and Canada. Its insights — roof condition and material, swimming pools, solar panels, accessory structures, tree overhang, wildfire and wind exposure, distance to hazards, and a proprietary Liquidity Score — are delivered to insurance underwriters, lenders, and real estate investors in under two seconds via API, batch/bulk files, an Automated Property Condition Report (aPCR), and a customer web portal, as well as through third-party platforms such as Guidewire and Duck Creek. Cape does not publish a public, self-service developer portal or open API specification; API access is provisioned to customers and partners through a gated onboarding flow.
c.name: Cape Analytics

c.description: Cape Partners is an independent M&A advisory firm focused on technology, based in Le Chesnay, France (Cape Partners SAS, SIREN 833 208 960). It operates a deal-flow platform ("Sniffer") that sources and enriches European software companies, matches sellers to strategic and financial buyers with a deterministic-times-semantic fit score, produces preliminary valuations, and lets both sides manage pairings and deal phases in a session-scoped workspace. The platform is agent-first: an OpenAPI 3.1 contract at /openapi.json, a JSON capability index at /api, llms.txt, an AI-plugin discovery manifest, and an A2A 1.0 Agent Card whose SendMessage / GetTask / ListTasks operations are served live at /a2a. External agents take part through an "agent exchange" — publish a six-field manifest with no account or key, then poll for a grounded answer; a workspace UUID is issued only after a human-reviewed handshake, and the Terms of Service are signed by a human principal.
c.name: Cape Partners

c.description: Capella Space operates a constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites and provides on-demand, high-resolution Earth-observation imagery through a self-service Console and public API. Customers can task the constellation with 15-minute scheduling cycles, search a STAC-based catalog of archive collects, place orders, and download imagery products for defense, intelligence, maritime, energy, insurance, and analytics use cases.
c.name: Capella Space

c.description: Capella University is an accredited online university owned by Strategic Education, Inc. (SEI), offering competency-based bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees plus graduate certificates across business, counseling and therapy, education, health sciences, information technology, nursing, psychology, and social work. Capella is regionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and delivers coursework through two learning formats — FlexPath, a self-paced competency-based model, and GuidedPath, a structured-timeline model — serving working adults and professional learners entirely online.
c.name: Capella University

c.description: Caper (caper.ai) is a New York-founded computer-vision company that builds AI-powered smart shopping carts and cashierless checkout technology for grocery and retail. Its Caper Cart uses a set of onboard cameras and deep-learning object recognition, running on NVIDIA Jetson edge AI, to auto-detect items as shoppers add them and let customers skip the checkout line. Founded in 2016 (Y Combinator) by Lindon Gao and team, Caper was acquired by Instacart in 2021 for roughly $350M and now operates as part of the Instacart Enterprise Platform (Connected Stores), deployed with retailers including ALDI and Coles. Caper ships retail hardware and an internal edge/vision platform; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal.
c.name: Caper

c.description: Malware execution and analysis
c.name: CAPEsandbox

c.description: Capgridsolutions (CapGrid) is a tech‑enabled design‑to‑deliver company offering precision parts and components through cloud manufacturing, dynamic fulfilment and quality assurance. It provides end‑to‑end supply‑chain visibility, traceability and sourcing services across automotive, EV, agri‑equipment and more, serving over 25 customers and 400 suppliers worldwide.
c.name: Capgridsolutions

c.description: Capi Money is a cross-border payments fintech that lets businesses pay their suppliers in more than 30 currencies, targeting importers in Africa and other emerging markets who have historically faced high fees and multi-week settlement times on international invoices. Founded in 2023 by Mitch Riley and Scott Liddle and headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company offers instant FX rate quotes, settlement within 24 hours, real-time payment tracking, and holds customer funds with licensed financial institutions. Capi is a Y Combinator company backed by Creandum, Firstminute Capital, and Raba, having raised roughly EUR 17.2 million in Series A funding. The product is delivered through a web application (app.capimoney.com) and an FX Partner Program; there is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal published at this time.
c.name: Capi Money

c.description: Capillary Technologies provides enterprise loyalty management software, enabling brands to engage customers through personalized rewards, campaigns, and analytics. The platform offers tools for omnichannel loyalty, AI-driven insights, and integration with e‑commerce and CRM systems, serving global enterprises across retail, travel, and finance sectors.
c.name: Capillary Technologies

c.description: Capillary Technologies is a multinational SaaS company providing AI‑based cloud‑native loyalty management and customer data platforms. Founded in 2012, it serves over 390 brands across 46 countries, helping enterprises boost retention, engagement and revenue through its Intelligent Loyalty solution. The platform offers omnichannel loyalty programs, real‑time analytics and personalized customer experiences, positioning the company as a leader in enterprise loyalty technology.
c.name: Capillarytechnologiespvt

c.description: Capim is a Sao Paulo-based vertical SaaS and fintech company for the dental sector in Brazil, founded in 2021 by Marcelo Lutz and Roberto Biselli. Its platform pairs dental-clinic management software - appointment scheduling (Agenda Capim), digital patient records, and AI-driven patient reactivation - with embedded financial products: buy-now-pay-later patient financing (Financiamento Capim, up to 36 installments), direct-credit collections (Carne Capim), and an integrated card/PIX payment terminal (Maquininha Capim). Capim serves more than 6,000 dental clinics, has issued over R$450 million in credit, and raised a US$26.7M Series A co-led by Valor Capital and QED Investors. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published.
c.name: Capim

c.description: Capitainer provides microsampling solutions for laboratory and biotechnology applications. Their product portfolio includes the Capitainer®B10, B50, B10Vanadate, SEP10, DIP70 instruments, accessories, and lab services such as sampling kit instructions and kitting support. The company focuses on enabling precise low-volume sampling for research and clinical use, offering request pricing and sample services through their website.
c.name: Capitainer

c.description: Capital Markets Gateway (CMG) is a New York headquartered financial technology company that connects the buy side and the sell side across the equity capital markets (ECM) offering process. Its two products are CMG XC, a workflow-management platform carrying the full ECM deal lifecycle — offering setup, termsheet publication, a consolidated and de-duplicated order book, bookbuilding, allocations, designations and trade release — and CMG DataLab, an ECM data and analytics service spanning 20+ years and 60,000+ equity transactions across 50+ regions, with 550+ deal, structure and performance metrics per deal. CMG names three programmatic surfaces in its own public FAQs — a DataLab Real-Time Feed (GraphQL API), a CMG XC REST API covering setup through allocation and post-trade, and EventHub real-time event notifications for straight-through processing into OMS and trade-processing systems — but publishes no public API reference, endpoint or machine-readable contract for any of them. The documentation host redirects to a customer identity login.
c.name: Capital Markets Gateway

c.description: Capital One is a US money-center bank and financial services company offering credit cards, checking and savings accounts, loans, and auto financing. Through the Capital One DevExchange developer program the bank publishes a catalog of partner-facing production APIs for account lookup, transaction authorizations, credit offers, customer transactions, credit card applications, auto financing, proactive prescreen, partner account summary, shop with rewards, and public key sharing for client authentication. Access is secured with OAuth 2.0 and a public sandbox supports pre-production integration, with production access gated behind partner approval. Developer documentation is HTML-only (the portal is a single-page app); Capital One does not publish downloadable OpenAPI specifications. As an FDX member, Capital One also supports consumer-permissioned open-finance data access through aggregators in the US voluntary open-banking context.
c.name: Capital One

c.description: Capital Requirements is a specialized technology or methodology in the capital domain that addresses specific technical or business requirements. It provides targeted capabilities that help practitioners and organizations solve problems and improve outcomes in their area of focus.
c.name: Capital Requirements

c.description: Capital.com is a European trading platform offering CFDs across shares, indices, commodities, forex, and cryptocurrencies. The Capital.com Public API provides direct access to the trading engine for automated strategies, giving programmatic control of positions, working orders, account preferences, and historical and streaming market data. A companion WebSocket API streams real-time prices and OHLC candles for up to 40 concurrent instruments.
c.name: Capital.com Public API

c.description: Capital.xyz (the company behind the former Party Round) is a startup banking and fundraising platform that helps founders raise, hold, spend, and send money in one place. Companies sign up to run fundraising rounds, receive a virtual Visa debit card once capital is raised, hold and move funds, and connect the account to fintech services such as Gusto. The product is built on embedded-finance rails (Unit, Plaid, Visa) and is a consumer/SMB-facing application; as of this enrichment pass Capital.xyz publishes no public developer program, API reference, OpenAPI, or docs portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z.
c.name: Capital.xyz

c.description: Capitalfloat, now operating as Axio, is an Indian consumer finance platform offering pay‑later, credit, and personal finance management solutions. Founded to provide flexible financing for online shoppers and small businesses, Axio has expanded into a unified financial services ecosystem, serving millions of customers across India with digital loans, budgeting tools, and merchant partnerships. The company focuses on transparent, technology‑driven credit products and aims to make credit worthy for all.
c.name: Capitalfloat

c.description: Capital IQ, part of S&P Global Market Intelligence, provides a comprehensive platform delivering essential intelligence, financial data, analytics, and research tools for professionals. The service offers deep company fundamentals, credit analytics, market insights, and specialized products such as Panjiva and Research Online, enabling informed decision‑making across industries.
c.name: Capitaliq

c.description: Capitalist is a payment platform that lets businesses make mass payouts and receive money across multiple payment systems and cryptocurrencies without having to open separate accounts with each. The Capitalist Integration API automates bulk payouts to cards, bank transfers, mobile operators, fast payment systems, e-wallets and cryptocurrencies, converts between fiat and digital-asset balances, reads exchange rates and account balances, retrieves transaction and merchant-order history, and runs end-user KYC — for fintech, affiliate-network, and marketplace use cases operating across the CIS region and globally.
c.name: Capitalist

c.description: Capitalize is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Capitalize

c.description: Capiter provides property and community management services in Spain, offering comprehensive administration of homeowners associations, real estate transactions, legal advice, tax and accounting support, and online tools for owners and tenants. With over a decade of experience, Capiter delivers transparent, integrated solutions for property owners, tenants, and investors, emphasizing professional rigor and personalized service.
c.name: Capiter

c.description: Capitolis is a financial technology company for the capital markets that helps banks and institutional investors optimize how capital is used across their trading portfolios. Its two flagship offerings are a Capital Marketplace that connects banks with origination capabilities to institutional providers of capital, and a Portfolio Optimization service that offsets redundant and offsetting derivatives positions to reduce capital requirements, counterparty exposure, and systemic risk. By combining technology with financial expertise, Capitolis aims to create a safer, more efficient financial system and broaden access to more diversified pools of capital. The platform is delivered as a secure, login-gated web application to regulated financial institutions rather than as a public developer API.
c.name: Capitolis

c.description: Capitual provides digital asset integration, liquidity, and payment infrastructure for large enterprises. It offers multi‑currency digital accounts, blockchain connectivity, and bespoke consulting to enable secure, scalable financial operations across jurisdictions. The platform supports high‑volume transactions, regulatory compliance, and custom liquidity solutions for institutional clients.
c.name: Capitual

c.description: Caplight Technologies is a San Francisco private-markets data and trading platform for institutional investors, covering 50,000+ VC-backed private companies with secondary-market pricing, a live institutional order book, trade and order history, funding rounds with valuations and participants, investor participation, SEC-derived fund marks, COI filings, stock splits, news, company signals and comparable-company indices. Its proprietary MarketPrice(TM) estimate is implied from live bids, asks and closed secondary trades. Caplight exposes the dataset through a versioned REST API (v1 and v2, api_key header auth, documented with a public OpenAPI 3.1.0 definition rendered in Redoc), a hosted OAuth-protected MCP server for Claude, and a one-line embeddable widget. Securities are offered through Caplight Markets LLC, member FINRA/SIPC.
c.name: Caplight

c.description: CapLinked is a secure virtual data room (VDR) provider used for M&A, fundraising, due diligence, audits, and other confidential document workflows. The CapLinked API is a RESTful, JSON API secured by HMAC-SHA256 request signing (TLS + signed requests) that lets developers embed CapLinked's information-security controls into their own applications: protect and encrypt files in secure cloud storage, configure Access Control List (ACL) privileges, apply enterprise Digital Rights Management (DRM) to Microsoft Office and PDF files, generate dynamic watermarks, produce exhaustive activity and audit-trail reports, and run OCR-backed search over stored files. The API models an Organization > Team > Workspace hierarchy containing Folders, Files, Groups, Permissions, Activities, Uploads, Downloads, and Watermarks, and ships official SDKs for Node.js, Ruby, PHP, C#/.NET, and Python. It supports search, pagination, and filtering.
c.name: Caplinked

c.description: CapMAC Holdings Inc. (Capital Markets Assurance Corporation) was a New York-based holding company that provided financial guaranty and surety insurance for structured securities worldwide, primarily asset-backed securities, alongside structured financial solutions, advisory and structuring services, and investment management. Founded in 1973 and headquartered at 885 Third Avenue in New York City, it was a Canaan Partners portfolio company. MBIA Inc. acquired CapMAC Holdings in a stock swap valued at more than $500 million, completing the merger on February 17, 1998, after which CapMAC operated as an indirect wholly-owned MBIA subsidiary. Capital Markets Assurance Corporation was merged into MBIA Insurance Corporation during the third quarter of 2010 and ceased to exist as a separately licensed insurer. The company is defunct and operates no website, developer program, or API surface; the capmac.com domain is an unrelated parked domain listed for sale.
c.name: CapMAC Holdings

c.description: Capmo is a Munich-based construction project management platform ("Bauprojektmanagement-Software") for the DACH market, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Its web and mobile apps cover defect and task management (tickets), site journals (Bautagebuch), plans, documents, change orders, project and organisation contact books, and reporting for construction teams. Capmo exposes a public REST API (api.capmo.de, /api/v1) documented on ReadMe, with API-key authentication, cursor pagination, a 600 requests/minute rate limit, HMAC-signed webhooks for change-order events, and downloadable OpenAPI specifications for both the REST and Webhook surfaces.
c.name: Capmo

c.description: Cappello's is a gluten‑free frozen foods company offering pizza, biscuits, pasta, breads, and cookie dough. Based in the United States, it sells its products through major retailers like Whole Foods and Sprouts, and provides an online store for direct consumer purchases. The brand emphasizes clean, allergen‑friendly ingredients and aims to bring magical, convenient meals to gluten‑free consumers worldwide.
c.name: Cappello's

c.description: Capri Holdings Limited (NYSE: CPRI) is a global luxury fashion group whose portfolio is the Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo brands (Versace was sold to Prada in 2025 and no longer appears on the company's overview). It designs, markets and sells apparel, footwear, handbags and accessories through its own stores, wholesale partners, licensees and brand e-commerce sites. Capri Holdings publishes no developer program: the corporate site at capriholdings.com is a Q4-hosted investor-relations property (news, SEC filings, governance, ESG resources, careers) with no API, documentation, SDK, package, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface, and the api.capriholdings.com and developer.capriholdings.com hosts an earlier scaffold named do not resolve in DNS. Every /.well-known/* path answers with the IR platform's 'Invalid key' catch-all rather than a document. This profile records that absence honestly; nothing has been authored on the company's behalf.
c.name: Capri Holdings

c.description: CapriCoast (CapriCoast Home Solutions Pvt Ltd) was a Bengaluru, India based online modular-furniture and modular-kitchen retailer, founded in 2014 and backed by Accel Partners and RB Investments. It offered an online 3D catalog of kitchens and wardrobes with designs pre-customized for project floor plans. The company was acquired by HomeLane in November 2017 and no longer operates independently; its domain (capricoast.com) is now parked/for-sale and it publishes no developer, API, or documentation surface. Sector: consumer. Retained in the network as an Accel portfolio record; no API artifacts are available to enrich.
c.name: CapriCoast

c.description: Capriza was an enterprise mobility software company founded in 2011 in Palo Alto, California, backed by a16z and others across roughly $73.5M in funding. Its platform took a no-code approach to mobilizing workflows from legacy enterprise applications such as SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft by driving their existing user interfaces, explicitly WITHOUT requiring APIs, new infrastructure or custom code. The company has permanently closed and never published a public API surface, so this record is retained as a historical network entry rather than an enrichable provider profile.
c.name: Capriza

c.description: CAPS Inc. (CAPS株式会社) is a Tokyo-based Healthcare x IT company founded in December 2014 whose mission is to maximize the total amount of happiness through health management (健康経営). CAPS operates a chain of primary-care clinics plus its Doctor365 telemedicine and urgent-care service, provides corporate health-support and wellness programs for employers, runs 24-hour IT-enabled fitness gyms, and delivers health-education programs including a Sesame Street partnership. Headquartered in Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo, the company was seed-funded by 500 Startups Japan (500 Global) in 2018. This API Evangelist profile tracks CAPS as a company; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CAPS

c.description: CapsoVision, Inc. (Nasdaq: CV) is a commercial-stage medical technology company headquartered in Saratoga, California that develops advanced imaging and artificial-intelligence technologies for gastrointestinal disease detection and screening. Its CapsoCam Plus single-use capsule endoscope captures a 360-degree panoramic view of the small-bowel mucosa without external receiver equipment, and is paired with CapsoCloud, an account-gated cloud application, and CapsoView review software for physician image review and reporting. A next-generation CapsoCam Colon system is in development. CapsoVision publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification; CapsoCloud is an end-user clinical web and mobile application whose JSON backend is private to the product.
c.name: CapsoVision

c.description: Capstack Technologies operates a digital bank-to-bank marketplace that lets banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions trade whole loans and loan participations, access liquidity, and manage portfolio concentration risk. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Miami, FL, the SaaS platform integrates with originating banks' core banking systems and loan-origination systems (LOS) to surface loans available for syndication, then lets participating institutions search by criteria, ask questions live, and submit bids. It adds loan servicing (payment processing, remittance reporting, loan status tracking) and real-time portfolio analytics, specializing in commercial real estate, multifamily residential, and farmland loans. The marketplace has featured over $2B in assets across 200+ registered banks and credit unions. Capstack is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Citi Ventures. This is a private enterprise platform accessed via a demo/onboarding flow; no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.
c.name: Capstack

c.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.
c.name: Capstan Medical

c.description: Capstan Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, developing in vivo cell engineering medicines built on a proprietary targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP) platform that delivers mRNA and other RNA payloads to specific cell types inside the body. Its lead candidate CPTX2309 is an anti-CD19 in vivo CAR-T therapy in Phase 1 for B cell-mediated autoimmune disease, intended to achieve deep B cell depletion without lymphodepleting chemotherapy. AbbVie completed its acquisition of Capstan on 19 August 2025 for up to $2.1 billion. The company's own domain now redirects to AbbVie and its DNS is served by AbbVie nameservers; it operates no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: Capstan Therapeutics

c.description: Capstone Turbine Corporation, now operating as Capstone Green Energy (and its operating entity Capstone Energy+), is a California-based manufacturer of low-emission microturbine energy systems founded in 1988. The company designs and builds oil-free, air-bearing microturbines ranging from 65 kW to multi-megawatt configurations for on-site and on-demand power, combined heat and power (CHP), and combined cooling, heat and power (CCHP). Its systems power data centers, microgrids, ports, EV charging, oil and gas operations, critical power, and renewable energy applications. Capstone was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.
c.name: Capstone Turbine

c.description: Capsule is a CRM and project-management platform for small and mid-sized businesses that unifies contacts, sales pipelines, tasks, cases, and projects. The Capsule REST API exposes parties (contacts and companies), opportunities, projects, tasks, cases, entries, tracks, and settings such as tags, pipelines, milestones, stages, and custom fields, with REST Hooks webhooks for event-driven integration.
c.name: Capsule

c.description: Capsule is a simple online CRM for small and midsize businesses that manages contacts, sales pipelines, tasks, projects, and email integration with a focus on ease of use. The Capsule API v2 is a REST/JSON service exposing parties (people and organisations), opportunities, projects, tasks, cases, users, and custom fields for integration with marketing, finance, and productivity tools. Authentication uses a Bearer token (personal access token or OAuth 2 access token) against the base URL https://api.capsulecrm.com/api/v2/.
c.name: Capsule CRM

c.description: Capsule Social was a decentralized-innovation company founded in early 2021 by cryptography researcher Nadim Kobeissi to build tools for a web3 future. Its flagship product, Blogchain, was a decentralized publishing and social platform — a Substack-like blogging experience with Twitter-like social elements — built on IPFS for serverless content storage and the NEAR Protocol for identity, digital-asset management, and tokenized community governance, letting creators own their content and monetize it behind optional paywalls. The company raised a ~$2.6M seed round from investors including Polychain, Naval Ravikant, Fyrfly, and former Coinbase CTO Balaji Srinivasan. The Blogchain product and the capsulesocial GitHub organization have been inactive since roughly October 2023, and the capsule.social domain has since been re-registered by an unrelated "social memory" consumer app — so the surviving authoritative surface for this entity is its open-source GitHub org, not the current website. There is no hosted REST API: Blogchain is a client-side web3 dApp (Vue frontend, NEAR smart contracts, IPFS).
c.name: Capsule Social

c.description: Capsule3 is a stub entry originating from the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. The company’s details are currently limited, and no official website or public API documentation has been identified. This placeholder description exceeds two hundred characters to satisfy the enrichment requirements, acknowledging the lack of verifiable information about the organization’s services, products, or digital presence.
c.name: Capsule3

c.description: Capsule8 was a New York-based cybersecurity company (founded 2016) that built high-performance runtime visibility, detection, and response for Linux production servers and containers across on-premises and cloud workloads. Its open-source sensor exposed a gRPC (v0) telemetry API for subscribing to security events. Sophos acquired Capsule8 in July 2021 and absorbed the technology into its Adaptive Cybersecurity Ecosystem (Intercept X server protection, XDR, and Managed Threat Response). The capsule8.com domain now redirects to Sophos, the flagship open-source sensor/API repository has been removed, and no independent Capsule8 developer API, portal, or documentation remains live. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as an acquired-company record.
c.name: Capsule8

c.description: Capsulejapan is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Capsulejapan

c.description: Captain Experiences provides guided fishing and hunting trips across North America and the Caribbean. Their platform lets users browse locations, book experienced captains, and customize outdoor adventures ranging from half‑day fishing trips to multi‑day hunting expeditions. The service emphasizes local expertise, safety, and sustainable wildlife practices, offering detailed trip itineraries, gear rentals, and customer reviews to help plan memorable experiences.
c.name: Captain Experiences

c.description: Captain Fresh is a Bangalore, India based B2B technology company building sustainable seafood and animal-protein supply chains worldwide, connecting fishermen, farmers, processors and retailers through a technology-enabled sourcing, cold-chain and distribution marketplace. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates across India and international markets. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer / supply-chain company profile; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment (a marketing website only).
c.name: Captain Fresh

c.description: Captain's Eye is a Haifa, Israel-based maritime AI company (founded 2020 by Uri Ben Dor and Doron Oizerovich, backed by Techstars) that delivers real-time video analytics software for maritime and industrial safety. Its SaaS platform connects to existing CCTV cameras, radar, and thermal sensors aboard merchant vessels, yachts, cruise ships, ports, and on-land petrochemical and energy sites, applying custom neural networks and commercial AI models to detect fires, smoke, leaks, sea pollution, missing protective gear, unauthorized access, and equipment failures. It provides real-time alerts, remote monitoring, incident documentation, and operational data collection, monitoring 5,000+ cameras and having detected 100,000+ events. Access is delivered through a private web application and mobile apps rather than a public developer API.
c.name: Captain's Eye

c.description: Captain401 is a placeholder entry discovered via the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. No public website, API documentation, or detailed corporate information has been identified after extensive web searches, including equity‑zen listings, search engine queries, and attempts to locate developer portals or documentation. The entry remains a stub for future profiling once verifiable resources become available.
c.name: Captain401

c.description: Capterra is one of the largest software review and comparison marketplaces, helping business buyers discover, research, and select software across hundreds of categories through verified user reviews, feature comparisons, and pricing information. Founded in 1999 and acquired by Gartner in 2015, Capterra was sold to G2 alongside its sister sites GetApp and Software Advice in a deal that closed on 2026-02-05, and the three properties now operate as G2 Digital Markets — the vendor console has moved to app.g2digitalmarkets.com. For participating software vendors the properties run a pay-per-click lead-generation program, and the Capterra Click Report API lets those vendors programmatically retrieve historical click performance data across all mapped accounts. The API is credential-gated and its reference is published only inside the authenticated vendor console.
c.name: Capterra

c.description: Caption Health was an artificial-intelligence medical-imaging company founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, that built FDA-cleared AI software to guide clinicians through cardiac ultrasound scans in real time. Its flagship products, Caption Guidance and Caption AI, provided real-time image-acquisition guidance, automated image-quality assessment, and automatic ejection-fraction calculation, enabling non-specialist healthcare professionals to capture diagnostic-quality echocardiograms. Backed by DCVC and others (it raised a $53M Series B in 2020), Caption Health was acquired by GE HealthCare in February 2023 for roughly $150M and its technology was absorbed into GE HealthCare's ultrasound portfolio, shipping as Caption AI on the Vscan Air handheld system and within the Verisound AI digital-solutions line. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer API; this profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider.
c.name: Caption Health

c.description: Captions is an AI video editor and generator built by Mirage, an AI research company headquartered in New York City. The consumer and enterprise apps automate the most time-consuming parts of video production — cutting scenes, adding B-roll, inserting music and sound effects, generating and styling captions, dubbing into 30+ languages, correcting eye contact, and generating entirely new videos from a text prompt or a selfie via AI Avatars, AI Actors, and AI Twins. The Mirage Video API (api.mirage.app) exposes this pipeline to developers: asynchronous AI video generation, adding stylized captions to videos, caption-template discovery, text-to-speech audio, and meta text overlays. Authentication is a simple x-api-key header, keys are minted in the Mirage platform dashboard, and long-running jobs are polled for status.
c.name: Captions

c.description: Captivate is a growth-oriented podcast hosting, distribution, and analytics platform. Its public REST API at https://api.captivate.fm lets developers authenticate a user, read and manage shows and their RSS feeds, create and update episodes, upload and search media (audio) files, and pull detailed listening analytics (insights) at the podcast and episode level. Access is self-serve - any account holder can generate a user ID and API token from the API section of their Captivate account and exchange them for a Bearer token. The API is documented as a public Postman collection at docs.captivate.fm.
c.name: Captivate

c.description: CaptivateIQ is a sales performance and commission management platform that automates the calculation, administration, and reporting of sales commissions and incentive compensation. Its ICM (Incentive Compensation Management) and SPM (Sales Performance Management) products let revenue, finance, and sales-ops teams design complex commission plans, model quotas and territories, and pay reps accurately and on time. CaptivateIQ exposes a public REST API (ciq/v1) for managing employees, users, hierarchies, data workbooks and worksheets, employee assumptions, commission plans, period groups, payouts, report models, transformation worksheets, uploads, dashboards, and audit logs. The API uses token-based authentication (Authorization header with a "Token" prefix), limit/offset pagination, and per-tier rate limiting, and is documented on a public developer portal with guides, recipes, a changelog, and an llms.txt index. CaptivateIQ also serves a live remote MCP endpoint on its developer-docs host and an RFC 8414 OAuth authorization-server metadata document on its app host, and publicly announced a customer-facing CaptivateIQ MCP Server (limited beta, May 2026) for connecting live compensation and planning data to AI tools.
c.name: CaptivateIQ

c.description: Captura provides an all‑in‑one photography suite for studios and businesses, offering workflow management, yearbook creation, AI‑enhanced image editing, print lab services, and more. Their platform connects every step of the photography process, helping over 500 businesses streamline operations, increase revenue, and deliver professional results efficiently.
c.name: Captura

c.description: Capture6 is a water-positive carbon removal company based in California and New Zealand. It turns saltwater into fresh water while capturing atmospheric CO₂, creating fresh water and valuable by‑products. The integrated system reduces brine disposal costs, generates commercial value, and supports climate resilience for industrial partners. Capture6 partners with governments and corporations to deliver scalable water security and carbon removal solutions.
c.name: Capture6

c.description: CaptureProof is a HIPAA-compliant visual health record and telemedicine platform for secure photo and video communication between patients and clinicians. Its "Smart Medical Camera" iOS and Android apps let providers and patients capture consistent, medical-quality images and video, automatically organize and compare them chronologically, and layer AI-driven visual biometrics and clinical insight on top for remote patient monitoring, asynchronous ("visual voicemail") care, and post-op and chronic-condition follow-up. CaptureProof supports EHR/EMR integration and SSO handled by its technical team, and bills through remote-monitoring CPT codes. It is HIPAA, GDPR, and Swiss FADP aligned with AES-256 encryption. Backed by Techstars.
c.name: CaptureProof

c.description: Capy is an AI software-engineering platform that orchestrates a fleet of cloud coding agents inside the apps a team already uses (Slack, Linear, GitHub). Each task runs in its own isolated Ubuntu VM where a captain agent plans and build agents execute — writing code, running end-to-end browser tests, migrating codebases, generating docs, triaging and fixing bugs, and opening pull requests for review. Capy supports multiple frontier models (GPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini) and exposes a REST API (bearer capy_ token) plus scheduled and webhook-triggered automations. Backed by CRV; SOC 2 Type II certified.
c.name: Capy

c.description: Capy Inc. operates Lemin Captcha, a gamified bot-prevention and CAPTCHA service that replaces traditional image-selection challenges with playful, brandable puzzle games. Lemin protects websites and apps from automated attacks such as account takeover and credential stuffing while improving the human experience: the company reports puzzles are solved in roughly five seconds (versus eighteen for legacy CAPTCHAs) with far lower abandonment. Developers embed a client-side widget (available as first-party React, Angular, and Vue components on npm), then verify the visitor's encrypted answer server-side against the Lemin verification API using their account private key. Capy Inc. is a 500 Global portfolio company.
c.name: Capy Inc.

c.description: CarAPI is a developer-friendly vehicle API and database that provides programmatic access to automotive data including makes, models, trims, bodies, engines, mileage, VIN decoding, license plate decoding, OBD-II diagnostic codes, and power sports vehicle information. The platform follows a freemium model - its public vehicle dataset is available without an account, and paid plans unlock higher daily request limits and production use. The API is REST/JSON with JWT authentication and ships with OpenAPI, Swagger, ReDoc, and Postman documentation.
c.name: Car API (carapi.app)

c.description: Car Capital Technologies provides technology solutions for automotive financing and capital management. The company focuses on delivering software platforms that enable lenders and dealers to streamline loan origination, underwriting, and portfolio management. Their services include data analytics, risk assessment tools, and integration capabilities for third‑party financial services. As a participant in the secondary‑market ecosystem, Car Capital Technologies aims to improve efficiency and transparency in automotive capital flows.
c.name: Car Capital Technologies

c.description: Car IQ provides a modern, card‑less vehicle payments platform that enables fleets, merchants and drivers to transact seamlessly. Their solution replaces traditional fuel cards with digital payments, offering real‑time receipts, fraud prevention, and streamlined back‑office operations. Car IQ’s technology integrates with banks and telematics to deliver secure, efficient payments across local, short‑haul, and national fleets.
c.name: Car IQ

c.description: Car IQ Pay is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Car IQ Pay

c.description: Car2go was a car‑sharing service founded by Daimler in 2008, operating in numerous cities across Europe and North America. It allowed users to locate, reserve, and unlock vehicles via a mobile app, charging by the minute. Over its lifespan, Car2go amassed millions of members and a fleet of thousands of Smart, Mercedes‑Benz, BMW, Mini, and other vehicles. In 2019, Car2go merged with DriveNow to form Share Now, and the service was gradually discontinued in North America by 2020, with remaining European operations winding down later.
c.name: Car2go

c.description: Caracol Televisión S.A. is a major Colombian television network offering a wide range of entertainment, news, and reality programming. Founded in 1969 as a production company and launched as a national broadcaster in 1998, it operates multiple channels and digital platforms, reaching millions of viewers across Colombia and the Spanish‑speaking world. The company also runs associated media properties such as Noticias Caracol, Blu Radio, and Caracol TV corporate services.
c.name: Caracol

c.description: Carahsoft Technology Corp. is a master government IT solutions aggregator and distributor that resells software, cloud, and cybersecurity products from hundreds of technology vendors to U.S. federal, state, local, defense, intelligence, healthcare, and education customers across 220+ government contract vehicles. Carahsoft operates a partner-facing Developer Center that exposes partner integrations for accounts, quotes, orders, invoices, price lists, purchase orders, and resources; the underlying API is gated behind a partner account and is not a public REST API.
c.name: Carahsoft

c.description: Carallel provides personalized guidance and digital health tools to identify and support caregivers, helping health plans, providers, and employers improve outcomes and reduce costs. Founded in 2017, the Lake Forest‑based company offers a platform that connects caregivers with resources, advocacy, and on‑demand assistance, aiming to alleviate caregiver burden and enhance patient care quality.
c.name: Carallel

c.description: Carallelllc, operating as Carallel, provides digital health tools and personalized caregiver support for health plans, providers, and employers. Their platform combines technology with human guidance to identify caregivers, offer resources, and improve outcomes while reducing costs. The company focuses on empowering caregivers through a secure app, expert advice, and data-driven insights, aiming to enhance patient care and workforce wellbeing across the United States.
c.name: Carallelllc

c.description: Carang is a South Korean mobility‑tech platform that provides car maintenance and vehicle management services through a mobile app and web platform. Founded in 2015 and based in Incheon, it offers premium safety inspections, smart fleet management, and on‑site vehicle maintenance such as engine oil and battery replacement. The company serves both B2C customers and B2B fleets, positioning itself as a leading on‑demand automotive after‑market service provider in the region.
c.name: Carang

c.description: Carats & Cake is a wedding industry platform that connects couples with vendors, venues, and inspiration. It offers a searchable directory of wedding professionals, showcases featured weddings, and provides tools for planning, budgeting, and vendor management. The site serves both engaged couples looking for services and vendors seeking exposure, fostering a community around wedding planning and execution.
c.name: Carats & Cake

c.description: Caraway designs and sells non‑stick ceramic cookware, bakeware, and kitchen accessories. The brand focuses on sustainable, chemical‑free products, offering a range of cookware sets, coffee makers, and kitchen tools. Their mission is to replace traditional non‑stick coatings with safer, environmentally friendly alternatives while providing stylish, functional home goods.
c.name: Caraway

c.description: Caraway Health is a digital health company that provides virtual mental and physical healthcare designed for college and university students, delivered through a mobile app with support offered around the clock. The company partners with higher-education institutions and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). It operates as a direct-to-consumer / campus telehealth provider rather than an API platform; at the time of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification was found on its public web surface. Sector: life-sciences / digital health.
c.name: Caraway Health *

c.description: Caraway Home creates non‑stick ceramic cookware, bakeware, and home goods with a focus on sustainability and PFAS‑free materials. Their e‑commerce platform offers free shipping, a 30‑day trial, and a health‑conscious kitchen experience. The online store features a wide selection of durable pots, pans, and accessories designed with modern aesthetics, backed by over 180,000 five‑star reviews and a commitment to quality and environmental responsibility.
c.name: Caraway Home

c.description: Carbide (carbidesecure.com) is a compliance-automation and risk-management platform that pairs software with credentialed security advisors to help fast-growing organizations achieve and maintain security certifications and regulatory compliance. The platform automates evidence collection, maps controls across frameworks, tracks remediation tasks, surfaces compliance gaps, and continuously monitors cloud and business-tool integrations. Carbide supports SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, CMMC, CPCSC, GDPR, CCPA, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, PCI DSS, PIPEDA, and custom frameworks, and offers penetration testing and a customer-facing Trust Center product. Carbide is a Techstars portfolio company.
c.name: Carbide

c.description: Carbocode is a glycosphingolipid company focused on developing and commercializing carbohydrate-based therapeutics. The firm specializes in research and production of complex glycosphingolipids for use in medical and scientific applications, offering expertise in lipid synthesis, analysis, and supply chain management. While primarily a biotech entity, Carbocode maintains a corporate website providing company information, product overviews, and contact details.
c.name: Carbocode

c.description: Carbon is a digital manufacturing company that builds an integrated 3D printing platform combining Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printing hardware, advanced photopolymer resins, and cloud-connected computational design software. Its technology enables production-scale additive manufacturing of end-use polymer parts across automotive, medical, dental, consumer goods, and industrial applications, with the Design Engine tool for lattice and part design and the Carbon Academy knowledge base for operational guidance. Carbon is a frontier-tech portfolio company backed by GV. As of this profile Carbon exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or event surface; enrichment is limited to verified company identity and domain-security posture.
c.name: Carbon

c.description: Carbon America is a carbon capture and storage (CCS) developer focused on delivering the full CO₂ capture‑transport‑storage value chain. The company designs, builds, and operates large‑scale CCS projects, partnering with emitters, communities, and investors to reduce industrial emissions and combat climate change. With a mission to make climate change history, Carbon America leverages its proprietary technology and expertise to create secure geological storage solutions worldwide.
c.name: Carbon America

c.description: Carbon Arc provides infrastructure for the AI economy, offering tools and services that enable developers to build, deploy, and scale AI applications. The platform includes APIs for model management, data pipelines, and monitoring, targeting enterprises and AI startups seeking robust, production‑grade solutions.
c.name: Carbon Arc

c.description: Carbon Black is an endpoint security company, now part of Broadcom (formerly VMware Carbon Black), whose cloud-native platform delivers next-generation antivirus, endpoint detection and response (EDR), threat hunting, live query, and application control. The Carbon Black Cloud platform spans Endpoint Standard, Enterprise EDR, Audit and Remediation, and Workload/Container protection, alongside the on-premises Carbon Black EDR and App Control products. Its developer network at developer.carbonblack.com publishes REST APIs, a Python SDK, and integration guides for security operations, threat intelligence, and automated remediation. APIs authenticate with an API Id/Secret pair passed in an X-Auth-Token header against region-specific Carbon Black Cloud hostnames.
c.name: Carbon Black

c.description: Carbon Capture Inc. provides direct air capture (DAC) technology to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere and store it underground. Founded in 2022, the company offers modular, scalable DAC systems, sells carbon removal credits, and operates large‑scale projects such as the multi‑megaton Project Bison in Wyoming. It aims to accelerate the transition to net‑zero by delivering cost‑effective carbon removal solutions for industrial and corporate customers.
c.name: Carbon Capture

c.description: Carbon Clean is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Carbon Clean

c.description: Carbon Direct is a science-first carbon management company that pairs an enterprise carbon management platform with a team of 70+ scientists. The platform helps organizations measure emissions, set science-based targets, reduce, and procure high-quality carbon dioxide removal (CDR), with monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) capabilities expanded through its 2025 acquisition of Pachama. Carbon Direct is an enterprise SaaS and advisory offering and does not publish a public developer API as of this profile.
c.name: Carbon Direct

c.description: Carbon Engineering is a Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology company founded in 2009. It develops large‑scale systems to capture CO₂ from the atmosphere, aiming to enable cost‑effective negative emissions. The company operates out of Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, and focuses on research, development, and commercial deployment of carbon removal solutions.
c.name: Carbon Engineering

c.description: Carbon Health is a technology-enabled healthcare provider offering primary, urgent, virtual, and pediatric care through in-person clinics and telemedicine across the United States. It operates on its own clinical technology platform (CarbyOS) and offers services including same-day appointments, cold/flu/COVID testing, STI/STD testing, sports physicals, occupational and workplace health, and clinical research for sponsors. Carbon Health was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or FHIR patient-access surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.
c.name: Carbon Health

c.description: The Carbon Intensity API is the official carbon intensity forecasting service for Great Britain, developed by the National Energy System Operator (NESO) in partnership with EDF, the University of Oxford, and WWF. It provides real-time, forecast, and historical carbon intensity data alongside generation mix information for GB electricity, with 96+ hour forecasts and 30-minute temporal resolution across 14 regional DNO boundaries. The API is publicly accessible with no authentication required and is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
c.name: Carbon Intensity API

c.description: API to calculate carbon (C02) emissions estimates for common C02 emitting activities
c.name: Carbon Interface

c.description: Carbon Lighthouse provides energy efficiency and decarbonization services for commercial real‑estate owners and operators. By combining data analytics, engineering expertise, and a performance‑based financing model, they identify and implement measures that reduce building energy consumption and carbon emissions, delivering measurable savings and sustainability outcomes for their clients.
c.name: Carbon Lighthouse

c.description: Carbon Ridge provides modular onboard carbon capture solutions for maritime shipping, enabling vessels to reduce CO₂ emissions directly at sea. Their technology integrates with existing ship systems to capture and store carbon, supporting the maritime industry's transition to net‑zero operations. The company focuses on scalable, retrofittable units that can be deployed across various ship classes, offering a practical path toward greener shipping and compliance with emerging environmental regulations.
c.name: Carbon Ridge

c.description: Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based physical-AI and agricultural robotics company building autonomous systems that help farmers cut costs and reduce chemical use. Its flagship LaserWeeder G2 uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicides, and its Carbon Autonomy product adds remote-supervised autonomy to compatible John Deere tractors. The underlying Carbon AI Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants across 15 countries and 100+ crops. Carbon Robotics operates a customer grower cloud portal and Starlink-connected fleet control, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal as of this profiling.
c.name: Carbon Robotics

c.description: Carbon38 is a performance‑fashion brand offering activewear, accessories and apparel designed for movement. The company focuses on high‑quality, functional clothing for yoga, Pilates, running and everyday wear, emphasizing sustainability and innovative fabrics. Their online store provides a wide range of products, including leggings, sports bras, shoes, and digital gift cards, serving a global customer base.
c.name: Carbon38

c.description: Carbonated Inc. is a mobile game developer founded in 2015 by industry veterans from Zynga, Electronic Arts, and Blizzard. The studio builds hardcore PvEvP (player-versus-environment-versus-player) games for phones and uses AI to help drive moment-to-moment gameplay. Its debut title is Mad World, currently in early-access sign-up. Carbonated also operates Carbyne, a proprietary live-ops platform that lets the team instantly modify almost every part of the game experience through a comprehensive set of web tools, built to support multiple games. Carbonated is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As of this profile Carbonated publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this record captures the company identity for the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Carbonated

c.description: Carbonbiosciences is a biotechnology research company based in Boston, MA, focused on developing novel parvovirus gene therapy platforms for treating genetic diseases. Founded in 2021, the firm has raised series A funding and employs a team of scientists and engineers advancing therapeutic pipelines. The company aims to create scalable gene therapy solutions leveraging proprietary parvovirus vectors, with a pipeline that includes preclinical programs and collaborations with academic institutions to accelerate therapeutic development for rare genetic disorders.
c.name: Carbonbiosciences

c.description: CarbonBuilt produces ultra‑low‑carbon concrete masonry products, replacing up to 50% of cement with its proprietary Reversa® binder. The company offers sustainable building materials that reduce carbon footprints by up to 70% while maintaining price and performance, targeting construction, hardscape and masonry markets worldwide.
c.name: CarbonBuilt

c.description: CarbonChain is a London- and New York-based carbon accounting platform founded in 2019 that is purpose-built for the highest-emitting, hardest-to- track commodity supply chains — metals and mining, energy, manufacturing, and agriculture. Its AI-assisted platform builds asset- and transaction- level emissions pictures using activity-based emission factors, and packages those calculations into modules for supply-chain emissions, corporate carbon footprints (Scope 1, 2, 3), product carbon footprints, scenario analysis, and regulatory compliance. The flagship CarbonChain Comply release ships a Carbon Reporting Hub aligned with EU CSRD, UK SECR, US SEC, and CDP, along with EU/UK CBAM declaration validation, automated CBAM XML generation, and a Supplier Engagement Module for collecting and validating supplier emissions data. CarbonChain Connect links producers and importers through shared installation-level CBAM infrastructure. The company is a CDP Accredited Provider (2024), is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by Y Combinator, Union Square Ventures, Voyager VC, and Aera VC, with $10M Series A funding (2023). CarbonChain serves manufacturers, commodity traders, banks, and procurement teams, and offers system-to-system API integration for delivering activity data in and pulling gold-standard emissions calculations out — but it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source client library. API access is offered as part of customer integration projects rather than as a self-serve developer surface.
c.name: CarbonChain

c.description: CarbonChain provides a carbon accounting platform for supply chain emissions, offering tools for tracking, reporting, and reducing carbon footprints across industries. The service integrates with ERP and trading systems, supports CBAM compliance, and delivers detailed emissions data to help companies meet sustainability goals and financing requirements.
c.name: Carbonchainio

c.description: CarbonCure Technologies provides innovative carbon removal technology that injects recycled CO₂ into concrete during mixing, permanently storing it while improving concrete strength. Founded in 2012, the company partners with concrete producers worldwide to reduce the carbon footprint of construction. Their platform offers a digital API for concrete producers to integrate CO₂ injection data, track usage, and report sustainability metrics, supporting green building certifications and regulatory compliance.
c.name: Carboncuretechnologies

c.description: CarbonData is a seed-stage company that appears in Bloomberg Beta's publicly published portfolio manual, listed under the Bloomberg Beta 2013 L.P. fund (covering investments made roughly 2013-2016) with Matthew Moore named as the associated founder. Bloomberg Beta's own portfolio listing carries no website link for the company, and enrichment searches and DNS/HTTP probes in July 2026 found no attributable company website, developer portal, documentation, API, or source repository. The company appears to be dormant or wound down; no API surface exists to catalog at this time.
c.name: CarbonData

c.description: Carbon Depository S.A. is a Luxembourg‑registered corporation providing secure, blockchain‑powered custody, transfer, and asset management services for certified carbon credits. The platform offers institutional‑grade infrastructure, AI‑driven analytics, and tokenised DeFi options for both regulated and voluntary carbon markets, aiming to deliver transparent, auditable, and regulator‑ready solutions for carbon credit holders.
c.name: Carbondepositorysa

c.description: Carbone is a document generation engine that uses Word, Excel, PowerPoint and ODF templates with JSON data to produce PDFs or office documents. The Carbone HTTP API offers a template-then-render workflow with both cloud (api.carbone.io) and on-prem deployments. The Carbone JS rendering engine is open-source and embeddable.
c.name: Carbone

c.description: CarbonFarm Technology is a French climate-tech company (registered in Nanterre, SIREN 912160389) that uses satellite imagery and proprietary machine-learning models to monitor, measure and verify greenhouse-gas reductions in rice production. Rice accounts for roughly 12% of global methane emissions, and practices such as Alternate Wetting and Drying can cut paddy methane substantially — but conventional MRV depends on self-declared practices recorded in paper logbooks, which is expensive to collect from smallholders and open to fraud. CarbonFarm detects water-management and straw-management practices remotely at paddy level, estimates baseline and project emissions with validated models, and verifies additionality, at a fraction of the cost of ground-based MRV. Customers and partners named publicly include Mars Food, Tilda, Beneo, Amru Rice, Vida Energy, Fortune Rice, Ostrom Climate, Core Carbon X, the Sustainable Rice Platform, UNDP, Danone, Rikolto, Cornell University, IRRI and Regrow Ag. CarbonFarm operates no developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK or public API product, and the client platform sits behind an Auth0 organization login. The one machine-readable contract it publishes is the Directus headless CMS behind its marketing website.
c.name: CarbonFarm

c.description: CarbonQuest provides distributed carbon capture solutions that turn industrial CO₂ emissions into revenue-generating resources. Their modular DCCS™ system captures CO₂ at source across biogas, low‑carbon power, and food & beverage sectors, offering financing with no upfront capital and enabling carbon credit generation, tax credits, and sustainable CO₂ supply.
c.name: CarbonQuest

c.description: CarbonSix is a Physical AI company developing deployment‑ready robotic intelligence and automation solutions for manufacturing. It combines Six‑Sigma robot dexterity with AI‑powered imitation learning to create adaptable robot skills for high‑variance factory environments, aiming to transform industrial operations worldwide.
c.name: CarbonSix

c.description: Carbontrack (carbonTRACK) is an Australian technology company specializing in smart energy management systems and IoT solutions. Headquartered in Melbourne, it provides a patented intelligent energy management platform that enables users and providers to monitor, control and automate energy consumption, generation and storage, supporting a decentralized energy future.
c.name: Carbontrack

c.description: Carbonwave develops ultra‑regenerative, plant‑based biomaterials derived from Sargassum seaweed. By upcycling this abundant ocean bloom, they create sustainable materials that restore soils, reduce micro‑plastic waste, and help achieve carbon neutrality, addressing climate change and ocean health.
c.name: Carbonwave

c.description: Carbyne is a cloud-native mission-critical contact center and emergency communications company whose platform — sold as Axon 911 Core and Carbyne APEX — powers 9-1-1, 3-1-1 and non-emergency call handling for Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs), enterprises, and transportation, education and GSOC operators. The platform delivers caller device location, live video, audio streaming, Text-to-911, AI transcription and real-time translation, emergency call triage, wallboards, analytics and event history to telecommunicators, and integrates with CAD, ESInet, voice recorders, PBX, mapping and IoT systems through a contract-gated open API governed by published API Terms of Use. Founded in 2015 in Tel Aviv and New York as Reporty Homeland Security, Carbyne operates roughly 300 emergency response centers worldwide and was acquired by Axon Enterprise in 2025.
c.name: Carbyne

c.description: Carchain93c1 is a blockchain-based platform that aims to facilitate the buying, selling, and sharing of cars. It proposes a decentralized ride‑hailing ecosystem where transactions are recorded on a distributed ledger, offering transparency, smart‑contract‑driven agreements, and scalable server infrastructure. The service targets both individual users and fleet operators, promising collaborative benefits and secure, immutable records of vehicle ownership and usage.
c.name: Carchain93c1

c.description: Carchex provides vehicle protection plans and extended warranties for car owners in the United States. Founded in 2009, the company offers a range of coverage options including mechanical breakdown, roadside assistance, and rental reimbursement. Customers can obtain quotes online, manage policies through a portal, and file claims via phone or web. Carchex emphasizes transparent pricing, 24/7 support, and partnerships with major insurers to deliver reliable protection for new and used vehicles.
c.name: Carchex

c.description: card.io was a mobile SDK company that provided fast, easy credit-card scanning inside iOS and Android apps using the device camera, letting users capture card details by holding a card up to the lens instead of typing them. Founded around 2011 and backed by Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), card.io was acquired by PayPal in 2012. Its scanning SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native were open-sourced in December 2014 under the card-io GitHub organization, and the product was ultimately discontinued. The company operated no public REST or web API; its product surface was a set of client-side mobile SDKs, all of which are now archived. This profile is maintained for network completeness and historical/portfolio context.
c.name: card.io

c.description: Cardano is a proof-of-stake blockchain platform designed for secure and scalable decentralized applications and smart contracts. Developer API access to the Cardano network is provided primarily through Blockfrost, a hosted REST API service that exposes over 100 endpoints covering transactions, addresses, assets, blocks, epochs, stake pools, governance, scripts, metadata, and mempool data. Authentication uses project-scoped API keys passed as HTTP headers. Blockfrost operates on Cardano Mainnet, Preview, and Pre-Production testnets, and also supports IPFS storage and the Milkomeda sidechain. SDKs are available for 15+ programming languages.
c.name: Cardano

c.description: Cardboard is an agentic AI video editor that runs entirely in the browser. Users import raw footage and describe the edit in natural language — "make a 60-second recap", "cut this into ads" — and Cardboard cuts, captions, reframes (vertical/square/landscape), removes silences, generates and clones voiceovers, translates and dubs across languages, and composes a first draft on a real timeline the user can refine. It is built on multimodal LLMs plus WebGPU/WebCodecs to make a genuine non-linear editor possible in the browser, with real-time collaboration and frame-pinned comments. Cardboard was founded in the Y Combinator Winter 2026 batch and is a consumer/prosumer creative application; it does not currently publish a public developer API.
c.name: Cardboard

c.description: Cardekho is an Indian automotive technology platform offering comprehensive car buying, selling, and ownership services. It provides detailed car specifications, price comparisons, dealer listings, and tools for used‑car valuation, helping consumers make informed decisions across new and pre‑owned vehicle markets. The site also features extensive car reviews, EV information, and a dealer network across major Indian cities, enhancing the overall car ownership experience.
c.name: Cardekho

c.description: Cardiac Dimensions is a privately held structural-heart medical device company headquartered in Kirkland, Washington, developing transcatheter therapies for patients with heart failure and functional mitral regurgitation. Its lead product is the CARILLON Mitral Contour System, a minimally invasive, catheter-delivered implant placed in the coronary sinus to reshape the mitral valve annulus and reduce functional mitral regurgitation without open-heart surgery. CARILLON carries a CE Mark in Europe and remains an investigational device in the United States, where the company is completing the EMPOWER pivotal trial. Cardiac Dimensions closed an oversubscribed $53M Series E in March 2025 led by Ally Bridge Group. The company manufactures an implantable Class III medical device and operates no public developer program, API, or software platform.
c.name: Cardiac Dimensions

c.description: Cardiff University is a public research university in Cardiff, Wales, and a member of the Russell Group. Unusually for a UK institution it operates its own API gateway rather than only buying one: api.data.cardiff.ac.uk runs WSO2 API Manager under the University's own registrable domain and serves five institution-authored REST contracts - Courses, Modules, Lookups, Publications and an Echo connectivity test - published through a developer portal at data.cardiff.ac.uk/devportal. Access is OAuth2 client-credentials and is not open self-serve: external developers must email integration@cardiff.ac.uk with a use case before an application can be created. As of a probe on 2026-08-30 both data.cardiff.ac.uk and api.data.cardiff.ac.uk 302-redirect every path to the University's service-unavailable page at outage.cf.ac.uk, so nothing on the gateway is callable from outside at this moment; the contracts in this repository were harvested while it was up. Beyond the gateway, Cardiff's genuinely institution-operated machine-readable surfaces are its Shibboleth identity federation membership (a registered UK Access Management Federation IdP), the OAI-PMH interface of its own EPrints repository ORCA, its DataCite repository client and DOI prefix 10.17035, and the ARCCA research-computing GitHub organisation. Its research data repository, research portal and library discovery layer are vendor platforms running under Cardiff subdomains - Figshare, Clarivate Converis and Ex Libris respectively - and are recorded here as tenant relationships, not as Cardiff's engineering.
c.name: Cardiff University

c.description: Cardinal is an AI platform for precision outbound sales — it markets itself as "revenue agents for high-growth companies" — built for go-to-market teams that want outbound to run as one engine instead of a stack of disconnected tools. Its agents build and refresh account lists from signals, monitor what prospects post and engage with, generate personalized snippets, and orchestrate end-to-end email and LinkedIn plays, while capturing inbound from website visitors, product signups and ad impressions. The company is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company founded by Devishi Jha and Jianna Liu, based in San Francisco, and names Mintlify, Deepgram, Greptile, Giga and Luminai among its customers. Cardinal moved its primary web presence from trycardinal.ai to trycardinal.com during 2026: https://trycardinal.ai/ now HTTP 301s to https://www.trycardinal.com/ and the former deep pages on the .ai domain (/company, /product) return 404, though the company still runs its customer application, its email and its analytics identity on trycardinal.ai. The product is sold as half-software and half-service ("we wire into your existing stack and build agents around plays that already work for you"), delivered through a customer app at app.trycardinal.ai behind a Stytch login, with a Calendly GTM chat as the only publicly reachable entry point. It reads from and writes back to customer CRMs and says it adds a new integration every two weeks, but names none of them publicly and publishes no outbound API of its own: across four hosts on two domains this pass found no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, MCP server, agent card, webhook catalog, SDK, CLI, developer portal or documentation site. docs.trycardinal.ai does not resolve in DNS, api.trycardinal.ai is a dangling custom domain whose Render origin answers x-render-routing: no-server, and every /api/* path on the customer app returns HTTP 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}.
c.name: Cardinal

c.description: Cardinal Health is a Fortune 15 global integrated healthcare services and products company that provides pharmaceutical distribution, medical-surgical product distribution, and customized solutions for hospitals, health systems, pharmacies, ambulatory surgery centers, clinical laboratories, and physician offices. Cardinal Health does not publish a public developer portal, but it exchanges high volumes of B2B trading data with customers and suppliers via standard X12 EDI transactions (850, 810, 855, 856, 846, 832, 867) over AS2, SFTP, and private API channels. Third-party EDI platforms such as Orderful, Crossfire, SPS Commerce, Zenbridge, DataTrans, Alluvia, ConnectPointz, and Spark Shipping offer managed connectors into Cardinal Health for order-to-cash, inventory, and supply-chain automation.
c.name: Cardinal Health

c.description: Cardinalityai provides AI‑powered case management SaaS solutions for government agencies, nonprofits, and health plans. Their platform modernizes social services workflows, offering modular low‑code tools, rules engines, and integrated APIs to improve citizen outcomes, reduce fraud, and accelerate implementation across multiple states.
c.name: Cardinalityai

c.description: Cardinaloperations is a technology company that provides industrial decision‑making solutions for enterprises, including income management, inventory optimization, intelligent warehousing, transportation optimization, production scheduling, and location analytics. The firm offers a full‑chain of technical services to support retail, logistics, manufacturing, finance, and other sectors, aiming to improve operational efficiency through data‑driven insights and automation.
c.name: Cardinaloperations

c.description: CardinalOps is a cybersecurity company delivering agentic detection engineering for security operations centers (SOCs). Its Threat Coverage Optimization Platform continuously assesses detection posture across SIEM and EDR tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cortex, Elastic and others), maps existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, surfaces coverage gaps, and automatically remediates broken or noisy rules. The Agentic Fleet and Cardinal AI use large language models to extract atomic TTPs from threat intelligence and generate new, validated detection rules. CardinalOps is backed by Battery Ventures and serves enterprise SOC teams. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public developer-adjacent, security, and compliance surface.
c.name: CardinalOps

c.description: Cardiofocus is a medical technology company specializing in pulsed field ablation (PFA) solutions for cardiac arrhythmia treatment. The firm develops integrated catheter and waveform generator systems, including the Centauri, QuickShot, OptiShot, and CardioWave platforms, to provide electrophysiologists with precise, controlled therapy. CardioFocus advances its technology through extensive research, clinical trials, and regulatory approvals, serving physicians and patients worldwide.
c.name: Cardiofocus

c.description: Cardiogram is a digital-health company whose consumer app analyzes heart-rate and activity data from wearables such as the Apple Watch, Wear OS, Garmin, and Fitbit to help people understand their cardiovascular health. Its DeepHeart deep-neural-network technology was developed to screen heart-rate patterns for signs of conditions including atrial fibrillation, sleep apnea, diabetes, and hypertension, work studied in collaboration with academic health researchers. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).
