This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass Cardiogram exposes no public developer or API surface and its primary website (cardiogram.com) does not complete an HTTPS/TLS handshake.
c.name: Cardiogram

c.description: Cardiointelligence (株式会社カルディオインテリジェンス) is a Japanese health‑tech company developing AI‑powered medical devices for cardiac diagnostics. Founded in 2019, it creates AI‑driven ECG analysis tools to support cardiologists, improve arrhythmia detection, and make heart‑disease care more accessible worldwide. The firm collaborates with clinicians and AI specialists, offering explainable AI solutions and pursuing innovative diagnostics for early detection and treatment of cardiovascular conditions.
c.name: Cardiointelligence

c.description: Cardiologs is a cloud-based ECG analysis platform that uses clinically validated artificial intelligence to streamline cardiac diagnostics, helping clinicians and healthcare providers reduce the burden of manual ECG interpretation while improving diagnostic scalability and accessibility. Founded in Paris in 2014, Cardiologs was acquired by Philips in 2021 and is now offered as part of Philips ambulatory monitoring and diagnostics (ECG monitoring) portfolio. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its primary domain redirects to the Philips healthcare product page.
c.name: Cardiologs

c.description: Cardiosense, Inc. is a Chicago-based medical technology company developing AI-powered, noninvasive cardiac hemodynamic monitoring for heart failure care. Its CardioTag device is a wearable chest biosensor that captures seismocardiographic (SCG), electrocardiographic (ECG) and photoplethysmographic (PPG) signals, and its PCWP Analysis Software is a standalone AI software-as-a-medical-device that estimates Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure from those signals without right heart catheterization or an implantable sensor. Both are authorized by the FDA as Class II medical devices, and the company received an FDA De Novo classification. Cardiosense publishes no developer program, SDK or API specification; its only machine-readable surfaces are an authored llms.txt, an extended AI-context document, an explicit AI-crawler allowance in robots.txt, and an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol server on its own host.
c.name: Cardiosense

c.description: Cardiovascular Devices was an early-stage healthcare company backed by Kleiner Perkins, which lists it in its partnerships archive as partnered since 1982, sector healthcare, stage early, and described simply as "cardiovascular monitoring devices". Kleiner Perkins records the company's status as acquired by 3M. It is a historical medical-device portfolio company that predates the public web: enrichment found no live corporate website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no public API surface of any kind, so this profile carries identity and provenance only. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a resolved venture-portfolio lead rather than as an active API provider, and no artifacts were generated because there is nothing real to harvest.
c.name: Cardiovascular Devices

c.description: Cardless, Inc. is a San Francisco fintech that operates an embedded co-branded credit card platform, letting consumer brands launch and run their own credit card programs natively inside their own apps and websites. The platform pairs a partner API surface with pre-built components covering the full credit journey — application and identity verification, real-time decisioning, checkout with instant virtual cards, card management and transaction disputes — while Cardless handles issuing-bank relationships, card production, underwriting, fraud, KYC/AML compliance, servicing and support behind the scenes. It is network-agnostic across Visa, Mastercard and American Express. Named partners include Coinbase (Coinbase One Card), Bilt, Qatar Airways Privilege Club, Alibaba.com, LATAM Airlines, Avianca LifeMiles, TAP Air Portugal and Avelo Airlines. Developer documentation at docs.cardless.com is gated behind a partner login, so no public OpenAPI, SDKs or sandbox credentials are published.
c.name: Cardless

c.description: Cardlytics is a commerce media platform that uses first-party purchase data from its financial-institution partners to help advertisers reach consumers inside banking apps with card-linked offers and measurable, closed-loop attribution. Advertisers plan, launch, and measure card-linked campaigns through Ads Manager and advertiser APIs, while banks and neobanks (publishers) embed Merchant Offers and the Cardlytics Rewards Platform into their digital channels via publisher APIs and SDKs. The company also operates the Dosh card-linked network and the Bridg offline purchase-intelligence business, giving advertisers person-level measurement across online and in-store spend. Cardlytics publishes three OpenAPI 3.0.1 definitions through its ReadMe developer hub — a Partner API for advertiser merchant and offer ingestion, reporting and a daily redemption feed; a Campaign Build API covering the Ads Manager campaign object model; and a Publisher API v2 for the bank-side rewards experience — alongside iOS, Android and web SDKs. Nothing is self-service: every credential is issued by an account manager under a partner agreement, and the API hosts answer 403 to anonymous callers. Cardlytics is a public company (NASDAQ: CDLX) and its platform is an enterprise, partnership-based product rather than a self-service developer API.
c.name: Cardlytics

c.description: CardMonster turns ideas and brands into games. The company designs and publishes premium IP-based tabletop titles with global partners such as Disney and Krafton, and builds CardMonster Forge, an AI-powered tool that helps creators turn their own ideas into playable digital prototypes. From physical board games to an online playtesting platform, CardMonster connects creativity and technology to make game creation faster, smarter, and more accessible. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass CardMonster publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.
c.name: CardMonster

c.description: CardMunch was a mobile business-card scanning service that used human transcription to turn photographed business cards into contact records on iOS. Founded as a Y Combinator and 500 Global backed startup, it was acquired by LinkedIn in January 2011 for a reported sum under $3 million and operated as a free LinkedIn-branded iPhone app. LinkedIn discontinued the app on July 11, 2014, migrating its users to Evernote's business-card scanning feature. CardMunch never published a public developer program, API, or SDK, and the cardmunch.com domain was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2016 and now hosts an affiliate content blog. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
c.name: Cardmunch

c.description: CardSpring was a card-linked offers and payments platform that provided an API for building card-linked applications, letting developers connect merchant point-of-sale systems and consumer payment cards to deliver digital coupons, loyalty rewards, and receipt-level offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company was acquired by Twitter in 2014 and subsequently wound down; as of this pass every path on cardspring.com (including the old /help/developer_faq.html) 307-redirects to an Afternic "cardspring.com is for sale" domain-sale lander, developer.cardspring.com fails TLS with no matching certificate, and no first-party CardSpring packages remain on npm or RubyGems. There is no live developer portal, documentation, API, or OpenAPI surface to enrich. Sector: payments.
c.name: CardSpring

c.description: Cardstream is an independent United Kingdom payment gateway providing a white-label payment platform that banks, PSPs, ISOs, acquirers and software companies resell under their own brand. It connects merchants to card schemes (Visa, Mastercard), digital wallets and 150+ Alternative Payment Methods from a single integration, with PCI DSS Level 1 processing, tokenisation, recurring billing, 3-D Secure 2 authentication, risk and fraud checking, and dynamic currency conversion. Its developer surface is a mature form-post gateway API exposed through three integration methods — Hosted (Hosted Payment Pages and Hosted Payment Fields), Direct (server-to-server), and Batch — documented in a public GitBook integration guide and supported by SDKs for PHP, Java, Node.js, Go, Ruby, C#, iOS and Android plus e-commerce modules. Requests are HTTP POST with application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields authenticated by merchantID plus optional password, HMAC message signing and IP allow-listing; the gateway does not publish a downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger definition or a JSON/REST surface.
c.name: Cardstream

c.description: Cardtonic is an Africa-focused fintech platform, operated by The Tonic Technologies, that lets users trade gift cards (sell unused cards for cash and buy over 14,000 local and international gift cards), issue virtual dollar cards, pay bills (airtime, data, electricity, TV, betting), purchase eSIMs in 140+ countries, and shop for gadgets through its Just Gadgets storefront. Cardtonic supports Naira and Cedi settlement for users in Nigeria and Ghana, carries a PCI DSS certification badge, and is registered with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as a Data Controller of Major Importance under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. For businesses, Cardtonic advertises a Gift Card Developer API (waitlist-only, no published contract) and separately publishes a real OpenAPI 3.0.1 contract for its Business API - business signup, login, 2FA, BVN and corporate KYC, and API-key issuance - through an Apidog-hosted documentation site at docs.cardtonic.com, against the base https://api.cardtonic.com/v1.
c.name: Cardtonic

c.description: Cardurion Pharma is a cardiovascular-focused biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for heart disease. It translates expertise in cardiovascular signaling pathways into groundbreaking treatments, acquiring assets, discovering new targets, and advancing programs such as PDE9 and CaMKII inhibitors. The company aims to address unmet patient needs through innovative drug candidates and expanded access programs, with a pipeline spanning multiple therapeutic areas.
c.name: Cardurion Pharma

c.description: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on transforming the treatment of cardiovascular disease and heart failure. Its research and development pipeline centers on novel small-molecule programs including PDE9 inhibition for chronic heart failure (HFrEF and HFpEF) and CaMKII inhibition for cardiac diseases such as catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). Cardurion combines target discovery, adaptive clinical trial design, and precision-medicine approaches, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). The company publishes a corporate and R&D website but does not expose a public developer API surface at this time.
c.name: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals

c.description: Care is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Care

c.description: Care GP is a Sydney-based healthcare technology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building a suite of AI agents that automate the administrative and operational work of Australian general practice clinics. Its products include Samantha (medical document allocation that files inbound emails, faxes, and scans), Veronica (24/7 inbound and outbound phone and booking management), and a Billing beta for billing and debt-collection automation. Care GP states it is ISO 27001 certified with onshore Australian data storage, multi-factor authentication, and encryption, and reports serving 400+ clinic operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a customer web application (agent.caregp.com.au) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition.
c.name: Care GP

c.description: Care.com is a two-sided online marketplace that connects families with caregivers across childcare, senior care, pet care, housekeeping, tutoring, and special-needs care, plus a "Care for Business" employer benefit used by companies such as Google, Starbucks, and Best Buy. Founded in 2007 by Sheila Lirio Marcelo, the company went public on the NYSE (CRCM) in 2014 and was acquired by IAC (IAC Inc.) in February 2020 for approximately $500 million, taking it private. Care.com is consumer- and enterprise-facing and does NOT publish a documented public developer API - there is no developer portal, no public API reference, and no self-service API keys. Its GitHub organization (github.com/caredotcom) contains only internal DevOps/infra tooling, not customer-facing API libraries. The only partner-facing programmatic surface is a private job-import integration inside Care.com Recruiting Solutions / Care for Business, used to sync job postings from an employer ATS; it is provisioned through a partnership agreement rather than openly documented. Note - Care.com is frequently confused with Caring.com (a separate senior-care directory owned by Caring, Inc. that DOES publish a JSON API at docs.caring.com); this entry is about care.com only. Access to the marketplace itself is via paid Basic and Premium memberships; there is no published API pricing.
c.name: Care.com

c.description: Care/of is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Care/of

c.description: CareAcademy (part of Activated Insights) is an online training, compliance, and workforce-management platform for post-acute care — home care, home health, hospice, and senior living organizations. It automates regulatory training assignment, caregiver onboarding, and audit-ready compliance reporting for 2,500+ organizations and 800K+ caregivers. The CareAcademy API lets integration partners (home-care software platforms) create agency organizations and caregivers, provide Single Sign-On into CareAcademy from their own product, and query course-completion and compliance data in real time. The partner API is an OpenAPI 3.0 REST interface using HTTP Basic authentication, published on SwaggerHub, with named integrations for WellSky, AxisCare, AlayaCare, eRSP, Aaniie, and Spectrum TeleTrack Services.
c.name: CareAcademy

c.description: CareBridge is a home and community-based healthcare company that delivers 24/7 virtual and in-home care coordination to high-risk, largely Medicaid populations on behalf of health plans. Its interdisciplinary care teams address members' physical, behavioral, and social health needs, and the company operates three core service lines: 24/7 member support, decision support (durable medical equipment and technology provisioning), and Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) technology used by state Medicaid programs and managed-care organizations. Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, CareBridge was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile therefore captures its public identity and domain-security posture only.
c.name: CareBridge *

c.description: CareClinic MCP is a private OAuth-connected health-tracking service for supported AI assistants: user-authorized schedule and wellness reads, observational summaries, and explicitly confirmed symptom or mood writes. Medication writes remain disabled. MCP-only surface -- there is no public REST contract, by design.
c.name: CareClinic

c.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Carecloud

c.description: Careem is the everything app for the greater Middle East, a super-app operating across the MENAP region (Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan) and headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Founded in 2012 and now owned by Uber, Careem combines mobility (rides, taxi, bike, car rental), food and grocery delivery (Careem Eat, Quik), courier and B2B logistics (Box, Express), and financial services (Careem Pay, remittance, donations) alongside the Careem Plus subscription. Careem does not currently operate a public developer API program or partner API portal; this profile captures its public identity, engineering surface, and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Careem

c.description: Career Karma is a consumer edtech platform that helps people find and compare career training programs and get matched to the right one based on their goals, learning style, schedule, and budget. Its catalog spans technology paths (coding bootcamps, software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, AI, UX design), skilled trades (CDL truck driving, HVAC, electrical), healthcare, beauty, and sales, alongside rankings, school comparisons, financing guidance (scholarships, deferred tuition, GI Bill), and a resource center of career guides. Backed by GV, Career Karma runs a guided quiz-and-advisor matching experience rather than a public developer API; this profile captures the company identity and the security and link surface probed from its public web properties.
c.name: Career Karma

c.description: Careerist is an online education platform that helps individuals launch tech careers quickly. It offers programs in AI automation, QA engineering, and software development, providing mentorship, internships, and a money‑back guarantee.
c.name: Careerist

c.description: Job search engine
c.name: Careerjet

c.description: Carefeed provides a unified platform for senior living communities, integrating admissions, AI‑assisted referrals, employee enablement, resident and family experience, e‑billing, and payments. The SaaS solution connects with existing EHR and HR systems, offering HIPAA‑compliant messaging, automated reminders, and analytics to streamline operations, improve care quality, and reduce administrative overhead. Built for skilled‑nursing and long‑term care facilities, Carefeed aims to replace fragmented software tools with a single, secure system.
c.name: Carefeed

c.description: Carefluence is a US health-IT interoperability vendor whose product is an ONC-certified, FHIR-based Open API platform that EHR, telehealth, remote patient monitoring, HIE and health-analytics vendors license to reach regulatory compliance and to exchange clinical data with other systems. The Carefluence Open API R4 was certified on 2022-06-29 under CHPL ID 15.04.04.2657.Care.R4.01.0.220629 against ONC criteria 170.315 (d)(1,3,9-10,12-13) and (g)(4-7,9-10), including the § 170.315(g)(10) Standardized API for Patient and Population Services; the company states it was the first FHIR-based Open API product to earn ONC 2015 Edition certification, in July 2016, and was an early participant in the Argonaut Project. The platform is a FHIR R4 server (US Core IG v3.1.1, 24 resource types) fronted by a first-party SMART on FHIR OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server, with a data translator for HL7 v2 and C-CDA normalization, adapters for non-FHIR back ends, a built-in integration engine, an asynchronous FHIRops product, and an announced Model Context Protocol server for AI agents.
c.name: Carefluence

c.description: Careforce (Helpcare AI, Inc., d/b/a Careforce) provides an autonomous AI workforce platform for healthcare operations. Its AI agents — Angelica, a care coordinator handling preventive-care outreach, appointment scheduling, reminders, and referral management, and David, a data analyst that pulls and analyzes patient data across EHR and portal systems — integrate with 30+ healthcare platforms including Epic, Cerner, Athenahealth, and NextGen to close care gaps and reduce staff workload. Backed by CRV. Careforce consumes third-party healthcare APIs rather than publishing a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs were found.
c.name: Careforce

c.description: Carefull is a financial safety platform that protects the personal finances of older adults and their family caregivers from fraud, scams, and identity theft. It monitors bank accounts, credit cards, and investment accounts across 12,000+ financial institutions (via Plaid, MX, and Finicity) to detect suspicious activity, duplicate billing, and unusual withdrawals in real time. The service bundles $1M identity theft insurance, dark web and credit-file monitoring, home-title monitoring, a ScamCheck message tool, a secure document Vault and LegacyKit, and view-only access for trusted contacts. Carefull is offered direct to consumers (about $29.99/month with a free trial) and B2B to banks, credit unions, wealth advisory firms, and employers. It is SOC 2 certified. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile enriches the company as a network lead; Carefull publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface (all /.well-known/* paths return the SPA HTML shell).
c.name: Carefull

c.description: CareFusion is a medical technology brand, acquired by BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) in 2015, best known for the Alaris infusion system and the Pyxis automated dispensing product line. CareFusion does not expose a public developer API; instead, its devices and dispensing systems interoperate with hospital EMRs and pharmacy systems over HL7 v2 messaging, smart-pump interoperability middleware, and vendor-managed integration services. The Alaris Infusion Interoperability program wirelessly transmits orders from EMRs (such as Epic and Cerner) into Alaris large-volume and syringe modules and returns infusion status back to the EMR in near real time, using the Alaris Guardrails drug library as a safety layer.
c.name: CareFusion (BD)

c.description: Caregility provides a connected care platform that enables hospitals and health systems to deliver bedside virtual care, telehealth, and remote patient monitoring. Their solutions integrate with Epic and other EHRs, offering virtual nursing, AI‑enhanced clinical insights, and a suite of smart room devices to improve patient outcomes across inpatient, outpatient, home, and rural settings.
c.name: Caregility

c.description: CareGuide is a Canadian company operating a network of online marketplaces that connect families with caregivers across child care, home care, pet care, and elder care, alongside HeartPayroll household payroll services. Its consumer brands include CanadianNanny.ca, Sitter.com, PetSitter.com, ElderCare.com, HouseKeeper.com and a family of "Meet A" professional directories. Backed by 500 Global, CareGuide is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. The company does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.
c.name: CareGuide

c.description: CareHarmony is a chronic care management company delivering coordinated, personalized health services. Their mission is to make personalized, coordinated care possible for every patient through fee‑for‑service programs, remote patient monitoring, and value‑based care solutions. They offer chronic care management, preventive care programs, annual wellness visits, transitional care management, and address social determinants of health.
c.name: Careharmony

c.description: CareJobs.Now aggregates US healthcare job listings and posted pay rates from over 258 employers, providing open datasets of hourly wages, job types, and employer information. Users can browse jobs, explore pay research, and download JSON/CSV files without authentication. The platform aims to increase transparency in healthcare compensation and simplify job search for nurses, CNAs, therapists, and other care professionals.
c.name: CareJobs.Now

c.description: Carelink Solutions Inc. provides mental health and substance abuse services through a network of licensed clinicians. Their platform offers 24‑hour support, online bookings, and personalized care plans, aiming to improve community wellness and holistic health outcomes.
c.name: Carelink

c.description: CareLuLu is a consumer marketplace that helps parents find and compare licensed child care — home daycares, child care centers, and preschools. Families can search across roughly 200,000 licensed programs and filter by location, age, hours, tuition, and availability, then view photos, verified parent reviews, and schedule tours or consultations. The service is positioned as an easy, fast, and free way to find safe, high-quality, affordable child care, and it also lets providers list and market their programs to local parents. Backed by 500 Global. Note — CareLuLu runs a consumer web application (an AMP/React SPA) and an internal API host (api.carelulu.com), but does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs — this profile captures its public website and identity surface only.
c.name: CareLuLu

c.description: Caremedi is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Caremedi

c.description: Caremedical3e74 is a local home medical equipment provider operating in Georgia, USA. It offers a range of medical supplies and equipment for home use, including respiratory devices, mobility aids, and daily living accessories. The company emphasizes compassionate, responsive service and community involvement, partnering with customers and referral sources to ensure high-quality care. Its website provides detailed service listings, contact information for multiple locations, and policies such as terms of use and privacy.
c.name: Caremedical3e74

c.description: CareMerge is a senior living technology company that builds family engagement, care coordination, community engagement, and communications software for senior living and long-term / post-acute care communities. Its platform connects residents, families, and care staff so communities can coordinate care, share activities and calendars, and keep families informed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass CareMerge publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface; its marketing site sits behind a SiteGround (sg-captcha) challenge and its GitHub organization contains internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party client SDK.
c.name: CareMerge

c.description: CareMessage is a healthcare technology non-profit that operates one of the largest patient engagement platforms serving low-income and underserved populations across the United States. Since 2013 the platform has reached more than 20 million patients and is used by roughly 1 in 7 federally qualified health centers plus 200+ free clinics. Its products include 1:1 direct messaging, appointment lifecycle messaging, population outreach, health coaching, closed-loop referrals, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) workflows, and Wellness Copilot, an AI-backed diabetes-management automation. CareMessage does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; access to the platform is through its web application and a login-gated help center. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from CareMessage's public web surface.
c.name: Caremessage

c.description: Caremo is a private in‑home caregiving company owned by Four Vanguards LLC, providing personalized nursing, therapy, and companion services to seniors and post‑operative patients in the San Mateo County area. Founded in 2018, CareMo emphasizes compassionate, family‑like care, offering customized care plans, 24‑hour support, and a range of specialized services such as stroke recovery, Alzheimer’s care, and COVID‑19 rehabilitation. The company’s mission is to make clients feel loved, valued, and well‑cared for through high‑quality, affordable home health solutions.
c.name: Caremo

c.description: Carenation is a scalable telehealth platform that enables complete remote care delivery. It provides virtual consultations, COVID‑19 home care programs, and a suite of digital health services across multiple countries including India, Spain, Greece, Peru, Bangladesh, Mexico, and Nepal. The platform is built to world‑class standards, offering patients and providers a comprehensive, secure, and user‑friendly experience for pediatric, adolescent, and adult care.
c.name: Carenation

c.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.
c.name: Carepatron

c.description: CarePort Health, powered by WellSky, is a healthcare technology company providing care coordination and patient transition management across the entire care continuum. Its platform connects hospitals, health systems, ACOs, physician groups, payers, and post-acute providers to manage discharge planning, referrals, transitions of care, emergency department optimization, utilization and authorization management, and value-based programs. Products include Guide, Connect, Insight, Care Management, Transition, Referral Management, Intake, and Discharge, with EHR integrations for Epic and Cerner. CarePort reports covering 14M lives across roughly 2,000 hospitals in 43 U.S. states. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead (500 Global, Techstars); no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.
c.name: Careport Health

c.description: Carepoynt is a healthcare and wellness focused rewards platform that incentivizes healthy behaviors by awarding Poynts for activities such as doctor visits, exercise, and healthy purchases. Users can redeem points for spa treatments, charitable donations, or gifts, while businesses, providers, employers, and payers can engage customers and improve health outcomes through the Carepoynt network.
c.name: Carepoynt

c.description: CareRev is a healthcare workforce management and on-demand labor marketplace that connects hospitals and health systems directly with local, credentialed clinical professionals — registered nurses, LPN/LVNs, CNAs, surgical and ER techs, medical assistants, respiratory therapists, phlebotomists and mental health techs — without a traditional staffing agency in the middle. Facilities post open shifts from their existing scheduling and HR systems and vetted clinicians browse, claim and self-schedule them in the CareRev mobile app, while CareRev handles credential verification, compliance and payment. The product line spans the CareRev Marketplace (external on-demand talent), IRP+ (internal resource pool control and float-pool visibility for a health system's own staff) and Smart Rates (dynamic rate modeling to control labor spend). CareRev is certified by The Joint Commission under its Health Care Staffing Services program and serves more than 650 facilities across the United States. Integration with a facility's VMS, scheduling and workforce-management stack (including UKG Dimensions via the UKG Connect Technology Partner Program) is delivered through private, partner-scoped API connections; CareRev publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass.
c.name: CareRev

c.description: CareSense Pte. Ltd. (CareSense.ai) is a Singapore-based preventive digital health company building AI-powered health coaching. Its flagship product is Mandy, a 24/7 AI health coach delivered over chat and voice, paired with the CareSense.ai app — a personal health dashboard covering nutrition, exercise, sleep and stress — and integrated health services including blood testing and telemedicine. The company sells both to individuals and to enterprise teams as a workplace wellbeing programme. CareSense was incorporated in Singapore on 14 June 2024 (UEN 202424008M), registered at 160 Robinson Road #14-04, and was founded by Lucas Ngoo, co-founder of Carousell, and Julian Koo, founder of the home-care platform Jaga-Me. As of this enrichment pass CareSense publishes no public API, developer portal, API documentation or SDKs; its technology surface is consumer and enterprise applications fronted by a Vanta-hosted trust center.
c.name: Caresense

c.description: Careship (operated by Care Companion GmbH, Berlin) is a German senior-care marketplace that connects elderly people and their families with vetted, non-medical everyday helpers ("Alltagshilfen") from their own neighborhoods. The platform covers companionship, shopping, household support, mobility and leisure, light personal care, and dementia support, and helps families finance care through statutory long-term care insurance (Pflegekasse). Careship operates across 20+ German cities including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, and Dresden. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum; it is a consumer care-services business with no public developer or API surface at this time.
c.name: Careship

c.description: CareStack is an all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management platform used by dental practices and DSOs (dental service organizations) for scheduling, patient management, clinical charting, billing, payments, revenue cycle management, and analytics. For developers, CareStack exposes a RESTful API surface covering patient resources (patient information, health conditions, payment summaries, communications, treatment/procedure codes, and documents) and practice resources, complemented by webhooks for real-time data propagation and scheduled data extracts. The platform is HIPAA compliant and carries SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, and GDPR attestations, published via its trust center. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
c.name: CareStack

c.description: Caresyntax is a surgical intelligence company that builds a vendor-neutral, enterprise-scale data platform for the operating room. Founded in 2013 in Berlin and now dual-headquartered in Berlin and San Francisco, it captures video, audio, image, device, EMR, financial and outcomes data from inside and around the OR and applies AI analytics to it — delivering pre-operative workflow optimization, real-time intraoperative decision support, and post-operative clinical safety, quality and utilization insights. The platform pairs the PRIME365 vendor-neutral OR / medical-device integration layer with the qvident surgical performance-management and analytics suite, and is deployed in more than 4,000 operating rooms worldwide. Caresyntax sells to hospitals and surgery centers, MedTech manufacturers and insurers, and integrates with EMR, PACS and scheduling systems. It operates an API gateway at api.caresyntax.com, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract — integration is delivered through enterprise and partner engagements.
c.name: Caresyntax

c.description: Caretaker is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Caretaker

c.description: Caretaker Medical provides the VitalStream platform, a device that delivers continuous, beat‑to‑beat hemodynamic monitoring both invasively and non‑invasively. The system is sold to hospitals and other care settings for use in pre‑operative, operating‑room, ICU, step‑down and ambulatory surgery environments, integrating with existing GE Carescape and Philips Intellivue monitors.
c.name: CareTaker Medical

c.description: Caretta is a Y Combinator-backed (W26) startup building a real-time AI platform for sales teams. Its assistant joins reps in live calls to take notes and surface relevant answers to information requests, questions, and objections in real time, drawing on an organizational knowledge layer it calls "Caretta Nous" that is built from company documentation, websites, internal playbooks, and top-performer conversations. After calls it supports teamspaces with analysis, morning briefs, and follow-up Q&A, and integrates with tools such as Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio, Odoo, Cal.com, Slack, Telegram and Notion. The company raised $1.3M in pre-seed funding. Caretta's developer surface is agent-first rather than REST-first: it publishes a documented remote Model Context Protocol server at gateway.caretta.app/mcp with OAuth-scoped access to calls, transcripts and todos, a signed HMAC-SHA256 webhook surface that pushes transcripts, AI notes and evaluated metrics to customer endpoints, and a Zoom meeting-link integration. Its docs host serves llms.txt, an A2A agent card and a published Agent Skill. Caretta's own documentation states that a public REST API for endpoint management is planned but not yet available, so no OpenAPI description is published.
c.name: Caretta

c.description: Carevision Inc. is an AI-powered digital health company whose platform turns any camera into a 60-second contactless cardiometabolic wellness scanner. Using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) and deep learning models trained on 12M+ patient records, it extracts 30+ physiological parameters — including heart rate, blood pressure indicators, stress index, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation — and produces a comprehensive digital health persona covering 15+ cardiometabolic conditions. Carevision operates under the FDA General Wellness Policy (it is not a medical device or diagnostic tool) and is delivered as a kiosk, an embedded/white-label SDK for iOS and Android, or a web integration to hospitals and clinics, health insurers, pharmacy chains, diagnostic laboratories, wellness apps, and teleconsultation platforms, integrating with EMR/HIS systems.
c.name: Carevision

c.description: Carewell is an online medical supply retailer offering a wide range of incontinence, nutrition, wound care, and personal care products. It provides a concierge service to help customers navigate healthcare needs, supports FSA/HSA eligible purchases, and delivers supplies across the United States with free delivery and autoship options.
c.name: Carewell

c.description: Carewellfamily is a healthcare-focused company identified through the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. While detailed public information is limited, the organization appears to operate in the health and wellness sector, potentially offering APIs related to patient care, health data management, or wellness services. Further investigation is required to uncover specific API offerings, documentation, and technical endpoints.
c.name: Carewellfamily

c.description: Careyaya is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Careyaya

c.description: CareZone is a consumer digital-health company (Care Zone Inc., backed by Obvious Ventures) offering a medication-management and family health-organization platform. Its mobile app lets people scan pill bottles to track medications, set reminders, log health readings such as blood glucose and blood pressure, and organize care information for themselves and loved ones, with a free medication delivery service and Medicare savings consultations. CareFlow, CareZone's pharmacy platform, automates traditional pharmacy workflows behind an ecommerce experience. The app reports over 5 million installs. CareZone operates as a consumer product and does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.
c.name: Carezone

c.description: CARFAX is a vehicle history reporting company that provides VIN-based history reports, dealer inventory solutions, QuickVIN license plate decoding, and used car valuations based on service records, accident history, ownership history, and title data. APIs are available to dealers, lenders, insurers, and service shops through enterprise partnership agreements.
c.name: CARFAX

c.description: Cargado, Inc. operates a modern freight marketplace and market intelligence platform for Mexico and Canada. It connects brokers with over 2,350 vetted carriers, offering real carrier bids and market rates. The service provides free access for carriers and paid plans for shippers, featuring API access, integrations, and detailed market insights.
c.name: Cargado

c.description: Cargo Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company focused on developing next‑generation CAR‑T cell therapies for cancer. After a merger with Concentra Biosciences, the company has restructured its pipeline and continues to explore strategic alternatives while maintaining a core platform for cell‑based therapeutics.
c.name: Cargo Therapeutics

c.description: Cargo X (CargoX) is a Sao Paulo based Brazilian logistics technology and fintech company, founded in 2013, that operates one of Brazil's largest digital freight marketplaces - matching shippers (embarcadores) with carriers (transportadoras) and independent truck drivers. Beyond freight brokerage the platform provides dedicated freight desk operations, driver qualification and real-time cargo monitoring, automated issuance of Brazilian transport tax documents (CT-e and MDF-e), cargo insurance, receivables financing and working-capital credit for carriers, and green-freight / ESG programs that reduce empty return trips. The company reached unicorn status with a USD 200M Series F in October 2021 co-led by Tencent and SoftBank, with Valor Capital Group, Lightrock and Oikos participating.
c.name: Cargo X

c.description: cargo.one is a Berlin-headquartered digital freight platform that operates as an AI-native operating system for air and ocean freight logistics. The platform unifies freight forwarder operations by centralizing rates, partners, and systems on a single end-to-end surface shared between human teams and AI agents. For freight forwarders, cargo.one provides air e-booking with 76+ integrated airlines (300+ total network), ocean freight rate management with 10+ liner integrations, multimodal quoting across air, ocean, road, and local charges, a Rate Management System for buy/sell/internal rates, a branded 24/7 self-service Customer Portal, analytics dashboards, a 24/7 Global Network for cross-timezone quoting, and an API Suite with native TMS integrations for CargoWise, Cargospot, and Descartes. For carriers, cargo.one delivers a market-intelligence and customer-access platform spanning the end-to-end commercial cycle. AI workflows are offered in three deployment modes — Co-pilot (approval-based), Supervised (autonomous with escalation), and Autonomous — covering rate management, rate procurement, quoting, booking, and customer support automation, backed by retrieval-augmented generation and a cargo.one MCP Server for custom solutions. Notable customers include Lufthansa Cargo, Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, Maersk, CMA CGM, Hellmann, and Rhenus Logistics. cargo.one's API and TMS integrations are partner / enterprise offerings — there is no public self-serve OpenAPI specification, developer sandbox, or open-source SDK published outside of customer onboarding.
c.name: cargo.one

c.description: CargoAi is a Singapore-headquartered air cargo technology company that operates CargoMART, a digital marketplace where freight forwarders search routes, schedules, capacity and rates across 680+ airlines, book them, transmit the electronic air waybill, and track the shipment end to end. It sits in the middle of the air cargo chain as an aggregator between forwarders and their TMS vendors on one side and airline reservation and messaging systems on the other. Its API posture is genuinely public in documentation and sales-gated in access - the CargoCONNECT developer portal at cargoai.readme.io is open to anyone with no login and publishes a real OpenAPI 3.1 definition per operation, but an x-api-key is issued only after a commercial conversation with the CargoAi enterprise team. The published contract is a proprietary REST shape rather than an IATA ONE Record interface, though the payloads it carries are IATA-native - AWB numbers with airline prefixes, IATA airport and airline codes, Special Handling Codes, IATA cargo status event codes, FWB and FHL message content, and CO2 figures computed per IATA Recommended Practice 1678.
c.name: CargoAi

c.description: Cargobase is a cloud-based Transportation Management System (TMS) for enterprise shippers that automates spot-buy and contract freight procurement across air, ocean, road, and courier modes. Shippers request quotes, compare carrier and forwarder rates apples-to-apples, award and execute shipments, track them in real time, audit freight invoices, and report on carbon emissions and logistics-provider performance from a single platform. Founded in 2013, Cargobase serves automotive, aviation, semiconductor, machinery, energy, and oil-and-gas shippers worldwide, is ISO/IEC 27001 certified and SOC 2 compliant, and is backed by 500 Global.
c.name: Cargobase

c.description: CargoBeamer provides a smart, reliable and environmentally friendly system for intermodal transport of semi‑trailers by rail across Europe. It connects logistics companies, freight forwarders and shippers with a growing network of routes and terminals, aiming to reduce road congestion and emissions while offering flexible, fast rail‑based freight solutions.
c.name: Cargobeamer

c.description: Cargobot provides a platform to build and manage local electric vehicle charging networks, enabling operators to deploy, monitor, and monetize charging stations. The solution offers hardware‑agnostic integration, real‑time usage analytics, and revenue‑sharing tools for fleet operators and site owners.
c.name: Cargobot

c.description: CargoDocs, operated by EssDocs, is a digital trade documentation platform that eliminates paper-based shipping documents by letting carriers, shippers, banks, and partner platforms issue, sign, transfer, and surrender original electronic bills of lading (eBoL), sea waybills (SWB), warehouse warrants (eWW), and supporting trade documents. CargoDocs DocEx is used by container lines, NVOCCs, bulk/tanker carriers, commodity shippers, and trade finance banks to move documents in minutes rather than days while retaining negotiability and legal effect. Developers interact with CargoDocs through three OpenAPI-described REST APIs hosted on ReadMe - the Partner API (embed DocEx in third-party platforms), the Issuer API (carrier/NVOCC issuance and amendments), and the Customer Data/Docs API (exporter drafting and back-office integration).
c.name: CargoDocs

c.description: Cargofy is a Ukrainian‑American logistics technology firm that develops AI agents, called digital workers, for shippers, freight brokers, carriers and third‑party logistics providers. These agents automate multi‑step logistics workflows, handling tasks such as dispatch, tendering, document processing and shipment tracking across integrated communication and transportation systems.
c.name: Cargofy

c.description: Cargolux Airlines International S.A. is Europe's largest all-cargo airline, headquartered at Luxembourg Findel Airport in Luxembourg and operating a global Boeing 747 freighter network under IATA designator CV and air waybill prefix 172 (with Cargolux Italia on prefix 356). In the logistics chain Cargolux is the main-leg air carrier: it sells capacity to freight forwarders and general sales agents rather than to shippers, hands cargo to terminal and ground handling operators such as its Luxcargo Handling subsidiary, and files customs and security data on behalf of the contracted forwarder. Its API posture is honestly a customer-contract one. Cargolux publishes no developer portal and no machine-readable contract of any kind — developer.cargolux.com, developers.cargolux.com and docs.cargolux.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ all return 404 on www.cargolux.com. The only public self-service surfaces are HTML: a track-and-trace widget and a flight scheduler on the marketing site, plus a login-walled Customer Portal at my.cargolux.com. A real quote-and- booking API exists, but it is a bilateral, commercially negotiated forwarder interface — piloted with Kuehne+Nagel in 2021 and extended to DB Schenker — with no published reference, and it is complemented by indirect distribution through the cargo.one, CargoAi and WebCargo by Freightos marketplaces. Underneath, Cargolux runs IBS Software's iCargo SaaS cargo management system and holds a large minority stake in Luxembourg's CHAMP Cargosystems, whose developer.champ.aero portal is the developer surface Cargolux's ecosystem actually reads — CHAMP's, not Cargolux's. IATA e-AWB "Single Process" is documented; no IATA ONE Record or Cargo-XML publication was found.
c.name: Cargolux

c.description: Cargomatic is a technology-enabled marketplace for local freight and drayage that connects shippers with a network of more than 35,000 professional truck drivers across the top 20 ports in the continental United States. Its platform automates quoting, booking, dispatch, tracking, and document exchange for drayage, intermodal, less-than-truckload (LTL), full-truckload (FTL), and white-glove final-mile delivery. Cargomatic exposes a public REST API (the Cargomatic Public API) so shippers and carriers can automate the same quoting, order-creation, shipment-status, stop-management, driver-assignment, and document workflows available in the Cargomatic portal, authenticating with JWT bearer tokens issued from an authentication endpoint. The company is headquartered in Long Beach, California and is backed by Canaan Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund.
c.name: Cargomatic

c.description: Cargon Tech B.V. is a supply-chain and logistics technology company backed by 500 Global. Its public presence at cargon.com positions Cargon as a fast, innovative supply-chain platform with powerful analytical tools for shippers and carriers, while the related Cargon TMS product (cargon.tech) offers a cloud transport-management system for small carriers and freight forwarders covering dispatch, fleet management, invoicing and Timocom integration. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (the cargon.com site is a client-rendered single-page app that returns its index shell for unknown paths), so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signal only.
c.name: Cargon Tech

c.description: CargoSmart (now operating as IQAX) is a global shipment management software provider that gives shippers, consignees, freight forwarders, and logistics service providers ocean freight booking, container tracking, vessel scheduling, and shipping documentation tools across multiple ocean carriers. CargoSmart co-founded the Global Shipping Business Network (GSBN), a blockchain-based data exchange for carriers, terminals, banks, and customs authorities, and exposes its APIs so trading partners can embed booking, visibility, schedule, and documentation workflows directly into TMS, ERP, and supply-chain platforms.
c.name: CargoSmart

c.description: Cargoson is an Estonian B2B cloud transport management software (TMS) platform for manufacturers and wholesalers. Its unified REST API lets shippers request freight rates, book shipments, generate labels, and track deliveries across 2,000+ carriers using one set of endpoints, authentication, and data formats. Cargoson is carrier-neutral; customers contract directly with their own carriers and upload their own freight rates.
c.name: Cargoson

c.description: CargoWise is WiseTech Global's logistics execution platform - a single-database ERP for international freight forwarding, customs, warehousing, transport, and landside logistics. Its integration surface is delivered primarily through eAdaptor, which pairs a RESTful XML inbound service (push, query, add, and update records) with a SOAP-based outbound service (a webhook equivalent that emits messages on milestones). Payloads use CargoWise's Universal XML schemas - Universal Shipment (XUS), Universal Event (XUE), and Universal Transaction - or the legacy Native XML format. Newer REST integration (eAdaptor Next / xHub) adds OAuth 2.0 authorization-code access. The integration API is real but heavily gated - the eAdaptor Developers Guide and endpoint details are released only after a customer purchases the eAdaptor modules, and partner access runs through WiseTech accreditation and certification. Endpoints below are modeled from public developer references; the authoritative specification is not publicly published.
c.name: CargoWise

c.description: CarGurus is an automotive shopping and dealer marketing platform that connects car shoppers with franchise and independent dealers through data-driven listings, its Instant Market Value (IMV) deal ratings, and dealer reviews. For developers and partners, CarGurus publishes a small set of documented HTTP APIs under /Cars/api/ - an open Car Selector API for building new/used search widgets, and partner/dealer-gated APIs for Instant Market Value, dealer reviews, and dealer performance statistics (leads, VDPs, SRPs, impressions). Dealer inventory itself is ingested through inventory feeds (feed providers / IMT), not a documented public pull API, and leads are delivered to dealer CRMs rather than exposed as a public REST endpoint.
c.name: CarGurus

c.description: Cari Health empowers clinicians with rapid, personalized methadone dosing data, delivering actionable clinical insights at the point of care. By bridging the data gap, CARI Health improves patient outcomes, supports clinicians with real-time metabolite measurements, and advances opioid use disorder treatment through innovative, data‑driven technology backed by NIH, NSF, and leading accelerators.
c.name: Cari Health

c.description: Caribou is a Denver-based fintech that helps drivers lower their monthly car payments by refinancing existing auto loans through a network of banks, credit unions, and community lenders. Customers check personalized rates with a soft credit pull (no score impact), compare offers, add co-borrowers, and complete refinancing online, and can bundle optional vehicle protection plans. Caribou reports 150,000+ customers and average savings of about $162/month. The company exposes a consumer web application and a contact-gated partner integration program (click-out and API options for affiliates); it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API at this time.
c.name: Caribou

c.description: Caribou Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative genome‑edited allogeneic cell therapies. Leveraging its proprietary CRISPR hybrid RNA‑DNA (chRDNA) technology, Caribou creates off‑the‑shelf CAR‑T cell therapies aimed at treating devastating diseases such as cancers and genetic disorders. The company emphasizes precision genome editing, armored cell therapies, and rapid patient access, positioning itself as a leader in the CRISPR field.
c.name: Caribou Biosciences

c.description: Caribou Financial is a fintech platform that helps consumers refinance auto loans by matching them with multiple lenders to find the best rates and terms. The service aggregates loan offers, provides personalized recommendations, and streamlines the application process through an online portal. Founded to simplify vehicle financing, Caribou Financial leverages data-driven insights to improve loan approval odds and reduce borrowing costs for borrowers across the United States.
c.name: Caribou Financial

c.description: Carillon Technologies is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Carillon Technologies

c.description: Cariloop provides a Caregiver Support Platform that helps employers offer backup care benefits and guidance to employees managing caregiving responsibilities. The solution includes expert tools, flexible support, and resources to enable working caregivers to manage care with confidence, improving employee wellbeing and retention.
c.name: Cariloop

c.description: Caring32b6 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Caring32b6

c.description: Cariqa provides backend-to-backend payment and access infrastructure for EV charging across Europe. Its Connect API lets OEMs, mobility services, fleets and platforms offer electric-vehicle charging through a single integration — discovering charging stations and live connector availability, creating and managing users, collecting payment methods via Stripe (PSD2/SCA compliant), starting and stopping charging sessions on 900,000+ charge points, and retrieving session history, debts and invoices. Cariqa removes reseller markups so charge point operators set the price drivers pay, while platforms earn a transaction revenue share. Backed by Anthemis and Techstars.
c.name: Cariqa

c.description: Caris Life Sciences is a molecular science and precision oncology company that delivers comprehensive tumor profiling (Caris Molecular Intelligence / MI Profiling) and a clinico-genomic real-world data platform (CODEai). Clinician access is through the Caris+Portal and partner-provisioned EHR integrations (Epic Orders and Results Anywhere, OncoEMR/Flatiron, iKnowMed, and other CMS-certified systems). Caris does not publish a public, self-serve developer API; integration is partner- and contract-based.
c.name: Caris Life Sciences

c.description: Caristodiagnostics is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Caristodiagnostics

c.description: Carium is a virtual care management platform delivering advanced remote patient monitoring and health engagement solutions. It integrates bi-directional EHR data, provides intelligent automation, and supports care teams with real-time analytics to improve patient outcomes and operational efficiency across health systems and payors.
c.name: Carium

c.description: Carketa is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Carketa

c.description: Carku (卡儿酷) is a Shenzhen‑based technology company founded in 2011, specializing in lithium‑battery powered emergency power solutions for trucks, commercial vehicles, and outdoor use. Their product line includes 12V/24V automotive jump‑start units, heavy‑duty truck power packs, portable solar panels, and inverter systems. The company emphasizes smart, lightweight emergency power and offers a range of accessories and services for vehicle and outdoor power needs.
c.name: Carku

c.description: Carla (carlaf042) is a next‑generation private travel platform offering seamless, transparent, and instant booking of private jets, yachts, and villas. It supports both fiat (Stripe) and cryptocurrency payments, provides 24/7 concierge service, and emphasizes privacy, security, and advanced data protection. The company operates from its website carla.com, presenting its services, pricing, terms, and privacy policies, and offers a loyalty program and partner opportunities for jet owners.
c.name: Carlaf042

c.description: Carlisle Companies Incorporated (NYSE: CSL) is a global diversified manufacturer of highly engineered building envelope products and solutions, serving commercial and residential construction, insulation, roofing, waterproofing, and specialty markets. Carlisle's primary operating segment is Carlisle Construction Materials (CCM), which includes brands such as Carlisle SynTec Systems, Hunter Panels, Henry Company, MB Technology, and WIP Industrial. Carlisle does not publish a public developer API; distributors and direct contractors transact through the Carlisle Customer Success Portal, and commercial trading partners integrate with Carlisle using standard X12 EDI transactions (850, 855, 856, 810) over AS2/SFTP.
c.name: Carlisle Companies

c.description: Carlsmed (Nasdaq: CARL) is a Carlsbad, California medical technology company that builds personalized spine surgery. Its aprevo technology platform combines AI-enabled segmentation of a patient's own imaging with prior-outcomes data to produce a personalized surgical plan and patient-specific interbody fusion devices, manufactured on a digital production line and delivered to hospitals in under ten days. The platform is FDA-cleared for lumbar and cervical indications, holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation, and earned CMS New Technology Add-On Payment status for cervical fusion in 2025. Surgeons review, approve and track plans through the myaprevo iOS application. Carlsmed operates under ISO 13485 and MDSAP certification and completed its IPO in July 2025. It publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.
c.name: Carlsmed

c.description: Carma is an Australian online used-car retailer that lets consumers buy, sell, and trade in pre-owned vehicles entirely online. Every car is inspected and reconditioned, and the platform bundles financing through partner lenders, home delivery, trade-in valuations, a 7-day money-back guarantee, a 3-month warranty, and NRMA roadside assistance as an alternative to the traditional dealership experience. Backed by General Catalyst since 2022, Carma is headquartered in Sydney, Australia. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched from Carma's public web surface; Carma publishes no public developer API at this time.
c.name: Carma

c.description: Carmatecinc is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Carmatecinc

c.description: CarMax (NYSE: KMX) is the largest retailer of used cars in the United States, operating an omnichannel business that spans brick-and-mortar stores, carmax.com online purchasing, home delivery, financing, appraisals, and trade-ins. CarMax does not publish a public developer portal, but its engineering organization operates an extensive internal API program built around distinct API roles (Data Access Layer, Business Logic Layer, Server-Driven UI, Backend for Frontend). Public-facing APIs documented by the CarMax Engineering Blog include a Store Locations API and a Vehicle Inventory API, and CarMax has publicly discussed a Server-Driven UI API that controls vehicle search filters across web and mobile. Partner and syndication integrations are handled case by case rather than through a self-service portal.
c.name: CarMax

c.description: CarMD specializes in automotive diagnostics and insights, selling the CarMD Connect vehicle-health device and publishing the CarMD Vehicle Health Index. Its developer story has two very different halves today. The historic CarMD Vehicle API (CarScan) — code definitions, vehicle images, repair and upcoming-issue prediction — is documented at api.carmd.com and still linked from the carmd.com footer, but that host refused TCP connections on ports 80 and 443 when probed on 2026-08-27, and the old carmd.com/api pricing page now returns 404. Meanwhile the rebuilt carmd.com storefront serves a live, anonymous agent surface: an llms.txt, a Universal Commerce Protocol merchant profile, a working MCP endpoint with thirteen commerce tools, and an anonymously introspectable Storefront GraphQL API.
c.name: CarMD

c.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.
c.name: Carmera *

c.description: Carmoola is a UK-based, mobile-first car finance platform that lets consumers get a pre-approved budget in minutes through its app, then pay dealers or private sellers directly with a virtual card. It offers Hire Purchase (HP) and Personal Contract Purchase (PCP) financing, soft credit checks that do not affect the applicant's score, flexible repayment terms, and the ability to refinance an existing car loan. Carmoola is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and is backed by investors including QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Carmoola operates a consumer app rather than a public developer API.
c.name: Carmoola

c.description: Carmot Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company focused on developing therapeutics for obesity and diabetes. In early 2024 the company was acquired by Roche, becoming part of the Roche Group. The company leverages a chemotype evolution platform to discover novel incretin receptor signaling targets, advancing a pipeline of potential treatments for metabolic disease.
c.name: Carmot Therapeutics

c.description: Carnegie Mellon University is a private research university in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, ranked 49th in the QS World University Rankings. It operates no central developer portal, no API gateway and no institution-wide developer program — api.cmu.edu and data.cmu.edu do not exist as developer surfaces — but unlike most of this cohort it does genuinely engineer public APIs, in three unrelated units that share no identifier, envelope or error model. The Delphi research group runs the Delphi Epidata API for real-time epidemiological surveillance; the CERT Coordination Center at the Software Engineering Institute runs the Vulnerability Notes API, the machine-readable record of coordinated vulnerability disclosure; and University Libraries self-hosts the Library Publishing Service, five open-access journals behind a REST API and a conformant OAI-PMH 2.0 provider on CMU's own hardware. None of the three publishes an OpenAPI, a changelog on the API host, a status page or a deprecation policy, and both research APIs return errors with HTTP 200. Everything else that carries CMU's name is a tenancy: KiltHub is figshare, Canvas is Instructure, and the eleven figshare-derived contracts this profile held until 2026-08-19 were a vendor's engineering credited to the university.
c.name: Carnegie Mellon University

c.description: Carnival Corporation & plc is the world's largest cruise company operating eight cruise line brands (Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, Cunard, P&O Cruises, Costa Cruises, AIDA Cruises), plus the White Pass and Yukon Route. Carnival operates the OceanMedallion wearable IoT technology and mobile experience platform, the Carnival HUB app, the Princess MedallionClass app, and a portfolio of guest-facing digital experiences across its fleet of over 90 ships.
c.name: Carnival

c.description: Carnival Mobile (carnival.io) was a mobile relationship management platform, backed by GV, that let marketers segment users and deliver push notifications, in-app messages, rich media and an in-app message stream from inside native iOS and Android apps. Sailthru acquired Carnival and rebranded the product Sailthru Mobile; it ships today as the Marigold Mobile SDK. The lineage is still directly observable: docs.carnival.io 301-redirects to docs.mobile.sailthru.com, which 301-redirects to sdkdevelopers.meetmarigold.com, and the current documentation still carries Carnival-era pages such as the iBeacons guide. The original carnivalmobile GitHub organization remains public, and the iOS, Android and React Native SDKs are still published to CocoaPods and npm under the first-party "carnival" maintainer account, which makes them the continuing distribution path for this company's developer surface. Carnival Mobile has no independently documented public REST API; its developer contract is an on-device SDK.
c.name: Carnival Mobile

c.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.
c.name: Carnot Fleet

c.description: Carnot Innovations is a Hong Kong-based building energy management company that applies AI, machine learning, and advanced data analytics to optimize HVAC systems and reduce energy consumption across commercial buildings, data centers, hospitals, railways, and sewage treatment facilities in the Asia-Pacific region. Its platform delivers AI-driven energy optimization, predictive maintenance and fault detection for chillers, pumps, cooling towers, and air handling units, analytics dashboards for facility managers, and continuous commissioning insights, reporting outcomes such as 15% energy cost reductions, 90% hidden-fault detection, and 15 million kWh per year of energy savings across its deployment portfolio. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Carnot Innovations does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.
c.name: Carnot Innovations

c.description: Carnotcompression (Carnot Compression Inc.) commercializes proprietary isothermal compression technology that delivers low‑temperature, oil‑free compressed air on a 100 % duty cycle. The patented process captures waste heat during compression, reducing energy use and carbon emissions for industrial, commercial and residential applications. The company is based in Scotts Valley, California and is currently beta‑testing models targeting 15‑30 CFM at 100‑150 PSI.
c.name: Carnotcompression

c.description: CarNow is an AI-enabled conversion platform built specifically for automotive dealerships, helping them turn more website visitors into leads, more leads into sales, and more buyers into lifelong service customers. Its product suite spans website solutions (AI-powered chat, digital retail, and shop-by-payment experiences), sales follow-up automation (Cruise Control, which prioritizes high-intent shoppers and automates nurture workflows), and service retention (Lane Assist, which drives post-sale engagement and service scheduling). CarNow works with more than 4,000 dealer partners and integrates with major OEM programs including Acura, Audi, BMW, Ford, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Land Rover, and Lexus. The company is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and is backed by Battery Ventures. CarNow does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its api.carnow.com endpoint is a partner/internal AWS API Gateway that requires authentication.
c.name: CarNow

c.description: Carolina BioOncology Institute (CBOI) is a physician-owned Phase I oncology clinical research clinic and translational laboratory in Huntersville, North Carolina, founded by Dr. John Powderly II. It runs first-in-human and early-phase immunotherapy trials for patients with advanced solid tumors, having opened more than 100 oncology trials over fifteen years, and operates the Human Applications Lab — a cGMP-capable cell-processing and biorepository facility developing autologous cellular therapies — alongside research-use-only analytical and clinical lab analysis services for trial sponsors. CBOI is the parent company of BioCytics and an openEHR Industry Partner. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract; the only machine-readable surface on its domain is the stock WordPress REST API its CMS emits, which is not a product API and is deliberately not registered here.
c.name: Carolina BioOncology Institute

c.description: CarOnSale is an AI-supported B2B marketplace for used-car trading across Europe, operated by Castle Tech GmbH. Licensed dealers, OEMs, fleet operators, and leasing companies buy and sell used vehicles through digital auctions built on standardized 110-point condition assessments, AI-based pricing and valuation, and integrated transport and financing services. The platform connects sellers (dealer groups, OEMs, leasing and rental companies) with a European network of professional buyers, handling procurement, price discovery, settlement, and logistics end to end. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.
c.name: CarOnSale

c.description: Carota is a cutting‑edge leader in vehicle OTA (over‑the‑air) solutions, providing FOTA and OTA services for smart mobility, smart cockpit, MaaS, fleet management, and AIoT. The company offers a platform that enables automotive OEMs and suppliers to deploy software updates securely and efficiently across connected vehicles, enhancing safety, functionality, and user experience.
c.name: Carota

c.description: Carousell is a Singapore-headquartered classifieds and recommerce marketplace founded in 2012 that lets people buy and sell secondhand and new goods, cars, and property across Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. The Carousell Group operates a family of consumer marketplace brands including Carousell, Cho Tot, Mudah, OneShift, Laku6, Refash, and Ox Street, spanning general classifieds, automotive, and recommerce verticals. Carousell was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; it is a consumer marketplace with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time.
c.name: Carousell

c.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.
c.name: Carpenter Technology

c.description: Carpool Logistics provides end‑to‑end vehicle logistics with a documented chain of custody, moving over 200,000 vehicles annually for dealers, OEMs, fleets and individuals. Their platform offers managed transport, white‑glove home delivery, auction services, and digital tools like a browser extension and CarPass identity‑verified vehicle release, all accessible via a modern web portal.
c.name: Carpool Logistics

c.description: Carpooling.com GmbH was one of Europe's largest ridesharing / carpooling platforms, founded in Munich, Germany and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It connected drivers with empty seats to passengers travelling the same route across Europe. In April 2015 the company was acquired by the French ridesharing operator BlaBlaCar and its operations were merged into that platform. The carpooling.com domain and every developer-facing subdomain (developer / api / docs) now redirect to BlaBlaCar (blablacar.co.uk), and no independent Carpooling developer portal, API, or specification remains. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record; there is no live API surface of its own to enrich.
c.name: Carpooling

c.description: Carputty provides flexible auto financing solutions, offering consumers real-time, transparent lines of credit for vehicle purchases. Their platform enables users to pre‑qualify for loans without impacting credit scores, choose financing terms, and manage the process online. Carputty aims to simplify car ownership by delivering clear, fast, and user‑friendly financing options, backed by proprietary valuation tools and a mission to rewrite industry rules.
c.name: Carputty
