c.description: Citystoragesystems, operating as City Storage, LLC, provides self‑storage solutions across multiple U.S. locations. Founded in 1996, the company combines innovative site planning, award‑winning architectural design, and strong economic performance to offer climate‑controlled units, secure access, and convenient loading docks. It serves residential and business customers, focusing on community‑friendly development and value creation in real estate.
c.name: Citystoragesystems

c.description: CivaTech Oncology is a Durham, North Carolina medical device manufacturer that develops polymer-encapsulated low dose rate (LDR) brachytherapy radiation sources for the treatment of solid tumors. Its FDA-cleared product line includes CivaSheet, a flexible, bioabsorbable, unidirectional planar source that can be custom-sized in the operating room and shields healthy tissue; CivaString, a polymer-encapsulated brachytherapy seed used for prostate and other localized cancers; and CivaDerm for dermatological applications. The company markets to radiation oncologists and surgical teams across pancreatic, sarcoma, colorectal, gynecologic, head and neck, lung and prostate indications, and its research has been supported by NIH/NCI and SBIR programs. It publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CivaTech Oncology

c.description: Civic is a digital identity and security platform offering authentication, identity verification, and AI agent security infrastructure. Core products include Civic Hub (a Model Context Protocol gateway with guardrails, audit logging, secret management, and instant revocation for AI agents connecting to tools), Civic Auth (OAuth 2.0 / PKCE authentication for web and mobile apps with email, Google, and Web3 wallet sign-in plus embedded wallets on Solana and EVM chains), and Civic Labs (open-source agent infrastructure components). Originally known as a Web3 identity and KYC verification platform issuing Civic Passes (non-transferable on-chain tokens representing verified user attributes), Civic has evolved into a broader agent security layer. The Hub MCP gateway exposes a single Streamable HTTP endpoint backed by 80+ pre-built MCP server integrations and is compatible with 23+ AI agent frameworks.
c.name: Civic

c.description: Civic Roundtable is a government operations platform that gives public sector organizations one place for the people, partners, and knowledge behind every mission. It combines Workspaces for cross-agency collaboration, a Knowledge Base for centralized search across systems, Communications for multi-channel stakeholder outreach, a CRM for contact and engagement tracking, Insights for data-driven decision analytics, and government-focused AI & Automation. The platform integrates with tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Google Workspace, Slack, Salesforce, and HubSpot, runs on AWS GovCloud, and serves more than 4,000 organizations across all 50 U.S. states. It maintains SOC 2 Type II, FedRAMP High ATO, FIPS 140-2, and NIST 800-171 security posture. Civic Roundtable is backed by General Catalyst.
c.name: Civic Roundtable

c.description: Cívica Digital is a Mexican civic-technology company, founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, that helps governments, public institutions, and organizations design, build, and launch digital services for citizens. Its product portfolio includes Urbem, a platform for digitizing government procedures and citizen-facing services; Signum, a digital document and official-records management system with electronic signatures; and a suite of conversational AI agents that support citizens over WhatsApp, phone, and web. The company focuses on digital government transformation across Latin America. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's public web presence, legal pages, and domain-security posture.
c.name: Civica Digital

c.description: CivicEye provides a full‑spectrum public‑safety software platform, offering cloud‑based records management (CivicRMS), digital evidence management (CivicDocs), and case management solutions for law enforcement, prosecutors, and courts. Their mission is to empower agencies with data‑driven insights, secure evidence handling, and streamlined workflows to improve community safety and judicial efficiency.
c.name: CivicEye

c.description: CivicPlus is a govtech company providing an integrated platform for local, state, and education government operations, serving 13,000+ public-sector customers. Its product suite spans municipal websites, agenda and meeting management, recreation management, community development (permitting, licensing, code enforcement), utility billing, mass notification, public records requests (NextRequest), Municode codification, payments (CivicPlus Pay), and the SeeClickFix 311 resident-request CRM. The most developer-facing public interface in the CivicPlus family is the SeeClickFix API v2, a REST API over civic service requests (issues), comments, users, places, and questions, which additionally exposes an Open311 GeoReport v2 compatible endpoint for interoperable civic-issue reporting.
c.name: CivicPlus

c.description: The Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) is Australia's independent statutory aviation safety regulator, established under the Civil Aviation Act 1988. It maintains the Australian Civil Aircraft Register (VH- marks), issues Airworthiness Directives, licenses flight crew and maintenance organisations, certifies air operators, and regulates drone and RPAS operations. CASA sits entirely OUTSIDE the travel distribution chain — it is a safety regulator, not a distributor, so it has no GDS, NDC, channel-manager or OTA position, and airline fare distribution, full-content agreements and consumer disclosure are not CASA functions. Its API posture is split and honest: two genuinely open, no-key, documented bulk data products (the full Airworthiness Directives listing as JSON/CSV and the complete civil aircraft register as a daily CSV, both served from services.casa.gov.au), and one approval-gated partner API — the CASA RPAS Digital Platform at data.casa.rpasplatform.net — whose endpoints are named in public PDFs but require a service account, a signed four-year agreement, a CASA onboarding check-out and a paid Airservices Australia airspace data licence. There is no self-serve developer portal, no OpenAPI, and new RPAS Platform onboarding is currently paused pending Airservices' Flight Information Management System.
c.name: Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA)

c.description: The Civil Infrastructure Platform (CIP) is a Linux Foundation collaborative project that builds an industrial-grade open source base layer for civil infrastructure systems such as transportation, power generation and distribution, building and city management, industrial control, and healthcare equipment. CIP curates a Super Long-Term Support (SLTS) kernel and core user-space packages that can be maintained for more than ten years, plus working groups for security (IEC 62443 alignment), software update, real-time, and testing. CIP's primary programmable interface is source code — the kernel, CIP Core images and tooling published through GitLab and Debian-derived package archives — and it publishes machine-readable product lifecycle data for those. CIP also serves one live REST API: its own event calendar at cip-project.org/wp-json, declared in an RFC 9727 /.well-known/api-catalog and described by OpenAPI documents the site serves itself.
c.name: Civil Infrastructure Platform

c.description: Civil Maps was a San Francisco autonomous-vehicle mapping company founded in 2015 by Sravan Puttagunta and Scott Harvey, with Fabien Chraim and Anuj Gupta on the founding team. It built AI software that turned vehicle LiDAR and camera data into machine-readable HD 3D maps and delivered real-time six-degrees-of-freedom localization at 15-20 cm absolute accuracy, crowdsourcing map updates from production fleets rather than from dedicated survey vehicles, and packaged that as the Atlas DevKit and Atlas Lite DevKit car-mounted units. It raised roughly USD 17 million across four rounds, including a USD 6.6 million seed led by Motus Ventures with Ford Motor Company, Wicklow Capital, StartX and AME Cloud Ventures, and was acquired by Luminar Technologies in mid-2022 - an acquisition Luminar announced at CES in January 2023 and folded into its Sentinel platform. Civil Maps no longer operates as an independent business: civilmaps.com is a frozen four-page marketing archive stamped "Copyright 2019" with no developer section, it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its 2015-era GitHub organization holds five C++ repositories last pushed between 2017 and 2020.
c.name: Civil Maps

c.description: Civilengineeringthermometercet is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Civilengineeringthermometercet

c.description: Civis Analytics provides an all‑in‑one analytics and AI platform for organizations to build data pipelines, perform advanced analytics, and generate actionable insights. Their solutions serve data engineers, scientists, decision makers, and IT teams across nonprofits, government, and enterprises, enabling unified reporting, data integration, and AI‑driven decision making.
c.name: Civisanalytics

c.description: Civitai is the largest open community for Stable Diffusion, SDXL, Flux, and video AI models — hosting over a million model checkpoints, LoRAs, embeddings, and VAEs uploaded and rated by creators. Beyond hosting, Civitai operates a hosted AI image, video, audio, and language generation service through its Orchestration API, which races workflows across providers (Flux 1/2, SDXL, SD1, Z-Image, Qwen, Seedream, Grok, WAN 2.1-2.7, Kling, LTX2, Vidu, Veo 3, HunyuanVideo) and supports LoRA training jobs. The Site API exposes the public catalog plus user vault, permissions, and AIR identifier resolution. OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and per-app Buzz spend caps lets third parties build delegated experiences without owning a user's full credit balance. Generation is metered in Buzz, a virtual credit topped up via memberships or one-off packs.
c.name: Civitai

c.description: Civitas Learning is a higher education technology company whose Student Impact Platform unifies student data, predictive analytics, and coordinated workflows to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, persistence, and completion outcomes. The platform consolidates data from SIS, LMS, CRM, and event systems into a data lakehouse, layers institution-specific predictive models (CivIQ) on top, and surfaces real-time, actionable insights to advisors, faculty, and administrators through products such as Explore, Inspire, Impact, Illume, College Scheduler, Degree Map, and Academic Planning. Civitas Learning serves institutions of all sizes and pairs its software with strategic advisory services. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public operational, security, and compliance surface.
c.name: Civitas Learning

c.description: Civitas Resources is an independent exploration and production company focused on developing oil and natural gas resources in Colorado's Denver-Julesburg Basin and the Permian Basin. The company emphasizes carbon-neutral operations and sustainable production practices. Civitas Resources does not currently publish a public developer portal or API. The company has announced a merger with SM Energy Company.
c.name: Civitas Resources

c.description: Civitas Therapeutics was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 (Chelsea/Cambridge, Massachusetts) that developed inhaled therapeutics using the proprietary ARCUS dry-powder pulmonary delivery platform. Its lead program, CVT-301, was an inhaled levodopa therapy for the rapid relief of OFF episodes in Parkinson's disease patients. The company was acquired by Acorda Therapeutics in 2014 for approximately $525 million and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a life-sciences / drug-development company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or technical integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and retained in the API Evangelist network for provenance.
c.name: Civitas Therapeutics

c.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.
c.name: CIX Technology

c.description: CJ Affiliate (formerly Commission Junction) is one of the largest affiliate marketing networks, connecting publishers with thousands of advertiser programs. Its current developer platform is three GraphQL APIs - Commission Detail at commissions.api.cj.com for near-real-time commission and transaction data, Product Search / Ads at ads.api.cj.com for product discovery, product feeds and catalog writes, and Advertiser Tracking at tracking.api.cj.com for submitting, restating and cancelling orders. Alongside them CJ still documents a family of classic XML REST APIs - Link Search, Advertiser Lookup, Publisher Lookup, the Automated Offer Feed and a deprecated Commission Detail - plus two JSON click-tracking APIs, the Click Events API and the Publisher Tracking API. Everything authenticates with a single long-lived personal access token minted by hand in the CJ developer portal; there is no OAuth, no scopes and no programmatic token issuance. GraphQL introspection is open and unauthenticated on all three endpoints.
c.name: CJ Affiliate

c.description: CKAN is an open-source data management system that powers data portals and hubs worldwide. It enables organizations to publish, share, and use data efficiently, supporting governments, enterprises, and communities across the globe. CKAN provides robust features for data cataloging, API access, and community-driven extensions, fostering open data initiatives and transparency.
c.name: CKAN

c.description: CK Regeon Inc. is a biotechnology‑based company focused on developing first‑in‑class drugs with clear mechanisms of action. The mission is to improve the quality of human life by treating metabolic diseases such as NASH, diabetes, and obesity. The site outlines its CEO message, mission and vision, R&D pipelines, platform technologies, and business targets, providing a comprehensive view of its research and development efforts.
c.name: Ckregeon

c.description: Clad Labs is a San Francisco developer-tools startup (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) building Chad IDE, a desktop development environment that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and OpenAI Codex — from a single interface. Developers spin up teams of parallel agents, keep each task isolated in its own workspace, then merge clean changes back together, while a built-in analytics dashboard tracks coding habits and productivity metrics. The IDE also fills AI-inference downtime with an in-app "Chad Browser" for entertainment that automatically hands focus back to the code when generation completes. Clad Labs ships a downloadable macOS and Windows application rather than a public web API; it exposes no REST/OpenAPI developer surface at this time.
c.name: Clad Labs

c.description: Cladwell is a smart-closet and outfit-planning consumer application that helps people build capsule wardrobes and get more wear out of the clothes they already own. The service digitizes a user's closet, then uses AI styling ("Ask Cladwell") together with weather and personal preferences to recommend daily outfits, reduce over-buying, and encourage sustainable, intentional dressing. With more than one million app downloads, Cladwell is delivered primarily as iOS/Android and web apps (app.cladwell.com) with a subscription model; it currently exposes no public developer API. Founded and led by CEO Erin Flynn, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.
c.name: Cladwell

c.description: Claim — legally Claim Digital Assets, Inc. — is a New York consumer rewards app that pays people cash back for showing up in person at restaurants and retailers. Every Thursday its "Drop" matches a user with three nearby merchants; the user picks one, pays with a card linked through Plaid, and Claim reimburses them automatically over Venmo. Users can also trade Claims with friends, the social mechanic behind its "Benefits with Friends" positioning. Merchants buy performance-based customer acquisition instead of impressions, and Claim markets the program as turnkey — "no integrations, no setup, no training, no fees" — paying only when a guest transacts. Claim raised a $12M Series A led by VMG Technology in October 2024 ($20M raised in total, with Sequoia Capital and Susa Ventures) and was acquired by Wonder Group, Inc. in January 2026, where it now scales inside Grubhub and Seamless. Claim publishes no developer program, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.
c.name: Claim

c.description: Claim Genius is an AI vehicle-inspection and automated damage-assessment company serving auto insurance claims, underwriting, dealerships, salvage, lease and rental, fleet and collision repair. Its GeniusINSPECT engine converts vehicle photos and video into structured, decision-ready data — per-part damage classification (scratch, dent, tear, glass, wheel), repair-versus-replace decisions, labor and paint hours, OEM part pricing, repairability status and total-loss probability. The capabilities are packaged as products (GeniusINSPECT for Claims, GeniusINSPECT for Underwriting, GeniusPrepost, GeniusOPS) and exposed to integrators through the GeniusAPI Suite, a JWT-authenticated REST API with asynchronous pipeline processing. The company has operated across the US, EU and Asia since 2018.
c.name: Claim Genius

c.description: Claim.MD is a medical-claims clearinghouse that connects healthcare providers and software vendors to thousands of payers. Its REST API (authenticated with an AccountKey) supports electronic claim submission (837P/837I), claim status tracking, electronic remittance advice (835 ERA), real-time eligibility (270/271), and file upload/download workflows.
c.name: Claim.MD

c.description: Claimglide (ClaimGlide) is an AI-powered software platform that automates the end-to-end prior-authorization process for private medical practices and healthcare providers. It generates prior-auth submissions using payer-approved language, auto-pulls clinical data from EMR systems, follows up with payers, tracks authorization timelines, and auto-generates appeal letters to increase the share of prior-auths approved and shorten turnaround time. Claimglide integrates with major EMR/EHR platforms including eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen Healthcare, and ModMed, and states HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 in Seattle by Nami Lindquist and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch), the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. No public API, developer documentation, or developer portal is published at this time.
c.name: Claimglide

c.description: claimsforce GmbH is a Hamburg-based insurtech building AI-powered software for property and casualty claims management and underwriting. Its platform helps insurers, loss-adjusting and expert organizations, and independent adjusters digitize the end-to-end claims process - automating report and calculation generation, enabling video-based remote case assessment, optimizing adjuster disposition and route planning to cut travel time, and surfacing real-time analytics for claims handling and risk management. Named customers include Zurich Gruppe Deutschland, HanseMerkur, Concordia, Crawford, Sedgwick and Die Regulierer. The product is a private, login-only SaaS with no public API or developer portal as of July 2026. The company is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified (TUV Rheinland) and backed by Point Nine.
c.name: claimsforce

c.description: ClaimSorted is a tech-enabled third-party administrator (TPA) for insurance claims, combining human claims-handling expertise with proprietary technology to process claims faster while lowering operating costs and fraud leakage for MGAs and insurance carriers. It offers a white-label electronic Notice of Loss (eNOL) intake system, a policyholder Claims Portal for status tracking and document upload, automated assessment workflows, and fraud-detection algorithms, with reporting delivered daily, weekly, or monthly and as live data feeds over SFTP/API. ClaimSorted supports commercial and personal property, auto, small commercial, general liability, accident & health, travel, and warranty lines of business, serving 30+ clients including Axis and Lloyd's.
c.name: ClaimSorted

c.description: Clair Inc is a New York-based financial technology company that provides free, compliant On-Demand Pay (earned wage access) as an embedded service inside the payroll, time-and-attendance and workforce-management platforms employees already use. Rather than selling a consumer app, Clair partners with platforms — Gusto Embedded Payroll, Check, 7shifts and others — and connects to them over a partner REST API that transmits employee, employment and attendance data, which Clair's underwriting engine uses to originate 0% APR earned wage advances through its FDIC-insured partner bank, Pathward N.A. Partners embed a Clair-hosted user experience (a WebView component, distributed for iOS as Swift packages) so employees can take an advance, review history and handle loan servicing without a separate login. Clair has raised roughly $218M in total capital, including a $23.2M Series B in May 2025.
c.name: Clair

c.description: Claira is an AI-driven platform that streamlines private market investment analysis and decision-making. Founded in 2018 and based in New York City, it offers an agentic AI system to capture, organize, preserve, and analyze institutional knowledge, accelerating deal flow for financial institutions and investors. Backed by leading investors, Claira provides tools for deal management, data extraction, and workflow automation across the private markets.
c.name: Claira

c.description: Clairity Technology Inc. is a Los Angeles based climate-tech company building gigaton-scale carbon dioxide removal using Direct Air Capture (DAC) paired with ex-situ mineralization. Their approach removes CO2 from the atmosphere with readily available, inexpensive chemicals and standard construction materials to produce concentrated CO2 streams for permanent removal and storage. Clairity operates Project Juniper, a live carbon-removal facility in Southern Nevada, and raised a $6.75M seed round in 2024. As a hardware and carbon-removal operator the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Clairity

c.description: Clairity, Inc. is an AI-driven healthcare company founded in 2020 and based in Boston, Massachusetts. It offers Clairity Breast, the first FDA-authorized platform that predicts a woman’s five‑year risk of breast cancer using existing mammogram images. Leveraging deep learning and radiomics, the service provides personalized risk assessments to patients and clinicians, aiming to shift cancer care from reactive diagnosis to proactive prevention.
c.name: Clairityinc

c.description: Claix is a Madrid-based B2B document intelligence API that converts PDFs, Excel/CSV, Word and text documents and images into strictly typed JSON against customer-defined schemas, keeps extracted documents as queryable context for AI agents (single-document and knowledge-space Q&A with deterministic nulls), and exposes one 20-operation contract three ways: REST (OpenAPI 3.0.3), a hosted MCP server at /mcp, and a native A2A agent at /a2a with a published, conformant agent card. Pay-as-you-go in euros after 100 free calls, with a free BYOK mode; official Python SDK and n8n node.
c.name: Claix

c.description: Clanbeat is an Estonian education-technology company whose app supports student and staff well-being by nurturing social and emotional learning (SEL) through co-creation. The platform provides well-being tracking, quality reflections, meaningful connections between students and educators, and tools to co-create SEL curriculum. It is used by international schools, educators, students, and fitness and lifelong-learning communities to evidence group emotional well-being and bring classes closer together. Clanbeat is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application at app.clanbeat.com; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or partner integration surface at this time.
c.name: Clanbeat

c.description: Clanztechnologies is a technology services company that provides integrated security and automation solutions for residential and commercial properties. The firm focuses on advanced alarm systems, smart home integration, and customized monitoring services, aiming to enhance safety and convenience for its clients. While detailed public information is limited, the company appears to operate primarily within the United States, serving both private homeowners and business customers with tailored security technology offerings.
c.name: Clanztechnologies

c.description: CLAP (주식회사 디웨일 / Dwhale Inc.) is a South Korean SaaS company offering an AI-powered, customizable performance management platform for enterprises. It covers the full performance lifecycle — multi-rater evaluations and calibration, OKR-style goal setting and alignment, continuous feedback and 1-on-1 meetings, and CLAP AI for diagnostics, feedback drafting, and automation — with tailored reporting and tool integrations. CLAP serves 1,000+ companies and claims to cut the HR time spent on performance management by up to 80%. The company is headquartered in Gangnam, Seoul, and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. CLAP publishes no public API or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and web properties.
c.name: CLAP

c.description: Clara is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, general-catalyst, ggv-capital, iconiq-capital, techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Clara

c.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Clara 2

c.description: CLARA Analytics is an AI-as-a-service provider for casualty insurance claims, serving carriers, MGAs/MGUs, reinsurers, third-party administrators and self-insured organizations. Its CLARAty.ai platform applies document intelligence, natural language processing, image recognition and predictive models to medical notes, legal demand packages, bills and other claim documents across workers' compensation, auto and general liability, with products for triage, fraud detection, litigation risk, treatment and provider selection, Medicare Secondary Payer compliance, and industry benchmarking. CLARA markets pre-built APIs for integration with RMIS and core claims systems and ships a Built-by-Guidewire integration for ClaimCenter through the Guidewire Marketplace, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CLARA Analytics

c.description: Clarabridge was a customer experience management (CEM) and conversational analytics company known for its natural-language-understanding platform that analyzed unstructured customer feedback — contact-center transcripts, chat, email, surveys, social media, and online reviews — to surface sentiment, emotion, effort, intent, and emerging topics. Qualtrics acquired Clarabridge in 2021, and the technology has since been integrated and rebranded inside the Qualtrics XM platform: Clarabridge Studio became Qualtrics XM Discover and Clarabridge Engage became Qualtrics Connect. Clarabridge no longer operates an independent developer portal or public API; its capabilities are now delivered through Qualtrics. This profile is retained as a company/brand record in the API Evangelist network with an acquisition pointer to Qualtrics.
c.name: Clarabridge

c.description: Clarafintech provides spend management and financial automation solutions for businesses in Latin America. The platform offers corporate cards, vendor payments, expense reporting, and AI‑driven insights to help companies control costs, improve compliance, and streamline financial operations across Brazil, Colombia, Mexico and other markets.
c.name: Clarafintech

c.description: Clarametyx Biosciences is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel immune‑enabling therapies targeting bacterial biofilms that drive chronic respiratory diseases such as cystic fibrosis. The company advances its pipeline through pre‑clinical and early‑stage clinical programs, aiming to modify disease progression rather than merely alleviate symptoms. Recent announcements include positive topline data from a Phase 2a study of CMTX‑101 and significant Series A financing to accelerate development.
c.name: Clarametyx Biosciences

c.description: Clarapath is a medical robotics company headquartered in Hawthorne, New York that automates the tissue sectioning step of the clinical histopathology workflow. Its FDA-registered SectionStar platform pairs patented tape-transfer sectioning with precision robotics, integrated optics and sensors, and computational quality control to turn paraffin blocks into standardized slides with quantitative quality metrics. The company also ships the TrimStar Pro trimming system, a HistoStation data repository for sample and image traceability, remote Telehistology operation, and histology consulting services for hospital, reference, and veterinary laboratories.
c.name: Clarapath

c.description: Claravine provides a Data Standards Platform that helps enterprises govern taxonomy and naming standards across marketing campaigns, content, and data pipelines. Their SaaS solution integrates with major ad platforms, CRM, and analytics tools, offering APIs for submitting and reading standardized data, security features like SOC 2 Type II, SSO, and RBAC, and tools for AI‑assisted taxonomy management. The company serves agencies, retailers, CPG, healthcare, automotive, and other industries, emphasizing data consistency at scale.
c.name: Claravine

c.description: Clari is an enterprise revenue orchestration platform that publishes three machine surfaces. The Clari Revenue API v5 (api.clari.com/v4) is an asynchronous, job-based export and ingest surface — queue a forecast, activity or audit export, poll until the job reads DONE, then download the results — plus a partner Ingestion API for pushing third-party data into Clari accounts and opportunities. The Clari Copilot REST API (rest-api.copilot.clari.com) is a synchronous conversation-intelligence and CRM surface covering calls, transcripts, AI summaries, action items, competitor sentiment, coaching scorecards, and CRUD over accounts, contacts and deals keyed on the customer's own CRM id. Clari also runs a first-party remote MCP server at mcp.clari.com/mcp, OAuth protected via Okta and listed natively in the Claude connector directory, which exposes live Clari + Salesloft revenue context to AI agents. Both HTTP APIs authenticate with header API keys, support no idempotency keys, and return no rate-limit headers.
c.name: Clari

c.description: Clarifai is an AI computer vision and NLP platform providing REST and gRPC APIs for image recognition, object detection, text analysis, visual search, and custom model training. The platform enables teams to build, deploy, and manage AI across shared cloud, on-premise, and edge infrastructure with support for model inference, workflow orchestration, vector search, and dataset management.
c.name: Clarifai

c.description: Clarifeye is an AI-native knowledge infrastructure platform that captures the undocumented knowledge locked in people's heads. Its AI interviewer, Clara, runs document-aware interviews with subject-matter experts, surfaces contradictions, and structures the results into versioned, reusable knowledge artifacts — briefs, playbooks, mental maps, and ontologies. That captured knowledge is exposed to AI clients such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot through a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and a REST API, so agents answer grounded in an organization's own logic with references back to source. Clarifeye targets regulated industries where undocumented processes create key-person risk, offers EU and US data localization with PII redaction at ingestion, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. Backed by EQT Ventures.
c.name: Clarifeye

c.description: Clarify is an AI-native CRM platform that automates sales workflows, integrates with email, calendar, and various tools, and provides a conversational AI assistant to manage contacts, deals, and pipelines. It offers a JSON:API‑compliant API for programmatic access to CRM data, enabling custom integrations, automation, and AI‑driven insights for sales teams.
c.name: Clarify

c.description: Clarify Health Solutions is a healthcare analytics and outcomes company that helps health systems, payers, and life sciences organizations understand cost, quality, and utilization across the care journey. Its flagship platform, Clarify Meridian, unifies referral intelligence, physician activation, consumer engagement, and outcomes attribution into a single analytics environment built on billions of longitudinal patient records and claims data. Clarify Health is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and, in 2026, acquired Loyal Health to expand its consumer engagement capabilities. The company operates a SaaS analytics product rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Clarify Health

c.description: Clarifymedical is a healthcare data analytics company that provides APIs for patient activation, growth intelligence, and health system orchestration. It offers services such as Meridian and Arrival to help health systems understand and improve care delivery, leveraging comprehensive health economics data. The company focuses on integrating patient data, provider contracts, and network analytics to drive better health outcomes and operational efficiency.
c.name: Clarifymedical

c.description: Clario provides clinical trial endpoint technology and evidence generation services, offering solutions for cardiac safety, blood pressure monitoring, ECG data collection, and comprehensive data management across all phases of clinical research. Their platform supports hybrid and site‑based trials worldwide, delivering precise, regulatory‑compliant data to accelerate drug development and improve patient outcomes.
c.name: Clario

c.description: Claripi provides innovative solutions for medical imaging through AI-powered image processing, data analytics, and software tools. Clarity AI reports coverage of 300K+ listed and private companies, 450K+ funds, and 400+ sovereigns, and serves asset managers, asset owners, banks, wealth managers, and corporates. The company exposes its data through a web application, data feeds, APIs, and emerging AI agent / MCP integrations, though its developer surface is gated behind an enterprise platform login rather than a public developer portal. Clarity AI is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

c.description: Clark ("Dein Versicherungsmanager") is a Germany-based digital insurance manager that lets consumers view, compare, optimize, and manage all of their insurance policies in one mobile app and web platform. Founded in Frankfurt in 2015, Clark pairs a licensed insurance brokerage with automated tariff comparison across more than 180 insurance providers and free expert consultation, covering health, liability, property, life, mobility, and retirement products. The company operates across Germany, Switzerland, France, and the UK, serves over 700,000 customers, and is backed by venture investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Clark exposes no public developer API or developer portal; it is a consumer-facing insurtech rather than an API producer.

c.description: Claros is a data center power delivery company reimagining how energy moves from chip to grid for AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. Based in Torrance, California with an office in McLean, Virginia, the company builds two hardware-and-software product lines: an Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) that targets the roughly 40 percent of chip power lost to heat at the point of delivery, and a Power Gateway that manages broader data center power distribution where 30 to 50 percent of power is lost to transmission, conversion, and cooling. Claros is an early-stage hardware company backed by General Catalyst and Red Cell Partners; its founding team collectively holds 286 patents and has brought more than 80 gigawatts of projects to market. c.description: Clasp Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage precision immuno-oncology company developing next-generation T cell engagers (TCEs) built on its proprietary pHLAre platform, which redirects T cells to mutant peptides — such as p53 R175H and mutant KRAS — presented by specific HLA molecules on the surface of tumor cells. The approach is intended to yield off-the-shelf, antibody-like medicines that hit common oncogenic driver mutations with tumor-exclusive specificity. Its lead candidate CLSP-1025 (p53 R175H / HLA-A*02:01) is in the Phase 1 GUARDIAN-101 trial (NCT06778863), and CLSP-5282, a first-in-class KRas-directed TCE, was unveiled at AACR 2026. Founded on research from Bert Vogelstein, Drew Pardoll and colleagues at Johns Hopkins, the company launched in March 2024 with $150 million led by Catalio Capital Management, Third Rock Ventures and Novo Holdings, and operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Rockville, Maryland. Clasp Therapeutics is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

Class also publishes a REST developer API (developer.class.com) that lets administrators and integrators provision classes, manage enrollments, generate learner launch links, schedule class dates, manage class templates, manage non-learner users, and pull attendance and engagement reporting, authenticated with a per-organization API key presented as a Bearer token and gated by permission scopes.

The company's revenue model is consumer subscriptions and tutoring; there is no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or webhook surface, and the GitHub organization at github.com/classdojo publishes only internal utilities, forks, and policy documents rather than developer-facing artifacts.

Its site listed sixteen such demo APIs — Fashion Style Classification, Custom Car Part Identification, Surgical Instrument Classification, Retail Planogram Compliance and others — each on its own landing page, alongside a "describe your use case" intake form. c.description: Classiq Technologies is a Tel Aviv, Israel headquartered enterprise quantum software company founded in 2020 by Nir Minerbi (CEO), Amir Naveh (CPO), and Dr. Yehuda Naveh (CTO), positioning itself as a high-level quantum algorithm design platform that lets organizations build, scale, and deploy quantum algorithms across any hardware or simulator without writing low-level gate code. Its flagship offering centers on Qmod, an intuitive quantum modeling language, and a hardware-aware synthesis engine that compiles functional quantum models into optimized circuits with constraint-driven optimization, transpilation, and execution session management across cloud quantum providers including AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, GCP, IBM Quantum, IonQ, OQC, Alice and Bob, and C12. The platform is delivered through the Classiq Studio web IDE at platform.classiq.io, a public Python SDK (`pip install classiq`) currently at version 1.14.0 covering synthesis, execution, analysis, and application libraries for chemistry (QSP), finance (IQAE), and quantum machine learning (QSVM, QML), plus an AI-assisted natural language interface for algorithm design. Classiq publishes the largest open quantum algorithm library on GitHub at github.com/Classiq/classiq-library (2,000+ stars, Jupyter Notebook, MIT license) with reference implementations across optimization, linear solvers, quantum machine learning, chemistry, finance, logistics, cybersecurity, and physical systems. Customers include Microsoft, AWS, NVIDIA, HSBC, Citibank, BMW, and Rolls-Royce; the company is SOC 2 and GDPR compliant. Classiq has raised over $200M including a $110M Series C in May 2025 with backers such as AMD Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, IonQ, Bank Leumi, Mirae Asset Capital, and SoftBank. Classiq's developer surface is the Python SDK and Qmod language — there is no public REST API or OpenAPI specification; the Mintlify-hosted `docs.classiq.io/api-reference/openapi.json` endpoint currently returns the default Mintlify Plant Store placeholder rather than a real API contract.
c.name: Classiq

c.description: ClassLink is an EdTech identity and access management platform purpose-built for K-12 school districts, providing single sign-on (SSO) to over 6,000 digital learning resources through its LaunchPad portal. The platform offers a OneRoster-compliant REST API for secure rostering and student data exchange, enabling automated provisioning and synchronization between student information systems and educational applications. ClassLink OneSync handles identity management and account provisioning integrations with any SIS, while Roster Server facilitates standards-based data sharing using OAuth 1.0 and OAuth 2.0. The Analytics and Analytics+ products expose usage telemetry APIs that help district administrators track edtech engagement and license utilization across all devices. ClassLink maintains open developer resources including multi-language request libraries (C#, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Python, Go) on GitHub and a partner developer portal.

c.description: CLAUDE.md is the markdown-based project memory format used by Anthropic's Claude Code CLI to give the model persistent, session-spanning instructions about a codebase. CLAUDE.md files are plain markdown that Claude Code loads at the start of every session by walking up the directory tree from the working directory, picking up files at organization-managed, user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), and local (./CLAUDE.local.md) scopes. The format supports an @path import syntax for composing files together (up to five hops, relative or absolute), HTML block comments that are stripped before injection, an AGENTS.md import pattern for compatibility with other agents, and a complementary .claude/rules/ directory of path-scoped markdown rules with YAML frontmatter. CLAUDE.md is the human-authored counterpart to Claude Code's auto memory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md, which Claude writes itself.
c.name: CLAUDE.md

c.description: ClawdChat (虾聊) is a Chinese-language social network built for AI agents, run from clawdchat.ai and its sister domain clawdchat.cn. Agents register over a public REST API (280 operations, FastAPI-served OpenAPI 3.1), receive a W3C did:web identity and a per-agent A2A Agent Card, and can post, comment, vote, join circles, exchange DMs, and relay A2A messages to any of the 11,500+ agents the platform hosts. A tool gateway fronts 3,700+ third-party MCP tools behind the same API key, and a hosted OAuth 2.1-gated MCP server runs at mcp.clawdchat.ai. Agents onboard by reading a published skill.md; humans claim their agents through WeChat, phone or Google.

c.description: ClawSpan is an agent-first work marketplace: autonomous AI agents register with a wallet signature (EIP-4361), claim bounded tasks in governed workspaces under leases, and settle against signed receipts. ShardLink is the live control plane (task orchestration, marketplace directory, billing, provider execution) at app.clawspan.cloud, exposing an OpenAPI 3.1 REST surface, a streamable-HTTP MCP server, and an A2A agent card; SignalHub is the economic plane, whose OpenAPI and agent card are published while its runtime is still in development.
c.name: ClawSpan

c.description: Clawvisor is the authorization layer for AI agents — a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) security gateway that sits between an AI agent and the tools it acts on (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, GitHub, Slack, Notion, Linear, Stripe, Twilio, iMessage). Agents never hold downstream credentials: they declare a task describing their purpose and the service/action pairs they need, the user approves that scope once, and Clawvisor enforces restrictions, task scope, and LLM intent verification on every request before injecting vaulted, short-lived credentials, executing through an adapter, and writing a full audit trail. It ships open-core as a self-hostable Go daemon with a CLI, web dashboard, TUI, and an OAuth 2.1 MCP server, plus an official Claude Code plugin. Agents integrate over a plain HTTP gateway or MCP — no SDK or agent-code changes required.
c.name: Clawvisor

c.description: Clean Harbors is the largest provider of environmental and industrial services in North America — hazardous and non-hazardous waste management, emergency response, industrial cleaning, remediation, and used-oil and solvent recycling through its Safety-Kleen subsidiary. It runs no developer programme: no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK in any registry, no GitHub organisation, and no /.well-known/ document on any host. Customers use the authenticated Clean Harbors Online Services portal at clhsaas.cleanharbors.com and the EPA's RCRA e-Manifest programme, whose machine-readable surface belongs to the EPA. Two callable contracts nonetheless run on Clean Harbors hosts, both found by direct probing: an anonymous, fully introspectable GraphQL endpoint at store.safety-kleen.com fronting six brand storefronts on one Adobe Commerce instance, and an unauthenticated Job Query API at careers.cleanharbors.com that the company documents in a published llms.txt.

c.description: Clean Urban Energy, Inc. was a Chicago, Illinois cleantech company that turned large commercial office buildings into grid-scale thermal energy storage assets. Its technology harnessed the existing thermal mass of a building — concrete, drywall, furnishings — by pre-cooling during off-peak hours and coasting through peak demand, effectively operating the building as a multi-megawatt battery for demand response and load shifting without installing dedicated storage hardware. The company raised a reported $7 million venture round and appears in the Battery Ventures list of all portfolio companies. As of a July 2026 review the company has no live corporate web presence: the cleanurbanenergy.com domain no longer serves company content, and no developer portal, API, documentation, or GitHub organization could be located. It is catalogued here as an inactive, non-API-provider company record.

c.description: CleanBoss is a consumer products brand offering non‑toxic, botanically‑derived cleaning solutions. Founded by Joy Mangano and Armando Christian Pérez, the company sells multi‑surface cleaners, laundry sheets, fruit‑and‑veggie washes, and other eco‑friendly products through its Shopify storefront. The brand emphasizes safety, effectiveness, and a “cleaning revolution” with a 100 % money‑back guarantee and free shipping on orders over $45.

c.description: CleanCapital is a New York based clean energy investment firm, founded in 2015, that develops, constructs, acquires, owns and operates distributed-generation solar and energy storage projects across the United States. It concentrates on the commercial and municipal middle market between residential rooftop and utility-scale generation, selling power to businesses, schools, nonprofits, municipalities and community solar subscribers, and it buys operating and late-stage development projects from developers through a dedicated project-acquisition practice. The firm reports more than $1.5 billion of capital deployed, 450+ MW under management, 235 MW developed and constructed, 200+ energy customers and over 1,000 GWh of emissions-free generation, backed by institutional partners including Manulife Investment Management / John Hancock, BlackRock and CarVal Investors. CleanCapital is an asset owner and investment manager rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its customer portal at app.cleancapital.com now redirects to the third-party Dock Energy platform.
c.name: CleanCapital

c.description: CleanCloud is cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) and business management software for dry cleaners, laundromats, laundry services, and shoe repair businesses. It handles orders, garment tracking, customers, pickup and delivery routing, payments, inventory, marketing, and reporting. CleanCloud exposes a documented public REST API (base https://cleancloudapp.com/api) for programmatic access to customers, orders, garments, products, price lists, inventory, pickup and delivery scheduling, payments, subscriptions, invoices, promotions, and reporting, plus outbound Webhooks for order and customer events. API access is available on the Grow and Grow+ subscription tiers, authenticated with a per-account API token and metered at 50,000 requests per month (max 3 requests per second).
c.name: CleanCloud

c.description: CleanCo is a United Kingdom-based beverage company, founded in 2019 by Spencer Matthews, that produces premium low- and no-alcohol alternative spirits. Its product line replicates the flavour profiles of traditional spirits across key categories, including CleanGin, CleanRum, CleanVodka and CleanTequila, aimed at consumers who want to reduce alcohol consumption without sacrificing taste. The company sells direct-to-consumer through cleanliquor.com and through grocery and hospitality retail channels across the UK and international markets. CleanCo raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2020. It is a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not publish a developer API, developer portal, or any machine-readable API surface; it is retained in the API Evangelist network only as an identified Lightspeed portfolio company, not as an API provider.
c.name: CleanCo

c.description: Cleancult provides eco‑friendly cleaning products delivered in refillable containers, aiming to reduce single‑use plastic waste. Their mission emphasizes sustainability, refill culture, and a cleaner lifestyle, offering detergents, soaps, and other household cleaners through a subscription model.
c.name: Cleancult

c.description: Cleancult is a sustainable cleaning products company offering refillable, eco‑friendly cleaning solutions for home and personal care. Their mission is to reduce single‑use plastic waste by providing reusable aluminum bottles and paper‑based refills for soaps, detergents, and sprays. The brand emphasizes powerful, chemical‑free formulas, a subscription‑style refill ritual, and a commitment to environmental stewardship, aiming to make clean living both effective and environmentally responsible.
c.name: Cleancult2

c.description: Cleanenergyconnect is a clean energy marketplace platform that connects renewable energy producers with buyers, facilitating transparent transactions, data sharing, and integration of sustainable energy assets. The company aims to accelerate the adoption of clean energy by providing tools for project financing, carbon accounting, and market analytics, supporting a greener energy future.
c.name: Cleanenergyconnect

c.description: Cleanhome is a startup focused on providing smart home cleaning solutions, integrating IoT devices and AI-driven scheduling to optimize household maintenance. The company aims to simplify cleaning routines through connected appliances, offering a platform for users to manage and automate tasks across multiple devices. While detailed public information is limited, the company positions itself within the smart home and automation market, targeting residential customers seeking convenience and efficiency.
c.name: Cleanhome

c.description: Cleanlab provides AI safety tools to detect and remediate hallucinations, retrieval errors, and policy violations in AI agents. The platform offers guardrails, monitoring, and automated evaluation for LLM outputs, helping enterprises deploy trustworthy AI. Acquired by Handshake AI, Cleanlab serves developers with APIs, SDKs, and a web UI for real‑time error correction and compliance.
c.name: Cleaninglab

c.description: Cleanlab is a data-and-AI trust platform. Its Trustworthy Language Model (TLM) wraps any LLM with a real-time trustworthiness score to catch hallucinations, Cleanlab Studio curates and labels training data and deploys reliable ML models, and Codex adds a safety, guardrail, and remediation layer for AI assistants and RAG. The open-source cleanlab library underpins it all with data-centric AI.
c.name: Cleanlab

c.description: Cleanly was a US-based on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning startup (backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator) that has since rebranded and now operates as ByNext at bynext.co. ByNext is an app-based, on-demand laundry, dry cleaning, and home cleaning pickup and delivery service operating 7 days a week (8am-8pm) with 24-48 hour turnaround across metro markets including New York City, New Jersey, the Washington D.C. area, and Los Angeles. Booking is handled through its iOS and Android apps with real-time driver tracking, pay-per-pound or subscription pricing, and free pickup and delivery. Cleanly/ByNext exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public web and consumer-app footprint. The original cleanly.com domain now redirects to bynext.co.
c.name: Cleanly

c.description: CleanRobotics, Inc. (株式会社CleanRobotics) is a Tokyo‑based company founded in 2025 that applies AI and IoT to modernize energy infrastructure. Their platform combines physical sensors with cloud‑based analytics to enable predictive maintenance, real‑time optimization, and open‑grid management for power plants and renewable assets worldwide. The mission is to make energy infrastructure accessible, efficient, and environmentally sustainable through intelligent automation.
c.name: Cleanrobotics

c.description: Cleanshelf was a San Francisco enterprise SaaS management platform that discovered and inventoried an organization's SaaS applications, optimized software licenses, tracked subscription spend, and surfaced shadow IT. At acquisition it claimed more than 3,000 integrations and managed roughly $700 million in SaaS spend for its customers. LeanIX acquired Cleanshelf on 24 March 2021 and relaunched the technology on 1 May 2021 as LeanIX SaaS Intelligence, with SaaS discovery and cataloging folded into the LeanIX Application Portfolio Management module; LeanIX itself was later acquired by SAP. Cleanshelf publishes no API, developer portal or documentation of its own today — cleanshelf.com 301-redirects to www.leanix.net and its former api, app and docs hostnames no longer resolve. The successor API surface is profiled separately under the LeanIX record.
c.name: Cleanshelf

c.description: CleanSlate (CleanSlate Centers) is a national outpatient medical group treating opioid and alcohol use disorder with physician-led, office-based medication-assisted treatment — FDA-approved medication combined with primary care and behavioral health therapy for polysubstance use and co-occurring disorders. Founded in 2009 in Massachusetts by Dr. Amanda Wilson in response to the opioid epidemic, it grew to more than 65 outpatient centers across eight states and raised roughly $79M in venture backing before being acquired by Spero Health on July 1, 2026. CleanSlate is a care-delivery organization: it operates clinics, not a software platform, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CleanSlate

c.description: Cleanup.pictures provides AI-powered photo cleanup, object and watermark removal via inpainting. The public API is hosted on the ClipDrop platform (now Jasper.ai) at https://clipdrop-api.co/cleanup/v1, billed at 1 credit per successful call.
c.name: Cleanup.pictures

c.description: URL shortener service
c.name: CleanURI

c.description: Cleanwatts accelerates the energy transition by developing, financing, and operating distributed solar energy projects and energy communities for commercial and industrial clients. The company enables organizations to consume renewable energy with zero upfront investment, offering predictable, competitive energy costs while reducing carbon footprints. Cleanwatts focuses on local solutions, leveraging solar installations at client facilities to drive sustainable power generation and support the broader shift toward clean energy.
c.name: Cleanwatts

c.description: Cleanwise (Cleanwise, Inc.) is a Jan/San procurement management company serving multi-location national and regional businesses. The company applies janitorial supply category knowledge and custom procurement management systems to help customers manage, measure, and control their janitorial and sanitation spend. Cleanwise describes itself as technology-enabled and customer-driven, combining in-house procurement systems, industry expertise, and supplier partnerships to deliver product efficiencies and standardized best practices across distributed facility footprints. Its published customer examples include the US Postal Service, JCPenney, and Best Buy, with claimed first-year savings of 10-20% of total Jan/San spend. Insight Partners has listed Cleanwise in its portfolio since 2022. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API artifact has been found for Cleanwise; the company operates as a procurement services provider rather than an API producer.
c.name: Cleanwise

c.description: CLEAR (clearme.com) is a secure identity company best known for its biometric identity network. For developers, CLEAR1 exposes an identity verification API: you create a verification session, hand the user off to CLEAR's hosted UI to capture a government ID and a selfie/liveness check, then retrieve the verified result and traits. The platform supports OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (with PKCE) for end-user identity tokens, bearer-key auth for the REST API, webhooks for session lifecycle events, a sandbox with synthetic test identities, and native integrations (Okta, Microsoft Entra, Ping, Amazon Connect, DocuSign, Greenhouse) across workforce, healthcare, financial services, and consumer use cases, including IAL2 identity proofing and TEFCA/Carequality access.
c.name: CLEAR

c.description: Clear Ballot Group, Inc. is an election technology company that builds transparent, verifiable voting systems for election administrators across the United States. Its flagship ClearVote platform spans vote-by-mail processing, in-person voting, ballot design, and independent post-election audit and results-verification software, alongside offerings for ranked-choice voting and elections-as-a-service. Clear Ballot operates as a closed, certified election-systems vendor rather than a public API platform, so this profile is identity- and security-focused: it captures the company's public web presence, domain-security posture, and its published vulnerability-disclosure program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
c.name: Clear Ballot

c.description: Clear Books is UK cloud accounting software with a REST API for managing invoices, expenses, bank transactions, contacts, reports, and tax submissions for small businesses.
c.name: Clear Books

c.description: Clear Capital is a real-estate valuation and property data platform serving mortgage lenders, investors, and capital markets. Its developer surface is exposed through two sales-led REST products - the Property Analytics API (ClearAVM automated valuations, comparables ranked by ClearRank, property characteristics, and market trends) and the Property Valuation API (ordering and fulfillment of appraisal and valuation products such as Hybrid/Desktop appraisal, BPO, CDA, and UDC). Access is gated behind a commercial agreement; full reference docs live at docs.api.clearcapital.com.
c.name: Clear Capital

c.description: Clear Channel Outdoor (NYSE: CCO) is one of the largest out-of-home (OOH) advertising companies in the world, operating billboards, street furniture, transit, airport, and digital out-of-home (DOOH) displays across 65+ U.S. markets and 55+ commercial airports, reaching "130 million Americans weekly." The CCO developer surface spans three layers: the CCO.IO Automated Direct REST API at direct.cco.io for programmatic-direct buying of inventory (OAuth 2.0 client credentials, open-source Go SDK at github.com/ClearChannelOutdoor/io-sdk-golang), programmatic digital out-of-home (pDOOH) buying through 20+ DSP partners using OpenRTB 2.6 with the DOOH object extension, and RADAR — CCO's first-party audience and attribution data suite (RADARView, RADARProof, RADARConnect, RADARSync, Inflight Insights) built on aggregated and anonymous mobile location data. CCO maintains a public fork of the IAB Tech Lab OpenDirect-OOH specification at github.com/ClearChannelOutdoor/ooh_open_direct.
c.name: Clear Channel Outdoor

c.description: Clear Labs builds automated next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms that combine laboratory robotics, cloud software, and bioinformatics to deliver genomic data and actionable insights. Its product lines span oncology research (Clear Dx), infectious-disease and microbial genomics (Clear Ix), and food-safety pathogen testing (Clear Safety) for organisms such as Listeria and Salmonella. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Clear Labs publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile; the record captures company identity and domain-security posture.
c.name: Clear Labs

c.description: Clear Skye is a private company listed on the Nasdaq Private Market platform. It provides liquidity solutions, investment opportunities, and data intelligence for pre‑IPO equity holders and investors. While its own website is currently under development, the company is represented on the Nasdaq Private Market marketplace, offering services such as tender offers, secondary market trading, and capital solutions for private firms and their stakeholders.
c.name: Clear Skye

c.description: Clear Street is a New York–based financial technology firm building independent, cloud-native prime brokerage, clearing, and execution infrastructure for institutional and active individual traders. It is a FINRA/SIPC member broker-dealer, a CFTC-registered Futures Commission Merchant, and FCA-authorised in the UK. Clear Street ships three public API surfaces: the Clear Street Trading API (OpenAPI 3.1, api.clearstreet.com) covering accounts, orders, executions, positions, instruments, market data, screeners, watchlists and the Omni AI financial copilot; the Clear Street Studio API (OpenAPI 3.0, prime-brokerage holdings, locates, easy-borrows, P&L, and Reg-T/portfolio margin) with a companion WebSocket activity stream; and an OAuth-protected remote MCP server for AI agents. First-party SDKs ship for Python, TypeScript, Go and Kotlin/Java, alongside a Go CLI (clst) and a published set of open Agent Skills.
c.name: Clear Street

c.description: Clear View Copper Foils is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clear View Copper Foils

c.description: Clearballotgroupinc is a technology company focused on providing secure, transparent, and verifiable ballot handling solutions for elections and organizational voting. The platform aims to modernize the voting process through digital tools that ensure integrity, accessibility, and auditability, catering to both public sector elections and private organizational decision-making. While detailed public documentation is limited, the company positions itself as a bridge between traditional ballot methods and innovative digital solutions, emphasizing security and compliance with electoral standards.
c.name: Clearballotgroupinc

c.description: ClearBank is a UK clearing and Banking-as-a-Service bank, founded in 2015 by Nick Ogden (founder of WorldPay) and Charles McManus and granted a banking licence in December 2016 as the first new UK clearing bank in more than 250 years. ClearBank Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority (FRN 754568), with a European subsidiary, ClearBank Europe N.V., authorised by the European Central Bank. It is privately owned, backed by Apax Partners and PPF Group. Built cloud-native on Microsoft Azure, ClearBank is a direct participant in the UK payment schemes (Faster Payments, CHAPS, Bacs) and offers Agency Banking, Embedded Banking, and Transaction Banking to banks, fintechs, and corporates through a single proprietary JSON REST API. Unlike the CMA9 retail banks, ClearBank is not a mandated Open Banking ASPSP and does not publish the OBIE Open Data (ATMs/Branches/Products) or OBIE Read/Write (AISP/PISP/CBPII) APIs; its public developer surface is the token-authenticated, RSA-signed ClearBank Financial Institutions API covering GBP accounts and payments, multi-currency accounts, FX, SEPA, cross-border payments, Confirmation of Payee, customer due diligence (KYC), and embedded/retail banking, with a full simulation environment for onboarding.
c.name: ClearBank

c.description: Clearbit is a B2B marketing and sales intelligence platform whose REST APIs resolve an email address to a person, a domain to a company, and an IP address to the business behind it, returning firmographic, technographic and persona data across a documented 100+ company and 60+ person attributes classified against GICS, SIC and NAICS. HubSpot acquired Clearbit in December 2023 and sells the capability as HubSpot Breeze Intelligence. The legacy Clearbit APIs (Enrichment, Streaming, Reveal, Prospector, Discovery, Risk, Name-to-Domain, Autocomplete) remain live and answer on their production hosts, but the provider is in publicly dated wind-down — new API keys have not been issued since 2023, free accounts were sunset 2025-04-30, and the free Logo API was sunset 2025-12-08 and its host no longer resolves. Only the free Autocomplete API is callable without a credential.
c.name: Clearbit (HubSpot Breeze Intelligence)

c.description: Search for company logos and embed them in your projects
c.name: Clearbit Logo

c.description: Clearbluemarkets provides carbon market intelligence and services, helping companies navigate compliance and voluntary carbon markets worldwide. Their platform offers market data, analytics, advisory, and tools for offset insight, position optimization, and EV credits aggregation, aiming to simplify decarbonization efforts and maximize financial benefits for clients.
c.name: Clearbluemarkets

c.description: Clearbos (clearorthod / 可丽尔博士) is a Chinese clear-aligner orthodontics company that designs and manufactures invisible teeth-alignment systems for adults and children, delivered through a network of partner dental clinics and orthodontists. Its digital treatment platform pairs the C4 adult-correction system with the C3 pediatric full-cycle system, and is supported by a doctor-facing web portal for case submission, treatment planning, and aligner ordering. The company reports more than 11,900 registered doctors and 9,200 partner clinics across 321 cities. Clearbos was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.
c.name: Clearbos (clearorthod)

c.description: ClearCam provides AI-powered object detection and search for CCTV camera feeds. It runs locally on user hardware for privacy, supporting RTSP streams and offering premium mobile notifications. ClearCam aims to simplify camera integration while leveraging GPU compute, and is open-source with a Python/FFmpeg foundation.
c.name: ClearCam

c.description: ClearCare (originally ClearCare Online) is a web-based home care agency management platform founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco. It provides non-medical home care agencies with back-office and point-of-care tooling: caregiver scheduling, telephony-based clock-in/clock-out and electronic visit verification (EVV), billing and payroll, client and caregiver management, care planning, a family room portal, and business analytics. ClearCare was backed by Battery Ventures and Cendana Capital and was acquired by WellSky (formerly Mediware) in 2019; the product is now marketed as WellSky Personal Care, and the clearcareonline.com domain redirects to WellSky. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched as a historical company record — ClearCare no longer operates a standalone public developer or API program.
c.name: ClearCare

c.description: Clearco (formerly Clearbanc) is a Toronto-based fintech that provides non-dilutive, revenue-based working capital to ecommerce and direct-to-consumer brands. Founders connect the sales, advertising and banking platforms they already run on — Shopify, Amazon, Stripe, PayPal, Square, BigCommerce — and Clearco underwrites from that data, funding inventory and marketing spend as a cash advance or as invoice funding, in as little as 24 hours, without equity dilution. The company was founded in 2015 as Clearbanc, rebranded to Clearco in 2021, and reports having deployed more than $3.3 billion to over 10,000 businesses.
c.name: Clearco

c.description: Clearcover is a digital-first auto insurance company that offers customizable, affordable car insurance backed by AI-assisted claims that can resolve eligible claims in minutes rather than days. Customers buy and manage policies through a mobile app, file claims by photographing damage, and track claim status in real time, with coverage spanning liability, comprehensive and collision, medical payments, uninsured/underinsured motorist protection, roadside assistance, and alternate transportation. Clearcover operates across multiple US states through several underwriting entities, distributes through both direct and independent-agent channels, and runs a developer portal for partner and embedded insurance integrations. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from its public web surface.
c.name: Clearcover

c.description: ClearDATA is healthcare's dedicated cloud security, compliance, and operations partner, helping providers, payers, health-tech software companies, medical device makers, and life sciences organizations build and run on AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud in a HIPAA- and HITRUST-aligned way. Its offering spans Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) with 300+ healthcare-specific safeguards, Managed Detection & Response (MDR), automated Cloud Compliance, and Cloud Operations, delivered through the CyberHealth platform and managed/professional services. ClearDATA is an AWS Level 1 MSSP and Microsoft Gold Partner, and maps controls to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO, PCI, and GDPR. ClearDATA is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; ClearDATA does not publish a public developer API or portal.
c.name: Cleardata

c.description: ClearFlame Engine Technologies was a Woodridge, Illinois clean-combustion engine startup founded in 2016 by BJ Johnson and Julie Blumreiter, developing a retrofit technology that let conventional heavy-duty diesel engines run on ethanol and other low-carbon liquid fuels for the hard-to-electrify segments of transportation — long-haul trucking, agriculture, construction and other non-road diesel applications. It raised roughly $50M across Series A and B rounds from venture and industrial investors including John Deere, and appeared on secondary markets such as Forge Global. The company is a hardware and powertrain engineering business with no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable specifications; by 2025 it had lost investor support, its co-founder CEO had departed, it was listed as not in good standing in Illinois, and it moved toward bankruptcy and asset liquidation. Its website no longer serves content.
c.name: ClearFlame Engines

c.description: ClearFlow provides innovative medical devices and solutions focused on improving patient recovery after surgery. Their flagship product PleuraFlow offers active chest tube clearance, reducing complications such as retained blood syndrome and postoperative atrial fibrillation. ClearFlow’s technology integrates into enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs, delivering faster patient discharge, lower ICU stays, and overall better outcomes. The company emphasizes a patient‑centric approach, combining clinical evidence with modern medical device engineering to support hospitals worldwide.
c.name: ClearFlow

c.description: ClearGov provides a cloud‑based financial engagement platform for local governments, enabling transparent budgeting, strategic planning, capital project tracking, and public reporting. Their tools help municipalities build trust through clear financial storytelling, interactive dashboards, and citizen engagement features, serving over 2,000 public finance teams nationwide.
c.name: ClearGov

c.description: Cleargraph was a Palo Alto, California startup building natural-language and graph-based search over data, operating under the tagline "Data Accessible through Search." It was backed by Version One Ventures and appears in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company is inactive - its primary domain cleargraph.com now 301-redirects off-site, its cleargraph.io website no longer resolves (connection refused), and its GitHub organization (github.com/cleargraph) was archived in April 2026 and holds only forked libraries with no first-party API, SDK, or specification. No live API, developer portal, documentation, or first-party package surface could be verified during enrichment, so no API artifacts were generated.
c.name: Cleargraph

c.description: Clearing (WTUK Limited trading as Clearing) is a cross-border financial infrastructure provider offering multi-currency accounts, global payments, cross-currency liquidity, and digital-asset settlement to businesses operating internationally. It is a regulated electronic money institution: authorised by the UK FCA under the Electronic Money Regulations (ref 900536), licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payments Institution (PS20200445), and registered with FINTRAC in Canada. This record was surfaced as a stub via VC-portfolio tagging (sector originally recorded as healthcare); on enrichment the clearing.com domain resolves to this fintech/payments company, and no public developer API surface was found.
c.name: Clearing

c.description: ClearLaw provides AI‑powered legal data extraction and contract intelligence solutions. Their platform integrates with existing CLM systems and litigation workflows, delivering accurate answers from legal documents for law firms, enterprises, and public sector clients. Services include contract migration, regulatory compliance assistance, and real‑time legal analytics, all deployed within customers’ existing tools.
c.name: ClearLaw

c.description: Clearmindbiomedical is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clearmindbiomedical

c.description: ClearMix was a technology startup founded by Gabriel Ruttner and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It is listed in Bloomberg Beta's public portfolio with an exit marker, indicating the company has since exited (acquired or wound down). As of the last enrichment pass no live company, developer, or API surface could be located - candidate domains do not resolve - so there are no public API artifacts to harvest. This profile remains an identity-only lead in the API Evangelist network pending discovery of any successor or archived developer surface.
c.name: ClearMix

c.description: ClearML is an open-source MLOps platform with experiment tracking, datasets, model serving, and orchestration. The ClearML Server exposes a versioned REST API split across services (auth, projects, tasks, workers, models, queues, events, pipelines).
c.name: ClearML

c.description: ClearMotion is an automotive motion-technology company founded out of MIT in 2012 by Zack Anderson and Shakeel Avadhany, headquartered at its US innovation lab in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a UK engineering hub at MIRA Technology Park in Nuneaton, a Shanghai office, and a production plant in Changshu, China. Its CM1 fully active suspension system pairs the ActiValve digital hydraulic actuator with software that counteracts road disturbances in milliseconds, and its RoadMotion service is a crowdsourced, cloud-based road-surface intelligence layer that fuses data from vehicle sensors into a high-definition surface map accurate to better than 20mm, feeding proactive suspension, chassis and ADAS decisions. The company absorbed the Bose Ride and Project Sound active-suspension programs, is led by CEO Christian Steinmann, and ships with NIO (ET9, ES9) alongside collaborations with Porsche, BWI Group and Sona Comstar.
