Marketing material describes RoadMotion as an "end-to-end cloud API solution", but ClearMotion publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or /.well-known discovery surface — the API is an OEM/B2B integration rather than a self-serve public API.
c.name: ClearMotion

c.description: ClearNote Health (formerly Bluestar Genomics) is a US cancer detection company with offices in San Diego and San Mateo, California. Its proprietary 5hmC epigenomic platform combines cell-free DNA sequencing from a standard blood draw with machine learning to identify DNA-based alterations as cancer develops. The company commercializes Avantect, a suite of early-detection liquid biopsy tests for pancreatic and ovarian cancer that clinicians order through its laboratory, and Virtuoso, a research-use-only epigenomics platform sold to biopharma for drug discovery, therapy response and resistance research. ClearNote Health publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification: the clinician ordering path is a hosted intake form, and its public GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source bioinformatics tooling.
c.name: ClearNote Health

c.description: ClearScore is a London-founded fintech (2015) that gives consumers free access to their credit score and report and matches them to financial products — credit cards, loans, car finance, insurance and more — through a personalised financial marketplace. It also runs ClearScore Protect (dark-web identity monitoring), DriveScore (driving-behaviour scoring) and Open Banking features, and operates across the UK, South Africa, Australia, Canada and New Zealand. Its B2B arm, ClearScore Connect, exposes credit-data and eligibility services to partner lenders through a partner-gated developer portal (docs.clearscore.com). Backed by QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearScore's developer API is documented behind a password-gated ReadMe.io portal, so no public OpenAPI or machine-readable spec could be captured.
c.name: Clearscore

c.description: Clearsense provides an enterprise healthcare data platform that enables organizations to unify, archive, and manage large volumes of clinical and operational data. Their solutions include data archiving, managed services, and research acceleration tools, helping healthcare providers improve cost savings, revenue recovery, and data accessibility across multiple systems. The company serves hundreds of hospitals and health systems, offering cloud‑native, scalable platforms for data integration, analytics, and compliance.
c.name: Clearsense

c.description: ClearSlide is a sales engagement platform, now part of Bigtincan, that unifies content management, communications (email, web conferencing, screen share), and real-time engagement analytics so sales teams can make every buyer interaction count. Its public Platform API lets customers and partners programmatically list presentations, create trackable links, retrieve engagement insights, manage users (including SCIM provisioning), upload content to Amazon S3, and reserve and manage scheduled meetings. The API uses OAuth 2.0 and is documented on a public ReadMe developer portal at developer.clearslide.com. ClearSlide was originally an a16z-backed company and is profiled here in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: ClearSlide

c.description: Clearspeed is a voice-based risk assessment company whose AI analyzes involuntary vocal characteristics — tone, cadence, hesitation and stress — in a subject's spoken yes/no answers to produce an objective, language-independent risk indicator without requiring PII. Founded in 2016, it serves insurance claims and underwriting, government and defense vetting, financial services fraud and AML/KYC, plus hiring and vendor screening. Clearspeed exposes the Clearspeed Integration API, a REST contract on regional US and UK hosts that lets customers create participants against a questionnaire, track outcomes, and manage scoped API keys, with assessment results delivered back by webhook rather than polling.
c.name: Clearspeed

c.description: Clearstep is a digital health company whose clinical AI agents automate patient triage, scheduling, and care navigation for hospitals and health systems. Built on gold-standard, nurse-developed clinical protocols and integrated with Epic and other electronic health record systems, Clearstep's conversational Symptom Checker and Clinical Triage products help patients understand their symptoms and get routed to the right level of care, while reducing call-center and emergency-department burden for provider organizations. The company sells to leading health systems nationwide and is a Techstars-backed portfolio company.
c.name: Clearstep

c.description: Clearstory is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clearstory

c.description: Clearstory Data was a big-data analytics startup (Menlo Park / Mountain View, CA) that built a cloud service for blending and visualizing enterprise and third-party data, backed by a16z, GV (Google Ventures), Kleiner Perkins and Khosla Ventures. It was acquired by Alteryx in 2016 and is no longer an independent company. Its former domain (clearstorydata.com) has lapsed and now 301-redirects to unrelated parked/spam sites, so it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio record; no live artifacts are producible.
c.name: Clearstory Data

c.description: Clearstream Banking S.A. is the Deutsche Borse Group post-trade infrastructure business, providing settlement, custody, collateral management and investment-fund order routing for international securities. Its programmable surface has two layers. The incumbent layer is regulated post-trade messaging: clients connect through ClearstreamXact (Xact Web Portal, Xact File Transfer over SWIFTNet FileAct, and Xact via SWIFT FIN), CASCADE via SWIFT and MQ, Vestima for fund order routing and CmaX for triparty collateral, exchanging ISO 15022 MT and ISO 20022 MX messages whose specifications Clearstream publishes to SWIFT MyStandards, with migration to ISO 20022 driven by the SWIFT CBPR+ programme. The newer layer is a genuine REST platform at api.clearstream.com, running an OAuth 2.0 password grant hardened by mandatory mutual TLS, whose first published API is SCIM 2.0 user management for the Xact Web Portal; a free synthetic Playground API and a CmaX collateral surface are live alongside it. The OpenAPI definitions are published into the Deutsche Borse Digital Business Platform catalogue, which requires registration.
c.name: Clearstream

c.description: Clearstreet8e71 is a financial technology company offering a modern, cloud‑native brokerage platform for institutional investors and family offices. It provides real‑time trading APIs, market data, clearing, financing, and AI‑driven execution tools. The platform serves over 700 institutional clients, handling billions in assets, and emphasizes speed, transparency, and scalability for sophisticated traders.
c.name: Clearstreet8e71

c.description: Cleartax (operating as Clear, clear.in) is an Indian fintech and financial-compliance automation platform that provides tax, GST, and e-invoicing software for individuals, tax professionals, and over 4,000 enterprises. Clear exposes a suite of developer APIs through its documentation portal at docs.cleartax.in, including the Clear Finance Cloud (CFC) ingestion APIs, the GST 2.0 / GSP filing API, the Max ITC input-tax-credit reconciliation API, the GLS API, the E-Invoicing and E-Waybill APIs (with government IRP/NIC-compatible endpoints and DSC signing), the Invoicing API, and KSA (Saudi Arabia) e-invoicing APIs. APIs authenticate with a client secret exchanged for an access token and run against production (api.clear.in) and sandbox (api-sandbox.clear.in) hosts.
c.name: Cleartax

c.description: Cleartrip is a leading online travel booking platform that enables users to search, compare, and book flights, hotels, and holiday packages. Founded in 2006, the company offers a user-friendly interface and a robust API suite for partners to integrate travel services into their applications. Cleartrip’s services focus on providing transparent pricing, secure transactions, and comprehensive travel options across multiple airlines and hotel providers, catering to both individual travelers and corporate clients.
c.name: Cleartrip

c.description: ClearVector is an identity-driven detection and response platform for cloud production environments. It attributes every action in real time to human, non-human, and third-party identities across AWS, GCP, and Azure, threading together activity across GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, cloud control planes, and runtime (EC2, Lambda, containers). Per-customer predictive behavioral models surface risky behavior, and one-click isolation contains compromised identities and resources without disrupting production. Offered as SaaS, an Enterprise plan, and a ClearVector Private SaaS deployment for teams that need complete infrastructure control. Backed by Menlo Ventures. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearVector publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — the product is delivered through a login-gated application at app.clearvector.com.
c.name: Clearvector

c.description: Clearview AI is a U.S.-based facial recognition company providing identity verification, investigative search, and biometric matching services primarily to law enforcement, government agencies, and approved financial sector customers. The platform indexes publicly available images and exposes proprietary facial recognition technology through a controlled, customer-vetted developer surface. Public technical documentation of the API is intentionally limited; access is gated, and integrations are scoped through customer agreements with strict use-case, audit, and transparency requirements.
c.name: Clearview AI

c.description: ClearVIN is a vehicle-history and VIN data provider and an approved NMVTIS data provider. Its REST API decodes North American (U.S. and Canada) VINs into 100+ specification data points and returns full vehicle history reports - title, junk / salvage / total-loss records, odometer events, and market valuation - sourced directly from government and industry data, covering model years 1981 to present.
c.name: ClearVIN

c.description: Clearwater Paper Corporation (NYSE: CLW) is a Spokane, Washington-based manufacturer of bleached paperboard for North American packaging converters and, historically, private-label tissue for retailers. It is a Fortune 1000 company with mills in Idaho, Arkansas and Georgia. Clearwater Paper publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable contract: its corporate site is an investor-relations platform with a customer-login landing page that describes, but does not name or link, a secure customer web portal, and the api./developer. hostnames an earlier version of this record pointed at do not exist in DNS. Trading-partner EDI (X12 850/810/856/997) is offered only through third-party VAN and integration vendors, not from a Clearwater Paper developer surface.
c.name: Clearwater Paper

c.description: Clearwave is a patient revenue-cycle and self-service engagement platform for healthcare practices, covering online scheduling, self-service registration and intake, multi-factor insurance eligibility verification, and patient payments. Rather than publishing an open developer API, Clearwave connects to more than 50 electronic health record (EHR) and practice management (PM) systems - including athenahealth, NextGen, eClinicalWorks, Modernizing Medicine, Veradigm, Nextech, Greenway, and Unlimited Systems - through formal, partner-gated API license and integration agreements. Data such as appointments, patient demographics, eligibility results, and payments flows bidirectionally between Clearwave and the practice's EHR/PM in real time. There is no public, self-service developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or documented public WebSocket API; the API surfaces below are logical capability areas modeled from Clearwave's product documentation, not publicly documented endpoints.
c.name: Clearwave

c.description: Clearwell Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of redpoint-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Clearwell Systems

c.description: Clearyst provides a sustainability operating system for mid‑market and enterprise organizations, offering tools for EPR compliance, GHG reporting, supply‑chain sustainability, workforce engagement, and other ESG initiatives. Their platform integrates data‑driven solutions to help companies meet regulatory requirements and sustainability goals across multiple jurisdictions.
c.name: Clearyst

c.description: Cledara is a SaaS management platform that helps companies manage, control, and optimize software spending. The platform provides visibility into all software subscriptions, virtual payment cards with per-vendor spending limits, approval workflows, vendor renewal tracking, usage analytics, and accounting and ERP integrations. Cledara serves finance, IT, procurement, and operations teams across companies looking to consolidate SaaS purchasing and reduce spend leakage.
c.name: Cledara

c.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.
c.name: Cleerly

c.description: Clementine (Clementine Labs) was a New York based enterprise communication startup founded in 2013 and publicly launched in September 2014, offering workplace messaging, chat, and conference calling that let colleagues reach each other without exchanging personal mobile phone numbers. It appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list and was acquired by Dropbox in April 2016, after which the Clementine service was shut down and the team folded into Dropbox collaboration efforts. The company operates no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs today: its primary domain, clementine.io, now issues an HTTP 301 redirect to dropbox.com. This profile is retained as a historical, non-operational record in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Clementine

c.description: Cleo is an AI-powered personal finance assistant delivered through a chat interface in iOS and Android apps. The platform helps consumers budget, track spending across linked bank accounts, set savings goals, and access features such as Cleo Wallet (savings), Cleo Cover (cash advance), and Cleo Builder (credit-building). Cleo connects to user bank accounts using Plaid for read-only transaction access and does not currently publish a public, third-party developer API.
c.name: Cleo

c.description: Cleo+Coco creates next-level clean, high-performance personal care products for every body. Their natural deodorants, body powders, dry hair shampoo, and functional sprays are aluminum‑free, synthetic‑fragrance‑free, and feature five odor‑fighting ingredients. The brand emphasizes safe, effective ingredients, real protection, and confidence, targeting consumers seeking clean, sustainable personal care solutions.
c.name: Cleo+Coco

c.description: Cleoai provides AI-powered customer support agents that automate ticket handling, email responses, and even code bug fixes. Their platform offers two main agents: a Support Agent for handling customer inquiries and an AI Engineer that can understand and patch software code. Built for SaaS companies, support teams, and agencies, CleoAI integrates with email inboxes, knowledge bases, and GitHub repositories to streamline support workflows, reduce response times, and improve customer satisfaction.
c.name: Cleoai

c.description: Clerio Vision is a development-stage ophthalmic medical device company based in Rochester, New York, commercializing LIRIC (Laser Induced Refractive Index Change) — a non-invasive femtosecond-laser platform, licensed from the University of Rochester's Center for Visual Science, that alters the refractive index of corneal tissue and of polymer optics without cutting or removing material. The company applies LIRIC across four ophthalmic segments: multifocal soft contact lenses for presbyopia, myopia control in children, post-implant intraocular lens (IOL) optimization after cataract surgery, and incisionless corneal refractive correction. Clerio has raised roughly $40 million from Safar Partners, Armory Square Ventures, Topmark Partners, Proxima Ventures, Atma Capital, Hegemon Capital and the National Science Foundation, and holds more than 90 patents across over 30 families. Its products are lasers, optics and lenses rather than software; the company publishes a single-page marketing and investor website and operates no public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal.
c.name: Clerio Vision

c.description: Clerk is a complete user management and authentication infrastructure platform offering embeddable UI components, flexible APIs, and admin dashboards. It provides full-stack authentication including multi-factor authentication, social sign-on, passkeys, organizations for B2B SaaS, billing, session management, and machine-to-machine authentication, with SDKs spanning Next.js, React, Expo, iOS, Android, Go, Python, Ruby, Java, PHP, and C#.
c.name: Clerk

c.description: Clerk.io is an e-commerce personalization platform that uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to deliver tailored product recommendations, on-site search results, audience-segmented email campaigns, and merchandising controls for online retailers. The platform exposes a REST API for product, category, order, and customer data ingestion, plus client-side JavaScript and Liquid templating for recommendation slots and search experiences.
c.name: Clerk.io

c.description: Clerka9b8 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clerka9b8

c.description: Clerkie, operated by Henry Labs Inc. and founded in San Francisco in 2016, is an AI-powered debt management and loan-recovery platform serving both consumers and institutional lenders. The consumer side offers a conversational financial assistant for budgeting, debt negotiation, and personalized repayment planning, while the B2B side — marketed as Fiber, launched in 2021 and now sold on its own domain getfiber.ai — gives lenders, banks, credit unions, and collection agencies an AI-driven recovery suite spanning CRM, an inventory management system (IMS), an AI agent, omnichannel communications, borrower scoring, a self-service payment portal, and workflow automation. Clerkie markets a RESTful API and multi-currency payment processing for lenders to integrate loan portfolios, real-time reporting, and automated repayment arrangements, but publishes no public developer documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer portal — integration is arranged through a sales conversation. The company has raised over $41M from Left Lane Capital, Flourish Ventures, Vestigo Ventures, and Citibank.
c.name: Clerkie

c.description: Clerky is an online legal service that helps startup founders handle their legal paperwork safely and efficiently. Designed by startup attorneys formerly at a Silicon Valley law firm, Clerky provides software and guided workflows for Delaware incorporation and post-incorporation setup, fundraising (SAFEs, convertible notes, board consents), hiring (offer letters, consulting agreements, equity compensation), commercial documents (NDAs), and ongoing corporate maintenance. Clerky is a Y Combinator portfolio company. It is a legal document assistant rather than a law firm, and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic integrations.
c.name: Clerky

c.description: Clerq provides a next‑generation bank payments platform that enables businesses to accept low‑cost, guaranteed payments directly from customers’ bank accounts, both online and in‑store. By integrating with over 5,000 banks, Clerc reduces card processing fees by up to 75 % and offers chargeback guarantees, helping merchants increase conversion and cut costs. The platform serves sectors such as automotive, powersports, and e‑commerce, offering developer tools, sandbox environments, and comprehensive documentation.
c.name: Clerq

c.description: Cleveland-Cliffs is North America's largest flat-rolled steel producer and supplier of iron ore pellets, operating an integrated business spanning mining, steelmaking, and downstream finishing for the automotive, infrastructure, and manufacturing markets. Cleveland-Cliffs does not publish a public developer portal, an OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, or any general-purpose REST API. Its documented machine-to-machine surface is batch EDI: ANSI ASC X12 version 4010 over SFTP or an IBM Sterling VAN, with 23 implementation guidelines and an X12 testing template published as public downloads for outside processors at Burns Harbor, Cleveland, Indiana Harbor and Kote. Its transactional applications (Outside Processors Portal, iSupplier, Customer Service Center, Vendor Inquiry) are login-gated, and the only machine-readable discovery documents it serves are OIDC and RFC 8414 metadata on its own Okta tenant at login.clevelandcliffs.com plus an RFC 9116 security.txt.
c.name: Cleveland-Cliffs

c.description: ClevelandDx, operating as Cleveland Diagnostics, provides innovative cancer diagnostic testing, including the IsoPSA test and the IsoClear platform. The company focuses on early detection of cancer through advanced protein biomarker analysis, offering services to clinicians and patients worldwide. Their mission is to improve cancer decision-making with more accurate and rapid diagnostic tools, supported by a leadership team and extensive research collaborations.
c.name: ClevelandDx

c.description: Clever is a K-12 EdTech identity platform that provides a unified single sign-on portal and roster synchronization service used by over 111,000 US schools, including 95 of the largest 100 districts. The Clever REST API enables application partners to securely access real-time student roster data, school and district information, class and section data, and user identity records through a single integration. Clever Complete offers Secure Sync for district-managed rostering, LMS Connect for gradebook syncing, and Single Sign-On via OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and SAML, eliminating the need for per-SIS integrations. Approximately 60 percent of US students log in monthly through Clever, making it the de facto identity layer for K-12 EdTech applications across the United States.
c.name: Clever

c.description: Clever Care Health Plan is a California Medicare Advantage (HMO and HMO C-SNP) plan headquartered in Huntington Beach, CA, that blends the healing therapies of Eastern medicine with the innovative practices of Western medicine to serve Los Angeles, Orange, San Diego, Riverside, and San Bernardino counties. In compliance with the CMS Interoperability and Patient Access rule (CMS-9115-F), Clever Care operates a secure, standards-based HL7 FHIR R4 API surface (WSO2 gateway) spanning 13 published resource APIs across three domains: Patient Access (CARIN Blue Button), Provider Directory (Da Vinci PDex Plan-Net), and Drug Formulary (Da Vinci US Drug Formulary). Patient Access resources are secured with SMART on FHIR OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect; directory and formulary resources are public and rate-limited. Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, and Prior Authorization APIs are planned for January 1, 2027.
c.name: Clever Care

c.description: Clever Care Health Plan is a California Medicare Advantage (HMO and HMO C-SNP) insurer that blends Eastern and Western medicine for seniors. For developers it publishes an HL7 FHIR R4 (4.0.1) API implementing the CMS Interoperability and Patient Access final rule (CMS-9115-F): a secured Patient Access API (Patient, Coverage, and CARIN Blue Button ExplanationOfBenefit) protected with SMART-on-FHIR OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, plus public, rate-limited Provider Directory and Drug Formulary APIs. The FHIR server runs on WSO2 Open Healthcare with a developer portal for app registration and API subscription.
c.name: Clever Care Health Plan

c.description: Clever Carnivore is a cultivated meat company dedicated to producing real beef, pork, and chicken from cell cultures, eliminating the need for animal slaughter. The company aims to create sustainable, healthier protein with a dramatically lower environmental footprint, addressing food insecurity and climate impact. Their process uses tiny tissue samples and nutrient‑rich media to grow meat in facilities similar to breweries, offering a scalable alternative to traditional livestock farming.
c.name: Clever Carnivore

c.description: Clever Real Estate operates a real‑estate brokerage platform based in Dallas, Texas, offering a low‑commission model for buying, selling, and renting properties. The site provides tools for agents, listings, community information, and a streamlined process for clients, emphasizing customer service and transparency. It includes a public API for accessing property data, agent details, and transaction services, supporting integration with third‑party real‑estate applications.
c.name: Clever Real Estate

c.description: CleverConnect is an award‑winning talent acquisition platform that empowers HR teams with AI‑driven candidate relationship management, CRM, and recruitment automation. The service helps organizations streamline hiring, improve candidate experience, and reduce costs through secure, data‑driven insights and integrations.
c.name: CleverConnect

c.description: CleverDeck is a spaced-repetition flashcard application for iOS, built by an independent developer to help people learn and retain vocabulary and other material more efficiently. It ships hand-made premium decks covering roughly the 3,000 most common words in major foreign languages — Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Russian and advanced English — with translations, transliterations, images, native-speaker audio, and example sentences in both English and the target language. The app uses the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm (as popularized by SuperMemo and Anki) with a customizable learning schedule, cross-device sync, and full offline support. It is free to create and study your own content, with unlimited access to the premium decks for $3 per month. CleverDeck is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or agent-facing surface.
c.name: Cleverdeck

c.description: Clevergy (The Clevergy Solution, SL) is a Madrid-based climate-tech SaaS company, founded in 2022, that sells white-label energy-management software to electricity and gas retailers, solar installers and energy advisors. Its platform ingests household consumption data — pulled directly from Spanish distributors and the Datadis smart-meter hub via the CUPS supply-point code, or from connected solar inverters and smart devices — and turns it into consumption analytics, invoice breakdowns, savings recommendations, appliance-level disaggregation, virtual battery and wallet balances, energy-community shares, and sales leads the retailer can act on. Integrators consume it two ways: the Connect API, a Swagger 2.0 REST API on connect.clever.gy with 83 operations spanning users, houses, contracts, invoices, tariffs, equipment, energy telemetry, tickets and sales opportunities; and a catalog of roughly thirty embeddable "microfrontend" web components that drop Clevergy's end-user experiences straight into the retailer's own app or webview, authenticated with a short-lived per-user JWT. Clevergy raised a €3.2M round in October 2025 co-led by Racine² (Serena and Makesense) and Axon Partners Group, with Satgana, Wayra and Angels participating.
c.name: Clevergy

c.description: CleverPet is a pet-technology company behind the CleverPet Hub, a programmable "game console for pets" that gives dogs and cats mental stimulation through puzzle games and dispenses food treats as rewards. The Hub is built on the Particle IoT platform, and CleverPet publishes hackerpet, an open-source Particle/Arduino C++ library that lets developers write, customize, and share their own games by controlling the Hub's lights, food pod, and tray motor through the HubInterface class. The company was part of the Techstars accelerator, and its team and open-source hardware/software work continued under the FluentPet brand.
c.name: CleverPet

c.description: CleverTap is a customer engagement and retention platform that helps businesses understand user behavior, segment audiences, and deliver personalized experiences across mobile push, email, SMS, in-app, web push, and WhatsApp channels. CleverTap exposes a comprehensive REST API surface covering profiles, events, campaigns, real-time analytics, catalogs, feature flags, and more, authenticated via account ID and passcode headers.
c.name: CleverTap

c.description: Clicampo is a Brazilian ag‑tech platform that digitises trade between farmers, food producers, retailers and restaurants. Founded to reduce intermediaries, it raised $7.5 million seed funding in 2022 to build a marketplace that connects producers directly with buyers, improving profitability and supply‑chain transparency across Brazil’s agricultural sector.
c.name: Clicampo

c.description: ClickMechanic is the UK's leading online car-repair marketplace, founded in 2012, that connects car owners with vetted mobile mechanics and independent garages for repairs, servicing, diagnostics, and MOTs. Customers enter their registration and symptoms to get an instant fixed-price quote, then book a vetted mechanic for same- or next-day work at home or the roadside, with payment taken only after the job is completed. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. ClickMechanic operates a consumer- and mechanic-facing web platform (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API catalog at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Click Mechanic

c.description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. is a New York-headquartered digital medicine company founded in 2012 by David Benshoof Klein that develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments — the category it named Digital Therapeutics. Its AI-enabled platform targets diseases with an underlying neurological or behavioral component through cognitive and neurobehavioral mechanisms, delivered as smartphone software used independently or alongside biomedical therapy (Software-Enhanced Drugs). Authorized and commercial programs include CT-152 (Rejoyn, major depressive disorder, developed with Otsuka), CT-132 (episodic migraine) and AspyreRx (type 2 diabetes), with a pipeline spanning schizophrenia (CT-155 with Boehringer Ingelheim, CT-156), opioid use disorder, multiple sclerosis, atopic dermatitis, obesity, oncology, insomnia and acute coronary syndrome. Click publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK — its software is distributed as regulated prescription therapeutics, not as a platform.
c.name: Click Therapeutics

c.description: Clickable is a marketing analytics and digital advertising platform founded in 2006 that serves as an ads and analytics partner for businesses and agencies. The company builds award-winning pay-per-click (PPC) advertising tools for search and social campaigns and delivers customized reporting that cuts through data overload so marketers can focus on the metrics that matter. Clickable also offers VIN retention reporting purpose-built for automotive dealerships to improve customer retention. Backed by Union Square Ventures, the company focuses on relationship-driven managed advertising and analytics services rather than a public developer API.
c.name: Clickable

c.description: Clickatell is a chat commerce and CPaaS company offering SMS and WhatsApp messaging (One API), the SMS API, Chat 2 Pay payments-in-chat, and Chat Flow workflow APIs for businesses.
c.name: Clickatell

c.description: Clicker is a consumer-facing streaming guide and discovery platform that helps people find where to watch popular and new movies and TV shows across streaming providers, aggregating title availability from services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Max, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, Paramount+, Peacock, Starz, BET+, Philo, and FuboTV into a single searchable catalog. The product is a web application (Next.js) organized around TV Shows and Movies browse and search experiences. Clicker is backed by Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Clicker publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; its only backend surface is a private, robots disallowed internal application API.
c.name: Clicker

c.description: ClickFunnels is a sales funnel and online business platform that lets entrepreneurs build landing pages, sales funnels, checkout flows, courses, membership sites, communities, blogs and email marketing campaigns without code. The ClickFunnels 2.0 REST API is a 418-operation OpenAPI 3.1 contract covering teams, workspaces, funnels, pages, blogs, products, discounts, orders, invoices, transactions, subscriptions, contacts, courses, communities, forms, workflows, email and analytics, authenticated with a team-scoped Bearer token or with workspace-scoped OAuth 2.0. It is discoverable the correct way: an RFC 9727 api-catalog links the spec, RFC 8414 metadata publishes the OAuth scopes, and sixteen Markdown Agent Skills are served from /.well-known/ for agents driving the API.
c.name: ClickFunnels

c.description: ClickHouse is a fast open-source column-oriented database management system that enables real-time analytical reporting using SQL. ClickHouse exposes multiple interfaces - an HTTP interface for SQL queries, native TCP, MySQL and PostgreSQL wire-compatible interfaces, and a gRPC interface - and the ClickHouse Cloud management plane offers a public OpenAPI-described REST API for provisioning and managing services, organizations, members, API keys, backups, and private endpoints.
c.name: ClickHouse

c.description: Monitor, compare and optimize your marketing links
c.name: ClickMeter

c.description: Clickocom is a technology company that provides a platform for managing click-based advertising campaigns and analytics. The company offers APIs that enable developers to integrate campaign creation, tracking, reporting, and optimization features into their own applications. Clickocom focuses on delivering real-time data, robust authentication, and scalable services for advertisers and partners seeking to automate their digital marketing workflows.
c.name: Clickocom

c.description: ClickPost is a logistics and supply chain platform that aggregates 500+ carrier integrations, multi-channel customer notifications, and 50+ storefront/OMS/WMS connectors behind a unified REST API. The platform covers carrier recommendation, order creation (single and multi-piece), serviceability, manifesting, pickups, real-time tracking with webhooks, proof of delivery, NDR (non-delivery report) management, returns, and expected delivery date forecasting for both Indian domestic and international shipments.
c.name: ClickPost

c.description: Clicks (Clicks Health) is an AI-native operations company that deploys AI agents to run complete healthcare back-office workflows. Its agents handle revenue cycle management (eligibility and insurance verification, prior authorization, claim status checking, denials management, and patient refunds), patient access, and other repetitive tasks by working inside a customer's existing EHR, practice-management, and payer systems either through APIs or the same screens staff use. Clicks integrates with major health IT platforms including Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, NextGen Healthcare, and MEDITECH, and states it is SOC 2 Type II audited and HIPAA compliant with end-to-end encryption for PHI. Founded in 2025, headquartered in Switzerland, and backed by Y Combinator (F2025).
c.name: Clicks

c.description: ClickSend is a cloud communications company providing a single REST API for business messaging across SMS, MMS, voice / text-to-speech, transactional email, and physical post - letters and postcards printed and mailed globally. The v3 API (rest.clicksend.com/v3) uses HTTP Basic authentication with a username and API key and covers sending, delivery receipts, inbound handling, contacts and lists, and account balance.
c.name: ClickSend

c.description: ClickSend is a global business communications platform for sending and receiving SMS, MMS, voice, email, fax, and physical post via API or web dashboard, with direct carrier routing and a 99.95% uptime SLA. The ClickSend REST API v3 provides endpoints for SMS, MMS, voice, email, fax, post letters, contacts, accounts, and webhooks, secured with HTTP Basic Authentication using a username and API key.
c.name: ClickSend SMS

c.description: Clicktivated is a video technology platform that turns existing video content into interactive, shoppable experiences without re-shooting or re-editing. Its "Activate, Distribute, Optimize" workflow makes any video clickable the same day, deploys it programmatically across DSPs, SSPs, publishers, and direct site embeds, and captures first-party intent signals - item-level and place-level - to improve targeting, measure lift, and drive better performance. The company serves retail brands closing the gap between inspiration and purchase, and tourism brands converting inspiration into itineraries. Founded as Clicktivated Video, Inc. and backed by Techstars, with offices in Detroit, New York, Dubai, and Sydney.
c.name: Clicktivated

c.description: ClickUp is a work management platform — tasks, Lists, Folders, Spaces, Docs, Chat, Goals, time tracking, dashboards and automations in one Workspace. It ships a public REST API in two concurrent versions: v2 (138 operations, the broad surface) and v3 (35 operations, Chat, Docs, attachments, audit logs and ACLs), both published as first-party OpenAPI documents and advertised through an RFC 9727 api-catalog at developer.clickup.com. Authentication is a single Authorization header carrying either a personal token or an OAuth 2.0 access token authorized per Workspace; there are no OAuth scopes. Webhooks are HMAC-SHA256 signed. ClickUp also runs a remote MCP server at mcp.clickup.com with its own OAuth authorization server, PKCE and dynamic client registration, exposing 48 documented tools. Rate limits are per token and set by the Workspace plan. There is no sandbox, no idempotency mechanism and no published deprecation policy.
c.name: Clickup

c.description: Clicky (ClickyPass) was an Argentine fitness-membership startup founded in 2015 in Cordoba by Ezequiel Bucai. It offered a single all-access monthly pass ($15-60/mo) that let members build their own fitness schedule across a network of gyms, studios and sports centers in Latin America - crossfit, zumba, yoga, running and more - on the same aggregator model as ClassPass and Gympass. It was backed by 500 Global, Start-Up Chile and Parallel18 (about $125K raised) and was acquired by ClassPass on March 2, 2020; founder Ezequiel Bucai joined ClassPass as Head of Partner Development for Chile and Argentina. The company no longer operates independently - the clickypass.com domain now 301-redirects to classpass.com - and it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal of its own. Retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired 500 Global portfolio lead.
c.name: Clicky

c.description: URL shortener service
c.name: Clico

c.description: Clicoh provides intelligent logistics solutions for e‑commerce businesses, offering AI‑powered warehousing, fulfillment, and last‑mile delivery across multiple countries. Their platform enables merchants to reduce costs, accelerate sales, and ensure high on‑time delivery rates through integrated storage, custom packaging, and real‑time tracking.
c.name: Clicoh

c.description: Clientbook is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clientbook

c.description: This is the index of API client, HTTP client, and API consumer tools repos being tracked by the API Evangelist network. The collection includes command-line HTTP clients, GUI desktop and IDE clients, language-native HTTP libraries, and API testing/consumption tools.
c.name: Clients

c.description: ClientSuccess provides a comprehensive customer success platform that helps businesses reduce churn, increase revenue, and deliver world‑class customer experiences. The SaaS solution combines AI‑driven insights, automation, and a unified portal for onboarding, journey management, and analytics, enabling teams to act on real‑time health scores, NPS, and product feedback. It integrates with major CRMs and support tools, offering a scalable, data‑driven approach to customer lifecycle management.
c.name: ClientSuccess

c.description: Cliffs Natural Resources is the legacy corporate name for what is now Cleveland-Cliffs Inc., a major mining and natural resources company that produces iron ore pellets primarily for steelmaking customers in North America. The company was renamed Cleveland-Cliffs in 2017 and the canonical profile lives at the cleveland-cliffs repo. Cliffs Natural Resources / Cleveland-Cliffs does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface.
c.name: Cliffs Natural Resources

c.description: Clikalia is a Spanish proptech founded in 2018 by Alister Moreno and Pablo Fernandez that operates an iBuyer model for residential real estate: it makes homeowners an instant purchase offer, can close a sale within days, then renovates and returns properties to the market in turnkey condition. The company pairs proprietary technology with a large operations team to digitize a historically slow home buying and selling process, and also offers mortgage brokerage (hipotecas) and renovation services (Studio by Clikalia). Backed by Fifth Wall and SoftBank Vision Fund, Clikalia operates across Spain, Portugal, France and Mexico. Clikalia does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and domain-security surface.
c.name: Clikalia

c.description: Climacell (styled ClimaCell) was a Boston-based weather-intelligence startup that pioneered a "Weather of Things" approach — deriving hyperlocal precipitation and atmospheric conditions from wireless-signal attenuation, connected devices, and its own proprietary numerical weather model — and exposed it through a developer-facing REST weather API. Backed by Canaan Partners among others, the company rebranded to Tomorrow.io in 2020 and its legacy climacell.co domain now 301-redirects to www.tomorrow.io. The surviving product is the Tomorrow.io v4 Weather API, which supersedes the original ClimaCell v3 API and exposes 60+ hyperlocal data layers (core weather, air quality, pollen, fire, flood, lightning, maritime, aviation, road) with realtime, forecast, historical, map-tile, and webhook-alert access. This profile is the historical ClimaCell identity; the enriched, live provider record lives in the api-evangelist tomorrow-io repository.
c.name: Climacell

c.description: Climate Engine is a geospatial climate and remote-sensing data platform that runs on Google Earth Engine. Its commercial REST API (api.climateengine.org) provides on-demand processing of satellite and gridded climate datasets - Landsat, Sentinel, MODIS, GRIDMET, ERA5, CHIRPS and more - returning timeseries, map tiles, zonal statistics, and pre-built reports over points, polygons, and feature collections.
c.name: Climate Engine

c.description: Climate FieldView is a digital agriculture platform from Bayer (originally developed by The Climate Corporation) that gives growers, agronomists, and agribusiness partners a single view of field-level operations. The platform ingests as-planted, as-applied, and as-harvested data from field equipment, combines it with imagery, weather, and soil layers, and exposes those agronomic datasets through a REST API at api.climate.com. Authentication is via OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant, and resources include fields, planting and harvest activities, application records, and soil samples.
c.name: Climate FieldView

c.description: Climate Robotics Network is a community-driven organization focused on advancing climate‑positive robotics across aerial, marine, and ground platforms. It connects innovators, researchers, and practitioners through projects, summits, internships, and consulting services, fostering inclusive collaboration to accelerate climate‑resilient technology development.
c.name: Climate Robotics

c.description: Climate X is a London-headquartered climate risk analytics company that translates physical climate hazards into financial loss metrics for banks, insurers, asset managers, real estate firms, and consultancies. Its Spectra product models a range of physical climate hazards across roughly 1.5 billion global assets under multiple emissions scenarios and time horizons, delivering asset- and portfolio-level annual loss, probability, and severity estimates via a web platform, CSV export, BI tools, and an Enterprise API. Additional products include Adapt (adaptation capex and ROI), Carta (global asset location and exposure mapping), and Adaptation Finance. Climate X is ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 14001 certified and a certified B Corporation. The Enterprise API is currently gated behind sales, so no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal is available.
c.name: Climate-X

c.description: ClimateAi (climate.ai) is a climate-intelligence company that turns global weather, climate and extreme-event modeling into decision-grade forecasts for agriculture, food and beverage, manufacturing, energy, finance, retail and federal/defense customers. Its ClimateLens products cover risk screening, monitoring and adaptation, and its developer surface is the LensConnect API — a REST weather and climate data API addressed by latitude and longitude that returns 30+ years of history (1995-present, ERA5-backed), a fixed 30-year climatology baseline, and AI-stitched probabilistic forecasts running from short-term through seasonal (~6 months) in a single continuous timeline, at ~25 km resolution with optional 1 km downscaling for select variables. A separate ClimateAI Platform gateway handles accounts, users, roles, permissions, device API keys and product routing.
c.name: ClimateAI

c.description: Climatiq provides a developer-first API for carbon accounting and emissions calculations. The platform packages a curated emission-factor database together with calculation endpoints that turn activity or spend data into auditable CO2-equivalent estimates aligned with the GHG Protocol. Capabilities span search across the factor catalog, generic activity-based estimation, and purpose-built endpoints for travel, freight (GLEC), energy, cloud computing, procurement, and the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The API is keyed (Bearer token) and hosted at api.climatiq.io.
c.name: Climatiq

c.description: Climavision is a Louisville, Kentucky weather intelligence company that combines a proprietary nationwide supplemental network of low-altitude X-band, dual-polarization gap-filling weather radars with AI-driven numerical weather prediction (NWP) to deliver enterprise-grade forecasts and observational data. Its Horizon AI product line includes Horizon Point for site-specific forecasts, Horizon Global for ground-to-high- altitude global models, Horizon HI-RES for custom high-resolution local forecasting, and Horizon S2S for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction. Climavision exposes a Weather API hosted at point-forecast-api.climavision.com with 1,800+ parameters, 15-day forecasts, and bearer-token authentication, plus a separate Radar Status API and Radar-as-a-Service offering that supplies Level II files, NetCDF, and GeoTIFF radar data products (reflectivity, velocity, dual-pol-derived QPE at 1km, precipitation type, tornado debris detection) for coverage below 4,000 feet where NEXRAD cannot see due to Earth curvature. The company integrates its radar feed into MRMS and has provided supplemental data into the National Weather Service's AWIPS software. Climavision processes 1.5+ billion datasets daily, serves customers across agriculture, aviation, commodity trading, drones and Advanced Air Mobility, energy and utilities, government, insurance and reinsurance, media, and transportation and logistics, and raised a $100 million strategic investment from TPG's Rise Fund. API access is gated through a sales-led contact process; no public sandbox or open-source SDKs are published, and the Climavision GitHub organization (github.com/Climavision) currently has only two minor public repositories (an archived Azure Table Storage helper and a GeoServer Helm chart fork).
c.name: Climavision

c.description: Climax Foods is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Climax Foods

c.description: Climbcredit provides flexible financing options for students pursuing career-focused education and training programs. It partners with educational institutions to offer loans and payment plans, aiming to make upskilling and credential programs more affordable and accessible. The platform offers an online portal for applications, loan management, and resources about financing education, targeting adult learners and professionals seeking new career paths.
c.name: Climbcredit

c.description: Climeworks AG is a Swiss carbon dioxide removal company founded in 2009 as an ETH Zurich spin-off by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher. It designs, builds and operates direct air capture (DAC) plants that filter CO2 out of ambient air through an adsorption-desorption cycle and then permanently mineralize it underground with storage partners such as Carbfix in Iceland - the Orca and Mammoth facilities. Through Climeworks Solutions it also sells risk-mitigated carbon removal portfolios that blend its own DAC removals with certified third-party suppliers, delivered within seven years of purchase and tracked by corporate buyers in an online customer platform. Climeworks is a supplier of carbon removal rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its removals reach programmatic buyers through third-party carbon marketplaces instead.
c.name: Climeworks

c.description: Clinbrain is a company identified in the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. After searching major public sources (Crunchbase, PitchBook, DuckDuckGo) no official corporate website could be located, indicating the company may not maintain a public web presence or it is not indexed. The entry remains a stub for further profiling as more information becomes available.
c.name: Clinbrain

c.description: Clinc is a conversational AI platform for banking and financial services, founded in 2015 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. It provides the Natural Language Understanding (NLU), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Natural Language Generation (NLG) engine behind virtual assistants and chatbots, and is ASR/TTS-agnostic so it can be connected to phone, mobile, web, or smart-speaker devices. Once a user utterance is converted to text, Clinc's AI engine interprets intent and calls the appropriate third-party systems (such as an external database) to answer or carry out an action. Clinc has been deployed with customers including USAA, Ford, Barclays, and İşbank, and is backed by Insight Partners, Drive Capital, and eLab Ventures. NOTE — Clinc's public developer surface (clinc.com and api.clinc.com) is offline as of 2026-07-18: the clinc.com AWS Route53 delegation is dangling and its authoritative nameservers return REFUSED, so the domain resolves SERVFAIL everywhere. The documentation and API URLs recorded here are the genuine published locations, recoverable via the Internet Archive.
c.name: Clinc

c.description: Clinc2 is a nascent technology company focused on developing advanced conversational AI platforms for healthcare and finance sectors. Founded in 2022, the firm aims to integrate natural language understanding with secure data handling to enable seamless patient‑clinician interactions and compliant financial advisory services. While still early in its product rollout, Clinc2 emphasizes privacy‑by‑design, leveraging on‑premise deployment options and robust API ecosystems to serve enterprise clients seeking AI‑driven conversational solutions.
c.name: Clinc2

c.description: Clinch is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clinch

c.description: Cline (formerly Claude Dev) is an open-source autonomous coding agent. The Cline VS Code extension has 5M+ installs; JetBrains is in early access; the Cline CLI is also available. Edits files, runs commands, uses the browser, and federates to multiple LLM providers. An MCP Marketplace extends Cline with custom tools. There is also a hosted/managed offering (Cline.bot) with free and paid tiers plus enterprise sales.
c.name: Cline

c.description: Clinflash (易迪希医药科技 / Clinflash Healthcare Technology) is a Chinese clinical-research technology company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud-based clinical trial information platform for pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and research sites. Its self-developed suite spans more than ten systems, including Clinflash EDC (electronic data capture), IRT/IWRS (randomization and trial supply management), eCOA/ePRO (electronic clinical outcome and patient-reported outcomes), Safety/PV (pharmacovigilance and drug-safety alerting), CTMS (clinical trial management), eTMF (electronic trial master file), eCTD, eConsent, eSign, Coder (medical coding), and ePAY (subject payment). Clinflash has supported thousands of clinical trial projects for over a thousand pharmaceutical, generic, medical-device, and IVD organizations, including pivotal Phase III and international multi-center studies. The platform is delivered as a login-gated SaaS at cloud.clinflash.com and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer/API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization.
c.name: Clinflash

c.description: Clingsystems (Cling Systems AB) brokers surplus and end‑of‑life batteries, helping owners sell them to buyers while handling compliance, waste classification and cross‑border shipping. Their mission is to accelerate circular battery value chains, offering a marketplace, inventory visibility and transparent pricing to unlock value that would otherwise be lost.
c.name: Clingsystems

c.description: ClinicalAuditAI provides an API that automates the generation of clinical audit reports for CROs, sponsors, hospitals and quality assurance teams. Using a provisioned X‑API‑Key, clients can submit source data, receive structured audit results, PDF reports, and webhook notifications. The service aims to reduce audit preparation time, improve compliance scoring, and streamline inspection readiness across the healthcare research lifecycle.
c.name: ClinicalAuditAI

c.description: ClinicalTrials.gov is the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) registry and results database of publicly and privately supported clinical studies of human participants conducted around the world. Operated by the National Library of Medicine (NLM), it provides a modern REST API (data-api v2) that returns study records, study metadata, search areas, and field definitions in JSON. The predecessor classic API remains available for legacy consumers but is being phased out in favor of the v2 API. Data is in the public domain and freely accessible without authentication.
c.name: ClinicalTrials.gov

c.description: Clínica SiM is a Brazilian health services provider offering in‑person and tele‑medicine consultations, diagnostic exams, dental care and subscription‑based health plans across Fortaleza, Recife and Salvador. Patients can book appointments online, access medical records, and receive virtual urgent care through its web portal and mobile apps.
c.name: Clinicasim

c.description: Clinikk (Clinikk Health Hub) is a Bangalore, India-based primary healthcare provider offering membership-based access to unlimited doctor consultations, free prescribed medicines and lab tests, 24/7 teleconsultation, and optional group health insurance in partnership with IndusInd General Insurance. Clinikk operates in-person Health Hubs across Bangalore alongside a consumer mobile app, and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.
c.name: Clinikk

c.description: Cliniko is practice management software for allied health practices and clinics - physiotherapy, osteopathy, chiropractic, podiatry, psychology, massage, and similar - covering patient records, appointment scheduling and online bookings, practitioners and businesses (locations), treatment notes, invoicing, and payments. Cliniko exposes a well-documented public REST API over HTTPS. The API is region-sharded - the base host is derived from the shard suffix on your API key (for example `https://api.au1.cliniko.com/v1/`) - and is authenticated with an API key passed as the username in HTTP Basic authentication. Every request must also send a `User-Agent` header containing an app/vendor name and a valid contact email, or requests may be blocked.
c.name: Cliniko

c.description: Clinkle was a Silicon Valley mobile-payments startup founded in 2012 by Stanford student Lucas Duplan. In 2013 it raised roughly $30 million in what was then reported as the largest seed round in history, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Peter Thiel, Marc Benioff, Accel's Jim Breyer, Richard Branson, and Intel Capital. The company promised a phone-to-phone payments technology but never shipped a viable product, launched a poorly received "Treats" debit-card app, cycled through multiple pivots and leadership turmoil, and lost its window to Venmo and Apple Pay. By 2016 Clinkle had quietly shut down with no official announcement. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead; it publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface today (clinkle.com resolves to a suspended-account page).
c.name: Clinkle

c.description: Clinomic provides data intelligence and network medicine solutions for critical care, offering platforms such as Mona PDMS, Mona OS, and cloud services to streamline patient management, interoperability, and analytics in intensive care settings. Their suite includes teleICU, webICU, and AI tool integration, aiming to improve clinical outcomes through standardized, automated data workflows.
c.name: Clinomic

c.description: Clinova is a healthcare technology company focused on delivering innovative digital solutions for clinical data management and patient engagement. The firm provides a platform that integrates electronic health records, telemedicine services, and analytics tools to improve care coordination and outcomes. Founded to address gaps in interoperability, Clinova aims to streamline workflows for providers and empower patients with secure access to their health information.
c.name: Clinova

c.description: Clinovas LTD (Clinova, clinova.ai) is an AI-powered patient recruitment platform for clinical trials. Per the company's own site, it matches eligible patients to trials in minutes rather than months using AI-powered patient matching against hospital electronic health records (EHR). The solution is hospital-based and HIPAA-compliant, targeting clinical research organizations and trial sponsors operating in emerging markets including Eastern Europe and the CIS region. Backed by 500 Global. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found at the time of enrichment.
c.name: Clinovas

c.description: Clio is a cloud-based legal practice management platform used by law firms for matter management, contacts, calendaring, time and billing, trust accounting, document management, tasks, and client communications. The Clio Manage API is a REST/JSON API at app.clio.com/api/v4 that uses OAuth 2.0 (authorization code flow) for authentication and exposes the full data model behind Clio Manage, with regional endpoints for the U.S., Canada, EU/UK, and Australia. Webhooks deliver near real-time event notifications, and the Clio App Directory hosts certified third-party integrations.
c.name: Clio

c.description: Clip (legal name Payclip) is a Mexico City-based fintech and SMB acquirer often described as the Square equivalent in Mexico. Founded in 2012, Clip enables merchants of all sizes to accept card, contactless, and QR payments through a family of mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) terminals — Clip Plus 2, Clip Pro 2, Clip Ultra, Clip Total 3, and the high-volume Clip PinPad — as well as Tap to Pay on iOS/Android smartphones, an online Checkout payment gateway, payment links, and the Clip Cuenta digital business account with same-day settlement and SMB loans. Clip operates the developer portal developer.clip.mx, which publishes the Checkout Redirect, Checkout Transparente, Transactions, Deposits, Refunds, and PinPad APIs along with the Checkout Transparente SDK and a Terminal SDK for embedding card acceptance into third-party POS apps. The company is backed by strategic investors including American Express Ventures, Banorte, Capital Group, and Morgan Stanley, and is consistently ranked among Mexico's top private fintech employers.
c.name: Clip

c.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.
c.name: Clipboard Health

c.description: ClipLine株式会社は、サービス業向けの動画ベースのマネジメントプラットフォームを提供する日本の企業です。2013年に旧社名株式会社ジェネックスソリューションズとして設立され、組織の業務効率化やナレッジ共有を支援するツール「ClipLine」を展開しています。ミッションは『できる』をふやすであり、動画を活用した研修・フィードバックシステムを通じて多店舗展開企業の生産性向上を支援しています。
c.name: ClipLine

c.description: ClippPR (later rebranded Primeloop) was a startup that helped brands and PR agencies clip and track their press coverage, measure the value of earned media, and re-engage audiences by turning clicks on shared links into targeted relationships. Founded around 2011 in Las Vegas and part of 500 Startups' eighth (first San Francisco) accelerator batch, the company has since shut down. Its primeloop.com domain is parked/for-sale, primeloop.co no longer resolves, and clipppr.com has been taken over by an unrelated blog. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI was ever published; the only surviving first-party surface is the company's GitHub organization.
c.name: ClippPR

c.description: Clipto.AI provides a local-first AI-powered platform that transcribes, searches, and organizes audio, video, and document media. Users can upload or sync their media files, and Clipto uses advanced machine learning to generate searchable transcripts, summaries, and insights, enabling quick retrieval and knowledge extraction. The service offers desktop applications for macOS and Windows, mobile apps, and integrations with popular tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and video editing software. Clipto emphasizes privacy by keeping data local unless cloud features are enabled, and targets professionals, creators, and enterprises needing efficient media management.
c.name: Clipto.AI

c.description: Cliq Products is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Cliq Products

c.description: CliQr Technologies was a San Jose, California cloud management software company, backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Google Capital, that built the CloudCenter platform for application-defined hybrid cloud orchestration. Its single application profile let enterprises model, deploy, and manage workloads across bare-metal, virtualized, and container environments and across public clouds (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, IBM SoftLayer, Rackspace) and private clouds (OpenStack, CloudStack, VMware vCloud). Cisco announced its intent to acquire CliQr for $260 million in March 2016 and folded the product into Cisco CloudCenter as part of its hybrid cloud strategy; CliQr no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no active developer surface, API, or documentation.
c.name: CliQr Technologies *

c.description: Clis6797 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Clis6797

c.description: Clivi is Mexico's largest digital clinic for diabetes and obesity care, delivering fully online telehealth treatment that combines endocrinologists, internists, nutritionists, and psychologists with continuous glucose monitoring and GLP-1 medications (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Saxenda, Rybelsus). Founded in 2020 and based in Mexico City, Clivi serves patients nationwide through WhatsApp-based virtual care, home medication delivery via its Farmacia Clivi digital pharmacy, and tiered treatment plans (Clivi Pro, Plus, Total, and Zero). Backed by 500 Global and other investors, Clivi operates as a consumer healthtech service; it publishes no public developer API, but does expose an llms.txt content index for AI agents.
c.name: Clivi

c.description: Clix is a US-based, developer-first mobile push notification platform for iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter — one CLI command (clix install) automates Firebase Cloud Messaging and APNs setup, and the console adds behaviour-triggered and API-triggered campaigns, real-time delivery logs, full-funnel analytics and device/user lifecycle management, priced free to 100K active devices then $30/month. For developers and agents it publishes a small REST API at https://api.clix.so (OpenAPI 3.1.0 generated from clix/external/v1/clix.proto: 11 operations across users, devices, events, messages:send, live-activities:start and campaigns/{id}:trigger, authenticated with X-Clix-Project-ID + X-Clix-API-Key), an A2A agent at https://api.clix.so/a2a whose card at /.well-known/agent-card.json is served in both 0.3.0 and 1.0 shapes and exposes four skills (create-user, track-event, send-push-notification, trigger-campaign) with idempotency keys, SSE streaming, task cancellation and task webhooks, a stdio MCP server (@clix-so/clix-mcp-server) plus a Mintlify docs MCP endpoint — both documentation-only — an open agent-skills repo, first-party SDKs on Maven Central, CocoaPods/SwiftPM, pub.dev and npm, a self-hosted status page with a published 99.5% monthly SLO, and console-configured PUSH_SENT/PUSH_FAILED webhooks.
c.name: Clix

c.description: Cloaked is a consumer privacy and identity-protection platform that lets people create unlimited unique identities to shield their real personal data. Each identity bundles a masked email address, a virtual phone number, an auto-generated password, and virtual payment cards so users can sign up for services without handing over their real contact information. The platform adds a built-in password manager, AI-powered spam call screening (Call Guard), dark web and SSN monitoring, automated data-broker removal across 120+ sites, and up to $1M in identity theft insurance. Cloaked emphasizes a zero-knowledge architecture with end-to-end encryption and is SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and PCI DSS compliant. Backed by General Catalyst, Cloaked ships consumer apps (iOS, Android, web, browser extension) and a Cloaked Enterprise offering for businesses; it is a consumer-facing product with no publicly documented developer API at this time.
c.name: Cloaked

c.description: Clockify is a time tracking and timesheet platform used by teams to track work hours across projects with a timer, manual timesheets, kiosk check-in, scheduling, expense tracking, invoicing, and reporting. The Clockify REST API exposes workspaces, users, projects, tasks, tags, clients, time entries, reports, and webhooks, and authenticates with an X-Api-Key header.
c.name: Clockify

c.description: Clockodo is a German-built, cloud-based time-tracking and project- management application used by service firms, agencies, and freelancers. In addition to its web and mobile apps, Clockodo exposes a REST API at my.clockodo.com that mirrors the objects in the UI: time entries, customers, projects, services, users, absences, holiday quotas, lump-sum services, and a real-time stop-clock. Authentication uses a per-user email plus per-user API key delivered as the X-ClockodoApiUser/X-ClockodoApiKey header pair (or HTTP Basic), and every call must include the X-Clockodo-External-Application header identifying the integrating application.
c.name: Clockodo

c.description: Clockspring is a technology company specializing in precision timing components and synchronization solutions for industrial automation, robotics, and consumer electronics. Founded to address the growing demand for reliable, high-performance clock mechanisms, Clockspring offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate real-time timing data, device health monitoring, and predictive maintenance capabilities into their applications. The company emphasizes robust security, extensive documentation, and developer-friendly tools to accelerate integration and foster innovation across sectors.
c.name: Clockspring

c.description: Clockster is a frontline staff-management super-app for food & beverage and retail businesses, consolidating attendance and time tracking, shift scheduling, automated payroll, earned wage access, business communication, tasks and checklists into a single mobile-first platform. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore with offices across Kazakhstan and Indonesia, Clockster serves more than 1,300 SMEs across Central and Southeast Asia — including brands such as KFC, Hardee's and Costa Coffee — and is backed by 500 Global, I2BF Global Ventures and Quest Ventures. It is delivered as iOS, Android and Huawei mobile apps plus a web console and currently exposes no public developer API surface.
c.name: Clockster

c.description: Clockwise was an AI-powered calendar optimization platform that helped individuals, teams, and organizations protect focus time, reduce meeting overload, and coordinate scheduling intelligently. The platform provided REST APIs for managing focus time blocks, meeting preferences, smart scheduling links, and team calendar coordination. Clockwise was acquired by Salesforce and shut down on March 27, 2026.
c.name: Clockwise

c.description: Clockwork Labs is a San Francisco software company (founded 2019) that builds SpacetimeDB, a relational database that is also an application server: developers upload their schema and server-side business logic as a WebAssembly "module" (written in Rust, C#, TypeScript, or C++) directly into the database, and clients connect over WebSocket to invoke reducers and subscribe to real-time state updates with no separate application server in between. SpacetimeDB exposes a versioned HTTP API (/v1/database and /v1/identity) for publishing modules, invoking reducers, running SQL, streaming subscriptions, and managing identities and JWT tokens, plus a first-party `spacetime` CLI and client SDKs for TypeScript, C#/Unity, Rust, Python, and C++. It is the production backend of BitCraft, the company's MMO. Clockwork Labs is backed by a16z, Supercell, Firstminute Capital, Skycatcher, 1Up Ventures, and Supernode.
c.name: Clockwork Labs

c.description: Clockworks Analytics is a Boston-area building-analytics company whose cloud platform performs automated fault detection and diagnostics (FDD) on HVAC and building systems. It ingests interval data from Building Management Systems through the Clockworks Connect gateway, runs a curated library of root-cause diagnostics, and quantifies each performance issue by avoidable energy cost plus energy, comfort and maintenance priority on a 0-10 scale. Its public REST API is delivered through Azure API Management on rest.buildingsapi.net as four containers — core-base (clients, buildings, equipment, points, users), core-diag (diagnostic records), core-kpis (KQL-driven aggregated datasets) and workorders (Tasks / CMMS work-order sync) — and is documented publicly at cw.clockworksanalytics.com plus a public Confluence developer guide set for CMMS and KPI integration.
c.name: Clockworks Analytics

c.description: Clojars is a community repository for open source Clojure libraries, providing a REST API for searching artifacts, retrieving version information, accessing user and group data, and managing deployment credentials via deploy tokens.
c.name: Clojars

c.description: Clone Robotics develops musculoskeletal, intelligent humanoid androids and robotic hands built on Myofiber, its artificial-muscle technology pioneered in 2021, driven by water-based hydraulics and biomimetic joints. Its flagship Clone Alpha is a full-body biomimetic humanoid with synthetic organs; the Clone Hand is its foundational dexterous-manipulation platform. The developer surface is a first-party Python client (clone_client) exposing a high-level gRPC (proto3) API to directly control the Clone Robot over the local network — actuating muscles via impulses/pulses/pressures, driving pinch and hydra valves, managing the water-pump pressure source, streaming IMU/pose/joint telemetry, and configuring cameras. There is no public HTTP/REST API or hosted endpoint; control is LAN-scoped gRPC discovered over zeroconf/mDNS by robot name or IP. Co-founded 2021 by Dhanush Radhakrishna and Lukasz Kozlik.
c.name: Clone

c.description: Cloocus is a global cloud management services provider headquartered in Seoul, South Korea. It is a Microsoft Azure Expert MSP offering consulting, migration, managed services, data innovation, AI business solutions, and multi‑cloud operations across Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and Naver Cloud. Founded in 2019, Cloocus serves enterprises with cloud strategy, implementation, and ongoing optimization.
c.name: Cloocus

c.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.
c.name: Cloover

c.description: cloro is one API for Google Search and AI answer engines: a REST surface at api.cloro.dev that submits a prompt to ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Grok, Google AI Mode, Google Search, Google AI Overview and Google News from a chosen country (and US state) and returns the engine's answer as structured JSON with parsed text, markdown, cited sources, brand entities, shopping cards and ads. Sync monitor endpoints answer in-line; async tasks and batches of up to 500 run in the background with polling or signed webhooks. Credit-based subscription billing, a free tier of 500 monthly credits, a hosted MCP server at mcp.cloro.dev with OAuth, official Python and TypeScript SDKs, n8n, Zapier and LangChain integrations.
c.name: cloro

c.description: Close is an inside-sales CRM with calling, email, SMS, and WhatsApp built in. The Close API exposes leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, activities (calls, emails, SMS, meetings, notes), pipelines, custom objects, sequences, smart views, scheduling, phone numbers, reporting, and webhooks for sales automation.
c.name: Close

c.description: Close Brothers Group plc (LSE: CBG) is a UK merchant banking group founded in 1878 and a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index, headquartered at 10 Crown Place, London EC2A 4FT. The group provides specialist lending across motor, premium, asset, invoice, and property finance; takes personal and business deposits through Close Brothers Savings; manages wealth through Close Brothers Asset Management; and trades securities through Winterflood. Its banking entity, Close Brothers Limited, is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA. Close Brothers is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks; it offers savings and deposit products rather than online payment (current) accounts, and therefore carries no UK Open Banking (OBIE / PSD2) Read/Write or Open Data publishing obligation. As of this profile no public developer portal, Open Banking Open Data endpoint, or documented API surface could be confirmed for the group.
c.name: Close Brothers

c.description: Product-intelligence platform that turns customer conversations and feedback (Gong, Fireflies, Slack, Zendesk, Intercom, Salesforce, HubSpot, surveys, product usage; 40+ integrations) into structured, source-traceable product insights, themes, buildable features, and prioritized roadmap decisions.
