c.description: Connective Health provides real-time, complete patient records using AI to analyze data and create concise, source‑backed summaries. Their platform helps providers, ACOs, and health plans improve outcomes, reduce costs, and meet value‑based care requirements. Founded in 2021, the Boston‑based company offers risk‑adjustment scores, clinical quality measurement, and secure data interoperability.
c.name: Connective Health

c.description: The Connectivity Standards Alliance (CSA) is a global industry consortium that develops and promotes open standards for the Internet of Things (IoT). It oversees the Matter, Zigbee, and Aliro specifications, providing certification programs, testing tools, and resources for manufacturers and developers to ensure interoperable, secure IoT products. CSA engages members worldwide through events, developer resources, and a community portal.
c.name: Connectivity Standards Alliance

c.description: Connectly is an AI-native platform delivering intelligent agents that sell, serve, and engage customers across industries such as retail, healthcare, financial services, telecommunications, utilities, and education. Backed by Unusual Ventures, Alibaba, and Volpe Capital, Connectly provides AI agents for large enterprises in the US, Latin America, and the Middle East, offering features like product recommendation, order handling, prescription processing, and compliance support, all ISO‑27001 certified and GDPR compliant.
c.name: Connectly

c.description: connectRN is a Waltham, Massachusetts based per-diem (PRN) healthcare staffing marketplace that connects nurses, CNAs and allied clinicians with open shifts at hospitals, home health and hospice agencies, and skilled nursing facilities across the United States. Clinicians browse and claim shifts through the connectRN mobile app with no minimum commitment, no required weekends or holidays, and same-day pay; facilities post shifts, auto-backfill open coverage and approve timesheets through a web platform at app.connectrn.com. In April 2026 connectRN merged with SnapCare, combining connectRN's PRN clinician community with SnapCare's Booker workforce technology platform. connectRN operates a public status page but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its API host api.connectrn.com serves the first-party mobile and web applications only.
c.name: ConnectRN

c.description: Connells Limited, trading as Connells Group, is the United Kingdom's largest estate agency and property services group, headquartered at Cumbria House in Leighton Buzzard, Bedfordshire, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Skipton Building Society. It states 1,200+ branches, 16,000+ colleagues, more than 80 local brands including Connells, Countrywide, Hamptons, Sequence, Bairstow Eves, Fox & Sons, John D Wood & Co, Gascoigne Halman and Blundells, roughly 115,000 property sales a year and about 10% market share, 165,000+ managed tenancies and £33bn+ of arranged mortgage lending. It occupies almost the entire residential value chain at once: estate agency, residential and corporate lettings, new homes, land and planning, auctions, surveys and valuations, conveyancing, mortgage services, asset management, affordable housing, EPCs and inventories, commercial agency and a research and consultancy practice. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla portal duopoly by way of agency CRM and website software rather than a shared pool, and Connells' own consumer property sites are built on the Homeflow platform. Its API posture is closed and undocumented. No developer portal exists: developer., developers., api. and docs.connellsgroup.co.uk do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/openid-configuration return 404 on both connellsgroup.co.uk and connells.co.uk. It publishes no OpenAPI, no GraphQL, no AsyncAPI, no MCP server and no client SDK — the only first-party package on any public registry is a dormant npm colour-token file for its website. Probing on 2026-07-26 did, however, find a small live JSON surface underneath the consumer site at https://www.connells.co.uk/api: six anonymous read-only Next.js route handlers serving the branch finder, people directory, testimonials wall and place autocomplete, plus a seventh (/api/properties) that returns HTTP 500. These are undocumented internal website routes, not a product — unversioned, unsupported, rate limited by Cloudflare, capped at 12 records because no paging parameter works, and carrying application errors inside HTTP 200 bodies. Only connells.co.uk exposes them; the sibling brand sites redirect /api/* away. The group's 88-URL corporate sitemap contains no developer path — its one /developers/ page is addressed to property developers, not software developers. Integration is real but partner-only: Connells Survey & Valuation advertises delivering "totally integrated panel and risk management technology solutions to lenders" for the 40+ lenders whose valuation panels it manages, and reaches them through third-party platforms such as Cotality's LenderHub, while Countrywide Surveying Services' Geoconnect engine is described as connecting internal and external data sources through API integrations it consumes rather than publishes. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the estate — RESO is a North American NAR/MLS mechanism and the UK has no MLS to certify against. Connells publishes no open data either; its research product, covering 88% of UK postcode areas from branch-level proprietary data, is sold through a brochure request and a contact form, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector (HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey), not to the brokerage.
c.name: Connells Group

c.description: Connexion is an open source Python framework that automatically handles HTTP requests based on OpenAPI specifications. Connexion 3 provides AsyncApp, FlaskApp, and ConnexionMiddleware as primary entry points, with built-in routing, request and response validation, parameter parsing, security enforcement, content negotiation, error handling, lifespan, and Swagger UI integration. Connexion takes a contract-first, design-first approach: the OpenAPI specification is the source of truth and Python handlers are resolved from operationId or via configurable resolvers.
c.name: Connexion

c.description: Connexis Cash is BNP Paribas's corporate digital banking and cash management platform. It gives multinational corporates a unified online channel for payment initiation, real-time payment tracking, account reporting, reconciliation, and liquidity management across BNP Paribas's global network. Connexis Cash also exposes PSD2-compliant Open Banking APIs through the BNP Paribas CIB developer portal so that third-party providers (TPPs) can retrieve account information and initiate payments on behalf of Connexis Cash users, as well as a Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) flow.
c.name: Connexis Cash

c.description: ConnexPay is a Milwaukee-founded B2B payments platform that combines merchant acquiring and card issuing in one integration, so a company's incoming customer payments directly fund its outgoing supplier payments with no float in between. An inbound Sale (PayIn) returns an Incoming Transaction Code that funds the virtual cards, ACH credits, push-to-card payouts, checks and international bank-to-bank transfers issued against it (PayOuts). The platform is used heavily in leisure and business travel, advertising and media buying, insurance claims, and embedded-payments software, and is delivered through ten REST APIs — Sales, Purchases, Push to Card, Payment Valet payment instructions, Checkout Session, Merchant Payor, Stop Payment, Chargebacks (CMS), and two Reporting surfaces — plus a browser payments SDK, a Hosted Payment Page, the Bridge operator console, and a 51-event webhook surface called CXP Eventing. ConnexPay is a registered ISO/MSP of The Central Trust Bank and MVB Bank.
c.name: ConnexPay

c.description: Connexus, Inc. is a non‑profit licensed supported living agency based in Tennessee. It provides community‑based and family‑based services for children and adults with physical, mental, and developmental disabilities, including residential care, personal assistance, supported employment, and vocational rehabilitation. The organization focuses on nurturing, teaching, and strengthening individuals and families with respect and professionalism, aiming to help them reach their full potential.
c.name: Connexus

c.description: Conniehealth is a Medicare advisory service that helps individuals find and enroll in Medicare plans. It offers personalized assistance through licensed agents, provides educational resources, and maintains a blog with guides on enrollment periods, plan options, and costs. The company operates a consumer‑focused website offering tools to compare plans, locate local agents, and access FAQs, aiming to simplify Medicare decision‑making for seniors across the United States.
c.name: Conniehealth

c.description: CONNSKILL GmbH & Co. KG is a web design, branding and marketing agency in Traunstein, Germany (HRA 14164, Amtsgericht Traunstein) that also builds and operates CONNSKILL Growth Services at agent.connskill.com — a pay-per-call marketplace for AI agents. It sells Google SERP and keyword research data, site audits, backlinks and competitor intelligence, SMS verification numbers and US number rentals, receive-only e-mail inboxes, social marketing orders, OpenAI-compatible LLM chat and embeddings hosted in Germany, x402 seller trust checks, leak exposure and domain security grades, read-only EVM chain data and cookieless website analytics, plus a free marketplace layer (wishlist, job board, curated x402 directory, published conformance reports). Every call is priced individually and paid in USDC on Base via x402 with no account or API key. The surface is published as OpenAPI 3.1, an A2A agent card, a hosted MCP endpoint and an npm MCP server, llms.txt, ai-plugin.json and an x402 discovery document.
c.name: CONNSKILL

c.description: Conntour is an Israeli AI video-intelligence company building a natural-language search engine for security camera systems. Its vision and language models let operators search any camera feed in plain language to find any object, person, or situation in real time, raise automatic alerts, and investigate recorded footage in seconds — turning passive surveillance into active intelligence. Unlike legacy analytics that depend on preset object or motion definitions, Conntour's models scale to thousands of concurrent feeds (up to roughly 50 feeds per consumer GPU such as an Nvidia RTX 4090) and deploy fully on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid mix, either augmenting existing VMS/security systems or serving as a standalone surveillance platform. Founded in 2024 by Matan Goldner and Tomer Kola, the company serves intelligence agencies, homeland security, law enforcement, military and defense, transportation, and enterprise customers. It raised a $7M seed round in March 2026 led by General Catalyst, with participation from Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Liquid 2 Ventures.
c.name: Conntour

c.description: ConocoPhillips is a leading global exploration and production company, headquartered in Houston, Texas, that is uniquely equipped to deliver reliable, responsibly produced oil and natural gas. The company operates in more than a dozen countries with conventional and unconventional crude oil, natural gas, LNG, and natural gas liquids assets. ConocoPhillips does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations portal, a vendor relations portal (powered by third-party platforms such as GEP and Taulia), an LNG technology and licensing program, and a custom sustainability report builder.
c.name: ConocoPhillips

c.description: Conquestplanning provides AI‑driven financial planning software for wealth firms, advisors, and institutions. Their Strategic Advice Manager (SAM) engine delivers verifiable, personalized advice at scale, integrating behavioral finance agents and compliance tools. The platform supports multi‑language locales, offers a pricing page, resources, and a developer portal for API access, aiming to modernize financial planning with transparent, auditable recommendations.
c.name: Conquestplanning

c.description: conrizon AG is a German holding company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in Essen, that unites four of Europe's leading Enterprise Content Management (ECM) brands - easy software, PROXESS, HABEL, and Portal Systems (Shareflex), alongside the friendWorks professional-services unit - under one roof. The group provides legally compliant, audit-proof digital archiving (GDPR, GoBD, eIDAS), document management (DMS), invoice and procure-to-pay (P2P) processing, contract management, and HR/HCM software with automated workflows, plus AI services and connectors for SAP and Microsoft 365 / SharePoint. Solutions are offered cloud-native, in a private cloud, on-premises, or hybrid, and are relied on by more than 8,700 companies and organizations worldwide. conrizon is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API or developer portal.
c.name: conrizon

c.description: Consensus is the distributed systems problem of getting a set of unreliable processes to agree on a value or sequence of values. Consensus algorithms power state-machine replication for databases, key-value stores, configuration systems, and blockchains. The consensus topic spans classical crash-fault tolerant algorithms (Paxos, Raft, Multi-Paxos, Zab, Viewstamped Replication) and Byzantine fault tolerant algorithms (PBFT, Tendermint, HotStuff, Casper FFG/CBC), and the impossibility result FLP that bounds what is possible in fully asynchronous models.
c.name: Consensus

c.description: Consensussystems is a company identified through the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market). It currently lacks a publicly accessible website or documented API endpoints. No concrete product or service information is available, and attempts to locate an official domain resulted in inaccessible or non-existent sites. This stub remains for future enrichment as more information becomes available.
c.name: Consensussystems

c.description: Consensys is a blockchain and Web3 software company founded by Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin that builds core Ethereum infrastructure and developer tooling for the decentralized web. Its product suite includes MetaMask (the self-custodial wallet and MetaMask Developer / Connect SDK), Infura (managed, high-availability JSON-RPC blockchain node APIs, IPFS, and a Gas API across Ethereum and 40+ EVM networks), Linea (a zkEVM Layer 2 network), Besu and Teku (execution and consensus clients), and Diligence/MythX smart-contract security tooling. Developers use Infura's API-key-authenticated JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoints to read and broadcast to Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Linea and more without operating their own nodes.
c.name: Consensys

c.description: ConsentX provides a consent management platform (CMP) that helps websites comply with privacy regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, DPDPA, LGPD, and others. It offers cookie consent banners, prior‑script blocking, consent records, audit evidence, region‑rule engine, and integrations with Google Consent Mode, Global Privacy Control, and AI‑driven privacy scanning. The platform includes tools for data residency, DSAR handling, and a suite of compliance features across multiple jurisdictions.
c.name: ConsentX

c.description: Conservation Labs is a Pittsburgh-based smart water technology company, backed by Techstars, Amazon, RET Ventures and SustainVC. Its flagship product, H2know, is a clamp-on acoustic smart water monitor that measures a building's inbound pipe every second and uses patented sound-detection technology and machine learning to translate those signals into accurate water-flow estimates, leak alerts and water-usage insights delivered through a companion mobile and web app. The company also offers Sustainable Machines, an edge-to-cloud platform for machine condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Conservation Labs serves residential homes, commercial real estate, restaurants and hotels, and industrial operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a consumer-facing app but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook documentation.
c.name: Conservation Labs

c.description: Consip Open Data is a government agency open-data portal for Italy running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 16 datasets.

c.description: CONSOL Energy was a Pittsburgh-based bituminous coal producer serving electric utilities, steelmakers and industrial customers. In January 2025 it merged with Arch Resources to form Core Natural Resources, Inc. (NYSE: CNR), and consolenergy.com now 301-redirects to corenaturalresources.com. The company publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no GitHub organization — but it runs its corporate site on WordPress and serves the WordPress REST API anonymously at https://corenaturalresources.com/wp-json/, a real machine-readable read surface with custom post types for mines (11, with an East/West taxonomy), leadership (16) and news releases (40), plus pages and a 173-item media library holding the supplier terms, Supplier Code of Conduct and sustainability PDFs. Each endpoint was called anonymously on 2026-09-05; writes and admin routes are authenticated (401). Financial data stays third-party, via the SEC EDGAR APIs. See arch-coal for the other merger half.
c.name: CONSOL Energy

c.description: Consola Finance is an enterprise-grade automated crypto accounting and finance platform for digital assets, acquired by and now operating as part of Request Finance. It lets finance and accounting teams monitor wallets across 25+ blockchains and 20+ exchanges (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, KuCoin and others), automate bookkeeping, categorize and label on-chain transactions, filter spam, and generate audit-ready reports — transaction history, historical wallet balances, team breakdowns, contact lists, and realized / unrealized gains and losses — exported to CSV, XLSX and JSON, with integrations into existing ERP and accounting systems. As part of Request Finance it shares the Request Finance REST API for accounts payable / receivable, invoicing and payroll, authenticated with API keys or OAuth over JSON/HTTPS.
c.name: Consola Finance

c.description: Console Group is an Australian property management software company, founded in 1992 in Brisbane, Queensland, that built the first property management and trust accounting software released in Australia and launched its cloud platform, Console Cloud, in 2017. It serves thousands of residential and commercial property management agencies across Australia and New Zealand with trust accounting, tenancy and lease management, inspections (Console Go + Inspect), maintenance, arrears, owner and tenant portals, SMS, analytics and payments (Console Pay). The company was acquired by the United Kingdom's Reapit and its flagship product has been rebranded Reapit PM, though the business continues to trade from console.com.au. In the Australian value chain Console Group sits on the property MANAGEMENT side rather than the sales-listing side, as the system of record for the rent roll, the trust account and the tenancy, downstream of REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain and separate from PEXA's conveyancing rail and from PropTrack and CoreLogic valuation data. Its API posture is honestly closed. Console Group publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or Swagger document and no partner developer program on console.com.au; the full sitemap contains no /developers, /api or /docs page, and the developer., developers. and docs. subdomains do not resolve. An api.console.com.au host answers as a Kong API Gateway but returns "no Route matched with those values" on every probed path, including GraphQL. A live integration marketplace at /integrate lists more than twenty two-way third-party products, so a working private integration API demonstrably exists, but access is by commercial marketplace arrangement only and nothing about it is published. The company does run a real public status page at status.console.com.au (Hund.io, Cloud and Accounts components, published uptime and response-time metrics), though its HAL+JSON status API is credential-gated. Australia has no MLS, so there is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in Console Group's stack, and the company publishes no open data.
c.name: Console Group

c.description: Consolidated Edison, Inc. (NYSE: ED) is a Fortune 500 utility holding company headquartered in New York City. It publishes no APIs of its own; it operates through its regulated subsidiaries, principally Consolidated Edison Company of New York (CECONY), which serves electric, gas and steam customers in New York City and Westchester County, and Orange and Rockland Utilities (O&R), along with Con Edison Transmission. The developer surface - Green Button Connect My Data (Share My Data) and Green Button Download My Data, both served from coned.com - belongs to CECONY and is profiled under the con-edison provider. This profile covers the holding company only.
c.name: Consolidated Edison

c.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.
c.name: Consona

c.description: Constancetherapeutics is a vertically integrated cannabis therapeutics company producing standardized, science‑based whole‑plant extracts. Since 2008 it has focused on quality, evidence‑based options and offers a range of CBD‑rich products through its online shop, serving thousands of customers and advancing insurance reimbursement initiatives for seniors.
c.name: Constancetherapeutics

c.description: Constanellis Aerospace is a cislunar infrastructure company developing manufacturing, qualification, cislunar awareness, and power provision and measurement. It provides systems, services, and commercial solutions for space missions, focusing on power, control, and production for demanding lunar and orbital operations.
c.name: Constanellisaerospace

c.description: Constant Contact is a small-business email and digital marketing platform offering email campaigns, automation, SMS, contact management, surveys, and events. The Constant Contact V3 API is a REST + JSON, OAuth2-protected service published at api.cc.email/v3 covering accounts, contacts, lists, tags, custom fields, segments, email campaigns, A/B tests, schedules and tests, bulk activities (CSV/JSON import, export, list and tag mutations), events with registration and check-in, reporting, and partner provisioning.
c.name: Constant Contact

c.description: Constantinople is a Sydney-based fintech providing an AI-native core-banking platform that lets banks run product, technology, data, operations, and compliance as a single modern fabric. It powers retail, business, and embedded banking across accounts, payments, cards, lending, mortgages, and term deposits, with headless APIs and SDKs, digital onboarding, an AI concierge for customers, and the "Justinian" AI workbench for bankers. Risk and compliance (fraud, financial-crime detection, regulatory reporting) are built into the platform, which is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. Constantinople is backed by Prosus Ventures (Series A, A$50M). The developer/API surface is a gated B2B platform; enrichment here is sourced from the company's public web presence.
c.name: Constantinople

c.description: Constella provides identity risk intelligence and dark web monitoring through high‑velocity APIs. It aggregates verified breach data, compromised credentials, and other identity signals from surface, deep, and dark web sources. The platform offers real‑time threat data via a secure API endpoint, enabling organizations to detect account takeover, session hijacking, ransomware precursors, and other identity‑based attacks. Constella serves enterprises, fintech, law‑enforcement, and security teams with curated, de‑duplicated data, extensive coverage of over 1 trillion records, and flexible integration options for risk modeling and investigative workflows.
c.name: Constellaintelligence

c.description: Constellation Brands is a Fortune 500 producer and marketer of beer, wine, and spirits brands such as Corona, Modelo, Robert Mondavi, and Casa Noble. Constellation publishes a partner-oriented API catalog at dev.cbrands.com that exposes product, brand, and digital-asset data (bottle shots, tasting notes, hot sheets, shelf talkers, neck hangers, recipes, and an items product API) to distributors, retailers, and on-premise partners. Most endpoints require an API key issued through the developer registration process.
c.name: Constellation Brands

c.description: Constellation Energy Corporation is a Fortune 500 clean-energy producer and competitive retail electricity and natural gas supplier in the United States, generating power from a fleet of nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar facilities. Constellation does not publish a public developer portal; programmatic interactions are delivered to enterprise and large commercial customers through the Energy Manager platform (account-managed onboarding, no public API specifications) and consumer interactions are handled through the My Constellation account portal. EDI 867 (usage) and 810 (invoice) remain the most common machine-to-machine integration paths and are arranged on a contract-by-contract basis.
c.name: Constellation Energy

c.description: Constellation Space Corp (ConstellationOS) is the ML-native operations platform for satellite fleets, founded in 2025 in Seattle and backed by Y Combinator. Operators connect ground telemetry through one API and one schema, run machine-learning link forecasts on live fleet context (SNR and link fade, traffic, weather, jamming, and conjunction), and act under operator policy with automated routing, stream isolation, and failover. The ConstellationOS HTTP API exposes fleet topology reads, telemetry ingestion, and predictions, secured with scoped bearer tokens, alongside a web console, a fleet agent CLI, and a public status page.
c.name: Constellation Space

c.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.
c.name: Constelli

c.description: Constrafor provides a construction‑focused platform that streamlines payments, risk management, and back‑office operations for general contractors and subcontractors. Their SaaS suite includes early‑pay financing, contract management, invoicing, and compliance tools, helping firms accelerate cash flow and reduce administrative overhead while ensuring regulatory adherence.
c.name: Constrafor

c.description: Constru (ConstruCompany) is a Brazilian construction firm delivering residential, commercial, shopping, hospital, and hotel projects. With over 1 million square meters built, they focus on quality, timely delivery, and client satisfaction, offering comprehensive services from design to post‑sale support.
c.name: Constru

c.description: Construction Monitor aggregates building-permit data from county and municipal sources nationwide and resells it as construction leads, contractor intelligence, and historical permit research. Programmatic access is offered through a REST + JSON API backed by Elasticsearch and a weekly data-dump option delivered over secure FTP. Both channels are account-managed; partners receive credentials and a documented endpoint contract directly from Construction Monitor.
c.name: Construction Monitor

c.description: ConstructionOnline is UDA Technologies' cloud construction project management platform covering estimating, scheduling, budgets, change orders, daily logs, file sharing, and client and subcontractor collaboration. UDA exposes the platform through a documented REST API available to ConstructionOnline Business and Enterprise customers, with read and write access for projects, contacts, schedules, and financials. Access is gated by an application process (api@uda1.com), authenticated with company-issued credentials, and rate-limited to 500 requests per hour per account.
c.name: ConstructionOnline

c.description: Constructor (Constructor.io) is an AI-powered ecommerce search and product discovery platform for online retailers. Its APIs cover autocomplete/autosuggest, keyword and natural-language search, image search, category browse, recommendations, quizzes, collections, offsite/email discovery, retail media (sponsored listings and display ads), an AI Shopping Agent and Product Insights Agent, plus a full catalog-management and configuration surface for items, variations, item groups, facets, searchabilities, synonyms, sort options, redirects and searchandising rules. Results are optimized against ecommerce KPIs (conversion, revenue per visit) using natural-language processing, behavioral re-ranking and per-user personalization, and are delivered through a REST API served from the ac.cnstrc.com family of hosts with first-party client libraries for JavaScript, Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Ruby, Swift and Kotlin.
c.name: Constructor.io

c.description: Consul Connect is the service mesh subsystem of HashiCorp Consul. Connect provides service identity, mTLS, traffic authorization via intentions, and L7 traffic management through Envoy sidecar proxies. Consul Connect ships with a built-in certificate authority that can also be backed by Vault or external PKI, supports mesh, terminating, ingress, and API gateways, and spans virtual machines, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, AWS Lambda, and Nomad runtimes. Operators interact with Connect through the consul CLI, the HTTP API, configuration entries, and Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions.
c.name: Consul Connect

c.description: The Consumer Data Right (CDR) is Australia's statutory consumer data-sharing regime, created under Part IVD of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 and extended from banking into electricity by the Consumer Data Right (Energy Sector) Designation 2020. It is run by three bodies: the ACCC as lead regulator and operator of the CDR Register, the OAIC as privacy regulator, and the Treasury Data Standards Body, which writes the binding Consumer Data Standards. In energy the regime obliges electricity retailers to expose plans, accounts, billing, invoices, payment schedules, concessions, service points, interval usage and DER data through one identical, versioned API contract, with AEMO acting as the Secondary Data Holder gateway for NMI standing data, metering data and the DER register. Unlike almost every other energy-sector data mandate, this one is verifiably implemented rather than merely announced: the public CDR Register listed 84 energy data holder brands with live public base URIs when probed on 2026-07-27, and 53 of those base URIs returned standards-conformant product data anonymously on the first request. Its API posture is a clean two-speed split — genuinely open, unauthenticated market data (retail plan and tariff reference data, plus the participant register itself) sitting alongside consumer data that is closed behind ACCC accreditation, mutual TLS, FAPI-grade OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect and explicit, revocable consumer consent. Home market Australia.
c.name: Consumer Data Right (Energy)

c.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) is the U.S. federal agency that supervises banks, lenders, and other financial companies, enforces federal consumer financial laws, and publishes large public datasets via open APIs. The CFPB Open Tech program publishes the Consumer Complaint Database (CCDB) search API and the HMDA Platform's Data Browser and Institutions APIs at ffiec.cfpb.gov, all unauthenticated and CC0-licensed for public use.
c.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

c.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) provides public REST APIs for searching consumer financial complaint data, accessing Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) mortgage lending records, and retrieving regulatory filing data. These APIs support financial researchers, journalists, developers, and the general public in understanding consumer financial markets and lending practices across the United States.
c.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)

c.description: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is the federal agency responsible for protecting the public from unreasonable risks of injury or death associated with consumer products such as toys, household items, electronics, and furniture. CPSC publishes a public, unauthenticated Recalls Retrieval Web Service that exposes recall records (with products, hazards, manufacturers, retailers, distributors, importers, and remedies) in JSON or XML, plus the SaferProducts.gov OData service for incident-report data accessed by application key.
c.name: Consumer Product Safety Commission

c.description: Industry-vertical index of APIs, data sources, syndication networks, and product information management (PIM) platforms that power the consumer packaged goods (CPG) and consumer products ecosystem. Catalogs corporate developer surfaces from large CPG manufacturers (P&G, Unilever, Nestle, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Mondelez, Kimberly-Clark, Colgate-Palmolive), product-identifier registries (GS1 Digital Link, GTIN/UPC lookup), open product databases (Open Food Facts, Open Beauty Facts), commercial syndication networks (Salsify, Syndigo, 1WorldSync), and PIM platforms (Akeneo, Pimcore, Plytix, Sales Layer).
c.name: Consumer Products

c.description: Consure Medical is a nurse-centric medical device company with Silicon Valley roots that develops incontinence and critical-care management solutions for hospitals. Its product line includes the QiVi family of truly external male and female urine management catheters, the Qora SMK manual stool management kit, and the Qoramatic automated stool management system, all designed to reduce catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI), incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD), and hospital-acquired conditions while improving patient dignity. The company operates from San Diego, California and New Delhi, India, and markets its devices through partners such as Medline. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Consure Medical publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface at the time of enrichment.
c.name: Consure Medical

c.description: Conta Azul is a Brazilian cloud accounting, financial-management and ERP platform for small and medium businesses, backed by Ribbit Capital. Its Nova API (v2, api-v2.contaazul.com) exposes the ERP over REST/JSON with OAuth 2.0 (AWS Cognito) authorization: financial events (accounts payable and receivable), installments, cost centers, categories and DRE, financial accounts and balances, sales, charges, products/inventory, proposals, contracts and settlements (baixas). The legacy API was sunset in November 2025 in favor of this versioned, OpenAPI-documented platform.
c.name: Conta Azul

c.description: Contabilizeicontabilidadeonline is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Contabilizeicontabilidadeonline

c.description: Contabo GmbH is a German hosting provider offering VPS, VDS, dedicated and GPU servers, S3-compatible object storage, private networking, DNS and domains. The Contabo API (https://api.contabo.com, OpenAPI 3.0.3, 157 operations) manages compute instances, snapshots, images, object storage, private networks, secrets, users, roles and tags using OAuth2 password-grant bearer tokens from auth.contabo.com; Contabo also ships the cntb CLI and a Terraform provider.
c.name: Contabo

c.description: ContactOut is a B2B email finder and professional contact data platform (ContactOut Pty Ltd, founded 2015, San Francisco) that provides verified personal and work emails, phone numbers and enriched people and company profiles for 350M professionals across 40M companies, delivered through a Chrome extension, search portal, bulk tools, a REST API at api.contactout.com and a hosted MCP server at contactout.com/mcp. Used by recruiters and sales teams; GDPR and CCPA compliant with a published opt-out, and intended for professional B2B use only.
c.name: ContactOut

c.description: Contactually was a cloud-based CRM (customer relationship management) platform focused on helping real estate agents, brokers, and other relationship-driven professionals nurture their networks through follow-up reminders, contact bucketing, pipelines, and automated outreach. Founded around 2011, it was acquired by real estate brokerage Compass on February 27, 2019, and had already been powering Compass's own CRM. Contactually permanently ceased operations on March 31, 2022. It historically exposed a v2 REST API (api.contactually.com) documented at developers.contactually.com for contacts, buckets, notes, tasks, and webhooks, but that developer surface, the API hosts, and all SDKs are now offline. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct provider; no live API, documentation, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.
c.name: Contactually

c.description: CNI (Container Network Interface) is a CNCF-incubating project that defines a specification and libraries for configuring network interfaces in Linux containers. It provides a simple exec/stdin interface between the container runtime and network implementation plugins, enabling pluggable networking for Kubernetes and other container orchestrators. The CNI spec defines four operations (ADD, DEL, CHECK, VERSION), a network configuration document format, and a plugin Result document. CNI also publishes a collection of reference plugins (bridge, ipvlan, macvlan, host-device, ptp, loopback) and meta-plugins (portmap, bandwidth, firewall, sbr).
c.name: Container Network Interface (CNI)

c.description: An industry-standard container runtime with an emphasis on simplicity, robustness and portability.
c.name: Containerd

c.description: A Containerfile is a plain text file that contains instructions for building container images. It is fully compatible with Docker's Dockerfile format and is the default file name used by Buildah and Podman. Containerfile instructions describe a base image (FROM), the steps to assemble the image (RUN, COPY, ADD, ARG, ENV), and runtime defaults (CMD, ENTRYPOINT, EXPOSE, USER, WORKDIR, VOLUME). Modern build engines extend the format with cache, secret, and SSH mounts and with platform-aware multi-stage builds.
c.name: Containerfile

c.description: Containous SAS is the France-founded (2016) cloud-native networking company that created Traefik, the open-source reverse proxy, ingress controller, and load balancer written in Go and downloaded billions of times from Docker Hub. Containous was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital, which led its Series A alongside Elaia Partners, 360 Capital, Kima Ventures, and OSS Capital. The company subsequently rebranded to Traefik Labs and its original containo.us domain now redirects to traefik.io. Under the Traefik Labs name it ships the open-source Traefik Proxy plus the commercial Traefik Hub product line (API Gateway, API Management, AI Gateway, and MCP Gateway). This repo is the company/parent profile; the full product and API surface (OpenAPI, CRDs, examples) lives in the api-evangelist/traefik repo.
c.name: Containous (Traefik Labs)

c.description: Contalink is a Mexican cloud accounting and payroll platform ("contabilidad en la nube") built for independent accountants, accounting firms (despachos) and SMEs. It automates repetitive Mexican fiscal work — bulk CFDI download and classification, electronic accounting, DIOT preparation, treasury and bank reconciliation, invoicing (facturación) and payroll (nómina) with digital stamping — across multiple companies and users. Contalink also exposes a REST API that lets external systems read and post accounting data: trial balance (balanza de comprobación), account balances, manual accounting policies (pólizas manuales), invoice reconciliation (conciliación), bank transactions (movimientos bancarios) and CFDI fiscal-document listing, upload and status checks. The API authenticates with a per-company API key sent in the Authorization header. Backed by 500 Global.
c.name: Contalink

c.description: Contasimples provides a digital banking platform for businesses in Brazil, offering corporate credit cards, payment services, expense management, and financial automation. The service includes features such as Pix transfers, batch payments, invoicing, and integration with ERP systems. It aims to simplify financial operations for startups and SMEs, providing tools for credit, cash flow management, and real‑time analytics.
c.name: Contasimples

c.description: Contego Medical develops integrated embolic protection and revascularization solutions for carotid and peripheral vascular disease, aiming to improve patient outcomes and procedural efficiency. The company partners with Medtronic for U.S. distribution and offers products such as Neuroguard IEP, Excipio, and Vanguard IEP, with a focus on simplifying complex vascular procedures.
c.name: Contego Medical

c.description: Conteller is a user-generated content (UGC) marketplace where brands pay for authentic media directly from their own customers and everyday, non-famous creators. Brands publish media briefs and the platform lets creators capture, submit, and store photos, videos, and TikTok-style content, then handles paying those creators for approved submissions. A Mexican/Spanish startup (Madrid) selected for Batch 19 of 500 Global's Somos Lucha accelerator program in Latin America, Conteller has run pilots spanning roughly 1,400 creators and a dozen brands. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of 500 Global. The public site is no longer serving: conteller.com and www.conteller.com both return HTTP 402 "Payment required / DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED" from Vercel on every path, the blog subdomain returns a Cloudflare 1014 and the admin subdomain a 522, and the Internet Archive holds no successful capture of the site after 2025-07-16. No public developer portal, API, documentation, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or agent-card surface has ever been found for Conteller, and its GitHub organization publishes no repositories.
c.name: Conteller

c.description: Contensis is an enterprise-level Content Management System (CMS) developed by Zengenti, designed to help organizations create, manage, and deliver digital content across multiple platforms and devices through HTTP, JavaScript, and .Net APIs.
c.name: Contensis

c.description: ContentBox is a blockchain infrastructure company for the digital content industry, built by the team behind Castbox, a global podcast platform serving millions of users across 135 countries. ContentBox aims to give the industry three things: a shared content pool, a shared user pool, and a unified, token-based payout system. Its products include BOX Payout (a blockchain multi-party payment system), BOX Passport (blockchain identity and attribution across applications), and BOX Unpack (a turn-key platform for content creators). The foundation publishes open-source blockchain infrastructure (boxd) and first-party developer SDKs in JavaScript, Python, and Java through its BOXFoundation GitHub organization. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.
c.name: contentbox

c.description: Contentful is a content management platform that allows businesses to create, manage, and deliver digital content across various channels and devices. By using Contentful, companies can streamline their content creation process, collaborate with team members, and ensure a consistent and cohesive brand message.
c.name: Contentful

c.description: Contentful Global is a global headquarter of Contentful, a leading content management platform now part of Salesforce. It provides APIs for managing content, assets, and digital experiences across web, mobile, and other channels. The company offers robust developer tools, extensive documentation, and enterprise-grade features for scaling digital experiences.
c.name: Contentful Global

c.description: Used to retrieve and apply transformations to images
c.name: Contentful Images

c.description: Content Guru is a global provider of cloud‑based Customer Experience (CX) solutions, founded in 2005 and serving enterprises in over 60 countries. The company offers the Storm CX platform, AI‑driven conversational tools, and integration services that help organisations improve customer satisfaction, automate processes, and leverage generative AI. Content Guru’s portfolio includes the brain® AI suite and the Storm® CX cloud, supporting industries such as finance, healthcare, utilities, and public sector. The firm emphasizes compliance, data security, and scalable cloud communications.
c.name: Contentguru

c.description: Contentladder Marketing, operating as Serpent API, provides developers with affordable, high‑volume search engine results (SERP) and related data across Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, and Brave. They offer transparent per‑unit pricing, a free tier, and a suite of APIs covering web search, image, video, news, shopping, maps, and social media data. The team of marketers built the service to reduce costs for data‑driven teams and supports AI‑enhanced ranking and custom data pipelines.
c.name: Contentladder Marketing

c.description: Contently is an end-to-end content marketing platform pairing enterprise content operations software with a vetted global network of 10,000+ freelance writers, editors, designers, and strategists, positioned for regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and insurance. Brands use Contently to plan editorial calendars, source and manage creative talent, run review-and-approval workflows with credentialed reviewers, publish across channels, and measure content performance. For developers Contently documents the Talent API, a REST-first JSON API secured with scoped OAuth2 that lets teams search vetted creators, open NDA-scoped projects, brief and message contributors, submit draft reviews, approve and pay out work, and check funded balances, with state-change webhooks over Slack, Teams, or raw HTTP. Contently also advertises an MCP server registering six tools, though no endpoint is published. No OpenAPI specification, reference documentation, or developer portal is published; API access is obtained through a sales conversation. Contently maintains SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA (BAA), and FINRA reviewer-pool posture with a published controls matrix.
c.name: Contently

c.description: Contentraven is a data aggregation and analytics platform that provides businesses with tools to collect, process, and visualize content from various sources. The company focuses on delivering APIs that enable integration of content streams, metadata enrichment, and real-time insights for enterprises seeking to enhance their digital presence and decision-making capabilities. While detailed public documentation is limited, the service appears to target marketing, media, and data-driven organizations looking to streamline content workflows and leverage AI-driven analysis.
c.name: Contentraven

c.description: Contentsdotcom provides an enterprise AI-powered content platform that enables creation, localization, and governance of copy, blogs, SEO, translations, images, video, and campaigns at scale. The service offers tools for content ideation, automated writing, multilingual translation, and brand voice management, targeting digital agencies and enterprises seeking to automate and optimize their content workflows.
c.name: Contentsdotcom

c.description: Contentsfirst is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. No official website could be verified; attempts to locate a corporate domain such as contentsfirst.com resulted in unreachable hosts, and the equityzen listing returns a 403. The company appears in various business directories but lacks a publicly accessible web presence.
c.name: Contentsfirst

c.description: Contentsquare is a digital experience analytics platform that captures every user interaction on web and mobile properties to surface friction points, conversion blockers, and behavioral insights via session replay, heatmaps, journey analysis, and zone-based analytics. The platform helps product, marketing, and UX teams optimize digital experiences with AI-driven recommendations. Contentsquare offers Data Export and Enrichment REST APIs authenticated via OAuth 2.0 client credentials with dynamic regional base URLs returned at authentication time.
c.name: Contentsquare

c.description: Contentstack is a composable, API-first content platform — an Agentic Experience Platform built around a headless CMS, a real-time customer data layer and an agent runtime. Developers reach it through a read-only Content Delivery API on a global CDN, a write-side Content Management API, a read-only GraphQL delivery surface, an on-the-fly Image Delivery API, and product APIs for Launch (front-end hosting), Automation Hub, Personalize, BrandKit AI and SCIM 2.0 user provisioning. Contentstack publishes a 95-scope OAuth 2.0 reference, an llms.txt, markdown twins of its API reference pages, and a first-party Model Context Protocol server exposing 206 tools whose definitions — including the REST call each one makes — it serves anonymously as JSON.
c.name: Contentstack

c.description: Context engineering is the practice of curating the information that large language models receive at inference time so that the model can perform a task reliably and cost-effectively. It treats the context window as a finite attention budget and looks for the smallest set of high-signal tokens that maximize the likelihood of the desired outcome. Context engineering subsumes and extends prompt engineering, system prompts, tool design, retrieval, agent loops, structured note taking, compaction, and multi-agent decomposition. It is a foundational discipline for building production AI agents and assistants.
c.name: Context Engineering

c.description: Context (context.ai) is a unified enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, and improving AI agents at scale. The product is organized into modular components: a Workspace for authoring agent workflows in plain English, an Engine with 800+ connectors and IdP-brokered identity, Unify as a knowledge/institutional-context repository, and Evals for rubric-based quality scoring. It is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, or open weights) and offers hosted, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment. The company originated as a GV (Google Ventures) and Theory Ventures backed product-analytics-for-LLMs startup and now operates as an enterprise agent platform used by teams including Qualcomm, Stripe, and Palantir. This repo carries no public developer/API surface: the provider publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation, so most machine-readable artifacts are not applicable.
c.name: Context.ai *

c.description: Context.dev is the unified web-context API for software and AI agents — one API that turns any domain or URL into structured, typed JSON. It covers brand intelligence (logos, colors, fonts, socials, address, industry codes, stock ticker / ISIN and transaction-descriptor resolution), web scraping and crawling to clean Markdown or HTML, screenshots, sitemap discovery, web search, structured data extraction against a JSON Schema, product extraction, document parsing to Markdown, NAICS / SIC classification, and website change monitoring with signed webhooks. Typed first-party SDKs ship for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go, and PHP, alongside a CLI, a hosted MCP server, and a published Agent Skill. Founded in 2025 by Yahia Bakour and backed by Y Combinator (S26).
c.name: Context.dev

c.description: Context7 is an Upstash service providing up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples for libraries and frameworks, exposed as both a REST API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI coding assistants can fetch authoritative reference material at prompt time.
c.name: Context7

c.description: ContextGem provides an AI-powered platform for extracting structured data from unstructured text using large language models. It offers pipelines for aspect extraction, concept identification, and decision modeling, enabling developers to integrate advanced natural language understanding into their applications. The documentation includes quickstart guides, installation instructions, and extensive examples for building extraction pipelines and leveraging supported LLMs.
c.name: ContextGem

c.description: Contextlogic2 is a stub company entry originating from the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. The company is associated with ContextLogic Holdings Inc., a publicly traded e‑commerce and technology firm that has undergone corporate reorganization and holds significant net operating loss assets. Public information indicates the firm operates a consumer-facing e‑commerce platform and maintains investor relations through its corporate website. Further details about its API offerings, documentation, and developer resources are not publicly accessible at this time.
c.name: Contextlogic2

c.description: ContextSDK is an on-device context intelligence layer for mobile apps, founded by Felix Krause and Dieter Rappold and backed by Speedinvest. Its SDK processes 300+ real-world device signals (accelerometer, gyroscope, motion, screen state, ambient signals) through on-device machine learning to determine what a user is doing in the moment — commuting, relaxing, working, or being active — within seconds of app launch, with no PII collected and a ~0.6 MB footprint. Two products build on this: ContextDecision for intelligent timing of in-app actions and messages, and ContextPush for context-aware push notification delivery. ContextSDK ships native clients for iOS (Swift), Flutter, React Native, and Unity, with Android in beta, and is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and GDPR compliant.
c.name: ContextSDK

c.description: Contextual AI is an enterprise RAG platform built around a Grounded Language Model (GLM) engineered to minimize hallucinations. Its REST API exposes end-to-end RAG agents (create, configure, query) plus standalone component APIs - Generate, Rerank, Parse, and LMUnit - over datastores of ingested documents, all authenticated with a Bearer API key.
c.name: Contextual AI

c.description: Contify is an AI-powered market and competitive intelligence platform that helps businesses track competitor activity, market trends, and industry news. It exposes a REST News API that delivers structured, deduplicated, and enriched business news data on companies, industries, and topics.
c.name: Contify

c.description: Continental AG is a German multinational automotive supplier and tire manufacturer headquartered in Hanover. As a global Tier 1 automotive supplier, Continental designs and manufactures tires, automotive electronics, brake systems, powertrain components, ADAS, and interior solutions for vehicle manufacturers worldwide.
c.name: Continental

c.description: Continental Resources, Inc. is a privately held independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and present on the web at clr.com. Its U.S. asset base spans the Bakken of North Dakota, South Dakota and Montana, the Anadarko Basin of Oklahoma, the Powder River Basin of Wyoming and the Permian Basin of Texas, with international positions in Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale and a joint venture in the Diyarbakir Basin of Turkey. The company was taken private in November 2022 in a $4.3B transaction with the Hamm family and is no longer publicly traded. Continental Resources publishes no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract of any kind; this profile catalogs its corporate, owner-relations, operational and sustainability web properties and records that its royalty-owner, vendor-invoicing and employee-access surfaces are each operated by a third-party software vendor rather than by Continental itself.
c.name: Continental Resources

c.description: Continua AI, Inc. is a Brooklyn-based startup founded by former Google Distinguished Engineer David Petrou and backed by GV, Bessemer Venture Partners, and angel investors. Its product, Wheelie, is a public Development OS for agentic coding work: a launch-preview platform where an agent starts from an existing checkout or public repo, uses a bring-your-own harness, takes one work item, and produces one reviewable diff with focused validation evidence. Wheelie ships a first-party CLI, a Capability Kit npm package, an agent-readable llms.txt docs index, a public support-state matrix, and a private-preview changelog and status page.
c.name: Continua

c.description: Continual was an operational-AI / MLOps platform for the modern data stack, founded by Tristan Zajonc (previously Sense, acquired by Cloudera) and Tyler Kohn (co-founder of RichRelevance). It let data and analytics teams declaratively build, deploy, and continuously maintain production predictive models directly inside cloud data warehouses — Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery — using SQL and dbt as the primary interface rather than bespoke ML pipelines. The company raised a seed round led by Amplify Partners and a $14.5M Series A in 2022. The product is now dormant: continual.ai is a parked single-page shell, the documentation host redirects to the homepage, and the last release of the first-party Python CLI + SDK on PyPI was in March 2023. This profile captures the verifiable public artifacts that remain — the PyPI package, the GitHub organization, and a live domain-security posture.
c.name: Continual

c.description: Continue is the open-source AI code assistant for VS Code and JetBrains, distributed under Apache 2.0. The Continue IDE extensions and the Continue CLI federate to any LLM provider — Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter, Ollama, and a Continue-managed proxy — and load their configuration from Continue Hub. Continue Hub (api.continue.dev) is the registry and IDE API that serves assistants, blocks, models, rules, prompts, docs, and MCP servers to the extensions, along with free-trial status, organization policy, secrets sync, and the Stripe checkout URL for the Models Add-On. Continue has also pivoted into "continuous AI" — source- controlled checks that live as markdown files under .continue/checks/ and run in CI as GitHub status checks.
c.name: Continue

c.description: Continuous Composites advances composite manufacturing with its patented CF3D® continuous fiber 3D printing technology. Founded in 2012 in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, the company delivers high‑performance aerospace and defense structures, offering rapid‑curing resins, intelligent automation, and scalable production for demanding applications.
c.name: Continuous Composites

c.description: The Continuous Delivery Foundation (CDF) is a Linux Foundation project that hosts vendor-neutral open source projects for continuous integration, continuous delivery, and DevOps. It is the home of CDEvents, Jenkins, Spinnaker, Screwdriver, Ortelius, JayeX, and was previously the home of Tekton (now a CNCF graduated project) and other CD-focused tooling.
c.name: Continuous Delivery Foundation

c.description: Continuum (gocontinuum.ai) is an AI-powered platform that automates B2B returns, warranties, and repairs for distributors and manufacturers. It handles the post-sales workflow end to end through four solution hubs: a Customer Hub with self-service warranty and return portals, a Warehouse Hub for one-click receiving, inspection and dispute processing, a Vendor & Finance Hub for automated vendor engagement and accounts-receivable management, and a Manufacturer Warranty Hub for warranty claim automation. The company reports outcomes such as a 70% reduction in returns labor cost, a 30% increase in profitability, and an 8% reduction in customer churn. Continuum integrates with major distribution ERP systems (Infor, NetSuite, Epicor, Oracle, Acumatica). Based in Chicago, it is seed-funded and backed by Cowboy Ventures. Continuum is SOC 2 audited and publishes a public trust center. No public developer API or documentation is available at this time.
c.name: Continuum

c.description: Continuumanalytics is a data analytics firm that provides continuous monitoring and analysis solutions for businesses. The company focuses on real-time data ingestion, processing, and visualization to help clients make informed decisions. It offers APIs for data collection, event streaming, and analytics dashboards, targeting sectors such as finance, healthcare, and e‑commerce. Continuumanalytics aims to simplify complex data workflows and deliver actionable insights through scalable cloud services.
c.name: Continuumanalytics

c.description: ContinuumCloud is a Tampa, Florida-based provider of cloud software purpose-built for behavioral health and human services organizations. Its integrated suite spans three products: Welligent, an electronic health record (EHR) platform for caseload management, scheduling, clinical documentation and revenue-cycle management; DATIS e3, a unified human capital management (HCM) and payroll system covering recruiting, onboarding, timekeeping, talent management and workforce analytics; and CaredFor, a patient-engagement platform that builds online communities connecting clients, alumni and families. Formerly known as Behavioral Holdings and founded in 2020, the company draws on 25+ years of domain focus and is backed by Battery Ventures. ContinuumCloud does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP server at this time; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.
c.name: ContinuumCloud

c.description: ContinuumRx provides home and site-based infusion therapies and services, partnering with healthcare systems to improve post-acute care coordination, patient outcomes, and financial performance. With over twenty years of experience, they offer antibiotic, enteral, parenteral, IVIG, heart‑failure, and biologic therapies, along with patient education and referral resources.
c.name: ContinuumRx

c.description: Continuumtechnology is an IT consulting firm based in Mount Rainier, MD, offering digital transformation, data platforms, AI services, and tailored technology solutions for businesses of all sizes. Their mission is to empower clients through expert consulting, cost‑effective solutions, and a focus on innovation and technology adoption.
c.name: Continuumtechnology

c.description: Contoro Robotics, founded in 2022 and based in Austin, Texas, develops AI‑powered autonomous robots that unload non‑palletized boxes from trailers and shipping containers. Their human‑in‑the‑loop platform combines teleoperation, AI training, and DuoGrasp grippers to provide a reliable, affordable, and safe solution for logistics operators, reducing labor costs and improving safety without requiring upfront capital or long‑term contracts.
c.name: Contoro Robotics

c.description: A Kubernetes ingress controller using Envoy proxy that provides dynamic configuration updates and advanced routing capabilities for managing external access to services in a cluster.
c.name: Contour

c.description: Contra is an independent-first, commission-free freelance marketplace and professional network for the jobs and skills of the future, founded in 2019 by Ben Huffman and Gajus Kuizinas and backed by Cowboy Ventures, Unusual Ventures, and NEA. Independents build a portfolio, get discovered, and manage work from inquiry to contract to payment without platform commissions. For developers, Contra exposes a read-only Public API (programs, filters, and expert profiles under https://contra.com/public-api/, authenticated with an X-API-Key header), an attribute-driven Webflow SDK, a React UI-kit, and a hosted, OAuth 2.1-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://contra.com/mcp (scope mcp:tools).
c.name: Contra

c.description: Contract Guard provides a deterministic JSON Schema validation API for software and AI workflows. It returns exact validation violations and optional conservative type normalization. The service is operated by WOODS HOLDING GROUP LLC and is currently in an experimental live state with billing disabled. It offers a public demo, OpenAPI 3.1 spec, MCP endpoint, ARD manifest, Postman collection, and product registry.
c.name: Contract Guard / Autonomous Utility Factory

c.description: Contractbook is a contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform that turns static contracts into structured, automatable data. Its Public API v3 (base https://api.contractbook.com/v3, Bearer API-key auth) lets teams generate pre-filled contract drafts from any data source, send documents for electronic signature, manage templates, organize documents into spaces, run automations, upload attachments, and receive webhook notifications on document life-cycle events. Contractbook covers the full contract lifecycle - drafting, negotiation, signing, storage, and post-signature management - for legal, sales, HR, and procurement teams.
c.name: Contractbook

c.description: Contractor Foreman is all-in-one construction management software for contractors - estimates, invoicing, scheduling, time cards, daily logs, change orders, and job costing - used by contractors in more than 75 countries. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference; the company's dedicated API subdomain (api.contractorforeman.net) displays only a "Coming soon" placeholder as of this review. The one confirmed API capability is a private, account-scoped API key (generated under Settings > Integration > Zapier) that powers Contractor Foreman's official Zapier app, exposing Customer and Lead create/archive/delete triggers and actions plus a File Uploaded trigger. That key and its underlying endpoints are not documented or published for direct third-party use outside the Zapier integration; broader third-party connectivity otherwise runs through native integrations (QuickBooks, Gusto, Google Calendar/Outlook, Stripe, Angi Leads, CompanyCam, MS Project, SweetPay) and Zapier/webhook automation rather than an open API.
c.name: Contractor Foreman

c.description: ContractPodAi, now operating as Leah, is an agentic AI platform that unifies contract lifecycle management, legal transformation, and source‑to‑pay automation. It delivers end‑to‑end solutions for legal, procurement, and finance teams, leveraging AI to streamline contract creation, analysis, compliance, and execution across enterprises.
c.name: ContractPodAi

c.description: ContraForce is the Agentic Security Delivery Platform for Microsoft security teams, MSPs, MSSPs, and security operations teams. It provides AI‑powered triage, investigation, response, tuning, ticketing, and reporting on Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. The platform offers a free 30‑day trial with no credit card required, enabling service providers to scale SOC delivery without hiring additional analysts.
c.name: Contraforce

c.description: Contraline is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing non-hormonal, long-acting, reversible contraceptive options for men and couples. Its lead product, ADAM, is an investigational implant designed to provide long-lasting reversible contraception, and NES/T is a daily topical gel intended to pause sperm production. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Contraline runs clinical trials and participant programs from its Charlottesville, Virginia base. Its products are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA. The company operates a marketing and clinical-trial website with no public developer program or API; this API Evangelist profile captures its web presence, privacy posture, and domain security for the network catalog.
c.name: Contraline

c.description: Contrast Security is an application security platform that uses instrumentation-based agents to provide Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST), Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA) across Java, .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go, and Ruby applications. The platform identifies, prioritizes, and defends against vulnerabilities and attacks in real time from inside running applications. Contrast's REST API enables programmatic access to TeamServer applications, libraries, vulnerabilities, and traces, authenticated via API key plus Authorization header (Base64 of username:service_key) and an Organization ID.
c.name: Contrast Security

c.description: Contrea, Inc. is a Tokyo‑based healthcare technology startup founded in 2020. It provides a cloud‑based informed‑consent platform called MediOS that streamlines patient‑provider communication, administrative procedures, and information exchange in medical institutions. The company focuses on SaaS solutions for the legacy healthcare sector, aiming to modernize consent management and digital patient engagement.
c.name: Contrea

c.description: CONTRIBUTING.md is a community health convention used by open source projects on GitHub and other platforms to document how external contributors can participate. The file communicates contribution guidelines, pull request processes, issue reporting procedures, coding standards, development setup, testing expectations, and code of conduct references. GitHub recognizes CONTRIBUTING.md placed in the repository root, the .github folder, or the docs folder, and surfaces a link to it whenever a contributor opens a new issue or pull request.
c.name: CONTRIBUTING.md

c.description: CONTRIBUTORS.md is an open source convention used to recognize the people and organizations that have contributed to a project. The file lists contributors by name, GitHub handle, and contribution type, ranging from code and documentation to design, testing, accessibility, and community organization. CONTRIBUTORS.md is often paired with the All Contributors specification, which standardizes contribution categories using emoji keys and supports automated table generation through the All Contributors bot.
c.name: CONTRIBUTORS.md

c.description: Control Seat is an AI-native industrial systems integrator building a modern replacement for legacy SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) platforms such as Ignition, WinCC, and FactoryTalk. It designs, builds, deploys, and runs the full industrial control stack, from PLC programming (Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and HMI/SCADA operator screens to OT/IT networking, historians, and analytics, on a single unified platform. The product connects to field devices over OPC UA and MQTT (Sparkplug B), integrates with AVEVA PI, Ignition, and standard SQL/time-series databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, InfluxDB, Prometheus) plus REST APIs, and streams 10k+ tags per second at sub-100ms latency. AI-native features let operators generate control screens in seconds, run anomaly detection and forecasting, and query the historian in plain English. Enterprise capabilities include SSO, SCIM, role-based access control, and audit logs, with deployment on managed cloud or self-hosted on-premises. Founded in 2025 by Jack Grodnick and Warren Shepard, Control Seat is based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026).
c.name: Control Seat

c.description: Control4 is a smart home and building automation platform, now part of Snap One / ADI Global (Resideo), headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. It unifies control of lighting, audio/video, home theater, climate, security, shades, and voice across residential and commercial spaces through a single interface on smartphones, touchscreens, and on-wall keypads. Control4 is delivered through a network of certified integrators rather than direct-to-consumer sales, and interoperates with more than 25,000 third-party devices. For developers it offers the DriverWorks SDK (a Lua-based framework for building device drivers), the Control4 Developer Portal for OAuth application registration against the Control4 cloud, and public first-party libraries on GitHub.
c.name: Control4

c.description: Controlant provides real‑time, GxP‑validated pharma supply‑chain visibility through its Saga devices and platform. It monitors temperature, location and status of shipments across the globe, offering data sharing via Delta Sharing, streaming, and an Integrations API. Founded in 2009, Controlant serves top pharma companies, delivering millions of shipments in over 180 countries with 24/7 monitoring and rapid response.
c.name: Controlant

c.description: Controlled Thermal Resources develops the Hell’s Kitchen project, an integrated geothermal power plant that generates renewable baseload electricity and extracts critical minerals such as lithium carbonate, zinc, manganese and potash. The company refines these minerals on‑site into battery‑grade products and supplies clean energy to advanced manufacturers, data centers and battery producers. Its vertically integrated model aims to reduce U.S. supply‑chain risk and support domestic energy and mineral needs.
c.name: Controlled Thermal Resources

c.description: ControlPlane provides a virtual cloud platform that unifies compute, networking, identity, and services across multiple clouds, bare metal, and on‑prem environments. It enables teams to build, ship, and scale applications with AI‑native automation, universal cloud identity, and zero‑ops operations, offering high availability and compliance features for enterprise workloads.
c.name: ControlPlane

c.description: ControlRooms.ai provides an agentic troubleshooting system for energy and chemical plant operations. It uses large harmony models to detect anomalies before traditional alarms fire, offering proactive advice, logging, and AI‑drafted shift summaries. The platform integrates with existing DCS, Teams, and mobile apps to help operators mitigate issues early, improving safety and efficiency across refining, fertilizers, petrochemicals, and related sectors.
c.name: ControlRooms.ai

c.description: ControlUp is a Digital Employee Experience (DEX) and Autonomous Endpoint Management (AEM) platform that monitors, scores and remediates the end-user computing estate — physical desktops and laptops, VDI and DaaS (Citrix CVAD / Citrix Cloud, Omnissa Horizon, Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Parallels RAS), the applications and sessions running on them, and the network path in between. The ControlUp ONE platform spans ControlUp for Desktops, for VDI, for Apps, for Frontline Workers and for Compliance, plus Synthetic Monitoring (Scouts and Hives), Workflows, and Pulse AI. It publishes a public REST API surface at api.controlup.com documented on a ReadMe hub at api.controlup.io, an RFC 9727 /.well-known/api-catalog linkset enumerating twelve OpenAPI definitions, an official Model Context Protocol server on npm (@controlup-ai/mcp) exposing 106 tools across six product domains, PowerShell cmdlets for monitor and agent automation, and llms.txt indexes on both the documentation and API hosts.
c.name: ControlUp

c.description: ControlUp provides an AI-powered digital employee experience platform that automates, monitors, and optimizes IT environments across desktops, applications, and cloud workloads. Their solutions include real‑time performance monitoring, automated remediation, and analytics to improve operational efficiency and end‑user experience. Founded to empower IT teams, ControlUp serves enterprises worldwide with a focus on proactive management and AI-driven insights.
c.name: Controlupinc

c.description: Contunity GmbH is a software and electronics development company based in Garching near Munich, Germany. It offers a cloud‑based B2B SaaS platform for digital transformation, providing services such as cloud solutions, data analytics, custom software development, and tools that automate schematic and PCB layout generation. The company serves clients in various industries, aiming to enhance operational efficiency and drive business growth through innovative technology solutions.
c.name: Contunity

c.description: Conundrum (Conundrum Industrial Ltd, Cambridge, UK) is an industrial AI company building AI-driven, closed-loop advanced process control (APC) and model predictive control (MPC) software for the metals, mining, and cement industries. Its platform combines physics-informed and machine-learning models with real-time controllers, optimizers, data-quality tooling, interactive process-flow diagrams, drag-and-drop dashboards, and a Python SDK for building configurable runtime applications. Conundrum optimizes crushing, grinding, flotation, and cement processes to raise throughput and metal recovery while reducing energy consumption, deployed on-premises or in the cloud across plants running 24/7. The company is backed by Speedinvest and reports deployments across multiple plants in several countries.
c.name: Conundrum

c.description: Convai builds conversational AI for interactive characters in games and virtual worlds. Its API covers character creation and configuration, chat sessions and history, knowledge banks, speech and text-to-speech, custom LLM integration and evaluation.
c.name: Convai

c.description: Convalifepharmaceuticals is a Shanghai-based biopharmaceutical company focused on innovative drug research and development, targeting tumor, antiviral and aging related diseases. The firm develops small-molecule, antibody-drug conjugate and other therapeutic platforms, and holds multiple patents and clinical trials. It operates primarily in China and is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange, with recent licensing agreements expanding its global reach.
