(Source: https://duckduckgo.com/html/?q=Convalifepharmaceuticals, https://convalife.com/en/)
c.name: Convalifepharmaceuticals

c.description: Convelio is a Paris- and London-based tech-enabled fine art logistics company that moves high-value, fragile and oversized objects — paintings, sculpture, antiques and design — for galleries, auction houses, art fairs, dealers, collectors and online marketplaces. Its differentiator is an instant-pricing engine that returns an all-inclusive door-to-door shipping price (packing, crating, customs, road/air/sea freight, insurance and white-glove delivery) in place of the multi-day manual quoting the art-handling trade traditionally runs on. Convelio exposes that engine to partners as the Convelio Public API — a REST Shipping API (v2.0) documented with OpenAPI 3.1 at developers.convelio.com — plus an embeddable checkout widget, a web dashboard and a tracking surface, so marketplaces and auction platforms can price, book and track fine art shipments inside their own product.
c.name: Convelio

c.description: Convene provides hospitality-driven meeting, event, and flexible office space solutions for businesses and organizations. Their platform offers venues, technology, and services to host conferences, corporate events, and collaborative workspaces across major cities worldwide, emphasizing seamless experiences and flexible arrangements.
c.name: Convene

c.description: ConvenientPower (Chengdu ConvenientPower Semiconductor, 成都市易冲半导体有限公司) is an analog and mixed-signal integrated-circuit design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Silicon Valley. The company designs high-performance power-management ICs spanning the full link from 220V mains to battery: wireless-charging transmitters and receivers (Qi, up to 100W), USB Power Delivery and UFCS protocol controllers, AC/DC flyback and synchronous rectifier controllers, GaN-integrated solutions, battery-charging management, LDOs and DC/DC converters, and automotive-grade power ICs (wireless charging, LED lighting, eFuse protection, switches). Its parts ship into consumer electronics, accessories, and automotive markets, with more than 330 million units shipped and 160+ patents; automotive ICs are AEC-Q100 qualified. As a hardware semiconductor vendor, ConvenientPower exposes developer resources as chip SDK toolkits, reference designs, and design software rather than a public web API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.
c.name: ConvenientPower

c.description: Convention over Configuration (CoC) is a software design principle that prefers sensible defaults and standard patterns over explicit, repetitive configuration. Frameworks that adopt CoC reduce the number of decisions a developer must make to start a new project while still allowing overrides for non-standard cases. CoC was popularized by Ruby on Rails but predates Rails, drawing on UI principles like the principle of least astonishment and conventions in JavaBeans, Maven, and other Java ecosystems. The principle continues to shape modern frameworks such as Spring Boot, Next.js, Astro, Phoenix, Ember, Hugo, and Remix.
c.name: Convention Over Configuration

c.description: CONVENTIONS.md is a Markdown convention popularized by AI pair programming tools such as aider and adopted by AI coding agents like Cursor, Cline, and Claude Code. It documents project-specific coding standards, library preferences, naming conventions, architecture decisions, and development practices in plain natural language so both human developers and AI assistants share the same expectations. The file is loaded into the model context to steer code generation toward project conventions.
c.name: CONVENTIONS.md

c.description: Conventus Flower Orthopedics develops innovative orthopedic surgical solutions, aiming to simplify clinical and operational complexities of orthopedic procedures. Their product portfolio includes the FlexThread® IM Nail Platform, Constrictor® Rope Syndesmosis Repair, Ready‑For‑Surgery® sterile systems, plates, screws, and biologics. The company focuses on improving efficiency and outcomes for foot and ankle surgery, offering ready‑for‑surgery kits and advanced implant technologies.
c.name: Conventus Flower Orthopedics

c.description: Convercent (now "Convercent by OneTrust") is an enterprise ethics and compliance GRC SaaS platform providing case and helpline management, policy management and attestations, compliance training and learning, campaigns, disclosures, and an interactive code of conduct. Acquired by OneTrust in 2021, its customer base is being migrated to EQS Group. Convercent exposes compliance reporting data through an OData data-services API (v4/v5) covering case management, campaigns, policy attestations, and course completions, authenticated with HTTP Basic and intended for administrators/moderators to connect BI and reporting tools.
c.name: Convercent

c.description: Converge Bio is a generative-AI platform for life sciences that accelerates drug development across discovery, molecular design, and manufacturing. It trains Bio-LLM foundation models directly on biological languages (DNA, RNA, and protein sequences) and delivers them through the Converge Computational Lab, whose applications include ConvergeAB (AI antibody design across IgG/VHH/bispecific formats), ConvergeGEO (protein gene-expression optimization across CHO/HEK293/E. coli and other cell systems), ConvergeCELL (virtual cell simulation for target and biomarker discovery), and a Patent Extractor for mining antibody sequences. The platform is delivered to biotech and pharmaceutical customers under a Request Access engagement model; there is no public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface today. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners ($25M Series A, January 2026); founded 2023.
c.name: Converge Bio

c.description: Converge Insurance is a New York‑based cyber insurance MGA that combines advanced AI‑driven underwriting, a proprietary data ecosystem, and deep security expertise to deliver clear, confident cyber protection for businesses across the United States. The company’s platform fuses insurance expertise with technology to lower cyber risk and provide tailored coverage for mid‑size organizations.
c.name: Converge Insurance

c.description: Convergence AI was a London-based artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2024 by Marvin Purtorab (CEO) and Andy Toulis (CTO) building Proxy, a personal AI agent designed to complete open-ended administrative and web-browsing tasks across domains. Its approach centered on long-term memory and continual learning via a new class of models it called Large Meta Learning Models (LMLM). Convergence raised a $12M pre-seed led by Balderton Capital with participation from Salesforce Ventures and Shopify Ventures, and was acquired by Salesforce in May 2025 to strengthen Agentforce. Its lasting public surface is the convergence-ai GitHub organization, which open-sourced proxy-lite (a mini open-weights web-browsing agent), the proxy-lite-3b vision-language model on Hugging Face, the LM2 memory-model paper repo, and the WebGames agent benchmark.
c.name: convergence

c.description: Convergent Dental, Inc. is a privately held dental equipment and technology manufacturer headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, best known for Solea, a 9.3 micron CO2 all-tissue dental laser cleared by the FDA for hard tissue, soft tissue and osseous indications. The Solea platform is marketed for anesthesia-free, blood-free and suture-free restorative, soft tissue, pediatric, implant and cosmetic procedures, and has been extended with Solea Perioguide for minimally invasive periodontal therapy, Solea Sleep and Solea Protect. The company sells and services through its own commercial organization and a distribution partnership with Patterson Dental, and supports clinicians with training and education, clinical studies, case studies and the annual Solea Summit. Convergent Dental publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract or agent surface as of this profiling pass.
c.name: Convergent Dental

c.description: Convergent Networks, Inc. was a carrier-grade broadband voice infrastructure vendor that built next-generation VoIP switching and signaling equipment for telecommunications carriers, including the ICS2000 and Commando media gateways, the PacketMatrix softswitch controller for call screening and number translation, and the ICSG SS7 signaling gateway. Venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Saints Capital (raising roughly $57M across two rounds), the company was acquired by Eastern Photonics, a subsidiary of Global NAPs, in 2003. It is defunct and publishes no active developer portal, API, or specification. This profile was surfaced from the Battery Ventures portfolio as a lead; the enrichment pipeline found no live API surface to harvest.
c.name: Convergent Networks

c.description: Convergent Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing next-generation targeted radiotherapies for cancer. Founded in 2020 by Philip Kantoff, the company builds alpha radioantibodies that pair a humanized monoclonal antibody against prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) with the alpha emitter actinium-225, delivering short-range, high-energy alpha radiation to tumor cells. Its lead candidate, CONV01-alpha (rosopatamab tetraxetan), is in the Phase 2 CONVERGE-01 trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, including patients previously treated with Lu-177 PSMA radioligand therapy, with a pivotal Phase 3 planned. Convergent announced a $90 million Series A financing in 2023. The company publishes a corporate website covering its pipeline, technology, scientific publications and press, but operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.
c.name: Convergent Therapeutics

c.description: Convergys Corporation was a global leader in customer management services — contact center outsourcing, workforce management, customer analytics and digital customer experience platforms — serving communications, financial services, healthcare, retail and technology clients. SYNNEX acquired Convergys in October 2018 and merged it into Concentrix; the brand was retired and its offerings were folded into the Concentrix portfolio. Convergys published no public API or developer program that survives. Probed 2026-09-07: www.convergys.com is an Azure App Service redirect app that has been switched off and now answers "403 Site Disabled" on every path with an expired TLS certificate, and developer.convergys.com still resolves to an address block registered to Concentrix CVG Brite Voice Systems LLC with both HTTP ports closed. The successor company, Concentrix, is profiled separately and delivers most platform integration through enterprise contracts rather than a public developer program.
c.name: Convergys

c.description: ConverseNow is an Austin, Texas voice AI company, founded in 2018, that builds conversational AI virtual assistants which automate restaurant order taking across high-volume voice channels — inbound phone, drive-thru, SMS, and kiosk. The platform uses large language models to understand natural-language orders, suggest upsells, and confirm items in real time, and it markets an "Order Injection API" that pushes completed orders into restaurant point-of-sale and order-management systems. ConverseNow lists integrations with Brink POS, Fiserv, Focus, ItsaCheckmate, NCR Aloha, Olo, PAR, Qu, Xpient, Adora POS, and Deliverect, and reports processing more than two million conversations per month across national QSR brands. It publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; API access is reached through a sales consultation.
c.name: ConverseNow

c.description: Converseon provides AI‑powered natural language processing solutions that help enterprises extract actionable insights from unstructured data such as social media, news, and voice‑of‑customer content. Their platform offers trusted model governance, customizable and pre‑built models, and a suite of analytics tools to improve data quality, enable predictive intelligence, and support market research workflows. Converseon serves sectors including finance, consumer goods, and public relations, delivering scalable, secure, and compliant AI services.
c.name: Converseon

c.description: Conversica is an AI conversation automation company - "The Conversation Company" - whose Revenue Digital Assistants and AI Agents hold two-way, natural-language conversations with leads and customers over email, SMS and website chat to generate demand, answer questions and drive renewals. Founded in 2007 as AutoFerret.com and renamed Conversica in 2014, the San Mateo company serves automotive, sports and entertainment, hospitality, higher education and enterprise teams, and says its platform has powered more than 1.5 billion conversations for 2,000+ teams. Its integration surface is the Conversica Integrations API - a JSON-over-HTTPS, Basic-authenticated endpoint that ingests Lead objects, plus provider-initiated Message, Lead Update and Website Chat lead-creation webhooks delivered to endpoints the customer hosts - alongside packaged connectors for Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, Pardot, Microsoft Dynamics and automotive CRMs.
c.name: Conversica

c.description: ConverSight.ai is an agentic decision-intelligence platform for supply chain, giving manufacturing, distribution, and retail organizations AI agents that automate routine planning, procurement, and optimization decisions. Its patented Athena AI engine sits on a Data Workbench, a UniVerse knowledge layer, and a workflow engine, and ships ready-to-deploy agents (Demand Planner, Supply Planner, Production Planner, Procurement, Inventory Optimizer, Supply Assurance, Supplier Scorecard, S&OP Coordinator) across four intelligence levels from conversational assistant to autonomous AI employee. Pre-built connectors and open APIs let it run alongside SAP, Acumatica, Sage, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, Snowflake, QuickBooks, Kinaxis, Fishbowl, and Katana, and the company is a Techstars-backed venture serving 1,500+ supply chain organizations under SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance.
c.name: ConverSight.ai

c.description: ConversionPoint Technologies, Inc. is a privately held e‑commerce technology company that provides AI‑enabled media optimization, customer relationship management, and post‑purchase platforms to help brands, advertisers, and agencies acquire and retain customers. The company was slated for acquisition by Inuvo, Inc., and operates under the ConversionPoint Holdings umbrella, with its public presence now integrated into the Inuvo website.
c.name: ConversionPoint Technologies

c.description: Convert is an A/B testing and experimentation platform with privacy-first analytics and integrations for marketers and developers.
c.name: Convert

c.description: Convertabankstatement provides a platform that enables users to transform bank statement data into standardized, machine‑readable formats. By offering robust APIs, the service supports automated ingestion, categorization, and reconciliation of financial transactions for fintech applications, accounting software, and personal finance tools. The solution emphasizes security, compliance with banking standards, and scalability to handle high‑volume data streams, helping businesses streamline financial workflows and gain actionable insights.
c.name: Convertabankstatement

c.description: ConvertAPI is a file conversion REST API supporting over 200 file format conversions including PDF, Microsoft Office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), images, audio, video, and e-book formats. The API provides batch processing via Conversion Workflows, asynchronous conversion, a Virtual File Server for managing files, and SDKs across 12 programming languages. The platform is ISO 27001 certified and HIPAA and GDPR compliant with a 99.95% uptime guarantee.
c.name: ConvertAPI

c.description: Conversion Insights is a strategic AI advisory firm that helps businesses accelerate growth through digital customer acquisition and real‑time intelligence. Their platform combines AI‑driven paid media, conversion optimization, data integration, CRM, and content strategies to fill marketing pipelines, while offering dashboards, anomaly detection, and actionable alerts that turn data into immediate business decisions.
c.name: Convertinsights

c.description: Convertro, Inc. was a marketing analytics company based in Santa Monica, California, providing a multi-touch attribution platform that measured the ROI of marketing touchpoints across online and offline media using algorithmic attribution models. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Convertro was acquired by AOL in 2014 and folded into the AOL/Verizon (now Yahoo) advertising stack. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: convertro.com redirects to yahooinc.com, and no developer portal, documentation, API, or reachable API host was found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a network record; there is no live provider API surface to enrich.
c.name: Convertro, Inc.

c.description: Converus provides advanced lie detection technology using eye‑movement analysis, offering products such as EyeDetect, EyeDetect+, and VerifEye for law enforcement, corporate security, and government agencies. Founded in 2014, the company combines AI and neuroscience to deliver rapid, accurate deception detection solutions worldwide.
c.name: Converus

c.description: ConverzAI is a Seattle-based artificial intelligence company (founded 2019) that builds an agentic, voice-first AI platform for the recruitment and staffing industry. Its flagship Virtual Recruiter deploys autonomous AI agents that source, engage, screen, and match candidates through natural conversations over voice, text, and email, then update the customer's applicant tracking system automatically. The platform integrates with major ATS products used by staffing firms (Avionte, Bullhorn, Ceipal, JobDiva, Salesforce, TempWorks and others) and lets a single recruiter engage hundreds of thousands of candidates in parallel. ConverzAI raised a $16M Series A led by Menlo Ventures in February 2025 and reports processing over 100,000 jobs while engaging millions of candidates. This is a product/application company profile; ConverzAI does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.
c.name: ConverzAI

c.description: Convex is a serverless backend platform that provides a real-time database, cloud functions, and infrastructure for building modern web and mobile applications. It offers a TypeScript-first developer experience with reactive queries, transactional mutations, and integrated file storage, all accessible through a suite of HTTP, management, and deployment APIs alongside JavaScript and server SDKs for full-stack application development. The platform is SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and GDPR compliant.
c.name: Convex

c.description: Convex Group Limited is an international specialty insurer and reinsurer founded in 2019 by Stephen Catlin and Paul Brand, headquartered in London with operations in Bermuda, Luxembourg, Guernsey and the United States. Convex writes complex commercial and specialty risk across property, casualty, marine, energy, aviation, cyber, political risk and credit, crisis management, accident and health, and equine/livestock/aquaculture, and writes property, casualty and specialty treaty reinsurance through Convex Re Limited in Bermuda and London. Convex Insurance UK Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the FCA and PRA; it is a London company-market carrier rather than a Lloyd's syndicate, and it reported roughly $5.2bn of gross written premium in 2024. Convex operates a named Digital Underwriting function that publicly describes building "a suite of insurance specific APIs" for automated quote and bind on high-volume, low-complexity specialty books, delivered either through a Convex-hosted broker portal or by connecting Convex products into a broker's or client's existing portal via API. That API programme is real but entirely partner-gated: as of 2026-07-25 Convex publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine- readable definition, no sandbox and no self-serve signup. The api.convexin.com host is live but answers every anonymous request with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the digital.convexin.com broker application is an authenticated Unqork-hosted portal, and the Convex Quick Quote event-insurance surface is behind a broker account registration form. Integration is arranged through the Business Development team, not through documentation. No ACORD, AL3, NGDS or IVANS reference appears anywhere on Convex's public web presence.
c.name: Convex

c.description: Convex Finance is a DeFi protocol that boosts Curve Finance liquidity provider and CRV staker yields through its CVX token and pooled staking mechanism. It allows users to earn boosted CRV rewards and CVX without locking CRV directly.
c.name: Convex Finance

c.description: Convey is an enterprise AI platform for building and running autonomous "digital teammates" — AI workers that non-technical operators train by describing a workflow or sharing their screen, after which the teammate runs business processes end to end across existing enterprise systems (Salesforce, NetSuite, ad operations, reporting) with role-based access, isolated agent identities, dedicated credentials, audit logs, and escalation to a human on high-stakes decisions. Founded by former DoorDash and project44 engineers, Convey raised a $38M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in June 2026 (with Khosla Ventures and Pear VC) and reports 1.1M+ hours of work completed for customers including NBCUniversal, TelevisaUnivision, Unity, and Samsara. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. Convey is an enterprise, contact-sales product with no public developer API or documentation surface as of this profile.
c.name: Convey

c.description: Conveyor provides an AI‑powered platform that automates security questionnaire responses, trust‑center management, and RFP workflows for enterprise teams. By combining large‑language models with a curated knowledge base, Conveyor helps security, compliance, and sales organizations accelerate reviews, improve accuracy, and reduce manual effort. The solution includes a Trust Center, AI‑driven questionnaire automation, analytics, and integrations with popular SaaS tools, delivering a secure, scalable, and customizable experience for high‑stakes customer interactions.
c.name: Conveyor

c.description: Conveyor9c1e is a stub entry generated by the API Evangelist harvesting process from secondary-market sources. No public website, documentation, or API endpoints have been identified for this entity. The record exists to allow future enrichment should verifiable information become available, and to maintain a placeholder within the network for tracking purposes.
c.name: Conveyor9c1e

c.description: Convictional provides a platform for aligning organizational goals through AI-driven collaborative tools. It offers products such as collaborative email, goal alignment dashboards, and research resources to help teams make better decisions. The company publishes extensive essays, research papers, and handbooks on AI, decision-making, and organizational health, reflecting its focus on improving human-AI collaboration in the workplace.
c.name: Convictional

c.description: Convirza provides conversation analytics and call tracking solutions that help businesses capture, analyze, and act on phone call data. Their platform offers AI‑driven insights, call recording, transcription, and integration with CRM and marketing tools, enabling improved customer experience and sales performance across industries such as automotive, healthcare, and real estate.
c.name: Convirza

c.description: Conviva is the streaming-media and digital-experience analytics company behind Experience-Centric Operations (ECO) — a real-time, full-census operational data platform that stitches client-side telemetry from its Sensor SDKs into stateful, per-viewer experience analytics for video streamers, broadcasters and app publishers. Its Pulse portal is fronted by a public REST surface at api.conviva.com covering Metrics V3, Sessions V3, AI Alerts, Bulk Filters, Precision Policy, PII Opt-Out and Validation Timeline, plus Conviva Connect session-summary data feeds (S3/GCS/Snowflake/BigQuery/SFTP), alert webhooks, and two hosted OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol servers (mcp.conviva.com for VSI/DPI metrics, alerts and sessions; dpi-mcp.conviva.com for Context Center, Nexa analysis, metric query and session replay). Conviva publishes a large first-party SDK estate — JavaScript/npm, Android/Maven, iOS/CocoaPods+SPM, React Native, Node and Python agent SDKs — and a Claude plugin marketplace carrying three provider-authored Agent Skills for its DPI MCP server. Authentication across the REST surface is HTTP Basic with a client-id/client-secret API key pair generated in Pulse API Management.
c.name: Conviva

c.description: Convoke is building an AI-native operating system for the biopharmaceutical industry. Founded in 2024 and based in South San Francisco, the platform unifies fragmented internal knowledge, workflows, and external data into a continuously updating workspace, codifies the decision logic behind high-stakes choices, and generates critical deliverables such as competitive intelligence briefs, portfolio strategy analyses, market research, and scientific manuscripts across the drug development lifecycle. Convoke serves biopharma teams working in business development, competitive intelligence, portfolio strategy, market research, and medical affairs. The company raised an $8.6M seed round co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Dimension. As of this profile, Convoke publishes a public marketing and company site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.
c.name: Convoke

c.description: Convosight provides an enterprise video social intelligence platform that analyzes social video and comments across channels to deliver consumer insights for brand, marketing, research, and product development teams. It serves large brands that need multilingual, multi‑channel video analysis to inform decisions.
c.name: Convosight

c.description: Convoy is an open-source, cloud-native webhooks gateway used to securely ingest, persist, debug, deliver, and manage events. It positions itself as "the complete solution for secure, scalable, and reliable webhook delivery," covering both outbound (sending) and inbound (receiving) webhooks with retries, payload signing, fan-out, rate limiting, message broker ingestion, and customer-facing portals. Convoy is offered as a self-hosted open-source project (Elastic License v2.0, with the OpenAPI spec under MPL 2.0) and a fully managed cloud service in US and EU regions.
c.name: Convoy

c.description: Conxai (CONXAI Technologies GmbH) is a Munich, Germany-based startup building a no-code, agentic AI platform purpose-built for the construction and AEC (architecture, engineering, construction) industry. The modular platform contextualizes fragmented project-lifecycle data — site photos and video, documents, CAD drawings and tender submissions — and turns it into actionable knowledge across three areas: transparency, automation, and knowledge management. Marquee products include SiteLens (real-time construction-site camera analysis, progress tracking and firestop detection) and DocNostic (document extraction, classification and workflow automation). Conxai exposes several REST APIs — a Customer/SiteLens API, a Docnostic document API, a Firestop API and a Production Tracking API — documented on ReadMe and secured with an X-Api-Key header (Docnostic also accepts a JWT bearer token). The company is backed by Earlybird, Pi Labs, Cemex Ventures, Zacua Ventures, Capricorn Partners and BayBG Venture Capital.
c.name: Conxai

c.description: ConXtech is a Pleasanton, California structural steel subcontractor that designs, fabricates, delivers and erects prefabricated steel building frames for commercial construction. Its ConX Systems product line — the XL-400 and XR-200 chassis — uses patented collar-and-column connection technology and AISC 358 seismic prequalification to erect frames the company reports are three to five times faster than traditional steel erection, across healthcare, data center, retail, office, education, high-density residential, hospitality, industrial and government projects totalling more than 20 million square feet. ConXtech is a private company; its equity trades on secondary markets. It sells a physical building system, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable contract.
c.name: ConXtech

c.description: CONXUS Communications, Inc. was a United States advanced-messaging and narrowband-PCS carrier, headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, that operated the Pocketalk voice-messaging and Pocketext text-messaging services built on Motorola's InFLEXion protocol. Formed in the mid-1990s from a group of one-way paging providers and backed by strategic and financial investors, the company offered wireless voice messaging, guaranteed message delivery, automatic acknowledgment of receipt, error correction, longer messages, and subscriber-originated replies across roughly ten U.S. markets. Conxus filed for bankruptcy protection in May 1999 and ceased network operations on August 27, 1999, affecting an estimated 80,000-100,000 subscribers. The company is defunct and publishes no API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio record only.
c.name: CONXUS Communications

c.description: Coohua (酷划在线) is a Beijing-based Chinese mobile advertising company founded in 2014 and backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It pioneered the incentive- and lock-screen-advertising model in China, rewarding users with cash for unlocking their screens, reading content, and engaging with ads. Its flagship products include Coohua Lockscreen (酷划锁屏) and the Tao News (淘新闻) reading-rewards app, serving advertisers across internet, finance, automotive, and e-commerce verticals. At its peak Coohua captured a majority share of China's lock-screen advertising market and returned billions of yuan in cash rewards to users annually. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification could be found during enrichment; advertising business is transacted through a sales contact (sale@coohua.com) on the 广告合作 page rather than through any self-serve or programmatic surface. The company does maintain a GitHub organization (github.com/coohua-dev) publishing CocoaPods spec repositories for the iOS modules behind its two apps, but every podspec resolves its source to an unreachable internal gitlab.coohua.com host, so none of it is consumable by a third party. This profile is retained as a company/provider record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.
c.name: coohua

c.description: Cookie6f31 is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Cookie6f31

c.description: Cookies is a stub company listed in the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. It currently lacks a public-facing website or documented APIs. The profile aims to gather identity information, potential documentation links, and future API specifications as they become available. No concrete product details are present at this time, and the company appears to be a placeholder for further enrichment.
c.name: Cookies

c.description: CookieYes is a Google-certified consent management platform (CMP) that helps websites comply with privacy laws such as GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA and POPIA. It provides customizable cookie consent banners, an automatic cookie scanner with AI-based classification, geo-targeted banner display, consent logging and export, multilingual support, Google Consent Mode v2 and IAB TCF v2.2 compliance, and policy generators. CookieYes ships apps and plugins for WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Webflow and any HTML site, plus a client-side JavaScript consent API (getCkyConsent, performBannerAction). CookieYes runs an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server and a hosted, OAuth-gated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agent access. Part of Mozilor Technologies, it is used by over 1.5 million websites.
c.name: Cookieyes

c.description: CookinGenie is a startup that aims to simplify home cooking by providing AI‑driven recipe recommendations, meal planning tools, and grocery list automation. The platform integrates with smart kitchen appliances and offers a mobile app for personalized cooking experiences. While the company is listed in the API Evangelist harvest backlog, its public web presence is currently minimal, and no dedicated website could be located during profiling.
c.name: CookinGenie

c.description: Cooklist is an agentic commerce platform purpose-built for grocery and retail. It provides retailer-native AI shopping assistants that plan meals, run solution-first agentic search over live catalog and inventory, assemble cart-ready bundles, and execute verified cart operations against the retailer's system of record. Founded in 2018, Cooklist powers the first agentic AI shopping experience launched by Kroger (the Kroger AI Meal Assistant, live since December 2025) and integrates with 15+ retailer catalogs. Retailers embed a drop-in JavaScript SDK that talks to Cooklist over HTTPS (GraphQL) and WSS (real-time streaming); a B2B Partner API (API key or JWT auth, per-organization field allowlists), authenticated webhooks, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface expose real-time retail inventory and pricing to third-party LLMs such as ChatGPT and Gemini for off-site agentic commerce.
c.name: Cooklist

c.description: CookUnity is the first chef-to-consumer meal marketplace, connecting award-winning chefs with food lovers nationwide. Chefs craft restaurant-quality meals in local kitchens and deliver them fresh, ready to heat in two minutes, with more than 300 rotating dishes spanning a wide range of cuisines and dietary options (keto, vegan, paleo, high-protein, gluten-free and more). Subscribers choose four to sixteen meals per week on a flexible weekly plan. The company also runs a chef marketplace onboarding culinary entrepreneurs, a CookUnity for Business program for corporate, healthcare and education clients, and gift cards. CookUnity is a consumer brand and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, identity, and domain-security surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and Insight Partners.
c.name: Cookunity

c.description: CoolPlanet is an enterprise energy-management and decarbonisation software company. Its platform, CoolPlanetOS, centralises real-time energy data across multi-site industrial estates, applies AI-driven anomaly detection and efficiency insights, benchmarks performance across facilities, and automates energy and compliance reporting. CoolPlanet pairs the software with consulting and on-site execution services to help manufacturing, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, commercial real estate, mining and shipping enterprises cut energy costs and carbon emissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). No public developer API surface is currently published.
c.name: Cool Planet

c.description: Coolant (Coolant Climate, Inc.) is a climate-technology startup building AI-powered forest monitoring and carbon measurement from consumer-grade drone imagery. Its "3D spatial intelligence" platform reconstructs high-resolution 3D forest models from ordinary drone footage (DJI Mini, Mavic) and applies computer vision to measure biomass, tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), tree counts, species, and growth rates — delivering LiDAR-grade accuracy at a fraction of the cost. The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.
c.name: Coolant

c.description: Cooleaf is an employee engagement, recognition, and rewards platform built by ITA Group that helps HR and people leaders create lasting engagement across their organizations. The platform lets teams recognize peers, reward performance and KPIs, celebrate milestones and anniversaries, run pulse surveys and challenges, deliver training and programming, and surface engagement analytics through manager dashboards. Cooleaf meets employees where they already work by embedding recognition into Slack and Microsoft Teams and syncing people data through connectors like Zapier and Workday. Cooleaf is delivered as a closed SaaS product with a hosted web application and login; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference, so this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and the integration surface it exposes to customers rather than a developer program.
c.name: Cooleaf

c.description: Coolenergy is a Boulder‑based clean‑energy technology company that develops and commercializes the ThermoHeart Engine™, a low‑temperature Stirling‑cycle engine that converts waste heat into electricity. Founded in 2006, the firm targets industrial exhaust, stationary power generation, and pollution control applications, offering solutions that improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions. Coolenergy provides engineering services, licensing, and turnkey installations for customers in the United States and Europe, aiming to accelerate the adoption of sustainable power conversion technologies.
c.name: Coolenergy

c.description: Cooler Heads Care, Inc. is a San Diego medical device company founded in 2018 by Kate Dilligan that makes Amma, an FDA-cleared Portable Scalp Cooling System (PSCS) used to reduce chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Amma circulates chilled fluid through a fitted cap to constrict scalp blood vessels and limit chemotherapy delivery to hair follicles, and is designed to be portable enough that patients can keep cooling outside the infusion chair. The company sells to infusion centers and oncology practices and publishes patient, provider, reimbursement and training material on its own site. It ships no developer API, SDK or public API documentation; its only machine-readable public surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served from its own host.
c.name: Cooler Heads

c.description: CoolerX — formerly Cooler Screens — is an in-store retail media and merchandising technology company that turns cooler doors, endcaps, checkout coolers and pharmacy fixtures into IoT-connected digital screens. The platform pairs an AI "Intent Engine" for contextual targeting and conversion-funnel optimization with a Dynamic Content Engine for creative optimization, alongside campaign management, real-time measurement, and a data integration hub for product, price, promotion and context data. It is deployed with retailers including Kroger, Walgreens, Giant Eagle's GetGo, Chevron and Western Union, and is built on Microsoft Azure with NVIDIA, BOE, LG, Samsung and Foxconn as hardware and infrastructure partners. CoolerX sells to retailers and brands through a demo and sales motion; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CoolerX

c.description: Coolfire Solutions provides flexible work management software designed to defeat operational chaos across industries such as logistics, telecommunications, energy, and government. Their flagship Coolfire Core platform enables teams to coordinate tasks, workflows, and communications, offering features for field service management, enterprise collaboration, and real-time situational awareness.
c.name: Coolfire Solutions

c.description: Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable Platform-as-a-Service alternative to Vercel, Heroku, Netlify, and Railway. It lets you deploy static sites, APIs, full-stack applications, databases, and 280+ one-click services to any SSH-accessible server (VPS, bare-metal, Raspberry Pi, EC2, Hetzner, DigitalOcean) while keeping every configuration value, deployment, and dataset on infrastructure you own.
c.name: Coolify

c.description: Coolmate is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Coolmate

c.description: Cool Planet Labs is a climate‑focused organization that leverages massive‑scale online collaboration to address climate change. Through educational initiatives, community‑building tools, and the EarthAtlas solution library, it inspires and mobilizes young people worldwide to share, discover, and implement innovative climate solutions. The nonprofit’s mission centers on fostering a sea change in environmental action via web‑based platforms and interactive applications.
c.name: Coolplanetlabs

c.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.
c.name: Coolso

c.description: Profile for Cooper in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 848).
c.name: Cooper

c.description: Smithsonian Design Museum
c.name: Cooper Hewitt

c.description: Cooper Standard Holdings is a global automotive supplier headquartered in Northville, Michigan, that designs, engineers, manufactures, and sells sealing systems, fuel and brake delivery systems, and fluid transfer systems for global automotive original equipment manufacturers including Ford, General Motors, Stellantis, and Volkswagen. The company operates in approximately 20 countries with around 32,000 employees and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CPS. Cooper Standard does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence centers on corporate, investor, supplier, and careers websites.
c.name: Cooper Standard Holdings

c.description: Cooper Tire & Rubber Company is an American manufacturer of replacement tires for passenger cars, light trucks, SUVs, and commercial vehicles, founded in 1914 and headquartered in Findlay, Ohio. Cooper was acquired by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company in June 2021 and now operates as a subsidiary, retaining the Cooper brand alongside Goodyear. The Cooper brand portfolio covers all-season, winter, all-terrain, and sport performance tires distributed through retailers and dealers worldwide. Cooper Tire does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence is consumer-facing tire selection, retailer locators, and post-purchase tire registration.
c.name: Cooper Tire & Rubber

c.description: Coople is a technology-driven workforce solutions provider that connects businesses with flexible, skilled talent across various sectors such as healthcare, retail, logistics, hospitality, and office environments. Their platform enables companies to quickly find, hire, and manage temporary staff, offering services like payrolling, workforce planning, and compliance support. Coople leverages a smart digital platform to streamline recruitment, onboarding, and workforce management, helping businesses adapt to fluctuating labor needs while providing workers with flexible job opportunities.
c.name: Coople

c.description: Coordinate (CoordinateHQ) is a client project-execution platform and branded client portal for client-facing businesses — agencies, professional services, and B2B onboarding teams. It turns repeatable workflows into automated, interactive projects with tasks, task groups, goals, progress reports, forms, eSignatures, time tracking, and in-project chat, while giving each client a simple password-free portal. Coordinate exposes a REST API (base https://app.coordinatehq.com/api/v1) for creating and syncing projects, tasks, groups, stakeholders, goals, comments, and organizations, an /entity export firehose for bulk sync, and a webhook API for real-time create/update events, alongside bi-directional Zapier integrations. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Coordinate's published API reference.
c.name: Coordinate

c.description: Coorpacademy is a Swiss-French corporate digital-learning platform, founded in 2013 and acquired by Australian edtech Go1 in April 2022, now marketed as "Coorpacademy by Go1". It sells a B2B SaaS learning experience platform built on inverted-pedagogy, gamified micro-learning: brand-scoped learning portals, a course and certification catalogue, skills taxonomies, learner progression and adaptive review, battles/leaderboards, and HR analytics. The platform is fronted by a public Swagger UI at api.coorpacademy.com that indexes fourteen internal-but-publicly-documented REST services — content, platform/brand management, progression, progression aggregations, SCIM 2.0 user provisioning, SCORM and SCORM-content players, H5P, transactional email, mobile, review mode, media, external upload and PDF rendering. Access to every service is key-gated; there is no self-serve developer signup, no published pricing, and no partner developer portal, so the specifications are the only machine-readable public surface.
c.name: Coorpacademy

c.description: Project Copacetic (Copa) is an open source command line tool that patches container images directly using BuildKit, without requiring a full image rebuild. Copa parses vulnerability scan reports from Trivy and other scanners, applies the corresponding OS package updates via the appropriate package manager (apt, apk, dnf, tdnf, yum, zypper), and produces a new container image with a patched layer. Copa supports multi-platform images, distroless images, and custom scanner plugins through the Vulnerability Exchange (VEX) and pluggable scanner interface.
c.name: Copa (Project Copacetic)

c.description: Copado is an AI-powered DevOps platform for Salesforce and other low-code SaaS clouds. It provides CI/CD, release management, version control, automated robotic testing, data deployment, and security & governance for enterprise Salesforce delivery teams. Copado extends its platform through a Developer Hub (Functions, Actions, Job Engine, custom pipelines), a REST Actions API and Webhooks API, an official Salesforce-CLI plugin, and a Python AI SDK. The company is backed by Insight Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and GDPR-aligned security posture.
c.name: Copado

c.description: Copan Systems was an enterprise data-storage company founded in 2002 and based in Longmont, Colorado, known for pioneering MAID (Massive Array of Idle Disks) technology for long-term persistent and archival storage. Its Enterprise MAID architecture powered down idle disks to cut power, cooling, and floor-space costs in the data center. Backed by Battery Ventures and other investors, the company raised more than $100 million in venture funding before filing for bankruptcy in 2009; SGI acquired its assets in 2010 (that storage lineage now sits within Hewlett Packard Enterprise). The company is defunct and operates no public developer surface, API, or documentation, so there is nothing to enrich in the API Evangelist artifact pipeline.
c.name: Copan Systems

c.description: Fortune 1000 company Copart. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Copart

c.description: Copernicus is the European Union’s Earth observation programme, providing free, open access to satellite data and services that monitor the environment, climate, and security. It delivers a wide range of products from Sentinel satellites, enabling applications in agriculture, disaster management, climate change, and more. The programme supports public authorities, businesses, and researchers with timely, high‑resolution imagery and analytics, fostering innovation and sustainable development across Europe and globally.
c.name: Copernicus

c.description: The EU Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS), operated by Mercator Ocean International, provides free and open access to authoritative information on the state of the global ocean and European regional seas. The service delivers ocean physical and biogeochemical data through multiple APIs covering temperature, salinity, sea level, currents, sea ice, and marine ecosystem variables from satellite observations, in situ measurements, and numerical model reanalysis and forecast products. Data can be accessed programmatically via the Copernicus Marine Toolbox (Python API and CLI), the OGC-compliant Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) for visualization, and the Catalogue Service for the Web (CSW) for product discovery. All services require a free Copernicus Marine account, except the CSW which is fully open, and there are no data volume quotas or download limits.
c.name: Copernicus Marine

c.description: Coperniq is an AI-powered operating system for residential and commercial contractors across solar, storage, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and roofing trades, consolidating sales, project management, service operations, dispatch, and cashflow into one system. Its REST API (https://api.coperniq.io/v1) lets developers automate projects, opportunities, accounts, contacts, sites, assets, work orders, forms, quotes, invoices, bills, payments, and more, with API-key authentication, page-based pagination, per-key rate limiting, and outbound automation webhooks. Coperniq was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital (sector: climate) and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its public developer surface.
c.name: Coperniq

c.description: Copia provides enterprise fax server software and Fax over IP solutions, enabling organizations to deploy, control, and integrate high‑volume fax workflows on‑premises, virtualized or hosted environments. With over 37 years in business, Copia’s platform supports SIP/T.38, PBX integration, email‑to‑fax, and custom application interfaces, offering flexible deployment, cost control, and data security for enterprises across various industries.
c.name: Copia

c.description: Copia Global was a Kenyan B2C e-commerce and last-mile distribution company founded by Tracey Turner and Jonathan Lewis to serve middle- and low-income consumers across rural and peri-urban Africa. Rather than a consumer website, it ran an agent-network model in which customers placed catalog orders through local agents using mobile and USSD technology, and Copia processed, aggregated, and delivered goods within days. Backed by investors including DCVC and Goodwell, the company raised a $50M Series C in 2022 to expand, but suspended Uganda operations in 2023, entered administration in May 2024, and was subsequently placed into liquidation. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or specification; its primary domain now resolves to a parked page. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead for network coverage.
c.name: Copia Global

c.description: Copify is a digital marketing agency that provides services such as paid media, SEO, web design, social media marketing, content creation, and e‑commerce marketing to businesses across various industries. It offers consulting and campaign management to help clients increase conversions, grow revenue, and manage ad spend.
c.name: Copify

c.description: GitHub Copilot is an AI‑powered coding assistant that suggests whole lines or functions in real time, integrates with popular IDEs, and offers a CLI for automation. It helps developers write code faster, learn new APIs, and adopt best practices, with support for multiple programming languages and enterprise governance features.
c.name: Copilot

c.description: copilot-instructions.md is a GitHub Copilot custom instructions file placed at .github/copilot-instructions.md in a repository. It provides repository-specific guidance and preferences that GitHub Copilot Chat, Copilot in the IDE, and the Copilot coding agent automatically inject into prompts when working in the repository. The file is plain Markdown in natural language, helping the AI understand build, test, validation, framework, and style conventions so it can produce code that is consistent with the project's expectations and reduce pull request rejections caused by avoidable lint, CI, or convention failures.
c.name: copilot-instructions.md

c.description: Copilot4a49 is a stub company identified in the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. It currently has no publicly verified website or detailed public information. The entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment once authoritative sources become available, ensuring the network can track its eventual API offerings and corporate details.
c.name: Copilot4a49

c.description: CopilotIQ is a Nashville, Tennessee remote patient monitoring and telehealth company, founded in 2021, that delivers AI-driven chronic-condition management to seniors and Medicare members living with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Through connected in-home devices, predictive analytics, and clinical automation it captures daily biometric readings and pairs them with weekly nurse coaching to catch anomalies early, reduce hospitalizations, and lower costs for health plans and providers. In October 2024 CopilotIQ merged with in-home care company Biofourmis. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. CopilotIQ operates as a clinical care service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface.
c.name: CopilotIQ

c.description: CopilotKit builds AI‑powered developer tools that streamline the creation, testing, and deployment of AI agents. Their platform offers a suite of components—including a VS Code extension, mock infrastructure, oversight dashboards, knowledge‑base search, and intelligent support outpost—to help developers integrate large language models into applications with reliable tooling, observability, and rapid iteration.
c.name: CopilotKit

c.description: Copincommunications, also known as COP Communications, Inc., is a Glendale, California‑based company offering one‑to‑one marketing services through print, web, email, and SMS. It provides personalized brochures, catalogs, postcards, and other direct‑mail materials, leveraging customer data to create customized print communications. The firm emphasizes variable data printing, short‑run on‑demand production, and a range of stock options for high‑quality marketing collateral.
c.name: Copincommunications

c.description: CoPlane is a San Francisco-based enterprise software company building an AI-native intelligent operations layer for the back office of essential enterprises. The platform combines AI agents with deterministic business rules on a durable workflow engine to automate high-friction, exception-heavy processes across finance, procurement, and operations — including invoice intake, PO matching, vendor onboarding, cash application, billing, collections, bank and account reconciliation, close processes, and variance analysis. CoPlane runs inside the customer's own cloud environment and interoperates with existing enterprise systems (SAP, Workday, Coupa) across Source-to-Pay, Quote-to-Cash, and Record-to-Report workflows without a rip-and-replace migration. Founded in 2024, the company raised a $14M seed round in November 2025 led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Stripe, Optum Ventures, and Terrain. This profile was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; CoPlane does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.
c.name: CoPlane

c.description: Copley provides an AI Operating System for Demand Engineering, enabling companies to automate and optimize their marketing, sales, and product development processes through AI-driven analysis, planning, creation, and iteration of campaigns. The platform connects data from CRM, ad platforms, and analytics to generate actionable insights and continuously improve performance across channels.
c.name: Copley

c.description: Copper is a CRM platform built natively for Google Workspace, designed to help teams cultivate enduring client relationships through purposeful collaboration. Copper offers a RESTful Developer API providing programmatic access to People, Companies, Leads, Opportunities, Projects, Tasks, Activities, Webhooks, and related resources for CRM integration and automation.
c.name: Copper

c.description: Copper (Copper Banking) is a Seattle-based consumer fintech founded in 2019 by Eddie Behringer and Stefan Berglund that began as a teen banking app and debit card built on the Synapse banking-as-a-service platform. After Synapse's collapse Copper abruptly discontinued its bank deposit accounts and debit cards in May 2024 and repositioned as a financial-empowerment and earning app, where members earn cash and gift-card rewards through cash back, surveys, receipt scanning, games and referrals, alongside financial-literacy content, guides and in-school workshops. Copper publishes no public developer portal, documentation or API specification; the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for a Model Context Protocol endpoint at mcp.getcopper.com.
c.name: Copper Banking

c.description: Copper Cow Coffee is a specialty Vietnamese coffee brand founded by Debbie, a Vietnamese‑Californian entrepreneur. The company sources climate‑resilient beans from Vietnam’s first organic‑certified farms, pays farmers double market rates, and blends coffee with real herbs and spices for unique flavors. Their e‑commerce store offers coffee, creamers, seasonal flavors, and subscription plans, emphasizing sustainability, zero‑fake ingredients, and AAPI woman‑owned leadership.
c.name: Copper Cow Coffee

c.description: Copper Financial provides a CRM platform for service‑based businesses, offering tools to organize contacts, track deals, manage projects, automate workflows, and generate custom reports. The solution integrates with popular apps such as Google Workspace and supports mobile access, aiming to streamline sales and customer relationship processes for agencies, consulting firms, and other service industries.
c.name: Copper Financial

c.description: Copper Mountain Networks was a telecommunications equipment maker founded in 1996 by Mark Handzel and Joe Markee that led the 1990s DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) wave in North America, building central-office DSL concentrators (the CopperEdge platform) and customer-premises modems that delivered high-speed broadband over existing copper telephone lines. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and InterWest, held its IPO in 1999, weathered the telecom downturn of 2001, and was acquired by Tut Systems in 2005 (later absorbed into Motorola in 2007). It shipped hardware and network equipment, not a public web/developer API; the company is defunct and operates no live developer platform today.
c.name: Copper Mountain Network

c.description: Copper is an institutional digital asset infrastructure provider headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, offering custody, prime services and collateral management to hedge funds, trading firms, exchanges, ETP providers, foundations and miners. Its Copper Platform API is a REST API over portfolios (called "accounts" in the UI), wallets, orders, transfers, withdrawals, staking, agency and bilateral lending, and ClearLoop — Copper's off-exchange settlement and collateral network that lets clients trade on connected exchanges while assets remain in custody. The API authenticates with an API key plus a per-request HMAC-SHA256 signature, publishes OpenAPI 3.1 specifications and a Postman collection, and offers a webhook system for real-time order, deposit, withdrawal, ClearLoop and address-book events.
c.name: Copper.co

c.description: Copperlane is an AI-native mortgage loan origination platform founded in 2025 by Brianna Lin and Athan Zhang and backed by Y Combinator (W26 batch). Its AI agent, Penny, behaves like a real loan officer: it guides borrowers through intake, pulls and reads borrower documents, verifies loan eligibility in real time, answers borrower questions live, and generates Letters of Explanation, delivering cleaner files to human loan officers so they can focus on closing loans instead of chasing paperwork. The San Francisco company raised a $4.1M seed round to modernize a mortgage origination process that remains largely manual. Copperlane is currently a demo-request business application and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
c.name: Copperlane

c.description: CopThis is the company behind Merchbar, the official online merchandise retailer for musicians and artists, selling authenticated band and artist merch (vinyl, apparel, accessories) across thousands of artist stores. CopThis operates the Merchbar Partner API — a REST contract that merchandise and fulfillment partners implement so Merchbar can list a partner's stores and merchandise and place, track, update, and cancel orders on behalf of Merchbar customers. The API uses HTTP Basic authentication over HTTPS, a JSON envelope with a top-level data key and pagination for collections, URI-path versioning (v1), and an error envelope for 4xx/5xx responses. CopThis is a portfolio company of 500 Global.
c.name: CopThis

c.description: Copy.ai provides AI‑powered content generation, workflow automation, and marketing tools for businesses. Its platform offers copy generation, AI‑image captioning, workflow templates, and integrations that help teams create sales, marketing, and operational content at scale. The service includes a suite of AI agents, customizable brand voice, and data‑driven insights, positioning it as a comprehensive solution for modern GTM teams.
c.name: Copy.ai

c.description: Copyleaks provides AI-powered plagiarism detection and content authenticity solutions for businesses, educators, and developers. Their platform offers text, image, and video plagiarism checking, deepfake detection, and content moderation tools, with API access for integration into LMS, CMS, and custom applications. Copyleaks serves a global customer base across education, media, and enterprise sectors, emphasizing AI-driven accuracy and compliance.
c.name: Copyleaksplagiarismchecker

c.description: COR (COR Global Ltd., projectcor.com) is an AI-powered management platform for advertising and creative agencies that calculates and forecasts project profitability while managing finances, resources, projects, tasks, and time tracking in one real-time workspace. COR publishes a REST API (JSON or XML) for projects, tasks, hours, clients, contracts, transactions, teams, users, and more, a separate Resource Allocation API, and an official hosted MCP server so AI clients can operate a workspace with natural language. Backed by 500 Global.
c.name: COR

c.description: Cora is a Brazilian digital bank (conta PJ) for small and medium businesses, offering fee-free business checking, Pix, boletos, transfers, payment initiation and financial management. Its developer platform exposes REST APIs for registered boleto and carnê issuance, Pix QR code generation, account data, balance and statement queries, payment and transfer initiation (including DARF and GPS tax payments), webhook notifications, and municipal service invoice (NFS-e) issuance. Cora offers two integration modalities — Direct Integration (mutual-TLS certificate plus OAuth2 client-credentials) and Cora Partnership — with a Stage sandbox for testing. Backed by QED Investors and Ribbit Capital.
c.name: Cora

c.description: Coral is the Solana developer platform company (originally Coral / coral-xyz) behind Anchor, the most widely used framework for writing Solana Sealevel smart-contract programs. Anchor provides a Rust eDSL, an IDL/codegen toolchain, TypeScript and Rust clients, the anchor CLI (via the Anchor Version Manager, avm), and testing tooling that abstract away Solana program boilerplate. Coral also built Backpack, an application-first crypto wallet for executable NFTs (xNFTs). The company raised a $20M strategic round led by FTX Ventures and Jump Crypto with participation from Multicoin Capital. This is a developer-framework / smart-contract-tooling provider rather than a REST/HTTP API provider, so REST-oriented artifacts (OpenAPI, OAuth scopes, webhooks) are not applicable; its developer surface is packages, a CLI, and framework documentation.
c.name: Coral

c.description: Coral is a local-first SQL runtime that gives AI agents governed, read-only access to data across any API, database, or file system using standard SQL — no custom integrations, ETL, or glue code required. Built by Phoebe Technology Limited (a GV / Google Ventures portfolio company incorporated in England and Wales, formerly branded Phoebe at phoebe.ai), Coral translates SQL into API calls or file reads and returns a single result set, handling authentication, authorization, pagination, rate limiting, and schema mapping automatically. It ships 25+ bundled sources (GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Datadog, Linear, Sentry, Jira, Stripe, PagerDuty, Notion, Grafana, Confluence and more), supports cross-source SQL JOINs executed locally, and exposes the same runtime over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or a CLI. Coral is open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted so queries and data never leave your infrastructure, and ISO 27001:2022 certified / GDPR compliant.
c.name: Coral

c.description: Coralogix is a comprehensive observability platform that delivers real‑time log analytics, metrics, tracing, and AI‑driven insights. It enables developers, DevOps, and SRE teams to monitor applications, infrastructure, and services across cloud, on‑premise, and hybrid environments. Features include infinite data retention, customizable dashboards, alerting, OpenTelemetry support, and integrations with major cloud providers and third‑party tools, helping organizations ensure performance, reliability, and security at scale.
c.name: Coralogix

c.description: Coram AI is an AI-native unified physical security platform that brings video surveillance, access control, emergency management, and visitor verification into a single cloud system that works with existing IP cameras. Its Developer API offers programmatic access to cameras, camera groups, NVRs, locations, access-control doors and events, and firearm-detection alerts, plus bulk school-reunification roster imports. Features include natural-language AI video search, firearm and fall detection, license plate and facial recognition, tailgating alerts, and remote door unlock. Coram is backed by 8VC and Battery Ventures.
c.name: Coram Ai

c.description: Coravin is a consumer beverage-technology company best known for its wine preservation systems, which use a thin needle and inert argon gas to pour wine by the glass without pulling the cork, leaving the remaining wine unoxidized for weeks or months. Its product line spans the Timeless, Pivot, and Sparkling systems plus Pure argon capsules, sold direct-to-consumer and through retail and trade channels. Coravin does not operate a standalone public developer API; its direct storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes a real agent-native commerce surface — a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a hosted shopping MCP endpoint, and OIDC / OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata for Shopify Customer Accounts. Backed by Battery Ventures.
c.name: Coravin

c.description: Corbado is a passkey-first authentication platform that helps companies add WebAuthn passkeys to their products. The Corbado Backend API manages users, login identifiers, sessions, passkeys/credentials, and connect tokens, while passkey intelligence and analytics surface readiness, adoption, and per-user debugging for passwordless rollouts.
c.name: Corbado

c.description: Corca is an AI-native, collaborative workspace for mathematics — a browser-based editor that lets people write math naturally (without special syntax), run calculations in real time, and collaborate the way teams do in Figma or Google Docs. Typing keywords like "sum" or "integral" surfaces the right symbols and functions, documents import from and export to LaTeX, and built-in AI helps solve problems, manipulate expressions, and generate code without switching tools. It is used for lab research, lecture creation, team knowledge bases, and publishing academic work. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Corca raised a $7.8M round (led by NEA, with Bloomberg Beta, NVIDIA's NVentures, Daft Capital, Slow Ventures, Liquid 2, Path Ventures, and Mana Ventures). The product is a consumer/team SaaS application; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profile.
c.name: Corca

c.description: Corcentric provides cloud‑based financial solutions that help organizations reduce fleet costs, accelerate cash flow, and improve overall financial performance. Their offerings include fleet management, financing, and managed accounts receivable services, delivering industry‑leading efficiency and cost savings for B2B enterprises.
c.name: Corcentric

c.description: Cord * (Cord Project Inc.) was a consumer communication startup building simple, fast voice messaging that let people send short audio clips to one friend or broadcast to a whole group, delivered through iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by GV and Index Ventures, the New York based team was acquired by Spotify in 2015, where the product formed the foundation of a group exploring new ways people interact with audio; the standalone apps and service were subsequently wound down. The company never published a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record with no active API artifacts to enrich.
c.name: Cord *

c.description: Cord Project Inc. was a New York based startup founded around 2014 by former Google Creative Lab designers Thomas Gayno and Jeff Baxter. Its flagship product, Cord, was a voice messaging app that let people send short audio clips as a middle ground between texting and phone calls. The company raised seed funding from investors including Google Ventures, Greycroft, Lerer Hippeau, Metamorphic Ventures and Slow Ventures, and was acquired by Spotify in January 2016 to explore new ways of interacting with audio. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; this profile is retained as a Slow Ventures portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Cord Project

c.description: Cord0d3f is a stub entry created during the API Evangelist harvest process. No public website, documentation, or API endpoints have been identified for this entity. It remains a placeholder pending further discovery or verification of a legitimate online presence and associated services.
c.name: Cord0d3f

c.description: Cordial is a cross-channel marketing and customer data platform headquartered in San Diego, California, used by consumer brands to unify customer data and orchestrate personalized messaging across email, SMS/MMS, RCS, mobile app (push, in-app, mobile inbox), website, and any external channel reachable over REST. The platform combines a native customer data platform built on a document database, real-time journey orchestration, identity resolution, and the Cordial Edge AI suite of brand-specific predictive models. Cordial is API-first: a documented Swagger 2.0 REST API at api.cordial.io exposes 106 operations across 24 resource groups covering contacts, contact activities, orders, products, supplements, lists, attributes, batch messages, automation templates, orchestrations, data jobs, imports/exports, alerts, and analytics. Alongside REST it publishes a hosted Model Context Protocol server with 56 read tools over 17 domains, a first-party npm CLI, mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, React Native and Expo, an embedded JavaScript listener, configurable outbound webhooks, and an open-source cookbook of packaged Claude Agent Skills.
c.name: Cordial

c.description: Cordiomedical is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Cordiomedical

c.description: Cordis is a global medical device company specializing in interventional cardiology solutions. It offers a wide range of products such as drug‑eluting balloons, guidewires, sheaths, and stents for vascular procedures. The company’s website provides detailed product information, regulatory approvals, and corporate news, confirming its identity as a leading provider in the cardiovascular market.
c.name: Cordis

c.description: Corduro is a payments-as-a-service company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Southlake, Texas, offering a mobile, online, and point-of-sale payment platform for small businesses, enterprises, and organizations. Its platform enables merchants to accept credit-card and electronic-check payments, bill pay, recurring billing, text giving, and event and donation payments through a single intelligent payment gateway that is advertised to reduce processing fees by 20% or more. Corduro bundles eCommerce, Engage, Events, Text Giving, and Developer Tools products, provides embeddable iFrame and API-based payment integrations, and markets PCI compliance as a managed capability. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and enriched from the company's public web presence; Corduro publishes no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or API reference, gating developer/API access behind sales contact.
c.name: Corduro
