c.description: Core & Main is a leading specialty distributor of water, wastewater, storm drainage, and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, contractors, and engineers across the United States. As a Fortune 500 company, Core & Main operates more than 320 branch locations and provides products and services for water infrastructure, geosynthetics, fusible HDPE pipe, smart metering, fire protection, and erosion control.
c.name: Core & Main

c.description: Core Automation provides automation solutions for enterprise workflows, integrating with various SaaS platforms to streamline processes such as data synchronization, task orchestration, and reporting. The company focuses on delivering low-code tools and APIs that enable businesses to automate repetitive tasks, improve efficiency, and reduce operational costs. Core Automation’s offerings include connectors, webhooks, and a developer-friendly API suite designed for rapid integration and scalability across cloud environments.
c.name: Core Automation

c.description: Core Labs is an early-stage product studio based in New York City building the future of professional identity and connection for the digital economy. Founded by serial entrepreneur Ajay Rajani (previously Grovo and Tala), the company operates in rapid-experimentation mode, incubating and testing consumer and productivity products. Its portfolio includes Mural, a simple portfolio-building tool for product managers, marketers, and digital workers that turns shared URLs into rich embeds; Core, a peer-and-expert mentorship platform used in university entrepreneurship programs and fellowships; and Makeshop, an on-demand marketplace for creative services. Core Labs is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform.
c.name: Core Labs

c.description: Core Loop is a game studio founded in 2020 by Vincenzo Alagna and Dan Chao, veterans of Machine Zone, GREE, and Funzio, building a modern cross-platform MMO at the intersection of massively multiplayer online games and web3. The studio is developing an AI-directed, dynamic world that evolves based on the actions of the community, with a blockchain-based, player-driven virtual economy in which participants truly own the assets they craft or earn and can potentially make a living in the game long-term. The game targets both PC and mobile. Core Loop raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Galaxy Digital, Block.one, 1Up Ventures, Dune Ventures, and others, and operates as a remote-first team headquartered in Oakland, California. As a game studio, Core Loop does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so this profile is identity-only.
c.name: Core Loop

c.description: Core Loop Games is a game development studio focused on building the next generation of massively multiplayer online (MMO) experiences. The company emphasizes large‑scale social cooperation and innovative gameplay loops that engage players in persistent virtual worlds. Based in Oakland, California, Core Loop Games aims to reimagine how players interact and collaborate across expansive game universes.
c.name: Core Loop Games

c.description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.
c.name: Core-Mark Holding

c.description: Core10, Inc. is a U.S.-based fintech software development and API integration firm founded in 2016 by Lee Farabaugh and Jeff Martin, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee with delivery centers in Martin, Tennessee and Huntington, West Virginia, built on a domestic-outsourcing model it trademarked as Hereshore(R). Core10 wrote custom software, core-banking integrations and API layers for community banks, credit unions and fintechs, and acquired Accrue Technologies in 2021 to add a Salesforce-based digital lending, account opening and treasury onboarding platform. In January 2024 it spun its implementation practice out as Monarch, and the Core10 brand has since been retired: core10.io now 301-redirects to monarchfts.com, where Monarch operates as an Intapp DealCloud implementation, configuration and managed-services consultancy for private capital firms, while the Accrue platform trades independently at getaccrue.com under its own leadership. Core10 built API integrations for other companies for nearly a decade but never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of its own, and as of 2026-08-11 neither successor brand does either.
c.name: Core10

c.description: Corebridge Financial (formerly AIG Life and Retirement) is one of the largest and most established retirement and insurance solutions providers in the United States. Spun off from AIG in September 2022 in the largest IPO of that year, Corebridge provides retirement solutions, life insurance, fixed and variable annuities, and institutional products. The company is a leading retirement plan provider for K-12 schools, healthcare, government, higher education, and other not-for-profit institutions. Corebridge Financial does not currently publish a public developer API; participant and plan sponsor access is provided through dedicated portals.
c.name: Corebridge Financial

c.description: CoreChain Technologies provides a scalable, secure B2B payments network and supply chain finance solutions. With over $1 billion in payments processed, the platform integrates with major ERPs, offers working‑capital lines, and is SOC‑2 compliant, targeting enterprises seeking to reduce fraud, lower operating costs, and automate vendor payments.
c.name: CoreChain Technologies

c.description: CoreDNS is a CNCF graduated DNS server written in Go that serves as the default DNS service for Kubernetes clusters. It is flexible and extensible through a plugin architecture, supporting DNS-based service discovery, forwarding, caching, and integration with etcd, Kubernetes, and other backends. CoreDNS can serve as an authoritative DNS server or a recursive resolver, with HTTP plugins exposing health, readiness, and Prometheus metrics endpoints for Kubernetes operations.
c.name: CoreDNS

c.description: CoreEL Technologies (India) Private Limited, established in 1999, is a world‑class engineering and technology company offering high‑end electronic system‑level products and solutions for aerospace, defence, space and manufacturing sectors. The firm provides RF & microwave, hardware‑mixed‑signal, SoC/FPGA, software and mechanical engineering services, and operates globally from its Indian headquarters. It focuses on high‑end electronic system level products and solutions, serving aerospace and defence customers worldwide.
c.name: Coreel

c.description: CoRegen, Inc. (CoRegen Science) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Houston, Texas developing adoptive cell therapies for aggressive solid tumors. Its platform, licensed exclusively from the O'Malley Lab at Baylor College of Medicine, uses CRISPR gene editing to knock out the SRC-3 steroid receptor coactivator gene in regulatory T (Treg) cells, reprogramming them from immunosuppressors into tumor-killing effectors. The lead program, CRG-150, received FDA IND clearance for a first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial in advanced solid tumors, and the underlying science won the 2023 Cozzarelli Prize. CoRegen is a therapeutics organization, not a software company: it publishes a nine-page marketing and science site (about, the science, preclinical studies, pipeline, publications, leadership, news, careers, contact) and no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.
c.name: CoRegen

c.description: Corelayer is an AI-native platform for production software support and maintenance — an AI SRE / AI on-call engineer for engineering teams. It continuously monitors alerts, logs, infrastructure, and underlying data for issues, uses AI agents to investigate and root-cause incidents, and works to prevent them before they impact users. Purpose-built for complex, data-intensive, and regulated environments like finance, fintech, healthcare, and insurance, Corelayer connects to the whole production environment — code, databases, deployments, and observability — with on-prem/BYOC deployment, configurable PII masking, and confidential compute. It exposes a v1 REST API, a first-party CLI, an MCP server, an installable agent skill, custom-webhook ingestion, and a metrics SDK. Backed by Y Combinator (W26); operated by Sevvy AI, Inc.
c.name: Corelayer

c.description: Corelight is a network detection and response (NDR) company founded by the creators of the open-source Zeek (formerly Bro) network security monitor. Its Open NDR Platform transforms network traffic into high-fidelity security evidence — logs, alerts, and metadata — powering threat detection, hunting, investigation, and incident response across on-premises and cloud environments. Corelight Sensors expose a comprehensive RESTful API for remote configuration and control, driven by the open-source corelight-client command-line client, with a Fleet Manager for centralized fleet management. Backed by Accel and General Catalyst, Corelight is listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace (In Process, Moderate).
c.name: Corelight

c.description: CoreLink is a surgical device manufacturer specializing in the design and production of spinal implant systems. Founded in 2007, CoreLink designs and manufactures over 99% of its portfolio in-house, offering a broad range of cervical, lumbar, and minimally invasive spinal solutions. The company is based in St. Louis, Missouri and serves surgeons worldwide with integrated technology and training resources.
c.name: Corelink

c.description: CoreLogic — rebranded as Cotality in 2025 — is a property data and analytics company providing real estate, mortgage, tax, hazard, and climate-risk information across approximately 99% of U.S. residential properties plus operations in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Canada, Germany, and India. The company was taken private by Stone Point Capital and Insight Partners in June 2021 in a $6B transaction. The primary public developer surface is Trestle (trestle-documentation.corelogic.com / api.cotality.com), which delivers MLS listing, member, office, media, and team data via a RESO Web API 2.0 / OData 4.0 endpoint, a RETS 1.8 endpoint, and a Direct Web API for Matrix CRM and MLO (member loan officer) integrations. Most other Cotality data products — 360 Property Data, Climate Risk Analytics, Discovery Platform — are delivered through cloud data shares (AWS, Databricks, Google Cloud, Azure, Snowflake) and SFTP rather than self-service REST APIs and are gated behind enterprise sales.
c.name: CoreLogic (Cotality)

c.description: CoreLogic Australia — trading as Cotality since the 2025 global rebrand, and operating the RP Data platform through RP Data Pty Ltd — is the dominant independent property data, analytics and valuation provider in Australia and New Zealand. It sits in the middle of the Australian property value chain: it aggregates state land-registry and valuer-general records, agent and portal listing campaigns, auction results and rental campaigns into a single property spine, then sells that spine back to banks, mortgage brokers, valuers, insurers, agents and government. Its commercial products include the RP Data / RP Professional desktop, the IntelliVal automated valuation model, the CoreLogic Home Value Index, Cordell construction cost data, Cityscope commercial property data, and the PSX valuation ordering exchange. Its API posture is genuinely developer-facing but commercially licensed: a live Backstage-based Cotality Developer Portal at developer.corelogic.asia offers self-serve signup and self-serve creation of sandbox OAuth clients against a deliberately restricted evaluation dataset with request quotas, while every production API host in the *.api.cotality.com.au family answers 401 "Access token is missing" and requires a signed commercial data licence. Australia has no MLS and no RESO mandate — CoreLogic's RESO Web API and Data Dictionary certifications belong to Trestle, its United States MLS platform, not to this Australian surface. The Australian APIs are proprietary REST/JSON over an Apigee gateway with OAuth 2.0 client credentials; no OData $metadata, no RESO endpoint, and no RESO Universal Property Identifier appears anywhere in the Australian developer portal.
c.name: CoreLogic Australia

c.description: CoreMed (Beijing) Biomedical Research Co., Ltd. is a China-based contract research organization (CRO) founded in 2013 that provides clinical professional services for innovative cardiovascular medical devices and structural-heart products. Its services span animal testing, human clinical trials, data management, statistical analysis, and independent core-laboratory imaging analysis, and it was among the first domestic providers in China to run trials for interventional heart valves, LAA occluders, and bioresorbable scaffolds. Headquartered in Beijing with branches in Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Chengdu, CoreMed is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. This is a services/CRO company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface; its site (coremed.com.cn) was unreachable at enrichment time (connection refused, expired TLS cert).
c.name: coremed

c.description: Coremedic GmbH is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Radolfzell, Germany, with a subsidiary in Biel, Switzerland. Founded in 2012 as a spin‑out from the University of Bern, Coremedic develops minimally invasive treatments for mitral valve regurgitation, notably the ChordArt TMVr system. The company focuses on innovative cardiology solutions, holds EN ISO 13485 certification, and operates within the European medical technology market, offering detailed product information, clinical data, and contact resources through its website.
c.name: Coremedic

c.description: Coremedical Group provides travel nursing, medical staffing, and healthcare workforce solutions. It connects qualified nurses, therapists, and advanced practice providers with healthcare facilities across the United States, offering contract, permanent, and interim placement services. The company also delivers talent management, HR benefits, and specialized travel resources for healthcare professionals.
c.name: Coremedical

c.description: Coremedicaltechnology, operating as Shenzhen Core Medical Technology Co., Ltd., develops and manufactures advanced artificial heart and ventricular assist devices. Founded in 2016, the company focuses on high‑tech medical implants, offering products such as the Corheart® 6 fully magnetic‑levitation artificial heart, approved by China’s NMPA in 2023. It aims to provide comprehensive solutions for heart‑failure patients worldwide.
c.name: Coremedicaltechnology

c.description: Coremetrics was a web analytics software company founded in 1999 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. It delivered a cloud-based (SaaS) digital marketing analytics platform used by more than 2,100 online brands to capture and analyze visitor and shopper behavior across web, social, and mobile channels for marketing optimization, attribution, and personalization. Backed by Accel and other venture investors, Coremetrics was acquired by IBM in 2010 and folded into IBM Digital Analytics and the IBM Watson Marketing / Enterprise Marketing Management suite. The standalone coremetrics.com developer surface is no longer operational, and no live public API, documentation, or SDK could be found during enrichment.
c.name: Coremetrics

c.description: Coremins is a provider of water and wastewater infrastructure solutions, offering a broad portfolio that includes pipe, valves, fittings, fire protection, HDPE fusible piping, metering, storm drainage, geosynthetics, and treatment plant equipment. The company serves utilities and industrial customers across the United States, delivering products and services that support reliable water supply, efficient waste management, and resilient infrastructure. Coremins emphasizes sustainability, innovation, and comprehensive support throughout project lifecycles.
c.name: Coremins

c.description: CoreOS was a San Francisco-based container infrastructure company founded in 2013 that built a lightweight, automatically-updating Linux distribution (Container Linux, originally CoreOS Linux) and a family of now-foundational cloud-native open source projects: etcd (the distributed key-value store at the heart of Kubernetes), the Quay container registry, the Tectonic enterprise Kubernetes platform, the rkt container engine, flannel networking, Clair image-vulnerability scanning, and Ignition provisioning. Red Hat acquired CoreOS in January 2018 for approximately $250 million. Its technologies were folded into Red Hat's portfolio — Container Linux became Red Hat CoreOS and the community Fedora CoreOS, Tectonic merged into OpenShift, Quay continues as Red Hat Quay, and etcd and rkt were donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The company no longer operates independently; coreos.com redirects to Red Hat OpenShift. The github.com/coreos organization remains active as the upstream home for Fedora CoreOS components such as Ignition, Butane, and fleetlock.
c.name: CoreOS

c.description: Corepowerholdingspteltd, operating as Core Power, is a UK‑based engineering company developing ship‑based nuclear energy systems to provide reliable, low‑carbon power for maritime and remote industrial applications. The firm designs, integrates and deploys modular reactors, propulsion technologies and supporting infrastructure, aiming to accelerate the energy transition for shipping, offshore platforms and coastal communities. With a focus on safety, regulatory compliance and scalable solutions, Core Power combines expertise in nuclear engineering, marine architecture and clean‑tech innovation to deliver power where it is needed most.
c.name: Corepowerholdingspteltd

No verifiable domain or API information could be located despite attempts to locate an official website or documentation. This entry serves as a placeholder pending further discovery of the company's digital presence and API offerings.

c.description: Coreraintechnologies is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Coreraintechnologies

c.description: Corerateintelligence is a data aggregation and analytics company that provides corporate intelligence solutions to businesses and investors. It offers a platform that consolidates public and proprietary data sources, enabling users to conduct market research, competitive analysis, and risk assessment. The service includes dashboards, API access, and custom reporting tools designed to help clients make informed strategic decisions based on comprehensive corporate data insights.
c.name: Corerateintelligence

c.description: Coreshell (Coreshell Technologies, Inc.) is a San Leandro, California battery technology company founded in 2017 that develops silicon-anode lithium-ion battery cells built on low-cost, domestically sourced metallurgical-grade silicon instead of graphite or refined polysilicon. A proprietary nanolayer surface coating stabilizes the silicon anode, and the company has unveiled commercial-scale 60 Ah cells aimed at electric vehicles, defense platforms and stationary energy storage. Coreshell is a materials and cell manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or public code repository.
c.name: Coreshell

c.description: Coresignal is a data-as-a-service company providing access to public web data on companies, employees, and jobs through a suite of REST APIs. The platform aggregates and refines more than 4.5 billion data records covering 75M+ companies (with 500+ data fields), 865M+ employee profiles (300+ fields), and 461M+ job postings (85+ fields). Coresignal offers Multi-source, Clean, and Base data tiers across Company, Employee, and Jobs APIs, plus specialized real-time, employee posts, agentic search, and company enrichment endpoints. Authentication uses a single apikey HTTP header.
c.name: Coresignal

c.description: CoreStack is a multi-cloud governance and security platform that unifies FinOps (cost visibility, budgets, anomaly detection, rightsizing and commitment optimization), CloudOps (workload lifecycle, tagging, automation and self-service), SecOps/compliance (policy guardrails, posture management and continuous assessment against ISO, NIST, HIPAA, PCI DSS, CIS and the AWS Well-Architected Framework), and Graphion, its AI-native CNAPP layer covering SBOM, container findings and vulnerability intelligence, across AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Every one of those capabilities is exposed through the CoreStack External API — a Swagger 2.0 contract of 838 operations across 767 paths, published live at the API host — and, since 2026, through a hosted unified MCP server that surfaces 100 documented tools to AI clients over OAuth or API key headers.
c.name: CoreStack

c.description: CoreStory is an AI code intelligence platform that ingests large brownfield and legacy codebases and reverse-engineers a persistent understanding of how they work — generating product requirements (PRDs), technical specifications, dependency graphs, and business-rule extractions directly from source. That intelligence is served to architects, product managers, engineers, and AI coding agents (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Devin) to accelerate modernization, migration, maintenance, and developer onboarding. CoreStory exposes a REST API (Bearer/JWT via Clerk) and a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so agents can query project PRDs, tech specs, and codebase conversations directly. San Francisco based; raised a $32M Series A in October 2025.
c.name: CoreStory

c.description: Coretigo enables faster and more flexible manufacturing by providing high-performance machine digitalization, wireless connectivity and edge solutions for machine builders, system integrators and industrial equipment manufacturers. Their products increase flexibility, adaptivity, modularity, cost-effectiveness, productivity and reduce downtime.
c.name: Coretigo

c.description: Coretissuebioengineering, operating as CoreTissue BioEngineering Inc., is a Japan‑based deep‑tech medical‑device startup founded in 2016. It develops regenerative ligament implants for ACL reconstruction using proprietary decellularization technology, aiming to restore athletes’ performance quickly. The company runs clinical trials and plans commercial rollout of its tissue‑regenerated ligaments.
c.name: Coretissuebioengineering

c.description: Coretsu is an AI‑focused technology company that presents itself as a platform for leveraging artificial intelligence to expand human creativity and productivity. The site emphasizes a vision of empowering individuals and organizations with AI tools while acknowledging the responsibility that comes with such power. It highlights a commitment to innovation, a range of engineering roles, and a mission to keep humanity relevant in an AI‑driven future.
c.name: Coretsu

c.description: CoreView provides Microsoft 365 cyber resilience solutions for enterprises, offering tools for policy enforcement, configuration resilience, privilege management, and tenant segmentation. Their platform helps organizations secure, manage, and automate Microsoft 365 environments, delivering risk insights, backup, and compliance across thousands of settings.
c.name: CoreView

c.description: CoreView (formerly 4ward365) is an enterprise Microsoft 365 governance, security, and automation platform. It secures the configuration, identity, and access layers of Microsoft 365 tenants and provides delegated administration, license management, reporting, and workflow automation. CoreView exposes a Public API secured with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (client-credentials flow) through a regional API proxy, plus a CoreFlow Workflow API for triggering and monitoring automation runs. Datacenters are available across the EU, East US, Canada, UK, Australia, and US Government (FedRAMP) regions. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and enriched from CoreView's public developer documentation.
c.name: CoreView (FKA 4ward365)

CoreWeave's control plane is Kubernetes-native and exposes APIs for CKS clusters, Inference deployments and gateways, VPCs, Object Storage, and Sandbox control.

c.description: Corflow Therapeutics AG develops diagnostic and therapeutic solutions aimed at restoring healthy microvascular blood flow in patients suffering from microvascular obstruction, such as those experiencing heart attacks. The company’s vision is to be the leader in delivering innovative platforms that address critical microvascular needs across the human body, leveraging advanced imaging and drug delivery technologies to improve outcomes.
c.name: Corflowtherapeuticsag

c.description: Corgi is an AI-native, full-stack business insurance platform for startups, offering modular coverage (Commercial General Liability, Directors & Officers, Tech Errors & Omissions, Cyber, EPLI, and fiduciary) quoted in minutes. Founded in 2024 and based in San Francisco, Corgi is a licensed insurance carrier rather than a broker, underwriting and issuing policies directly with pricing tailored to a startup's stage (pre-seed, Series A, growth). Backed by Kindred Ventures and TCV, the company was reported as an AI insurance unicorn in 2026. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Kindred Ventures' portfolio; Corgi does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

c.description: Corillian Corporation was a leading provider of Internet banking software and services, headquartered in Hillsboro, Oregon. The company was formed in 1997 when CheckFree spun off InteractiveSolutions Corporation, and it went on to build the Corillian Voyager online banking platform used by many U.S. banks and credit unions for online banking, bill payment, and real-time financial services integration. Backed by Battery Ventures, Corillian became a public company and expanded through the acquisitions of InteliData Technologies (2005) and qbt Systems (2006). In February 2007 CheckFree agreed to acquire Corillian for approximately $245 million; CheckFree was itself acquired by Fiserv later that same year, after which the Corillian brand was retired. The company no longer operates independently and maintains no public API, developer portal, documentation, or other live developer surface.
c.name: Corillian

c.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.
c.name: Corio, Inc.

c.description: Coris is an AI platform for merchant and payment risk, providing modern risk infrastructure for vertical SaaS platforms, payment processors, ISOs, PayFacs, and sponsor banks. Its MerchantProfiler product returns 100+ structured data attributes on any business — pulled from Secretary of State records, online presence, customer reviews, website/content signals, adverse media, and operational data — to power faster, more accurate merchant onboarding, KYB, underwriting, and ongoing risk monitoring. The platform also spans transaction monitoring, AI risk agents, and managed risk workflows, exposed through both a no-code console and REST APIs so customers can automate the full merchant lifecycle. Founded in 2022 and based in Palo Alto, Coris is backed by Lux Capital, Exponent Founders Capital, and Y Combinator, and works with companies including GoFundMe, Kajabi, Clio, and Cherry. Developer documentation is published on a password-gated ReadMe portal; this profile was enriched from public surfaces (marketing site, status page, trust center, legal pages).

c.description: Cority is an enterprise Environmental, Health, Safety, and Quality (EHSQ) and sustainability software provider, founded in 1985 as Medgate and headquartered in Toronto, Canada. Its CorityOne platform converges occupational health, safety and incident management, industrial hygiene, environmental and ESG/sustainability reporting, quality, and audit/compliance management for more than 1,500 enterprise organizations worldwide, layered with its Cortex AI agents. Cority exposes RESTful integration through the Cority Enviance API (Swagger-documented), used to connect CorityOne with corporate and third-party systems under a Connectors license.
c.name: Cority

c.description: Corma is a SaaS license and access governance platform for modern IT teams that automates SaaS discovery, access reviews, provisioning, and deprovisioning. Recognized in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SaaS Management Platforms, Corma helps organizations centralize all applications in one place, identify shadow IT, and reduce software spend by 10 to 15 percent. Corma offers extensive native integrations with identity providers (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace), HR platforms (Workday, BambooHR, Personio), financial tools (Spendesk, Qonto, Pennylane, Agicap), and productivity and business tools (Slack, Notion, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk). A public developer API is not currently published.
c.name: Corma

c.description: Cormint Data Systems, Inc. is a Texas-based, vertically integrated developer and operator of power infrastructure for large-scale data centers and compute. The company designs, manufactures, deploys and operates its own electrical and site infrastructure in-house — from PDU wiring and PLC controls through transformer integration and substation work — and runs 130 MW energized today at its Fort Blocks site near Fort Stockton in West Texas, with a second 58 MW site (Bobcat) under construction near Orange Grove in ERCOT Load Zone South and a stated pipeline of roughly 370 MW across 707 controlled acres. Cormint built the operating platform in bitcoin mining, where it reports power costs of 2.3–3.1 cents per kWh and a #1 peer ranking on cost efficiency, and is now positioning the same platform for AI and HPC workloads as a colocation and EPC-style infrastructure owner-operator. It is an energy and data-center infrastructure business rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable specification of any kind.
c.name: Cormint

c.description: Cormint Data Systems designs, manufactures, and operates high‑performance power infrastructure for large‑scale data centers and Bitcoin mining operations. The company builds modular power systems in‑house, operates multiple sites in Texas, and provides turnkey solutions for AI‑intensive workloads, emphasizing cost‑efficiency and reliability.
c.name: Cormintdatasystems

c.description: Cornami is a Santa Clara, California high-performance computing company building morphable silicon and a stream-centric software stack for privacy-preserving and AI workloads. Its FracTLcore Fabric and TruStream dataflow programming model power the Tigris 16nm ASIC, MX8 board, and rack-scale MX64 system, delivering real-time Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), private LLM inference, blockchain, and signal-processing acceleration at greatly reduced power and latency. Cornami is a frontier-tech company backed by SoftBank Vision Fund; this profile tracks its public developer and API surface within the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Cornami

c.description: CorneaGen provides a comprehensive surgeon portal offering corneal tissue services, products, and educational resources. The platform enables eye surgeons to request tissue, access product information, view reimbursement details, and engage with training materials. It also includes regulatory information, adverse reaction reporting, and a range of corneal surgical solutions such as DSAEK, DMEK, and pre‑loaded grafts, supporting ophthalmic professionals worldwide.

c.description: Cornelis Networks provides high‑performance networking solutions for AI and HPC workloads, offering Omni‑Path and Ethernet products such as the CN5000 and CN6000. The company focuses on ultra‑low latency, lossless scale‑out fabrics, and advanced networking hardware for large‑scale compute environments.
c.name: Cornelisnetworks

c.description: Cornell University is a private Ivy League and statutory land-grant research university in Ithaca, New York. It operates no central developer portal, no API gateway and no published API program, and this profile records that plainly. What it does operate, directly and on its own hosts, is a small set of real machine-readable surfaces: the Class Roster API on classes.cornell.edu (public, read-only, version 2.0, maintained behind the scenes by the Office of the University Registrar), the Cornell University Library's self-hosted Blacklight catalog and CUGIR geospatial repository, both of which answer JSON on every route, its own Shibboleth identity provider published as SAML 2.0 metadata and registered with InCommon/eduGAIN, and — through the Cornell Lab of Ornithology — the token-gated eBird API 2.0. Everything else that looks like a Cornell API belongs to somebody else: the events calendar at events.cornell.edu is a Localist tenancy, eCommons is a 4Science-managed DSpace instance, and arXiv, hosted at Cornell for twenty-five years, spun out as an independent nonprofit on 2026-07-01 and is no longer a Cornell surface at all. The Cornell Open Data Initiative specs that once padded this profile described a dining API, a campus-map API and a Cornell Days API that are all dead as of 2026-08-19.
c.name: Cornell University

c.description: Corner Health is a primary care provider network operating in Arizona and Washington that connects patients with independent nurse practitioners and advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs). The company offers everyday and preventative care, chronic condition management, women's health, weight management and metabolic health, and hormone management, with longer appointment times, acceptance of major insurance plans, same-day/evening/Saturday availability, and continuity with the same provider across visits. It is a patient-facing healthcare service that publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of homebrew and enriched with verified identity and domain-security signals.
c.name: Corner Health

c.description: Corner Therapeutics is a biotech company developing dendritic cell‑based immunotherapies for cancer and infectious diseases. Founded in 2019 and based in Watertown, Massachusetts, the firm aims to create rapid, patient‑friendly, low‑cost vaccines and treatments that generate durable memory T‑cell and antibody responses. It has raised multiple rounds of funding, including a $54 million Series A, and collaborates with academic and industry partners to advance its platform.

c.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.
c.name: Cornershop by Uber

c.description: Cornerstone Building Brands, Inc. is a Fortune 1000 manufacturer of exterior building products in North America — vinyl siding and accessories, metal and rainware, fence and railing, windows and entry doors, and metal roofs, walls and buildings — sold under brands including Ply Gem, Simonton and Mastic through dealers, distributors and builders rather than as software. It operates no developer program and publishes no API documentation, SDK or developer portal: the hosts its earlier catalog record named, developer.cornerstonebuildingbrands.com and api.cornerstonebuildingbrands.com, do not resolve. Its machine-readable surface is what the corporate WordPress estate on www.cornerstonebuildingbrands.com exposes — an anonymously readable WordPress REST content API (press releases, industry pages, leadership profiles, pages, media, taxonomies and search) and, notably for a manufacturer, a live remote Model Context Protocol server published through the WordPress MCP Adapter, advertised by real RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata and RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, with tools/list OAuth-gated. The company's partner-facing integration surface — orders, ASNs, warranty claims — sits behind the Windows & Doors Customer Portal, which signs in with Microsoft Entra ID over an Azure API Management gateway whose developer portal is unpublished.
c.name: Cornerstone Building Brands

c.description: Cornerstone OnDemand is an enterprise talent management platform offering REST APIs for learning management, performance reviews, succession planning, recruiting, and workforce analytics. The APIs are RESTful, support OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials authentication, and return JSON (with some XML support). Developers can integrate with modules including Core HR, Learning, Performance, Recruiting, Reporting, Bulk data import, Connectors, and Webhooks through the Cornerstone Developer Portal at csod.dev.
c.name: Cornerstone OnDemand

c.description: Cornerstone Robotics (CSR) is a Hong Kong-headquartered surgical robotics manufacturer founded in 2019 at Hong Kong Science Park, building the Sentire Endoscopic Surgical System (C1000) — a multi-specialty, minimally invasive robot-assisted surgery platform developed entirely in-house and indicated for general surgery, gynecology, thoracic and urology. The Sentire system has received regulatory clearance in China (NMPA), the European Union and Singapore, and has completed multicenter clinical trials in China and the United Kingdom. The company operates three global R&D hubs, six business centers and a 30,000 square meter manufacturing facility, and sells a regulated physical medical device rather than software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable specifications.

c.description: Corning Incorporated is a Fortune 500 American technology company that specializes in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics. Founded in 1851, Corning manufactures specialty glass, ceramics, and related materials and technologies for industrial and scientific applications. Corning's businesses include Optical Communications (fiber optic cable and hardware), Display Technologies (LCD and OLED glass substrates), Specialty Materials (Gorilla Glass for mobile devices), Environmental Technologies (ceramic substrates and filters for emissions control), and Life Sciences (laboratory glassware, cell culture, and bioprocess products). Corning does not publish a public developer API.

c.description: Coro is a cybersecurity company that consolidates endpoint protection, email security, network protection (ZTNA, VPN, encryption), cloud app security, data protection, and security awareness training into a single AI-driven platform built for lean IT teams, growing organizations, and managed service providers (MSPs). Coro's public REST API (v1) exposes the same workspace security data through region-specific hosts (US, Canada, Germany), organized around workspaces as tenant containers with subscriptions, tickets, devices, protected users, portal users, usage metrics, audit logs, and webhook configurations. It authenticates with OAuth 2.0 client credentials and offers real-time webhooks and an official MCP server so AI tools can query Coro securely. Coro was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital.

A single platform and dashboard consolidate endpoint protection, email protection, network protection (ZTNA/VPN), cloud app security, data governance, and security awareness training. The Coro Public API lets service providers and developers build applications that integrate with the platform: it is organized around workspaces (regular, channel, and child tenants) and exposes endpoints for managing workspaces, subscriptions, portal users, protected users and devices, device licensing, tickets, audit logs, and usage. c.description: Corpay is a global S&P 500 corporate payments company (NYSE: CPAY) that resulted from the March 2024 rebrand of FLEETCOR Technologies. The company serves more than 800,000 business clients across 200+ countries in 140+ currencies and processed approximately $400 billion in payments in 2024 with reported revenue of about $4.0B. Corpay operates across five product lines built largely through acquisition — Commercial Cards (including Corpay Mastercard), AP Automation (extended by the 2024 acquisition of Paymerang), Cross-Border Payments (built on the 2017 acquisition of Cambridge Global Payments and the 2025 acquisition of Alpha Group International), Fuel & Fleet Cards (the original FLEETCOR business plus the 2014 acquisition of Comdata), and Workforce Lodging & Travel. Despite this scale, Corpay does not operate a public developer portal — there is no developer.corpay.com, no public OpenAPI catalog, no public GitHub presence, and no self-service API key issuance. All integration surfaces (ERP connectors for NetSuite, Sage, Microsoft Dynamics, QuickBooks, Acumatica, CMiC, Deltek, Trimble; the former Cambridge cross-border payments API; AP-automation API hooks) are sales-led and gated behind enterprise contracts.

c.description: Corporate Travel Management (CTM) is a Brisbane-founded, ASX-listed (CTD) travel management company established in 1994 that procures, books and services corporate, government, meetings and events, resources, sport and leisure travel across Australia and New Zealand, North America, Europe and Asia. CTM sits on the buy side of the travel distribution chain: an IATA-accredited agency that aggregates supplier content from GDS, direct airline APIs and airline NDC connections and resells it to corporate clients through its own proprietary technology stack — the Lightning online booking tool, CTM Portal, CTM Mobile app, CTM Approve pre-trip approval, CTM Fare Forecaster and CTM Data Hub reporting. Its API posture is closed. CTM publishes no developer portal and no public API: developer.travelctm.com, developers.travelctm.com, api.travelctm.com and docs.travelctm.com do not resolve in DNS, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/security.txt all return HTTP 404 across the AU, US and UK sites. The only live non-marketing front door is a customer login — CTM Portal at portal.travelctm.com and www.ctmsmart.com.au. CTM's technology pages assert secure integration with client HR, expense, finance, ERP and single sign-on systems, but no interface contract, schema or endpoint is documented anywhere in public: the integration surface is proprietary and undocumented, reachable only under a managed-travel commercial agreement. The only published exit path is a GDPR/CCPA data-portability request by email to privacy@travelctm.com or DPO@travelctm.com; there is no self-service export.
