c.name: Corti

c.description: Cortica is a Tel Aviv, Israel based Autonomous AI company founded in 2007 that builds and spins out category-leading AI companies. Its self-learning, unsupervised "Autonomous AI" is modelled on the mammalian cortex — signatures instead of labels, adaptive architecture, and self-learning neural networks that index high volumes of visual, audio, radar and time-series signal on low-compute platforms. Cortica states it has invested more than $250M over 15 years and holds 300+ patents, and it operates as a venture builder rather than a product vendor: its technology reaches the market through partner joint ventures and spin-outs including Autobrains (autonomous driving), Corsight AI (facial recognition), Corsound AI (voice), SeeTrue (airport security screening), CordiGuide (medical imaging) and Lean AI / Qualisense (industrial quality inspection, with Johnson Electric). Cortica itself publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification on its own domain.
c.name: Cortica

c.description: Corticaa254, operating under the Cortica brand, provides autism care and ABA therapy services for children. The company offers evidence‑based treatments, diagnostic evaluations, and in‑network insurance support across multiple locations. It emphasizes a whole‑child model, research, and family resources, aiming to improve outcomes for children with autism spectrum disorder.
c.name: Corticaa254

c.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.
c.name: Cortico

c.description: Cortina Systems, Inc. was a venture-backed fabless semiconductor company founded in 2001 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, that designed high-speed communications and networking integrated circuits for optical transport, carrier Ethernet, framer/mapper and PHY devices, and broadband access (EPON/GPON and DSL). The company grew through acquisitions and was itself acquired by Inphi Corporation in 2014; Inphi later merged into Marvell Technology in 2021, and the cortina-systems.com domain now redirects to Marvell. Cortina was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a hardware semiconductor business with no public developer platform or API surface, so no API artifacts apply.
c.name: Cortina Systems

c.description: Coru is an enterprise-grade AI company transforming financial services across Latin America with conversational AI agents. Its "Adi" platform lets banks, fintechs, and insurers build and customize agentic workflows for digital loan origination, 24/7 customer service, collections management, insurance quoting, claims handling, and commission reconciliation across web, app, and WhatsApp channels in Spanish, Portuguese, and English, with multimodal input (text, voice, audio, documents) and OCR-based document capture. Coru serves financial institutions including Bradesco, Banorte, and Neon, and is backed by QED Investors. Coru markets a hosted, enterprise agent product and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs.
c.name: Coru

c.description: Corui Technology Co., Ltd., founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, China, manufactures and develops high‑performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and ultra‑high performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) systems, LC‑MS/MS instruments, and related analytical solutions. The company serves scientific research, environmental testing, and food safety markets, offering fast, accurate, and cost‑effective chromatography equipment to improve operational efficiency for laboratories worldwide.
c.name: Corui

c.description: Corva is a Houston-based AI software company providing a real-time drilling, completions, geoscience and sustainability analytics platform for upstream oil and gas. Corva ingests rig sensor and operational data and exposes it through TWO REST APIs on two hosts: the Platform API at api.corva.ai (wells, rigs, pads, programs, frac fleets, users, dashboards, alerts and apps; 513 paths and 771 operations described by a published Swagger 2.0 contract) and the Data API at data.corva.ai (time, depth, reference and timeseries dataset records, aggregations and permitted customer writes; described by a published OpenAPI 3.1 contract). Corva Dev Center is an SDK and app-hosting environment where customers build frontend, backend, scheduled, stream and task applications on Corva data, with a Python SDK, npm component libraries and a public app marketplace. Access is enterprise-only: there is no public pricing, no free tier and no self-serve signup, and API key creation is not enabled by default for most customer users.
c.name: Corva AI

c.description: Corventis, Inc. was a healthcare technology company that developed wearable cardiac monitoring devices — including the PiiX adhesive sensor and the NUVANT Mobile Cardiac Telemetry (MCT) system — for remote patient monitoring and arrhythmia detection. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, the company was acquired by Medtronic in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent entity. The corventis.com domain now resolves to Medtronic infrastructure (Medtronic nameservers; TLS certificate scoped to Medtronic domains). No public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface exists for this provider.
c.name: Corventis

c.description: Corvera is an AI-native context layer for consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands, backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026). It unifies data from retailers, distributors, logistics providers, ERP systems, data warehouses, and ecommerce platforms into a single governed source of truth that AI tools can query directly over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Rather than shipping a traditional REST API or SDKs, Corvera exposes a hosted, OAuth-secured MCP server at https://mcp.corvera.ai/mcp that any MCP-capable tool (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Lovable, Replit) can connect to; the tools an account can call are gated by the integrations it has connected. Capabilities span category management, pricing and promotion ROI, demand forecasting, inventory management, cashflow tracking, and marketing-mix ROI, with role-based dataset access controls, a shared business glossary (Context), canonical entity mappings, and an admin activity feed. The platform normalizes cross-retailer sales calendars, resolves product mappings across sources, and makes governed datasets legible to AI-native CPG teams without dedicated data engineers.
c.name: Corvera

c.description: Corvia Medical, Inc. is a medical device company headquartered in Tewksbury, Massachusetts that develops interventional cardiology solutions for heart failure. Its lead product is the Corvia Atrial Shunt System (IASD), a transcatheter implant indicated for improving quality of life and reducing heart-failure symptoms in patients with elevated left atrial pressures who remain symptomatic despite guideline-directed medical therapy. The company has been backed by General Catalyst since 2009. Corvia Medical publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface; its web presence is clinical, patient, and regulatory information only.
c.name: Corvia Medical

c.description: Corvidia Therapeutics is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company based in Waltham, MA, focused on developing precision cardiovascular and cardio‑renal therapies using functional genomics. Founded in 2015, the company leverages genetic susceptibility insights to create targeted treatments for complex diseases, aiming to improve patient outcomes through innovative drug development and commercialization strategies. It was acquired by Novo Nordisk in 2020, reflecting its strategic importance in the heart‑focused therapeutic space.
c.name: Corvidia Therapeutics

c.description: Corvus Insurance — now operating as Corvus by Travelers — is a cyber-insurance managing general agency and insurtech company that pairs property and casualty underwriting with security-focused data science. It offers Smart Cyber Insurance and Smart Tech Errors & Omissions coverage, a Cyber Risk Dashboard that continuously scans policyholders' external attack surface for vulnerabilities and delivers threat intelligence and remediation guidance, 24/7 incident response and claims support, and broker tooling for collaborative quoting and renewal management. Founded in 2017 and backed by Insight Partners and Obvious Ventures, Corvus was acquired by Travelers in 2024 and now operates as a Travelers company. The public site exposes marketing, broker resources, and a broker portal, but no public developer API program.
c.name: Corvus Insurance

c.description: Corvus Robotics provides autonomous warehouse inventory management solutions using AI‑powered drones and robotics. Their platform, including Corvus One, Cold Chain, and Trident, enables real‑time inventory tracking, cold‑chain monitoring, and automated material handling for Fortune 500 enterprises across North America. The company focuses on reducing labor costs, increasing accuracy, and improving supply‑chain efficiency through advanced perception and navigation technologies.
c.name: Corvus Robotics

c.description: Corvus Energy, founded in 2009, provides zero‑emission energy storage solutions for the maritime industry. The company designs, manufactures and deploys battery systems that power hybrid and fully electric vessels, aiming to reduce diesel consumption and CO₂ emissions worldwide. With over 1,300 installations and more than 50% market share in maritime zero‑emission solutions, Corvus Energy serves a global customer base across shipping, offshore, and ferry sectors, delivering innovative, reliable and sustainable power.
c.name: Corvusenergy

c.description: CorWave SA is a French clinical-stage medical device company, incorporated in 2012 by the startup studio MD Start and headquartered in Clichy, France, that develops implantable cardiac assist pumps for patients with advanced heart failure. Its patented wave membrane technology — a biomimetic polymer membrane driven by an electromagnetic actuator, inspired by the undulating movement of marine animals — produces truly pulsatile, physiological blood flow, differentiating the CorWave LVAS and Nemo pumps from commercially available rotary-pump LVADs. The company has raised more than EUR 80 million, operates an urban manufacturing facility in Clichy, employs more than 90 people, and announced the first in-human implantation of its Left Ventricular Assist System in 2025. CorWave LVAS remains an investigational device and is not approved for commercial use in any country. CorWave publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.
c.name: CorWave

c.description: A Chinese state-owned multinational shipping and logistics conglomerate and the world's largest container shipping fleet by capacity. Operates container shipping, port terminals, bulk cargo services, and digital supply chain platforms (Syncon Hub, My Reefer, Hi-Dolphin) across global trade routes.
c.name: COSCO Shipping

c.description: Cosemitech (意瑞半导体（上海）有限公司) is a high‑tech semiconductor solutions provider founded in 2014, designing and producing sensing and control ICs such as Hall switches, current sensors, linear Hall and speed sensor ICs for automotive, industrial, energy and consumer electronics markets. The company has shipped over 700 million units to more than 300 global customers, offering high‑performance, reliable and functional‑safety‑focused products.
c.name: Cosemitech

c.description: Cosign is the command-line client of the Sigstore project for signing, verifying, and storing container images, OCI artifacts, blobs, and in-toto attestations. Cosign supports keyless signing using OpenID Connect identity providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft) by obtaining short-lived certificates from the Fulcio certificate authority and recording signing events in the Rekor transparency log. Signatures and attestations are stored alongside the signed artifact in any OCI-compliant registry, and cosign integrates with policy controllers, KMS providers, hardware tokens, and SBOM workflows for software supply chain security.
c.name: Cosign

c.description: Cosihospitality operates under the Così brand, providing catering services and fresh food ordering through its website getcosi.com. The company offers a range of menu options, location-based catering, and an online ordering platform for events and corporate clients. It serves multiple US cities, supports online quotes, loyalty programs, and integrates with third‑party delivery services. The platform includes detailed FAQs, a story about the brand, and contact options for catering inquiries.
c.name: Cosihospitality

c.description: Cosm is a Los Angeles-based immersive technology, media and entertainment company formed in 2020 from the merger of LiveLike VR (now Cosm Immersive) and C360, followed by the acquisition of planetarium pioneers Evans & Sutherland and Spitz. It operates three lines: Cosm Tech (the CX System LED dome, Digistar planetarium software, and end-to-end immersive display systems sold to planetariums, museums and attractions), Cosm Media (immersive content production and licensing through Cosm Studios) and Cosm Venues (the "Shared Reality" experiential venues in Los Angeles and Dallas, with Atlanta, Detroit and Cleveland following). Cosm sells and operates systems and venues rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification. The one API it markets — the Digistar scripting/automation interface, advertised as "the most fully featured API across the planetarium industry" — is documented only inside the customer support portal at partners.cosm.com, which requires a login.
c.name: Cosm

c.description: Cosmart is an Indonesian membership-only B2B e-commerce and procurement platform, founded in 2021 by Alvin Kumarga and Robert Tan, where members (individuals and SMEs) purchase their recurring daily and business needs in larger quantities at competitive prices. The platform lists over 100,000 products across categories including office supplies, electronics, household items, automotive parts, industrial equipment, furniture, and services, with nationwide delivery, flexible payment terms, and dedicated relationship managers for corporate clients. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Lightspeed India Partners. Cosmart does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Cosmart

c.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. Its first market is utility-scale solar energy, with expansion planned into data center construction. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. Cosmic Robotics is currently a hardware and fleet-software company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and any agent-facing surfaces (such as its published llms.txt) as the API Evangelist network enrichment pipeline monitors it for a future API.
c.name: Cosmic Robotics

c.description: Cosmic Shielding is a stub entry created by the API Evangelist harvest process. The company is identified as a provider of shielding solutions for cosmic radiation, targeting aerospace and satellite industries. While detailed public information is currently limited, the entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment as more data becomes available through subsequent profiling steps.
c.name: Cosmic Shielding

c.description: Cosmiccloud provides an auto‑DevOps platform that enables developers to deploy, scale, and monitor applications across multiple cloud providers with minimal effort. Their solution offers a no‑code backend, automated release and rollback, logging, DNS integration, and comprehensive monitoring, targeting startups and small‑scale companies seeking to reduce operational overhead and accelerate delivery.
c.name: Cosmiccloud

c.description: Cosmico is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Cosmico

c.description: Cosmicsingularity is currently a minimally documented entity discovered in the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. No public website, API documentation, or detailed corporate information could be located despite automated searches of common domains, search engines, and known hosting platforms. The stub entry records only the company name and placeholder maintainer contacts, awaiting further verification or discovery of official resources.
c.name: Cosmicsingularity

c.description: Cosmo Tech is a predictive and prescriptive AI-simulation (digital twin) platform for industry, based in Lyon, France and backed by Insight Partners. Its open-source Cosmo Tech Cloud Platform API (Kotlin, MIT) lets teams model organizations, workspaces, solutions, datasets, runners and runs, then configure and execute large-scale what-if simulations across supply chains, asset investment planning and enterprise operations. The API is modular across seven service specs (organization, workspace, solution, dataset, runner, run, meta), authenticates via OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (Keycloak), and ships auto-generated TypeScript and Python clients plus the Babylon CLI.
c.name: Cosmo Tech

c.description: Cosmocompany is a technology company specializing in satellite communications and IoT connectivity solutions. It provides a suite of APIs for device provisioning, telemetry ingestion, and network management, targeting enterprise and developer audiences. The company focuses on secure, low-latency data transfer across global satellite networks, enabling remote monitoring and control for industries such as agriculture, logistics, and energy.
c.name: Cosmocompany

c.description: CosmoLex is a cloud-based legal practice management platform that combines matter management, time tracking, billing, trust accounting, and client engagement in a single system. It provides a web services API for integrating matters, time entries, billing, trust accounting, and compliance workflows, subject to a per-user-license monthly call quota. CosmoLex serves solo practitioners and law firms up to 100 users and is designed to satisfy state bar trust accounting compliance requirements.
c.name: CosmoLex

c.description: Cosmonic provides an AI sandbox platform that secures and runs code generated by AI agents. It offers a cross‑platform desktop app and cloud‑hosted control servers, enabling developers to build, test, and deploy sandboxed workloads from laptop to cluster. The service emphasizes capability‑based security, privacy, and easy integration with wasmcloud and other cloud‑native tools.
c.name: Cosmonic

c.description: COSMOPlat (卡奥斯 COSMOPlat) is the industrial internet platform incubated by Haier Group and operated by COSMOPlat Digital Technology (Qingdao) Co., Ltd. Launched in 2017, it was China's first self-developed industrial internet platform built around mass customization, digitally integrating user interaction, R&D, procurement, production and service across a factory and its supply chain. Its product line spans smart-factory and MES systems, industrial IoT device connectivity, chemical-park management, smart energy control, equipment health management and a D3OS digital-twin offering, and it has been applied across roughly twenty industries and more than twenty countries. The developer-facing surface is the 物联开发平台 (IoT development platform), which publishes a public HTML API reference covering product, device, alarm, rule-chain, thing-model, telemetry and device-RPC operations, alongside an MQTT telemetry publish/subscribe surface. COSMOPlat also runs an open-source developer community at openlab.cosmoplat.com and a GitHub organization at cosmoplat-dev.
c.name: Cosmoplat

c.description: Cosmos is an interoperable blockchain ecosystem providing a modular framework (Cosmos SDK) for building sovereign, high-performance application-specific blockchains. The Cosmos SDK exposes LCD (Light Client Daemon) REST APIs on port 1317, generated automatically via gRPC-gateway from Protobuf definitions. These endpoints cover accounts, balances, transactions, governance proposals, staking delegations, IBC transfers, minting, distribution, and ABCI app data. The Cosmos Hub (cosmoshub-4) is the flagship chain; the same API surface is shared by 150+ chains in the ecosystem.
c.name: Cosmos

c.description: Cosmose AI (Cosmose Inc.) is a Singapore-headquartered, Polish-founded retail intelligence company that measures, predicts and influences offline shopping behaviour at scale, claiming reach across roughly one billion consumers through an SDK embedded in partner mobile applications. Founded in 2014 by Miron Mironiuk with offices in Singapore, Warsaw, Paris, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Tokyo, it sells offline footfall and purchase-intent analytics plus online-to-offline ad targeting to brands including LVMH, Richemont, L'Oreal and Estee Lauder, and operates two consumer-facing products — Cosmose Media (the advertising side) and KaiKai / KaiKaiNow, a gamified "shoppertainment" and lock-screen app built with the NEAR Foundation. Cosmose does not run a public developer program: there is no developer portal, no published API reference, no pricing page and no self-serve signup. Its API surface is nonetheless partly public — an unauthenticated springdoc OpenAPI 3.0.1 document for the KaiKai Deal Hunter registration service is served from the Singapore gateway, and its iOS SDKs are distributed through a first-party CocoaPods spec repository on GitHub.
c.name: Cosmose AI

c.description: Cosmossingularity is a stub entry discovered in the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest. No public website or API documentation could be located despite searches on equityzen.com, Google, and DuckDuckGo. The company appears to have no publicly accessible digital presence at this time, and further investigation may be required to verify its existence and any available services.
c.name: Cosmossingularity

c.description: Cospowers (昆宇电源) is a leading Chinese lithium‑ion battery and energy‑storage solutions provider. With over 30 years of R&D, it offers integrated storage systems for power, industrial, data‑center, residential and communication applications, aiming to be a global smart‑energy solutions leader.
c.name: Cospowers

c.description: Costanoa Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in June 2012 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with an additional office in San Francisco. Costanoa invests primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, writing checks of roughly $1M to $10M and taking concentrated 10-15% ownership across about 35 companies per fund. The firm's thesis is to fill the "missing middle" of early-stage venture by providing unusually hands-on, operator-led support to founders building applied AI, AI and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security / defense tech, fintech, and enterprise software companies. Costanoa was founded by Greg Sands (an early Netscape product manager) and manages roughly $2.8B in assets. In September 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Fund V at $275M alongside Opportunity Fund III at $119M, doubling down on AI-enabled B2B technology. Portfolio companies include Alation, Cyberhaven, Quizlet, PayNearMe, Auterion, Vannevar Labs, Kepler Communications, and Muon Space.
c.name: Costanoa Ventures

c.description: CoStar Group is the dominant commercial and residential real estate data, analytics, and marketplace company. The portfolio spans the flagship CoStar commercial real estate intelligence platform, LoopNet (CRE marketplace), Apartments.com network (residential rentals, including ForRent.com and Westside Rentals), Homes.com and Homesnap (for-sale residential), Ten-X (online CRE auctions), BizBuySell (business-for-sale marketplace), STR (hotel data), Visual Lease (lease management), Matterport (3D spatial capture), and international properties including OnTheMarket (UK), Emporis (Germany), and a controlling stake in Domain Group (Australia). Distribution to partners is via enterprise data licensing, syndication feeds, and brand-specific marketplace tooling rather than a public self-serve developer portal.
c.name: CoStar Group

c.description: Costco Wholesale Corporation is a Fortune 500 American multinational membership-only big-box retail chain that operates warehouse clubs offering a wide selection of merchandise at discounted prices. Costco does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading partner integrations are conducted through EDI and B2B channels using ANSI X12 transactions and the Costco Supplier Portal. Costco operates an e-commerce site, the Costco Travel and Costco Pharmacy properties, and the Costco Photo Center.
c.name: Costco Wholesale

c.description: Cosuno is an AI‑based tendering platform for the construction industry in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. It connects clients and subcontractors, offering over 4,000 private/commercial tenders per month from 600+ clients, helping contractors win jobs with AI‑assisted bid creation and delivering average cost savings of 5‑7%.
c.name: Cosuno

c.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.
c.name: COSY

c.description: Cotatrack is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. No public website or documentation could be located after exhaustive web searches, and the only reference is the equityzen listing. Consequently, detailed information about its services, APIs, or branding is unavailable at this time.
c.name: Cotatrack

c.description: CoTeach is an AI-powered curriculum co-planning assistant for K-12 mathematics teachers, built by Teaching Lab and deeply integrated with the Illustrative Mathematics (IM v.360) curriculum. Through a chat interface, teachers adapt lessons, generate curriculum-aligned practice problems and worksheets, build scaffolds and differentiated supports for multilingual learners and students with IEPs, and produce IM-style math diagrams (number lines, tape diagrams, area models), exporting to PDF or Google Docs. CoTeach preserves IM's pedagogical framework, collects no student data, and meters usage by message credits. It also exposes a hosted, OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (the "Coteach Claude connector") and publishes an llms.txt so AI agents can discover the product and hand off to it.
c.name: CoTeach

c.description: Coterie Insurance is a technology-first commercial insurance provider for small businesses, offering Business Owners Policy (BOP), General Liability (GL), Professional Liability (PL), and Workers' Compensation (WC). Its REST API lets appointed agents and digital partners build applications, generate bindable quotes, bind and issue policies, look up industry/NAICS classifications, retrieve policy documents, and subscribe to webhooks for an embedded small-business insurance experience.
c.name: Coterie Insurance

c.description: Coterie Insurance provides small business insurance solutions that streamline coverage and underwriting for agents, brokers, and owners. The platform offers digital, real-time underwriting, instant binding, and a range of policies including General Liability, Business Owners Policy, Professional Liability, Cyber Insurance, and Workplace Violence coverage. It serves agents and small business owners through an online portal with API integration options, aiming to simplify the insurance process and accelerate quote-to-bind times.
c.name: Coteriee1d3

c.description: Coterra Energy Inc. (formerly Cabot Oil & Gas, combined with Cimarex Energy in October 2021) was a Houston-headquartered independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company with positions in the Permian Basin, the Marcellus Shale and the Anadarko Basin. On May 7, 2026 Coterra completed an all-stock merger with Devon Energy; the combined company operates as Devon Energy (NYSE: DVN), Coterra's shares were deregistered (Form 15-12G filed 2026-05-19) and investors.coterra.com now redirects to investors.devonenergy.com. The coterra.com site has been reduced to a five-page holding site for interest owners. Coterra never operated a public developer program or API: owner statements are delivered through EnergyLink and production data through PDS Energy, both third-party platforms. The only programmatic access to Coterra data is the SEC's own EDGAR API, listed here as a clearly labeled third-party government API.
c.name: Coterra Energy

c.description: Cotool is an AI platform for the defensive security "blue team" — AI agents that scale detection, response, and threat hunting across an organization's security stack. Its three products, Detect, Respond, and Hunt, let teams author detections from natural-language descriptions, automate alert response and playbook execution with human-in-the-loop controls, and monitor threat intelligence for relevance and coverage gaps. Cotool's stated mission is to "scale defensive security with tokens," giving defenders machine-speed operational advantages instead of being limited by headcount, improving coverage and cutting mean-time-to-respond (MTTR). Cotool is a San Francisco company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, WndrCo, and Homebrew. As of this profile it publishes a product and marketing site only — no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or MCP server was found.
c.name: Cotool

c.description: Cotopaxi is a Certified B Corporation outdoor gear and apparel brand (backpacks, jackets, and accessories) known for its "Do Good" mission and Gear for Good model. It sells direct-to-consumer on a Shopify storefront at cotopaxi.com. Cotopaxi publishes no first-party developer API, but its Shopify platform exposes real machine surfaces: OAuth2/OIDC customer authentication (Shopify Customer Accounts) at account.cotopaxi.com, a hosted Storefront MCP server at /api/mcp, and an authenticated Customer Account MCP API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Forerunner Ventures.
c.name: Cotopaxi

c.description: Coty Inc. is one of the world's largest beauty companies with an iconic portfolio of brands across fragrance, color cosmetics, skin and body care. The company operates two divisions: Prestige (premium fragrance, cosmetics, and skincare brands such as Gucci, Burberry, Calvin Klein, Hugo Boss, Marc Jacobs, Tiffany, Chloe, Davidoff, Lancaster, philosophy, and Kylie Cosmetics) and Consumer Beauty (mass-market color cosmetics, hair care, and body care brands such as CoverGirl, Rimmel, Max Factor, Sally Hansen, Bourjois, and Adidas). Coty does not publish a public developer API; supplier and partner integrations occur through the Coty Supplier Portal and B2B / EDI channels.
c.name: Coty

c.description: Couchbase is a distributed, document-oriented NoSQL cloud database platform that combines the flexibility of JSON, the power of SQL++ querying, and the performance of an in-memory key-value store. The Couchbase product line includes Couchbase Server (self-managed), Couchbase Capella (fully managed database-as-a-service across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud), Sync Gateway and App Services for mobile and edge synchronization, and Couchbase Lite embedded databases. Couchbase exposes a comprehensive set of REST APIs covering cluster administration, SQL++ query execution, full-text and vector search, analytics, eventing, backup, cross data center replication, and Capella management.
c.name: Couchbase

c.description: Couchsurfing is a community-driven travel and hospitality-exchange platform that connects travelers with local hosts offering free accommodation, local meetups, and cultural exchange across more than 200,000 cities worldwide. Members build trust through verified profiles, references, and community events, and use the service to find places to stay, meet locals, and discover events while traveling. Couchsurfing publishes no official public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web, trust, and policy surface for discovery and monitoring, and was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and Point Nine.
c.name: Couchsurfing

The company appears to be a platform related to international couchsurfing services, but no official website or detailed public information could be located after exhaustive web searches. This entry records the limited known metadata and will be updated when verifiable sources become available.
c.name: Couchsurfinginternational

c.description: Coulomb Technology is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
c.name: Coulomb Technology

c.description: CSOAI Ltd — public name Council of AI (UK Companies House 16939677, London; second domain csoai.org) — is an independent AI-governance MEASUREMENT body: "measurement, not certification". It publishes the living GSPC board (Governance · Safety · Provenance · Continuity) as a keyless, CORS-open JSON API, Ed25519-signed measurement cards verifiable offline against a did:web:csoai.org key document, a Merkle public root with inclusion proofs, an EU AI Act Article 50 machine-marking detector, and a dated corrections ledger. The estate is exposed to agents three ways: a 141-operation OpenAPI 3.1 contract at https://councilof.ai/openapi.json (plus a 7-operation read-surfaces spec), a remote MCP server at https://councilof.ai/mcp (13 tools with anonymous tools/list; npm stdio twin csoai-gspc-mcp; MCP Registry io.github.CSOAI-ORG/gspc), and an A2A v1.0 agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json with eight skills. Ten REST doors and four MCP tools are metered per artefact by x402 (USDC on Base, amounts only inside the 402 challenge); the board, verification and every preview are free and need no account.
c.name: Council of AI

c.description: The Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) is an office within the Executive Office of the President of the United States that coordinates federal environmental policy, advises the President on environmental and natural resource policies, and oversees the implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). CEQ does not publish a public developer API. Federal NEPA documents and related environmental data are surfaced through partner federal agencies and platforms (NEPAtool, the Federal Permitting Dashboard, regulations.gov, EPA EJScreen, and the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool).
c.name: Council on Environmental Quality

c.description: Counsel Health is a telemedicine company multiplying the world's healthcare capacity by pairing an AI medical assistant with board-certified physicians delivered through chat. Individuals get free AI medical guidance and can connect with a licensed doctor for a flat $29 per consultation, seven days a week, for urgent care, primary care support, medication refills, lab testing, and health-record management. Counsel also ships an embedded product — a WebView / iFrame surface plus a server-side Counsel API — that partners integrate into their own applications, documented at docs.counselhealth.com with example apps published on GitHub. Backed by GV (Google Ventures).
c.name: Counsel Health

c.description: Countable was a civic-engagement technology company backed by Canaan Partners (seed, partner Joydeep Bhattacharyya) that built a digital platform helping citizens understand what Congress was doing in Washington and contact their elected representatives directly, later extending the same advocacy tooling to organizations and brands. As of this enrichment pass the Countable brand is no longer operating independently: both countable.com and countable.us HTTP 302 to https://www.myactionable.com/, the home of Actionable, a self-service advocacy campaign platform made by CSAG that offers petitions, pledges, lawmaker-message campaigns, supporter video collection, lead capture, polling and in-platform real-time campaign reporting on a $29.99/month self-service plan. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, package, webhook catalog, MCP server or /.well-known discovery surface was found on either the legacy Countable hosts or the successor Actionable host during this pass.

c.description: Counter (counter.dev) is an open-source, privacy-friendly web analytics service. A lightweight tracking snippet POSTs a single aggregated hit per visit to a public collect endpoint (t.counter.dev), and a token-authenticated dashboard data feed returns aggregated stats. Counter uses no cookies, no logging, and no IP fingerprinting. It is AGPL-3.0 licensed and can be self-hosted; the hosted service is pay-what-you-want.
c.name: Counter

c.description: Counterpane Internet Security, Inc. was a managed security services provider founded by cryptographer Bruce Schneier, growing out of his Counterpane Systems cryptography consultancy. Counterpane pioneered Managed Security Monitoring (MSM) — outsourced, 24x7 human-staffed security operations centers that monitored customer networks and devices for intrusions, rather than selling security products. It was venture-backed, with Accel among its investors, and was acquired by BT Group in 2006, after which its operations were folded into BT's managed security business. The company is defunct as an independent entity: it operates no product, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface today. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe, counterpane.com resolves (209.17.116.163, Network Solutions nameservers) but refuses HTTPS on port 443, and plain HTTP redirects to https://www.schneier.com/ — Bruce Schneier's personal site. www.counterpane.com returns HTTP 404. There is no MX, SPF, DMARC, or CAA record on the domain. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
c.name: Counterpane

c.description: Counterpart provides an enterprise platform that gives executives real‑time visibility and control over strategic goals, investment planning, program delivery, financials, resources and governance. It unifies portfolio, program and project data into a single model, eliminating silos and manual reporting, enabling faster, data‑driven decisions across large organizations.
c.name: Counterpart

c.description: CounterTack, Inc. was a Waltham, Massachusetts endpoint detection and response (EDR) vendor whose Sentinel and Endpoint Threat Platform products applied behavioral analysis, memory forensics and machine learning to detect zero-days, rootkits and advanced persistent threats. In June 2018 CounterTack acquired its channel partner GoSecure, a managed detection and response (MDR) provider, and in March 2019 rebranded the combined company as "GoSecure powered by CounterTack"; the CounterTack name has since been retired in favour of GoSecure, which today markets a managed extended detection and response (MXDR) service and the GoSecure Titan platform covering EDR, IDR, NGAV, SIEM and professional services. Founded in 1925 by Illinois Agricultural Association members, COUNTRY today offers auto, home, life, farm, crop, and commercial insurance along with investment, retirement planning, and trust services through a captive agent network in 19 U.S. states. COUNTRY does not publish a public developer API; partner and agency integrations occur through internal agency systems.

c.description: Country Style Cooking Restaurant Chain (乡村基, Xiangcunji) is a large Chinese quick-service restaurant group founded on 23 November 1996 in Chongqing by Li Hong and Zhang Xingqiang. The group operates two directly-managed chain brands — Xiangcunji (乡村基) and Mr. Rice (大米先生) — serving Sichuan-style fast food cooked to order in restaurant kitchens under a long-standing "good taste at affordable prices" operating philosophy. The company formerly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CCSC and was, at the time, the only Asia-headquartered restaurant chain listed on the NYSE. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hongshan. Country Style Cooking publishes a Chinese-language corporate website (csc100.com) covering its restaurants, brands, group news, recruiting, and procurement bidding, but it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts — this profile records that verified absence of an API surface.

The files are commonly consumed as a lightweight country-data dataset for forms, country pickers, and analytics enrichment.

Coupang exposes an Open API platform for marketplace sellers (vendors) to integrate product catalog, order, return, cancellation, settlement, and inquiry workflows.
c.name: Coupang

c.description: couple (couple.me) is an AI companion chat platform operated by Fab AI LTD and backed by Slow Ventures. The consumer-facing product lets users create and customize an AI girlfriend, boyfriend, or anime character, then hold personalized text conversations and request AI-generated images from that companion. It offers a free tier with an optional premium subscription. It is a consumer app with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures the company identity and the domain-security posture only.

c.description: COUR Pharmaceuticals Development Co., Inc. (COUR Pharma) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in the Chicago area (Northbrook/Skokie, Illinois), spun out of research at Northwestern University. COUR develops antigen-specific immune tolerance therapies built on its proprietary COUR Nanoparticle (CNP) platform: biodegradable polymer nanoparticles of roughly 500 nm carrying about 1% disease-specific antigen, which mimic apoptotic bodies so that antigen-presenting cells in the liver and spleen re-recognize the antigen as self, deleting pathogenic T cells and expanding regulatory T cells. Active clinical programs include CNP-103 for Type 1 Diabetes and CNP-106 for Myasthenia Gravis, with earlier work in Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Celiac Disease. COUR is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

c.description: Courier Health is the patient experience platform for life sciences and biopharma. It gives pharmaceutical patient services, market access, and field reimbursement teams a single command center to manage the patient journey from prescription through long-term treatment adherence, using AI-generated patient summaries, workflow automation and orchestration, and integration of data across systems and partners. The company reports gains in patient starts, six-month persistency, and team productivity, and delivers the product as a HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II SaaS platform. Courier Health is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer or API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and its published security/compliance posture.
c.name: Courier Health

c.description: Course Hero is an online learning platform where students and educators access more than 25 million course-specific study resources — practice problems, study guides, class notes, step-by-step explanations, essays, and lab reports — alongside 24/7 tutoring and AI-assisted study tools. Founded in 2006 by Andrew Grauer at Cornell University and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Course Hero is part of Learneo, a family of learning and productivity brands that also includes QuillBot, Symbolab, LitCharts, CliffsNotes, Scribbr, Bartleby, and LanguageTool. Course Hero exposes only internal, undocumented web APIs (under /api/) that power its consumer web and mobile apps; it publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or partner API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, Sierra Ventures, and SV Angel.
c.name: Course Hero

c.description: Coursebase is an AI-powered corporate Learning Management System (LMS) used by over 1,000 organizations to create, deliver, and manage employee training across online, in-person, and blended formats. The platform offers a library of 1,000+ pre-built eLearning courses, AI-assisted content generation (auto-generated test questions and course summaries), analytics and reporting dashboards, single sign-on, multi-language support, and API-based integration with external HR systems for syncing user account information. Coursebase was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched in the API Evangelist network; the public surface is a marketing site with an enterprise "contact us" API integration offering rather than a self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI.

The platform offers an API that enables developers to integrate court rule searches, compliance checks, and legal intelligence into products, supporting both free tier access and paid plans for higher volume and advanced features.

c.description: CourtListener is a free legal research platform operated by the Free Law Project, a nonprofit organization. It provides a comprehensive REST API for accessing US court opinions, dockets, oral arguments, judge biographical data, financial disclosures, and citation networks from federal and state courts. The platform archives over 9 million case law decisions, 500 million PACER-related items, 3.4 million minutes of oral arguments, and data on 16,000+ judges. Access is available through a membership model with rate limits scaling by tier; an EDU tier is free for academic users.
c.name: CourtListener

c.description: Free Law Project is a nonprofit organization that provides free access to legal information and tools. It operates CourtListener, a comprehensive searchable database of United States court opinions, oral arguments, and other legal documents, along with related services such as RECAP and Bots.law. The platform aims to make the legal ecosystem more equitable and competitive by leveraging technology and open data.
c.name: CourtListener

c.description: Courtyard (courtyard.io) is a marketplace and tokenization service for physical collectibles — trading cards, luxury watches, and other graded assets. Collectors vault a physical item in Courtyard's insured facility and receive a blockchain-backed digital token (an NFT on Ethereum/Polygon) representing verified ownership, which can then be instantly bought, sold, bid on, or redeemed for physical shipment. The platform combines a "Proof of Integrity" authentication process, KYC-gated onboarding, a hosted wallet with fiat funding, digital pack drops and auctions, and a curated showroom experience. Courtyard is a Forerunner Ventures portfolio company operating in the commerce / collectibles sector; it exposes a consumer web application and smart contracts rather than a public developer API.

c.description: Coutts & Co is a British private bank and wealth manager founded in 1692, headquartered in London and serving high-net-worth individuals, families, commercial and institutional clients. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of NatWest Group (formerly The Royal Bank of Scotland Group), one of the UK CMA9 banking groups mandated to deliver Open Banking. Coutts is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA (FCA Firm Reference 001b000000MfEueAAF). As an Account Servicing Payment Service Provider (ASPSP) it participates in UK Open Banking under PSD2, exposing its account, payment and confirmation-of-funds surfaces through NatWest Group's "Bank of APIs" developer platform. Those Read/Write APIs conform to the Open Banking Implementation Entity (OBIE) Read/Write Standard and are secured with FAPI-grade OAuth2/OIDC, PSD2 strong customer authentication, and mutual-TLS client authentication using OBIE/eIDAS certificates. Coutts additionally publishes OBIE Open Data reference information for its commercial/business current accounts.
c.name: Coutts

c.description: Cova is an AI-native home care agency licensed in Michigan and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026). The company serves Medicaid, long-term care insurance (LTCI), and private-pay patients, pays caregivers the highest base rate in the state, and helps unpaid family caregivers get paid through programs they may not know they qualify for. Cova operates a home care platform that connects caregivers with families needing in-home assistance, using an AI-driven operational model to reduce traditional agency overhead while maximizing caregiver compensation. Founded in 2026 by Jordan Ibe and Ansh Tandon, the team is based in Detroit, Michigan. Cova also runs MichiganHomeHelp.com as a Medicaid Home Help information resource. As a consumer home-care service, Cova does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.
c.name: Cova

c.description: Coval is the deployment-readiness platform for voice and chat AI agents. Teams simulate thousands of realistic conversation scenarios before launch, monitor real production calls, and improve reliability with metrics and human review. Coval supports inbound/outbound voice, standard chat, chat over WebSocket, chat A2A (JSON-RPC), voice-to-voice models (OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live), SMS, Pipecat, and LiveKit agents. Its v1 REST API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, Homebrew CLI, and hosted MCP server let developers connect agents, define personas and test sets, launch simulation runs, ingest production conversations and OpenTelemetry traces, define deterministic/statistical/ML/LLM-judge metrics, and route critical calls to human reviewers. Coval is backed by General Catalyst and is SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant.
c.name: Coval

c.description: Coval is a simulation and evaluation platform for AI voice and chat agents. Inspired by autonomous-vehicle testing, it simulates end customers across realistic scenarios, personas, accents, and background noise, then scores agent behavior with built-in and custom metrics. The REST API manages agents, test sets and test cases, personas, metrics, simulation runs, and production conversations.
c.name: Coval

c.description: Covalent provides multi-chain blockchain data infrastructure, published as the GoldRush APIs. Its API covers token balances, transactions, transfers, ABIs, NFTs, DeFi positions and cross-chain queries across supported networks, including Bitcoin and Hyperliquid.

c.description: Covalent (Covalent Networks) is a workforce operations software company for industrial manufacturing teams in the aerospace & defense and automotive sectors, with Fortune 500 manufacturing clients including Boeing. Its platform connects workforce skills, task execution and production data to digitize on-the-job training, capability and skills management, intelligent work allocation, workforce scheduling, and workflow automation with audit reporting, replacing paper-based shop-floor processes. Covalent exposes a GraphQL API and bidirectional integrations to move workforce, skills and production data across enterprise systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, UKG, Microsoft, and LMS/ERP/MES platforms. API access is authenticated with AWS Cognito (OAuth2/OIDC with MFA) and provisioned per tenant. The company is headquartered in Boston, MA and is backed by Felicis.

c.description: Covalto (formerly Credijusto) is a Mexican digital bank for small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Mexico City. It offers business and personal checking accounts, fixed-rate investment products, quick working-capital credit (Agil Covalto), factoring, leasing (arrendamiento), and fiduciary trust services (fideicomisos). Covalto acquired a regulated Mexican banking license, making it one of the first fintechs in Mexico to become a fully licensed bank. Its digital surface spans online banking, digital account opening, and a credit application flow. Covalto is backed by QED Investors. As of the latest review it publishes no public API developer portal; its developer documentation at docs.covalto.com is gated behind Google Identity-Aware Proxy for internal use.

In 2023, the clinical development business was spun off as Fortrea, an independent CRO headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, operating in 90+ countries and serving the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries with clinical trial management, central laboratory, and bioanalytical services. No public API or developer portal is currently published; integrations are arranged through sponsor and partner agreements.
c.name: Covance (Fortrea)

c.description: Covariant is an Emeryville, California warehouse-robotics AI company founded in 2017 (originally as Embodied Intelligence) by UC Berkeley professor Pieter Abbeel and his former students Peter Chen, Rocky Duan, and Tianhao Zhang. The company builds the Covariant Brain, a universal AI platform that enables industrial picking robots to handle virtually any SKU regardless of shape, size, or packaging, and in March 2024 it introduced RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model 1), an 8-billion-parameter multimodal transformer trained on text, images, video, robot actions, and numerical sensor readings to give robots human-like reasoning over the physical world. Covariant ships AI-powered solutions for order picking, sortation, item induction, kitting, depalletization, and goods-to-person workflows, delivered through long-running integration partnerships with KNAPP (Pick-it-Easy Robot, since 2020) and ABB (warehouse robotics, since 2020), as well as deployments with retailers and logistics providers worldwide. In August 2024, Amazon announced a non-exclusive license to Covariant's robotic foundation models and hired its three co-founders along with roughly a quarter of its workforce in a reverse-acquihire arrangement; Covariant continues to operate independently under COO-turned-CEO Ted Stinson and co-founder Tianhao Zhang. The Covariant Brain and RFM-1 are proprietary, deployed on-premise on partner robotics hardware, and the company has no public developer API, SDK, open-source release, or third-party developer program.
c.name: Covariant

c.description: Covatic is a UK-based, B Corp certified advertising technology company providing privacy-preserving audience intelligence and addressability for media owners, broadcasters, publishers, and advertisers. Its platform uses on-device (edge) processing to build audience segments and demographic cohorts without third-party cookies, shared user IDs, or personal data leaving the device. Products include Covatic Sense for individual-level connected TV (CTV) addressability and attribution, a next-generation audience DMP for enrichment, clean-room data sharing, retargeting and attribution, plus audio, podcast, and smart-speaker targeting. Covatic integrates via the Covatic Tag (no-code tag manager), the Covatic SDK (on-device processing), and a server-to-server Covatic API, with a Google Ad Manager publishing path and client data stored in EU, AU, or US regions to meet local requirements.
c.name: Covatic

c.description: Cove is a visual workspace for thinking with AI — an AI collaborator that works alongside you on projects big and small in a spatial, canvas-style interface rather than a linear chat. The product pairs an on-screen agent that can search the web, write and run code, and cite sources with a flexible visual surface for organizing ideas, and it ships an accompanying Chrome browser extension. Cove is a consumer/prosumer application backed by the venture firm Homebrew; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation. This entry tracks Cove in the API Evangelist network, with domain-security posture captured by the enrichment pipeline.
c.name: Cove

c.description: cove.tool (rebranded to "cove" in 2025) is an Atlanta, Georgia building-performance analysis platform for architects, engineers and contractors, founded in 2017 by Sandeep Ahuja, Patrick Chopson and Daniel Chopson. Its analysis.tool engine runs energy, daylight, glare, embodied carbon, water, radiation, shadow and cost-versus-performance optimization on early-stage building designs. The company publishes a public REST API — marketed as api.tool — that lets software vendors and design firms create projects, upload building geometry, select an energy code, kick off daylight and energy simulation, poll job status and retrieve EUI, sDA and ASE results without using the web application. Two OpenAPI 3.0 definitions are served from the developer portal: a three-operation v1 and a thirteen-operation v2.

c.description: Coventry Building Society is the United Kingdom's second-largest building society, a member-owned mutual founded in 1884 and headquartered in Coventry, England, offering savings and residential mortgages to millions of members and in January 2025 completing its acquisition of The Co-operative Bank. As an FCA-authorised and PRA-regulated deposit-taker and Account Servicing Payment Service Provider (ASPSP), it participates in UK Open Banking under PSD2 and the Open Banking Implementation Entity (OBIE) standards. It is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks, but operates a public developer portal at developer.coventrybuildingsociety.co.uk that publishes CBS v2.0 Open Banking APIs - Account Information Services (AIS), Payment Initiation Services (PIS), and Confirmation of Funds (CBPII) - conformant to the OBIE Read/Write API Standard, alongside a public FCA Service Metrics open-data endpoint and a sandbox for TPP onboarding. Read/Write access is secured with FAPI-grade OAuth2/OIDC, PSD2 strong customer authentication, and mutual-TLS using Open Banking WAC or eIDAS QWAC certificates, with registered TPP onboarding handled via open.banking@thecoventry.co.uk.

The Coveo platform exposes a family of REST APIs covering search, content indexing (Push and Stream), usage analytics, machine learning, commerce, and platform administration.

c.description: Cover (Cover Technologies Inc.) is a Los Angeles-based construction technology company that designs and builds custom, architect-grade backyard homes, accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and residential spaces using a prefabricated, factory-manufactured building system. Cover handles the full development process end to end, from initial consultation and design through permitting, manufacturing, and on-site installation, delivering custom spaces in weeks rather than years. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. Cover is a physical-product homebuilder and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

Its Connected Platform helps providers, health plans, and employers improve diagnostic accuracy and care coordination across high-cost conditions including musculoskeletal disorders, cancer, neurological disease, heart disease, chronic pain, and metabolic disease. Certified as a Patient Safety Organization by AHRQ, Covera focuses on reducing misdiagnosis, unnecessary cost, and patient harm from the point of diagnosis through care delivery, prior authorization, and claims administration. Backed by Insight Partners.

c.description: Coverdash is a digital business insurance agency that provides fully‑digital, instant business insurance solutions for small and medium‑sized enterprises. Founded in 2022 and based in New York City, Coverdash offers a range of coverages—including General Liability, Workers’ Compensation, Cyber, Professional Liability, and Commercial Auto—through a streamlined online platform that connects businesses with top‑rated carriers, delivering quotes and policies in minutes without brokers or paperwork.

c.description: CoverForce is a commercial insurance distribution infrastructure platform headquartered in New York City. It provides a unified RESTful API and white-label software that let insurance agencies, agency networks, wholesalers, carriers, insurtechs, and developers digitally submit, quote, compare, bind, pay, and issue commercial insurance policies across 40+ carriers and MGAs through a single integration. Coverage spans Workers' Compensation, General Liability, Business Owners Policy (BOP), Cyber, Commercial Auto, Inland Marine, Management Liability (D&O, EPLI, Fiduciary), Product Liability, and Miscellaneous Professional Liability across all 50 US states. The API exposes Applications, Quotes, Bind, Document AI, Renewals, Appetite, Status, Analytics, and Documents endpoints, backed by AI capabilities for document reading and carrier-code mapping. Founded in 2021 and backed by Insight Partners, Nyca Partners, and QED Investors; named to the CB Insights Insurtech 50 in 2025.
c.name: Coverforce

c.description: Coverfox is one of India's largest online insurance distribution platforms, offering retail insurance products including car, bike, health, and life insurance alongside embedded insurance solutions for lenders, NBFCs, and fintechs. The company partners with 37+ IRDAI-approved insurers to compare, purchase, and manage policies online, and has reached roughly 10 million households across India. Coverfox was backed by Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer program or API at this time.
c.name: Coverfox

c.description: CoverHound is an InsurTech marketplace, now part of Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO), that lets consumers and small businesses compare and buy insurance online from A-rated carriers across all 50 states. Its platform covers personal lines — auto, homeowners, and renters — alongside business insurance including general liability, workers' compensation, professional liability, commercial auto, cyber, and directors & officers coverage. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Carpinteria, California, CoverHound provides digital quote comparison, agent-assisted purchasing, and an insurance learning center. It operates as a consumer/SMB web marketplace and publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface.
c.name: CoverHound

c.description: CoverStar is a safe social platform designed as an alternative to TikTok for children and teens aged 9-16. It emphasizes creativity, positivity, and safety through AI‑assisted and human moderation, with no direct messages and strict content controls. The app offers avatar‑based creation, live streaming, challenges, and a marketplace for creative expression, aiming to provide a secure online community for young users.
c.name: CoverStar

c.description: CoverWallet, an Aon company, is a digital insurance marketplace with a REST API for quoting, binding, and managing small business insurance policies across multiple carriers. The platform supports general liability, business owners policy (BOP), professional liability, workers compensation, commercial property, and other commercial lines. Partners can integrate real-time quoting, underwriting, binding, billing, and servicing capabilities directly into their applications.

Their continuous underwriting engine uses real‑time vehicle data, telematics and risk analytics to underwrite policies in minutes, helping fleets reduce losses and improve safety. c.description: Coviu is an Australian telehealth company, headquartered in Sydney and spun out of CSIRO's Data61, that provides a purpose-built video consultation platform for healthcare providers, allied health, and enterprise clinical networks. Its browser-based, WebRTC video calling supports virtual care workflows including waiting rooms, in-call clinical tools, screen and file sharing, medical device integrations, and payments. For developers, Coviu ships a secure OAuth2-protected REST API (base https://api.coviu.com) that lets applications create and manage video consultation Sessions and Participants, monitor Waiting Area queues in real time, retrieve Collections (submissions, files, and audio recordings), and receive event Webhooks, plus an in-call Plugin API and embedded iframe mode. Coviu is a telehealth video/interoperability layer rather than an EHR or FHIR data platform, so its documented public surface is REST + webhooks, not HL7 FHIR.
c.name: Coviu

c.description: Covr Financial Technologies provides a digital insurance platform for financial institutions and advisors, simplifying life, long-term care, disability, and specialty insurance sales. The SaaS solution connects consumers with multiple carriers, offering personalization, speed, and choice, and serves over 30,000 financial advisors and 40 million consumers.
