c.description: Cowbell is a Pleasanton, California-based adaptive cyber insurance provider serving small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and the middle market with standalone cyber liability coverage, technology errors & omissions (Tech E&O), management liability, and excess cyber products. Founded in 2019, Cowbell pioneered continuous underwriting through its proprietary Cowbell Factors risk benchmarking, which scores organizations against millions of data points to surface vulnerabilities and prioritize remediation. The company pairs its policies with a closed-loop resiliency program (assess-insure-respond-improve) that includes complimentary risk assessments, Cowbell Insights threat detection, incident response planning, cybersecurity awareness training, micro-penetration testing, and vendor risk assessments, plus subscription-based managed detection and response (MDR), penetration testing, identity monitoring (IdentityAI), and Compliance-as-a-Service (COMPaaS). Cowbell operates across the United States (all 50 states plus DC), the United Kingdom, and Australia, is backed by reinsurance partners including Zurich, and offers a public developer program at developers.cowbellcyber.ai exposing REST APIs for agencies, accounts, risk factors, quoting, binding, policy management, and webhooks across its Prime 100, Prime 250, and PrimeOne products. The API surface powers digital aggregator integrations with partners such as Bold Penguin, Herald, Semsee, Sayata, Limit, iBynd, and AmWins. No public OpenAPI specification or open-source SDK is published by Cowbell.
c.name: Cowbell

c.description: Cowbell Cyber, Inc. provides AI‑native adaptive cyber and specialty insurance for small and medium‑size enterprises. Leveraging data and artificial intelligence, it offers real‑time risk assessment, automated underwriting, and API‑based quoting to simplify cyber coverage and improve resilience for businesses.
c.name: Cowbellcyberinc

c.description: Cowboy is a Brussels-based mobility company that designs and manufactures premium connected electric bicycles for urban commuting. Its lineup — the Cruiser, Cruiser ST, Cross, and Cross ST — pairs a lightweight frame with removable batteries, integrated GPS tracking, crash detection, and its proprietary AdaptivePower motor assistance, all managed through the Cowboy mobile app. The company sells direct-to-consumer and through a network of 125+ service centers and mobile technicians across 40+ European cities, complemented by leasing, business, and student programs. Backed by Index Ventures, Cowboy operates a Shopify-based storefront and a connected-bike app platform; it does not publish a public developer API. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the company's real identity, legal, support, and security surfaces.
c.name: Cowboy

c.description: Cowboy Clean Fuels (CCF) is a Denver, Colorado climate-technology company, founded in 2020 and operating in Gillette, Wyoming, that produces carbon-negative renewable natural gas (RNG) while permanently sequestering atmospheric carbon dioxide. CCF injects non-food-grade organic biomass — residue products of sugar-beet refining such as molasses — into depleted coal bed methane (CBM) wells in the Powder River Basin, where naturally occurring methanogenic microorganisms convert the feedstock into methane and carbon dioxide; the coal seam then selectively adsorbs and permanently stores the CO2. Its lead development is the Triangle Unit Renewable Energy and Carbon Capture and Storage Project (TRECCS) near Gillette, Wyoming, and in May 2025 it signed an offtake agreement with Mercuria for RNG produced under its BiCRS+RNG methodology. Cowboy Clean Fuels is an energy and carbon-dioxide-removal operator, not a software vendor: it sells molecules and carbon removal credits, and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification.
c.name: Cowboy Clean Fuels

c.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is an American orbital-infrastructure company founded in 2024 by Baiju Bhatt, co-founder and former co-CEO of Robinhood, headquartered in San Carlos, California with a second site in Seattle, Washington. It operated as Aetherflux Inc. from founding until May 2026, when it renamed to Cowboy Space Corporation and broadened its mission from space-based solar power alone to vertically integrated orbital infrastructure for the AI era, spanning launch vehicles, space-based power generation and in-orbit compute. Its flagship program is Stampede, a Low Earth Orbit constellation of satellites that harvest solar power to run on-orbit GPU data centers, with the first Galactic Brain data-center node targeted for early 2027 using NVIDIA Space-1 Vera Rubin modules and a small infrared power-beaming demonstrator satellite planned for 2026. The company concluded that launch supply was the binding constraint on orbital compute and is therefore also developing its own rocket, sized between Falcon 9 and Starship at roughly 20,000-25,000 kg of payload, whose upper stage is itself the payload - each one intended to become a one-megawatt orbital data center - with a first launch targeted for the end of 2028. It has raised roughly USD 365 million to date, including a USD 50 million Series A in April 2025 and a USD 275 million Series B in May 2026 at a USD 2 billion valuation, led by Index Ventures with IVP, Blossom Capital, SAIC, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA and Interlagos participating. Cowboy Space is a space hardware and energy infrastructure company, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no public GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its entire public web presence is a four-page Framer-hosted marketing site (home, terms, privacy, media terms of use) plus an Ashby-hosted careers board.
c.name: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux)

c.description: Cowboy Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Aileen Lee (who coined the term "unicorn" for billion-dollar startups) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The firm backs pre-seed and seed-stage founders building "life-changing" products for large and growing markets, with roughly 70% of investments made pre-product and a strong seed-to-Series A graduation rate. Typical first checks run from about $100K up to $1M, with a sweet spot near $500K–$800K. Cowboy invests across enterprise software, fintech, software infrastructure and security, healthcare, consumer, future of work, and vertical software, primarily in the United States. The firm has made 100+ early-stage investments and cultivates a curated community of founders, operators, and tech leaders. Notable portfolio companies include Chime, Guild, Drata, Dollar Shave Club, Ironclad, Aura, Kiavi, Crunchbase, and Product Hunt.
c.name: Cowboy Ventures

c.description: Cowin & Company, Inc. is a Birmingham‑based mining construction firm founded in 1924, offering a wide range of underground and surface mining services such as highwall stabilization, aggregate mining, tunnel construction, and shotcrete. With over a century of experience, the company emphasizes safety, skilled personnel, and custom engineering solutions for clients across the United States.
c.name: Cowin

c.description: An independent search and comparison platform for coworking spaces and flexible workspace across Europe and the Middle East, exposing a read-only REST API and a hosted MCP server with operator-published prices, amenities and location data. Holds no availability and books nothing; free with no commission and no API key required for reads.
c.name: CoworkingView API

c.description: Cowrywise is a Nigerian wealth management platform and SEC-licensed fund manager offering savings plans, investment portfolios, dollar accounts, and financial goal tracking for individuals. The Embed API provides investment-as-a-service capabilities, enabling developers to integrate regulated African investment products — including savings, mutual funds, treasury bills, Eurobonds, and equities — into their own applications via a single REST API with OAuth 2.0 authentication.
c.name: Cowrywise

c.description: Cox Automotive is one of the world's largest providers of products and services spanning the automotive ecosystem, operating a portfolio of brands that includes Manheim (wholesale vehicle auctions and remarketing), Kelley Blue Book (vehicle valuations and editorial data), Autotrader, Dealertrack (DMS, registration and titling, credit applications), vAuto, VinSolutions, Xtime, Dealer.com, HomeNet and Esntial. Its public API surface is split across several developer properties: the Kelley Blue Book Developer Portal (developer.kbb.com) publishes Swagger 2.0 contracts for the IDWS 4.0 vehicle and editorial services, the Advertising Data API, the Instant Cash Offer API and the Batch VIN API; the Manheim Developer Portal (developer.manheim.com) documents a hypermedia REST suite covering auctions, inventory, marketplace offerings, valuations, condition reports, images, users and a publish/subscribe event notification service; and the Cox Automotive Integration Platform / API Storefront (developer.coxautoinc.com) fronts the partner-gated catalogue of more than seventy runtime services visible on the public Cox Automotive API status page. Access to every environment is granted after a review by a Cox Automotive account representative, with keys issued through the Boomi/Mashery gateway.
c.name: Cox Automotive

c.description: Cox Communications is a leading American telecommunications provider offering broadband internet, cable TV, and phone services for residential and business customers. Cox provides REST APIs for account management, service configuration, network diagnostics, and customer portal integrations across its broadband, cable television, and voice service platforms.
c.name: Cox Communications

c.description: Coyote Logistics is a global third-party logistics (3PL) provider and freight brokerage platform, now part of RXO, offering REST APIs for truckload capacity, less-than-truckload (LTL) shipping, freight quoting, shipment tracking, load management, customs brokerage, and supply chain visibility. Originally founded in 2006 and acquired by UPS in 2015, Coyote was subsequently acquired by RXO in 2024. The CoyoteGO API platform serves both shippers and carriers, providing real-time freight quotes, live tracking updates, and load booking capabilities. The API uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow and is backed by a network of 100,000 carriers serving 15,000 customers. Integration is available at no additional cost for shippers and carriers working with Coyote, with native connectors to leading TMS, WMS, and ERP systems.
c.name: Coyote Logistics

c.description: Cozen O'Connor is a full-service U.S. law firm founded in 1970 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with more than 1,000 attorneys across 33+ offices in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The firm is ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and is best known for its nationally recognized subrogation, insurance, labor and employment, global corporate, intellectual property, and government relations practices. Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies, the firm's bipartisan federal, state, and local government affairs and lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. and major state capitals. The firm operates an unusually broad thought-leadership network of LexBlog/WordPress-powered blogs and podcasts (subrogation, cyber law, health law, state AGs, transformative AI, OSHA, employment law, family law, property insurance, casualty coverage, real estate / land use, professional responsibility, and a Public Strategies feed), each of which exposes a standard `/feed/` RSS endpoint. Cozen O'Connor does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization. This profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface — practice and industry pages, attorney directory, ancillary businesses, lobbying arm, and the blog/podcast RSS network — rather than a developer platform.
c.name: Cozen O'Connor

c.description: Cozy Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) risk-management protocol that helps onchain protocols unlock safety-seeking capital through composable, institutional-grade coverage. Its Cozy Safety Module (CSM) lets teams deploy onchain safety modules, rewards managers, and controllers that backstop capital against security incidents and market risk, using mechanisms such as tranching (junior/senior yield), reserves, and market-based protection contracts. The protocol is used by teams around protocols such as Euler, Lido, and Aave, and is backed by Polychain Capital, Electric Capital, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures. The integration surface is Solidity smart contracts documented at csm-docs.cozy.finance, with TypeScript / ethers.js developer guides; there is no REST or HTTP API.
c.name: Cozy Finance

c.description: CPA.com, founded in 2001 as an affiliate of the American Institute of CPAs (AICPA), empowers accounting firms and finance teams for the digital age. It offers technology solutions, advisory services, and resources across practice areas such as audit, tax, and practice management. The company provides insights, research, webinars, and a community to help firms adopt innovative technologies and stay competitive.
c.name: CPA.com

c.description: cPacket Networks provides advanced network observability, packet broker, and packet capture solutions powered by AI. Their platform offers unified visibility across on-prem, hybrid, and multi‑cloud environments, delivering real‑time analytics, security insights, and automated workflows. With a focus on AI‑driven operations, cPacket helps enterprises reduce mean time to resolution, improve security posture, and streamline network management through scalable, agentless solutions.
c.name: cPacket Networks

c.description: CPower Energy is a commercial and industrial (C&I) virtual power plant (VPP) operator that helps organizations monetize the flexibility of their energy assets through demand response and distributed energy resource (DER) programs. Its CPower CONNECT platform lets customers view, manage, and unlock revenue from energy assets while supporting grid reliability and sustainability goals. CPower serves data centers, crypto mining, healthcare, education, retail, commercial real estate, industrial operations, and the public sector, and has operated distributed energy programs across the U.S. since 2015. CPower was acquired by NRG Energy and operates a combined C&I VPP platform. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent deep-tech lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; CPower publishes a customer portal and a security and compliance posture but no public developer API at this time.

c.description: CPS (Cheapest-Power Scheduler) provides a cloud-based platform that enables users to schedule and optimize power usage for compute workloads. By integrating with major cloud providers, CPS offers cost-effective power allocation, real-time monitoring, and automated scaling to reduce electricity expenses while maintaining performance. The service includes a dashboard, API access, and billing options for pilot and production use.
c.name: CPS (Cheapest-Power Scheduler)

c.description: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) is an architectural pattern that separates read and write operations for a data store into distinct models. Commands mutate state and produce events; queries return data optimized for the read side. CQRS is frequently combined with Event Sourcing, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), and message-based integration to scale complex domains. The pattern is most associated with Greg Young, building on Bertrand Meyer's Command-Query Separation principle, and is widely covered in writings by Martin Fowler and the Microsoft Patterns and Practices team.
c.name: CQRS

c.description: CQuotient is the artificial intelligence and shopper-data technology that powers personalization and predictive commerce for Salesforce B2C Commerce (Commerce Cloud) Einstein. Originally an independent commerce-personalization startup, CQuotient was acquired by Demandware in 2013, and Demandware was in turn acquired by Salesforce in 2016. Today the CQuotient engine underpins Einstein product recommendations, predictive sort, Einstein search dictionaries, and shopper activity capture. Its developer surface is the Salesforce B2C Commerce Einstein API (also referred to as the CQuotient API), documented within the Salesforce Developers documentation rather than on a standalone CQuotient portal.
c.name: CQuotient

c.description: Crabi is a Mexican digital auto-insurance company (insurtech) offering fully online vehicle policies purchasable in about fifteen minutes from a mobile device. Coverage spans material damage, theft, third-party civil liability, medical expenses, and roadside and legal assistance across 27 Mexican states, sold and serviced through its mobile apps, online quoter (cotizador), and customer login portal. The company is regulated in Mexico by the CNSF and CONDUSEF and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Crabi publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.
c.name: Crabi

c.description: Cracked is a tool router for AI agents: one API key and one prepaid balance to discover, inspect, run and poll thousands of third-party tools. It exposes 9,521 endpoints from 1,183 providers plus 50,000+ Apify actors, publishing measured success rate, median latency and per-call price per tool.
c.name: Cracked API

c.description: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. is an American chain of restaurants and gift shops with a Southern country theme, offering home-style meals and retail merchandise. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Lebanon, Tennessee, Cracker Barrel operates roughly 656 restaurant and retail locations across 44 U.S. states. No public API or developer portal is published; the company offers a consumer website, iOS and Android mobile ordering apps, To-Go and catering ordering, gift cards, and the Cracker Barrel Rewards loyalty program for guests.
c.name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store

c.description: Cradle is a Dutch–Swiss biotechnology software company founded in 2021 with headquarters in Amsterdam and an office in Zurich, building an AI-powered protein engineering platform for industrial biotech and biopharma R&D teams. The platform combines proprietary generative AI models — trained on billions of natural protein sequences and on data produced in Cradle's own Amsterdam wet lab — with a web application and REST API/Python SDK so that scientists can design, simulate, and co-optimize amino-acid sequence variants across multiple measurable properties such as activity, binding affinity, stability, expression, and developability. Core platform capabilities include AI candidate generation, multi-property co-optimization, virtual plate design, experimental data management with full versioning and audit trails, task orchestration (analyze data, diversify, engineer, select, search, train) across modalities including antibodies/mAbs, enzymes, vaccines, therapeutic peptides, and food ingredients, plus a Custom Predictors framework letting customers plug in their own ML models. Cradle is sold as enterprise SaaS to R&D organizations — disclosed customers and partners include Johnson & Johnson Janssen, Bayer, Novozymes/Novonesis, and Twist Bioscience, with the platform serving six of the top 25 global pharma companies and over 50 active R&D programs. The company has raised approximately $115M to date across a seed round (Index Ventures, 2022), a $24M Series A (Index Ventures, 2023), and a $73M Series B (IVP, 2024). Co-founders are Stef van Grieken (CEO), Jelle Prins, Elise de Reus, Eli Bixby, and Harmen van Rossum.
c.name: Cradle

c.description: Cradlepoint is a Boise, Idaho-based provider of cloud-managed wireless edge routers, 5G adapters, branch-in-a-box appliances, and the NetCloud platform for enterprise wireless WAN (LTE/5G), in-vehicle networks, branch connectivity, and IoT. Ericsson acquired Cradlepoint in 2020 (closed November 2020 for approximately US$1.1B) and Cradlepoint now operates as the core of Ericsson Enterprise Wireless Solutions, working alongside Ericsson Private 5G and the Ericsson NetCloud SASE offering. Cradlepoint exposes its NetCloud Manager (NCM) platform through a documented RESTful API — NCM API v2 (Swagger 1.2, paired X-CP-API-ID/X-CP-API-KEY + X-ECM-API-ID/X-ECM-API-KEY headers, base https://www.cradlepointecm.com/api/v2/) and a newer NCM API v3 (OpenAPI 3.0, bearer-token authentication) — plus a NetCloud Router SDK for on-router Python applications and webhook destinations for alert delivery. The developer area (developer.cradlepoint.com), customer support article base (customer.cradlepoint.com), and Ericsson Enterprise Wireless docs portal (docs.cradlepoint.com) host the Getting Started guides, API reference, sample collections, and Postman bundles.
c.name: Cradlepoint

c.description: Cradlewise offers an all‑in‑one smart bassinet and crib that converts from a newborn bassinet to a toddler crib for up to 24 months. It includes a built‑in baby monitor, sound machine, and sleep‑tracking features, aiming to simplify nighttime care for parents. The product integrates IoT sensors and a companion app to provide real‑time insights and soothing sounds, positioning Cradlewise at the intersection of baby care and smart home technology.
c.name: Cradlewise

c.description: Craft (Craft Docs Ltd.) is a consumer and team productivity app that combines notes, documents, tasks, and daily planning in a single cross-platform workspace for macOS, iOS, iPadOS, Windows, and web. Beyond the end-user app, Craft exposes a developer surface through its "Imagine" platform: an official eXtension API (a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK, @craftdocs/craft-extension-api, for building extensions that run inside Craft), a Craft Connect REST API that exposes a user's Space, Daily Notes, tasks, and selected documents, and an official remote MCP server that connects Craft to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP clients. Documentation is published on a Mintlify help center with a machine-readable llms.txt, and the company states SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance.
c.name: craft

c.description: Craft CMS is a flexible, self-hosted PHP content management system built on Yii 2, designed for creating bespoke digital experiences. It features an auto-generated GraphQL API for headless implementations, enabling queries against entries, assets, categories, and custom fields via token-based authentication. The Element API plugin extends Craft with configurable JSON REST endpoints for any element type, using URL pattern routing and the Fractal transformation library. Craft supports multi-site architecture, unlimited content types, and is deployable on-premise or via Craft Cloud, the official managed hosting platform.
c.name: Craft CMS

c.description: Craft Ventures is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in late 2017 by repeat entrepreneurs David Sacks and Bill Lee, built "by founders for founders" and rooted in the operator playbook of the PayPal Mafia. The firm invests across early and growth stages, writing checks that range from micro-seed positions through double-digit millions, and specializes in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, and enterprise software prized for high-growth, high-margin, recurring-revenue economics. Craft is known for its rigorous, metrics-driven SaaS operating framework and hands-on support spanning talent, go-to-market, community, and finance. Beyond core SaaS, the portfolio spans artificial intelligence, developer tools, fintech and crypto, cybersecurity, digital health, defense, and frontier technology. The firm manages roughly $3.3 billion in assets across four early-stage funds and two growth funds, including Craft Ventures IV ($712M) and Craft Ventures Growth II ($608M). Notable investments include Airbnb, Affirm, Reddit, Uber, Lyft, Palantir, Slack, ElevenLabs, Supabase, Anduril, and Neuralink. Headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Austin, Texas, and a primarily United States geographic focus.
c.name: Craft Ventures

c.description: Craft.io is a product management platform with a REST API for managing product backlog, specifications, OKRs, roadmaps, and customer feedback across product teams. The public API provides enterprise customers programmatic access to workspace, portfolio, and feedback portal data, enabling integration with BI tools and organizational communication channels.
c.name: Craft.io

c.description: Craftable is hospitality's back-office software platform for restaurants, bars, hotels, and resorts, originally known for its Bevager and Foodager products, that connects purchasing, inventory, recipes, and accounts payable with accounting and sales data. Its suite spans Intelligent Ordering (eProcurement), AP Automation with Invoice AI, Inventory and Recipe Management, and Daily Actionable Insights, plus AI features such as Operator AI and the Crafty in-app assistant. Craftable is SOC 2 compliant and SSO-capable, with more than 1,000 POS, EDI, and vendor/API integrations spanning systems such as Toast, Square, Lightspeed, Clover, SpotOn, TouchBistro, Aloha by NCR Voyix, Restaurant365, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, and Xero. Craftable does not publish a public self-service developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; integrations are delivered through its implementation team during onboarding, and API access to a connected platform is provisioned by requesting a scoped API key from that platform's support team.
c.name: Craftable

c.description: Craftbank is a construction‑tech startup that operates an online platform matching general contractors with subcontractors, streamlining project sourcing and collaboration in the construction industry. It also hosts networking events for construction professionals and provides digital management solutions for the property sector.

c.description: Craft Coffee is a direct-to-consumer specialty coffee company operating since 2011 that sources, roasts, and ships freshly roasted coffee to subscribers across the United States. c.description: The Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA) is the national industry body for Canadian residential real estate, representing roughly 160,000 REALTORS through some 60 member boards and associations, owning the MLS and REALTOR trademarks in Canada, and operating REALTOR.ca - the country's single national consumer listing portal. Where the United States fragments into roughly 500 independently governed MLSs, Canada consolidates: CREA runs the REALTOR.ca Data Distribution Facility (DDF), one national syndication seam that collects listing content from member boards' MLS Systems and redistributes it to member websites, franchisor pools, and a network of Real Estate Advertising Websites. That makes CREA simultaneously the standards-setter (it writes the DDF Policy and Rules that boards must adopt and enforce), the operator of the pipe, and the gatekeeper of the data. Its API posture is unusually good for an industry body and still firmly gated. Three real machine-readable contracts are downloadable anonymously - an OpenAPI 3.0.4 document for the DDF Web API served from ddfapi.realtor.ca/swagger/v1/swagger.json and embedded in the public Redoc site at ddfapi-docs.realtor.ca, an OpenAPI 3.0.1 document for the REALTOR.ca Board API at boardapi-docs.realtor.ca, and a full OpenID Connect discovery document at identity.crea.ca. The DDF Web API is an OData v4 surface normalized to the RESO Data Dictionary and described by CREA as built on the RESO Web API specification, but CREA is RESO-aligned rather than RESO-certified - it does not appear in RESO's public certification directory of 578 organizations, where the only Canadian entries are individual boards such as the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board and Greater Vancouver REALTORS, none of them Certified Current. Nothing is self-serve. There is no signup, no sandbox and no free tier; client_id and client_secret are, in CREA's own words, provided by CREA. A REALTOR must opt in through the DDF Dashboard on CREA's member portal, and a third-party developer must enter a data access agreement with CREA as a Technology Provider operating a National Pool Website or Member Website on behalf of that opted-in member. The OData $metadata document, the actual RESO contract, returns HTTP 401 to anonymous callers. No open, unlicensed Canadian listing dataset exists behind any of it.
c.name: CREA (REALTOR.ca)

Its public REST API — documented on a Stoplight portal at apidocs.creatoriq.com and served from https://apis.creatoriq.com — exposes the customer's own CRM: publishers (creators), campaigns, lists, one-sheets, notes, divisions, social accounts and post/account metrics, an asynchronous reporting surface of forty report views, ecommerce promo codes and transactions, affiliate link tracking, conversion metrics, SafeIQ brand-safety scoring, and a Payments API for payouts and payables. A pub/sub webhook API lets integrators subscribe to campaign, creator, one-sheet and list events with MD5 and SHA-256 signed callbacks. Authentication is a single `x-api-key` header issued per partner or per division by a CreatorIQ account manager; there is no self-serve signup.
c.name: CreatorIQ

c.description: CRED is an Indian consumer fintech that started with premium credit-card bill payments and rewards and has expanded into peer-to-peer payments (Scan & Pay, Tap to Pay, RuPay credit card on UPI), short-term credit (CRED Cash, CRED Mint), wealth (CRED Money), e-commerce (CRED Store), and travel. CRED's surface area is overwhelmingly consumer-app and the company does not publish a public, self-service developer portal. Its engineering organisation contributes to the broader ecosystem via the engineering.cred.club tech blog and open-source repositories under the CRED-CLUB GitHub org. B2B integrations (merchant acceptance, issuer partnerships, etc.) are negotiated directly with the partnerships team.
c.name: CRED

c.description: Cred6ab0 is a stub company identified in the secondary-market harvest. It currently has no publicly documented API or website. The profile aims to gather any future information about its services, documentation, and API offerings as they become available, ensuring the API Evangelist network can track its development and potential integrations.
c.name: Cred6ab0

c.description: Credence MedSystems is a healthcare technology company focused on providing advanced medical device integration platforms for hospitals and clinics. The firm offers middleware solutions that connect diagnostic equipment, electronic health records, and patient monitoring systems, enabling seamless data exchange and workflow automation. Their services aim to improve clinical efficiency, data accuracy, and patient outcomes through secure, scalable integration services.
c.name: Credence MedSystems

c.description: Credentially is a UK-founded, healthcare-only onboarding and compliance automation platform used by NHS trusts, private providers, urgent care and clinical staffing agencies in the UK and US. It brings pre-employment checks, DBS and right-to-work validation, primary source verification, credentialing and continuous compliance monitoring onto one platform, cutting the platform-managed steps of onboarding clinical staff from an industry average of around 60 days to as little as 5. The Credentially Public API (OpenAPI 3.1) exposes profiles, placements, documents with OCR auto-fill, DBS checks, references, right-to-work status and compliance packages, with a companion Webhook API for state-change events.
c.name: Credentially

c.description: CredFlow AI provides AI‑driven credentialing and payer enrollment solutions for healthcare providers. Their platform automates credentialing software, services, and modules, offering network lookup, payer directory auditing, and AI telecaller agents. The service supports CAQH, Medicare PECOS, and major insurers, handling applications across 22 payer portals with high completion rates.
c.name: Credflow

c.description: Credgenics is an AI-powered debt collection and loan recovery SaaS platform used by banks, NBFCs, housing-finance companies, microfinance institutions, fintechs and asset-reconstruction companies (primarily in India). Its REST Recovery API lets lenders push loan, customer, payment and transaction data into the platform and read collections status, DPD and penalties back, alongside digital communications, a GenAI voicebot (Swara), predictive dialing (DialNext), field collections (CG Collect), litigation management, online dispute resolution and the Billzy loan-repayment payments product. Authentication is a client-credentials exchange returning a short-lived `authenticationtoken`; every request carries the tenant `company_id`.
c.name: Credgenics

c.description: Credi2 GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based fintech that operates a white-label, cloud-native embedded lending platform enabling banks, card issuers, and merchants to launch Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and installment financing products under their own brand. The modular platform covers five financing products - pay per invoice (14-day BNPL), split pay (3-12 month installments up to EUR 5,000), installment loans (up to EUR 50,000 over 84 months), revolving credit lines, and subscription financing - and handles the full lifecycle including core banking operations, credit and risk management, servicing, and collections. Use cases span eCommerce and point-of-sale financing, subscription payments, installment-on-cards, and cash loans, with omni-channel integration and go-live in weeks. Credi2 is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified and is backed by Speedinvest.
c.name: Credi2

c.description: Credibly is a small business lending platform offering a REST API (API V2) for originating merchant cash advances, working capital loans, business lines of credit, equipment financing, and SBA loans through an approved broker and referral partner network. The API supports application submission, multi-part document uploads, stipulation identification, and webhook-based status notifications within a SOC 2-compliant environment.
c.name: Credibly

c.description: CrediFi is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-20 found no independent live surface for CrediFi — credifi.com redirects to actovia.com, a commercial real estate data provider — so this profile is retained as a historical record rather than an active API provider.
c.name: CrediFi

c.description: Credijusto, now operating under the brand Covalto, is a digital bank for businesses in Mexico offering unsecured financing, credit lines, and financial services through an online platform. The service provides quick, fully digital loan approvals, supports various business needs, and is backed by the IPAB and regulated by Condusef, ensuring security and compliance for SMEs.
c.name: Credijusto

c.description: CrediLinq is a Singapore-founded embedded-finance and B2B lending fintech that lets platforms and marketplaces offer white-labeled credit to their business customers. Its API-first "Credit as a Service" powers two products: B2B PayLater (buy-now-pay-later for buyers) and GMV Financing (working-capital advances for sellers), with AI/data-driven credit underwriting, automated onboarding and KYC, credit-line management, loan drawdowns, repayments and reconciliation, and partner reporting. The CrediLinq REST API (OpenAPI 3.0, Auth0 client-credentials bearer auth, sandbox/staging/production environments, HMAC-signed webhooks) is documented at docs.credilinq.ai.
c.name: Credilinq.ai

c.description: Credit Agricole is a leading French banking group offering a wide range of retail, corporate and investment banking services. It serves millions of customers through an extensive network of branches and digital channels, providing accounts, loans, payments, insurance and wealth management solutions. The group emphasizes innovation and digital transformation, supporting developers with online services and APIs across its financial ecosystem.
c.name: Credit Agricole

c.description: Credit Benchmark is a financial data company that aggregates internal credit risk assessments contributed by more than 40 leading global financial institutions into anonymized, consensus Credit Consensus Ratings and analytics covering roughly 120,000 public and private entities — over 90% of which are unrated by the traditional credit rating agencies. Its REST API delivers consensus ratings, rating distributions, aggregate credit trends, entity rating changes, and portfolio analytics, along with entity-name-to-CBID resolution (matching) and contributor-data analytics. Delivery is also available via a web app, an Excel Add-In, and file/SFTP feeds. Access is enterprise/sales-gated; the JWT-authenticated API base is https://api.creditbenchmark.com.
c.name: Credit Benchmark

c.description: Credit Genie is a consumer fintech operated by Creditly Corp. (Wilmington, Delaware, founded 2019) that runs a mobile-first money app for people living between paychecks. Its Cash Boost product advances $10-$150 with no interest and no hard credit check, funded against a linked bank account rather than a credit score, while Money Manager layers spending tracking, cash-flow prediction and subscription detection on top of that same bank connection. A Line of Credit product and AskGenie, an AI financial assistant, are in early access. Creditly Corp. is registered with the California DFPI under the CCFPL (registration 04-CCFPL-1956127-3514680) and has raised roughly $21M from Fortress Investment Group, Khosla Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures, Tippet Venture Partners and Gabriel Investments. Credit Genie is a direct-to-consumer app company: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind.
c.name: Credit Genie

c.description: Credit Karma is an AI-powered personal finance platform founded in 2007 and owned by Intuit since 2020, serving more than 140 million members in the US, UK and Canada. It began as a free credit-score and credit-monitoring destination and has grown into a broad consumer finance marketplace spanning credit cards, personal and auto loans, mortgages, auto and home insurance, banking (checking, savings and credit-builder accounts), tax filing, and identity monitoring. Credit Karma monetizes through personalized recommendations and lead generation rather than a public developer or partner API; it maintains no external consumer-facing API program. It does run an active engineering culture with 29 public open-source repositories on GitHub (Thrift and GraphQL tooling), a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program via HackerOne, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security certifications.
c.name: Credit Karma

c.description: Credit Key provides a B2B payment platform that offers buy‑now‑pay‑later financing, net‑30 terms, and installment options for wholesale distributors, technology vendors, and restaurant equipment suppliers. By underwriting credit at the point of sale, Credit Key enables merchants to increase conversions, average order value, and cash‑flow efficiency while assuming the risk of repayment. The platform includes a merchant portal, a consumer‑facing Credit Key Card, and an API for integrating financing into e‑commerce and in‑store checkout flows.
c.name: Credit Key

c.description: Credit Sesame is a consumer financial health platform that provides free daily credit-score monitoring, credit reports, and personalized recommendations for credit cards, loans, and insurance based on a member's approval likelihood. Members can build credit through everyday debit purchases and upgrade to the Sesame+ premium tier for three-bureau credit reports, advanced credit tools, and identity-theft protection. Credit Sesame operates consumer web and mobile applications and, as of this profile, does not publish a public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile backed by Menlo Ventures.
c.name: Credit Sesame

c.description: Creditas is a Brazilian digital lending fintech founded in 2012 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, operating in Brazil and Mexico. It provides secured consumer credit - loans backed by real estate (home equity) and vehicles, plus private payroll (consignado privado) loans - alongside auto insurance, multi-bank real estate and vehicle financing, and a corporate benefits platform (salary advance, flexible-benefits cards, and financial education). Regulated by the Banco Central do Brasil, Creditas has originated over R$12 billion in credit. It is backed by QED Investors and the SoftBank Vision Fund. No public developer API program or OpenAPI has been identified; this profile captures the company public identity, its published llms.txt, and its domain security posture.
c.name: Creditas

c.description: CreditPullEngine provides real‑time credit intelligence APIs that aggregate nationwide credit data into clean, actionable insights. Their platform serves fintechs, lenders, and debt‑settlement companies, offering products such as consumer reports, scoring models, and industry‑specific data. The service emphasizes compliance, security, and easy integration via RESTful endpoints, supporting developers with comprehensive documentation and sandbox environments.
c.name: CreditPullEngine

c.description: Credix47fb is a decentralized credit platform that provides borrowers in emerging markets with access to capital through a blockchain-based protocol. It offers credit lines to high-quality borrowers and attractive yields for global investors, leveraging AI and data analytics to assess credit risk. The company was founded in 2021 and focuses on financial inclusion, enabling credit access where traditional banking is limited.
c.name: Credix47fb

c.description: Credly is a digital credential and open badge platform, owned by Pearson (acquired 2022), used by more than 2,000 organizations to issue, manage, and verify verifiable digital badges and certifications. The Credly Web Service API (base https://api.credly.com/v1, with a sandbox at https://sandbox-api.credly.com/v1) lets issuing organizations create and manage badge templates, issue and revoke badges to recipients, read organization and employee data, pull an events feed, and expose recipient credentials via Open Badges Infrastructure (OBI) endpoints. Authentication is HTTP Basic (the organization's authorization_token as the username with a blank password) or OAuth 2.0 client_credentials. Real-time notifications are delivered via outbound webhooks (HTTPS POST callbacks), not a WebSocket.
c.name: Credly

c.description: Credo AI is an enterprise AI governance, risk, and compliance platform used to discover, register, risk-classify, and continuously govern every AI model, application, agent, and third-party AI vendor an organization runs. The platform pairs an AI Registry (use cases, models, vendors, agents, shadow-AI discovery) with a policy engine that turns regulatory frameworks — the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, NYC Local Law 144, Colorado SB21-169, OMB M-25 — into machine-enforced policy packs, controls, questionnaires, risk scenarios, and audit-ready evidence artifacts. Programmatic access is delivered through a multi-tenant JSON:API REST surface at api.credo.ai (300 operations across use cases, models, vendors, questionnaires, policy packs, policy controls, risks, tasks, teams, users, triggers, and Shadow AI), a first-party Python SDK (pycredoai) and TypeScript SDK (@credo-ai/sdk), and a published Claude Code plugin marketplace of eleven AI-governance Agent Skills backed by a gated Governance Intelligence Pro MCP server.
c.name: Credo AI

c.description: Credo Health is an AI‑powered SaaS platform that enables physicians, health plans, MSOs, and ACOs to deliver value‑based care. It integrates with leading EHRs, provides analytics, and supports patient diagnosis and treatment workflows. The platform offers solutions such as Acquire, Inspect, Engage, and Optimize, and serves a broad range of healthcare organizations to improve outcomes and efficiency.
c.name: Credo Health

c.description: Credo AI provides an AI governance platform that helps enterprises responsibly develop, adopt, procure, and use artificial intelligence at scale. The solution automates oversight, risk management, and compliance with emerging regulations such as the EU AI Act, NIST, and ISO standards, while keeping human control over AI systems. Founded in 2020 and based in Palo Alto, CA, Credo AI is recognized by CB Insights, the World Economic Forum, and Fast Company for its innovative approach to trustworthy AI.
c.name: Credoai

c.description: Credorax, now part of Shift4, provides a unified payments and commerce technology platform. It offers integrated solutions for online payments, point‑of‑sale, mobile, and contactless technologies across industries such as food & beverage, hospitality, sports & entertainment, travel, and retail. The platform enables businesses to deliver seamless customer experiences, manage fraud prevention, and access analytics through a comprehensive API suite.
c.name: Credorax

c.description: CredRight is a fintech technology provider based in Hyderabad, India, offering digital lending solutions for micro, small and medium enterprises. Founded in 2016, it uses alternate data and AI to assess creditworthiness, enabling fast, unsecured business loans to credit‑starved companies. The platform serves lenders and borrowers through an online portal and API-driven services, aiming to expand financial inclusion for underserved businesses.
c.name: Credright

c.description: Credy is a large advertising network operating in the consumer credit market, connecting publishers with lenders across 18 countries and 3 continents. It offers short‑term, payday, instalment and cash loans, serving over 1 million satisfied customers. The company provides a platform for advertisers to generate high‑quality leads and for publishers to monetize finance‑related traffic, with multilingual support and a presence in Spain, Mexico, Colombia, Vietnam, Philippines, Kazakhstan, Poland, Ukraine, Romania and more.
c.name: Credy

c.description: Creech Medical Technology Development is a company listed on EquityZen, offering pre-IPO shares for investors. The firm focuses on developing innovative medical technologies, aiming to improve patient outcomes through advanced devices and solutions. While detailed public information is limited, the listing indicates active engagement in capital raising and a commitment to advancing healthcare technology.
c.name: Creechmedicaltechnologydevelopment

c.description: Creed (Creed Labs, operated by Lemon Tree Labs Inc.) is a Brooklyn-based faith-tech company building an AI-powered Bible study, prayer, and Christian community app used by more than two million people. The consumer product pairs a voice-enabled AI companion (Lenny) with daily prayers, devotionals, scripture retrieval, a moderated prayer wall, learning plans, gratitude and prayer journaling, friend streaks, church discovery, leaderboards, and gamification. Creed also ships tools for churches and creators to grow and engage their congregations. Its public backend is a FastAPI service at api.usecreed.com exposing 191 operations across chatbot, prayer, church-admin, social, and gamification domains, secured with Supabase-issued JWT bearer tokens.
c.name: Creed

c.description: Creekstone Energy develops purpose‑built, behind‑the‑meter power generation for hyperscale AI data centers. Combining natural gas, solar, and storage, the company delivers multi‑source, high‑density, reliable electricity directly at AI campuses. Their flagship Delta Gigasite in Utah showcases over 10 GW in development, 100 % behind‑the‑meter generation, and 60+ kW per rack density, positioning Creekstone as a critical infrastructure provider for AI workloads.
c.name: Creekstoneenergy

c.description: Creem is a merchant-of-record payments platform built for SaaS and AI startups. Its REST API handles products, hosted checkouts, customers, subscriptions, transactions, discounts, and software license keys, while Creem acts as the merchant of record to manage global sales tax, VAT, fraud, and compliance on the seller's behalf.
c.name: Creem

c.description: Crema.co is an online specialty-coffee subscription platform and curated marketplace that connects coffee drinkers with independent roasters. Customers take a preference quiz, pick a delivery cadence ranging from every few days to monthly, and receive freshly roasted beans by mail from a rotating selection of more than a thousand coffees sourced from dozens of small-batch roasters. Crema also runs a workplace coffee program for offices. This is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer API or developer platform; the repository is retained in the network for completeness and provenance.
c.name: Crema

c.description: CreoPop is a consumer 3D-printing pen that lets you draw three-dimensional objects freehand. Unlike filament 3D pens it has no hot parts or melting plastic; instead it uses photopolymer "cool ink" cartridges that are solidified by built-in LEDs, and it is battery operated and charged over mini-USB. The product line includes specialty inks (elastic, magnetic, glow-in-the-dark, aromatic, temperature-sensitive, and electrically conductive). CreoPop is a hardware/consumer-electronics brand with a marketing and direct-to-consumer e-commerce website; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.
c.name: Creopop

c.description: Crescendo is an AI-native customer experience (CX) platform that unifies AI agents for chat, voice, email, and messaging with quality assurance, workforce management, and business insights. The Crescendo Platform API (OpenAPI 3.1) is a tenant-scoped HTTP API for provisioning tenant configuration and documents, exporting assistant and voice-of-customer (VOC) conversations for reporting with cursor pagination, uploading audio recordings for asynchronous VOC processing, and driving assistants through a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) bots server over Streamable HTTP. Authentication is a tenant-scoped bearer API key. Crescendo is backed by General Catalyst and Trinity Ventures.
c.name: Crescendo

c.description: Crescendo Bioscience was a molecular-diagnostics company based in South San Francisco, known for Vectra DA (later Vectra), a multi-biomarker blood test that measures disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and other venture investors, it was acquired by Myriad Genetics in 2014 and its diagnostic product now sits within Myriad. It has no independent public developer surface: no API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, and its former domains no longer resolve. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; no API artifacts apply.
c.name: Crescendo Bioscience

c.description: Crescendo Lab is a Taiwan-based, Asia-leading AI omnichannel customer communication software company (cresclab.com) serving 800+ global brands, and a LINE Biz-Solutions Gold Partner. Its platform spans MAAC (AI marketing automation), CAAC (conversational applications), and DAAC (data intelligence) across LINE, WhatsApp, SMS, email, and social channels. Its developer-facing surface is MAAC Go (sms.cresclab.com) — a self-serve, NCC-compliant Taiwan SMS API with a published OpenAPI spec, first-party Node/Python SDKs, a CLI, an official MCP server, and delivery webhooks. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Crescendo Lab

c.description: Crescendo874d is a software company offering a full-stack customer service platform that combines advanced AI with a global service team. Founded in 2024 and based in San Francisco, CA, it provides scalable solutions to optimize frontline and back‑office operations for fast‑moving, digitally‑native enterprises. The platform enables outcome‑driven results through augmented‑AI customer experience technology, targeting enterprises seeking personalized, data‑rich interactions.
c.name: Crescendo874d

c.description: Crescitalia is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, originating from a secondary-market harvest. The company’s public presence is currently limited, with no verified corporate website or detailed public documentation. This placeholder entry awaits further discovery of official resources, such as a corporate domain, API specifications, or developer portals, to enrich its profile for API consumers and integrators.
c.name: Crescitalia

c.description: Cresilon is a Brooklyn, New York biotechnology company founded in 2010 by Joe Landolina and Isaac Miller that develops, manufactures and markets hemostatic medical devices built on a proprietary plant-based hydrogel that stops moderate to severe bleeding in seconds without manual pressure. The company operates a GMP-certified, ISO 13485:2016 quality-managed biomanufacturing facility in Brooklyn's Industry City and sells two commercial products: VETIGEL, launched to the veterinary market in 2020 and licensed for animal-health distribution, and TRAUMAGEL, cleared by the FDA under 510(k) in 2024 and launched nationwide in the United States in January 2025 for prehospital, military and hospital control of traumatic external hemorrhage. Cresilon was named the number one medical-device company on Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies list in 2024 and returned to that list in 2026. Cresilon is a medical-device manufacturer rather than a software vendor, and publishes no commercial or developer-facing product API. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at cresilon.com, captured here for discovery purposes.
c.name: Cresilon

c.description: Cresset is a trusted Family Office & Private Wealth Management Firm for Entrepreneurs, CEOs, Founders, and UHNW families. It offers holistic financial planning, private investments, tax and estate strategies, trust services, exit planning, and more, managing over $237B AUM/AUA as of 2026.
c.name: Cresset Capital

c.description: Cresta (legally Cresta Intelligence, Inc.) is a Palo Alto, California enterprise Customer Experience AI company spun out of the Stanford AI Lab and founded in 2017 by Zayd Enam, Tim Shi, and Sebastian Thrun, and led since 2023 by CEO Ping Wu, the former co-founder of Google Contact Center AI. The platform unifies human and AI agents for the enterprise contact center across voice, chat, email, and SMS, combining real-time agent assist, autonomous omnichannel AI agents, conversation intelligence, an AI analyst, a knowledge agent, coaching, a training simulator, and automated quality management, all orchestrated through Cresta Opera, a no-code AI orchestration layer, with Cresta Conductor as the developer facing agentic engine for building and optimizing AI agents. Cresta runs a multi-model architecture composed of 20+ large and small language models, fine-tuned on customer-specific transcripts and synthetic data, with enterprise guardrails, supervisory models, and automated pre-release AI agent testing. The AI Agent consumes external tools through API-based function calling and the Model Context Protocol; Cresta itself does not publish an MCP server. Voice integrations span Five9, Genesys (Cloud CX and Engage), NICE CXone, Amazon Connect, Twilio Flex, Talkdesk, 8x8, Vonage, Gladly, TCN, RingCX, Avaya Infinity, Cisco UCCE/PCCE/UCCX, and SIPREC across Oracle, Ribbon, Avaya SBC, and Cisco CUBE via SIP, PSTN transfer, CCaaS native streaming, WebSocket, gRPC, and raw RTP. Cresta is privately held at Series D with $280M+ raised from Greylock, Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, Tiger Global, Coatue, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Porsche Ventures, World Innovation Lab, and the Qatar Investment Authority, plus strategic investors including Genesys, Five9, Accenture, Comcast, Qualcomm, JP Morgan, and Workday Ventures. It is the first Customer Experience AI provider to hold ISO/IEC 42001 certification, alongside SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, TISAX, CCPA, and PCI DSS posture. A production API host is live at api.cresta.com — a gRPC-JSON transcoding gateway that answers anonymously with a google.rpc.Status error envelope — but the Cresta API and SDK are gated behind a customer / partner engagement: there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published API reference or base-path documentation, no public SDK release on any package registry, no public pricing, and no developer self-service signup.
c.name: Cresta

c.description: Crestif is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions in the fintech sector. It offers a suite of APIs that enable seamless integration of financial data, payment processing, and compliance automation for businesses seeking to modernize their financial operations. The company emphasizes security, scalability, and developer-friendly documentation to support rapid development and deployment.
c.name: Crestif

c.description: Crestwood Equity Partners LP was a master limited partnership that owned and operated midstream energy assets across the United States, including natural gas, NGL, and crude oil gathering, processing, storage, and transportation businesses. Crestwood was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in November 2023, with Crestwood common and preferred units ceasing trading on the NYSE on November 3, 2023; ongoing operations and partner contracts have been integrated into Energy Transfer's pipeline and midstream network. Crestwood does not publish a public developer API program; technical interfaces such as nominations, scheduling, and capacity portals are now handled through Energy Transfer's commercial systems.
c.name: Crestwood Equity Partners

c.description: Crete Professionals Alliance (rebranded in 2025 as "Current", current.co) is a growth platform for independent accounting firms, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The alliance provides member firms with technology, talent, capital, and strategy to compete at enterprise scale, spanning 48 partner firms across 39 states and 3 countries with more than 2,000 employees. Service lines include accounting, advisory, audit and attest, client accounting services, and tax. This is a professional services / accounting company, not a developer-facing API provider: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. The record is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph coverage of Bessemer holdings.
c.name: Crete Professionals Alliance

c.description: Crew is a digital workplace platform for frontline and deskless teams, connecting frontline staff to corporate leadership across distributed workforces. The product bundles real-time team communication and employee engagement, labor optimization and shift scheduling, task execution, culture and recognition, knowledge management, a Command Center for administration and analytics, a compliance and safety suite, and third-party integrations. Crew reports serving more than one million frontline workers across companies including Taco Bell, Wendy's, Planet Fitness, and Harps Foods. It is backed by Greylock and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface was found during enrichment.

c.description: CREW Carbon supplies a calcium‑based alkalinity enhancement product for wastewater treatment facilities. The product is dosed into existing biological treatment processes to improve nutrient removal, settleability, and operational cost while permanently removing greenhouse gases. It is marketed to plant owners, operators, and affiliates seeking process intensification and carbon removal solutions.
c.name: CREW Carbon

c.description: Crew32 was a stealth-stage technology startup based in Santa Monica, California, working in the human resources, employment, and workplace-culture space. It was founded by Jason Nazar (previously co-founder and CEO of Docstoc), George Ishii (co-founder of Betterworks, Geni, and Yammer), and Yadid Ramot, and raised roughly $5.8 million in early funding around 2016. The company is publicly associated with the comparably.com workplace-culture and compensation review platform. Crew32 was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public API, developer portal, or SDK has been identified for this company.
c.name: Crew32

c.description: CrewAI Cloud (CrewAI AMP) is the managed Agent Management Platform for deploying, monitoring, scaling, and governing CrewAI multi-agent workflows in production. AMP exposes a per-crew REST API for kickoff, status, inputs, and human-in-the-loop resume operations, plus webhook streaming for task, step, and crew events. The platform ships in two deployment modes — AMP Cloud (managed, multi-tenant at app.crewai.com) and AMP Factory (self-hosted on AWS, Azure, or GCP) — and layers RBAC, SSO, secrets manager federation (AWS/Azure/GCP), agent and tool repositories, a marketplace, A2A communication, automations and triggers, traces with PII redaction, and observability exports on top of the open-source CrewAI framework.
c.name: CrewAI Cloud

c.description: Crewline is an autonomous heavy-equipment company that retrofits existing construction machinery to operate self-driving. Its hardware retrofit kit installs on-site in about an hour and adds autonomy to drum rollers today (compatible with Caterpillar, Bomag, Hamm, Volvo, and CASE), with dozers on the 2027 roadmap and rock trucks, excavators, motor graders, and wheel loaders in development. It is offered on a subscription model with zero upfront cost, a fixed monthly rate per machine, and 24/7 technical support, targeting earthworks and grading crews. Crewline is backed by Initialized Capital and headquartered in San Francisco. It publishes no public API or developer program at this time.
c.name: Crewline

c.description: Crews by Core was a construction field-execution platform based in Palo Alto, California (with a Tokyo office), founded and led by CEO Di-Ann Eisnor. Branded "Mission Control for the Field," its mobile-first product gave superintendents and foremen a single tool for lookahead scheduling, jobsite logistics, drawings, and field-to-office messaging, layered with AI-driven risk detection to quantify and mitigate schedule and financial risk on the jobsite. The company was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among ten investors and was acquired by construction IoT company WakeCap on July 1, 2024, folding its scheduling and communication tooling into WakeCap's worker-productivity sensor platform. Crews by Core did not expose a public developer API; this profile documents the company for the API Evangelist network.

c.description: CREXi (Commercial Real Estate Exchange, Inc.) is a Los Angeles-based commercial real estate marketplace and data platform founded in 2015, operating a sales marketplace, lease marketplace, auction platform, Broker PRO tools and the Crexi Intelligence property-records product. Its API surface is partner-gated rather than self-serve: the Crexi Listing API is a one-way syndication feed that lets MLSs, Realtor Boards, brokerages and data providers push listings into the marketplace (RESO, RETS, WebAPI and XML feeds, synced daily, with Crexi stating 100% compliance with the RESO Data Dictionary and 100+ partner organizations), while the Crexi Exchange API is documented in a password-protected Theneo portal at api-docs.crexi.com and fronted by an API-key-gated Swagger UI at exchange.crexi.com. c.description: Creyon Bio (branded Creyon) is a San Diego drug-development company operating an AI-powered nucleic acid engineering platform, NucleIQ, that designs oligonucleotide and RNA therapies with tissue- and cell-specific delivery. Creyon uses aptamer-based delivery, lipid nanoparticles, and transferrin-receptor aptamers to cross the blood-brain barrier, targeting immunology, central nervous system (CNS), and neuromuscular indications including late-onset Pompe disease. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of DCVC and currently advances three wholly-owned programs. This profile is a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network; Creyon publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.
c.name: Creyon Bio

c.description: CRI-O is a CNCF graduated, lightweight container runtime built specifically for Kubernetes. It implements the Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI) gRPC API and uses any Open Container Initiative (OCI) compatible runtime, including runc and crun, as the underlying container executor. CRI-O integrates with the containers/image and containers/storage libraries, the conmon container monitor, and CNI plugins to deliver a minimal kubelet-facing runtime surface, while also exposing an HTTP status API and Prometheus metrics endpoint for operations and observability.
c.name: CRI-O

c.description: Cribl is an observability pipeline company providing a suite of products for collecting, processing, routing, searching, and storing telemetry data at scale. Cribl's developer platform offers REST APIs across Stream, Edge, Search, Lake, and the As Code product line, exposing programmatic control over data pipelines, edge agents, federated search jobs, lake datasets, and infrastructure-as-code configuration management. The Cribl Cloud API acts as a centrally managed control plane across all deployments and authenticates with OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
c.name: Cribl

c.description: CricAPI (now operating as CricketData.org) is a cricket data API platform that has provided free, high-performance cricket data since September 2015. The API delivers live scores, ball-by-ball updates, match details, player statistics, team rankings, schedules, and fantasy cricket scorecard data for international and domestic tournaments including ICC, IPL, T20, BBL, and PSL. Developers can access historical match data going back to 2000, widgets for website integration, and a fantasy cricket API designed for league operators. The platform is ISO 9001:2015 certified and uses its own AI engine with human data entry rather than scraping third-party sources.

c.description: Cricheroes is a sports technology company that provides a platform for cricket enthusiasts to engage with the game through fantasy leagues, player statistics, and community features. Its programs span hemoglobinopathies, immuno-oncology, regenerative medicine, and in-vivo editing; its lead therapy CASGEVY (exagamglogene autotemcel), developed with Vertex Pharmaceuticals, is the first approved CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing treatment for sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia. c.description: Crogl is an enterprise AI security operations platform that deploys autonomous AI agents to investigate security alerts and threat advisories entirely within a customer's own infrastructure. Using a neurosymbolic approach that combines knowledge graphs, large language models, and security best practices, Crogl gathers context, queries existing security tools, and cross-references data across SIEM, EDR, ticketing, and data-lake systems without exfiltrating data. It is tool-agnostic — integrating with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, Jira, Databricks, Snowflake, Amazon S3, and Cribl — and every action is auditable so human analysts retain final decisions. Crogl is offered as a free single-user deployment and an enterprise plan with SSO, RBAC, and 24/7 SLAs. It is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. Crogl does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer SDK; its API surface (connectors) is part of the on-premises product.

c.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

c.description: Crosslayer Labs is a network and web-infrastructure security company spun out of a Princeton University security research lab. The company protects enterprises from website and API hijacks by discovering, analyzing, and continuously monitoring every layer of first- and third-party network infrastructure, correlating attack signals across the network stack for advanced threat detection and rapid mitigation.
