c.description: Cyence is a cyber risk analytics and modeling solution — originally an independent InsurTech startup (backed by IVP and others) and acquired by Guidewire in 2017 — that helps insurers, reinsurers, brokers, and managing general agents quantify, underwrite, and manage cyber insurance risk in financial terms. It combines internet-scale data collection, data science, and economic loss modeling to produce exposure signals, breach-probability estimates, and portfolio accumulation and catastrophe scenarios. Cyence data and scores are delivered to carriers through Guidewire Cloud and are available via a REST API for pricing, risk selection, and underwriting workflow automation. API access is partner-gated through a Guidewire account rather than a public self-serve developer portal.
c.name: Cyence

c.description: Cyera is an AI-native data security company whose Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) platform discovers, classifies, and secures sensitive data across cloud service providers (AWS, GCP, Azure), SaaS applications, data warehouses, and on-premises stores using an agentless architecture that scans hundreds of petabytes without impacting performance. Cyera exposes a versioned REST API (api.cyera.io, with an EU region at api-eu.cyera.io) secured with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect and short-lived JWT bearer tokens, a published Model Context Protocol server (Cyera MCP over DataPort, a per-customer managed Snowflake warehouse) for natural-language querying of data-security findings, and a SafeBase-powered trust center covering SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
c.name: Cyera

c.description: CYGIA (Zhuhai CYGIA Automation Equipment Co.) is an intelligent-factory equipment and solution provider founded in 2006 and headquartered in Zhuhai, China. It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.
c.name: CYGIA

c.description: CYGNVS (an acronym for "CYber GuidaNce Virtual Space") is a Silicon Valley SaaS company that operates an out-of-band command center for cyber crisis preparedness and incident response. The platform runs independently of an organization's corporate infrastructure so that response teams — security, legal, executives, insurers, and external stakeholders — can coordinate securely even when internal systems are compromised or down, preserving legal privilege and chain of custody. CYGNVS provides guided playbooks, tabletop exercises, regulated-response execution with regulatory reporting templates across many jurisdictions, and bundles CISO personal-liability insurance underwritten by AIG. Founded in 2020 by Arvind Parthasarathi, the company raised a $55M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in January 2023. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from public surfaces; CYGNVS exposes no public developer API — the application is delivered as a secured out-of-band product across regional domains.
c.name: CYGNVS

c.description: Cylake is an AI-native cybersecurity company founded in 2026 by Nir Zuk, Wilson Xu, and Ehud (Udi) Shamir — veterans of Palo Alto Networks — to deliver complete, data-driven security for the world's largest and most regulated organizations that require total data sovereignty. Its platform combines hardware and software with agentic workflows on a single, sovereign data foundation, running on-premises or in a private cloud with no dependence on public cloud or external AI services. Cylake launched publicly in March 2026 with a $45M seed round led by Greylock Partners (with IQT participating), is being built alongside several design partners, and plans general availability in early 2027. As of this writing Cylake does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs — this profile tracks the company's identity and public surface pending an API program.
c.name: Cylake

c.description: Cylib is a German battery recycling company founded in 2022 as a spinoff from RWTH Aachen University, headquartered in Aachen, Germany. It transforms end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, production scrap, and black mass back into critical raw materials, recovering lithium, graphite, nickel, cobalt, and manganese through a proprietary, largely water-based hydrometallurgical process that the company reports achieves over 90% recycling efficiency with an ~80% reduced carbon footprint versus primary extraction, powered by 100% renewable electricity. The company is backed by Speedinvest and other investors. Cylib operates as an industrial cleantech / circular-economy materials business and does not currently publish a developer program, public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software integration surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and carries only identity and public web properties.
c.name: Cylib

c.description: Cymbal was a consumer blockchain data startup founded in 2022 in Menlo Park by Eric Feng, Nick Chang and others, building a "human readable" Ethereum block explorer with a visual, social interface and AI-generated conversational summaries of wallets, NFTs and transactions. The company raised $18.5M in 2023 from investors including First Round Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Solana Ventures, Patron, Acrew and GV. In July 2025 Yahoo acqui-hired the Cymbal team into a new AI research group. Cymbal published no public developer API or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile is a GV-portfolio company record.
c.name: Cymbal

c.description: Cymetica (Berkeley, California; founded November 2025 by Kasian Franks) is the company behind EventTrader, an AI-native perpetual prediction market and hybrid CEX-DEX exchange: a central limit order book with 500+ pairs, EVCDX event-card index markets, clonable AI trading agent species, AI-managed funds and a token launchpad, with off-chain matching and on-chain settlement on Base L2 and Ethereum. It publishes an unusually complete agent-facing surface from one origin — a curated OpenAPI 3.1 REST contract, a hosted MCP server with an open tools/list, an A2A agent card, an AsyncAPI 3.0 WebSocket description, llms.txt, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and RFC 8414/9728 discovery, UCP/ACP/x402 commerce manifests, security.txt and TypeScript/Python SDKs.
c.name: Cymetica

c.description: Cynergy Bank is an FCA- and PRA-authorised UK specialist bank (FCA reference 575105) serving the blended personal and business banking needs of business owners, property entrepreneurs, and family businesses. It was formed in December 2018 when Cynergy Capital acquired Bank of Cyprus UK for approximately £103m and rebranded the business as Cynergy Bank. Although it is not one of the nine CMA-mandated banks (CMA9), as a UK ASPSP it complies with PSD2 and the UK Open Banking Standard, publishing a dedicated third-party interface for the Open Banking Implementation Entity (OBIE) Read/Write APIs — Account & Transaction Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), and Confirmation of Funds (CBPII). Access is restricted to FCA- or EEA-regulated Third Party Providers and is secured with FAPI-grade OAuth2/OIDC, mutual-TLS client authentication, and PSD2 strong customer authentication using OBIE/eIDAS certificates, onboarded through the bank's Open Banking developer portal.
c.name: Cynergy Bank

c.description: Cynet is a unified, AI-powered cybersecurity platform built for MSPs and lean IT/security teams that consolidates endpoint (EDR/EPP), network, email, cloud/SaaS, mobile, and identity protection into a single agent and console. Its CyAI machine-learning engine automatically detects and remediates the majority of threats, CyOps delivers 24x7 managed detection and response, and built-in SOAR playbooks automate response across 80+ pre-built integrations. Cynet exposes a REST API (Cynet 360) for programmatic access to alerts, hosts, remediation, scanning, and account operations, offered as an On-Prem V1 API and a SaaS V3 API, authenticated with a tenant-scoped access token. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
c.name: Cynet

c.description: Cyneta Networks, Inc. was a wireless data networking equipment company founded around 2000 and headquartered in Plano, Texas, with an additional presence in Cockeysville, Maryland. Backed by Battery Ventures, it developed intelligent hardware and software for wireless data networks — packet control, network element management, and network monitoring / service-quality optimization for mobile operator core networks — and accumulated a patent portfolio in wireless and core network monitoring. The company is a dot-com-era venture that no longer maintains an active public web presence: its former domain, cyneta.com, no longer serves a Cyneta site and its DNS is now operated by an unrelated party. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, package-registry libraries, or any API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record; there is nothing to catalog on the API supply side.
c.name: Cyneta Networks

c.description: Cyngn (NASDAQ: CYN) is a Mountain View, California autonomous vehicle technology company that develops and deploys industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for material handling. Its flagship DriveMod stack is a vehicle-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy system that retrofits onto standard industrial vehicles such as tuggers and forklifts, paired with the Cyngn Insight fleet-management, teleoperation, and analytics platform and the Cyngn Evolve data toolkit — together marketed as the Enterprise Autonomy Suite. Cyngn targets warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics operators facing labor shortages and safety challenges, and integrates with major warehouse management systems (Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM). The company traces its corporate lineage to Cyanogen Inc. (the CyanogenMod company), whose dormant GitHub organization still links to cyngn.com.
c.name: Cyngn

c.description: Cynomi is an AI-powered, automated virtual CISO (vCISO) platform built for MSPs, MSSPs, and cybersecurity consultancies to deliver scalable security and compliance services to their clients. The platform automates risk assessments, generates tailored security policies and prioritized remediation plans, and maps controls to leading frameworks including NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR, NIS2, and HIPAA, tracking security posture over time. Cynomi exposes a platform-agnostic Public API for bi-directional task synchronization with any PSA or ticketing system (ConnectWise, ServiceNow, Autotask, HaloPSA, Kaseya, NinjaOne, Atera), pushing remediation tasks out and pulling status updates back, alongside pre-built integrations with vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) and cloud security tools. Authentication is handled through an Auth0 tenant using OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect. Cynomi is backed by Canaan Partners and Insight Partners.
c.name: Cynomi

c.description: Cyota, Inc was a cybersecurity company founded in 1999 in New York City by Naftali Bennett, Lior Golan, Michal Tzur, and Amir Orad, focused on online banking fraud, e-commerce fraud, and anti-phishing protection. Cyota pioneered token-less consumer authentication and risk-based fraud detection for financial institutions, reportedly holding a majority share of the US and UK e-commerce authentication markets. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, the company was acquired by RSA Security on December 30, 2005 for approximately $145 million, after which its technology was folded into RSA's Identity and Fraud portfolio (RSA Adaptive Authentication / FraudAction). Cyota no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no live developer surface, API, or documentation. This profile is retained for historical/network provenance only.
c.name: Cyota, Inc

c.description: Cypherium is a permissionless Layer-1 blockchain built to bridge centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) finance and bring real-world assets on-chain at scale. It runs CypherBFT, a hybrid consensus that pairs GPU proof-of-work committee election with HotStuff Byzantine Fault Tolerance for near-instant finality, and is EVM/Solidity compatible (EVM chain ID 16166). Products include CypherLink (cross-ledger notary), Cypherium Connect (bank integration plugin, marketed as ISO 20022 compliant), the Cypherium Validator, and Cypherium ID (decentralized identity). Developers integrate through an Ethereum-style JSON-RPC node API (eth/web3/net/ personal/miner/txpool/admin namespaces over HTTP, WS and IPC) and a Coinbase Rosetta API implementation for exchange and wallet integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
c.name: Cypherium

c.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.
c.name: Cypress

c.description: Cypress Semiconductor was a US-based semiconductor company known for its PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity stacks, NOR Flash memory, CapSense capacitive touch sensing, and Traveo automotive microcontrollers. Infineon Technologies completed its $9.4 billion acquisition of Cypress on April 16, 2020, and Cypress now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Infineon. The former Cypress product lines (PSoC, AIROC formerly WICED, NOR Flash, CapSense, Traveo) remain in active development under Infineon branding, and the cypress.com domain redirects to infineon.com. The former Cypress developer surface — including PSoC Creator (legacy) and the modern ModusToolbox embedded development ecosystem — is now hosted on the Infineon GitHub organization (github.com/Infineon) which contains 2,143 public repositories spanning code examples, board support packages, HAL libraries, middleware, and configurators for PSoC, AIROC, Traveo, XMC, and AURIX device families. The original Cypress GitHub organization (github.com/cypresssemiconductorco) has been wound down to four placeholder repos that redirect users to the Infineon org. Cypress' APIs are predominantly embedded software APIs (C/C++ HAL, PDL, middleware libraries) rather than HTTP/REST surfaces, consumed by firmware engineers via ModusToolbox, Eclipse, and Visual Studio Code workflows.
c.name: Cypress Semiconductor

c.description: Cypress.io, Inc. builds Cypress, an open-source, JavaScript-based end-to-end and component testing framework that runs tests directly in the browser with time-travel debugging, automatic waiting, and cross-browser support. Its commercial Cypress Cloud service adds test parallelization, smart orchestration, analytics, Test Replay, UI Coverage, and automated accessibility checks, plus an enterprise Data Extract API for exporting test and run analytics in CSV, JSON, or XLSX. Cypress is widely adopted across CI/CD pipelines for reliable, developer-friendly web application testing.
c.name: Cypress.io

c.description: Cyral is a data security and governance platform (founded 2018, Milpitas CA; acquired by Varonis in March 2025) that provides an agentless, stateless data-layer sidecar for monitoring and governing access to data repositories such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Amazon S3, Kafka, and Oracle. Cyral was built API-first: its Control Plane exposes a REST API secured with OAuth2 client-credentials, fully automatable through the official Cyral Terraform provider (cyralinc/cyral) and supporting Terraform modules for AWS, Azure, and Okta. Following the Varonis acquisition, cyral.com now redirects to Varonis' Database Activity Monitoring product, but the first-party developer tooling remains published on the cyralinc GitHub organization and the Terraform Registry.
c.name: Cyral

c.description: Cyren Call Communications Corp. was a wireless communications company founded in 2005 by Nextel co-founder Morgan O'Brien to advocate for a nationwide public-safety broadband network. Its central proposal asked the FCC to reallocate 30 MHz of 700 MHz-band spectrum (freed by the 2009 analog-TV shutdown) to public-safety users, and it later served as advisor to the Public Safety Spectrum Trust (PSST) after PSST became the nationwide licensee for public safety's 10 MHz of 700 MHz broadband spectrum. The FCC dismissed Cyren Call's original petition as inconsistent with auction requirements, and the PSST advisory relationship ended in early 2009. The company is permanently closed. It never operated a developer program, public API, or SDK surface, so no API artifacts are available for enrichment.
c.name: Cyren Call

c.description: Cyrus Biotechnology is a Seattle-based protein-design and drug-discovery company building novel biologics for serious unmet medical needs by re-engineering existing proteins with a tight loop between computational modeling and lab testing. Its flagship product, Cyrus Bench, is a cloud-based protein modeling and structure-prediction platform that packages the Rosetta software suite (alongside deep-learning tools such as AlphaFold, OpenFold, RoseTTAFold and ProteinMPNN) behind a browser-based interface for homology modeling, protein/protein and enzyme/ligand interface design, protein stabilization, protein/ligand and protein/protein docking, and X-ray molecular replacement. Cyrus Bench is delivered as a hosted web application with user documentation rather than a public developer REST API; the company is backed by Trinity Ventures.
c.name: Cyrus Biotechnology

c.description: Cyscale is an agentless, cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) that continuously monitors multi-cloud environments to surface, contextualize, and prioritize security risk. It unifies Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM), Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM), Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM), and Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) into a single control plane, using a graph-based "Security Knowledge Graph" to map relationships between misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, identities, and data so teams know what to fix first. Cyscale connects to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and identity providers through secure, provider-native mechanisms and maps findings to compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, and NIST. Cyscale is a Seedcamp portfolio company; it exposes API keys for CI/CD and developer-tool integrations but does not publish a versioned public REST API specification.
c.name: Cyscale

c.description: CytomX Therapeutics is a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company based in South San Francisco, California, pioneering a novel class of masked, conditionally activated biologic therapeutics built on its proprietary Probody platform. The Probody technology is engineered to remain inactive in healthy tissue and to become selectively unmasked and activated within the tumor microenvironment, with the goal of producing more potent, less toxic cancer medicines. The company's pipeline spans antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), T-cell engaging bispecific antibodies, and immunotherapies, advanced both internally and through partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies. CytomX is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq CTMX). This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; as a biopharmaceutical research organization CytomX does not publish a public developer API, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.
c.name: CytomX Therapeutics

c.description: Cytora is a London-headquartered insurtech, founded in 2012 as a University of Cambridge spinout, that sells a digital risk processing platform to commercial insurers, wholesale brokers, MGAs and reinsurers. Its software ingests inbound submissions arriving as email, PDF, spreadsheet and broker API payloads, digitises them against pre-built line-of-business schemas (property, commercial combined, construction, cyber, fleet, general liability, professional liability, D&O, E&O, management liability), augments them from a data ecosystem of roughly sixty third-party risk-data partners, evaluates them against appetite and priority rules, and routes them into downstream underwriting and claims systems. Use cases span new business, renewals, mid-term adjustments, claims FNOL and post-FNOL intake, and facultative and treaty reinsurance submissions. Named customers include Zurich, Chubb, Markel, Beazley, Travelers, Tokio Marine, Ecclesiastical, Arch, Everest and TransRe. Applied Systems acquired Cytora in September 2025. Its API posture is partner-gated and enterprise-only: Cytora runs a real production API gateway at api.cytora.com and a real ReadMe-hosted API reference at docs.cytora.com, but the documentation site is entirely password-protected (HTTP 302 to a password wall, robots.txt Disallow) and the gateway resets anonymous TLS connections. There is no self-serve developer signup, no public OpenAPI, no public Postman collection and no published webhook or event catalog. The only externally verifiable technical surface is the Auth0 OIDC discovery document at auth.cytora.com, which confirms OAuth 2.0 client-credentials and authorization-code flows for provisioned partner integrations. The United Kingdom home market has no open-insurance mandate, so nothing compels Cytora to expose any of this publicly.
c.name: Cytora

c.description: Cytovale is a San Francisco-based medical diagnostics company that develops early-detection technology for sepsis. Its flagship product, IntelliSep, is the first and only FDA-cleared in vitro diagnostic test for sepsis: it uses microfluidics, high-speed video, and computer-vision algorithms to measure the biophysical rigidity of tens of thousands of white blood cells, detecting the immune activation that signals sepsis risk and returning a risk stratification in roughly eight minutes. The test runs on the Cytovale System medical device in emergency-department settings. Cytovale is venture-backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sands Capital, and the Global Health Investment Corporation. The company operates as a clinical/diagnostics device maker and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.
c.name: Cytovale

c.description: Cyvera was an Israeli cybersecurity startup, founded in 2011 and backed by Battery Ventures, that pioneered exploit-prevention endpoint security. Its flagship product, TRAPS (Targeted Remote Attack Prevention System), blocked unknown, zero-day attacks by obstructing the exploitation techniques attackers rely on rather than relying on signatures. Cyvera was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in April 2014 for roughly $200M, and TRAPS was folded into Palo Alto's endpoint offering that ultimately became Cortex XDR. The independent company no longer operates; the cyvera.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live developer portal, public API, or artifact surface to enrich.
c.name: Cyvera

c.description: Cyware is a New York-headquartered cybersecurity company, founded in 2016, that builds an AI-powered threat intelligence and security operations platform for enterprise SOC teams, ISACs and ISAOs, government agencies, CERTs and MSSPs. The Cyware Intelligence Suite spans Intel Exchange (its threat intelligence platform, formerly CTIX), Collaborate (bi-directional threat sharing for member communities), Orchestrate (security orchestration and automation), Respond (incident case management) and Cyware AI (agentic security analyst workflows). The platform ingests, deduplicates, enriches, scores and operationalizes structured and unstructured cyber threat intelligence using STIX 2.x, TAXII 2.x and MITRE ATT&CK, and pushes it into SIEM, EDR, firewall and ITSM tooling through 400+ integrations. Programmatic access is delivered through the Intel Exchange v3 Open API and the Orchestrate Open API — both tenant-hosted, both authenticated with HMAC-SHA1 signed Open API credentials — plus an open-source Model Context Protocol server that exposes threat-intelligence and playbook actions to LLM agents.
c.name: Cyware
