c.name: Czech Namedays Calendar

c.description: A collection of exchange rates
c.name: Czech National Bank

c.description: TV programme of Czech TV
c.name: Czech Television

d.description: D-EDGE Hospitality Solutions provides a comprehensive suite of hotel technology and marketing solutions, including central reservation systems, channel management, booking engine, data intelligence, and digital marketing tools. Their platform helps hotels increase direct bookings, improve revenue management, and enhance guest experiences across multiple channels worldwide.
d.name: D-EDGE Hospitality Solutions

d.description: D-ID is an AI-powered platform for generating talking-head videos and interactive digital human experiences from still photos, text scripts, and audio narration. Developers can access REST APIs to produce pre-rendered talking avatar videos, perform real-time streaming agent conversations via WebRTC, translate videos into 100+ languages with voice cloning and lip-sync, and create custom AI agents backed by LLMs and RAG knowledge bases. The platform has generated over 150 million videos and supports parallel processing of tens of thousands of simultaneous API requests. D-ID serves use cases ranging from enterprise training and customer service to personalized marketing campaigns and language learning applications.
d.name: D-ID

d.description: d-Matrix builds ultra-low-latency, energy-efficient AI inference infrastructure for generative AI in the datacenter. Its memory-centric compute architecture, next-generation I/O, and stacked-DRAM approach are delivered through the Corsair inference accelerator (chiplet-based, supporting models up to 100B parameters), the JetStream accelerator-to-accelerator communications platform, the SquadRack disaggregated rack-scale solution, and the 3DIMC 3D digital in-memory compute technology. Founded by Sid Sheth and Sudeep Bhoja and headquartered in Santa Clara, the company has raised roughly $450M (including a $275M Series C) from investors such as Qatar Investment Authority, Temasek, and SK Hynix. d-Matrix also maintains the open-source dmx-compressor (DMX) PyTorch toolkit for co-designing models to its inference hardware. This API Evangelist network profile tracks d-Matrix as a compute-hardware provider; it does not currently publish a public web API.
d.name: d-Matrix

d.description: D-Tools Inc. builds estimation, system design, project management and field-service software for audio-visual, low-voltage, security and systems-integration contractors. Two products carry two distinct public APIs. D-Tools Cloud is the web-native platform, and its REST API (dtcloudapi.d-tools.cloud) exposes Clients, Products, Opportunities, Quotes, Projects, Change Orders, Purchase Orders, Service Contracts, Files and Time Entries with documented rate limits, webhooks and a downloadable Postman collection. D-Tools System Integrator (SI) is the on-premises/hosted Windows product; because SI itself has no directly reachable API, D-Tools operates a cloud middleware queue at api.d-tools.com/si where third parties publish projects, change orders, tasks, service orders, purchase orders, time sheets, product catalogs, clients and vendors to an SI user and subscribe to what that SI user exports. Both APIs publish machine-readable specifications: OpenAPI 3.1.1 for SI and OpenAPI 3.0.4 for Cloud.
d.name: D-Tools

d.description: D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NYSE: QBTS) is the leader in commercial quantum annealing computing and developer of the Advantage and Advantage2 quantum systems. D-Wave's Leap quantum cloud service provides real-time access to D-Wave QPUs and to the Leap hybrid solver family (BQM, CQM, DQM, NL) capable of solving industrial optimization problems with up to ~2 million variables and constraints. The open-source Ocean SDK — dimod, dwave-system, dwave-cloud-client, dwave-hybrid, dwave-samplers, dwave-optimization, minorminer, dwave-inspector, and 40+ companion packages — provides the canonical developer experience, with the underlying Solver API (SAPI) exposed as a versioned REST interface for solver discovery, problem submission, status polling, answer retrieval, and cancellation. Companion APIs include the Metadata API for region discovery and the Leap Account API for OAuth-based project and token management.
d.name: D-Wave

d.description: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder by volume in the United States, building and selling single-family homes in dozens of states across multiple price points. The company is a Fortune 500 enterprise with affiliated financial services including DHI Mortgage, DHI Title, and DRH Insurance.
d.name: D.R. Horton

d.description: D1 Capital Partners is a New York City-based global investment firm founded in July 2018 by Daniel Sundheim, the former Chief Investment Officer of Viking Global Investors, who seeded the firm with more than $500 million of his own capital. The name "D1" references Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's "Day One" philosophy. D1 deploys capital across both public and private markets: in public markets it runs a global long/short equity strategy (including equity derivatives and convertible bonds) targeting medium- to long-term returns, while in private markets it takes later-stage, non-controlling growth-equity stakes in expanding companies. The firm's private portfolio spans consumer, business services, financial services, healthcare, industrials, real estate, and technology, media and telecommunications, with notable positions in companies such as SpaceX, Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI, Ramp, Robinhood, GitLab, and Instacart. As a "Tiger Cub" descended from Viking Global, D1 grew from roughly $3 billion at launch to more than $20 billion by the end of 2020, and has been reported managing on the order of $24 billion in assets. It is headquartered at 9 West 57th Street in Manhattan.
d.name: D1 Capital Partners

d.description: D2G Oncology is a precision-oncology company based in Mountain View, California, reported to have been founded in 2018 by Ian Winters. Public company descriptions characterize its work as applying quantitative and multiplexed functional cancer genomics to relate drugs to genotypes in order to advance precision cancer therapeutics. The company operates INSITE, a login-gated internal research portal at www.d2g-insite.com supporting preclinical study management and result exploration. D2G Oncology publishes no public developer API program, no developer portal, no API documentation, and no client SDKs, and third-party company trackers list the company as inactive as of 2026. It was surfaced through the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio and is retained here as an identity-only profile.
d.name: D2G Oncology

d.description: D2iQ (formerly Mesosphere, maker of DC/OS) was an enterprise Kubernetes company whose flagship product, the D2iQ Kubernetes Platform (DKP), delivered production-grade Kubernetes cluster provisioning, day-2 operations, and application management across cloud, on-premises, edge, and air-gapped environments. D2iQ was acquired by Nutanix in early 2024; DKP was folded into and rebranded as the Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP), which launched in May 2024. The independent D2iQ web and developer surfaces are now retired: d2iq.com redirects to nutanix.com/d2iq and docs.d2iq.com redirects to the Nutanix support portal, so D2iQ no longer operates a first-party public API, developer portal, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical / acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: D2iQ

d.description: D2L Brightspace is an enterprise learning management system (LMS) used by higher education, K-12, and corporate organizations. Its public REST API is the Valence Learning Framework API, exposed under https://{host}/d2l/api/ and split into two product components - "lp" (Learning Platform - users, roles, enrollments, org units, data hub) and "le" (Learning Environment - content, grades, assignments/dropbox, quizzes, discussions, calendar, news, learning outcomes). Routes are versioned per component (for example lp 1.x and le 1.x) and authenticated with OAuth 2 bearer tokens issued by the D2L auth service; the older ID-Key (app-id/user-id) scheme is deprecated. D2L is the vendor; Valence is the historical name of the API framework.
d.name: D2L Brightspace

d.description: D3 is a crypto-infrastructure company building the internet's domain layer, tokenized. Through its Doma Protocol, D3 brings ICANN domain names on-chain as tokenized name assets and unlocks "DomainFi" — programmable DNS, fractionalized domain tokens, an on-chain marketplace, and agentic commerce. Developers use the Doma API (a GraphQL subgraph plus REST Poll and Orderbook APIs), the doma CLI, and portable Agent Skills to register, tokenize, trade, and manage domains across the Doma mainnet (chain 97477) and testnet (97476). D3 is backed by Paradigm.
d.name: D3

d.description: DAASH is an AI-powered predictive commerce intelligence platform built specifically for the beauty and cosmetics industry. It combines consumer shopping panels covering 6M+ people with social and advertising trend data and enriched product attributes to estimate sales performance, market share, and emerging trends at the SKU level. DAASH delivers weekly competitive intelligence to beauty brands, manufacturers, and financial services firms so they can uncover category shifts, benchmark competitor performance, and spot growth opportunities. The company was founded at the intersection of predictive intelligence and consumer products by retail and data experts (Philip Smolin, CEO; Justin Stewart, CTO; Melissa Munnerlyn, CMO), and is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital. DAASH is delivered as a hosted SaaS application (my.daash.co); it currently exposes no public developer API surface.
d.name: Daash

d.description: Dabba (Wifi Dabba) is a Web3-powered decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that brings affordable internet connectivity to emerging markets, starting in India. It deploys low-cost Dabba Lite WiFi hotspots through a network of local cable operators (LCOs) and rewards hotspot owners, location owners, backhaul providers, and hardware manufacturers with DBT tokens as data is consumed. Network activity — NFTs, subscriber revenue, and bandwidth usage — is reported onchain, and the token flows through a mint, buyback, and burn model. Surfaced as a Multicoin Capital portfolio company; profiled here from public developer, documentation, and onchain surfaces.
d.name: Dabba

d.description: Dabchy is a Tunisia-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned and new lifestyle goods including fashion and clothing, accessories, home decor, sporting equipment, and books. Serving the Tunisian market in French (fr_TN), it lets individuals list their own items and discover deals from other sellers, positioning itself as a simple, fast, and secure platform for giving everyday objects a second life. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Dabchy publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; api.dabchy.com is a locked-down (HTTP 403) application backend and the public site is a client-rendered single-page app with no exposed spec.
d.name: Dabchy

d.description: Dabee (dabee.com.br) is a Brazilian consumer-technology review and comparison website that helps shoppers make informed purchasing decisions about electronics and gadgets. It publishes hands-on reviews, side-by-side comparisons, and buying guides across notebooks, smartphones, tablets, monitors, smartwatches, gaming consoles, smart TVs, and networking equipment, with 'vale a pena' (is-it-worth-it) verdicts and price tracking pulled from Amazon Brazil. The site monetizes through affiliate commissions. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead.
d.name: Dabee

d.description: Dacast is a unified live streaming and video hosting (OTT) platform that lets businesses broadcast live channels, host and monetize video on demand (VOD), organize content into playlists, and embed a white-label HTML5 player. Dacast exposes a RESTful JSON API (base https://developer.dacast.com/v2) for programmatically creating live channels, uploading and managing VOD, building playlists, and reading viewer analytics. API requests authenticate with an X-Api-Key header. API access is gated to Scale and Custom plans (trial accounts can request temporary access from sales), so the endpoints below are grounded in Dacast's public developer docs but several exact paths beyond the confirmed /v2/channel, /v2/vod, and /v2/playlist are honestly modeled.
d.name: Dacast

d.description: icanhazdadjoke is a free REST API providing access to the internet's largest selection of dad jokes. It offers random joke retrieval, a searchable joke database, Slack slash command integration, Discord bot support, and plain-text or JSON responses — all with no authentication required.
d.name: Dad Jokes (icanhazdadjoke)

d.description: Dada Group (Dada Nexus, NASDAQ: DADA) is a leading Chinese instant retail and local on-demand delivery platform, headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2014. It operates an open, crowdsourced delivery network of more than one million rider partners serving supermarkets, pharmacies, fresh-food and restaurant merchants across thousands of counties and cities, alongside merchant fulfillment products such as the Haibo in-store logistics system and the Dada Youjian picking service. Now integrated into the JD.com ecosystem, its core delivery brand was rebranded to JD Instant Delivery (京东秒送) in May 2024. Dada runs a merchant Open Platform (开放平台) for order, delivery-tracking and fulfillment integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
d.name: Dada

d.description: Dados abertos Distrito Federal is a open data portal open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 176 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
d.name: Dados abertos Distrito Federal

d.description: Dados Abertos POA is a open data portal open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately an open datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
d.name: Dados Abertos POA

d.description: Dados RS is a open data portal open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 404 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
d.name: Dados RS

d.description: DAERO (Daero Group) is a construction-technology company building mobile-first tools for trades and field teams. Its flagship product, ZeroPunch, is a field-operations platform that turns real-time field intuition into structured construction data: voice-first capture lets crews speak field observations in natural language, photos are paired with contextual field data, work is auto-assigned by scope, and stream-of-consciousness notes are converted into organized daily logs. ZeroPunch offers a two-way integration with Procore for project-management sync. The company positions itself around the daily needs of the people actually doing the work, aiming to make construction operations smarter and faster. As of this profile DAERO publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is partnership-level (Procore) and inquiries go to support@daerogroup.com. Backed by Threshold Ventures.
d.name: Daero Group

d.description: Daffy (the Daffy Charitable Fund) is a modern donor-advised fund (DAF) platform that helps people be more generous, more often. Co-founded by Adam Nash, Daffy lets members set aside money for charity, invest it tax-free across ETFs, individual stocks, and 300+ crypto assets, and then recommend grants to any of 1.7M+ eligible US charities on their own timeline. It offers flat-rate membership pricing starting at $3/month, family funds for up to 24 members, advisor integration, and Daffy for Work employer giving. Daffy Charitable Fund is a tax-exempt public charity under IRC 501(c)(3). Backed by Ribbit Capital, it operates as a consumer fintech app with no public developer API surface as of this profile.
d.name: Daffy

d.description: Dagangan is an Indonesian tech-enabled wholesale e-commerce platform serving small and medium retailers (SMEs) in tier 3-4 cities and rural areas. Through a hub-and-spoke network of 50+ micro-warehouses across remote regions, it connects large suppliers to traditional local retailers, giving them affordable mobile access to daily necessities and groceries while reducing delivery costs and supply-chain friction. The company operates a consumer/retailer Android shopping application (Dagangan Mall), is backed by 500 Global, and is recognized as a Rural Digitalization Partner of Indonesia's Ministry of Villages, Disadvantaged Regions, and Transmigration. As of this profile, Dagangan publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI specification.
d.name: Dagangan

d.description: Dagger is an open-source programmable CI/CD engine that runs pipelines in containers using a unified, introspectable GraphQL API. Pipelines are written as code in the developer's preferred language (Go, Python, TypeScript, PHP, Java, .NET, Elixir, or Rust) using Dagger SDKs and packaged as Dagger Modules that can be published to the Daggerverse module index. The Dagger Engine exposes Container, Directory, File, Secret, and CacheVolume as first-class GraphQL types backed by a content-addressed store, enabling deterministic builds and aggressive caching. Dagger Cloud provides the hosted control plane for pipeline traces, checks, and module observability. Dagger does not expose a public REST API; clients connect to a per-session Dagger Engine GraphQL endpoint and the optional Dagger Cloud Web UI.
d.name: Dagger

d.description: Image manipulation and processing
d.name: Dagpi

d.description: DagsHub is a GitHub-like platform for ML and data teams that combines code, data (DVC), experiments (MLflow), and labeling. It exposes a Gitea-compatible REST API for repository operations plus DagsHub-specific endpoints for data and experiments.
d.name: DagsHub

d.description: Dagster is a data orchestration platform centered on software-defined assets with strong observability and testing support. It exposes a GraphQL API for programmatic interaction with Dagster instances and a REST API for reporting external asset materializations, checks, and observations from outside pipelines.
d.name: Dagster

d.description: Daily provides WebRTC video and audio infrastructure for developers — REST APIs for rooms, recordings, transcripts, meetings, dial-out and Daily Bots / Pipecat Cloud (voice AI agents), plus client SDKs for Web, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter.
d.name: Daily

d.description: Daily Gobble was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub sourced from the 500 Global portfolio. A 2026-07-20 enrichment pass found no operating company behind it. The dailygobble.com domain is a GoDaddy parked domain that serves a JavaScript redirect to a /lander page, carries no MX records, and publishes no content. The relevantmobile.com URL carried on the original stub does not belong to Daily Gobble; it now serves an unrelated Indonesian-language gambling and SEO spam site, and it has been removed rather than retained as a Website pointer. No first-party client libraries were found on npm or PyPI. There is no API, developer program, documentation, or event surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical record.
d.name: Daily Gobble

d.description: Daily Harvest is a direct-to-consumer health food delivery company. It sells organic, ready-to-prepare frozen foods — smoothies, oat bowls, elixirs, protein, and boosters — that customers order on daily-harvest.com (a Shopify storefront) and receive shipped frozen to their door, with no subscription required. Daily Harvest is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no first-party developer API; its only public programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth2 authorization layer exposed at account.daily-harvest.com.
d.name: Daily Harvest

d.description: DailyDeal.de is a German consumer deals, coupons, and discounts platform ("Deals, Gutscheine & Schnäppchen") that aggregates daily deals across categories including electronics, fashion, home and garden, beauty, kids, sports, and free-to-try product samples ("gratis testen"). Shoppers browse discounted products, brand vouchers, and shop-specific coupon codes, and read shopping guides in the site's Magazin. Originally founded in Berlin in 2009 and briefly owned by Google, DailyDeal today operates as a WordPress-based consumer commerce and content site and publishes no public developer API program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio lead.
d.name: DailyDeal.de

d.description: Dailyhunt is India's largest local-language content and news aggregation platform, operated by VerSe Innovation (Bengaluru). It aggregates news, video, and short-form "DailyShare" cards from more than 600 publisher partners across fourteen Indian languages and distributes them through its own apps, mobile web and PWA, and — for approved partners — through a signed Content Syndication API that pushes the same catalogue into partner apps, OEM device home screens and browsers. Alongside syndication, Dailyhunt runs an advertising stack: the Dailyhunt Direct self-serve ad platform, a JavaScript Tracker SDK (with a Google Tag Manager path) for down-funnel conversion tracking on advertiser sites, and an E-Commerce Shopping Catalog API for vendors to batch-upload product feeds. VerSe Innovation also operates the Josh short-video app. API access is partner-gated: keys, secrets and partner codes are provisioned during onboarding rather than self-service, and the production feed host is not publicly resolvable.
d.name: Dailyhunt

d.description: DailyMealz is a Saudi Arabia-based meal subscription service that delivers fresh daily lunches and full-day meal plans sourced from a network of more than sixty partner restaurants. Subscribers choose a package (healthy, keto, diet, and similar options), select meals from a rotating menu, and control delivery timing through the DailyMealz mobile app. The company also operates a DailyMealz for Business offering for corporate meal programs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; DailyMealz is an app-first consumer brand and publishes no public developer API surface, documentation portal, or API specifications as of this profiling round.
d.name: DailyMealz

d.description: Dailymotion Developer API
d.name: Dailymotion

d.description: DailyPay is an on-demand pay (earned wage access) platform that lets employees access wages they have already earned before the scheduled payday. The company sells to employers across healthcare, retail, restaurants, manufacturing, hospitality and the public sector, and integrates with 180+ HCM, payroll and time-management systems. Its developer surface — the DailyPay REST API — is a json:api-shaped OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect API covering people, jobs, organizations, paychecks, accounts (including the EARNINGS_BALANCE account that carries available earnings), transfers and PCI-scoped debit-card tokenization, complemented by DailyPay Elements, a set of hosted drop-in iframe components for embedding on-demand pay into partner applications.
d.name: DailyPay

d.description: Dairy Queen (International Dairy Queen, Inc.) is an American chain of soft-serve ice cream and fast-food restaurants operating thousands of franchised locations worldwide, known for its Blizzard treats, cones, sundaes, and grill menu. A subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, it reaches consumers through its website, mobile app, and loyalty program. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead; Dairy Queen publishes no public developer API program, so this repo currently carries only a probed domain-security profile and identity metadata.
d.name: Dairyqueen

d.description: DAIVIN! is a deep-tech hardware company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, based in San Francisco and Finland) building tankless diving technology. Its core product, SPRING, is marketed as the "world's first tankless diving technology": instead of carrying heavy pressurized oxygen tanks, a diver wears a lightweight vest of electrolyzers and a battery belt that use electricity to split water on demand into breathable oxygen (O2) and hydrogen (H2), targeting depths up to 200 meters / 650 ft. Founder Leo Kankkunen frames breathing as "fundamentally an energy problem," and the company envisions applications beyond recreational and professional diving across space exploration, high-altitude rescue, hospitals, and aircraft. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital portfolio lead surfaced via y-combinator. Daivin runs a conceptual marketing website (Wix) and a news blog; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface, so no API artifacts apply to this provider.
d.name: Daivin

d.description: dajiabao is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of the Chinese venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no reachable public surface: dajiabao.com resolves in DNS (139.196.207.93, an Alibaba Cloud Shanghai address, nameservers at eName) but both TCP/80 and TCP/443 time out, so there is no website, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known/ discovery surface to profile. Mail is delegated to Tencent Exmail (mxbiz1/mxbiz2.qq.com), which indicates the registration is still actively used even though the web presence is dark. Searches of npm, PyPI, and crates.io returned no packages under this name, and the company publishes no OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or MCP surface that the network can index. This profile is retained as a verified-dark lead and should be re-probed on a later round in case the company relaunches a public site.
d.name: dajiabao

d.description: DalCor Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, with offices in Zug, Switzerland, Leatherhead in the United Kingdom, and Sarasota, Florida. It is developing dalcetrapib, positioned as the first pharmacogenetic precision medicine in cardiovascular disease, targeted specifically at patients carrying the AA genotype at the rs1967309 variant of the ADCY9 gene — a genotype present in up to 20% of the general population and in more than 40% of populations of African ancestry. DalCor holds the worldwide exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialise dalcetrapib together with rights to the companion genetic marker. The compound is being evaluated in Dal-GenE-2 (DAL-302), a Phase 3 double-blind randomized placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes confirmatory trial in 2,000 post-acute-coronary-syndrome patients with the ADCY9 AA genotype, coordinated by the Montreal Health Innovations Coordinating Centre and following the dal-GenE (DAL-301) trial, which showed a 21% relative risk reduction in fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarction across 6,149 patients in 34 countries. DalCor runs no developer program and publishes no product API; the only machine-readable surface it exposes is the anonymously readable WordPress REST content API behind dalcorpharma.com, which serves the bilingual English/French corporate site.
d.name: DalCor Pharmaceuticals

d.description: Daleela, by MotherBeing, is an AI-powered women's health application for the MENA region that combines medically-verified guidance with clinical services. The app offers a privacy-first AI health assistant whose answers are reviewed and approved by women's-health specialists, period and cycle tracking that monitors menstrual cycles and hormonal phases with personalized lifestyle recommendations, on-demand doctor consultations connecting users with specialists in gynecology, dermatology, nutrition, and sexual health within 24 hours, and expert-led educational programs covering hormones, fertility, and fitness. Daleela is distributed as a consumer mobile application on iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play). It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a consumer mobile product it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.
d.name: Daleela

d.description: Dalma is a French insurtech offering pet health insurance for dogs and cats, reimbursing veterinary bills (up to 100%, no deductible, EUR 2,500 annual ceiling) with fast payouts (50% within 30 seconds) and unlimited teleconsultations with veterinarians via its mobile app. Founded in Paris and backed by Northzone, Dalma insures 60,000+ pets across France and has expanded to Germany. It is a direct-to-consumer insurance brand with a member app (app.dalma.co) and a quote/subscription funnel; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal at this time.
d.name: Dalma

d.description: Daloopa is an AI-powered fundamental financial data platform for institutional investors, providing analyst-verified, source-linked financial data extracted from SEC filings, earnings transcripts, investor presentations and press releases. Coverage spans 6,000+ global public companies with roughly 14 years of history, and every datapoint is hyperlinked back to the exact location in the original source document for auditability. The company sells to hedge funds, mutual funds, investment banks, equity research and private equity teams, and delivers the same dataset across a REST API, a hosted remote MCP server, an Excel add-in, prebuilt Data Sheets, the Scout AI modeling agent, and native cloud-warehouse shares via Snowflake, Databricks and AWS S3.
d.name: Daloopa

d.description: Damae Medical is a Paris-based medical device company developing non-invasive imaging technology for dermatology and skin cancer diagnostics. Its flagship deepLive system is built on proprietary LC-OCT (Line-field Confocal Optical Coherence Tomography), which pairs deep tissue penetration with cellular resolution to produce histology-like vertical and confocal-like horizontal 3D views of the skin in vivo. deepLive received CE Mark Class IIa certification in 2023 and FDA 510(k) clearance in March 2025, and integrates quantitative analysis tools such as 3D surface segmentation, cellular network visualization, melanin distribution mapping, and dermal fiber segmentation. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.
d.name: Damae Medical

d.description: Damon Motorcycles (Damon Inc.) is a Vancouver, British Columbia electric motorcycle company founded in 2017 by Jay Giraud and Dominique Kwong, and an alumnus of the Techstars accelerator. Damon builds high-performance electric motorcycles led by the HyperSport and HyperFighter models, and is known for two safety and ergonomics technologies: CoPilot, a 360-degree advanced warning system that uses radar, cameras, and sensors to alert riders to surrounding hazards, and Shift, a transformable ergonomics system that adjusts the riding position between commuter and sport stances. The company has faced significant financial and going-concern difficulties, and its public web presence at damon.com currently returns errors, so no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be verified during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Damon Motorcycles

d.description: Dana Incorporated is a global supplier of fully integrated drivetrain and electrified propulsion systems for passenger vehicles, commercial trucks, and off-highway equipment. Dana operates a developer portal at developer.danaaftermarket.com offering eight APIs for aftermarket parts search, availability, pricing, ordering, and shipment tracking across its global distribution network.
d.name: Dana

d.description: DanAds is a global advertising technology company offering a self‑serve ad platform that streamlines ad sales, operations and creative management. It enables advertisers and publishers to automate workflows, maximize revenue, and expand globally through a unified solution. The platform provides tools for campaign creation, inventory management, reporting, and integration with major ad exchanges.
d.name: DanAds

d.description: Danaher Corporation is a global life sciences and diagnostics conglomerate whose operating companies include Beckman Coulter, Leica Microsystems, Cepheid, SCIEX, IDT, Cytiva, Abcam, Aldevron, Beckman Coulter Diagnostics, Radiometer, and others. Danaher itself does not publish a corporate-level developer API; product and service APIs are provided by individual operating companies under the Danaher portfolio.
d.name: Danaher

d.description: Thousands of anime artist database to find good anime art
d.name: Danbooru Anime

d.description: Dance is a Berlin-based electric mobility subscription company that offers e-bikes and e-mopeds as an all-in-one monthly subscription. A single fixed monthly fee bundles the vehicle together with on-demand repairs and maintenance, fast replacements, and theft protection, so members can ride without owning or servicing the hardware themselves. Dance operates in Berlin, Hamburg, and Paris, with product lines including the Dance One and Dance One Step e-bikes and the Dance Moped. Founded in 2020 by SoundCloud co-founders Alexander Ljung and Eric Quidenus-Wahlforss with Jimdo co-founder Christian Springub, Dance is a consumer-facing, app-based service backed by HV Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, help, and security surface.
d.name: Dance

d.description: Dandelion Energy is a residential geothermal heating and cooling company that designs, engineers, and installs ground-source heat pump systems for homeowners and new-home builders. Its systems tap the earth's stable subsurface temperature to heat and cool homes year-round, cutting utility bills and carbon emissions versus conventional fossil-fuel HVAC. Dandelion delivers end-to-end service from ground-loop drilling through turnkey installation, and offers a leasing program that removes the upfront cost for buyers. The company reports thousands of installations across the United States. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the frontier-tech and climate sector; it currently exposes no public developer API.
d.name: Dandelion Energy

d.description: Dandy is a digital dental lab platform for dentists, dental practices, and dental service organizations (DSOs). It combines intraoral scanner hardware, cloud-based case management software, and in-house dental lab manufacturing into a single scan-to-lab workflow. Dentists capture digital impressions with a Dandy intraoral scanner, submit cases through Dandy software, collaborate in real time with lab technicians via chat, video, and chairside scan review, and receive finished restorations manufactured by Dandy. Product lines include crowns, bridges, implants, clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards, splints, and sleep apnea devices. Dandy positions itself as an AI-powered digital dental lab modernizing restorative and orthodontic dentistry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes an agent-facing llms.txt and ai-index.json but does not currently expose a public developer API.
d.name: Dandy

d.description: Dangdang (当当, dangdang.com) is a Chinese business-to-consumer e-commerce company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Beijing. It began as one of China's largest online booksellers and expanded into a broad general-merchandise marketplace spanning books, e-books and e-readers, digital reading, consumer electronics, apparel, home goods, and maternal and baby products. Once listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DANG) before being taken private, Dangdang was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No active public developer program, open platform, or machine-readable API surface was reachable during enrichment (the site is geo-restricted); this profile carries a probed domain-security posture and awaits any discoverable API artifacts.
d.name: Dangdang

d.description: Danger, Inc. was a Palo Alto, California mobile computing company founded on December 9, 1999 by Andy Rubin, Joe Britt, and Matt Hershenson, all former Apple, WebTV, and Philips engineers. Danger built the Danger Hiptop, sold in the United States as the T-Mobile Sidekick, an early client-server ("cloud") smartphone whose downloadable application catalog prefigured the app stores later shipped by Android and iOS. Andy Rubin left Danger in 2003 to found Android. Microsoft acquired Danger on February 11, 2008 for a price reported at roughly $500 million and folded the team into "Project Pink," which shipped as the short-lived Microsoft Kin. Most former Danger staff had left Microsoft by October 2009 and the company was wound down by approximately 2011. Danger was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a historic Redpoint Ventures portfolio holding. It is defunct: the danger.com domain no longer resolves and there is no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.
d.name: Danger

d.description: Database of malicious Discord accounts
d.name: Dangerous Discord Database

d.description: Open energy data from Energinet to society
d.name: Danish data service Energi

d.description: The Danish Meteorological Institute is a government agency responsible for providing meteorological and climate services in Denmark. DMI publishes weather observations, climate data, ocean observations, and lightning data through its Open Data API and supplies forecast products via the AWS Open Data registry. The agency operates weather stations, radar systems, and satellites to monitor and forecast weather across Denmark, Greenland, and the Faroe Islands.
d.name: Danish Meteorological Institutes

d.description: Danske Bank (UK) is the trading name of Northern Bank Limited, a retail and commercial bank headquartered in Belfast and the largest bank in Northern Ireland. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of Denmark's Danske Bank Group and is authorised by the UK Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and PRA. As "Northern Bank Limited t/a Danske Bank" it is one of the CMA9 - the nine largest current-account providers mandated by the UK Competition and Markets Authority to implement the Open Banking standard - and an FCA-authorised ASPSP under PSD2. It publishes the UK Open Banking (OBIE) API family: a public, unauthenticated Open Data API (ATMs, branches, personal and business current accounts, unsecured SME loans, commercial credit cards) and the FAPI-secured Read/Write APIs for Account and Transaction Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), Confirmation of Funds (CBPII), Variable Recurring Payments (VRP), and Events, alongside a suite of premium corporate APIs (account transaction and balance reporting, payment collection, corporate payment initiation, and FX trade reporting and execution) exposed through the Danske Bank developer portal.
d.name: Danske Bank (UK)

d.description: Dant3 is a public-beta social and work network, operated from London by Snooptsz Group LTD, where Humans, AI Agents, Bots and Robots participate under visible identity and operator-accountability rules. It publishes a machine-first surface on dant3.net: a 15-operation Machine API (OpenAPI 3.1.0, policy version 2026-08-24.v5) for two-field provisional machine join, heartbeat, bounded public replies and posts, public Room join/create, Human claim and claimed-machine job posting; a free anonymous remote MCP server (seven tools over Streamable HTTP, listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.snooptsz/dant3); an A2A 1.0 Discovery Agent with a live JSON-RPC endpoint; installable Agent Skills, llms.txt, an ARD ai-catalog and public Human, machine and job feeds. Machine credentials are scoped bearer tokens (dant3_live_*) with a 30-day provisional window, published numeric rate limits, and no payment, private-room or physical-actuation authority.
d.name: Dant3

d.description: DAOex (DAO Exchange, product-branded "Commune") was a web3 community relationship management platform positioned as an all-in-one tool for understanding, engaging, and growing DAO and NFT communities. Its advertised surface covered member directories bridging on-chain and off-chain data, referral programs with unique member/affiliate links, quests, contests and bounties as rewards infrastructure, Discord-native engagement and role assignment, and payouts of tokens, NFTs or Discord roles on Ethereum mainnet and Polygon via an automatically provisioned Gnosis Safe, with a points-and-CSV fallback for pre-token communities. Surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears DEFUNCT: daoex.app no longer resolves in DNS (NXDOMAIN, no SOA), the site was a single-page Webflow marketing site last published 2022-09-22 and last archived 2023-03-21, and no API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, package or GitHub organization was ever published.
d.name: DAOex

d.description: Dapper was an advertising-technology and web-data company founded in 2006 by Jonathan Aizen and Eran Shir, seed-funded by Accel. It ran two surfaces: Dapper Ads, an intent-driven dynamic-ad product that pulled live product and inventory data from an advertiser's own site into targeted creative without IT integration; and open.dapper.net (the "Dapp Factory" / Dapper: The Data Mapper), a hosted tool that turned any web page into structured feeds, web services and widgets — XML, RSS, JSON, YAML, CSV, iCalendar, Google Gadgets, Netvibes modules and image loops — effectively letting anyone "create an API for any site" before providers published their own. Dapper was acquired by Yahoo! in 2010 and both surfaces were shut down; dapper.net now resolves to Yahoo nameservers with no host, and open.dapper.net no longer resolves. There is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.
d.name: Dapper

d.description: Dapper Labs is the blockchain company behind the Flow network and a portfolio of consumer NFT experiences including NBA Top Shot, NFL All Day, Disney Pinnacle, and LaLiga Golazos. Its primary public developer surface is the Flow Access API — a public, unauthenticated blockchain node API available over REST (rest-mainnet.onflow.org), gRPC, and WebSocket event streaming — used to read on-chain data (blocks, transactions, accounts, collections, events), execute read-only Cadence scripts, and submit signed Cadence transactions. Flow and its client tooling (FCL, the Flow CLI, Go/JS SDKs) are maintained under the onflow GitHub organization. This profile began as a VC-portfolio stub and has been enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Dapper/Flow's real developer artifacts.
d.name: Dapper Labs

d.description: DapperDox is an open-source API documentation generator that creates beautiful, customizable reference documentation from OpenAPI specifications. It supports theming, overlays, and cross-referencing across multiple API specifications, making it suitable for teams managing complex API ecosystems. DapperDox is a developer tool rather than a hosted service, so it does not expose its own public web API.
d.name: DapperDox

d.description: Dappier provides AI-driven conversational ad experiences for publishers, enabling them to monetize content through agentic ads and AI answer interfaces. It offers a platform where advertisers can reach consumers via AI agents, with a storefront that allows autonomous purchases without signup. The service includes tools for launching AI answer experiences, managing ad formats, and integrating with publisher workflows, aiming to create new revenue streams in the AI era.
d.name: Dappier

d.description: DappRadar is a blockchain application discovery and analytics platform, widely described as "the world's dapp store." It tracks decentralized applications (dapps), NFT collections, tokens, and DeFi activity across many blockchains, providing rankings, portfolio tracking, and on-chain market intelligence to consumers, builders, and investors. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, DappRadar is a Prosus Ventures portfolio company. This profile was seeded from that portfolio and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
d.name: DappRadar

d.description: Dapr (Distributed Application Runtime) is a portable, event-driven runtime that makes it easy for developers to build resilient, stateless, and stateful applications that run on the cloud and edge. It provides building block APIs for state management, pub/sub messaging, service invocation, bindings, actors, workflows, secrets, configuration, distributed locks, cryptography, jobs scheduling, health checks, and metadata.
d.name: Dapr

d.description: Dapta is a no-code AI voice and text agent platform for small and medium businesses, letting teams build AI phone agents, SMS and WhatsApp bots, meeting notetakers, and workflow automations in minutes without writing code. Voice agents answer inbound and place outbound calls in 20+ languages, qualify leads, book appointments, and handle support 24/7; text agents automate SMS and WhatsApp conversations; Flow Studio wires no-code automations across 1000+ tools with CRM connectors for HubSpot, Salesforce, and GoHighLevel. Dapta exposes a hosted, workspace-scoped Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at mcp.dapta.ai so AI clients such as Claude and Codex can drive a workspace, plus an outbound webhook surface for call, meeting, flow, and campaign events. The company is backed by 500 Global and says it serves 50,000+ businesses.
d.name: Dapta

d.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).
d.name: Daqstra

d.description: Darden Restaurants is the largest full-service restaurant company in the world, owning and operating brands such as Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Yard House, The Capital Grille, Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Eddie V's, Seasons 52, Bahama Breeze, Ruth's Chris Steak House, and Chuy's. Darden does not publish a public developer API; consumer-facing ordering and loyalty are exposed only via internal mobile apps and partnerships such as Uber for delivery.
d.name: Darden Restaurants

d.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.
d.name: Dare Drop

d.description: Darewise Entertainment is a European game studio founded by AAA industry veterans — game director Benjamin Charbit (Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag) and engine tech lead Samuel Kahn (Ubisoft Snowdrop, Crytek CryEngine) — with offices in Paris, London and Barcelona. It builds Life Beyond, a free-to-play sci-fi MMO on Unreal Engine 5 set on the alien world Dolos, combining Web3 asset ownership (NFTs and ERC-20 tokens) with player-driven settlement and governance. Animoca Brands announced the acquisition of a majority stake in April 2022, and the studio now trades as Life Beyond Studios. The original darewise.com website last served content in April 2025 and the host now refuses TCP connections on 80 and 443. Darewise publishes no API, developer portal, or API documentation of any kind; the only machine-readable developer artifact it has ever released publicly is an open-source AsyncAPI generator template that emits Unreal Engine C++ from an AsyncAPI 3.x document, published to npm under its own scope.
d.name: Darewise

d.description: Daring Foods is an American plant-based food company, founded in 2018 by Ross Mackay and Eliott Kessas, that makes 100% plant-based chicken from a deliberately short ingredient list with soy as the protein base. Trading simply as "Daring", it sells retail Plant Chicken in shredded, diced and breaded-pieces formats plus a line of ready-to-heat Plant Chicken Bowls and Plant Chicken Wings through more than 15,000 US grocery stores, and runs a separate foodservice business supplying bulk and gluten-free product to restaurants, campus dining and institutional kitchens. The company raised over $120 million across 2020-2021 during the plant-based protein boom and was acquired by the Australian plant-based meat manufacturer v2food in 2025, under which it retains its own brand. Daring Foods is a consumer packaged goods business, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no product API, and offers no portal, SDKs or developer support. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind daring.com, which is anonymously readable and unusually well-stocked for a CPG site - 208 recipes classified by cooking method, 14 retail products, 7 foodservice products, 17 marketing pages and a 749-item media library - captured here for discovery purposes.
d.name: Daring Foods

d.description: Dark Sky is a hyperlocal weather forecast REST API (now part of Apple) that provided minute-by-minute precipitation forecasts, hourly weather conditions, and multi-day outlooks powered by machine-learning models. The API delivered real-time and historical weather data for any latitude and longitude worldwide, including current conditions, 60-minute minutely precipitation intensity, 48-hour hourly forecasts, and 7-day daily summaries. It was acquired by Apple in March 2020; new developer signups closed immediately, and the API was permanently shut down on March 31, 2023. Apple's WeatherKit REST API is the successor service.
d.name: Dark Sky

d.description: Darktrace builds the ActiveAI Security Platform, an AI-native cybersecurity platform powered by Self-Learning AI that models normal behavior across network, email, cloud, identity, OT, and endpoint environments to detect novel threats without relying on predefined signatures. The platform spans Network, Email, Cloud, Identity, OT, Endpoint, and Secure AI products plus cross-platform capabilities including Cyber AI Analyst, Proactive Exposure Management, Attack Surface Management, Adaptive Human Defense, and Forensic Acquisition & Investigation. Darktrace exposes a gated REST API at <instance>.cloud.darktrace.com/omniapi for partner and customer integrations. Named a Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for NDR; serves 10,000+ customers globally.
d.name: Darktrace

d.description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.
d.name: Darling Ingredients

d.description: Darrow is an AI legal-intelligence company (founded 2020, offices in New York, Miami, Arizona and Tel Aviv) that scans public real-world signals — regulatory filings, court dockets, incident reports, corporate disclosures and web behavior — to detect legal violations at scale, size the affected class, predict outcomes and value the resulting cases. Its platform serves plaintiff law firms (case origination, predictive litigation analytics, portfolio management, PlaintiffLink intake), insurers (predictive underwriting) and corporate compliance teams (Privacy Radar, listed in the Microsoft Marketplace). Darrow publishes no public developer program: the product is delivered through an Auth0-protected customer portal at portal.darrow.ai, and the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the OpenID Connect discovery document served by its identity tenant.
d.name: Darrow

d.description: Dartmouth College is a private Ivy League research university in Hanover, New Hampshire. Its programmable footprint is small, mostly gated, and largely operated by vendors on Dartmouth's behalf — the ordinary shape for a research university, which is a federation of buyers rather than an API producer. Exactly one institution-operated interface is open to the public without credentials: the JSON backend of Dartmouth Class Search (courses.dartmouth.edu), which returns the full timetable of class meetings keyless and which Dartmouth does not document as an API. Everything else Dartmouth itself runs is behind authentication: DartAPI at api.dartmouth.edu answers 401 on every resource path and issues JWTs only against a hand-issued API key tied to a Dartmouth Service Account, its developer portal at developer.dartmouth.edu redirects to Microsoft Entra SAML so not one reference page is readable from outside, and the Dartmouth Chat AI API requires a DARTMOUTH_API_KEY. The one genuinely open machine-readable artifact Dartmouth publishes is its SAML identity-federation metadata in InCommon. The research and data surfaces — Dartmouth Open Data on ArcGIS Hub, Dartmouth Digital Commons on bepress/Elsevier, Dartmouth Dataverse — are Dartmouth's data on someone else's contract and are recorded here as tenant relationships, not as Dartmouth engineering.
d.name: Dartmouth College

d.description: Darwin AI is an AI governance platform built exclusively for state, local, and education (SLED) government agencies, providing a centralized, secure hub for the public sector to safely adopt, manage, and govern AI tools while ensuring compliance, accountability, and public records requirements are met. The platform serves IT departments, innovation and digital services teams, city and county management, and data governance professionals across municipal and state government. Its core product surface includes the Control Center, which delivers cross-departmental visibility into AI usage along with records management and FOIA compliance tracking; the Policy Wizard, which helps agencies establish and refine AI policies aligned to regulatory requirements using 30+ policy frameworks and 15+ city and county regulation packs; Risk Management, which detects unauthorized or unvetted AI applications; the AI Navigator, which monitors departmental adoption patterns and surfaces actionable insights; and the Marketplace, an organization-wide hub of approved AI applications. Darwin AI was named to Government Technology's 2026 GovTech 100. The company also publishes a free public Policy Wizard tool. Darwin is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a government-sector company profile. As of this enrichment pass Darwin publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.
d.name: Darwin

d.description: Darwinbox is a cloud-based HRMS platform offering a REST API for managing employee records, recruitment, performance, payroll, attendance, travel, and workforce analytics in enterprise organizations. The API supports programmatic access to data stored in Darwinbox instances and enables importing data into the platform. Access is provided on a request-only basis to privileged users and supports token-based authentication using SHA512 hashing.
d.name: Darwinbox

d.description: DAS Technology (formerly Digital Air Strike) is an automotive-retail marketing and customer-experience technology company serving more than 9,300 dealerships and OEMs. Its AI-native CDXP (Customer Data and Experience Platform) unifies sales, service, and retention data across three product lines: Attract (multi-channel digital advertising across Google, Facebook, Microsoft, Amazon, and TikTok), Convert (AI-powered lead response, instant quotes, and long-cycle nurturing), and Retain (reputation management, equity mining, and service-retention campaigns). DAS Technology ships a real REST API — the DAS Web API — served from its legacy Digital Air Strike domain and documented by two publicly readable Swagger 2.0 documents covering 136 operations across accounts and dealer-group hierarchy, reviews and reputation, surveys and NPS, enterprise statistics, transactional messaging, users, vehicles and transactions. The contract is discoverable but the program around it is not: there is no developer portal, no pricing, no SDK, no sandbox, no status page and no changelog, and access is arranged through the dealer, OEM or partner relationship.
d.name: DAS Technology

d.description: Dascena was an Oakland, California health-technology company that built machine-learning diagnostic and clinical decision support algorithms for hospitals, most notably InSight, a sepsis prediction model that scored electronic health record vitals and labs in real time to flag patients at risk hours before onset, plus FDA breakthrough-designated models for acute kidney injury and gastrointestinal bleeding. The algorithms were delivered as an embedded integration inside a customer hospital's EHR under a services and laboratory agreement rather than as a public developer API, so the company never operated a developer portal, published a machine-readable contract, or shipped client SDKs. CirrusDx acquired the Dascena Labs laboratory business effective 5 August 2022 and the company identity now trades as DBA CirrusDx; the dascena.com domain no longer resolves.
d.name: Dascena

d.description: Dasera is a data security company in the data security posture management (DSPM) and data governance space, founded by Ani Chaudhuri and backed by Sierra Ventures. Its platform was built to continuously discover, classify, and monitor sensitive data across cloud and on-premises data stores (databases, warehouses, data lakes) and to surface data security, privacy, and compliance risk across the data lifecycle. As of this enrichment pass the standalone dasera.com origin is unreachable (a Cloudflare 1001 origin error with a failed TLS handshake), so no live developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be harvested; this profile records the domain-security posture that could still be probed via DNS/TLS and remains a stub awaiting a live API surface.
d.name: Dasera

d.description: Dash is a peer-to-peer cryptocurrency network offering fast, low-cost payments with InstantSend, privacy via CoinJoin mixing, and decentralized governance through Masternodes. Developers can query blocks, transactions, addresses, UTXOs, governance objects, and real-time network events through the open-source Insight REST and WebSocket API, and can access Dash Platform layer-2 (DashPay identity, data contracts, documents, tokens) through the Decentralized API (DAPI) over gRPC and JSON-RPC.
d.name: Dash

d.description: Dash0 is an OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for engineering teams who want full visibility into logs, metrics, traces, profiles and events without operating complex pipelines or proprietary agents. Founded in 2023 (Series B, $110M, 2026), Dash0 ingests OTLP natively, correlates signals automatically, and offers dashboards, PromQL-based alerting, SLOs, synthetic and website monitoring, a service map, transparent cost controls, and Agent0 AI SRE agents. Its public API is a 108-operation OpenAPI 3.1 surface (regional AWS/GCP hosts) covering Observability-as-Code (dashboards, check/recording/ sampling rules, views, spam filters, notification channels, synthetic checks, automations), telemetry query (spans/logs/traces/SQL), and a Prometheus HTTP API, plus an OAuth-protected MCP server, a Go CLI and a Terraform provider.
d.name: Dash0

d.description: Dashbase, Inc. was a San Jose, California based developer of a next-generation log analytics and search platform, positioned as a lighter, real-time alternative to heavier log-management and observability stacks for DevOps and engineering teams. The company was a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (dashbase.io) no longer resolves / times out and its GitHub organization retains only a single archived fork, so the company appears to be defunct or to have been acquired and wound down; no live developer surface, API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation could be located. This profile is retained as a network record with only verifiable facts.
d.name: Dashbase

d.description: Dashbot is a conversational-data analytics platform (now operating as Dimension Labs) that ingests chatbot, voice-assistant, live-chat, call, survey and other unstructured customer conversations and enriches them into structured "dimensions" for causal intelligence and reporting. Data is sent in through a Universal REST tracker and dozens of one-click integrations (Twilio, Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, Salesforce, Amazon Lex/Connect, Google Dialogflow, Genesys, Cognigy, Kore.ai, Rasa, and more), then explored through dashboards, data explorer, flows and an analytics Agent. A REST Export API (api.dimensionlabs.io) and first-party JavaScript, Python and Ruby SDKs let teams pull enriched data back out programmatically. Dashbot was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners; the company rebranded to Dimension Labs while the API and SDKs retain the Dashbot name (api.dashbot.io still responds).
d.name: Dashbot

d.description: Dashlane is a password manager and credential-security platform for individuals, families, and enterprises, protecting against credential reuse, phishing, and account takeover with zero-knowledge encryption, passkey support, and AI-powered phishing detection. For developers, Dashlane publishes a read-only Public API (OpenAPI 3.0) that returns real-time team data — member roles/status/usage metrics, activated devices, and password-health analytics (weak, reused, compromised credentials) — authenticated with a bearer DLP token. Dashlane also ships an open-source CLI (dcli), a GitHub Action for injecting vault secrets into CI/CD, SCIM provisioning, and SSO federation.
d.name: Dashlane

d.description: dashmobile (listed by Slow Ventures as "Dash Labs") was surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no operating public surface: the listed domain dashmobile.co has no DNS records at all (no A record, no NS delegation) and returns no HTTP response, and the Internet Archive holds exactly one capture of the domain (2022-05-24), which was itself a .CO registry domain-expired parking page rather than company content. The company therefore has no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no discoverable artifacts of any kind. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct portfolio lead and is not a candidate for further enrichment unless the company relaunches on a new domain.
d.name: dashmobile

d.description: Dasient was a web anti-malware company founded in 2008 in Sunnyvale, California by ex-Google engineers Neil Daswani and Shariq Rizvi with McKinsey consultant Ameet Ranadive. It sold cloud-based protection against web-based malware and malvertising, scanning customer websites and ad networks with its Malware Analysis Platform. It shipped a JSON-RPC over HTTP "Web Protection API" that let customers schedule and run on-demand malware scans of individual domains and URLs, with tiered pricing by scans per day. Twitter acquired Dasient in January 2012 for a reported $19.1 million; the product was retired, dasient.com went dark in late 2012, and the domain is now a parked defensive registration held by Twitter. This company is DEFUNCT and has no live API surface to enrich.
d.name: Dasient

d.description: Dassault Systèmes provides the 3DEXPERIENCE platform with thousands of publicly available REST APIs for product design, simulation, and manufacturing industries. The platform covers SolidWorks, CATIA, ENOVIA, and 3D collaboration tools, exposing web services across engineering items, manufacturing processes, CAD collaboration, project tasks, and partner order management through standardized RESTful endpoints.
d.name: Dassault Systèmes

d.description: DAT Freight & Analytics operates the largest truckload freight marketplace in North America - the DAT One load board - along with RateView, the industry's benchmark for spot and contract freight rates drawn from hundreds of billions of dollars in real transactions. DAT exposes these products to Transportation Management Systems (TMS) and freight platforms through the DAT Developer Portal (developer.dat.com), a RESTful API suite covering load posting and search, RateView rate lookups, BookNow instant booking, and shipment tracking. Access is subscription-gated: RESTful integration requires a DAT One load board subscription and a service (organization) account, and RateView access requires a Combo Pro or Combo Premium plan. Every request is authenticated with a two-tier token model - an organization token issued from service-account credentials plus a user token for the account making the call.
d.name: DAT Freight & Analytics

d.description: Data is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
d.name: Data

d.description: Data Commons is an open knowledge graph initiative led by Google that aggregates and harmonizes the world's public data into a single graph, making global statistical data simple to explore, query, and integrate through REST, Python, BigQuery, web component, and MCP interfaces.
d.name: Data Commons

d.description: Data Driven Bioscience (now operating as Duoseq, a ddb.bio service) is a cancer genomics testing company that performs comprehensive molecular profiling of both DNA and RNA from a single sample in an on-site workflow, delivering results from sample to report in roughly two days. Its platform detects mutations, expression levels, gene fusions, and clonotype information, and integrates directly with Epic and other leading EHR systems so results flow into the patient chart. The company is a portfolio company of initialized-capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes a marketing/clinical website but no public developer or API surface.
d.name: Data Driven Bioscience

d.description: Data Elite Services, Inc. was a San Francisco company associated with Data Elite, a venture lab and early-stage accelerator for big-data startups and data scientists founded in 2013 at 135 Main Street, San Francisco, California. The entity was registered in California on 2013-08-27 as a foreign stock corporation and its filing status is recorded as forfeited by the Franchise Tax Board, indicating the business is no longer active. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live company website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The dataelite.com domain resolves but redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale parking lander rather than a company site, and no other candidate domain resolved. This record is retained as an inactive historical entry in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich; it should not be treated as an active API provider.
d.name: Data Elite Services

d.description: Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs) are graphical models that depict how data moves through a system across processes, data stores, external entities, and flows. The technique spans Yourdon/DeMarco and Gane-Sarson notations, hierarchical context and level-N decomposition, and modern tooling for threat modeling, software architecture, and data governance.
d.name: Data Flow Diagrams

d.description: Data Format covers the syntactic conventions used to represent, exchange, and persist information. The landscape spans text formats (JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, TOML), binary formats (Protocol Buffers, Avro, Parquet, ORC, MessagePack, BSON, CBOR, Arrow), and schema languages and IDLs that govern how those formats are validated and evolved.
d.name: Data Format

d.description: DATA GO JP is a national government open-data portal for Japan running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 18,366 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
d.name: DATA GO JP

d.description: Data Innovations LLC is a clinical laboratory informatics company that builds enterprise laboratory management and instrument-connectivity software for hospitals, health systems, and diagnostic labs. Its flagship Instrument Manager middleware connects analyzers, laboratory information systems (LIS), and EHR platforms such as Epic Beaker and Oracle Cerner, while EP Evaluator supports method validation and quality control, and Lab GPS delivers operational analytics. The company helps clinical labs optimize productivity, connectivity, and risk management across regional, community, and federal health systems. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.
d.name: Data Innovations

d.description: Data Modeling is the discipline of designing structured representations of data to organize information, define relationships, and govern how data is stored, accessed, and managed. It spans conceptual, logical, and physical models across relational, dimensional, NoSQL, graph, and data vault paradigms, supported by standards and tools from the OMG, DAMA, Erwin, PowerDesigner, dbt, and modern data modeling platforms.
d.name: Data Modeling

d.description: Data Models are structured representations of entities, attributes, and relationships that define how data is stored, accessed, and exchanged. The landscape spans relational, hierarchical, network, object, document, graph, key-value, columnar, and event-sourced models, plus shared semantic models like Schema.org, FIBO, FHIR, ISO 20022, and W3C RDF/OWL.
d.name: Data Models

d.description: Data Privacy Standards is the landscape of laws, regulations, frameworks, and technical standards that govern the collection, processing, sharing, and protection of personal data. It spans GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, PIPL, HIPAA, ISO/IEC 27701, NIST Privacy Framework, OECD Privacy Principles, and emerging machine-readable consent and preference signals such as IAB TCF, GPC, and W3C DPV.
d.name: Data Privacy Standards

d.description: Data Quality Standards is the landscape of frameworks, standards, and tools used to define and measure the accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness of data. It spans ISO/IEC 25012 and ISO 8000, the DAMA-DMBOK data quality dimensions, EDM Council DCAM, and open source and commercial tooling like Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests, Monte Carlo, and Anomalo.
d.name: Data Quality Standards

d.description: Data Sciences International (DSI) is a preclinical research instrumentation and services company for in vivo physiology and translational research, operating as part of Harvard Bioscience. DSI builds implantable and external telemetry systems, respiratory measurement (plethysmography, airway mechanics, pulmonary function), inhalation and smoke-exposure systems, iPRECIO infusion pumps, and behavioral monitoring (VivaMARS), paired with analysis software (Ponemah, FinePointe, NeuroScore) and surgical, data-analysis, GLP-validation and training services. It is a laboratory-instrument and life-sciences vendor rather than an API provider; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Data Sciences International

d.description: Data Sutram is an enterprise AI trust platform for the financial services sector, using external and alternative data intelligence plus agentic workflows to power fraud detection, identity and address verification, credit assessment, and collections. Its products - Trust (fraud and trust scoring), Auth (authentication and verification), and Echo (collections intelligence) - are applied across the customer lifecycle from acquisition and onboarding through portfolio monitoring and debt recovery. Data Sutram serves leading Indian banks and fintechs including HDFC, Axis, ICICI, Kotak, IndusInd, Jupiter, Navi, and Fibe, and maintains ISO 27001, ISO 27018, and SOC 2 certifications along with DPDP compliance. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and is also backed by B Capital.
d.name: Data Sutram

d.description: Data Theorem provides application security solutions that protect APIs, cloud-native applications, and mobile apps throughout the software development lifecycle. Their platform offers API security, code security, cloud security, and mobile security, leveraging AI to detect and remediate vulnerabilities, enforce compliance, and secure runtime environments.
d.name: Data Theorem

d.description: Data Warehouse Schemas is the landscape of analytical schema patterns used to organize fact and dimension data for business intelligence and reporting. It spans star, snowflake, and galaxy schemas, the Kimball dimensional modeling methodology, the Inmon Corporate Information Factory, Data Vault 2.0, and modern lakehouse table formats like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Hudi.
d.name: Data Warehouse Schemas

d.description: data.ai provides a comprehensive mobile app market intelligence platform, delivering app store analytics, market trends, competitor insights, and user acquisition data for businesses and developers worldwide. The platform aggregates data from major app stores, offering dashboards, reports, and API access to help clients make data‑driven decisions about product strategy, marketing, and investment.
d.name: data.ai

d.description: Data.ai (founded as App Annie in 2010, rebranded to data.ai in 2022) was a mobile app market-data and analytics provider, offering estimates of app downloads, revenue, usage, and competitive market intelligence across the iOS App Store and Google Play for publishers, brands, and investors. The company historically exposed a market-data API (api.data.ai) for programmatic access to app performance and store intelligence. Data.ai was acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024 and now operates as a Sensor Tower company; its standalone site is a gated login and the former public API host serves a default page, so its independent API surface has been consolidated into Sensor Tower and effectively retired. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an ivp portfolio company.
d.name: Data.ai

d.description: data.egov.bg is the national government open-data portal for Bulgaria, operated by the Ministry of e-Government (Министерство на електронното управление). It is a custom Laravel application exposing a REST API with action-style endpoints (predominantly POST with JSON bodies) under the /api prefix. It is not CKAN. Public read endpoints require no key; write/admin endpoints require an api_key obtained via a free account.
d.name: data.egov.bg (Open Data Portal of Bulgaria)

d.description: Data.gov is the United States federal government's open data catalog, operated by the General Services Administration (GSA) Technology Transformation Services. It indexes over 300,000 datasets, tools, and resources from federal, state, local, and tribal governments, as well as universities and non-profits. The catalog runs on CKAN 2.11 and exposes the standard CKAN Action API at catalog.data.gov/api/3/action for programmatic discovery and retrieval of datasets, organizations, groups, tags, and resources. Data.gov also publishes the federal Project Open Data (POD) schema (data.json) catalog endpoint at /data.json on every federal agency site, which Data.gov harvests into the central catalog. Related properties include inventory.data.gov (publisher-facing CKAN inventory), resources.data.gov (open data policy resources), and the api.data.gov shared API gateway used by 25+ federal agencies for 450+ APIs.
d.name: Data.gov
