d.description: DBND (Databand) is an open-source Python framework — a library, a set of APIs, and a CLI — for building, tracking, and observing data pipelines across data ingestion, preparation, ETL/ELT, and machine-learning workflows. It collects pipeline metadata (runs, metrics, dataframes, schemas) to give data-engineering teams a system of record for runs and to detect pipeline failures and data quality issues before they hit downstream consumers. The DBND SDK integrates with Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Databricks, dbt, and IBM DataStage. Databand was acquired by IBM in 2022 and is now IBM Databand, part of IBM's data observability offering; the open-source DBND SDK remains published on PyPI and GitHub under the databand-ai organization.
d.name: Databand

d.description: Database Normalization is the formal process of structuring relational schemas to reduce redundancy and avoid update, insert, and delete anomalies. It is governed by Codd's normal forms (1NF through 6NF) and the Boyce-Codd Normal Form, and is the foundation of relational design, taught in academic curricula and applied across all major SQL databases.
d.name: Database Normalization

d.description: Database Schema Design is the practice of defining the tables, columns, data types, constraints, indexes, and relationships that make up a database. It applies to relational, document, key-value, columnar, and graph stores, and is supported by ER tooling, schema-as-code formats like DBML and Prisma, migration tools like Liquibase and Flyway, and emerging schema registries for streaming and document data.
d.name: Database Schema Design

d.description: Databento is a market data platform that delivers historical and live financial market data through a single, normalized API. It covers equities, futures, options, and other asset classes across major venues, with full order book depth (MBO/MBP), trades, OHLCV bars, and reference data. Historical data is served over a REST HTTP API (hist.databento.com) with pay-as-you-go billing per byte streamed, while live data is delivered over a low-latency raw TCP binary protocol using Databento Binary Encoding (DBN). Official Python, C++, and Rust client libraries wrap both surfaces, and a Reference API provides security master, corporate actions, and adjustment factor data.
d.name: Databento

d.description: Databolt is a digital design agency that builds software applications, websites, and custom web platforms for startups and businesses. The agency offers UI/UX design, web development, WordPress and Prestashop premium themes, SEO services, and operates GPU- and CPU-optimized clusters for rendering and computational data processing.
d.name: Databolt

d.description: Databook is an AI-powered decision system for enterprise sales teams, combining verified market intelligence with structured reasoning to give sellers visibility into their largest deals. The platform pairs an "Outside-In Radar" of signals beyond the CRM with an advanced reasoning engine, a dynamic Customer Context Graph modeling every buying group, guided sales agents tuned to specific KPIs, a CRO dashboard for leadership, and a Value Coach for executive narratives. It serves enterprise revenue organizations across cloud, cybersecurity, managed services, and software. Databook is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Threshold Ventures. It publishes a machine-readable REST API — the DatabookAI REST API, OpenAPI 3.1.0 at https://api.databook.com/openapi.json — exposing a catalog of 66 account-research insights, asynchronous CSV batch jobs that run those insights across many target accounts, a threaded chat endpoint, and a deep-reasoning endpoint that returns cited, structured analysis. Access is not self-serve: bearer tokens are provisioned by Databook support.
d.name: Databook

d.description: Collection of Databricks REST APIs for managing workspaces, clusters, jobs, and data operations.
d.name: Databricks

d.description: Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) provide an infrastructure-as-code approach to managing Databricks data and AI projects. Bundles enable version control, CI/CD, deployment, and management of Databricks resources such as jobs, pipelines, apps, schemas, experiments, and model serving endpoints across workspaces using the Databricks CLI. Databricks renamed the product to Declarative Automation Bundles on 2026-03-16; the DABs acronym, the databricks.yml configuration file and the `databricks bundle` command surface are unchanged. The contract is a first-party JSON Schema for databricks.yml published in the databricks/cli repository and readable at runtime with `databricks bundle schema` — there is no OpenAPI, because bundles are driven by the CLI rather than by an HTTP API of their own.
d.name: Databricks Asset Bundles

d.description: DataCamp is an online learning platform (DataCamp, Inc.) for building data and AI skills through interactive, browser-based courses, guided projects, skill/career tracks, assessments, and certifications across Python, R, SQL, spreadsheets, Power BI, Tableau, Git, and generative AI. Learners write and run real code in the browser with instant feedback. DataCamp for Business adds team management, learning analytics, SSO/SAML, and user provisioning for organizations upskilling their workforce. DataCamp does not publish a public developer REST API; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record. Individual plans are Basic (free), Premium, and Teams.
d.name: DataCamp

d.description: Datacircle is a B2B data co-op API: customers send the original request of a supported data provider (currently the Up2Data, HarvestAPI and Fetchin LinkedIn profile APIs) to api.datacircle.dev with a Datacircle key at the provider's own price with no markup, and receive a daily flat file of pooled co-op data. It also ships a remote MCP server at api.datacircle.dev/mcp.
d.name: Datacircle

d.description: DataCite is a leading global non-profit organization that provides DOI (Digital Object Identifier) registration and persistent identifier services for research outputs, enabling researchers to cite, discover, and access scholarly data. DataCite maintains a REST API for minting and managing DOIs, querying metadata records, and accessing the global research data graph. Membership-based access allows institutions to register DOIs through APIs and the Fabrica web interface, while public metadata retrieval is freely available to anyone. DataCite also offers a GraphQL API, a legacy Metadata Store (MDS) API, usage statistics via its Usage Reports API, and scholarly event tracking via the Event Data API.
d.name: DataCite

d.description: Datacor is an enterprise software company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, that builds industry-specific business management and engineering software for process manufacturers, chemical distributors, and animal-nutrition producers. Its business-automation suite spans ERP, CRM, MES, WMS, formulation management, BLISS LIMS, regulatory and nutrition labeling, and TrackAbout asset tracking, while its engineering line delivers chemical process simulation and flow-modeling tools including CHEMCAD, Fathom, Arrow, Impulse, and xStream. Datacor serves the petrochemical, refinery, energy, feed, and specialty-chemical sectors, and has begun layering AI-driven capabilities across its products. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Datacor does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specifications; this profile captures its verified public identity while the API surface (if any) remains behind its customer support portal.
d.name: Datacor

d.description: DataCore Software is a software-defined storage and data management vendor serving approximately 15,000 customers worldwide, from Fortune 500 enterprises to small and medium businesses. Its portfolio includes SANsymphony (SAN and HCI storage virtualization), Swarm (scalable S3-compatible object storage for archives and backups), Nexus (a high-performance parallel file system for HPC and AI workloads), Puls8 (container-native persistent storage for Kubernetes), and StarWind hyperconverged infrastructure for edge, ROBO, and SMB deployments. DataCore does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI-described REST API; programmatic access is delivered through product-embedded interfaces and open-source integration plugins (CSI, Docker Volume Plugin, OpenStack Cinder) maintained on its GitHub organization.
d.name: Datacore

d.description: DataCrunch is a European (Finland-based) GPU cloud offering on-demand and reserved NVIDIA GPU instances (H200, H100, B200, A100, L40S, V100) plus a serverless inference and container deployment platform. Its REST API at https://api.datacrunch.io/v1 uses OAuth2 client-credentials to issue Bearer tokens and exposes instances, instance types, availability, images, SSH keys, startup scripts, volumes, balance, and serverless containers, with an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint for deployed models.
d.name: DataCrunch

d.description: Datacurve is a San Francisco-based AI infrastructure company that positions itself as "the data engine for frontier AI," building high-quality, expert-annotated datasets, reinforcement-learning environments, long-horizon agent tasks, benchmarks, and supervised fine-tuning demonstrations used to train and evaluate frontier AI models. Its offerings include off-the-shelf and custom datasets, agent-trajectory capture (tool calls, pivots, recovery attempts), and domain-sensitive evaluations across software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, machine learning, and research. Datacurve is backed by Homebrew and publishes research such as the DeepSWE long-horizon coding benchmark. The company sells through direct engagement (contact@datacurve.ai) and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.
d.name: Datacurve

d.description: Datadog is a monitoring and analytics platform that helps organizations gain insight into their infrastructure, applications, and services. It allows users to collect, visualize, and analyze real-time data from a variety of sources, including servers, databases, and cloud services. Datadog's platform enables companies to track performance metrics, troubleshoot issues, and optimize their systems for peak efficiency.
d.name: Datadog

d.description: Datadog APM provides end-to-end distributed tracing, continuous profiling, and real-time performance monitoring for applications and microservices. It automatically instruments applications to provide deep visibility into request traces, latency, and error rates across distributed systems.
d.name: Datadog APM

d.description: DataDome is a real-time bot and online fraud protection platform that inspects every web, mobile, and API request and decides — within milliseconds — whether it should be allowed, challenged, or blocked. The platform combines a JavaScript tag and mobile SDKs (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) on the client side with 40+ server-side integrations (Nginx, Apache, IIS, OpenResty, HAProxy, Cloudflare Workers, AWS CloudFront, Fastly, Bunny, Node.js, Python ASGI, Go, Ruby, Java, ASP.NET Core, Kong, Apigee, Tyk, Traefik) that forward signals to DataDome's decisioning service. Products in the platform include Bot Protect, Account Protect, Ad Protect, Page Protect, Priority Protect, Agentic Trust (governing AI agent traffic), and DDoS Protect.
d.name: DataDome

d.description: Dataedo provides a comprehensive data governance and data quality platform for mid-size organizations. It offers a centralized AI‑ready data catalog, data lineage visualization, data quality rules, and governance tools to help businesses discover, organize, and trust their data. Features include metadata scanning, AI governance, compliance readiness, and extensive connector support for SQL Server, Snowflake, Power BI, Tableau, and more, enabling efficient data management and compliance.
d.name: Dataedo

d.description: Datafiniti is a Data as a Service (DaaS) provider that collects, organizes, and standardizes large-scale data from the public web, delivering ready-to-use datasets for property, people, business, and product data through their API, web portal, and bulk downloads.
d.name: Datafiniti

d.description: DataFleets was a privacy-preserving data science and federated computation platform that let organizations run analytics and machine learning across distributed, siloed, or regulated datasets without centralizing or exposing the underlying raw data, using techniques such as federated learning and differential privacy to keep data in place while still enabling cross-silo insight. Founded as a venture-backed startup and backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, DataFleets was acquired by LiveRamp in early 2021. Its former datafleets.com domain now redirects to liveramp.com, and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API, or documentation, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.
d.name: Datafleets

d.description: COVID-19 live statistics into sites per hour
d.name: Dataflow Kit COVID-19

d.description: Datafold is a data reliability platform providing a REST API for running data diffs, monitoring column-level lineage, validating data pipelines, and detecting data regressions before deployment. It supports CI/CD integration, automated anomaly detection, schema change alerts, and cross-database comparison across major cloud data warehouses.
d.name: Datafold

d.description: DataForSEO is an SEO data platform offering REST APIs for SERP results, keyword data, backlink analysis, on-page audits, domain analytics, and competitor research across 100+ search engines. It provides pay-as-you-go access to structured SEO and digital marketing data for software developers, agencies, and enterprise teams.
d.name: DataForSEO

d.description: DataFox was a San Francisco company-intelligence and sales-prospecting startup, backed by GV among others, that used machine learning to collect and score signals about private and public companies (funding rounds, hiring, news, growth signals) and delivered them to sales and marketing teams through a web application, CRM integrations, and a company-data API. Oracle acquired DataFox and folded its company-and-signals data into the Oracle Cloud CX / Oracle Fusion Marketing stack. The independent product has been fully retired: as of this profile the datafox.com apex and www hosts are served from Oracle infrastructure and every path under www.datafox.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 to Oracle marketing pages, while api.datafox.com and app.datafox.com resolve to a parked Oracle address that accepts no connections. There is no surviving DataFox developer portal, documentation, API reference, or specification to harvest, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired company record rather than an active API provider.
d.name: DataFox

d.description: Datafy is a location-analytics and advertising platform, founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ogden, Utah, that helps destinations and communities turn visitation, spending, and behavioral signals into marketing decisions. It serves travel and tourism boards, attractions, downtowns, retail partners, and civic organizations with three core offerings — data analytics, targeted advertising, and real-world attribution — alongside Tally, a hardware attendance-measurement sensor. Datafy does publish a public API reference at https://www.datafy.com/docs covering the Datafy Data API, a self-described beta JSON-over-HTTP reporting API at api.datafy.com with three endpoints (data, options, progress), authenticated by a 30-day portal-issued bearer JWT that a customer-experience representative must unlock before the API Access page becomes visible. No OpenAPI, SDK, package, or self-service signup is published, and the company's widest developer-touching surface is its per-customer measurement tag family — website pixel, 1x1 media impression pixels, and click tags. The company reports 500+ clients and holds a SOC 2 Type II certification from A-LIGN.
d.name: Datafy

d.description: DataGrail is a San Francisco-based data privacy platform founded in 2018 by Daniel Barber and Ignacio Zendejas that helps enterprises automate privacy operations and manage regulatory compliance risk across GDPR, CCPA, and other global privacy regimes. The platform combines a Live Data Map for real-time visibility into where personal data lives across an organization's SaaS and cloud footprint, a Request Manager for orchestrating Data Subject Requests (access, deletion, opt-out) across thousands of downstream systems, a Consent solution for cookie and tracker compliance with automated enforcement, a Risk Management module for privacy and AI risk assessments (PIA, DPIA, AI risk), and an embedded agentic AI named Vera that surfaces context-aware recommendations across the platform. DataGrail exposes a documented public REST API at /api/v2 covering authentication, assessments, privacy requests, opt-out requests, integrations, webhooks, integration files, and consent audit logs, alongside an open-source ecosystem on GitHub that includes mobile Consent SDKs for iOS and Android, a Google Tag Manager consent template, and a Terraform AWS ECS module for deploying Request Manager Agents. The company serves enterprise customers including Salesforce, HubSpot, Okta, Netgear, and Dexcom, advertises 2,000+ pre-built integrations across CRM, marketing, communications, HR, data, e-commerce, and support platforms, holds patents on its Live Data Map and Smart Verification technology, is SOC 2 and ISO certified, and is backed by Felicis Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, Okta Ventures, Basis Set Ventures, Cloud Apps Capital, Operator Collective, Thomson Reuters Ventures, and Third Point Ventures.
d.name: DataGrail

d.description: DataGravity was a data management and security software company founded in April 2012 in Nashua, New Hampshire by Paula Long (co-founder of EqualLogic) and John Joseph. It pioneered the "data-aware storage" category, shipping hybrid storage arrays that indexed, classified, and audited data in place so that security, governance, and search became properties of the storage tier rather than bolt-on tooling. The company raised venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, CRV and others, won Best of Show at VMworld 2014, and began shipping in October 2014. In February 2016 it pivoted from appliances to a software-only behavioral data-security product. DataGravity ceased operations in June 2017 and its assets were assigned to a liquidator; HyTrust acquired the technology and roughly twenty employees, folding the product into HyTrust CloudAdvisor (HyTrust was itself acquired by Entrust in 2021). The datagravity.com domain no longer belongs to the company and now 301-redirects to an unrelated business (anomalo.com). No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification survives, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe.
d.name: DataGravity

d.description: DataHub is LinkedIn's generalized metadata search and discovery platform, providing a unified data catalog, lineage graph, governance tooling, and event-driven Actions Framework. It exposes GraphQL, OpenAPI, and Rest.li APIs along with Python and Java SDKs and a CLI for metadata ingestion.
d.name: DataHub

d.description: Dataiku provides an enterprise AI and analytics platform that empowers data teams to collaboratively prepare data, build predictive models, and deploy AI-driven applications at scale. The platform integrates data engineering, machine learning, and operationalization tools, offering a unified environment for data scientists, analysts, and business users to turn data into actionable insights. It supports a wide range of use cases from data preparation to model monitoring, enabling organizations to accelerate AI adoption across the enterprise.
d.name: Dataiku

d.description: Datainsurance is an early-stage US company listed in the Anthemis Group venture portfolio under the Insurance & Risk Management thesis. Anthemis publishes no company website, logo, or description for the listing, and this enrichment pass found no live public web presence: datainsurance.com, .io, .net and .tech all resolve to parked domain-sale landers, and there is no GitHub organization or public repository under the name. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API artifact could be located, so the company is carried in the API Evangelist network as an unresolved venture-portfolio lead rather than an API provider. It appears to be defunct, never publicly launched, or operating under a different brand name.
d.name: Datainsurance

d.description: DataInt is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
d.name: DataInt

d.description: Datajoy was a data-science / analytics SaaS startup surfaced as a portfolio-company lead (sector: Applicative SaaS). As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment probe the datajoy.com domain no longer serves an independent product: it issues an HTTP 301 redirect to https://www.databricks.com/product/business-intelligence, indicating the company/brand has been acquired by or folded into Databricks. No independent Datajoy public API, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known/ discovery surface exists (api.datajoy.com and docs.datajoy.com do not resolve; /.well-known/security.txt returns 404). This stub is retained for lineage; there is no live provider surface to enrich, so no API artifacts were generated.
d.name: Datajoy

d.description: Datakrew is a Singapore-based deep-tech company, a spin-off from NTU Singapore supported by Enterprise Singapore, building EV battery intelligence, fleet management, and AI-driven telematics for logistics and delivery, public transport, vehicle OEMs, rental/leasing and shared mobility operators, and mining and construction fleets. Its integrated hardware, software, and AI stack spans the OxRed (MyFleet) fleet-management and intelligence platform, OxRed Lens camera-based visualization telematics, OxRed AutoCert automated certification and compliance, GuardianAI driver-safety and collision-warning analytics, the Ask OX natural-language fleet assistant, and the ITUS Max and ITUS AutoScan edge terminals for telemetry, CAN-bus integration, and vehicle diagnostics, all aimed at optimizing battery health, safety, and operational efficiency.
d.name: Datakrew

d.description: Datalastic is a maritime data API providing real-time AIS vessel tracking, historical ship movements, vessel specifications, and global port data over a simple REST interface. A database of 750,000+ ships is queryable by MMSI, IMO, or UUID for live position, speed, course, heading, destination, and ETA, plus zone traffic monitoring around any coordinate or port, up to 31 days of historical track per request, vessel and port finder search, and asynchronous bulk reports. Access is subscription-based with a monthly credit model and api-key authentication.
d.name: Datalastic

d.description: Datalogix was a consumer-purchase and marketing data company that connected offline buying behavior to digital advertising audiences, enabling measurement and targeting for brands and ad platforms. Backed by General Catalyst and IVP, it was acquired by Oracle in 2014 and folded into the Oracle Data Cloud. The datalogix.com domain now 301-redirects to Oracle's acquisitions page, and no standalone Datalogix developer portal, API, or documentation remains publicly available.
d.name: Datalogix

d.description: Datalogue was a self-service data integration and preparation startup founded in 2015 that used machine learning to automatically classify, transform, and standardize data from disparate sources for analytics teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company was acquired by Nike in February 2019 and its standalone product was discontinued; the datalogue.io domain now serves an unrelated blog. This profile is retained for the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record. The only surviving first-party developer artifacts are the company's public GitHub organization and an unmaintained Python SDK ("datalogue") still published on PyPI.
d.name: Datalogue

d.description: Dataloop is an enterprise AI data platform for the full unstructured-data lifecycle — ingesting images, video, audio, text and LiDAR from cloud or on-premises storage, labeling and reviewing it through managed annotation tasks and recipes, orchestrating it with pipelines and serverless functions (FaaS), and turning it into governed, model-ready datasets. The platform is programmable end to end: a JWT-authenticated REST API at gate.dataloop.ai/api/v1, a first-party Python SDK and `dlp` CLI (dtlpy), a JavaScript SDK, and a Vue component library for building in-platform applications. Founded in Israel in 2017, Dataloop was acquired by Dell Technologies in December 2025 and the platform is now marketed as the Dell Data Orchestration Engine (DDOE).
d.name: DataLoop

d.description: Datalot (now operating under parent company Centerfield Insurance Services) is an analytics-driven digital customer-acquisition and live lead/call marketplace platform for the insurance industry, spanning auto, home, life, health, Medicare, and commercial lines. It runs digital demand-generation campaigns, qualifies consumers in a real-time marketplace, and routes them by data to carriers and agents, adding agent-presence and telephony management, TCPA/regulatory compliance tooling, and secondary-market handling for unmatched consumers. Named carrier clients include Liberty Mutual, Allstate, Farmers, Progressive, Travelers, Aetna, and Humana. The company is SOC 2 certified. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners; the customer-facing surface is an authenticated carrier/agent portal at app.datalot.com with no public API, SDK, or developer documentation.
d.name: Datalot

d.description: Datameer is a business analytics and data transformation platform purpose-built to run natively inside Snowflake. It lets data engineers, warehouse administrators, and business users collaboratively prep, govern, and deliver analytics-ready data through visual no-code/low-code workflows, SQL, version control, data-quality checks, pipeline automation, cost monitoring, and AI-assisted documentation. Datameer operates as a SaaS application layered over Snowflake rather than exposing a public developer REST API; this profile, originally surfaced as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead, has been enriched from the company's public web surface (documentation, trust center, legal, and blog).
d.name: Datameer

d.description: DataMind is the company behind Unistream, an enterprise-grade data platform that simplifies complex data processing while adding agentic AI capabilities. Unistream unifies fragmented data across systems with 600+ pre-built connectors, automated data-lake and data-warehouse creation with schema detection, AI-powered ETL and transformation, and an integrated BI system with interactive dashboards, a browser-based SQL editor, and AI-driven query generation. Its agentic "AI Data Minds" run complex analysis and assisted data cleansing, and a built-in MCP server exposes read-only querying, schema exploration, and Mind interactions to agents such as Claude Desktop. Built on ClickHouse with high compression, it offers RBAC, multi-level encryption, a Zero Data Retention policy, GDPR compliance, a 99.9% SLA, and on-premise deployment. DataMind is backed by 500 Global and based in Georgia.
d.name: DataMind

d.description: Dataminr delivers AI-powered real-time event, threat and risk intelligence, detecting breaking events and emerging risks across more than one million public data sources using proprietary large language models and multi-modal fusion AI. Its product lines span corporate security, cyber defense, public sector (First Alert) and newsroom situational awareness, serving government agencies and a large share of the Fortune 50. The Dataminr Pulse API exposes real-time alert consumption plus watchlist and account management over an OAuth2-secured REST gateway (gateway.dataminr.com), enabling integrations with SIEM, SOAR and security operations tooling.
d.name: Dataminr

d.description: Datamuse operates a word-finding query engine and lexical search service for developers, educators, and creative-writing applications. The Datamuse API exposes a /words endpoint that finds words matching a rich combination of semantic, phonetic, orthographic, and vocabulary constraints (means-like, sounds-like, spelled-like, synonyms, antonyms, hypernyms, meronyms, triggers, rhymes, homophones, and more) plus a /sug autocomplete endpoint. Free for non-commercial use up to 100,000 requests per day with no API key required; commercial use, custom vocabularies, and higher rate limits are available via a paid commercial agreement. Datamuse also runs OneLook, OneLook Thesaurus, RhymeZone, Rimar.io, and CivicSearch — consumer-facing word search tools built on the same lexical infrastructure.
d.name: Datamuse

d.description: DataNeuron provides a no-code platform for LLM customization, data annotation, and agentic workflows. It offers tools for data curation, fine-tuning, evaluation, model distillation, and classic NLP pipelines, enabling enterprises to build high-quality datasets and tailor large language models efficiently. The platform includes a knowledge hub, security features, and integrations for rapid deployment.
d.name: DataNeuron

d.description: Datanomik is a Brazilian open finance and treasury-management platform that gives mid-to-large enterprises real-time, consolidated visibility across their bank accounts, balances, investments and payments through a single API. Authorized by Banco Central do Brasil as a Payment Transaction Initiator (ITP) and a participant in Brazil's Open Finance ecosystem, Datanomik connects to 30+ Brazilian financial institutions (Banco do Brasil, Itau, Bradesco, Caixa, BTG, Nubank, Safra, Mercado Pago and others) to deliver bank connectivity, cash and liquidity management, investment-portfolio tracking, cash-flow forecasting, cash pooling and transfers, automated bank statements and financial reporting. The company exposes two REST APIs - an OpenBanking data API and a Treasury/Remuneration API - secured with HTTP Basic API keys, documented on a ReadMe developer portal with a public Postman workspace and a dedicated sandbox. Backed by a16z, its clients include iFood, Magalu, Flamengo and Unimed.
d.name: Datanomik

d.description: Datanyze is a sales intelligence and technographic data provider owned by ZoomInfo. It offers a free browser (Chrome) extension that surfaces business contact information — work email addresses, direct-dial and mobile phone numbers, and company firmographics — for prospects on LinkedIn profiles and company websites. Datanyze pioneered "technographics," the practice of tracking the web technologies and software a company uses to power targeted B2B sales and marketing outreach. ZoomInfo acquired Datanyze in 2018 to deliver real-time technographic data to its customers. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's discoverable web and security surface.
d.name: Datanyze *

d.description: Datapad is an autonomous AI data analyst platform that lets business teams analyze their data by asking questions in natural language. It connects to 50+ data sources — SQL databases, BigQuery, Snowflake, Google Ads, Facebook Ads, Shopify, HubSpot and more — and uses Text2SQL and Python code generation (powered by models such as Claude and ChatGPT) to turn questions into queries, dashboards, and insights, with a Slack bot for conversational analytics. Datapad is a San Francisco company backed by a16z. It is an end-user SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer REST/GraphQL API, SDKs, or webhook surface; this profile captures its identity, security, and compliance posture.
d.name: Datapad

d.description: Datapeople is an AI-powered job description management platform (acquired by PayScale) that helps talent and recruiting teams centralize, standardize, and optimize their job content across the hiring workflow. Its products include a Smart Editor for job-content management, a First Draft writing AI, Insights performance and compliance analytics, Guidance and Compliance AI for review and recommendations, and Datapeople Anywhere, which surfaces its guidance inside existing ATS and HRIS systems. Datapeople integrates with applicant tracking systems including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Lever, and Gr8People. The company publishes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI; its integration surface is delivered through native ATS/HRIS connectors rather than a self-serve API.
d.name: DataPeople

d.description: Datarails is an Excel-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform for the office of the CFO, marketed as FinanceOS. It consolidates data from ERP, CRM, HRIS, billing and operational systems into a single finance data model, then lets finance teams budget, forecast, consolidate, report and build dashboards while continuing to work in Excel through the Datarails Flex add-in. Its API surface is deliberately narrow and unusually agent-first: the primary programmatic interface is a hosted Model Context Protocol server at mcp.datarails.com, secured with OAuth 2.1 and PKCE, exposing roughly two dozen read-only tools for discovering data models, profiling fields, running filtered queries and asynchronous aggregations, and extracting validated financials into Excel. Datarails also ships a first-party Claude Code plugin carrying nineteen published Agent Skills, plus connectors for ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Lovable. The only documented conventional REST operation is the Data Gateway Service file-upload endpoint used to push CSV and Excel files into a Filebox.
d.name: Datarails

d.description: DataRobot is an enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, governing, and monitoring predictive and generative AI models and agentic workflows. It exposes a public REST API (v2), first-party Python and R clients, a `dr` command-line tool, and an MCP surface (Global MCP plus deployable standalone servers) that lets agentic coding environments call DataRobot tools and resources. Developers authenticate with personal API keys (bearer tokens) against regional endpoints (US/EU/JP), while OAuth 2.0 / OIDC via app.datarobot.com backs agent and integration auth. The platform covers AutoML, MLOps deployment and monitoring, model governance and compliance documentation, and code-first GenAI/agent development. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Techstars, and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
d.name: DataRobot

d.description: Datasaur is an enterprise AI lab that builds private, secure LLM and data solutions deployed on a customer's own infrastructure. Its Data Studio is a collaborative data-labeling platform (span, row, document, bounding-box, conversational and audio tasks) with ML-assisted labeling, while LLM Labs covers sandboxing, deployment, knowledge bases, model integrations and evaluation. Products include an enterprise chatbot, document intelligence, PII/PHI redaction and private agents, serving legal, healthcare, finance, insurance, eCommerce and government. Developers integrate through a GraphQL API (OAuth2 client credentials) at app.datasaur.ai/graphql, the Robosaur CLI, webhooks, and SAML/SCIM for workspace SSO.
d.name: Datasaur

d.description: Datasembly is a real-time retail intelligence platform that collects hyperlocal pricing, promotion, and assortment data from physical and online retail locations. The company reports gathering 12+ billion weekly prices across 150K+ stores from 230+ retailers, building a dataset of more than 2 trillion observations that consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and retailers use to optimize pricing strategy, measure trade-spend effectiveness, monitor competitors, evaluate key value items, and plan seasonal launches. Datasembly delivers this competitive intelligence as fully shareable data and analytics rather than a public developer API. The company was acquired by SPINS. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public API, developer portal, or API documentation was found on the provider's surface at the time of enrichment.
d.name: Datasembly

d.description: dataset.gov.md is the national government open-data catalog for the Republic of Moldova (Portalul Datelor Deschise). The landing portal at date.gov.md links out to this catalog, which runs CKAN 2.10.4 and exposes the standard CKAN Action API over approximately 1,275 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. No API key is required for read endpoints.
d.name: dataset.gov.md (Portalul Datelor Deschise)

d.description: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.) was a pioneering social data platform that provided real-time and historical access to social media firehoses (Twitter, Facebook Topic Data, and more) through its CSDL filtering language and its Push, Historics, and Managed Sources REST APIs. Founded in 2007 and backed by Insight Partners and others, the company was acquired by Meltwater in 2019; the datasift.com domain now redirects to meltwater.com and the standalone DataSift developer platform and APIs have been discontinued. Official first-party client SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, Java, and Node.js remain published on public package registries under the datasift GitHub organization as historical artifacts.
d.name: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.)

d.description: DataSine was a London-based AI personalization startup, founded in 2015 and backed by Techstars, that applied machine learning and behavioral psychology to help marketers tailor content, imagery, and copy to audience personality traits. The company was acquired by Shutterstock and folded into Shutterstock's AI/creative-intelligence work; its datasine.com domain is now registered to Shutterstock, Inc. (MarkMonitor) and HTTP 301-redirects to shutterstock.ai. DataSine no longer operates an independent product or a developer/API surface, so this profile is retained as an acquired-company record rather than an active provider awaiting API artifacts.
d.name: DataSine

d.description: DataSnipper is an AI-powered, agentic productivity platform built specifically for audit, tax, and finance teams. It automates repetitive testing and analysis work - extracting, matching, and analyzing data across documents and systems - while keeping human professionals in control of final decisions. Capabilities include AI Agents for end-to-end workflows (revenue testing, tests of detail, royalty calculations), Excel Agents that run analysis directly inside spreadsheets, and document intelligence that collects and cross-references evidence. The platform serves external audit, internal audit, tax, financial control, government audit, and advisory teams, with a security-first posture (no training on customer data, encryption, and 24-hour document deletion). Backed by Index Ventures and Insight Partners.
d.name: DataSnipper

d.description: DataStax is the company behind Astra DB, a serverless, multi-cloud database and vector-search platform built on Apache Cassandra, along with Langflow, RAGStack, and the Astra Streaming (Apache Pulsar) event platform for building generative-AI and real-time applications. Developers interact with Astra DB through the Data API (JSON document, table, and vector operations), the legacy REST, Document, and GraphQL APIs, and the Astra DevOps API for programmatic administration of databases, keyspaces, access lists, roles, users, tokens, private links, and CDC. DataStax publishes official client SDKs (Python astrapy, TypeScript astra-db-ts, Go astra-db-go), the Java-based Astra CLI, and an official Astra DB Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agentic access. DataStax was acquired by IBM in 2025 and its Astra products are now part of the IBM watsonx data portfolio, while the developer surface remains hosted on datastax.com, docs.datastax.com, astra.datastax.com, and github.com/datastax.
d.name: DataStax

d.description: DataSynca provides an integration, automation, and AI gateway platform that connects disparate systems, automates workflows, and incorporates AI-driven decision making. The platform offers a visual canvas, pre-built connectors for 400+ apps, data mapping, and enterprise deployment options, targeting regulated industries such as banking, insurance, healthcare, and the public sector.
d.name: DataSynca

d.description: Datavant is a United States health-data logistics company, formed from the 2021 merger of Datavant and Ciox Health, that connects and de-identifies healthcare data across a "network of networks" spanning 350+ real-world data partners, 80,000+ hospitals and clinics, and a majority of the largest US health systems. Its core capabilities are privacy-preserving record linkage using Datavant tokens, HIPAA Expert Determination and de-identification, medical record retrieval / release of information, and real-world evidence generation for life sciences, payers, providers, and government. Datavant publishes a real machine-readable contract for the retrieval side of that business: an OpenAPI 3.1.0 document for the Datavant REST API (36 paths, 54 operations, OAuth 2.0 client credentials, base https://api.datavant.io/v2) is served anonymously at https://developer.datavant.com/openapi.json, even though that host's root returns HTTP 404. Access is still enterprise and contract-gated - there is no self-serve sign-up, no published pricing beyond a single AWS Marketplace listing, no published scopes or rate limits, and no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Home market is the United States.
d.name: Datavant

d.description: DataVisor is a Mountain View, California fraud and risk platform company founded in 2013 that applies unsupervised machine learning, rules, device intelligence and link analysis to detect fraud and financial crime in real time for banks, credit unions, fintechs, digital payments, life insurance and digital enterprises. The platform covers ACH and wire fraud, account onboarding, application fraud, account takeover, card fraud, check fraud, FinCrime/AML and promotion abuse, and is delivered as an API-integrated detection engine: customers stream events to a DataVisor integration endpoint over real-time synchronous HTTPS REST (TLS 1.2) or batch/cloud-bucket pipes, and consume detection results, scores and reason codes back through APIs or bucket push. Named product modules include the Fraud and Risk Platform, the dEdge device intelligence SDK and WebAPI, dOps fraud and risk operations, dVecto managed ML detection, the UML Modeling Studio and the Vera conversational AI agent. API references and the integration guide are published publicly, but the API guide itself, the detailed endpoint documentation and the admin console are gated behind customer accounts and technical account managers.
d.name: DataVisor

d.description: Datavolo is a dataflow infrastructure company building multimodal data pipelines for generative AI and unstructured data, powered by Apache NiFi. Founded by the original creators of Apache NiFi, Datavolo delivers fast, horizontally scalable pipelines that can be instantly reconfigured, with built-in data lineage, for AI/ML and data engineering teams working with documents, images, audio, and other unstructured sources. Datavolo was acquired by Snowflake in November 2024 and its technology continues under the Snowflake data platform. The company operates a hosted cloud service (cloud.datavolo.ai / app.datavolo.ai), a documentation site, a developer DevCenter of tutorials, and open-source tooling for the Apache NiFi ecosystem published under the datavolo-io GitHub organization.
d.name: Datavolo

d.description: DataXu was a Boston-based programmatic advertising technology company, founded in 2009, that built a cloud-based demand-side platform (DSP) for automated, data-driven media buying across display, video, mobile, and connected TV. DataXu no longer operates as an independent brand: its primary domain (dataxu.com) 301-redirects into Roku's advertising site, and there is no independent DataXu developer portal, public API, SDK, or documentation surface. DatologyAI operates as an enterprise, contact-sales service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation portal.

d.description: Datorama was a cloud-based marketing intelligence and analytics platform founded in 2012 in Tel Aviv and New York. It unified marketing, advertising, and sales data from thousands of disparate sources into a single AI-powered reporting and dashboarding layer, using its "Genius" machine learning engine to automate data harmonization across ad, social, web, and CRM APIs. Salesforce acquired Datorama in August 2018 for a reported ~$800 million and rebranded it as Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence. The marketing, pricing, legal, trust and support surfaces have moved to salesforce.com, but the developer surface is still live on the original domain: a Gatsby developer portal at developers.datorama.com documents an Intelligence Platform API and a synchronous Query API on https://api.datorama.com/v1, both authenticated with a per-user personal access token in an Authorization header, both rate limited per user (60 platform req/min, 200 query req/min, 20,000 calls/day UTC) with X-PlatformRateLimit-*, X-QueryRateLimit-* and X-DailyQuota-* response headers, plus an asynchronous Reporting API for large exports, a header-switched sandbox mode, an Apps JavaScript SDK and a `dato` CLI on npm, a custom-connector framework, and — new in July 2026 — a first-party MCP server (@datorama/mci-mcp-sdk) that proxies MCP JSON-RPC to a tenant /api/mcp endpoint using an OAuth2 service-account key. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, llms.txt, /.well-known/ document or A2A agent card is published anywhere on the surface. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a lightspeed-venture-partners portfolio lead.
d.name: Datorama

d.description: Datos IO was a Silicon Valley data-management startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that built RecoverX — an "application-centric" backup, recovery and data-mobility platform for cloud-native and distributed databases. RecoverX targeted NoSQL and cloud data stores including Apache Cassandra, DataStax, MongoDB, Couchbase and Amazon DynamoDB, alongside relational sources such as Microsoft SQL Server, and used parallel data streaming, semantic deduplication and a distributed metadata catalog to back up in native formats and recover across private, hybrid and public cloud. Datos IO was acquired by Rubrik in 2018 and operated for a period as "Rubrik Datos IO" before the brand was retired. The company has no independent presence today: the datos.io domain has lapsed and is listed for sale through a domain broker, and no live developer portal, documentation or API surface remains. d.description: Datost Inc. is a New York applied research lab building hardware and intelligent systems that operate in your environment without demanding constant attention — "computers that come after the screen." Its first public product is ED1TH, a 25-gram pair of AI augmented-reality smart glasses with a 640x480 green Micro-LED in-lens display readable in direct sunlight, hot-swap battery cells, a companion steel smart ring for gesture control, and a privacy-first design with zero cameras and a single hardware-mutable microphone. ED1TH runs ED1TH-OS and handles email, calendar, turn-by-turn navigation, live translation, and meeting transcription in the wearer's field of view. Datost is backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and OpenAI. As a consumer hardware and applied-research company, Datost does not currently publish a public web API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.
d.name: Datost

d.description: Datrium was a Sunnyvale, California enterprise infrastructure company founded in 2012 by Brian Biles and Hugo Patterson (both formerly of Data Domain / EMC). Its flagship DVX ("Distributed Virtual X") platform introduced an "open convergence" architecture that separated compute from durable storage for virtualized data centers, and the company later pivoted toward cloud disaster-recovery-as-a-service (Datrium DRaaS with DRaaS Connect and ControlShield). Datrium was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, NEA, and others, and was acquired by VMware in July 2020, with its technology folded into VMware Cloud Disaster Recovery. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no active developer portal or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record surfaced from Lightspeed Venture Partners' portfolio.
d.name: Datrium

d.description: Dattch (now HER, weareher.com) is a dating and social community app for LGBTQ+ women, nonbinary, and queer people, founded by Robyn Exton. The platform pairs one-to-one matching with community spaces, events, and social feeds, and reports more than 15 million users across 114+ countries. It operates as a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android with no publicly documented developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Dattch

d.description: Datto is a data-protection and IT-management vendor for managed service providers (MSPs) and internal IT teams, now part of Kaseya. Its platform spans business continuity and disaster recovery (SIRIS, ALTO, Endpoint Backup), SaaS Protection for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, Remote Monitoring and Management (Datto RMM), Autotask professional services automation (PSA), networking (Wi-Fi, switches, firewalls, Secure Edge), and cybersecurity (Managed SOC, EDR, antivirus). Datto RMM publishes a versioned REST API (v2, OpenAPI 3.1) with platform-specific regional hosts on the CentraStage infrastructure, OAuth 2.0 access tokens, request-rate limiting, and paginated responses, letting partners programmatically manage sites, devices, alerts, jobs, audits, and account variables. Datto runs a formal Developer Program offering sandbox environments, technical enablement, and an integrations marketplace for vendors building on its solutions.
d.name: Datto

d.description: Datum is an open source network cloud built for AI, founded in 2024 and backed by $13.6M from Amplify Partners, CRV, Encoded Ventures, Cervin Ventures, Ex/Ante, Step Function, and Vine Ventures, and founded by Zac Smith and Jacob Smith (ex-Equinix, Packet). Datum gives AI-native developers and alternative cloud providers critical, neutral network infrastructure to compete at scale: an Envoy-based AI Edge with a Coraza OWASP WAF, Layer 7 HTTPProxy/HTTPRoute traffic management, authoritative DNS and programmatic domain management, QUIC-based secure tunnels (Connectors) powered by Iroh, and a Galactic VPC global backbone, all deployed across 17+ global network locations. The platform is exposed through a Kubernetes-style declarative control-plane API at api.datum.net, the datumctl CLI, an official MCP server, and packaged agent Skills, with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authentication and a forever-free Builder tier. Core platform is licensed AGPLv3.
d.name: Datum

d.description: Datumate is a construction technology company whose cloud-native SaaS platform, DatuBIM, turns drone imagery, laser-scanning, and site data into real-time progress tracking, deviation detection, automated reporting, and actionable analytics for heavy civil infrastructure projects. It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.
d.name: Datumate

d.description: Datumo provides an advanced LLM evaluation platform that offers automated generation of golden question sets, custom metric support, and comprehensive red‑team testing for AI models. Their services include Datumo Eval for model benchmarking, AI Red Team for adversarial analysis, and a dataset store with premium and open datasets for training and evaluation. The platform aims to help developers and researchers improve LLM performance, safety, and reliability through detailed analytics and actionable insights.
d.name: Datumo

d.description: Daupler provides a cloud-based Response Management System (RMS) for utilities, public works, and service organizations that automates and coordinates emergency and service-request response. Its product suite spans Daupler Answering (after-hours call center), Dispatch Assist and AI-driven call management, Callout crew notification, Notify mass notification via SMS/email/phone, Engage customer portal, Event Detection for multi-incident coordination, and Analytics for incident and team-performance insight. Daupler serves water, sewer, electric, multi-utility, trash-collection, and public-works operators. The RMS is built on RESTful services and integrates with CMMS, work-order, AMI, IoT sensor, billing, CIS, CRM, OMS, GIS, and citizen-request systems, though Daupler exposes no public self-serve developer API or documentation. Backed by Techstars.
d.name: Daupler

d.description: Dave is a U.S. consumer financial-technology company (Nasdaq: DAVE), founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that operates a mobile banking app serving roughly 14 million members. Its products include ExtraCash short-term cash advances of up to $500 (underwritten with its CashAI cash-flow model rather than credit scores), an FDIC-insured Dave Checking account with early direct deposit and Round-Up savings, and a Goals savings account. Banking services are provided through partner banks such as Coastal Community Bank. Dave is a consumer app and does not publish a first-party public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal: there is no developer.dave.com / docs.dave.com, and api.dave.com is the app's private, undocumented mobile backend. Programmatic access to Dave-held consumer data is aggregator-mediated — Dave both consumes Plaid (to let members link external accounts) and is reachable as a supported institution through open-finance aggregators. This profile captures its public identity, aggregator-only open-finance posture, commercial link surface, and domain-security posture.
d.name: Dave

d.description: David AI is an audio data research company building high-quality speech and conversational datasets to bring AI into the real world through voice. Using a rigorous six-step research process (hypothesize, design, experiment, evaluate, productionize, release), the team produces datasets such as Converse (channel-separated two-speaker English conversations), Atlas (multilingual data spanning 15+ languages with dialect and accent metadata), Chorus (multi-speaker conversations for speaker separation and diarization), and Dialog (expert domain conversations). Its data is licensed to Fortune 100 companies and research labs working on speech recognition, translation, synthesis, and conversational AI. Access is arranged through samples, consultation, and a data license agreement rather than a self-serve API. David AI is backed by Amplify Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.
d.name: David AI

d.description: David Energy is a clean-energy technology company and licensed electricity retailer that installs free plug-in smart batteries for homes and businesses. Its software charges batteries when grid power is cheap and discharges them during peak-price periods to lower customers' monthly utility bills, alongside bill-monitoring and thermostat-management advisory tools. Backed by Union Square Ventures, David Energy operates in the New York City market with a stated mission of powering the grid on 100% clean energy and shifting the balance of energy control from institutions toward consumers.
d.name: David Energy

d.description: David is a New York nutrition company founded in 2023 by RXBAR co-founder Peter Rahal, selling high-protein bars (28g protein, 150 calories, 0g sugar), the Bronze and Gold bar lines, and protein ice cream pints direct-to-consumer, through wholesale, and in retail. David runs no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, but its Shopify-hosted storefront at davidprotein.com serves a complete agent-commerce surface from its own hostnames: an agents.md / llms.txt instruction document, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect discovery documents, and three live Model Context Protocol servers covering catalog search, product lookup, cart, checkout, shop policy Q&A, order status and returns.
d.name: David Protein

d.description: DaVita Inc. is a Fortune 500 kidney care company operating in-center hemodialysis, home hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis programs in the United States and abroad, alongside transplant support, integrated kidney care, hospital partnerships, and clinical research. DaVita runs no developer program and publishes no API documentation, but its own web platform serves a live, public, unauthenticated REST API at https://www.davita.com/wp-json/ with a first-party davita/v1 namespace: a dialysis center locator, a Kidney Smart class finder, a USDA-sourced food and nutrient lookup shaped for the kidney diet, and 1,258 kidney-friendly recipes, 570 education articles and a kidney vocabulary alongside them. Clinical integration remains sales-led through payer, hospital and physician partnerships and EHR data exchange; there is no public FHIR endpoint.
d.name: DaVita

d.description: Dawaai is Pakistan's leading digital healthcare platform, operating a licensed online pharmacy alongside telehealth and diagnostic services. Founded on a licensed retail pharmacy (License #1265, 2014) and headquartered in Karachi, Dawaai lets patients order authentic prescription and OTC medicines for temperature-controlled doorstep delivery, book doctor and mental-health consultations, order home-based lab tests and checkups, arrange home nursing and medical services, and subscribe to chronic-care programs for diabetes and obesity. It is a LegitScript-certified healthcare merchant that sources directly from manufacturers and distributors, with qualified pharmacists handling procurement, storage, and dispensing. Dawaai is backed by 500 Global and operates across Pakistan, including Karachi and Rawalpindi. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network via the venture portfolio pipeline; Dawaai publishes no public developer/API program at this time.
d.name: Dawaai

d.description: DaWanda.com was a German online marketplace for handmade, unique, and custom-made products, founded in 2006 in Berlin. It connected independent makers and small designers with buyers across Germany and Europe, comparable to Etsy in the DACH region. DaWanda ceased operations on 30 August 2018 and partnered with Etsy to migrate its sellers and buyers; the www.dawanda.com domain now redirects to Etsy Germany. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. No public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment; the company is defunct and retained here as a historical/portfolio record.
d.name: DaWanda.com

d.description: Dawn (Sleepedy, Inc. dba Dawn) is a digital-health company offering a clinician-guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) program delivered through a mobile app. The service pairs users with licensed sleep coaches and therapists for weekly video sessions and between-session chat, daily 5-7 minute sleep lessons, live sleep-performance insights, and weekly progress reports, with the goal of treating primary and chronic insomnia and reducing reliance on sleep medication. Dawn is in-network with major U.S. insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, United Healthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and offers an employer/enterprise workplace-wellness program. Backed by Kindred Ventures. Dawn publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.
d.name: Dawn

d.description: Dawsat is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
d.name: Dawsat

d.description: Day & Zimmermann is a privately held, family-owned diversified industrial services company founded in 1901 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company operates across four primary business segments — Maintenance & Construction (power, nuclear, fossil, renewable, and chemical plants), Munitions (ammunition manufacturing, storage, and demilitarization for the U.S. military, including operation of the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant), Government Services (security, EOD, facility management, and architecture/engineering for federal agencies), and Workforce Solutions (staffing and talent placement via Yoh). The Yoh family has controlled the company since 1961; Harold L. Yoh III serves as Chairman and CEO. Day & Zimmermann reported approximately $2.7 billion in revenue in 2023 with roughly 43,000–52,000 employees across approximately 150 global locations. Day & Zimmermann does not publish any public developer APIs; its business is delivered through long-cycle service contracts, government-owned contractor-operated (GOCO) facilities, and direct client engagements.
d.name: Day & Zimmermann

d.description: Day One Biopharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing targeted therapies for people of all ages living with life-threatening diseases, with an initial focus on pediatric and rare cancers. Its lead product OJEMDA (tovorafenib) is an FDA-approved treatment for relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma, and its pipeline includes DAY301 and the antibody-drug conjugate Emi-Le. Headquartered in Brisbane, California, the company was acquired by and is now part of the Servier Group as of March 2026. Day One was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it maintains a corporate and investor-relations web presence but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.
d.name: Day One Biopharmaceuticals

d.description: PT Daya Medika Pratama (DMP) is an Indonesian healthcare IT company in Central Jakarta that builds and implements hospital information systems and insurance core systems. It has worked in IT since 2007 — first as a systems integrator building data-acquisition systems for textile production machinery, later as a Microsoft Business Solution Partner in healthcare and education — and today sells AFYA Better HIS (a hospital information system with an openEHR-based clinical data repository, stated as connected to BPJS Kesehatan, Kemenkes/SATUSEHAT, FHIR and Better, and in use at more than 40 Indonesian hospitals), AFYA Insurance (policy and claims management), implementation of the Better digital health platform, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 as hospital back office. It is an openEHR industry partner and a Better (better.care) partner for the Indonesian market, and runs AFYA Better Academy, an openEHR and FHIR training programme for hospital IT staff. Its positioning line is "One Patient One Record for Better Health". DMP publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract; the standards it names are national platforms its products consume on a hospital's behalf, not APIs it ships.
d.name: Daya Medika Pratama

d.description: Daybreak Health is a B2B mental health company that delivers teletherapy and mental health programs for K-12 students (ages 5-19) in partnership with school districts and health plans. Its services include one-on-one teletherapy, in-person and hybrid onsite programs, universal mental health screeners, and mental health classes, with programs tailored for BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and low-income student populations. Daybreak is a care-delivery organization sold to schools and payers rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture.
d.name: Daybreak

d.description: DayDayCook is a home-cooking content-to-commerce platform founded in Hong Kong that publishes recipes, cooking videos, and food storytelling (its "Taste & Tales" blog) alongside a direct-to-consumer shop selling its own branded sauces, ingredients, and prepared foods under the tagline "Easy Cooking, Festive Flavours." The business pairs a culinary media audience with a consumer-packaged-goods and e-commerce operation. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass DayDayCook publishes a consumer web presence and online shop but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.
d.name: DayDayCook

d.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.
d.name: DayDream Dental

d.description: Dayforce provides a comprehensive, AI‑powered Human Capital Management (HCM) platform that unifies HR, payroll, talent, workforce management, and analytics. The cloud‑based solution helps enterprises automate HR processes, gain real‑time insights, ensure compliance, and improve employee experiences across global workforces.
d.name: Dayforce

d.description: Dayforward is a New York-based life insurance technology and services group founded in 2019 by Aaron Shapiro. It owns Commercial Travelers Life Insurance Company (NY-domiciled carrier) and Dayforward Insurance Agency LLC (licensed in all 50 states), and sells income-replacement term life insurance direct to consumers at dayforward.com. Since pivoting to B2B at dayforward.io it licenses Workbench — a SaaS platform covering the full life insurance lifecycle from agent selling and automated underwriting through policy administration and service — plus managed distribution, underwriting and administration services to other carriers and distributors. Workbench is marketed as including "APIs, plug-and-play widgets, single sign-on support, and robust administration tools", but Dayforward publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or SDKs.
d.name: Dayforward

d.description: Dayjob is an AI-powered scheduling agent built for waste management and skip hire fleets, operated by Gaea Technology Ltd and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Its autonomous agents analyze millions of potential route combinations to build optimized daily schedules that factor in travel times, skip sizes, driver availability and priority job assignments, then continuously re-optimize in real time as new jobs, driver changes and exceptions arrive. Dayjob integrates with existing ERP and telematics systems (Weighsoft, PurGo, Wastelogics, plus custom report setups) and claims customers see revenue and efficiency gains, tighter time-window hit rates and materially less planning admin. It is a vertical logistics application rather than an API platform - no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs are published at this time. This profile has been enriched from the company's public website.
d.name: Dayjob

d.description: Daylight (Daylight Security) is an AI-native Managed Detection and Response (MDR) provider delivering what it calls Managed Agentic Security Services (MASS) — combining agentic AI with elite human analysts to run security operations end-to-end, from real-time threat detection through Tier 1 triage, deep Tier 3 investigations, and full incident response, 24x7x365. The platform ingests signals across endpoints, cloud, and networks, learns each customer's business context (identity platforms, HR systems, even Slack), and connects into the customer stack (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, Slack, Microsoft Teams). Daylight exposes a partner API at api.daylight.ai (OAuth2 / OIDC, Bearer) plus an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so security teams can connect investigations to AI assistants such as Claude and Cursor. Daylight is SOC 2 Type II certified and ISO 27001 compliant. Founded in 2024 by Hagai Shapira and Eldad Rudich; backed by Craft Ventures, Bain Capital Ventures, and Maple VC ($40M raised). Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery.
d.name: Daylight

d.description: DayOne is a hyperscale data center company delivering next-generation digital infrastructure for cloud, AI, and edge computing workloads. Spun out of the GDS International business and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, DayOne develops and operates strategically located, interconnected data center campuses across Asia-Pacific — Singapore, Johor (Malaysia), Batam (Indonesia), Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Bangkok — and is expanding into Europe with a launch market in Finland. The company positions itself as a build-to-suit and hyperscale partner focused on power availability, connectivity, and sustainable operations rather than as a public API or developer-platform provider; there is no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface at this time.
d.name: DayOne

d.description: Daytona is open-source, secure, and elastic infrastructure for running AI-generated code. Daytona sandboxes spin up in under 90 milliseconds and provide isolated Linux, Windows, and macOS environments where autonomous agents and developer workflows can execute untrusted code, perform file system and Git operations, run language servers, drive virtual desktops, and persist state via snapshots and volumes. The platform exposes a control-plane REST API (sandboxes, snapshots, volumes, organizations, runners, webhooks) and an in-sandbox Toolbox API (file system, Git, LSP, process execution, PTY, computer use, interpreter), with official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go, and Java, plus a Go CLI and Homebrew/Windows installers.
d.name: Daytona

d.description: Dayuse is a global online marketplace for daytime hotel bookings, letting travelers reserve 3-to-5-star hotel rooms by the hour or for a microstay during the day rather than for an overnight stay, at discounts of up to 75% off the nightly rate. Founded in France in 2010, the platform connects consumers with more than 9,000 partner hotels across roughly 29 countries, with use cases spanning remote work, layovers, wellness and spa access, and privacy. Hoteliers join through the Dayuse partner network and manage daytime inventory via the partner portal. Dayuse is backed by Partech and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile captures identity, partner surface, and domain-security posture only.
d.name: Dayuse

d.description: Daz 3D is a Salt Lake City based 3D content and software company best known for Daz Studio, a free figure posing, morphing and rendering application, and for the Genesis line of morphable 3D human figures. The company runs a large first-party and marketplace store of 3D characters, clothing, props and environments, publishes the DSON (Daz Scene Object Notation) JSON-based scene file format, and licenses synthetic 3D character datasets for AI training through the surface that was formerly the Tafi brand. Its developer surface is an application SDK rather than a web API: a free C++ plug-in SDK, the DAZ Script ECMAScript scripting API documented in the public Daz Documentation Center, and open-source Daz-to-Blender / Unity / Unreal / Maya / Cinema 4D / 3ds Max bridge plug-ins published on GitHub. No public REST, GraphQL or event API is published.
d.name: DAZ 3D

d.description: Daze is a mobile "freeform chat" application for iOS and Android, published by Marble Media (Android package com.marblemedia.dazechat, iOS App Store id 6497405419). It is a consumer social messaging product with an active Discord community and is venture-backed by a16z, Kindred Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, Daze exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface (all /.well-known/ and /llms.txt probes returned 404); it is a consumer app rather than an API provider. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company record.
d.name: Daze

d.description: DAZN is a global over-the-top live sports streaming service headquartered in London and owned by Access Industries. Launched in 2015 out of the former Perform Group, it streams boxing, football, MotoGP, UFC and other rights to subscribers across more than 200 countries and territories, and has expanded through the acquisitions of Eleven Group, Foxtel/Kayo Sports and ViewLift, alongside the DAZN Bet and DAZN Media brands. DAZN operates a large Node.js microservice estate on AWS and publishes open source engineering tooling (the Kopytko Roku ecosystem, dazn-lambda-powertools) from its GitHub organization, but it runs no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable specification for the consumer platform APIs that power its apps.
d.name: DAZN

d.description: Dazz is a cloud security company specializing in Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) and code-to-cloud risk remediation. Its platform correlates findings across code, cloud, and on-prem infrastructure into a single unified view, maps vulnerabilities back to their root cause in source code, and gives security and engineering teams a remediation engine to prioritize and fix issues across the application lifecycle. Co-founded and led by CEO Merav Bahat, Dazz was backed by Insight Partners, Greylock, Cyberstarts, and others. Wiz announced its acquisition of Dazz on November 21, 2024 to extend its Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) with Dazz's remediation capabilities; the dazz.io domain now redirects into Wiz. This profile has no independent public developer/API surface.
d.name: Dazz

d.description: Dazzle AI is an early-stage, pre-launch artificial intelligence company backed by Forerunner Ventures, with the stated mission of closing the gap between what people want and what they can do with AI. As of mid-2026 the product is invite-only: the public site collects waitlist sign-ups and publishes About, Jobs, Press, Support, Terms of Service, and Privacy Policy pages, but exposes no developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a lead awaiting a public API surface.
d.name: Dazzle AI

d.description: DB Schenker (Schenker AG, headquartered in Essen, Germany) is one of the world's largest freight forwarders and contract logistics providers, moving air, ocean, land and rail freight and running warehousing for shippers across roughly 1,850 locations. As a forwarder it sits in the intermediation layer of the supply chain — between the shipper who owns the cargo and the carriers, terminals and customs authorities who move and clear it — buying capacity it does not own and reselling visibility it did not have to publish. Its API posture is honestly a customer-contract posture, not a public developer posture. Deutsche Bahn sold DB Schenker to DSV A/S, completing 30 April 2025, and as of this profile www.dbschenker.com 301-redirects to dsv.com while the global developer portal at api-portal.dbschenker.com answers HTTP 410 Gone. The one DB Schenker-branded machine-readable API surface still live is the Nordic parcel "Partner services API" at parcelservices-se.dbschenker.com/Apipartner, which publishes four Swagger 2.0 documents openly but returns 401 on every operation without HTTP Basic credentials issued against a signed Swedish transport agreement. Its EDI endpoints are proprietary JSON, not EDIFACT or X12, and no DCSA, IATA ONE Record, GS1 EPCIS or WCO Data Model conformant contract was found on any reachable host.
d.name: DB Schenker

d.description: DBnomics is the world's economic database - a free, open-source aggregator run by Cepremap that harvests macroeconomic time series from more than 90 national and international providers (IMF, ECB, Eurostat, World Bank, OECD, BLS, BEA, Banque de France, Federal Statistical Office Germany, and many more) into one standardized format. Hundreds of millions of series covering economic indicators, government statistics, prices, employment, trade, and finance are refreshed daily and served through a documented public REST API (api.db.nomics.world/v22) that requires no API key, plus official Python and R clients and community clients for Julia, Matlab, Stata, EViews, and Gretl.
d.name: DBnomics

d.description: DBOS is a durable execution platform built on Postgres for running resilient workflows, scheduled jobs, durable queues, and Kafka consumers. The core library (DBOS Transact) is available for Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java, with a managed serverless runtime offered as DBOS Cloud.
d.name: DBOS

d.description: DBpedia is a community project that extracts structured data from Wikipedia and publishes it as Linked Open Data on the Web. It provides a SPARQL endpoint, a Lookup Service for entity resolution, a Spotlight API for text annotation, a Live endpoint for real-time Wikipedia data, and Linked Data access via HTTP content negotiation — forming a queryable cross-linked knowledge graph of Wikipedia-derived facts.
d.name: DBpedia

d.description: dbt Labs operates dbt Cloud, the managed platform for the open-source dbt (data build tool) used to transform data inside cloud warehouses. dbt Cloud exposes a set of APIs for managing accounts, projects, jobs, and runs programmatically (Administrative API), inspecting project metadata (Discovery API), and querying governed metrics (Semantic Layer API).
d.name: dbt

d.description: DBT Capital provides corporate loans to growing businesses in Sweden, offering financing from 5 to 150 million SEK for acquisitions, growth, refinancing, or working capital. The company emphasizes flexible loan terms and partners with the European Investment Fund (EIF) to guarantee financing, aiming to support companies throughout their development stages.
d.name: DBT Capital
