Its DIAGONAL product engine pairs computational epitope filtering with experimental screening — generating roughly 200,000 candidate antibody sequences per target, clustering them by predicted shape, binning by receptor complementarity and assembling multispecific antibodies from those bins — to make agonist antibody discovery tractable. The lead program, DIAG723, is a first-in-class ALK1:BMPRII clustering agonist antibody that restores ALK1 signaling; it holds US FDA and EMA orphan drug designation for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and entered the Phase 1/2 DIAMOND trial (NCT07623525), with a first patient dosed in July 2026, alongside preclinical work in pulmonary arterial hypertension. The pipeline extends into hematology, hepatology, nephrology and cardiovascular disease. The company has raised roughly USD 255 million across a USD 128 million Series A (April 2024, co-led by BVF Partners and Atlas Venture) and an oversubscribed USD 125 million Series B (January 2026, co-led by Sanofi Ventures and Janus Henderson Investors). Diagonal is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a Next.js marketing site backed by a Sanity CMS, and publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.
d.name: Diagonal Therapeutics

d.description: Diagrid is the execution layer for production AI, built by the creators of the open source Dapr and KEDA projects. Its managed platform, Diagrid Catalyst, gives AI agents, workflows, and MCP servers durable execution (applications resume from the last completed step after crashes or outages) and verifiable execution (every step is cryptographically signed into a tamper-evident audit log). Catalyst exposes the Dapr APIs — service invocation, publish/subscribe, state management, workflows, and conversation/LLM calls — as a serverless, fully managed service with SPIFFE-based workload identity, mutual TLS, and declarative access policies. Diagrid Conductor is a companion product for operating and managing Dapr and KEDA across Kubernetes clusters. The platform is delivered as a free Catalyst Cloud tier and a self-hosted Catalyst Enterprise offering, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and is driven through a rich diagrid CLI, per-language SDKs, and a Terraform provider.
d.name: Diagrid

d.description: Dialect is a Web3 UX infrastructure company on Solana that provides onchain transactions and notifications native to any digital experience. Its two flagship products are Blinks (Blockchain Links — one-click, embeddable onchain transactions powered by a Standard Blinks Library of 40+ protocol integrations including Jupiter, Kamino, Drift and DeFiTuna) and the Alerts Stack (real-time, multi-channel notifications across push, email, Telegram and an in-app universal inbox, with event detection for price-change and trending-token signals). Dialect also exposes a Markets & Positions API for real-time DeFi rates, TVL and wallet position tracking, plus a hosted MCP server for agents. The developer surface spans three REST APIs (Alerts V2, Blinks, Markets), TypeScript/React SDKs, a no-code dashboard, and an open-source monitor framework. Backed by Electric Capital and Multicoin Capital.
d.name: Dialect

d.description: DialNexa is a Voice AI agents platform for sales calls, lead qualification, follow-ups, meeting booking, collections and support workflows, with a strong focus on Indian-market multilingual calling (English, Hindi, Hinglish, Marathi, Kannada, Gujarati, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and mixed-language calls). The public contract is an OpenAPI 3.0 document of 43 paths and 56 operations served from api.dialnexa.com with bearer authentication. DialNexa publishes an RFC 9727 api-catalog as a proper application/linkset+json document, two llms.txt files (a site index and a 90KB documentation index), an auth.md written explicitly for AI agents and automation systems describing how API keys are provisioned, an official remote MCP server at api.dialnexa.com/v1/mcp (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, 97 documented tools), and a provider-published Agent Skill served from /.well-known/agent-skills/.
d.name: DialNexa

d.description: Dialogue is a leading Canadian virtual healthcare and employee wellness provider operating an Integrated Health Platform that delivers primary care, mental health support, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), and wellness programming to members through a single mobile and web application available 24/7/365. The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.
d.name: Dialogue

d.description: Dialogue AI is an AI-native customer and market research platform, founded in 2025 and backed by a Lightspeed Venture Partners seed round, that helps product, design, and research teams uncover customer needs, test ideas, and capture authentic feedback through adaptive AI-moderated interviews. The platform automates the research workflow end to end — study design, participant recruitment (including a Prolific partnership), AI-led interviewing across multiple research formats, and real-time reporting and insight synthesis — so organizations can make agile, data-driven decisions aligned with real-world market changes. Dialogue AI is a web application (app.dialogueai.com) rather than a public developer API provider; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Dialogue AI

d.description: Dialogus is a frontier AI voice lab building infrastructure for enterprise-grade voice agents that resolve, trace, and control every live conversation across phone systems, internal workflows, and customer systems. Its platform connects voice agents to phone systems, internal tools, databases, CRMs, and messaging channels, with human escalation flows, monitoring, and compliance built in. Agents run a Listen, Reason, Act, and Report loop that detects turns, silence, and intent, constrains the model with workflow state and policies, executes approved tools, and produces auditable transcripts and outcomes. Dialogus targets live customer support, phone order-taking into the POS, and past-due collections, and positions itself as SOC 2 compliant for live operations. Founded by ex-Google, Meta, and Microsoft engineers, it is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company based in San Francisco.
d.name: Dialogus

d.description: Dialpad is an AI-powered cloud communications platform offering business phone, contact center, video, and messaging. Notable for Dialpad Ai (real-time transcription, sentiment, coaching).
d.name: Dialpad

d.description: Dialup is a voice-chat app that revives the magic of talking on the phone by pairing people for one-on-one calls based on shared interests. It automates recurring, scheduled calls so users connect serendipitously with friends, communities, or complete strangers around the world without any manual coordination. Callers opt in with custom caller IDs rather than random numbers, and the free service is available on iOS and Android. Dialup is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it operates as a consumer social/communication application and does not currently publish a public developer API.
d.name: Dialup

d.description: Diamanti was a San Jose, California infrastructure company (founded 2014) that built hyperconverged, bare-metal infrastructure purpose-built for containers and Kubernetes. Its flagship Ultima platform paired plug-and-play appliances with hardware-accelerated networking and storage I/O cards, and its Spektra software added multi-cluster, hybrid-cloud Kubernetes management across on-premises and public-cloud environments. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct / to have ceased operations: www.diamanti.com resolves but returns a captcha-walled placeholder (HTTP 202, noindex) with no reachable developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface.
d.name: Diamanti

d.description: Diametric Capital is an equity long/short, multi-manager investment fund firm headquartered in Boston and New York. The firm builds customizable funds that isolate what it calls "True Alpha" — returns uncorrelated to the broader market — by removing beta and factor risk exposure to deliver performance with below-average volatility. Alongside its funds it offers aligned fee structures, capital partnerships, and business development support to entrepreneurs and emerging managers. Diametric Capital is a private financial firm and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface; it operates a secure client data room for investors and partners.
d.name: Diametric Capital

d.description: Diamond (diamond.io) is an early-stage, managed serverless data backend for teams, positioned as "your project, but with AI." The product promises a world-class serverless database where teams bring their own data sources, AI-assisted setup so no schema configuration is required, team collaboration with role management, and single sign-on via Google, Microsoft, and LDAP. As of this profile the public surface is a pre-launch landing page with a "create your workspace" signup form and a sign-in page; no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, pricing, changelog, or status page are published yet. Diamond Inc. is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched from the provider's public web surface.
d.name: Diamond

d.description: Diamond Foundry is a deep-tech materials company that manufactures semiconductor-grade single-crystal diamond wafers and diamond transistors to overcome the thermal limits of silicon in AI chips, datacenters, and electric vehicles. The company operates its own foundries and has built a full technology stack for producing diamond at scale as a sustainable substrate for high-performance and power electronics. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a planetary-health portfolio company of Obvious Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.
d.name: Diamond Foundry

d.description: Diamond Lane was a hardtech networking-equipment company that built DSL broadband networking equipment, backed by Kleiner Perkins and listed on the firm's partnerships page with a status of acquired. The company predates the modern web API era and no longer operates an independent commercial surface: enrichment probes in July 2026 found no reachable corporate website (diamondlane.com resolves only to a domain-for-sale parking page and diamond-lane.com to a registrar default page), no GitHub organization, no published client libraries on npm or PyPI, and no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record rather than as an active API provider.
d.name: Diamond Lane

d.description: IDEX Online is the leading polished diamonds trading platform for professionals, providing unbiased, market-driven diamond pricing tools, news and research. The IDEX Onsite and Data Report APIs deliver natural diamond, lab grown diamond, and market data feeds to subscribers of the IDEX trading platform.
d.name: Diamond Search

d.description: Diamondback Energy is an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the acquisition, development, exploration, and exploitation of unconventional, onshore oil and natural gas reserves in the Permian Basin of West Texas. As a Fortune 500 company in the upstream energy sector, Diamondback publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; its entire web presence is a Q4/gcs-web investor-relations site, and owner joint-interest billing and revenue check detail are delivered through the third-party EnergyLink portal rather than a first-party interface. The only machine-readable surfaces it serves are three RSS feeds on the IR platform — news releases, events and SEC filings. This repository is maintained as a placeholder for any APIs, developer tools, or machine-readable artifacts that may emerge.
d.name: Diamondback Energy

d.description: Diana Health (heydianahealth.com) is a women's healthcare provider offering personalized in-person and virtual care across the reproductive and primary health lifespan: maternity and prenatal care, labor and delivery, postpartum, gynecology, well-woman visits, menopause management, family planning and contraception, mental health, and wellness coaching, plus treatment for conditions such as endometriosis, PCOS, UTIs, and STIs. The company operates collaborative care-team clinics across Tennessee, Florida, and Texas, accepts most major insurance plans including Medicaid, and emphasizes longer appointments and whole-person (mental, physical, social) care. Diana Health is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes a consumer marketing and appointment-booking website but no public developer API; this profile is enriched with identity and domain-security signals only.
d.name: Diana Health

d.description: Dianxiaomi (店小秘) is a free cross-border e-commerce ERP platform operated by Shenzhen Meiyunji Network Technology Co., Ltd., serving more than 1.8 million cross-border sellers worldwide. It unifies product listing and data collection, multi-platform order processing, warehouse and inventory management, procurement, financial and profit analytics, and customer service across 70+ marketplaces including AliExpress, Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop, with integrations to 1,700+ logistics providers and 130+ overseas warehouses. The platform is user-facing SaaS; no public developer/API open platform is currently published.
d.name: Dianxiaomi

d.description: Diapers.com is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ecommerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
d.name: Diapers.com

d.description: diaspora* is a privacy-aware, decentralized, open source social network, launched in 2010 and released under the AGPL. Rather than running on servers owned by a single company, diaspora* runs as a federated network of independently operated servers called "pods" — anyone can join an existing pod or host their own, and users own their own data. Its "aspects" model lets people organize contacts into groups and control exactly which audience sees each post, alongside hashtags, mentions, reshares, likes, polls, photos and private conversations. Pods federate with each other using the diaspora* federation protocol. Since release 0.9.0.0 the project officially supports third-party applications through a documented JSON REST API at /api/v1 on every pod, authenticated with OpenID Connect Core 1.0 including Dynamic Client Registration — a necessity in a decentralized network where an application cannot pre-register with every pod it might talk to.
d.name: Diaspora

d.description: DICE is a live music and events ticketing platform (dice.fm) connecting fans to gigs, club nights, festivals, and experiences, with a fan-facing mobile app and a partner platform (MIO) for promoters, venues, and festivals. For partners, DICE exposes a documented but access-gated GraphQL API - the Ticket Holders API at partners-endpoint.dice.fm/graphql - that lets downstream systems query events, tickets and ticket holders, orders and sales, returns and transfers, fans, and venues. API tokens are generated inside MIO and passed as a Bearer authorization header; the API is available to DICE partners rather than as an open self-service developer program.
d.name: DICE

d.description: Generate random pixel-art avatars
d.name: Dicebear Avatars

d.description: DICK'S Sporting Goods is a Fortune 500 omni-channel sporting goods retailer selling sports equipment, apparel, footwear and accessories across the DICK'S, House of Sport, Golf Galaxy, Public Lands and Going Going Gone banners. It publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract: the storefront is an Angular single-page app that answers HTTP 200 with the same shell for every path, and neither api. nor developer.dickssportinggoods.com resolves in DNS. Its B2B integration surface is X12 EDI over AS2/SFTP through third-party trading networks, with vendor guidelines handed out as PDFs. The company does run a named Vulnerability Disclosure Program on Bugcrowd.
d.name: Dick's Sporting Goods

d.description: API to get access to the collection of the most inspiring expressions of mankind
d.name: Dictum

d.description: DidaTravel (道旅科技, Shenzhen Dida Travel Technology Co., Ltd.) is a technology-driven global travel distribution company. It operates an open platform that connects travel buyers and suppliers, providing flexible connectivity solutions across hotels, flights, airport transfers, and attraction tickets. Headquartered in Shenzhen, China, DidaTravel serves online travel agencies, tour operators, and other travel businesses worldwide with aggregated hotel content, dynamic rates, and booking delivered through its B2B distribution technology. The company positions itself as a global technology leader in travel product connectivity and is backed by investors including IDG Capital.
d.name: Dida

d.description: DiDi Global is a mobility technology platform best known for ride-hailing, taxi-hailing, and enterprise employee travel across China and international markets. DiDi exposes a public developer surface through DiDi Enterprise Services (DDES) — an Open API for corporate travel management covering approval workflows, bills, budget/cost centers, orders, single sign-on, users, roles, and company entities. The DDES API (base URL https://api.es.xiaojukeji.com) is documented at opendocs.xiaojukeji.com/version2024, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials plus per-request signing, and shipped with official Java and Go SDKs under the github.com/didi organization. DiDi is backed by Hillhouse and the SoftBank Vision Fund.
d.name: Didi

d.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: DiDi Autonomous

d.description: Didimo is a digital human and 3D character technology company whose flagship product, Popul8, automates the creation of game-ready NPCs, crowds, and digital humans at scale. Popul8 Express lets studios generate thousands of fully-rigged, high-quality characters from a single 3D base template, with automated asset fitting, shape and rig transfer, intersection solving, material and deformable variation, and crowd rendering optimized for Unity and Unreal Engine. Beyond the desktop application, Popul8 ships a headless command-line tool (Popul8 CLI) for automating crowd-generation pipelines in CI/CD, plus Unity and Unreal bridges for bringing characters and crowds directly into game engines. Didimo is headquartered in Clearwater, Florida with offices in Portugal and the UK, and was backed by Techstars.
d.name: Didimo

d.description: Didit is a developer-first identity verification and fraud-prevention platform that exposes one unified API for KYC (ID verification, passive/active liveness, face match and search, age estimation, proof of address, NFC), KYB business verification (registry, UBO/ownership, officers, entity AML), AML sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring (KYT), crypto wallet screening, and FATF/EU Travel Rule. It spans 220+ countries, 14,000+ document types and 50+ languages with sub-two-second inference, pay-per-call pricing from $0.30 and a 500-verification monthly free tier. The v3 REST API authenticates with an x-api-key header, ships Web/iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter SDKs, HMAC-signed webhooks, a live hosted MCP server, and Agent Skills. Backed by Y Combinator and Robinhood Ventures.
d.name: Didit

d.description: Didomi is a Paris-based consent and preference management platform (CMP/PMP) that helps publishers, advertisers, retailers, and large enterprises collect, manage, and act on user privacy choices across web, mobile, CTV, and AMP surfaces. The platform covers GDPR, CCPA and the wider US state-law landscape, IAB TCF v2.x, Google Consent Mode v2, the IAB GPP, GPC, the EU DMA, Chilean Law 25, Australian privacy law, and other regulations through a single multi-regulation configuration model. Didomi exposes a JSON REST API (https://api.didomi.io/v1/) plus first-party SDKs for Web, iOS/tvOS, Android/Android TV, Unity, React Native, Flutter, Vega OS, and AMP, alongside IAB-compliant consent string tooling and reverse-proxy boilerplates for Fastly, CloudFront, and Cloudflare.
d.name: Didomi

d.description: Diebold Nixdorf is a global provider of connected commerce technology for the financial and retail industries — ATMs and self-service terminals, retail point-of-sale hardware, the Vynamic software portfolio (Payments, Transaction Middleware, Self-Service, Security, Retail Platform) and the managed services around them. Its integration surface is enterprise and customer-deployed rather than self-serve: eight public OpenAPI definitions for the Vynamic banking stack are published through the company's SwaggerHub organization, while the Vynamic Retail Platform developer portal sits behind a login and the former developer community no longer resolves. There is no public signup, pricing page or published rate limit, and every specification names a customer-hosted server.
d.name: Diebold Nixdorf

d.description: Diem is a consumer social search engine, delivered as an iOS and Android app, that surfaces community-driven answers to questions people are often reluctant to ask elsewhere - positioning itself as "a search engine that feels like you're asking questions in a girl's bathroom at 1am." The Diem experience centers on a women-focused community, a Gems rewards program redeemable for products and features, a weekly newsletter, a merch shop, and companion products such as the Twin Flame astrology-compatibility app. Diem is backed by a16z, Ribbit Capital, and Techstars. It is a consumer application with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.
d.name: Diem

d.description: Food & nutrition data REST API with 4.7M+ foods, calories, macros, micronutrients, Nutri-Score and EAN/UPC barcode lookup, with confidence-ranked full-text search. Data primarily from Open Food Facts (ODbL) and USDA FoodData Central, EU-hosted, with key-optional read access.
d.name: DietlyAPI

d.description: Diffbot is a company that provides AI-powered web scraping and data extraction services. Their technology allows businesses to automatically extract and organize data from any website, turning unstructured web content into structured data that can be easily analyzed and used for various purposes. Diffbot's solution is used by companies across industries to gather competitive intelligence, monitor market trends, track online mentions, and more.
d.name: Diffbot

d.description: Diffusion Software is a small independent software vendor that develops audio-encoding and RDS (Radio Data System) tooling for FM radio broadcasters. Its flagship product, Airomate, is a software-based RDS/RBDS encoder that generates a high-quality RDS signal using a 192 kHz-capable soundcard, letting stations broadcast professional-looking RDS information (station name, RadioText, program service data) at low cost without dedicated hardware. The company also ships complementary broadcast utilities: StereoCoder (an FM stereo/MPX encoder), Little SineGen (a sine-wave generator that runs at any sample rate the soundcard supports), and Chronos (a free scheduler that sequences Programme Service name and RadioText messages for Airomate). The products are Windows desktop applications distributed as low-cost licensed downloads. Diffusion Software is a seed-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a network identity record.
d.name: Diffusion

d.description: Dify is an open-source platform for building AI applications, combining Backend-as-a-Service and LLMOps to streamline the development of generative AI solutions for developers and non-technical innovators alike. Teams build agentic workflows, chatflows, agents and RAG knowledge pipelines on a visual canvas, then publish each one as a web app, an embeddable widget, a REST API or an MCP server. Dify is operated by Langgenius, Inc. and ships as Dify Cloud, a self-hosted Community Edition and a commercial Enterprise edition.
d.name: Dify

d.description: Digbi Health is a digital therapeutics company delivering a precision-biology virtual clinic for food-related and inflammatory illnesses — obesity, cardiometabolic disease, type 2 diabetes, digestive disorders (IBS, GERD), MSK chronic pain, PCOS, sleep and mental health. Its FoodRx program combines host-genetics and gut-microbiome testing with app-based coaching, precision nutrition, and pre/probiotic therapies, delivered to members through health plans and employers. Digbi Health is backed by Accel. The company operates a consumer-facing storefront and member app rather than a public developer API; this profile captures the public web, agent, and security surfaces observable at digbihealth.com.
d.name: Digbi Health

d.description: Digby was an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service provider of mobile commerce and mobile engagement solutions for large retailers, operating under parent company 30 Second Software Inc. Its platform — including the Localpoint location-based marketing product — delivered branded mobile web experiences and native shopping apps, connecting digital engagement to physical stores for customers such as Cabela's, Kohl's, Catalina Marketing and Hasbro. Digby raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, S3 Ventures, Daylight Ventures, Relay Ventures and the BlackBerry Partners Fund. The company was acquired by fellow Austin mobile company Phunware in May 2014 (along with its Movaya subsidiary in Seattle and Chengdu), terms undisclosed, and the Localpoint technology was folded into Phunware's product line. Digby no longer operates as an independent company: digby.com no longer resolves to a live site (last Internet Archive capture February 2015) and there is no current developer portal, documentation, API, SDK or other public API surface to catalog.
d.name: Digby

d.description: Digg is a technology news aggregation and community curation platform, relaunched under new ownership and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and True Ventures. It surfaces trending stories, discussions, and video signals drawn largely from X/Twitter, ranking them by community engagement and editorial signals. The platform tracks contributor rankings, rising stories, today's highlights, and GitHub repository activity, positioning itself as an AI-assisted discovery hub for technology, startups, and AI news. As surfaced here, Digg is a consumer web product with no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; this profile captures its identity and web/domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Digg

d.description: Digg – Myndigheten för digital förvaltning – is Sweden’s digital government agency responsible for digital transformation, providing digital services, coordination, analysis and support to public sector actors. It develops and operates digital platforms, promotes e‑legitimation, and works on initiatives such as Sweden Connect and the Single Digital Gateway, aiming to create a sustainable welfare society through technology.
d.name: Digg

d.description: Digger (diggerhq), backed by Initialized Capital, builds developer infrastructure across two open-source-rooted product lines. OpenTaco (formerly the Digger CE project) is an Infrastructure-as-Code orchestration and Terraform/OpenTofu state-management platform that runs plan/apply inside your existing CI pipeline, with PR automation, PR-level locks, drift detection and remediation, RBAC via Open Policy Agent, and FIPS 140 support; it is self-hostable via Docker Compose, Railway, and Kubernetes. OpenComputer is the company's flagship agent-infrastructure product: persistent, long-running cloud VMs for AI agents — real Linux machines that hibernate when idle and wake in seconds, with checkpoints, preview URLs, per-tenant package control, a REST API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, the oc CLI, durable agent sessions, and signed, retriable webhooks for sandbox lifecycle events.
d.name: Digger

d.description: Retrieve price and inventory of electronic components as well as place orders
d.name: Digi-Key

d.description: digiantnz is a Christchurch, New Zealand operator that runs a2a-browser, a self-hosted, account-less, pay-per-query web retrieval agent published as an A2A 0.3 agent card at a2a-browser.digiant.nz. The agent exposes two skills over a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint — Web Search (SERP query with LLM synthesis and entity extraction) and Page Fetch (Playwright-rendered fetch with a 50k-character cap) — identifies callers by an Ed25519 public key instead of a signup, runs a free FIFO tier at 10 requests/hour, and quotes a paid tier live in satoshis (10 per search, 20 per fetch, 1,000 minimum, Lightning) that the card still marks alpha. No OpenAPI, documentation site, MCP server or SDK is published; the registrable domain digiant.nz redirects to a Web3 name (digiant.crypto) that public DNS does not resolve.
d.name: digiantnz

d.description: Digicert is a leading provider of digital security solutions, specializing in SSL/TLS certificates, PKI solutions, and website security. They help organizations of all sizes protect their websites, data, and communications from cyber threats by providing secure encryption and authentication services. Digicert's CertCentral platform exposes a suite of REST and GraphQL APIs for certificate lifecycle management, discovery, automation, and reporting.
d.name: Digicert

d.description: DigiFinex is a centralized cryptocurrency exchange offering spot, margin and perpetual swap (USDT-margined) trading, OTC, copy trading and a crypto card. It publishes a public developer API: a signed REST API for spot and margin (openapi.digifinex.com/v3), a REST API for perpetual swaps (openapi.digifinex.com/swap/v2), and WebSocket market and account streams, documented at docs.digifinex.com. Private endpoints are signed with ACCESS-KEY, ACCESS-SIGN (HMAC-SHA256) and ACCESS-TIMESTAMP headers.
d.name: DigiFinex

d.description: Digiflex (listed by Battery Ventures as "Digiflex, Ltd.") was an Israeli manufacturer of inkjet-based computer-to-plate and digital printing systems, best known for the Flexojet line of flexographic plate-making printers. It was a hardware company: the product was a physical printing press, not software, so it never had a developer program, a public API, or any machine-readable contract to publish. PV Nano Cell signed a $10M all-stock letter of intent in March 2017 and closed the acquisition on 3 December 2017, folding Digiflex in as a wholly-owned subsidiary to carry the Flexojet systems into printed electronics; Battery Ventures now carries the name on its list-of-all-companies page as an exited investment. The brand has since been fully absorbed — the acquirer's current site (pvnanocell.com, HTTP 200) makes no mention of DigiFlex, and digiflex.com, while still registered through Dynadot to an April 2027 expiry, has no working nameservers and returns SERVFAIL with no A record. The live domains sharing the name are unrelated third parties: digiflex.io is a West Midlands web-design agency, digiflex.co.uk is a separate UK business, and digiflex.ai sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge with no verifiable link to the Battery investment. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, package-registry presence, or any other API artifact exists for this company. This profile is retained as an honest record of an acquired and absorbed portfolio lead with no API surface rather than being enriched with speculative attribution.
d.name: Digiflex

d.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.
d.name: DigiLens

d.description: Provides information about digimon creatures
d.name: Digimon Information

d.description: Search for Digimon cards in digimoncard.io
d.name: Digimon TCG

d.description: Digio is an India-based digital trust and paperwork automation platform. Its REST APIs deliver legally-valid Aadhaar and OTP eSign, eStamping, KYC (CKYC, KRA, DigiLocker, offline Aadhaar, and Video KYC), eNACH/NACH eMandates and UPI Autopay recurring payments, AML/CFT screening, and template-based document and agreement management. All endpoints use HTTPS with HTTP Basic authentication.
d.name: Digio

d.description: Digioh is a US-based onsite personalization and zero-party data platform for ecommerce brands. It ships product recommendation quizzes, pop-ups, banners, sidebars, inline embeds, landing pages, email/SMS preference centers and post-purchase surveys as a JavaScript widget layer installed on a merchant's storefront, plus Digioh Passport for cross-session visitor identification and Digioh Pipelines for routing form submissions into ESP/CRM destinations such as Klaviyo, Iterable, Braze, Attentive, Ometria, HubSpot and Salesforce. Its developer surface is client-side rather than server-side - a documented browser JavaScript API (DIGIOH_API.LIGHTBOX), an outbound "API Form POST" webhook integration that posts submission JSON to a customer-controlled endpoint, iOS and Android embed SDKs, and a WordPress plugin and Shopify app. Digioh publishes no public inbound REST API, no OpenAPI definition and no developer portal.
d.name: Digioh

d.description: Digit was a consumer fintech company that built an automated personal-savings app: it analyzed a user's checking-account activity and quietly moved small, safe amounts into an FDIC-insured savings account, later expanding into automated investing and retirement (Digit Invest, Digit Retirement). Founded in 2013 in San Francisco by Ethan Bloch and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, Digit was acquired by Oportun in late 2021 and folded into Oportun's savings product. The standalone Digit brand is now retired: digit.co and hellodigit.com redirect to oportun.com/savings, and there is no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no active developer surface.
d.name: Digit

d.description: Digitail is a cloud-based, AI-native veterinary practice management software (PIMS) that consolidates scheduling, electronic medical records, AI SOAP dictation, client communication, billing, inventory, and reporting into one platform, paired with a Pet Parent mobile app for booking, records access, and payments. The Digitail Open API is a documented REST API (base https://developer.digitail.io/api/v1) secured with OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant with PKCE, giving clinics, technology partners, and ecosystem players (labs, insurers, pharmacies, telemedicine, analytics) programmatic, real-time access to clinic data. API credentials are provisioned via an access registration; Open API access is included across Digitail subscription plans.
d.name: Digitail

d.description: Digital Asset is the company behind Canton, a privacy-enabled public blockchain built for regulated institutional finance, and Daml, the smart-contract language that runs on it. Its commercial products sit on top of the Canton Network: the DA Registry, a production platform for issuing, minting, burning, transferring and redeeming institutional-grade tokenized assets with credential-based allowlists, blocklists and proof-of-transfer; xReserve, which brings Circle's USDC onto Canton; and a Covalidation Service for operating validator infrastructure. Its public developer surface is the Utilities (Operator Backend) API plus four Canton Token Standard (CIP-56) off-ledger APIs — token metadata, transfer instruction, allocation and allocation instruction — all published as OpenAPI 3.0 and served across MainNet, TestNet and DevNet environments. Digital Asset also publishes an A2A agent card and a packaged Agent Skill for its Registry workflows.
d.name: Digital Asset

d.description: Digital Currency Group (DCG) is a cryptocurrency and blockchain holding and venture company founded in 2015 by Barry Silbert and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. DCG builds, incubates, and invests in companies across the digital asset ecosystem, including subsidiaries such as Grayscale Investments and Foundry. It operates as an investor and parent company rather than a direct API provider; this network profile tracks DCG's public web presence and corporate surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures. Sector: fintech / digital assets.
d.name: Digital Currency Group

d.description: Digital Diagnostics is a healthcare AI company based in Coralville, Iowa, founded by Dr. Michael Abramoff. It builds autonomous artificial-intelligence diagnostic systems that make a medical diagnosis at the point of care without requiring a physician to interpret the result. Its flagship product, LumineticsCore (formerly IDx-DR), was the first FDA-cleared autonomous AI diagnostic system and detects diabetic retinopathy from fundus images in about 30 seconds, reimbursed under CPT code 92229 and integrated with EHR systems such as Epic. A companion product, SphereDx, provides securely hosted diagnostic result management. The company is a portfolio company of 8vc and is researching additional indications including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative disease detection via retinal imaging. Digital Diagnostics emphasizes ethical, equitable AI ("AI the right way") and holds ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certification. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
d.name: Digital Diagnostics

d.description: Digital Iron is an AI platform delivering aftersales intelligence for heavy machinery. It helps equipment dealers and OEMs turn scattered service data — machine history, product documentation, customer records, bills of materials, work orders, and technician notes — into faster troubleshooting, accurate parts identification, and reliable job quoting. The platform surfaces recurring failure patterns across fleets (excavators, crushers, compaction rollers, and similar equipment) to improve first-time fix rates. Digital Iron is backed by Seedcamp and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; the product is delivered as a hosted web application and no public API has been identified to date.
d.name: Digital Iron

d.description: Digital Market was an enterprise-software company that built electronic-components B2B commerce software, backed by Trinity Ventures. It was acquired by Agile Software and no longer operates as an independent provider. It is not an API provider and publishes no live developer surface, documentation, or specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio record rather than an active, enrichable API.
d.name: Digital Market

d.description: Digital Mortar is an in-store and physical-location people-journey analytics company. Its DM1 platform measures shopper and visitor journeys - path, queue, occupancy, throughput, dwell and space utilization - using LiDAR and stereoscopic-camera sensors, delivering heat mapping, funnel analysis, real-time queue and occupancy tracking, display and merchandising measurement, and door/people counting as a SaaS analytics tool. It serves retail, airports, malls, stadiums and events. Digital Mortar is now part of PMY Group; its digitalmortar.com domain is dormant (mail-only, no live website) and it exposes no public developer or API program.
d.name: Digital Mortar

d.description: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc. is an American multinational technology company and cloud service provider. The company is headquartered in New York City, New York, US, with 15 globally distributed data centers. DigitalOcean provides developers, startups, and SMBs with cloud infrastructure-as-a-service platforms.
d.name: Digital Ocean

d.description: The Digital Public Library of America (DPLA) provides a free REST API that gives access to metadata for 50 million+ cultural heritage items aggregated from 4,000+ US libraries, archives, and museums. The API supports full-text search, field-specific queries, geographic and date range filtering, faceted browsing, and JSONP callbacks. All results are returned as JSON-LD. API keys are issued free of charge via a self-service email-based registration endpoint. DPLA aggregates contributions from cultural heritage institutions across the United States and makes the combined metadata freely available to researchers, developers, and the public.
d.name: Digital Public Library of America

d.description: Digital Realty is a global provider of data center, colocation, and interconnection solutions. Operating over 300 data centers in 55+ metros worldwide, it serves enterprises and service providers with secure, scalable infrastructure for AI, cloud, and hybrid workloads. The company emphasizes sustainability, high availability, and extensive partner ecosystems, delivering 99.999% uptime and comprehensive compliance certifications.
d.name: Digital Realty

d.description: Profile for Digital Realty Trust in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 746).
d.name: Digital Realty Trust

d.description: Digital Room is an e-commerce and manufacturing company that for nearly three decades has helped small and medium-sized businesses reach customers, promote products, and build their brands. It sells customized marketing products through ten uniquely branded storefronts — UPrinting, Signs.com, NextDayFlyers, PrintPlace, PrintRunner, eSigns, 48HourPrint, LogoSportswear, Packlane and Packola — backed by purpose-built ordering and design software and a coast-to-coast production network of nine U.S. facilities plus two in the Philippines, covering print, signage, packaging, apparel and promotional products. Sycamore Partners acquired the company from H.I.G. Capital in December 2021; Insight Partners is also an investor, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. Digital Room publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, MCP server or agent card. Its one machine-readable agent surface is llms.txt — all ten brand storefronts serve a substantive, hand-authored file, several with explicit "For AI Agents" routing instructions, while the corporate host serves none.
d.name: Digital Room

d.description: Digital Shadows is a London-founded digital risk protection (DRP) company whose SearchLight platform monitors the open, deep and dark web for data leakage, exposed credentials, brand impersonation, exposed infrastructure and threat-actor activity affecting a customer's organization. ReliaQuest acquired Digital Shadows in July 2022 and the entity now trades as ReliaQuest UK Limited, with SearchLight folded into ReliaQuest GreyMatter Digital Risk Protection. The SearchLight Portal API remains live at portal-digitalshadows.com/api/ and is consumed by first-party tooling (the shadowline Python CLI and the Splunk SOAR connector) and by a wide third-party integration surface (Cortex XSOAR, ThreatConnect, Splunk, Sekoia, Axonius, TheHive, Atlassian Marketplace). The API reference itself is published only inside the authenticated customer portal.
d.name: Digital Shadows

d.description: DigitalAPI is an API catalog, marketplace, and management platform that unifies APIs across multiple gateways into a single searchable catalog with governance, discovery, access control, and analytics.
d.name: DigitalAPI

d.description: DigitalBPM provides a no‑code automation platform that enables businesses to integrate SaaS applications without writing code. It offers a visual workflow builder, pre‑built connectors for popular services, and the ability to create custom integrations. Targeted at small to medium‑size teams, DigitalBPM aims to streamline processes, reduce manual effort, and accelerate digital transformation across enterprises.
d.name: DigitalBPM

d.description: Digitale Seiten is a German online marketing company that operates a network of 28+ industry-specific business directories for craftspeople and local service providers (for example Elektriker.org, Klempner.org, Maler.org and Dachdecker.org). The platform lets tradespeople create free business listings, distributes regional customer inquiries and job requests to registered companies as leads, improves their search-engine visibility, and provides review-collection tools. According to the company it lists 869,000+ registered businesses and has matched 765,000+ job assignments. It is a B2B directory and lead-generation service and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by Point Nine.
d.name: digitaleseiten

d.description: DigitalGenius is an AI agent platform purpose-built for ecommerce and retail customer service. It automates pre- and post-purchase support, fully resolving customer issues such as order tracking, returns and exchanges, subscription management, and warranty claims by orchestrating "flows" that deeply integrate with a brand's existing systems (helpdesks like Zendesk, Freshchat, Freshdesk, Kustomer, Gorgias and Salesforce Service Cloud, plus dozens of carriers, WMS/OMS and logistics providers). Developers connect via a documented HTTP API, an embeddable Genius Chat headless SDK (web, iOS, Android, Expo), and an official hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, with region-scoped EU and US hosts and Auth0-backed platform authentication.
d.name: DigitalGenius

d.description: Digitalk, Inc. was an American object-oriented software tools vendor and a Trinity Ventures portfolio company, best known for Smalltalk/V — a commercial Smalltalk development environment first released in 1986 for MS-DOS, preceded by "Digitalk Methods" in 1983. It was founded by George Bosworth, Jim Anderson, Mike Teng and Barbara Noparstak, and its product line grew into Visual Smalltalk Enterprise. In July 1995 Digitalk merged with its principal competitor ParcPlace Systems; the combined company was later renamed ObjectShare, announced a shift away from Smalltalk toward Java in 1997, and active development of the Digitalk line ended shortly after. The final release, Visual Smalltalk Enterprise 2000, shipped in September 2000. Cincom retains the right to sell and support VSE 2000 for existing licensees and Seagull Software owns the virtual machine. Digitalk predates the public web API era and operates no developer platform, public API, or live web presence today; this profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Digitalk

d.description: Status of all DigitalOcean services
d.name: DigitalOcean Status

d.description: DigitalOwl is an AI-powered platform that transforms unstructured medical records into structured, actionable data for the life insurance, property & casualty insurance, and legal industries. Its products (View, Triage, Connect, Chat, Workflows, and Case Notes) automate medical record review, summarization, triage, and data extraction to accelerate underwriting, claims processing, and legal demand-package analysis. The Connect Data API maps source documents, classifications, and medical mentions (conditions, procedures, medications) into structured layers for integration into existing carrier and law-firm systems. DigitalOwl operates on AWS and Google Cloud with SOC 2 (Type II), HIPAA, and GDPR compliance. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
d.name: DigitalOwl

d.description: Digital Surgery (originally Touch Surgery / Kinosis) is a London-based surgical artificial intelligence company backed by Balderton Capital and acquired by Medtronic in 2020, where it now operates as part of Medtronic's Covidien surgical business. It builds the Touch Surgery ecosystem of surgical simulation and training tools and Touch Surgery Enterprise, an AI-powered platform for recording, analyzing, and reviewing surgical video in the operating room. The company does not publish a public developer program or API; digitalsurgery.com now redirects to Medtronic's Digital Surgery product page. This profile remains a network stub awaiting a real developer surface.
d.name: digitalsurgery

d.description: Digits is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping platform for startups and their accountants, built around the Autonomous General Ledger (AGL) that auto-books the majority of transactions in real time. The Digits Connect API opens the AGL programmatically over REST with OAuth 2.0, letting partners send raw transaction, party, and dimension data for AI categorization and vendor enrichment, and read back ledger entries and financial statements. Digits also publishes an MCP server for AI agents (ChatGPT, Claude) to query the ledger.
d.name: Digits

d.description: Dija is a consumer-sector company surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment pass the company has no live web or developer surface: its candidate domains do not resolve (dija.co, dija.com) and dija.co.uk is a parked domain listed for sale by a third-party broker. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API artifact could be located, so no provider artifacts were generated or derived. The 2026-07-20 pass re-verified this independently: dija.co and dija.com return NXDOMAIN, dija.co.uk resolves to an Aftermarket.com parking page advertising the domain for sale (Nominet registration active to 2026-12-10) and returns 404 for every /.well-known/ discovery path and /llms.txt. Note for future runs: the github.com/dija organization and the dija.now and dija.sa domains are UNRELATED name collisions (Dija, a Saudi Arabia software firm, and a separate reminder app) and must not be attributed to this company. This profile remains a lead with no active public API surface.
d.name: Dija

d.description: Dil Mil is a South Asian dating and matchmaking platform built to help singles find meaningful, culturally-grounded connections. Its mobile app offers matching algorithms, interest-based community chat rooms, global matching that reaches beyond geography, and a VIP Elite membership tier with premium features such as unlimited likes, rewind, and advanced filtering. The company markets itself under the tagline "Find Something Real" and highlights thousands of documented success stories among South Asian singles worldwide. Dil Mil is a consumer mobile application with no public developer or API surface; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.
d.name: Dil Mil

d.description: Diligen provides machine‑learning powered contract analysis software that helps law firms, legal service providers, and corporations streamline review, extract key provisions, generate summaries, and manage projects at scale. Its AI‑driven platform automates insight extraction, improves review efficiency, and supports regulatory change response, delivering faster, higher‑quality outcomes for legal teams.
d.name: Diligen

d.description: DiligenceSquared is an AI-powered commercial due diligence and market research platform serving private equity firms, credit investors, and corporate clients. It deploys AI voice agents to run hundreds of simultaneous investor-grade expert interviews, then organizes the findings into structured, fully source-traceable market intelligence for investment decision-making. Backed by Y Combinator, the company operates a customer web application at app.diligencesquared.com and publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface.
d.name: Diligencesquared

d.description: Diligent (Diligent AI, godiligent.ai) builds autonomous AI agents for financial-crime compliance, automating the reasoning-heavy KYC/AML workflows that banks and fintechs run at scale. Its API exposes Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and business/merchant verification, name screening against sanctions and PEP providers with AI-powered alert remediation, ongoing monitoring with alerting, company identification and registry document retrieval, a blocked-company list, and an experimental instant website screening endpoint. The platform is API-first (X-API-KEY auth, production and sandbox environments, idempotency, and signed webhooks) and is used by fintechs and banks including Scalapay, Flywire, Allica Bank, Tamara, Teya, Vivid and Alma. Diligent is SOC 2 Type II certified, ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. It is backed by Speedinvest, Y Combinator and Shapers, and operates out of London and Berlin.
d.name: Diligent

d.description: Diligent Corporation is a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company best known for its board management portal (Diligent Boards / Boardbooks) and the broader Diligent One Platform, which unifies board management, enterprise risk, audit, compliance, entity management, and ESG. The board portal itself is a security-hardened product with no public developer API - it is integrated through SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM provisioning, and packaged connectors (Okta, Microsoft 365/Teams, Zoom, DocuSign). Diligent does, however, publish a real developer portal at developer.diligent.com covering the GRC side of the platform - the HighBond (Diligent One) REST API for audit/risk/compliance data, a GraphQL Entities API for legal-entity and subsidiary management, an ESG API for activity/usage data, and a Workflow API for jobs, tasks, and campaigns. API access is customer/partner-gated (a HighBond API key or SSO-scoped token is required) and pricing is quote-based via Diligent sales.
d.name: Diligent

d.description: Diligent Pharma, Inc. is a Princeton, New Jersey clinical-trial quality and compliance company, founded in 2015, that operates a centralized vendor qualification and oversight platform for pharmaceutical and biotech sponsors and their service providers. Its Diligent360 platform unifies the vendor lifecycle — AI-assisted discovery across a network of 2,000+ clinical vendors, capability evaluation through standardized questionnaires, risk scoring across quality, compliance, cybersecurity and AI risk domains, qualification against ICH E6(R3) and GxP expectations, and ongoing oversight monitoring. Companion products DiligentRespond (automated vendor questionnaire response) and DiligentQualified (qualification package management) sit alongside a GxP audit services practice. The company raised an $8.27M Series A led by FCA Venture Partners in 2023 and has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list. The platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at 360.diligentpharma.com; Diligent Pharma publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.
d.name: Diligent Pharma

d.description: Diligent Robotics is an Austin, Texas-based healthcare robotics company founded in 2017 by Andrea Thomaz (CEO) and Vivian Chu (CIO), both trained as roboticists at MIT, Georgia Tech, and the University of Texas at Austin. The company builds Moxi, a socially intelligent mobile manipulator that operates autonomously inside hospitals to handle non-clinical material transport — delivering medications, lab samples, supplies, PPE, and patient items so nurses and clinical staff can focus on patient care. Moxi combines mobile manipulation (grasping, opening doors, riding elevators), social navigation, and human-guided learning, and is deployed 24/7 with minimal facility infrastructure (existing Wi-Fi). Operationally, Moxi has logged 500,000+ deliveries and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides across customer hospitals including UTMB, Shannon Health, ThedaCare, Carilion Giles Community Hospital, and Medical City Denton. The platform is HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II audited, and TX-RAMP Level 2 certified. Diligent has raised roughly $100M across rounds led by Canaan, True Ventures, Tiger Global, DNX Ventures, Next Coast Ventures, and Northwestern Medicine Innovation. Diligent's revenue model is robot deployment/leasing and enterprise services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Moxi or its underlying robotics stack.
d.name: Diligent Robotics

d.description: Diligent Software is an entry harvested from Battery Ventures' public "list of all companies" (https://www.battery.com/list-of-all-companies/), where it is marked with an asterisk denoting an EXITED investment. Battery publishes only the company name for this entry — no URL, no sector, no description, and no acquisition or IPO detail — so the underlying company could not be positively identified during enrichment. It appears to be a legacy/defunct or long-since-acquired enterprise software investment rather than an operating API provider. The only live host at diligentsoftware.com is an unrelated single-proprietor custom .NET software consultancy in Liberty Hill, Texas (Peter Stephens), whose static site has not been updated since February 2014; it is NOT treated as this company. This profile is explicitly NOT Diligent Corporation, the GRC/board-management vendor at diligent.com — that company is catalogued separately in the network as diligent-boards (developer.diligent.com, HighBond/Entities/ESG/Workflow APIs) — and it is NOT Diligent AI (godiligent.ai), the KYC/AML compliance API catalogued as diligent. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, package, well-known surface, or event surface was found for this entry. No artifacts were produced because none exist to harvest.
d.name: Diligent Software

d.description: Dillard's, Inc. is a Little Rock, Arkansas department store chain selling apparel, footwear, cosmetics, handbags, menswear and home goods through its stores across the United States and dillards.com. Dillard's publishes no developer program, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, gRPC or SOAP contract, and no MCP or A2A agent surface — contract discovery on 2026-09-06 found every /.well-known/ and /openapi.json path answering with the storefront single-page-app shell under HTTP 200, matching a nonsense control path. Its two real machine-facing surfaces are a first-party llms.txt at https://www.dillards.com/llms.txt that maps the retail catalog for language models, and an ANSI ASC X12 EDI trading-partner program (810/816/820/832/850/856/860/864/997 over the OpenText/GXS VAN) whose implementation guide and vendor portal are gated behind a login on the Dillard's eBiz extranet.
d.name: Dillard's

d.description: Dimension is a nationwide, on-demand waste management and junk removal platform (formerly Trash Warrior) backed by 500 Global. It offers digital booking with instant AI-generated pricing (their "Mirror Mirror AI" quoter), same-day and next-day pickup for cardboard, appliances, mattresses, hazardous and medical waste, plus dumpster rentals, for both businesses and individuals. Every job includes tracking with detailed diversion data, receipts, and photos, and can be booked as a one-off or recurring service. Dimension has been awarded a State of California RFP contract for PPE waste removal. The company operates a customer-facing booking application and help center but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.
d.name: Dimension

d.description: Dimensional is a Toronto-based personality-science company whose consumer mobile app assesses more than 200 traits across 15 dimensions — including cognition, values, communication styles, interests, love styles, attachment style, conflict resolution, strengths, and political ideology — to build detailed personality profiles. Users compare results with friends and explore relationship compatibility, positioning the product against social-media highlight reels in favor of authentic connection. The app is available on iOS with an Android beta, and the company is backed by Bloomberg Beta. No public API, SDK, or developer platform is published at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and security surface.
d.name: Dimensional

d.description: A data modeling technique used in data warehousing that structures data into fact tables containing measurable metrics and dimension tables containing descriptive attributes, optimized for query performance and business intelligence reporting. Organizations use it to track key metrics, identify trends, and optimize business outcomes.
d.name: Dimensional Modeling

d.description: Dimensions is a research data platform from Digital Science providing access to publications, grants, patents, clinical trials, datasets, and policy documents. The Dimensions Analytics API offers programmatic access to this research data via the Dimensions Search Language (DSL), enabling citation analysis, researcher discovery, organization benchmarking, and topic identification. The API is subscription-only and is not intended for bulk data extraction or to power dashboards or other derivative products.
d.name: Dimensions

d.description: Dimeq is a Norwegian maritime safety technology company working to prevent loss of life at sea and set new health, safety and environmental (HSE) standards for the maritime sector. Its Eye-D System is an IoT-based digital ecosystem that delivers real-time positioning of crew and passengers to one-meter accuracy during emergencies, man-overboard detection using environmental sensors, automatic mustering that registers people in seconds, and statistical analysis for accident documentation and prevention, while keeping data anonymous and GDPR-compliant outside of emergencies. The D-Router gateway supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet, PLC, fiber optics, UWB, Bluetooth, LoRa, ZigBee and MATTER connectivity. This is a hardware/IoT product company with no public developer portal, API, SDK or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.
d.name: Dimeq

d.description: Dinari provides tokenized US stocks and ETFs (dShares) backed 1:1 by real securities, giving businesses an API to offer global customers regulated access to over a hundred equities and index tokens across 85+ jurisdictions. The Dinari Enterprise API covers entity onboarding and KYC/KYB, brokerage account management, market data (prices, quotes, splits, dividends, news), managed and on-chain (EIP-155 permit) order requests, order fulfillment, blockchain wallet connection, token transfers, withdrawals, and a USD+ stablecoin for dividend payments. dShares settle on-chain across Arbitrum One, HyperEVM, and Avalanche C-Chain. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Version One Ventures and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
d.name: Dinari

d.description: Dingdong (Dingdong Maicai / 叮咚买菜) is a Shanghai-based on-demand fresh-grocery e-commerce company operating a front-warehouse (dark-store) model that delivers fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and prepared foods to consumers, typically within about 30 minutes, through its mobile app. The company is publicly listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DDL) and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Its public surface (ddxq.mobi) is a consumer mobile-app backend rather than a developer platform; no public developer portal, API documentation, or open API program was found during enrichment, and the host is not reachable outside of China.
d.name: Dingdong

d.description: Dingdong Maicai (叮咚买菜), operated by Shanghai Yibai Mi Network Technology Co., Ltd., is a Chinese on-demand fresh grocery e-commerce and delivery platform. It runs a mobile-app marketplace for fresh produce, meat, seafood, prepared foods, and daily groceries, backed by a network of front-line neighborhood micro-fulfillment stations that enable fast, same-hour delivery in major Chinese cities. The company is publicly listed on the NYSE (ticker DDL) and was backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It is a consumer-facing operation with no public developer program or open API surface; this profile is a network lead maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.
d.name: Dingdong Maicai

d.description: Dinii (株式会社ダイニー) is a Tokyo-based restaurant-technology SaaS company, founded in June 2018, offering an "All in One Restaurant Cloud" for food-service businesses. Its integrated modules span POS register, customer mobile ordering, mobile self-checkout payment, customer management/CRM (with LINE integration), staff attendance and scheduling, reservation ledger, and management analytics dashboards (daily P&L, labor-cost optimization, QSC monitoring). Dinii reports 3,000+ installed locations and 20 million+ end users, with offices in Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo, and Nagoya. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Dinii publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.
d.name: Dinii

d.description: DinMo is a composable Customer Data Platform (CDP) that turns a cloud data warehouse into a marketing activation engine. It connects directly to Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Amazon Redshift, PostgreSQL, Microsoft Fabric, and ClickHouse, lets non-technical teams model customer data and build no-code segments, and activates those audiences to more than a hundred destination platforms (ad networks, CRMs, marketing and messaging tools) via Reverse ETL with a zero-data-copy architecture built for GDPR and FADP compliance. DinMo also exposes a Personalization API for retrieving activated model records in real time, plus AI predictions (LTV, churn), identity resolution, a Customer Hub, and event tracking. The company is Paris-based and backed by Seedcamp.
d.name: DinMo

d.description: dinovamedtech is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
d.name: dinovamedtech

d.description: Diplomat Pharmacy was an independent provider of specialty pharmacy services that helped patients with chronic and complex conditions access and manage specialty medications. The company was acquired by UnitedHealth Group's OptumRx, and operations have been integrated under that brand. No publicly documented developer APIs are offered under the Diplomat Pharmacy name.
d.name: Diplomat Pharmacy

d.description: DIPS AS is Norway's largest supplier of electronic health record (EHR) systems to hospitals, in operation since 1987 and headquartered in Bodø. Its DIPS Arena EHR is built on the openEHR reference model and exposes standardised HL7 FHIR R4 and openEHR REST interfaces. Through Open DIPS — a public developer portal and synthetic-data sandbox at dips.developer.azure-api.net — DIPS publishes an OpenID Connect provider (DIPS Federation Service), a FHIR Patient API and a SMART on FHIR launch surface, backed by a public FHIR R4 Implementation Guide and an openEHR archetype repository on GitHub.
d.name: DIPS

d.description: Diraq is a quantum computing company headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices in Palo Alto, California and Boston, Massachusetts. Spun out of UNSW Sydney in 2022 by Professor Andrew Dzurak, Diraq builds quantum processors from silicon spin qubits — quantum information encoded in the spin of single electrons held in quantum dots formed inside structures derived from conventional CMOS transistors, so the qubits can be fabricated on standard semiconductor foundry lines. The company works with imec, NVIDIA and Quantum Machines, has advanced through DARPA's utility-scale quantum computing initiative, and targets a first commercial processor toward the end of the decade. Diraq is a pre-commercial hardware and research organization: as of this profile it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its stated commercial pathway — cloud access to its processors — is still on the roadmap rather than in market.
d.name: Diraq

d.description: Direct Hire (directhireagents.com) is an agent-first professional network and discovery directory for autonomous AI agents. Agents self-register through a public onboarding API without a human account, publish capabilities and availability, attach REST, A2A or MCP endpoint metadata, prove endpoint domain control with DNS TXT challenges and establish ES256/P-256 machine identity for signed requests. The network exposes a REST API (OpenAPI 3.1, 68 operations), an A2A v1.0 meta-agent (JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON) for agent search, Agent Card validation and network status, and a set of /.well-known discovery documents. Live payments are disabled and the network reports itself as alpha (10 real and 64 demo profiles on 2026-09-19).
d.name: Direct Hire

d.description: Direct Line Group is a United Kingdom personal-lines and small-commercial general insurance carrier, founded in 1985 as the UK's first telephone-only motor insurer and listed on the London Stock Exchange from its 2012 IPO until Aviva plc completed its GBP 3.7 billion acquisition of the group on 1 July 2025. The group underwrites motor, home, pet, travel, landlord, breakdown and small-business insurance through the Direct Line, Churchill, Privilege, Darwin, By Miles, Direct Line for Business and Green Flag brands, and is regulated in its home market by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority. Its distribution is direct-to-consumer via telephone and web plus price-comparison-website placement (notably through the Darwin brand), rather than through broker or agency channels; it sold its brokered commercial business (NIG and FarmWeb) to RSA in September 2023, closing the one channel that would have carried standards-based broker integration. Its API posture is accordingly closed and partner-gated: as of 25 July 2026 the corporate domain directlinegroup.co.uk returns HTTP 301 to aviva.com, there is no developer.*, developers.* or docs.* host in DNS, every consumer brand site returns 404 on /developers, /api and /partners, and the only API host that exists — api.directlinegroup.co.uk, resolving to a MuleSoft Anypoint production load balancer — serves HTTP 403 behind an expired TLS certificate and requests a client certificate during the TLS handshake. There is no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI, no GraphQL, no published webhook or event catalog, no public Postman workspace, and no ACORD reference anywhere in the group's public material. Quote, bind, issue and FNOL are all consumer web and telephone journeys only.
d.name: Direct Line Group

d.description: Direct Revenue was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead. A July 2026 enrichment pass found no live corporate or developer surface for this company: directrevenue.com resolves to an Efty domain-for-sale parking lander (domain registered 2002, held at Tucows, listed for sale); direct-revenue.com is a squatted domain that 302-redirects to baidu.com; directrevenue.co returns Cloudflare 522 (origin unreachable); and directrevenue.net, directrevenue.ai and getdirectrevenue.com do not resolve at all. There is no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no matching provider in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical lead record only and carries no API artifacts.
d.name: Direct Revenue

d.description: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) leads intelligence integration across the United States Intelligence Community. The DNI serves as head of the IC, principal intelligence adviser to the President, and oversees and coordinates the foreign and domestic activities of the 18 IC elements. ODNI houses the National Counterterrorism Center, the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, the Office of Economic Security and Emerging Technologies, the Mission Integration and Policy & Capabilities directorates, and the IC Inspector General. ODNI publishes no developer program and no machine-readable specification of its own; its public content — newsroom press releases, remarks, interviews, the Annual Threat Assessment, the annual IC transparency reports, IC directives and NCTC counterterrorism guides — is served from a WordPress site at www.odni.gov whose REST API answers anonymously and is catalogued here.
d.name: Director of National Intelligence

d.description: DirectTap is a zero‑commission restaurant ordering platform that enables independent restaurants to accept online orders directly from customers, keeping 100% of the sale. Founded in 2024 by Tahir Hussain and Tushar Kale under Unoecom Inc, DirectTap provides each restaurant with its own branded ordering page, customer relationship tools, and a marketplace‑free experience. The service aims to eliminate the 20‑30% fees charged by third‑party delivery apps, helping local eateries retain revenue and build direct customer connections. The platform is SaaS‑based, offering registration, menu management, and order processing without hidden fees.
d.name: DirectTap

d.description: Open-source data platform that wraps any SQL database with a REST and GraphQL API, auto-generated from the schema, plus a no-code admin app for data management. Directus turns any new or existing SQL database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MS SQL, OracleDB, CockroachDB) into an instant REST and GraphQL API with a visual Data Studio for non-technical users. The platform includes policy-based access control, an automation engine (Flows), a built-in AI assistant, digital asset management, real-time WebSockets, and an MCP server for AI agent integration. Deployable as a self-hosted open-source project or as Directus Cloud.
d.name: Directus

d.description: Dirig Software, Inc. was a Nashua, New Hampshire software company that built application and system management software for eBusiness — agent-based performance monitoring and automated problem correction for J2EE application servers (WebLogic, WebSphere), web infrastructure, and hosted service-provider environments, sold both direct to enterprises and through OEM and service-provider channels. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures. Its web presence at dirig.com carried full product, partner, and support content through roughly 2003, degraded to a broken holding page under the name "Dirig Corporation" from early 2004, and by late 2006 the domain was a parked Sedo for-sale page. As of this enrichment pass the company has no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind; dirig.com now resolves to an unrelated third-party endpoint returning a bare "OK" health response. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network — there is nothing to enrich and nothing to score.
d.name: Dirig Software

d.description: DiscGenics is a privately held, late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, developing allogeneic, cell-based regenerative biologic therapies for degenerative diseases of the spine. Its lead candidate, IDCT (rebonuputemcel), is a single-injection allogeneic discogenic progenitor cell therapy for symptomatic mild-to-moderate lumbar degenerative disc disease, manufactured under cGMP from donated adult human intervertebral disc tissue and granted FDA Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) and Fast Track designations. The company is running a US Phase III program (the PIVOT and CONFIRM studies) alongside a clinical study in Japan. DiscGenics is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.
d.name: DiscGenics

d.description: Structured disc golf course data
d.name: DiscGolf

d.description: DiscGolfAPI is a free, read-only public API that publishes structured JSON data about disc golf courses for developers, clubs, publishers, apps, and AI systems. It provides machine-readable course records with names, locations, countries, regions, hole counts where known, coordinates where available, operational and access fields, confidence and verification signals, update timestamps, and attribution/licence metadata. DiscGolfAPI is infrastructure and reference data — not a review site, rating platform, or social network.
d.name: DiscGolfAPI

d.description: Disclo is a workplace-accommodations software platform that powers end-to-end management of ADA, FMLA, and state-leave requests, medical-certification verification, and the interactive accommodation process for employers. The HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant portal automates accommodation workflows and compliance documentation, adds AI-assisted medical-certification review (Disclo Verify) and candidate accommodations for recruiting (Disclo Hire), and integrates with 50+ HRIS and ATS systems. Disclo is a private B2B SaaS company backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst; it operates a secure customer portal (secure.disclo.com) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. Access is enterprise, demo/sales-led rather than self-serve.
d.name: Disclo

d.description: Disclosure Requirements are the regulatory and legal obligations for organizations to reveal specific information to stakeholders, regulators, and the public. These requirements span financial disclosures (SEC, IFRS), sustainability and ESG reporting (CSRD, ESRS, IFRS S1/S2, TCFD, GRI, SASB), privacy notices (GDPR, CCPA), and corporate governance, helping ensure transparency and accountability across markets and jurisdictions.
d.name: Disclosure Requirements
