f.description: Facilio is a connected operations platform for facility, property, and asset management, built around an AI-powered CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System). It unifies maintenance teams, vendors, tenants, and building systems so operators can run work orders, service requests, assets, inventory, purchasing, and portfolio data across multi-site real estate at scale. The platform spans Connected CMMS, the Atom AI suite, Connected Buildings (energy and sustainability), and Connected Refrigeration (IoT monitoring). Facilio exposes a versioned REST API (v5), a FOQL SQL-like query language, embeddable Connected Apps, and a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so ERP, accounting, BMS, IoT, CRM, and reporting systems — and AI agents — can query and act on operational data using the caller's existing Facilio permissions. Facilio serves retail chains, healthcare, commercial real estate portfolios, FM service providers, and education across US, EU, UK, AU, AE, and SA regions.
f.name: Facilio

f.description: Fact Base Inc. (株式会社Fact Base) is a Japanese manufacturing-technology company on a mission to make manufacturing seamless by driving the digitization of small and mid-sized factories (町工場). Its corporate site presents the company mission and vision for connecting Japan's fragmented small-factory manufacturing base through digital tooling. Surfaced through the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation is published on the corporate domain.
f.name: Fact Base

f.description: Factiva is Dow Jones' business information and research service, providing licensed access to a global news and data archive drawn from more than 33,000 sources across 200 countries and 28 languages. Its API suite lets organizations search and retrieve licensed articles, run one-time historical extractions (Snapshots), subscribe to real-time filtered news streams over Google Cloud Pub/Sub, resolve the ~350,000-code Dow Jones Intelligent Identifiers taxonomy of companies, industries, regions and news subjects, and feed copyright-compliant content into retrieval-augmented generation stacks. Access is contract-based: there is no self-service signup and no published pricing, and credentials are issued by Dow Jones after a trial request.
f.name: Factiva

f.description: Factorial is an all-in-one HR, payroll, time, talent, finance, and IT management platform headquartered in Barcelona, Spain, used by 16,000+ companies worldwide. The Factorial public API is a date-versioned REST API (current major 2026-04-01 "Legendre") covering employees, contracts, attendance, time off, payroll, ATS, performance, trainings, projects, finance, banking, procurement, IT assets, documents, webhooks, and an Approvals workflow surface. Authentication uses OAuth2 (on behalf of a user) or an x-api-key header (on behalf of the company), with 30+ scopes for granular partner access. Factorial publishes the OpenAPI schema and generated SDKs (Ruby, Python, Java, PHP, TypeScript, Node.js) at github.com/factorialco/oas and exposes an llms.txt index for AI agents.
f.name: Factorial

f.description: Factory is an agent-native software development platform whose Droids act as autonomous AI engineers that plan, execute, and maintain code work across CLI, desktop app, IDE plugins, and cloud. The product is B2B sales-led with a public Droid SDK (TypeScript), Droid Exec for CI/CD, a plugin marketplace, and MCP support. No public REST API surface is documented as of May 2026 - integration happens through the Droid CLI, SDK, and Droid GitHub Action.
f.name: Factory

f.description: FACTORY I/O is a software simulation tool that allows users to create and simulate industrial automation systems in a virtual environment. It provides a realistic and interactive platform for training, testing, and troubleshooting automation processes without the need for physical equipment. Users can design their own control systems, program PLCs, and observe the behavior of machines and processes in real-time.
f.name: FACTORY I/O

f.description: Factory OS (styled Factory_OS) is an off-site construction company founded in 2017 by Rick Holliday and Larry Pace that industrialized multifamily and affordable housing production on an assembly line inside a 275,000-square-foot facility in Building 680 on Mare Island in Vallejo, California. Union carpenters build wood-frame housing modules across roughly two dozen stations in a 33-step process, and the finished modules are trucked to the project site and assembled — an approach the company says cuts production time by about half and production cost by a quarter against conventional site-built construction. It raised roughly $132 million across three rounds, including $60 million from JPMorgan Chase and Saint-Gobain in 2021, and delivered more than 4,000 homes across California and Hawaii, about 90 percent of them affordable housing. In May 2024 the company was recapitalized and renamed Harbinger Homes (legal entity Harbinger Production Inc.), with Tom Smith as CEO and Kevin Brown as president; factoryos.com now 301-redirects every path to harbinger.homes. Harbinger filed a WARN notice on 12 February 2026 covering all 280 employees, citing a lack of new business and loss of capital funding, with layoffs beginning 13 April 2026. Factory OS is a manufacturer of physical housing modules, not a software company: it operates no developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its GitHub organization has no public repositories.
f.name: Factory OS

f.description: Factory Works (Factory Berlin) is a Berlin-based venture-building and company-builder firm that partners with entrepreneurs, visual artists, and musicians to turn early ideas into scalable businesses. Positioning itself as a "neo company builder," Factory builds and scales ventures in exchange for equity while handling strategy, product, brand, marketing, legal, accounting, and operations, and it runs a physical Berlin venue with event, restaurant, and studio infrastructure alongside a mentor and investor network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Factory publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform, so this profile carries company identity only.
f.name: Factory Works

f.description: Factris is a European fintech that provides invoice financing (factoring) for small and medium-sized enterprises, converting unpaid B2B invoices into working capital within 24 hours. Its services span invoice financing, debtor management and collections, credit insurance, and credit-risk assessment, delivered through the self-service FAB platform where customers upload invoices and track payments. Factris operates across the Netherlands, Lithuania, and other European markets and has financed over two billion euros in receivables. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is being enriched in the API Evangelist network; Factris publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.
f.name: Factris

f.description: FactSet creates flexible, open data and software solutions for tens of thousands of investment professionals around the world, providing instant access to financial data and analytics that investors use to make crucial decisions.
f.name: Factset

f.description: Factual Inc. was a Los Angeles-based location-data company (backed by a16z, DCVC and Index Ventures) that operated the Global Places database and Geopulse audience/location APIs, giving developers programmatic access to a worldwide catalog of business points of interest, categories, attributes and geotagged mobile audience data. Factual was acquired by and merged into Foursquare in 2020; factual.com now redirects to foursquare.com and the standalone Factual Places/Geopulse API has been discontinued. This profile preserves the historical first-party client drivers (Java, Python, Node.js, Clojure) still published in their package registries and captured as real artifacts in the API Evangelist network.
f.name: Factual

f.description: Facturama is a cloud-based Mexican electronic invoicing (CFDI) platform that lets businesses generate, stamp, download, and cancel digital tax receipts (Comprobante Fiscal Digital por Internet) through a REST API. It serves 55,000+ clients — mostly SMEs and startups — and exposes two API products: API Web (single issuer, tied to a Facturama account) and API Multiemisor (multi-issuer, for platforms that invoice on behalf of many taxpayers). The API supports CFDI 4.0 invoices, payroll receipts (nómina), payment complements (complemento de pago), credit notes, Carta Porte (cargo/transport), foreign trade (comercio exterior), and donation receipts, plus management of clients, products/services, branch offices, series, and SAT catalogs (postal codes, currencies, payment methods, tax regimes). Authentication is HTTP Basic. A sandbox environment and 15 free test invoices during a 30-day trial are available, along with first-party SDKs for PHP, Java, .NET, Node.js, JavaScript, Python, and Ruby and a public Postman collection.
f.name: Facturama

f.description: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED is a Saudi Arabian holding company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at fai.sa is a WordPress property served from nginx behind a WAF that returns HTTP 403 to every external request except /robots.txt, so no company description, developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be retrieved during the enrichment pass. No public API, specification, SDK, or event surface has been observed to date; the domain-security posture was probed successfully and is recorded in security/. Re-probe from an allowed network on a later round to confirm whether a developer surface exists behind the block.
f.name: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED

f.description: The mission of the Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity (FHEO) is to eliminate housing discrimination, promote economic opportunity, and achieve diverse, inclusive communities by leading the nation in the enforcement, administration, development, and public understanding of federal fair housing policies and laws. FHEO administers the Fair Housing Assistance Program (FHAP) and the Fair Housing Initiatives Program (FHIP), enforces Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act, and owns the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) rule and its Data and Mapping Tool. FHEO does not run a developer portal of its own; its program data is published as anonymously callable ArcGIS REST feature services inside HUD's ArcGIS Online organization and through the HUD Open Data site, and its AFFH-T map and report services run on HUD's eGIS ArcGIS Server.
f.name: Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity

f.description: Fairbanc (PT Fairbanc Technologies Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based digital finance platform that uses AI/ML-powered credit scoring to deliver embedded, revolving supply-chain financing and buy-now-pay-later "terms of payment" to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across Indonesia. Working with trusted financial institutions and distributor/supply-chain ecosystems, Fairbanc provides merchants with an instant digital facility limit and short-term working-capital liquidity at the point of purchase — with no formal loan application, smartphone, or app required — plus data intelligence and consulting that help distributors reduce bad-debt risk and grow transaction value. The company reports its terms-of-payment product drove roughly 35% distributor sales growth. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fairbanc publishes a consumer-facing marketing and onboarding site but no public developer/API program at this time.
f.name: Fairbanc

f.description: Faircraft is a biotechnology company creating a new class of cultivated materials, starting with real leather grown in the lab from animal cells rather than raised on farms. Using cell biology and protein engineering, it produces genuine leather (product lines FCL_001 through FCL_006) with the look, feel, and performance of traditional hides but with a lower environmental footprint and no animal farming, and customizable properties for fashion, automotive, and luxury brands. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Faircraft is a materials-science company with no public developer or API surface at this time.
f.name: Faircraft

f.description: Faire is a wholesale marketplace connecting independent retailers with brands. The Faire External API v2 supports both sides of the marketplace: brand-side endpoints for products, orders, inventory, and shipments, and retailer-side endpoints for browsing and ordering.
f.name: Faire

f.description: Fairlyne is a French travel-technology company offering a white-label Resale-as-a-Service platform that lets travel brands turn no-shows and low-yield bookings into new revenue by allowing passengers and guests to resell non-refundable tickets and reservations. Founded in 2021 by former Accor executives Gilles de Richemond and Michael d'Eboli, the platform serves airlines, railway and road-transport operators, and hospitality chains, and powers programs such as SNCF Ouigo's resale experience. Fairlyne raised a 3M EUR seed round from Speedinvest, Kima Ventures, Evolem, and FJ Labs. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Fairlyne. No public developer API or documentation portal has been identified at this time.
f.name: Fairlyne

f.description: Fairmarkit is an autonomous sourcing and strategic procurement platform that uses AI agents to automate the full sourcing lifecycle — from intake and request creation through RFQ/RFP/RFI events, supplier bidding, award, and purchase-order handoff to ERP and P2P systems. Fairmarkit publishes a public, OpenAPI 3.1-described Buyer Self-Service REST API (v3 and v4) and a Supplier Public API, secured with an X-FM-API-KEY header, covering RFQ/RFP events, requests and request items, suppliers, purchase orders, price books, datasets/data fields, business units, categories, identities, permission sets, data exports, and file attachments, plus a rich webhook notification catalog for procurement events. The company is backed by GGV Capital and Insight Partners.
f.name: Fairmarkit

f.description: FairMoney is a credit-led digital bank for emerging markets, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Paris, France, with operating subsidiaries in Nigeria and India. The company began life as a France-incubated micro- lending app and pivoted to focus on Africa, becoming one of the largest digital lenders in Nigeria after the Central Bank of Nigeria granted its subsidiary a Microfinance Bank (MfB) license. FairMoney's consumer mobile app offers near-instant collateral-free personal loans, FlexiCredit, asset finance, savings products (FairLock, FairSave, FairTarget, FairDollar), a current account, debit cards, bill payments, and peer-to-peer transfers. Its Business Banking arm extends current accounts, payments, and credit to Nigerian SMEs. In India, FairMoney operates as a digital lender disbursing small-ticket personal loans through its mobile app. FairMoney does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a third-party developer portal; integration is internal and partner- driven, and the company's only public technical surface is its engineering GitHub organization, which mirrors infrastructure-as-code and open-source tooling forks (Terraform AWS modules, GitHub Actions, rubocop, puma plugins, salesforce_bulk_api) rather than a product API.
f.name: FairMoney

f.description: FairPay Ltd. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: FairPay Ltd.

f.description: Fairplay is a Mexican fintech offering flexible, collateral-free business financing for e-commerce sellers, marketplaces, retailers, and wholesalers. Its products include revolving credit lines (MXN 2-30 million), invoice advances/factoring, and working-capital financing, underwritten from a company's sales and analytics data with offers issued in as little as 48 hours through a 100% digital process. Fairplay operates as a Sociedad Financiera de Objeto Multiple, Entidad No Regulada (SOFOM E.N.R.) under Mexican CNBV and CONDUSEF supervision and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and Speedinvest. Fairplay serves financing and account data to customers through a private insights dashboard; no public developer API is currently published.
f.name: Fairplay

f.description: Fake Store API is a tool that allows users to access a database of fake products, customers, and orders. Users can use the API to generate test data for their e-commerce applications or to practice integrating with external APIs. The Fake Store API provides a simple and easy-to-use interface for retrieving information such as product details, customer information, and order history.
f.name: Fake Store API

f.description: Service to generate test and fake data
f.name: FakeJSON

f.description: FakerAPI is a free, no-authentication REST API that returns realistic fake data for developers, designers, and QA engineers. Built on top of the PHP Faker library by Alessandro Pietrantonio, it exposes a uniform set of GET endpoints for addresses, books, companies, images, persons, places, products, texts, users, and a fully custom resource builder. Every endpoint accepts the same three control parameters (_quantity, _locale, _seed) and returns the same envelope, making it trivial to use for prototypes, mock servers, workshop fixtures, and integration tests.
f.name: FakerAPI

f.description: Fakespot was an AI-powered fake-review detection service, founded in 2016, that graded the trustworthiness of product reviews on Amazon and other online marketplaces through a browser extension, mobile apps, and website. Mozilla acquired Fakespot in 2023 and integrated its technology into Firefox as the Review Checker. Mozilla discontinued the product in 2025 — the Firefox Review Checker on June 10, 2025 and the Fakespot browser extension, mobile apps, and website on July 1, 2025 — and fakespot.com now redirects to a Mozilla announcement. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface exists; this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.
f.name: Fakespot

f.description: Faks is a French SaaS platform that digitizes and streamlines the commercial relationships across the pharmacy ecosystem. It gives pharmacies, pharmacy groups (groupements), and laboratories a single place to manage supplier relationships, commercial claims and disputes (litiges), expired and returnable product handling, promotions, and sell-in / sell-out performance. Faks connects to pharmacy management systems (LGO), purchasing platforms, and accounting tools through its Konnect integrations to automate what has traditionally been manual, paper, and email-driven work between the ~18,000 pharmacies, ~100 groups, and ~500 laboratories it targets in France. The company is backed by Seedcamp. Faks does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the enrichment surfaces that could be probed.
f.name: Faks

f.description: fal (Features and Labels, Inc.) is a generative media platform providing the world's fastest API for running image, video, audio, and multimodal generative AI models. Through a unified queue-based REST API at https://queue.fal.run, plus realtime WebSocket and SSE streaming surfaces, fal serves 1,000+ production models — including FLUX, Veo 3, Kling, Wan, Seedream, Nano Banana, and Stable Diffusion — on autoscaling GPU infrastructure. fal Serverless lets developers ship custom models with `@fal.function` / `fal.App` / BYO containers, while fal Compute provides dedicated H100/H200/A100/B200 instances. Trusted by Canva, Perplexity, Poe, and 1.5M+ developers; Series D funded ($140M, Sequoia-led, December 2025); SOC 2 with 99.99% uptime.
f.name: fal

f.description: Falco is a cloud-native runtime security tool that detects unexpected application behavior and alerts on threats at runtime using eBPF. It is a CNCF graduated project that continuously monitors Linux kernel syscalls and compares them against configurable security rules to detect intrusions, privilege escalation, and other suspicious behaviors.
f.name: Falco

f.description: Falcon (Falcon Financial Services, falconfs.com) is a global embedded-finance and Banking-as-a-Service platform that lets fintechs, banks, and enterprises launch credit and payment products in days rather than months. Its developer-first REST APIs and no-code tooling cover the full issuance and lending lifecycle: issuer and program onboarding, enterprise and user KYC, credit-card issuance (virtual, physical, add-on, co-branded, corporate), accounts and credit limits, transactions, statements, repayments and auto-debit, EMI conversion and amortisation, disputes, rewards, interest, fees, funding, and reconciliations. Falcon holds its own lending and issuance licenses, is built on a modular multi-tenant architecture, and is certified against PCI DSS, ISO 27001:2022, and SOC 2. Product lines include Falcon CardFX (issuance), CreditFX (lending), WalletFX (prepaid/wallets), and SurgeFX (AI growth and portfolio tools).
f.name: Falcon

f.description: FalconX is an institutional digital-asset prime brokerage that provides trading, credit and financing, custody, and market-access services to banks, asset managers, hedge funds, and other financial institutions. The platform offers spot, derivatives, options, and FX execution across 400+ tokens via an OTC desk, an execution-management system, and direct market access (DMA) with cross-margining and one-click borrowing, alongside margin loans, structured products, staking, and ETF liquidity provision. FalconX exposes a REST trading API (api.falconx.io) for price quotes, order execution, trade history, balances, transfers, and trade limits, documented publicly on a Stoplight developer portal and monitored via an Atlassian status page. FalconX entities are regulated as a CFTC-registered swap dealer and a Malta MFSA crypto-asset service provider.
f.name: FalconX

f.description: Fama is an AI-powered social media and online screening platform for employment decisions. Its REST API lets HR platforms and background-screening providers submit candidate checks and retrieve behavioral findings — flagged posts, web content, and social profiles — mapped to workplace-misconduct categories across 30+ languages while filtering out protected-class information for EEOC/FCRA-aligned adjudication. Reports are delivered via completion callbacks or polling as JSON or a signed PDF, powering pre-employment screening (Fama Plus), comprehensive candidate assessment (Fama 360), and ongoing employee monitoring (Fama Pulse).
f.name: Fama

f.description: Famebit was an influencer-marketing marketplace, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that connected YouTube, Instagram, and Vine creators with brands for sponsored branded-content campaigns. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), it was acquired by Google in October 2016, rebranded as "FameBit by YouTube," and later folded into YouTube BrandConnect. The standalone platform has been shut down and famebit.com now redirects to a Google/YouTube Help support page, so there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.
f.name: Famebit

f.description: Family Dollar is a chain of discount variety stores in the United States offering a broad assortment of merchandise in the $1 to $10 range, including consumables, household and home products, apparel, seasonal goods and electronics. Stores are concentrated in neighborhood locations and in food deserts where other retailers do not operate. Dollar Tree, Inc. divested the Family Dollar business on 7 July 2025 to Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management; Family Dollar now operates as a standalone private retailer headquartered in Chesapeake, Virginia, and also runs the Chesapeake Media Group retail media network. Family Dollar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, webhook catalog or agent surface: contract discovery on 2026-09-07 probed every well-known and specification path across www.familydollar.com, corporate.familydollar.com and careers.familydollar.com and returned no machine-readable contract of any kind.
f.name: Family Dollar Stores

f.description: Family First is an employee caregiving benefits provider that pairs certified Care Experts with a Care Hub mobile app to support working caregivers. The platform helps employers, health plans, and small businesses deliver caregiving advocacy, backup and subsidized care, and expert guidance across aging-parent care, mental health, chronic illness, caregiver burnout, fertility, childcare, veterans support, end-of-life planning, and financial and legal planning. The company operates under SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST i1, HIPAA, CCPA, and GDPR frameworks and is Techstars-backed. Family First does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security posture.
f.name: Family First

f.description: FamilyLeaf was a private social network for families, launched in 2012 and marketed as "a place to share your life with your family" — a closed, invite-based space for sharing photos and updates among relatives rather than a public feed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-20 found no operating company: familyleaf.com is registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2027-03-09) but delegated to no nameservers at all, so it has no A record, no mail, no website and no API surface. The last live archived snapshot of the product (2014) carries a banner announcing that FamilyLeaf had become part of Origami; by the 2023 archived snapshot the domain was serving a registrar parking page. There is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, GitHub organization, or any other API artifact to capture. This profile is retained as a historical company record.
f.name: FamilyLeaf

f.description: Famous (famous.co) returns a 301 to Amaze (amaze.co), the creator-commerce platform operated by Amaze Holdings, Inc. Amaze describes itself as building the operating system for creator-led businesses, bringing commerce, content, media, and live shopping into one connected ecosystem. Its products include Amaze Commerce (creator storefronts and AI-powered product creation, at amazecommerce.com), Spring (spri.ng, the creator storefront brand formerly known as Teespring), Amaze Live (shoppable livestreams), and Amaze Media (performance marketing and audience targeting for brands). The company reports 190K+ creators, 1.7B+ lifetime fan reach, and operations across 183 countries. Surfaced originally as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. A public, machine-readable API surface WAS found on the second enrichment pass: the Spring Seller API, a Swagger 2.0 contract with 24 operations served live at api.teespring.com (Spring's legacy API host), documented behind a Swagger UI at https://api.teespring.com/docs. Amaze also publishes first-party Protobuf/gRPC service contracts to npm under the @teespring scope.
f.name: Famous

f.description: The First API 100% Dedicated to Family Travel. Designed for developers, travel apps, and businesses, the Famxplor API delivers personalized, family-focused recommendations tested and loved by real families. Seamlessly integrate to provide location-based activities, global travel ideas, and engaging content that enhances user experiences and engagement. Famxplor offers tiered pricing from Starter ($4.99/mo) to Enterprise (custom), with a 14-day free trial.
f.name: Famxplor Family Travel API

f.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.
f.name: Fan Controlled Football

f.description: Fanatics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of softbank-vision-fund, thrive-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Fanatics

f.description: Fanbread is a defunct venture-backed company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Its primary domain fanbread.com no longer resolves to a live site — the HTTPS handshake fails and HTTP returns 410 Gone from a parking host — and no website, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable API surface remains anywhere. The company's GitHub organization survives under the login FanBread but is now titled "Wild Sky Media FnB" and points at wildskymedia.com; its seven public repositories are forks and small front-end utilities with no first-party API artifacts and no activity since April 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record and a dead-domain marker, not as an active API provider.
f.name: Fanbread

f.description: FanBridge was an email and SMS marketing platform for musicians, artists, bands, and creators, letting them grow and message their fan mailing lists, run newsletters, and capture subscribers from shows and social channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirmed FanBridge is defunct - it was acquired by Kit (formerly ConvertKit) and ceased operations on April 11, 2022, with active accounts migrated to the Kit platform. The domain fanbridge.com now 302-redirects to kit.com/fanbridge. There is no standalone FanBridge developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface; the developer docs linked from the destination site belong to Kit, not FanBridge.
f.name: Fanbridge

f.description: FanCraze is an International Cricket Council (ICC) officially licensed platform for cricket collectibles, trading, and fantasy gaming, serving more than 500,000 cricket fans worldwide. Its flagship products are Grails, a digital collectibles experience where fans pull officially licensed ICC player cards (Common through Legendary), trade them with other fans, and complete themed sets; and Matchday, a free-to-play fantasy cricket game where fans build squads from their collectibles and compete on live challenges tied to real ICC tournaments including Men's and Women's Cricket World Cups, T20 World Cups, and U-19 World Cups. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and is backed by investors including Tiger Global, Sequoia, Coatue, Dapper Labs, and Coinbase Ventures. FanCraze operates as a consumer (B2C) mobile and web app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.
f.name: FanCraze

f.description: Fancy Technology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Fancy Technology

f.description: Fandango is a leading online ticketing platform for movies, offering users the ability to browse showtimes, purchase tickets, and discover entertainment content. The company provides a consumer-facing website and mobile apps, and exposes APIs for partners to integrate ticketing, pricing, and promotional features into their services. Fandango’s services include movie listings, theater information, ticket sales, gift cards, and loyalty programs, serving millions of moviegoers across the United States.
f.name: Fandango

f.description: Fandom (formerly Wikia) is the world's largest entertainment fan-wiki platform, hosting hundreds of thousands of community-run wikis covering television, film, games, anime, and pop culture. Every Fandom wiki runs on MediaWiki (currently 1.43.9, PHP 8.3) and exposes the standard MediaWiki Action API at /api.php on each wiki subdomain, giving programmatic read and write access to page content, revisions, full-text and OpenSearch search, media files, templates, and account operations. Fandom layers its own extension modules on top of core MediaWiki (create-new-wiki, theme designer, interactive maps, portable infoboxes, embedded video, notifications). Fandom does not publish a bespoke OpenAPI; the self-documenting api.php help endpoint, the Fandom Developers Wiki (dev.fandom.com), and the upstream MediaWiki API docs are the reference surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched from Fandom's live, public API.
f.name: Fandom

f.description: FanDuel is a major US sports betting and daily fantasy sports operator (FanDuel Sportsbook, FanDuel Casino, FanDuel Fantasy, FanDuel TV). FanDuel does not publish a public developer REST API for its sportsbook, casino, or fantasy products. Internal/private APIs power the apps and a Sportradar/SBTech-derived trading stack but are not available to third-party developers.
f.name: FanDuel

f.description: FangTek (Shanghai Fangtek Electronics Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Shanghai. It designs highly integrated analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits for mobile phones, portable devices and consumer electronics, with a product line spanning audio power amplifiers, voice and audio processing, image processing, LED drivers, power management ICs, analog switches and DC boost converters. Qiming Venture Partners lists FangTek in its portfolio as "a leading provider of highly integrated circuit solutions for cell phone, portable device, voice processing, audio processing and image processing." FangTek is a silicon component vendor that reaches customers through electronics distributors; it publishes no public developer platform, web API, SDK or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.
f.name: FangTek

f.description: Fanhouse was a creator-subscription social platform, backed by a16z, that let fans pay creators directly for exclusive posts, photos, and community access rather than through ad-driven feeds. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The original product operated at fanhouse.app, which no longer resolves to the company (it now redirects to an unrelated domain), indicating the a16z-backed platform is defunct. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be located for the original Fanhouse product, so no scored API artifacts could be produced without fabrication. This profile is retained as a company/lead record.
f.name: Fanhouse

f.description: Fanimal was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Re-verified on 2026-07-20, the primary domain fanimal.com remains a parked, Cloudflare-fronted redirect — every path probed (root, /llms.txt, /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/api-catalog, and the api./developer./docs. subdomains) returns HTTP 301 to https://tickpick.com/?fanimal=y. The ?fanimal=y attribution marker on a redirect into a ticket-resale marketplace indicates the property is defunct or has been absorbed by TickPick. No package was found on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, or crates.io; the github.com/Fanimal organization exists but is empty (0 public repos, no profile metadata) and cannot be verified as the same company. No independent Fanimal API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or reachable /.well-known/ surface exists to enrich; there is no spec-bearing developer surface to ground any artifact against. The registered domain is still administered (live TLS, HSTS, SES SPF, Google and Klaviyo site-verification TXT records), which is captured in the probed domain-security artifact.
f.name: Fanimal

f.description: fanli (返利网, fanli.com) is a Chinese cashback and shopping-rewards platform that aggregates promotions, coupons, and rebate offers across major online retailers, letting consumers earn money back on purchases they route through the site. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, fanli.com is a live consumer-facing web property; no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API definition, /.well-known discovery surface, llms.txt, or published security/vulnerability-disclosure program was found.
f.name: fanli

f.description: Fannie Mae, officially known as the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a government-sponsored enterprise that plays a critical role in the American housing market. Established in 1938, Fannie Mae operates as a secondary mortgage lender, purchasing mortgages from banks and other financial institutions. By buying these loans, Fannie Mae helps to provide liquidity to the mortgage market, enabling banks to lend more money to homebuyers. Fannie Mae operates a developer portal that hosts API integrations for mortgage industry partners; access typically requires authenticated business relationships.
f.name: Fannie Mae

f.description: Fantasmo builds CPS (Camera Positioning System), a computer-vision positioning technology it positions as a "camera-powered GPS replacement" delivering hyper-accurate localization that works indoors and in dense urban environments where satellite GPS degrades, using only a device camera and a data connection rather than additional infrastructure. Its target applications span micromobility (scooter/bike tracking and theft prevention), robotics navigation, mobile augmented-reality experiences, and automotive lane-level positioning. Fantasmo was a Techstars-backed startup and was acquired by Niantic in 2022; the public fantasmo.io site remains online but exposes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at this time. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web presence and live DNS/TLS/HTTP probes.
f.name: Fantasmo

f.description: Fantasy Akhada is an Indian daily-fantasy-sports platform operated by Super Six Sports Gaming Private Limited (CIN U72900HR2019PTC083570) of Gurugram, Haryana, founded in 2020 by Amit Purohit, Sumit Kumar Jha, Sahil Ahuja, Amit Bhardwaj and Ankit Upreti, with cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle as brand ambassador. Users build virtual teams for real cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey fixtures and enter free and cash contests, with the platform taking a commission on entry fees; it marketed itself on the lowest commission rates in the category and claimed 3.5 to 4 million registered users. The product shipped only as a consumer iOS app and a sideloaded Android APK plus a React single-page web lobby - there is no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal of any kind, and none has ever been published. As of the August 2026 probe the brand's own web presence is broken: www.fantasyakhada.com is a dangling CNAME to a deleted AWS ap-south-1 load balancer, the apex carries no address record, every backend service host referenced by the company's own JavaScript bundles has been withdrawn from DNS, and only stale static CloudFront/S3 builds remain. India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 banned real-money online games nationwide in August 2025.
f.name: Fantasy Akhada

f.description: Fantiger is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Fantiger

f.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.
f.name: FANUC

f.description: TeamUp Inc. operates fanZ (fanzapp.io), a gamified football (soccer) fan-engagement mobile app for iOS and Android. fanZ combines fantasy football (fantaZ), social following of teams, leagues and players, prediction challenges and mini-games, a rewards system of points, badges and digital collectibles, an official merchandise store, and global leaderboards, plus news, match highlights and video content. The product is a consumer-facing mobile application operated by Wathbah for Information Technology and backed by 500 Global; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment.
f.name: fanZ

f.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations operates FAOSTAT, the world's largest freely accessible database for food and agriculture statistics. FAOSTAT provides REST APIs for programmatic access to agricultural production data, food security indicators, trade flows, land use, environmental indicators, food balances, and prices covering 180+ countries from 1961 to present across 70+ thematic domains.
f.name: FAO FAOSTAT

f.description: Faqtor, Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Faqtor

f.description: Faraday Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a Seattle, Washington clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 as a spinout of Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, built on the elemental-reducing-agent research of Dr. Mark Roth. It developed therapies intended to prevent and treat cardiac and skeletal muscle loss after acute critical illness, led by FDY-5301 — a proprietary intravenous formulation of sodium iodide designed to neutralize reactive oxygen species and limit reperfusion injury in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The company raised roughly $120M from an investor group led by ARCH Venture Partners and Polaris Partners. Its Phase 3 trial read out in late 2025 and failed to meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and Faraday announced in February 2026 that it had ceased operations and was winding down the business. Faraday never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its faradaypharma.com website is no longer served. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
f.name: Faraday Pharmaceuticals

f.description: Faraway is a web3 gaming company building an interoperable gaming ecosystem for players, creators, and studios. Its platform lets game studios integrate player-driven, blockchain-based economies into their titles across EVM-compatible chains and Solana, with a unified player identity and wallet (id.faraway.com), a creator platform for user-generated content and monetization (create.faraway.com), and an in-game marketplace and secondary-trading shop (shop.faraway.com). Faraway publishes a developer platform with an API reference and an llms.txt index at docs.faraway.com. The company is backed by a16z, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Pantera Capital.
f.name: Faraway

f.description: Farcaster is a decentralised social protocol built on Snapchain, an append-only state machine that stores casts, reactions, follows, and user profile data. The protocol publishes a Hub / Snapchain reference implementation, the Mini Apps SDK (formerly Frames) for distributing interactive apps inside Farcaster feeds, Sign In with Farcaster (SIWF) for authentication, and AuthKit for React-based sign-in. The Warpcast client (now rebranded Farcaster app at farcaster.xyz) is the primary consumer surface. Indexer providers such as Neynar host scaled Hub APIs and value-added read / write / webhook APIs at api.neynar.com.
f.name: Farcaster

f.description: FareHarbor provides online booking software for tours, activities, rentals, and attractions, enabling businesses to manage reservations, payments, and customer experiences through a scalable, cloud‑based platform. The solution supports multi‑channel sales, staff management, reporting, and integrations with partners, aiming to simplify operations for tour operators and activity providers worldwide.
f.name: FareHarbor

f.description: Farfetch is a global luxury fashion technology platform and online marketplace connecting consumers with boutiques, brands, and department stores across more than 190 countries, offering designer womenswear, menswear, kidswear, shoes, bags, and accessories. Beyond its consumer marketplace, Farfetch historically operated a B2B arm, Farfetch Platform Solutions (FPS), providing e-commerce, fulfilment, and logistics technology to luxury retailers; the group was acquired by Coupang in early 2024. No public developer portal or API documentation is currently reachable for the marketplace or the platform arm.
f.name: Farfetch

f.description: The Farm Credit Administration (FCA) is an independent US federal agency that regulates and examines the Farm Credit System (FCS) — a nationwide network of cooperatively owned banks and associations providing credit and financial services to farmers, ranchers, agricultural cooperatives and rural infrastructure — and the Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corporation (Farmer Mac). FCA publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no OpenAPI, and its own digital strategy still lists "make existing high-value data and content available through web APIs" as Not begun, due May 2013. It does, however, serve one live, anonymous, machine-readable API that is linked from no developer page: an Esri ArcGIS Server REST surface at wgis.fca.gov publishing Farm Credit System institution headquarters, branch offices and chartered-territory polygons as JSON, GeoJSON and PBF, keyed on the UNINUM institution identifier that also keys the quarterly Call Report bulk downloads.
f.name: Farm Credit Administration

f.description: The Farm Machinery and Equipment API is a software solution that provides developers with access to a database of information related to various types of farm machinery and equipment. This API allows users to retrieve detailed specifications, usage instructions, maintenance tips, and other relevant data for a wide range of agricultural tools and devices.
f.name: Farm Machinery and Equipment API

f.description: As directed by the OPEN (Open, Public, Electronic, and Necessary) Government Data Act and through its commitment to United States agriculturalists and interested public, FSA provides numerous data resources through reports, visualizations, and other formats.
f.name: Farm Service Agency

f.description: FarMart is an AI-powered food sourcing and procurement platform that connects suppliers, food manufacturers, processors, and logistics providers across the global food and energy supply chain. It provides end-to-end procurement infrastructure including verified supplier discovery, five-minute AI-powered KYC verification, compliance management, market-to-factory batch traceability, automated invoicing and e-way bill generation, and real-time payment settlement in one to four hours. FarMart serves food companies, HoReCa (hospitality) buyers, and bio-fuel supply chains, with a network spanning 100+ premium buyers, 50+ food categories, and 10,000+ suppliers.
f.name: FarMart

f.description: FarmDash is a zero-custody intelligence and control layer for DeFi agents and airdrop farmers, combining Trail Heat opportunity scoring, Signal Architect swap routing, wallet and Sybil-risk intelligence, and Hyperliquid futures research across EVM, Solana, HyperEVM and StarkNet. It is one of the most thoroughly agent-instrumented providers in the catalog: a live OpenAPI 3.1.0 with 27 operations, an 84-tool MCP manifest carrying full input schemas, an A2A-flavored agent card, an ai-plugin manifest, llms.txt, ai.txt, a machine-readable agent report, and a runtime capability contract that the provider declares authoritative over tool discovery. Auth is tiered API keys (Scout free / Pioneer $39.99 / Syndicate $199, all USDC) with a verified live x402 machine-payment fallback settling on Base. Writes are gated by mandatory pre-execution simulation and user-held EIP-191/EIP-712 signatures — FarmDash never broadcasts and never holds keys.
f.name: FarmDash Agent Hub

f.description: Farmeron was a dairy herd-management and farm-analytics SaaS founded in 2011 in Osijek, Croatia, that helped dairy producers track animals, feed, milk production, and farm operations through a web platform and data integrations. The company went through the 500 Startups accelerator and was acquired by the machine-vision agriculture firm Cainthus in 2016, after which the standalone Farmeron product was wound down. This network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio lead; the farmeron.com domain is registered but no longer serves a live website or API, so there is no public developer surface to enrich.
f.name: Farmeron

f.description: Farmers Business Network (FBN) is a farmer-to-farmer ag-tech network serving 117,000+ member farms across the U.S. and Canada. Its membership platform pairs the FBN Direct inputs marketplace with seed and farm analytics, crop marketing, agricultural financing, and Norm, an AI agronomy advisor. FBN exposes these as member-facing web and mobile product surfaces; it does not publish a public or partner developer API.
f.name: Farmers Business Network

f.description: Farmers Edge is a precision-agriculture and digital-farming company whose FarmCommand platform combines satellite imagery, connected weather stations, in-field telematics (the CanPlug IoT device), agronomic modeling, carbon-program tooling, and soil/lab products such as LabCommand and Hefty/FESoils. The public FarmCommand API is a Django REST (drf-yasg) service on admin.farmcommand.com that handles self-serve client onboarding and verification, token-based login for FarmCommand, LabCommand, GridCalc, RecEngine and Hefty users, password resets, CanPlug device lookup, and inbound integration webhooks (Stripe billing, DocuSign envelopes, LEAF field alerts). Authentication is a FarmCommand API token passed as a query parameter.
f.name: Farmers Edge

f.description: Farmers Insurance Exchange is a Fortune 500 inter-insurance exchange and the largest of the three reciprocal exchanges that make up the Farmers Insurance Group of Companies, underwriting auto, home, specialty property, life and commercial lines across the United States and managed by Farmers Group, Inc. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Farmers Insurance Exchange. Farmers operates a developer portal at developer.farmers.com titled "Farmers Insurance APIs", but the entire portal is an Okta sign-in wall: no OpenAPI, API reference, quickstart or pricing page is reachable without partner credentials, and the same wall stands in front of the ePartner portal. No public API contract has been observed.
f.name: Farmers Insurance Exchange

f.description: FarmLogs was a farm management platform founded in 2011 (by Jesse Vollmar and Brad Koch, operating as AgriSight Inc.) offering field mapping, in-season satellite imagery, weather/rainfall tracking, yield estimation, and profitability tools for row-crop farmers. FarmLogs was acquired by Bushel in June 2021, and in March 2023 Bushel retired the FarmLogs brand in favor of "Bushel Farm," the next generation of its farm management software. As of this review, farmlogs.com 301-redirects to bushelfarm.com, which itself redirects to bushelpowered.com - the standalone FarmLogs product and website no longer exist. Bushel does publish a public API, but it is for a separate product line (Bushel Fulfillment and Bushel Production, covering grain contracts and scale-ticket data for grain merchandising) rather than for the FarmLogs-lineage farm-management capabilities (fields, imagery, weather, yield). No self-serve, openly documented public API exists for the farm-management product as of the review date.
f.name: FarmLogs

f.description: Farmonaut is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: space) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
f.name: Farmonaut

f.description: Open-source farm management and record-keeping system with a JSON:API-based REST API for managing assets, logs, plans, and farm records. Supports self-hosted deployments and managed hosting via Farmier. Authentication uses OAuth2 with Authorization Code, Password Credentials, and Client Credentials grant types.
f.name: farmOS

f.description: FarmWise Labs is an agricultural technology company building AI-powered robotics for specialty crop farming. Its flagship product, Vulcan, is an intra-row weeder and precision cultivator that uses computer vision and machine learning to identify and mechanically remove weeds without herbicides, covering up to three acres per hour and saving growers an estimated $250+ per acre. The self-calibrating machine operates in all field conditions and receives over-the-air software updates. Founded in San Francisco and backed by GV (Google Ventures), FarmWise is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.
f.name: Farmwise

f.description: Faro Health is an AI platform for clinical development that helps biopharma and clinical research teams design and execute better studies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Diego, California, Faro provides study design optimization, automated protocol document authoring, and clinical workflow automation, digitizing and structuring trial protocols so teams can accelerate development without compromising scientific rigor, patient safety, or patient-centricity. Faro is backed by investors including General Catalyst.
f.name: Faro

f.description: Faros AI is an engineering-operations intelligence platform (software engineering intelligence / SEI) that ingests data from across the SDLC toolchain into a connected canonical model and exposes it for querying. The platform offers a REST API for events and data ingestion at https://prod.api.faros.ai plus a GraphQL query API over the canonical model, with an open-source Faros Community Edition.
f.name: Faros AI

f.description: Farther is a technology-driven wealth management and registered investment advisory (RIA) firm that pairs human financial advisors with a proprietary "Intelligent Wealth Platform." The firm has recruited more than $23 billion in client assets and positions itself among the fastest-growing US financial services firms (Inc. Magazine, Deloitte Technology Fast 500). Services span financial and retirement planning, investment and portfolio management, tax-intelligent optimization, trust and estate planning, generational wealth, small-business services, Farther Asset Management, and institutional offerings. The client experience runs through a single-page web/mobile application at app.farther.com and integrates account aggregation via Plaid. Farther does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures the firm's public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
f.name: Farther

f.description: Fashinza is a tech-enabled apparel manufacturing and supply-chain platform that connects fashion brands and retailers with a vetted global network of garment manufacturers. It streamlines end-to-end production: sourcing designs and fabrics, AI-powered supplier matching, tech-pack and sample creation, real-time production tracking, quality control, and merchandising and forecasting support so brands can move from design to delivery in shortened 30-45 day cycles. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates a buyer login and a supplier onboarding surface but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.
f.name: Fashinza

f.description: Fashion AI is a cutting-edge technology that uses artificial intelligence to revolutionize the way we shop for clothing. By analyzing vast amounts of data on trends, styles, and customer preferences, Fashion AI can predict the next big fashion trends, personalize recommendations for shoppers, and even create custom designs based on individual tastes. This innovative technology not only streamlines the shopping experience but also helps retailers optimize their inventory and marketing strategies.
f.name: Fashion AI

f.description: AI fashion design and commercial photography platform for brands and creators, offering a generative AI fashion suite — virtual try-on, AI model and outfit generation, flat lay production, background change and removal, garment recolor, face swap and fashion video. Fashion Diffusion exposes a bearer-key REST Public API at https://www.fashiondiffusion.ai/api/public/v1/ built on a submit-and-poll task model: a generation request returns HTTP 202 with a task id, and the caller polls until the task reaches SUCCEEDED or FAILED. The published reference documents four operations across two capabilities — Virtual Try-On and AI Inpainting submission plus task query and cursor-paginated task list — while marketing advertises more than 18 endpoints. There is no OpenAPI, GraphQL schema, Postman collection, MCP server, agent card, SDK, webhook surface, status page or changelog, and the reference states plainly that this version carries no idempotency protection.
f.name: Fashion Diffusion

f.description: Fashion, Inc. was the legal entity behind Fab.com, the design-focused e-commerce and flash-sale marketplace founded in 2010 by Jason Goldberg and Bradford Shellhammer after pivoting from the Fabulis social network. Fab raised roughly $150M across rounds led by Menlo Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Atomico, listed Battery Ventures among its backers, and passed ten million members by December 2012 before layoffs and a collapse in growth. PCH International acquired Fab's digital assets in March 2015; the site was later repositioned around health and fitness goods and went offline in December 2022. The company is defunct and operated no public developer program or API. The fab.com domain is today registered to Epic Games, Inc. and serves Epic's unrelated Fab digital-asset marketplace, so nothing currently published at that host belongs to this company.
f.name: Fashion, Inc. (Fab.com)

f.description: Fashionara was an Indian premium online fashion retailer that launched in 2012 as a curated "e-fashion mall" selling ladies, men's and kids apparel, footwear and lifestyle goods. It ran a flash-sale "events" model on a Magento storefront, carried more than 200 international labels alongside Indian brands including Kenneth Cole, Calvin Klein, Fossil, Adidas, Benetton, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Clarks and Arrow, and operated a quirky in-house sub-brand called F.lea Bazaar. It offered free shipping over Rs. 799, free returns, next-day delivery in eight Indian cities, a style-advisor booking service and an Android app (com.fnara.main). The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Fashionara never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or OpenAPI definition — a scan of more than 8,000 archived fashionara.com URLs found no /api, /developer, /docs, /swagger, /oauth or /graphql paths, and no api/developer subdomain was ever archived. The storefront went dark in mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
f.name: Fashionara

f.description: FashionLab Nordic Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: FashionLab Nordic

f.description: FASHN AI is an AI-first company specializing in human-centric generative image models tailored for fashion applications. The public API offers an asynchronous prediction workflow against a catalog of models including Try-On Max, Product to Model, Face to Model, Model Create, Model Swap, Edit, Reframe, Image to Video, and Background Remove.
f.name: FASHN AI

f.description: Fast Break Labs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Fast Break Labs

f.description: FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is a platform specification developed by HL7 that defines a set of capabilities for use across the healthcare process, in all jurisdictions, and in many different clinical and administrative contexts. It standardizes how electronic health information is exchanged between systems via REST APIs.
f.name: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources

f.description: Fast Retailing is a global Japanese retail holding company, best known as the parent of Uniqlo, GU, Theory, and other apparel brands. It operates a vast network of clothing stores worldwide, focusing on innovative design, high-quality manufacturing, and efficient supply chain management. The company leverages technology and data-driven strategies to enhance customer experiences and streamline operations across its brands. Fast Retailing continues to expand its international presence while maintaining a commitment to sustainability and corporate responsibility.
f.name: Fast Retailing

f.description: FastAPI is a modern, fast (high-performance), web framework for building APIs with Python 3.7+ based on standard Python type hints.
f.name: FastAPI

f.description: Federal workplace enforcement records on 2.3M US employers across 16 federal agencies — OSHA, WHD, MSHA, EPA ECHO, NLRB, FMCSA, OFLC, BLS SOII, SAM.gov, CMS, USAspending, CPSC, NHTSA, SEC, and the UVA Corporate Prosecution Registry — exposed as a single normalized JSON API. Query inspections, violations, penalties, wage theft cases, severe injury reports, federal contract awards, and recalls.
f.name: FastDOL

f.description: Fasten Health is a healthcare data interoperability company offering a unified medical record platform that gives patients and developers access to clinical data across the U.S. healthcare system. Fasten began as an open-source project — Fasten OnPrem, a self-hosted personal/family electronic medical record manager that ingests FHIR Bundles and is distributed under GPL-3.0 with 2.7k+ GitHub stars. The team then productized the connectivity layer as Fasten Connect, a commercial REST + FHIR API and Stitch client SDK suite that lets developers retrieve clinical records from 50,000+ healthcare systems and 60,000+ organizations including Epic, Cerner, MyChart, Kaiser Permanente, HCA, Ascension, Humana, and Medicare. Founded by engineers who lived through the fragmentation of health data firsthand and based in New York City, Fasten ships GPL/MIT/Apache 2.0 open source repos alongside the hosted Fasten Connect platform.
f.name: Fasten Health

f.description: Fastenal is a leading distributor of industrial and construction supplies, offering fasteners, tools, safety equipment, and other industrial products through stores, vending, and e-commerce. While Fastenal provides EDI integrations and supply chain programs like FAST 360, FASTBin, and FASTStock to enterprise customers, no publicly documented API specifications are available.
f.name: Fastenal

f.description: FastForex is a fast, reliable REST API providing real-time and historical currency exchange rates for 160+ world currencies, 500+ cryptocurrencies, and 2,300+ FX trading pairs. Features include currency conversion, many-to-one and multi-rate lookups, OHLC candlestick data, bid/ask pricing, WebSocket streaming, and up to 55 years of historical data. Average response time of 21ms with 100% uptime SLA.
f.name: FastForex

f.description: FastGPU provides a broker service offering live cloud GPU rental pricing and availability across major providers such as RunPod, Vast.ai, Lambda, AWS, Azure, and GCP. It aggregates real-time market data, enabling users to compare costs, reserve capacity, and integrate pricing into FinOps tools via a RESTful API and a streaming MCP endpoint. The platform also includes a workload matcher to align GPU resources with AI model requirements, supporting developers and enterprises in optimizing compute spend.
f.name: FastGPU

f.description: Fastify is a fast and low-overhead web framework for Node.js, designed for building high-performance APIs and microservices. It features a powerful plugin architecture, JSON Schema-based request and response validation, automatic serialization, comprehensive logging with Pino, and TypeScript support out of the box.
f.name: Fastify

f.description: Fastino Labs is an applied research lab building production-ready small language models (SLMs) for agentic AI — structured data extraction, classification, PII detection, and safety moderation. Its Pioneer platform is an agentic fine-tuning and inference API that lets teams generate synthetic training data, fine-tune GLiNER encoder models and open-source decoder LLMs (Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek, Gemma), evaluate them against labeled datasets, and serve inference through native, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Fastino also maintains the open-source GLiNER2 schema-based information-extraction model and the GLiGuard safety-moderation model.
f.name: Fastino Labs

f.description: FastLane Labs is a blockchain infrastructure provider building maximal extractable value (MEV) and liquid staking products on the Monad blockchain. Its core products are shMON, a liquid staking token that pairs staking rewards with revenue from FastLane's on-chain MEV auction and holds the majority of Monad's liquid-staking TVL; Smart Vault, a USDC-denominated yield product; and hMON, a yield-donation token. FastLane operates a public, on-chain MEV auction that a majority of Monad validators route blocks through, exposing developer surfaces for searchers (the FastLane Sidecar and auction-handler contracts), validators (a Leader API and validator onboarding), and stakers. It also maintains Atlas, an open-source execution-abstraction framework, with a Go SDK and JSON-RPC tooling published on GitHub. Developer integration is via JSON-RPC APIs and Solidity smart contracts rather than a REST/OpenAPI catalog.
f.name: FastLane

f.description: Fastly is an edge cloud platform that helps customers create great digital experiences quickly, securely, and reliably by processing, serving, and securing their applications closer to their users. The platform spans CDN, Edge Compute (WebAssembly), Object Storage, AI Accelerator (semantic caching for LLMs), AI Bot Management, Next-Gen WAF (Signal Sciences), DDoS Protection, Image Optimizer, Live & Video Streaming, Fanout real-time messaging, and an MCP Server for AI-driven control.
f.name: Fastly

f.description: Fastmail provides secure, private email and calendar services for individuals and businesses. Founded in 1999, Fastmail emphasizes data protection, user privacy, and a feature‑rich experience with powerful filtering, custom domains, and cross‑platform synchronization. Their service includes robust spam protection, two‑factor authentication, and a focus on delivering a fast, reliable email platform without advertising or data mining. Fastmail also offers business plans with administrative controls, migration tools, and dedicated support, catering to professionals who need secure communication and reliable uptime.
f.name: Fastmail

f.description: FastMCP is the fast, Pythonic framework for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients, and apps. Originally created by Jeremiah Lowin and maintained by PrefectHQ, FastMCP 1.0 was adopted into the official Anthropic MCP Python SDK in 2024, and the standalone FastMCP project (now at v3) remains the most widely used way to ship MCP servers in Python — the project reports powering roughly 70% of MCP servers across all languages. FastMCP turns ordinary Python functions into MCP tools, resources, prompts, and apps via decorators, auto-generates JSON Schemas from type hints, handles transport negotiation (stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE), and ships first-class OAuth/OIDC authentication, server composition and proxying, OpenAPI/FastAPI import, a CLI for running and installing servers into Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor / ChatGPT / Gemini CLI / Goose, middleware, lifespan management, elicitation, sampling, progress reporting, OpenTelemetry, and a client library and apps runtime for building interactive UIs rendered inside MCP host conversations.
f.name: FastMCP

f.description: FastPix is a developer-first video platform offering APIs for video on-demand (upload, ingest, encoding, playback), live streaming, simulcasting, secure and DRM playback, in-video AI (transcription, summaries, chapters, moderation), and video views analytics. A Mux-style, pay-per-minute video infrastructure with a single REST API at api.fastpix.io/v1 using Basic auth.
f.name: FastPix

f.description: FastRouter.ai provides a unified API gateway for large language models, enabling enterprises to route, compare, and operate across over 200 AI models via a single OpenAI‑compatible endpoint. It offers features such as automatic model selection, cost‑optimization insights, response caching, prompt management, and comprehensive analytics, helping teams build scalable, reliable AI applications while reducing latency and expense.
f.name: Fastrouter

f.description: Fastshot is an AI-powered, no-code mobile app builder that turns a plain-language prompt into a real native iOS and Android application. A multi-agent AI workflow handles design, branding, asset generation, and functionality end to end, then deploys the finished app to the Apple App Store and Google Play. The platform includes integrations for a Supabase backend (authentication, database, storage), GitHub source-code management, Expo builds, and in-app-purchase monetization, letting non-technical founders and businesses ship a working mobile app in minutes rather than hiring an agency or in-house team. Fastshot is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company founded by ex-Google engineers Dmitry Fatkhi and Elvira Dzhuraeva.
f.name: Fastshot

f.description: FastSpring is a full-service ecommerce and merchant-of-record platform for SaaS, software, and digital product companies, handling global payments, tax compliance, subscription billing, checkout, and revenue management. The FastSpring API is a REST interface for managing orders, subscriptions, products, coupons, customers, and webhook events, secured via HTTP Basic Authentication using credentials issued from the FastSpring App Dashboard and with HMAC SHA-256 signing available for webhook payload verification.
f.name: FastSpring

f.description: Fasturn is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
f.name: Fasturn

f.description: Fastwork is Thailand's leading freelance and services marketplace, connecting businesses and individuals with roughly 200,000 vetted service providers across about 300 categories — including design and graphics, web and app development, AI development and automation, marketing and advertising, writing and translation, photography and video, and lifestyle services. An escrow-based "Fastwork Guarantee" holds payment until work is delivered, protecting both buyers and freelancers. The platform serves individuals, SMEs, and enterprises with a dedicated business portal, and is expanding from Thailand into Indonesia and Vietnam. Fastwork is backed by 500 Global and Partech. No public developer API is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web surface and domain-security posture.
f.name: Fastwork

f.description: Fat Zebra is an Australian payments company (founded 2012, Sydney) providing a card-present and card-not-present payment gateway and processing platform for merchants, ISOs, and software platforms across Australia and New Zealand. Its API-first Gateway handles Visa, Mastercard, and Amex purchases, authorizations and captures, refunds and voids, card tokenization, 3D Secure, recurring payment plans, direct debits and direct credits over local bank rails, chargeback handling, batch processing, and hosted payment pages (PayNow), alongside wallet acceptance for Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Click to Pay. A separate Partner API lets platforms and ISOs create and board their own sub-merchants onto acquirer connections programmatically. The developer surface is a genuine, well-documented ReadMe hub at docs.fatzebra.com with four downloadable OpenAPI definitions, and the runtime platform is branded pmnts (gateway.pmnts.io). Authentication is HTTP Basic using a username and API token.
f.name: Fat Zebra

f.description: Fatcat is a versioned, user-editable open catalog of published research works maintained by the Internet Archive. It tracks bibliographic metadata, links papers to full-text copies, and preserves access to scholarly publications including journal articles, conference proceedings, and datasets across millions of research works.
f.name: Fatcat

f.description: Fathom Analytics is a privacy-first website analytics platform that provides GDPR-compliant, cookie-free analytics as an alternative to Google Analytics. The platform serves thousands of companies, including Fortune 100 enterprises and government agencies, offering simple and accurate traffic metrics without tracking personally identifiable information. Fathom exposes a REST API with base URL https://api.usefathom.com/v1, enabling developers to manage sites, events, and milestones, generate aggregated custom reports, and retrieve real-time visitor counts. Authentication is via Bearer token API keys, which are generated in the account settings area and support configurable permissions scoped to admin, all sites, or individual sites.
f.name: Fathom Analytics

f.description: Fatora is a Qatar-based online invoicing and payment platform operated by MaktApp, serving more than 120,000 merchants across Arabic-speaking markets in the Gulf and wider MENA region. It combines professional invoicing, a hosted online store, POS/cashier tooling, WhatsApp/SMS/email payment links, and a card payment gateway (routing through processors such as Stripe, TAP and TESS) behind a single merchant account. Fatora publishes a REST API at api.fatora.io/v1 for programmatic checkout, tokenization, refunds and payment verification, plus full CRUD over invoices, clients and products, and AI helpers for product content. First-party SDKs are provided for PHP, Laravel, .NET, JavaScript, React, iOS, Android and Ionic, alongside ready-made plugins for WooCommerce, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop, Shopify and Wix. This profile was enriched from Fatora's public developer surface.
f.name: Fatora

f.description: fatsecret is a global nutrition and wellness platform whose Platform API exposes a verified database of more than 2.3 million foods across 58 countries and 26 languages, plus recipes, exercises, image recognition, natural language processing, and user-scoped food diary, exercise diary, and weight tracking. The API is used by more than 50,000 developers and serves over 700 million calls per month. Bootstrapped and profitable since 2006, fatsecret has never raised venture funding.
f.name: fatsecret

f.description: Fauna, Inc. built a distributed document-relational database delivered as a cloud API, combining the relational query power of SQL with the flexibility of documents, global serverless distribution and strictly serializable ACID transactions over plain HTTPS. Fauna announced End-of-Service in March 2025 and shut the hosted service down on 2025-05-30; as of 2026-09-17 every Fauna service host returns NXDOMAIN and the apex domain forwards to an unrelated company. This profile is maintained as an archival record of the API surface as it stood at shutdown.
f.name: Fauna

f.description: Fave is a Malaysia- and Singapore-based lifestyle and payments app offering deals, cashback, rewards, eCards, and QR-code payments, operated by Fave Asia Technologies and owned by Pine Labs. For merchants and platforms, Fave exposes the FavePay Omni (FPO) partner API: create single-use QR codes or payment URLs, process customer-presented (merchant-scan) charges, look up, list, and acknowledge transactions, issue full or partial refunds, and receive signed webhook callbacks on every status change. Every request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret key Fave issues during partner onboarding. FavePay Omni operates across Malaysia (MY), Singapore (SG), and Indonesia (ID).
f.name: Fave

f.description: Favorited is a mobile-first live streaming platform that helps content creators run interactive, real-time shows with their audiences. The app centers on participatory formats — games, giveaways, and community interactions — so that viewers feel like they are playing together with a creator rather than passively watching a broadcast, alongside monetization tools for creators. Favorited ships as consumer iOS and Android apps and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment and monitoring.
f.name: favorited
