Their modular platform includes hardware like Safe Remote Control Pro, software such as FORT Manager, and services ranging from safety architecture to fleet analytics. Backed by Lemnos Labs, the company focuses on integrating safety into AI-driven physical devices, enabling secure deployment and operation across industries.
f.name: Fort Robotics

f.description: Forta is a decentralized, real-time detection network for monitoring the security and operational health of Web3 systems. Spun out of OpenZeppelin and backed by a16z crypto, Forta runs thousands of community-built detection bots across independent scan nodes that inspect every transaction and block on chains such as Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism, emitting alerts that DeFi protocols and security teams subscribe to via email, Slack, Telegram, Discord and webhooks. Developers query alerts and threat intelligence through a GraphQL API, build and deploy detection bots with the Forta Bot SDK and CLI (JavaScript/TypeScript and Python), and the Forta Firewall product uses the Forta Chain (a Layer 3 network) to block smart-contract exploits before they execute.
f.name: Forta

f.description: Forta Health operates the largest virtual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) network in the United States, delivering autism therapy to children through two models: Virtual ABA over a HIPAA-secure telehealth platform across 43 states, and In-Home ABA in Dallas, Houston and San Antonio, Texas. Founded in 2021 and led by CEO Edan Morag, Forta pairs Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) who design and supervise individualized treatment plans with Registered Behavior Technicians (RBTs) and trained parents who deliver live sessions, using proprietary software and machine-learning models that ingest medical records and session data to surface relevant case data for clinicians and personalize each treatment plan. The company works with major commercial payers and state Medicaid programs to shorten the typical six-to-eighteen-month ABA waitlist to roughly ninety days. Forta publishes no public developer program; its clinical operations platform is a private, bearer-token-authenticated REST API.
f.name: Forta Health

f.description: Fortaleza Dados Abertos is a open data portal open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 635 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
f.name: Fortaleza Dados Abertos

f.description: Fortanix is a data-security company building the Fortanix Data & AI Security Platform, a unified control plane for enterprise cryptography. Its products include Data Security Manager (DSM) — a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated key-management, HSM, tokenization and secrets service delivered as SaaS or as on-premises appliances; Confidential Computing Manager (CCM) for enclave conversion, attestation and workload signing on Intel SGX and AWS Nitro; Key Insight for cryptographic discovery, posture and post-quantum readiness across cloud and on-premises estates; and Fortanix Armor. All three products publish public REST APIs with machine-readable OpenAPI/Swagger contracts, and Fortanix ships first-party client SDKs (Java, Python, Go, Rust, C#, PHP, JavaScript), a Python CLI (sdkms-cli), Terraform providers, and legacy cryptographic interfaces (PKCS#11, Microsoft CNG, Java JCE).
f.name: Fortanix

f.description: Fortastra is a spacecraft manufacturer building low-cost, maneuverable orbital defense systems designed for scalability and autonomous operation. Its spacecraft protect space-based infrastructure with autonomous navigation that detects, analyzes, and responds to orbital anomalies without relying on distant ground-based sensors. The company's open software architecture spans sensing, maneuvering, coordination, and response functions, and its hardware is validated through component testing, simulation, and orbital deployment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.
f.name: Fortastra

f.description: Forte builds on-chain compliance and economic tooling for games and Web3 applications. Its flagship developer product, the Forte Rules Engine, is an open-source EVM protocol that lets developers define powerful, flexible, and composable on-chain policies — for regulatory compliance, risk management, and token-economy design — without hardcoding rules into their smart contracts. The engine centers on policies, rules, trackers, and calling/foreign contracts, ships client contracts for the ERC20/721/1155/721A token standards, and is consumed through a TypeScript SDK. Forte was founded in 2019 and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Canaan. This profile catalogs Forte's public developer surface — Rules Engine documentation, SDK, and GitHub organization.
f.name: Forte Labs

f.description: Fortem Technologies is an airspace security and defense company based in Lindon, Utah that builds counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) for military, government, critical infrastructure, and commercial customers. Its SkyDome System combines TrueView AESA radars, long-range TrueView cameras, RF sensors, and the autonomous DroneHunter interceptor into a single detect-track-defeat capability, orchestrated by SkyDome Manager command-and-control software. SkyDome Manager exposes REST, realtime, and track-only integration APIs so third-party C2 platforms (such as the U.S. Army FAAD C2 and Lockheed Martin systems) can exchange over a hundred fields and commands for airspace awareness and drone mitigation. Fortem is backed by Lockheed Martin, DCVC, Toshiba, Boeing, and other strategic investors, and its systems have been selected for high-profile deployments including protection of venues at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
f.name: Fortem Technologies

f.description: Forter is a fraud prevention and digital identity platform for online commerce. Its Decision API returns real-time trust-or-not decisions for orders, payments, account signups, and logins, drawing on a global identity graph and machine learning trained across a large network of merchants. Beyond fraud management, Forter covers chargeback recovery, abuse prevention, payment optimization, 3DS orchestration, and identity protection. Access is enterprise / contact-sales - API credentials (a per-account site ID and API key) are provisioned by Forter during onboarding, and requests are sent to a dedicated per-tenant host.
f.name: Forter

f.description: Fortera is a Silicon Valley materials-technology company advancing zero-CO2 cement. Its ReCarb process economically converts captured CO2 into ReAct green cement that meets regulatory standards and can be blended with or used in place of Ordinary Portland Cement inside existing production infrastructure. Fortera operates its first commercial ReCarb plant in Redding, California, holds 100+ patents, and is backed by Khosla Ventures and Temasek. The company is a climate-tech materials producer rather than a software/API provider; it publishes a public marketing website and an llms.txt but no developer API surface.
f.name: Fortera

f.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.
f.name: Forterra

f.description: Forterro is a pan-European industrial software company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, that provides enterprise resource planning (ERP) and specialised business software to the industrial mid-market. Built through a series of acquisitions, Forterro operates a portfolio of regional and vertical ERP brands - including Abas, Jeeves, Garp, Proconcept, Sylob, Silog, Myfactory, Orderwise, Clipper, 123Insight, BPSC, Helios, Proffix, Prodaso and its cloud-native Fortee product - alongside best-in-class point solutions such as warehouse management (WMS), point of sale (POS), material requirements planning (MRP) and business intelligence. The company serves more than 13,000 industrial businesses across manufacturing, warehousing, wholesale and retail from 40+ offices worldwide.
f.name: Forterro

f.description: Fortify is a comprehensive application security platform from OpenText that provides static application security testing (SAST), dynamic application security testing (DAST), and software composition analysis (SCA) capabilities. It helps organizations identify and remediate vulnerabilities across the software development lifecycle.
f.name: Fortify

f.description: Fortigo Network Logistics Pvt. Ltd. (4TiGO) was a Bengaluru, India technology-enabled logistics and supply-chain network platform, founded in 2015, operating an online marketplace for freight/truck transportation alongside a Digital Supply Chain Control Tower SaaS. It was backed by Accel and Nandan Nilekani's NRJN Family Trust, raising roughly $23.5M across five rounds. As of this enrichment pass the company appears deadpooled/defunct: its 4tigo.com site is unreachable (connection refused across all hosts) and no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition could be located. No API artifacts were enriched because there is no live developer surface.
f.name: Fortigo

f.description: Fortinet is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Fortinet API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
f.name: Fortinet

f.description: FortisBC is a British Columbia energy utility and a subsidiary of Fortis Inc., delivering natural gas to more than 1,054,000 customers and electricity directly to close to 185,000 customers across the province's Southern Interior, plus liquefied natural gas from the Tilbury and Mt. Hayes facilities, renewable natural gas, and EV charging. It sits at the regulated distribution tier of the value chain — the wires-and-pipes monopoly that meters the customer — under British Columbia Utilities Commission oversight, in a province with no wholesale electricity market and no consumer energy data right. Its API posture is honestly none: no developer portal, no published API, no OpenAPI, and no Green Button. British Columbia sits outside Ontario's Green Button regulation (O. Reg. 633/21) and outside Australia's Consumer Data Right, and the Green Button Alliance reports only "minor discussions of Green Button in British Columbia to-date". Consumer usage data is reachable only by the account holder through a SiteMinder-protected customer login at accounts.fortisbc.com, or — for commercial gas customers only — pushed into the US EPA's ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager via that platform's data exchange, an arrangement FortisBC participates in rather than an API it publishes. No open market, grid, or system data is published. Consumer data closed, market data closed.
f.name: FortisBC

f.description: Fortive Corporation is a Fortune 500 diversified industrial technology conglomerate headquartered in Everett, Washington. The company operates across two main segments, Advanced Healthcare Solutions and Intelligent Operating Solutions, providing essential technologies for medical device safety, radiation protection, workflow automation, hazard detection, and predictive maintenance through its operating companies. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Fortive at the parent company level. Most APIs and developer resources are maintained by Fortive's individual operating companies.
f.name: Fortive

f.description: Fortnite Tracker, by Tracker Network, exposes a small REST API surface (api.fortnitetracker.com/v1) covering player profile lifetime stats, regional leaderboards, competitive power rankings, the rotating in-game store, and the weekly challenges feed for Fortnite. Authentication is a single TRN-Api-Key header obtained from the Fortnite Tracker site. The service has reached a silent end-of-life in recent years (some endpoints are intermittently unavailable) but remains the canonical community profile of how Tracker Network packages Epic Games' Fortnite telemetry as a developer API.
f.name: Fortnite Tracker

f.description: Fortnox is a Swedish cloud accounting, ERP, and business-administration platform for small and medium-sized businesses and accounting bureaus. Its REST API at https://api.fortnox.se/3/ programmatically manages accounting and financial data - invoices, customers, articles, orders, offers, vouchers, accounts, suppliers, supplier invoices, projects, and financial years - authenticated with OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow. Fortnox also publishes a duplex WebSocket event stream at wss://ws.fortnox.se/topics-v1 that pushes minimal change notifications across domains so integrations can react to changes instead of polling.
f.name: Fortnox

f.description: Forto is a digital freight forwarder and supply chain platform that combines technology with logistics expertise to provide sea, air, and rail freight services across 100+ countries. The platform offers a public REST API for booking management, shipment tracking, transport plans, document handling, and webhook subscriptions, enabling shippers, enterprises, and partners to integrate Forto freight operations directly into their ERP, TMS, and supply chain systems via standard HTTPS APIs, EDI, or fully customized integrations.
f.name: Forto

f.description: Fortu (Fortu Wealth Ltd) is a London-based fintech, founded in 2019, offering digital private banking for high-net-worth individuals and their businesses, including borderless multi-currency accounts, payments, and a curated selection of investment opportunities across fintech and real-estate-driven debt strategies. Fortu also operates a business-to-business Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets private banks, wealth managers, and multi-family offices roll out their own branded investment and payments products, with automated payment processing and an API-driven compliance-monitoring tool. Co-founded by co-CEOs Firdavs Shakhidi and Azmat Sultanov, the company was selected for the 500 Global startup accelerator and raised an oversubscribed crowdfunding round (~GBP 500k) on Seedrs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Fortu does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, and its primary web deployment was offline (HTTP 402, disabled deployment) at the time of enrichment.
f.name: Fortu

f.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.
f.name: Fortuna Health

f.description: Fortune Brands Innovations is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Fortune Brands Innovations API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
f.name: Fortune Brands Innovations

f.description: Fortune Technology, listed by Qiming Venture Partners as one of the largest commercial factoring companies in China, historically operating at china-fif.com. Commercial factoring is a trade-finance business: purchasing accounts receivable from suppliers at a discount to provide working capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe the company publishes no developer surface of any kind — no public API, no documentation portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. The china-fif.com domain no longer serves the company: HTTPS is refused outright (port 443 closed) and plain HTTP returns an unrelated Chinese Premier League sports-streaming site running EmpireCMS. This record is retained as an honest negative result for the API Evangelist network rather than deleted.
f.name: Fortune Technology (China FIF)

f.description: ForTunes was a Vienna-based mobile music data analytics application for self-publishing and DIY artists, managers, and small labels. The app collected and visualized performance data across Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and other platforms into a single intelligent feed, with notifications for playlist adds and follower growth, a Spotify playlist recommendation engine, public artist profiles, and team collaboration. Backed by Speedinvest (2018), the company was acquired by Utopia Music in 2023. As of this profile the primary web domain (fortunes.io) no longer resolves and no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; the product surface is the consumer iOS and Android apps.
f.name: Fortunes

f.description: Forty Seven, Inc. was an immuno-oncology biotechnology company founded in 2015 to commercialize CD47 immune-evasion research licensed from Stanford University (Irv Weissman and colleagues). Its lead program was magrolimab, a monoclonal antibody targeting CD47 — the "do not eat me" signal tumor cells use to evade macrophage-mediated killing — studied in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Backed by GV, the company was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2020 for roughly $4.9 billion; the fortyseveninc.com domain now redirects to gilead.com. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface.
f.name: Forty Seven *

f.description: Forum is a centralized exchange offering exposure to engagement-backed assets — "the first exchange to trade on attention." It turns online attention across social, search, and streaming data into measurable, tradable attention indices, then lists continuous perpetual-style futures contracts on top of them so participants can go long or short on cultural relevance as a new asset class. Forum (Y Combinator W26, based in New York City) exposes a full public developer surface: an OpenAPI 3.1 REST API at api.forum.market/v1 for market data, order management, positions, and account queries, and an AsyncAPI 3.0 WebSocket feed at wss://api.forum.market/ws/v1 for real-time order book, ticker, trade, index, and funding updates. Authentication is HMAC-SHA256 request signing with read/trade API-key permissions, and the docs ship an agent-native discovery surface (llms.txt, agent-card, agent-skills, and a documentation MCP server).
f.name: Forum

f.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.
f.name: Forum Mobility

f.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.
f.name: Forus

f.description: Forus Health Pvt Ltd is a Bengaluru, India based medical device manufacturer specializing in advanced eye-care and retinal-imaging technology. Its 3nethra family of devices covers adult and neonatal retinal imaging, refraction and myopia management, and anterior-segment imaging, complemented by the FH-POISE AI diagnostic platform that screens for diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, cataract, hypertensive retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, and dry eye. Forus also operates connected telemedicine platforms (FH TeleCare, FH TeleEye, FH TeleOpticals) for remote eye screening. The company reports more than 5,000 installations across 85+ countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.
f.name: Forus Health

f.description: Forvia is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier formed in 2022 by the combination of Faurecia and Hella. Forvia designs and manufactures cockpits, seating, interiors, lighting, electronics, hydrogen storage, and clean mobility systems for global automakers.
f.name: Forvia

f.description: Forward Air is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Forward Air API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
f.name: Forward Air

f.description: Forward Earth is a Berlin-based climate technology company building AI-automated carbon management software that helps businesses measure, track, and reduce their carbon footprint in line with environmental regulation. Its platform covers Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) accounting certified to the GHG Protocol, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) calculation, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) compliance reporting, with an emphasis on automating data collection and emissions calculation to save time and cost. Forward Earth also offers a white-label / partner offering that embeds its carbon management capabilities into GRC, ESG, supply-chain, and consultancy software, exposing environmental and partner-specific APIs plus single sign-on through a sandbox that partners access on request. The company is backed by Speedinvest and is moving toward agent-native product carbon footprinting.
f.name: Forward Earth

f.description: Forward Networks builds network digital-twin software (Forward Enterprise) that creates a mathematically accurate, vendor-agnostic model of large hybrid and multi-cloud networks. Networking, security, cloud, and compliance teams use it to verify network behavior before and after changes, trace packet paths, run automated policy checks, analyze CVE/vulnerability exposure, and query the network as structured data through the Network Query Engine (NQE). The Forward Enterprise Complete API is an OpenAPI 3.2.0 surface of 189 operations across 108 paths — covering Networks, Snapshots, Checks, Path Search, NQE, Vulnerability Analysis, and system administration — secured with HTTP Basic authentication and complemented by a Go client, a Terraform provider, and an open-source MCP server.
f.name: Forward Networks

f.description: FORWARD Platform is a govtech SaaS company (a Techstars portfolio company) offering one secure platform for administering public-benefit programs. It serves governments, nonprofits, and foundations with tooling for program management, online form building, eligibility determination, case management, client communication, referrals, payment disbursement, reporting and analytics, and fraud prevention. FORWARD supports service-delivery programs such as guaranteed basic income, housing assistance, and emergency management, and is packaged in Direct, Pro, Enterprise, and Ally tiers. Enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer portal — this is a product/marketing web presence only.
f.name: Forward Platform

f.description: ForwardLane Technologies builds Signal Studio, a decision intelligence platform that transforms enterprise data into auditable actions rather than dashboards. Users ask questions in natural language and receive Next Best Actions with complete audit trails in seconds, powered by a semantic data layer, multi-agent AI orchestration, a no-code signal builder, and in-database processing so data never leaves the customer environment. Validated across eight years of Fortune 500 production, Signal Studio serves financial services, private credit and private equity, real estate, energy and oil and gas, and government, with BYOK support for any LLM, cloud, or inference provider. Led by CEO Nathan Stevenson. ForwardLane exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.
f.name: Forwardlane

f.description: Show random image of car from Forza
f.name: Forza

f.description: FOSSA is a software supply chain security and open source management platform that scans codebases, containers, and binaries to detect open source dependencies, then enforces open source license compliance, vulnerability management, and SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) obligations across the software development lifecycle. FOSSA exposes a REST API at app.fossa.com/api plus the language-agnostic FOSSA CLI, integrating with 20+ build systems and CI/CD to surface licensing, security, and quality issues, generate attribution and audit reports, and gate pull requests on policy violations. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Norwest Venture Partners.
f.name: Fossa

f.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.
f.name: Fossil Group

f.description: Fossil SCM is an open-source, distributed version control system that includes an integrated bug tracking, wiki, and web interface. It provides a self-contained, easy-to-deploy solution for software configuration management, suitable for both small projects and large codebases. The system emphasizes simplicity, reliability, and a single-file repository model, making it a coherent alternative to other SCM tools.
f.name: Fossil SCM

f.description: FOSSology is a Linux Foundation project providing open source license compliance software that scans source code for licenses, copyrights, and export control information. It helps organizations manage their open source license obligations through automated scanning, human clearing workflows, and SPDX/compliance reporting via a self-hosted REST API.
f.name: FOSSology

f.description: Found is a fintech business-banking app for the self-employed, freelancers, and sole proprietors that combines a free business checking account (banking services provided by Lead Bank, Member FDIC) with built-in bookkeeping, real-time tax estimates and payments, invoicing, and contractor management. As of the 2026-06-20 review Found exposes no public or partner developer API; the surfaces below are documented as in-app product features, not programmatic APIs.
f.name: Found

f.description: Foundation is a creator-focused NFT marketplace built on Ethereum that enables digital artists to mint, showcase, and auction unique digital artworks. The platform provides a GraphQL API via The Graph protocol for querying artwork, auctions, bids, collector profiles, offers, buy-now listings, and edition drop data. Foundation smart contracts remain live on Ethereum mainnet, and the subgraph continues to index on-chain activity for programmatic access.
f.name: Foundation

f.description: Foundation Building Materials (FBM) is a leading North American distributor of interior building products — drywall, steel framing, acoustic ceilings, insulation, and complementary construction supplies — serving commercial and residential contractors across the United States and Canada. Headquartered in Santa Ana, California, FBM operates a national branch network and a unified customer ordering platform at myfbm.com (consolidating the legacy fbmsales.com, MyRIS, and MyFBM portals) along with iOS/Android mobile apps for contractors. In April 2025, FBM acquired KCG/Rew Materials, adding 800 employees and 45 distribution branches across 23 states. In August 2025, Lowe's announced an agreement to acquire FBM. Brand families operating under FBM include FBM, RIS, Pacific Source, and Unified Door. FBM does not currently expose any public developer APIs, OpenAPI documentation, partner integration program, SDK, or GitHub organization — its digital surface is limited to buyer-facing e-commerce (search, ordering, order tracking, quick-order PDF/photo ingestion via "Quick Order Entry") rather than a developer/integration product.
f.name: Foundation Building Materials

f.description: Foundation Medicine is a molecular information and precision cancer diagnostics company that develops comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) tests for solid tumors, blood cancers, and sarcomas, including its FoundationOne family of assays. Its testing analyzes patient tumor and liquid-biopsy samples to identify genomic alterations that can inform targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and clinical-trial matching, and it partners with biopharma on companion diagnostics and clinical-trial enrollment. A Roche company, it has delivered more than 1.5 million patient CGP reports and supports 950+ clinical trials. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead (gv, kleiner-perkins) and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public developer API or portal, so this record captures its public web, legal, and security-disclosure surface.
f.name: Foundation Medicine

f.description: Foundation Robotics Labs — trading publicly as Foundation and incorporated as Foundation Future Industries, Inc. — is a San Francisco humanoid robotics company founded in April 2024 by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc. It builds Phantom, a general-purpose humanoid robot aimed at industrial automation, logistics, inspection, disaster response and defense, and Cortex, the company's self-described physics foundation model built on Deep Variational Bayes Filters that pairs physics-informed prediction with vision-language reasoning to drive the robot. The company's published master plan runs from building humanoids through fleet coherence and on to building cities, and it states explicitly that it designs for military environments, unlike U.S. competitors committed to non-weaponization. Foundation has raised a reported $111M and is traded on the secondary market via Forge Global. As of this profile Foundation publishes NO public developer surface — no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI definition, SDK, package, MCP server or agent card. Its entire public web presence is a five-page Framer marketing site (home, Phantom, Cortex, master plan, culture, careers) with no /docs, /developers, /api, /pricing, /terms or /privacy paths and no llms.txt. Its GitHub organization (github.com/foundationbot, verified first-party by @foundation.bot commit-author domains) holds internal test benches and forks of open-source robotics tooling — Drake, jetson-containers, Kalibr, PlotJuggler, Fast-DDS, an EtherCAT master, actuator dyno benches and NXP S32K MCU demos — and contains no API specification of any kind.
f.name: Foundation Robotics Labs

f.description: Founder Collective is a seed and pre-seed stage venture capital firm that describes itself as stage-focused, sector agnostic, and proudly anti-thematic. Founded more than fifteen years ago and operating from Cambridge, MA (Harvard Square) and New York, NY (SoHo), the firm positions itself as founder-aligned, backing capital-efficient companies from idea through IPO. General partners include Micah Rosenbloom, David Frankel, and Amanda Herson, with Eric Paley as partner emeritus. Notable portfolio companies include Uber, SeatGeek, WHOOP, The Trade Desk, Airtable, Cruise, Coupang, Verkada, Shield AI, and Suno. Added to the API Evangelist network via the venture-capital portfolio graph.
f.name: Founder Collective

f.description: FounderDating was an online network that helped entrepreneurs find co-founders, advisors, and early team members to start companies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirms FounderDating has been merged into CoFoundersLab: the founderdating.com domain now redirects to cofounderslab.com, a founder-matching and startup-community platform. Neither the legacy FounderDating brand nor the CoFoundersLab successor publishes a public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, developer portal, SDK/package, or any /.well-known discovery surface, so there are no API artifacts to search, generate, or derive. The founderdating.com host is additionally unreachable over HTTPS (connection times out; DNS points at a parked Tucows IP). This profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an active API provider.
f.name: FounderDating

f.description: Founders Fund is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Peter Thiel, Ken Howery, and Luke Nosek, best known for the credo "we wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters" and a contrarian appetite for hard science and frontier technology over incremental consumer apps. The firm backs category-defining, often monopoly-scale companies across aerospace and defense, artificial intelligence, biotech, fintech and crypto, energy, semiconductors, robotics, and deep tech, investing from seed through late-stage growth with an increasingly concentrated, high-conviction style (its recent growth funds put hundreds of millions of dollars into a small number of companies). Founders Fund manages roughly $17 billion in assets as of 2025 and is headquartered at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in San Francisco's Presidio. Its portfolio includes many of the defining technology companies of the era, among them SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Stripe, Airbnb, Facebook, Neuralink, OpenAI, DeepMind, Ramp, Nubank, Spotify, and Figma.
f.name: Founders Fund

f.description: Foundry Group is a Boulder, Colorado venture capital firm founded in 2007 by Brad Feld, Seth Levine, Ryan McIntyre, and Jason Mendelson. The firm invests in early-stage technology startups across the United States, organizing its work around long-lived, horizontal investment themes (such as "glue", "protocol", "distribution", and "human computer interaction") rather than narrow verticals, with a particular affinity for hardware, robotics, consumer internet, developer tools, and B2B SaaS. Foundry pioneered a "network-driven" model that operates both as a direct investor in startups and as a limited partner in a curated network of more than 40 partner venture funds. The firm manages more than $3.0B for its limited partners, has made 320+ investments and 70+ exits, and is known for radical transparency through the books, blogs, and podcasts of its partners. Notable investments include Fitbit, Zynga, SendGrid, MakerBot, Gnip, Mapbox, SeatGeek, and WHOOP. In 2022 the partners announced Foundry would not raise another fund, continuing to steward its existing funds and portfolio through their life.
f.name: Foundry Group

f.description: Fountain is a high-volume, frontline hourly hiring and workforce management platform used by enterprises to source, screen, schedule, and hire large numbers of hourly workers. The Fountain Developer API (Hire API v2) lets customers programmatically manage applicants, openings, positions, stages, labels, documents, scheduling slots, and webhooks across their hiring funnels.
f.name: Fountain

f.description: Four Pillars is a research-driven blockchain enterprise headquartered in Asia, operating through three divisions: FP Research publishes primary analysis of crypto protocols, markets, and policy with deep regional expertise across Korea and the broader Asian market; FP Validated runs validator and node infrastructure across proof-of-stake networks, pairing research with live operations; and FP Institution advises banks, financial institutions, and corporates on blockchain strategy. The firm serves founders, funds, and regulators, and is a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. It is a research and advisory business rather than a developer-facing API platform, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal as of this enrichment pass.
f.name: Four Pillars

f.description: Fourier is an energy technology company building on-site, on-demand hydrogen production systems. Its core product is a modular, scalable device that generates hydrogen where it is needed, removing the transport and storage barriers of conventional hydrogen supply. Fourier targets three application areas: long-duration distributed storage for renewable energy, alternative fuels for heavy transportation, and cleaner feedstock for chemical and manufacturing industries. The company commercially launched its onsite hydrogen system in late 2025 and raised an $18.5M Series A led by Paramark Ventures and General Catalyst. Fourier is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software developer surface.
f.name: Fourier

f.description: Fourier (Fourier Intelligence, founded 2015 and headquartered in Shanghai, China) is a full-stack robotics company that develops core robot technology and finished robot products. It began in rehabilitation robotics — exoskeletons and upper/lower-limb rehab devices such as the ArmMotus and ExoMotus lines and the RehabHub intelligent rehabilitation ecosystem — and has expanded into general-purpose humanoid robots (the GRx series, including GR-1 and GR-2), smart actuators (FSA), and dexterous hands. Fourier publishes first-party developer SDKs for robot control through its FFTAI GitHub organization: the RoCS (Robot Control System / General Robotics OS) client libraries for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the fourier-grx control stack for the GRx humanoid series. Fourier is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. These are device/robot-control developer libraries rather than a hosted web API; the company publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface.
f.name: Fourier Intelligence

f.description: FourKites is a real-time supply chain visibility platform that tracks shipments and assets across road, rail, ocean, and yard modes worldwide.
f.name: FourKites

f.description: Foursquare is a location intelligence platform that maintains a global graph of more than 100 million points of interest (POI) and provides developer APIs and SDKs for place search, geotagging, autocomplete, audience measurement, and visit detection across web and mobile.
f.name: Foursquare

f.description: Fourth is an AI-powered workforce management and inventory platform built for restaurants and hospitality, uniting recruiting, HR, payroll, labor scheduling, purchasing, and inventory management in a single system across 120,000+ locations globally (customers include Taco Bell, Dunkin', KFC, Pizza Hut and Culver's). Its product family includes HotSchedules for scheduling, Fourth iQ for restaurant performance, Human Capital Management for talent and payroll, and Adaco inventory for hotels. Fourth publishes a developer portal of REST APIs covering POS transactions, recipe & menu engineering, menu cycles, workforce (UK employee, labor productivity, schedules), notifications, tasks, SCIM identity provisioning, and Adaco hotel inventory. APIs authenticate with OAuth 2.0 (client_credentials and password grants) or Basic Auth; production and test host locations are provisioned per mutual customer and are not publicly disclosed.
f.name: Fourth

f.description: Fourth Power is a grid-scale thermal energy storage company building a "thermal battery" that stores electricity as heat. Surplus wind and solar power is used to heat blocks of graphite to roughly 2,400 degrees Celsius; molten tin, circulated by an all-ceramic pump, moves that heat in and out of storage, and thermophotovoltaic (TPV) cells convert the stored heat back into electricity when the grid needs it. The company positions the system as a cheaper, longer-duration alternative to lithium-ion for firming a clean grid, and operates a megawatt-scale demonstration facility near Boston. Fourth Power raised a Series A led by DCVC in 2023. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fourth Power is a hardware and energy company and does not publish a public developer API.
f.name: Fourth Power

f.description: Fourthwall is a creator commerce platform for building a branded online shop and storefront, selling physical merch, digital products, memberships, and accepting donations and gifts. It exposes a public Storefront API (storefront token) for headless product/collection/cart experiences and a Platform / Open API (Basic Auth API key or OAuth) for managing orders, products, promotions, gifting, memberships, and webhooks.
f.name: Fourthwall

f.description: Fox Factory Holding Corp. (NASDAQ: FOXF) designs and manufactures performance ride dynamics products — FOX suspension for mountain bikes, trucks and powersports vehicles, plus Race Face and Easton Cycling components, Method Race Wheels, Tensor Tire and Marucci Sports. It runs no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, but its direct-to-consumer storefronts do expose a real, callable agent surface: ridefox.com serves a live Model Context Protocol endpoint implementing the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP 2026-08-25) at https://ridefox.com/api/ucp/mcp, answering an anonymous tools/list with 13 tools for catalog search, product lookup, cart lifecycle, checkout lifecycle and order retrieval. The store also publishes llms.txt and agents.md agent instructions, a UCP merchant profile, and OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery documents for customer accounts. The same surface is served by the Race Face, Easton Cycling and Method Race Wheels storefronts.
f.name: Fox Factory Holding

f.description: Fox Rothschild LLP is a national US law firm with approximately 1,000 attorneys across 30+ offices. The firm has no public developer APIs. Its programmatic surface is limited to publication and content distribution: subscription-based email alerts and 21+ topical attorney-authored blogs hosted on the LexBlog (WordPress) platform, each of which exposes a standard WordPress RSS 2.0 feed at /feed/. This index catalogs the firm and the RSS-able LexBlog network as the consumable surface.
f.name: Fox Rothschild

f.description: FOX-TECH CO. is a New Taipei City, Taiwan IoT company (founded 2016, backed by 500 Global and SparkLabs Taipei) that digitally transforms farming, logistics, cold-chain, and manufacturing operations. Its TempHawk platform pairs wireless temperature, humidity, CO2, light-intensity and soil-EC sensors over Sigfox LPWAN with web and mobile apps and cloud data analytics, helping the perishable-goods value chain monitor conditions, manage risk, and meet policy compliance. Recognized on the Forward Fooding FoodTech 500. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published.
f.name: Fox-Tech

f.description: Foxconn Industrial Internet Co., Ltd. (FII, 工业富联) is a Shanghai Stock Exchange-listed subsidiary of Hon Hai Precision Industry (Foxconn), headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It is a smart-manufacturing and industrial-internet company producing cloud computing infrastructure and AI servers, communication and networking equipment, and precision tooling, and it offers factory-automation, lighthouse-factory, and industrial-internet platform services for global electronics OEMs. FII operates as a contract manufacturer and industrial platform rather than a public API provider: it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal. This profile tracks the company's corporate identity in the API Evangelist network; there is no API artifact surface to enrich.
f.name: Foxconn Industrial Internet

f.description: Foxglove Technologies, Inc. (foxglove.dev) builds a multimodal data platform for robotics, autonomy and physical AI. Its products cover visualization and debugging of robot data (3D scenes, images, plots, logs, maps), cloud and self-hosted data infrastructure for recording ingest and retention, fleet and device management, and an agent layer that lets AI assistants inspect recordings. Foxglove publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 REST API at api.foxglove.dev/v1 for devices, recordings, sessions, events, event types, custom properties, sites, tokens, extensions and layouts; a webhook event surface; SDKs for Python, Rust, C++, C, Go and TypeScript; a Go CLI; and the open-source MCAP container format and Foxglove message schemas.
f.name: Foxglove Technologies

f.description: Foxintelligence was a French e-commerce measurement and consumer-insights company that aggregated anonymized online purchase data from email receipts across millions of e-shoppers to give brands and retailers competitive intelligence on where, when, and how much consumers buy online. It was acquired by NielsenIQ and operates today as the "NIQ Digital Purchases" product; the original www.foxintelligence.io domain now 301-redirects to nielseniq.com. The surviving first-party surface is the customer web application at app.foxintelligence.io (login only). No public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation is published; this profile is maintained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.
f.name: Foxintelligence

f.description: Foxit Software provides Foxit eSign, a solution that enables organizations to send, sign, and manage agreements through secure electronic signature workflows. The service is offered to businesses that need to handle legally binding signatures, integrate signing into document processes, and manage signed documents at scale. It is part of Foxit’s broader portfolio of PDF and document productivity tools.
f.name: Foxit eSign

f.description: Foxtons Group plc is a London-focused UK estate agency, founded in 1981 and listed on the London Stock Exchange, running residential sales, lettings and property management from roughly 40 branches across London and Surrey, plus independent mortgage broking through its Alexander Hall subsidiary. It sits on the brokerage rung of the value chain — it originates and holds the client and the listing rather than operating a portal or a data exchange — and distributes its stock to Rightmove and Zoopla through the UK's portal feed arrangements rather than through any shared cooperative, because the UK has no MLS. Its technology is deliberately proprietary: an internally built CRM/ERP called BOS underpins the whole business, and the My Foxtons customer portal is the consumer face of that same system. API posture, stated honestly, is none-published — no developer or partner portal, no api./developer./docs. host resolves, no OpenAPI or OData contract is served, and the only machine-readable public surface is schema.org JSON-LD embedded in its web pages. RESO is absent, as expected outside North America. The genuinely open UK property data layer belongs to government (HM Land Registry, Ordnance Survey), not to Foxtons.
f.name: Foxtons

f.description: Foxtrot (Foxtrot Market, foxtrotco.com) is a Chicago-based retail chain of upscale convenience stores and cafes combining a neighborhood corner store with a coffee shop and a curated selection of local and specialty food, drink, and grocery goods, plus on-demand delivery and pickup. Surfaced as a portfolio company of d1-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment the public site (foxtrotco.com) is a minimal placeholder and the company exposes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.
f.name: Foxtrot

f.description: Foxy.io (formerly FoxyCart) is a developer-focused shopping cart and e-commerce platform providing a hosted hypermedia REST API (hAPI) for managing products, customers, subscriptions, transactions, and order workflows. The platform supports physical products, digital goods, subscriptions, donations, and services, and integrates with 100+ payment gateways including Stripe, PayPal, and Square. The API uses HATEOAS design with OAuth 2.0 authentication and has processed over $3 billion in transactions globally.
f.name: Foxy.io

f.description: Fractal Software (fractalsoftware.com) is a venture studio that partners with entrepreneurs and investors to launch AI-driven vertical SaaS companies that transform how whole industries operate. Rather than shipping a single product, Fractal functions as an incubator and holding company, standing up sector-specific software startups across produce, healthcare, government, storage, distribution, and security-services verticals, with more than $650M raised across its portfolio. As a venture studio it exposes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation of its own; this profile captures its identity, portfolio surface, and domain-security posture. Note the recorded x-backed-by (multicoin, paradigm, a16z, 8vc) was surfaced via name-matching during portfolio ingestion and may conflate a distinct crypto-era "Fractal"; the enriched identity below reflects the fractalsoftware.com venture studio.
f.name: Fractal

f.description: Fractal Analytics Limited (fractal.ai) is an enterprise artificial intelligence services and products company founded in 2000, headquartered in New York with a large delivery footprint in India and roughly 5,000 employees across 18 global locations. Fractal sells AI consulting, data engineering, decision-science and design services to Fortune 500 clients in consumer packaged goods, retail, healthcare and life sciences, technology/media/telecom, financial services, insurance and industrials, and builds products on top of that practice — most notably Cogentiq, its enterprise agentic AI platform (with MCP and agent gateways, low-code agent builder and pre-built domain agents), LLM Studio, and consumer/vertical brands including Flyfish, Asper.ai, Kalaido.ai, Vaidya.ai and iqigai. The company listed on the NSE and BSE under the symbol FRACTAL in February 2026. Its API surface is delivered inside client engagements and gated product tenants rather than through a public developer program: as of this profiling pass Fractal publishes no public developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API contract, and no hosted MCP server or A2A agent card.
f.name: Fractal Analytics

f.description: Fractile is a UK-based semiconductor startup, founded in 2022 and headquartered in London with an engineering base in Bristol, designing a new class of AI inference processors. Its architecture physically interleaves memory and compute to overcome the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that limits large language model inference, targeting frontier model serving up to 25x faster and at roughly 1/10th the cost of existing hardware. The company takes a full-stack approach spanning transistor-level circuit design through cloud inference server logic, and in May 2026 raised $220M to build the next generation of inference hardware. Backers include Accel and Felicis. Led by founder and CEO Walter Goodwin, Fractile is a hardware/compute company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
f.name: Fractile

f.description: Fractyl Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GUTS) is a clinical-stage metabolic therapeutics company developing treatments that target the root causes of type 2 diabetes and obesity rather than managing symptoms. Its lead product, Revita, is an outpatient endoscopic procedure that resurfaces the duodenal lining to address a driver of metabolic disease, and Rejuva is an early-stage pancreatic islet-cell gene therapy platform designed for durable, one-time metabolic remission. The company is headquartered in Massachusetts and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst. Fractyl publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its corporate, product, and investor web presence.
f.name: Fractyl Health

f.description: Fragment is a ledger API for engineering teams. It provides a real-time, double-entry ledger to track money movement, model balances, and reconcile against external systems (banks, processors, PSPs). The product is GraphQL-first - developers define a Schema (chart of accounts and entry types), create Ledgers, post immutable Ledger Entries composed of balanced debit/credit lines, and read balances and lines back through a single GraphQL endpoint. Every write mutation is idempotent.
f.name: Fragment

f.description: Frame Technology Corp. was a software company that developed FrameMaker, a structured desktop-publishing and technical-documentation authoring application widely used for long, complex documents. Founded in the 1980s and taken public, Frame Technology was acquired by Adobe Systems in 1995; FrameMaker continues today as an Adobe product. This is a historical/acquired portfolio company of Canaan Partners with no independent developer or API surface of its own.
f.name: Frame

f.description: Frame Payments is a payments and compliance platform ("operating system") for high-compliance and high-risk merchants across regulated verticals including travel, crypto, telemedicine, gaming, gambling, the creator economy, and AI businesses. The frameOS platform unifies payments, payouts, KYC/KYB, identity verification, fraud detection (Sonar), geocompliance, disputes, subscriptions, and usage-based billing behind one REST API at api.framepayments.com/v1. Frame ships backend SDKs (Node, PHP, Ruby), mobile SDKs (iOS, Android, React Native), the Frame.js browser SDK with embeddable elements, a sandbox-only CLI, and HMAC-signed webhooks. Backed by Techstars.
f.name: Frame Payments

f.description: Frame Security is an AI-powered human risk management and security awareness platform that defends organizations against human-targeted attacks such as phishing, deepfakes, and social engineering. Frame generates personalized security awareness training in 70+ languages, hyper-realistic email, voice, and video phishing and deepfake simulations built from an organization's own context, employee risk scoring with targeted interventions, automated phishing triage of reported suspicious emails, and cross-platform reporting and integrations. The company is backed by Index Ventures and raised a $50M round in 2026.
f.name: Frame Security

f.description: Frame.io is a cloud-based video review and collaboration platform, now part of Adobe, used by video and media production teams to upload media, leave frame-accurate comments, manage versions, and route work through review and approval. Its V4 developer platform exposes a REST API (base https://api.frame.io/v4) covering accounts, workspaces, projects, folders, files and uploads, comments, version stacks, shares and reviewers, collections, groups, custom actions, metadata fields, and webhooks. Authentication is OAuth2 via Adobe IMS (authorization-code for user apps and client-credentials for server-to-server), plus a Camera to Cloud (C2C) device-integration surface, an official Python SDK, the fioctl CLI, and a hosted MCP server.
f.name: Frame.io

f.description: Framed (framed.io), formerly Framed Data, was a GV-backed predictive-analytics / customer churn-prediction machine-learning startup. As of 2026 the framed.io domain no longer hosts a product or developer surface: it serves a static Squarespace landing page titled "Framed + Square" that points visitors to Square Capital (squareup.com/capital), indicating the team/product moved to Square. No API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable artifact surface survives, so there is nothing to enrich against; this record is retained as a dormant/acquired lead.
f.name: Framed *

f.description: Framer is a design tool and CMS for shipping production websites without code. The Framer developer surface is centred on in-editor extensibility: the Plugin API for building tools that interact with the Framer Editor and CMS, Code Components for custom React components, Code Overrides for HOC-style mutations, and Fetch for letting designers wire site content to external APIs without code. Framer does not publish a general-purpose REST API for site management at the time of reconciliation.
f.name: Framer

f.description: FrameThrower is a film-still reference library for filmmakers, students and creative teams, indexed frame by frame on lighting, lens character, shot size, camera angle, colour palette, mood and era. A REST API (OpenAPI 3.1 at https://framethrower.ai/api/v1/openapi.json, 11 endpoints, bearer-token auth) and an MCP server at https://framethrower.ai/api/mcp (four tools, OAuth 2.1) expose visual-reference search and film and frame information; an npm SDK (framethrower-ai) and an MIT-licensed MCP repository (github.com/framethrower-ai/framethrower-mcp) are published. Free plan with usage-based paid upgrades. Submitter-stated by the founder, Leo Kadieff.
f.name: FrameThrower

f.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. The platform pulls patient data from electronic health records over any FHIR R4 endpoint, generates discharge and treatment-adherence education tailored to the individual using institutional protocols and drug-information databases, and delivers it by SMS in 75+ languages with no app and no login. It then tracks patient comprehension in real time, giving care teams engagement data to flag which patients need follow-up. Framewise integrates with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), Athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks, and NextGen, and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant with an AWS BAA and end-to-end encryption. It targets hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and private clinics seeking to improve patient outcomes and medication adherence.
f.name: Framewise Health

f.description: Francis Medical is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota, founded in 2018 by Michael Hoey and named for his father, who died of prostate cancer in 1991. It develops the Vanquish Water Vapor Ablation System, a transurethral outpatient platform that ablates targeted prostate tissue using the thermal energy stored in sterile water vapor delivered in short bursts through a catheter, with the aim of treating localized disease while avoiding the incontinence and sexual dysfunction associated with radical prostatectomy and radiation. The company received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in 2023 and 510(k) clearance for prostate tissue ablation in December 2025, and it is running the VAPOR 1 and VAPOR 2 clinical studies alongside a long-term registry; it has signalled intent to extend the same water vapor platform to bladder and kidney cancer. Francis Medical has raised roughly $160 million to date, including an $80 million Series C in January 2025 co-led by Solas BioVentures and Arboretum Ventures, with earlier participation from Coloplast. It is led by president and CEO Mike Kujak. Francis Medical publishes a physician locator, an electronic instructions-for-use (eIFU) library and a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy for its devices and embedded software, but operates no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.
f.name: Francis Medical

f.description: FranConnect is a franchise and multi-location management platform used by 1,500+ brands across roughly one million locations, covering franchise development and sales, franchisee/unit information management, field operations and audits, financials and royalties, and CRM. Its FranConnect Sky product exposes a RESTful API - organized by module (Franchise Sales "fs", CRM "cm", Info Manager "fim", Finance "manage-finance", and Admin "admin") - that lets customers import and export data between FranConnect Sky and third-party applications. All API calls are made over HTTPS and authenticated with an Authorization-Token header. API access is not open/self-serve - it is gated behind a FranConnect Sky customer or partner account, with credentials provisioned by FranConnect, and the reference documentation portal (docs.franconnect.net) requires a signed-in account.
f.name: FranConnect

f.description: Frankford Candy & Chocolate Company is a privately held, family-owned confectionery manufacturer headquartered in the Frankford neighborhood of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Founded in 1947 by Russian immigrant Sam Himmelstein, the company describes itself as the "#1 Marketer of Licensed Confectionary in the United States," producing licensed novelty candy, holiday plush, hot chocolate bombs, gummies, Valentine heart boxes, and seasonal collectibles under partnerships with M&M's, Hershey, Pez, Oreo, Sour Patch Kids, Peeps, Welch's, Jif, Kraft, Disney, Marvel, Netflix, Nickelodeon, Minecraft, Super Mario, SpongeBob, Stitch, Care Bears, Elf on the Shelf, Baskin-Robbins, Dunkin', KFC, and Smucker's. Frankford acquired the Cap Candy and Wonder Ball lines from Hasbro and Nestlé in the 2000s and is one of the largest producers of chocolate Easter rabbits in the United States. This repository captures the publicly observable web surface for Frankford Candy; the company exposes no public developer API, portal, SDK, status page, or machine-readable artifacts.
f.name: Frankford Candy

f.description: Frankfurter is an open-source (MIT) currency exchange rates API that blends foreign-exchange reference rates published by 50+ central banks and monetary authorities. It hosts a free, no-key public endpoint at api.frankfurter.dev (current v2 and frozen v1) and ships as a Docker image for unlimited self-hosting. Historical data extends back to 1948 and covers 201 currencies; the API serves JSON, NDJSON, and CSV.
f.name: Frankfurter

f.description: FrankieOne is an identity verification, compliance, and fraud prevention platform connecting applications to hundreds of global data sources through a single API for KYC, KYB, document IDV, ongoing monitoring, and matchlist management.
f.name: FrankieOne

f.description: Franklin Resources, doing business as Franklin Templeton, is a global investment management organization offering investment management and related services to retail, institutional, and high net worth clients. It ran a public developer program — the "Detailed Product APIs", seven read-only fund reference, NAV, distribution and AUM operations at api.franklintempleton.com/v1, fronted by a portal at developer.franklintempleton.com — and retired it without a published deprecation notice. Both hosts now have no DNS record; the Swagger 2.0 contract is still served publicly from Franklin Templeton's own SwaggerHub organization, and the company publishes a first-party llms.txt on its main site.
f.name: Franklin Resources

f.description: Franklin Whole Home (FranklinWH Energy Storage Inc.) builds whole-home energy management and storage hardware for residential solar: the aPower lithium iron phosphate AC battery, the aGate energy management and controller unit, and the FranklinWH mobile app, together forming an ecosystem that coordinates solar, battery, grid, generator and EV power sources for backup, self-consumption, time-of-use arbitrage and off-grid operation. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, the company designs and manufactures nearly all of its own components and sells through a certified installer and distributor channel. FranklinWH publishes a partner API - a unified developer access platform for authorised third-party owners, financiers, installers and service providers to read device and site data, monitor system performance, receive operational alerts and perform approved remote device control.
f.name: Franklin Whole Home

f.description: Frappe is a fully featured, low-code web framework written in Python and JavaScript that powers ERPNext, the open-source ERP for accounting, inventory, payroll, and operations. The Frappe REST API auto-exposes every DocType for CRUD plus whitelisted Python method calls.
f.name: Frappe

f.description: Fraud.net (FraudNet) is an enterprise fraud, risk and compliance platform used by payment processors, acquirers, PSPs, fintechs, banks and digital commerce platforms. Its Public API is a risk-decisioning surface: Check operations submit a transaction, order, loan application, account application or login for real-time scoring, and Update operations relay the eventual outcome (approved, declined, chargeback, fraud disposition) back so the models keep learning. Every Check returns a 0-100 risk score, a risk group and rule tags, drawn from supervised models, anomaly detection and a global anti-fraud network, alongside device fingerprinting, identity, entity screening and AML/KYC-adjacent compliance workflows.
f.name: Fraud.net

f.description: Fraudio is an Amsterdam-based payments fraud detection and financial-crime scale-up founded in 2019 by João Moura (CEO), Nathan Trousdell (COO), and team, with additional offices in London, Lisbon, and Barcelona. Fraudio delivers AI- and machine-learning-driven fraud detection as a managed service to merchant acquirers, payment service providers, card issuers, and banks, with a product line that covers card payment fraud, merchant initiated fraud, anti-money laundering, authorised push payment (APP) fraud, and money mule detection. The company markets itself as "Generation 3" fraud detection, advancing past rule-based (Gen 1) and bespoke per-customer ML (Gen 2) approaches by training a single centralized "patent pending AI super brain" on the pooled transaction history of all of its customers, claiming network-effect performance gains versus single-tenant models. Fraudio integrates with customers through a plug-and-play real-time scoring API with sub-100ms response times, configurable risk-appetite thresholds, and no upfront integration or setup cost. Customers include Viva Wallet, Silverflow, Pismo, Bancontact, Fazz, PayTabs, IXOPAY, Bold.co, SaltPay, WiPay, ePayco, and LOQR. Fraudio is ISO 27001 certified, was selected for the Visa Innovation Program (2023), is co-financed by the EU Lisboa 2030 programme, has raised roughly $3.3M seed plus a Series A round (March 2025), and counts BigStar Ventures, BYND Venture Capital, Teya, Viva Wallet, Portugal Ventures, Iberis Capital, Shilling, and CTT among its investors. There is no public developer portal, no open API reference, no public OpenAPI spec, no SDK, and no GitHub organization — the fraud-scoring API is delivered as a gated B2B integration through a commercial sales process.
f.name: Fraudio

f.description: Screen order information using AI to detect frauds
f.name: FraudLabs Pro

f.description: Fraugster is a Berlin-based artificial intelligence company focused on payment fraud prevention and transaction risk scoring for online merchants, payment service providers, and acquirers. Its machine-learning platform was designed to analyze payments in real time to detect and block fraudulent transactions while reducing false declines and chargebacks. The company was surfaced through venture portfolio data (backed by Seedcamp) and added to the API Evangelist network. During this enrichment pass the company's public developer surface was not reachable to automated clients (the primary domain returns HTTP 403), so no API specifications, SDKs, or documentation could be harvested; only live infrastructure/domain-security signals were probed.
f.name: Fraugster

f.description: Frax Finance is a fractional-algorithmic stablecoin protocol offering FRAX (USD-pegged stablecoin), FPI (Frax Price Index stablecoin pegged to a consumer goods basket), frxETH (liquid ETH staking derivative), and supporting DeFi infrastructure including Fraxswap, Fraxlend, and Fraxtal L2. The protocol operates Algorithmic Market Operations (AMOs) to manage collateral and generate revenue, and exposes public REST APIs for querying token supply, collateral ratios, AMO positions, pool APRs, and frxETH staking analytics.
f.name: Frax Finance

f.description: Frax Finance is a fractional-algorithmic stablecoin protocol featuring FRAX (a stablecoin), FXS (Frax Shares governance token), and Fraxswap — a TWAMM-based AMM DEX. The protocol is deployed across multiple chains and exposes its on-chain data via The Graph subgraphs.
f.name: Frax Finance

f.description: FRAYT (Frayt Technologies, Inc., Cincinnati, Ohio) operates an on-demand and scheduled middle-mile and last-mile delivery marketplace that connects shippers to a vetted nationwide network of owner-operator drivers running everything from cars and midsize vehicles to pickups, cargo vans and box trucks. The FRAYT Client API is a versioned REST API (v2.2) over JSON, secured with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials bearer tokens, that lets a TMS, ERP or storefront price a delivery as an "estimate", authorize it into a "match", track it through the driver lifecycle, tip a driver and cancel it — with webhook callbacks defined in the OpenAPI itself for real-time match and driver-location updates. A full sandbox environment mirrors production.
f.name: FRAYT

f.description: Frazer Consultants is a funeral-home technology company providing all-in-one death-care software - responsive funeral home websites, the FrazerGO funeral home management system, Tribute Pay payments, the Tribute Store (flowers, gifts, trees), and the Tribute Center (tribute videos, personalized stationery, and live or delayed webcasting). Frazer is now part of Tribute Technology, and its products connect into the Tribute Technology full-stack platform. Frazer markets an "open-source API" that lets its websites integrate with third-party data management, call forwarding, and webcasting software, and Tribute Technology connects Premier Partners to its Platform Services through proprietary APIs. However, as of this writing there is NO public developer portal, no published API reference, and no self-serve OpenAPI - API/integration access is partner-gated and arranged directly with Frazer / Tribute Technology. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the access model rather than a documented public API.
f.name: Frazer Consultants

f.description: Frec is a San Francisco fintech offering tax-aware, automated direct indexing for retail investors. Its products — Classic Direct Indexing, Long Short Direct Indexing, Diversify, Trade, Treasury cash management, and a Portfolio Line of Credit — replicate market indices with individual stocks while running automated tax-loss harvesting to minimize capital gains taxes at fees starting around 0.09%. Frec is an SEC-registered investment adviser and SIPC member managing over $1.25B in assets, founded by Mo Al Adham and backed by Greylock. The company ships a consumer investing app and website but does not currently expose a public developer API, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.
f.name: Frec

f.description: Freckle is an adaptive learning platform from Renaissance that delivers differentiated, standards-aligned math and English Language Arts (ELA) practice for K-12 students. Teachers assign work and monitor progress while students practice at their own level, with the platform adapting question difficulty to each learner across 70,000+ math questions and 1,000+ ELA passages. Administrators manage rosters and dashboards at the school and district level. Freckle is a school- and classroom-facing application acquired by Renaissance Learning; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.
f.name: Freckle Education

f.description: The Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) API is a public web service operated by the Research Division of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. It provides programmatic access to more than 800,000 economic time series drawn from 100+ data sources (BLS, BEA, OECD, World Bank, Census, Treasury, Eurostat, Federal Reserve Board, and others). The API exposes five primary endpoint families — Categories, Releases, Series, Sources, and Tags — plus an Observations endpoint that returns the underlying data values for any series, with optional frequency aggregation, unit transformations, and real-time / ALFRED vintage support. A companion Maps (GeoFRED) API surfaces regional data and GeoJSON shape files. All endpoints are HTTPS, return XML or JSON (CSV / Excel for observations), and require a free API key.
f.name: FRED

f.description: Freddie Mac (Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation) is the government-sponsored enterprise that provides liquidity, stability and affordability to the U.S. housing market by purchasing and securitizing single-family and multifamily mortgages. Its Single-Family API programme is published through the Freddie Mac Developer Portal and spans the whole mortgage lifecycle: origination (Affordable Check, Income Limits, Loan Look Up, Property Insights, Current Mortgage Snapshot, Beyond ACE), closing (Loan Closing Advisor Loan Submission), selling and delivery (Cash and Guarantor Pricing, Committing and Settlement Purchase Statement, Loan Import into Loan Selling Advisor), post-close data retrieval (Loan Advisor Data Share, Data Share Bid Tape) and default servicing (the Resolve workout, liquidation and valuation/pricing decisioning services). The public catalog publishes 20 OpenAPI 3.0 contracts covering 45 operations; the request and response payloads are modelled on the MISMO reference model and the GSE Uniform Mortgage Data Program datasets (UAD, ULAD, ULDD, UCD).
f.name: Freddie Mac

f.description: Free Agency is a careers company and talent marketplace that pairs technology professionals with an AI-powered Talent Agent which proactively surfaces relevant work — full-time roles and short project engagements with defined deliverables, duration, and compensation. Founded by Sherveen Mashayekhi and backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company has raised a $10M Series A and counts talent placed at companies such as OpenAI, Stripe, and Figma. It also publishes Intent, a newsletter for careerists, and runs CareerMakers, a cohort course hosted on Maven. As of August 2026 the entire public surface is a single waitlist landing page with two Tally intake forms — one for individual talent and one "For AI companies" — plus the Intent newsletter and an Ashby-hosted job board. Free Agency exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind; this profile tracks it in the API Evangelist network as a company stub with a probed, verified absence rather than an unexamined gap.
f.name: Free Agency

f.description: The Free Cocktail API is a resource that provides access to a vast database of cocktail recipes, ingredients, and images.
f.name: Free Cocktail API

f.description: Free Currency API provides real-time and historical currency exchange rate data for 150+ currencies via a simple REST API. No registration is required for basic usage, making it ideal for hobby and development projects. The API offers daily-updated current exchange rates, historical rates dating back to 1999, and multi-currency support with official SDKs for JavaScript, Python, PHP, Go, Ruby, Rust, C#, and R.
f.name: Free Currency API

f.description: Definitions, phonetics, pronounciations, parts of speech, examples, synonyms
f.name: Free Dictionary

f.description: Free Exercise DB is an open, public-domain exercise dataset published by yuhonas on GitHub: 873 individual JSON documents describing strength, stretching, plyometric, powerlifting, olympic-weightlifting, strongman and cardio exercises, each with a stable id, name, difficulty level, force and mechanic classification, required equipment, primary and secondary muscle groups, step-by-step instructions and demonstration images. Every record validates against a published JSON Schema (draft-04) that also acts as the project's controlled vocabulary for muscles, equipment and categories. There is no REST API and no OpenAPI: consumption is by unauthenticated HTTPS GET of the combined dist/exercises.json array (or of a single exercise document) from raw.githubusercontent.com, with images served from the same host. A Vue.js browsable/searchable frontend is published to GitHub Pages. The whole dataset is released under the Unlicense.
f.name: Free Exercise DB

f.description: Free Law Project is a non-profit organization that seeks to increase access to justice and transparency in the legal system through the use of technology and open data.
f.name: Free Law Project

f.description: FREE NOW is one of Europe's leading multi-mobility "super apps," letting riders book taxis and private-hire vehicles and, in many cities, e-scooters, e-bikes, e-mopeds, carsharing and public-transport tickets from a single application. Founded in Hamburg in 2009 as mytaxi and rebranded FREE NOW in 2019, the company operates across nine European countries and 150+ cities. It ran as part of the YOUR NOW mobility joint venture between Mercedes-Benz and BMW and was acquired by Lyft. FREE NOW exposes a partner/business integration API (FREE NOW for Business) through a password-gated developer portal at developer.free-now.com, and maintains an active open-source presence — including the Wave design system — under the freenowtech GitHub organization.
f.name: FREE NOW
