g.description: GunTab is a payment processing service designed for online firearms marketplaces and retail websites. The GunTab API enables businesses to integrate safe and convenient firearms transaction payments into their platforms.
g.name: GunTab

g.description: Gunzilla Games is a AAA game developer founded in 2020 with studios in Frankfurt, Kyiv and London, best known for the cyberpunk battle-royale shooter Off The Grid. Alongside the game the studio operates GUNZ, a permissioned Avalanche L1 (subnet) blockchain purpose-built for game developers, with GUN as its native gas coin. The public technical surface is EVM-shaped: a public Ethereum/Subnet-EVM JSON-RPC node at rpc.gunzchain.io (chain ID 43419), a mirrored Avalanche-hosted RPC, and the GUNZScan block explorer at gunzscan.io, which exposes a Blockscout REST v2 API, an Etherscan-compatible module/action API, an open GraphQL endpoint and a WebSocket subscription surface. A gated marketplace/minting API sits behind api.gunztoken.io.
g.name: Gunzilla Games

g.description: Guokang (国康私人医生 / Guokang Private Doctor, 深圳市国康健康管理服务有限公司) is a Shenzhen-based corporate and personal health-management service provider founded in 2005. It positions itself as one of China's leading health-management companies, integrating more than 1,000 domestic and international medical resources — private physicians, specialist experts, tertiary hospitals, and health-examination centers — to deliver private doctor services, family medical-care programs, and corporate health services such as medical screening, employee assistance programs (EAP), group insurance, and on-site corporate health centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture network; no public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment (the site is served behind a Huawei Cloud WAF).
g.name: guokang

g.description: Gupshup is a conversational messaging and CPaaS platform (headquartered in India) that lets businesses send and receive messages across WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, and other channels, plus build chatbots and conversational AI journeys. The developer platform exposes REST APIs on api.gupshup.io - most prominently the WhatsApp Business API (send session and template messages, opt-in management, templates, media, and inbound webhooks) - authenticated with an apikey header and scoped to a registered app. Separate SMS, RCS, and Partner API surfaces are also documented.
g.name: Gupshup

g.description: Fast and Accurate Gurbani RESTful API
g.name: GurbaniNow

g.description: Guru is an AI-powered knowledge management and enterprise search platform that captures company knowledge into verifiable cards organized into collections, surfaces answers directly inside the apps employees already use (Slack, Chrome, Microsoft Teams, Salesforce), and uses AI to keep content trusted and up to date. The Guru REST API provides programmatic access to cards, collections, boards, users, groups, tags, analytics, and verifications. Authentication uses HTTP Basic Auth with a user token or Collection token generated by a Guru admin.
g.name: Guru

g.description: GuruHotel is AI-native direct-booking infrastructure for independent hotels: an AI-powered hotel website builder, a conversion-optimized direct booking engine, and a Stripe-powered payment-orchestration platform that turns a hotel's official website into a commission-free direct booking channel with real-time inventory, multi-currency checkout and a guest-first experience. Founded in 2019, GuruHotel is trusted by 1000+ hotels, serves 200,000+ guests a year and processes $15M+ in annual gross booking value across the United States, Mexico, the Caribbean and Europe. It connects to hotel PMS platforms directly (Cloudbeds) and through Channex (280+ PMS incl. Mews, apaleo, Oracle OPERA Cloud, Guesty, Hostaway), plus Google for Hotels. GuruHotel is a portfolio company of 500 Global and Anthemis.
g.name: GuruHotel

g.description: Gurú de Viaje is a Mexico-based travel-deals company and flight-deal hunter ("cazador de ofertas de viaje") that publishes daily cheap-flight promotions and airfare offers so travelers can fly cheaply and see the world. Its Spanish-language consumer website and mobile/push experience surface daily discounted airline tickets and travel promotions, with a focus on departures from Mexican cities such as Guadalajara and Mexico City. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass Gurú de Viaje operates a consumer Next.js web property (gurudeviaje.com) and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.
g.name: Gurú de Viaje

g.description: Gust is a comprehensive platform that empowers entrepreneurs to start, grow, and fund their ventures. It offers tools for company formation, fundraising, investor relations, and access to a vast network of accelerators and angel groups. With over 800,000 founders, Gust provides educational resources, benchmarking, and a marketplace for startup services, making it a central hub for the startup ecosystem.
g.name: Gust

g.description: Gustav is a vendor management platform (VMS) and sub-vendor marketplace for the staffing industry, enabling staffing firms to source talent from their trusted vendor network, share open jobs, collect and screen candidate submissions, run standardized hiring pipelines, schedule interviews, message vendors, and track performance in one place. Vendors organize into "Gustav Circles" with tiered job-release controls, and candidate submissions sync to applicant tracking systems including Bullhorn and JobDiva. Originally a Speedinvest-backed startup, Gustav is now operated by the member-owned Fuse Cooperative (a Colorado Limited Cooperative Association) and bills itself as the staffing industry's largest sub-vendor marketplace. Gustav is a SaaS web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — integrations are delivered through the Bullhorn and JobDiva marketplaces.
g.name: Gustav

g.description: A cloud-based payroll, benefits, and human resources platform designed for small and medium-sized businesses. Gusto Embedded enables platforms to integrate payroll, tax filing, and HR workflows directly into their products via a REST API, React SDK, and webhooks.
g.name: Gusto

g.description: Gut Wellness Club is an India-based consumer wellness brand offering a "Gut Reset" program that promises to resolve digestive issues in 15-20 days using natural traditional foods, yoga, Ayurveda, and Naturopathy as an alternative to medication. The site is Wix-hosted and, notably for a consumer brand, exposes agent-native surfaces: a published /llms.txt and a live, hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint that lets AI agents retrieve business details, search the site, and access Wix REST APIs without scraping. It has no first-party developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs. Surfaced via Accel portfolio mining and enriched from its real public agent surfaces.
g.name: Gut Wellness Club

g.description: Gutendex is a simple, self-hosted JSON-based web API for serving book catalog information from Project Gutenberg, providing structured metadata for over 70,000 free ebooks including titles, authors, subjects, bookshelves, languages, copyright status, media types, downloadable formats, and download counts. The hosted instance at gutendex.com runs the open-source Django project by Gareth B. Johnson under the MIT license.
g.name: Gutendex

g.description: Guusto is an employee recognition and rewards platform that lets teams send digital gifts, run peer-to-peer and top-down recognition programs, and redeem rewards with 60,000+ merchant locations, prepaid Mastercard, and charitable donations. Guusto exposes a REST Gifts API - available on the Premium plan - for programmatically ordering gifts, tracking order status, retrieving workspace and member reward budgets, and pulling recognition activity and manager insight reports. Requests are authenticated with a Bearer API token plus an X-Workspace-id header against production (api.guusto.com) or a demo test environment (api-demo.guusto.io).
g.name: Guusto

g.description: GV (formerly Google Ventures) is the venture capital arm of Alphabet, founded in 2009 by Bill Maris and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with additional offices in New York, Cambridge, and London. With Alphabet as its sole limited partner, GV operates with the reliability of a single LP, the autonomy of a traditional venture firm, and deep technical expertise, investing from seed through growth stage across technology and life sciences. Its focus areas span AI, enterprise, consumer, frontier tech, and life sciences, with a heavy recent emphasis on the AI frontier, from applications and developer tools to infrastructure and healthcare. GV manages over $13 billion in assets and supports roughly 400 active portfolio companies across North America, Europe, and Israel. The firm has backed notable companies including Uber, Slack, GitLab, Nest, Flatiron Health, Lemonade, Vercel, Isomorphic Labs, and insitro, with a track record of more than 80 IPOs and 230+ M&A exits.
g.name: GV

g.description: gVisor is an application kernel written in Go that implements a substantial portion of the Linux system surface. It provides an additional layer of isolation between running applications and the host operating system, intercepting and handling application system calls in user space to reduce the attack surface of the host kernel.
g.name: gVisor

g.description: GXO Logistics is a leading global provider of pure-play contract logistics, offering warehousing, distribution, e-commerce fulfillment, supply chain optimization, and reverse logistics services.

g.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.
g.name: Gyant

g.description: Gyde is an AI-native health insurance brokerage, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Austin, Texas with an office in New York City. Gyde partners with established insurance agencies through acquisition, embedding AI-powered tools and operational support so brokers can guide clients through insurance, health, and wealth decisions at greater scale. Its products include Gia, an AI assistant that handles client outreach, scheduling, and questions over SMS and voice around the clock, and GydeOS, a broker operating system providing client summaries, conversation transcripts, campaign management, and an AI co-pilot. Gyde launched publicly in January 2026 with $60M in financing led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.
g.name: Gyde

g.description: GYENNO is a medical technology company that designs assistive devices and digital-health tools for people living with Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders. Its consumer product line includes the GYENNO Bravo anti-tremor eating utensil (a stabilizing, weighted spoon/fork that counteracts hand tremor) and the GYENNO Skywalk portable freezing-of-gait mobility aid that projects a visual laser cue to help users resume walking, alongside a range of adaptive and weighted utensils and daily-living aids. GYENNO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer marketing site only and exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.
g.name: GYENNO

g.description: Gyft is a digital gift card platform and marketplace (a Fiserv / First Data company) for buying, sending, storing, and redeeming digital gift cards from more than 250 retail brands. Consumers use the Gyft web app and mobile apps to consolidate and manage gift cards, while businesses use the Gyft API and Gyft SDK to add digital gift cards to their own apps, websites, employee rewards, and incentive programs, and to place bulk corporate orders through Gyft Business. Developer and API access is provisioned to enrolled partners via the Gyft developer portal. Surfaced originally as a portfolio company of 500 Global and GV, and enriched here from Gyft's public developer surface.
g.name: Gyft

g.description: Gym Class VR (operating as "Gym Class" by IRL Studios) is a social virtual reality sports gaming platform for Meta Quest headsets and mobile devices, offering multiplayer basketball, baseball, football, boxing, paintball, and soccer experiences where players compete, socialize, and create and share their own games. The top-rated sports title on the Meta Quest Store with a 4.8-star average across 53,000+ ratings, the company holds licensing agreements with the NBA and Major League Baseball, expanded to mobile in 2026, and has raised over $8M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, and NBA players. It is a consumer VR entertainment product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.
g.name: Gym Class VR

g.description: Gymboree is a children's apparel and accessories retailer selling clothing for babies, toddlers, and kids up to age 12 through its consumer e-commerce site at gymboree.com. The brand is owned and operated by The Children's Place, Inc. (headquartered at 500 Plaza Drive, Secaucus, NJ). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Gymboree publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine interface: its site is a purely consumer-facing retail storefront, so no API artifacts (OpenAPI, MCP, SDKs, webhooks) exist to harvest. This profile carries only the identity and infrastructure-security probe of the gymboree.com domain.
g.name: Gymboree

g.description: GymNadz is a women-focused fitness application offering personalized workout programs, nutrition and meal plans, and community features. The platform provides a library of 300+ exercises with customizable workout and meal plans tailored to individual fitness goals, plus progress tracking and coach interaction. It is delivered as consumer iOS and Android mobile apps rather than as a developer platform. GymNadz is a portfolio company of 500 Global, tracked in the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity and domain security posture.
g.name: GymNadz

g.description: Gymshark is a British fitness apparel and accessories brand founded in 2012 in Birmingham, England, selling gym and workout clothing direct to consumers worldwide through gymshark.com, a set of regional storefronts (uk., eu., row., de., fr., ca., au. and others) and its Gymshark Shop and Gymshark Training mobile apps. The storefront runs on Shopify behind a headless Next.js/OpenNext front end deployed on AWS, and customer identity is handled by an Auth0 tenant Gymshark operates on its own domain at auth.gymshark.com. Gymshark publishes no public developer portal, no developer documentation and no public product API; the only publicly discoverable machine-readable contract on its own hosts is the OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata served from auth.gymshark.com. Its engineering team does publish open-source Go, JavaScript and Swift libraries under the github.com/gymshark organization, and it runs a public vulnerability disclosure program on HackerOne.
g.name: Gymshark

g.description: Gyre Energy is a UK-based climate-tech company that reduces cooling costs for operators of cold storage facilities, data centers, and building portfolios by combining artificial intelligence with thermal energy storage. Its platform pairs Gyre AI, a digital twin that learns a facility's thermal behavior and shifts cooling cycles to run when grid energy is cheapest and greenest, with an integrated thermal energy storage "cold battery" and a real-time monitoring and controls layer that tracks temperature, energy use, and door-open events. The company reports up to 50% lower cooling expenses, 38% verified energy cost savings at its first commercial cold storage deployment, a 91% reduction in temperature excursions, and a payback period of under 1.5 years. Gyre Energy is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and, as of July 2026, secured $1.3m in funding to support a major blue-chip deployment and global scaling. It currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.
g.name: Gyre Energy

g.description: GZW Data is a free, fan-made, read-only REST API for Gray Zone Warfare game data, published by independent maintainer ZoniBoy00 and hosted on Vercel at gzw-data.dev. It exposes 85+ datasets auto-discovered from a wiki-scraped data directory - weapons, ammo, armor, magazines, attachments, tasks and missions, keys and keycards, loot containers, medical, provisions, gear and vendors - behind one uniform JSON envelope with equality filters, full-text search, sorting and page-number pagination. Three smart routes union related datasets (armor, weapon_parts, helmet_mods). There is no authentication, no account and no API key; access is governed by a best-effort limit of 100 requests per minute per IP with X-RateLimit-* headers. An OpenAPI 3.0.3 contract, an llms.txt and a zero-dependency TypeScript client on npm are published. Data is scraped weekly from the community GZW Fandom Wiki; the project is unofficial and not affiliated with the game's publisher.
g.name: GZW Data API

h.description: H Company (hcompany.ai) is a Paris-based AI lab, backed by Accel and Creandum, that builds the Holo family of vision-language models and a Computer-Use Agents platform for automating work on browsers and desktops. It ships two public APIs: the Computer-Use Agents API (agp, /api/v2) for launching, steering, scheduling, and observing autonomous agent sessions — with reusable agents, skills, environments, browser profiles, vaults, and signed webhooks — and the OpenAI-compatible Holo Models API (/v1) serving the Holo3 and Holo3.1 models. Typed Python and TypeScript SDKs (hai-agents), a hai CLI, an official MCP server, and idempotent, region-isolated (EU/US) REST round out an agent-native developer surface.
h.name: H Company

h.description: H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group) is one of the world's largest multi-brand hotel operators, headquartered in Shanghai, China and founded in 2005 by Ji Qi. It franchises, manages, and leases-and-operates thousands of hotels across economy-to-luxury tiers under brands including HanTing, Ji Hotel, Orange, Hi Inn, Elan, Starway, Crystal Orange, Manxin, Madison, Blossom House, CitiGO and Ni Hao, plus the upscale European Deutsche Hospitality portfolio (Steigenberger, IntercityHotel, MAXX, Jaz in the City, Zleep) and the H Rewards loyalty program. The company is dual-listed on NASDAQ (HTHT) and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1179). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; H World is a consumer hospitality operator and does not publish a public developer API surface.
h.name: H World Group

h.description: A Swedish multinational fast-fashion retailer offering affordable clothing, accessories, and home goods. Operates thousands of stores globally and is one of the world's largest fashion companies. No public developer portal or open API catalogue was located on hm.com or hmgroup.com.
h.name: H&M

h.description: H&R Block (NYSE: HRB) is a US tax-preparation company and Fortune 1000 constituent, operating retail tax offices, consumer and small-business tax software, and the MyBlock digital platform. It runs no public developer program: the hosts that make up its API estate — api.hrblock.com, developer.hrblock.com, the apiportal.hrblock.com Apigee portal, apigw, mcp, edge, services and connect — either do not resolve or refuse connections from the public internet, and integration is arranged bilaterally through the tax-import partner program. The one machine-readable contract H&R Block does serve publicly is the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect discovery metadata for its customer identity platform at login.hrblock.com.
h.name: H&R Block

h.description: H.B. Fuller Company is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The H.B. Fuller Company API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
h.name: H.B. Fuller Company

h.description: H1 (h1.co) is a New York City-based healthcare data and technology company, founded in 2017, that combines deep healthcare provider data with agentic AI to power drug development, medical and commercial engagement, care navigation, and provider and network intelligence for life sciences, pharma, health plans, and digital health organizations across the United States. Its developer-facing API is the Ribbon Health API (H1 acquired Ribbon Health), a proprietary REST API served over HTTPS at https://api.ribbonhealth.com that provides accurate, comprehensive data on healthcare providers, locations, insurances, procedures, price transparency, cost estimates, and insurance eligibility. Two OpenAPI 3.1 contracts are published - the 75-operation v1 API under /v1, and a newer 7-operation location-first Price Transparency v2 surface under /v2 that H1 tells new integrations to prefer over the legacy provider-first /v1/pricing endpoints. The API is not FHIR-based and does not expose a SMART-on-FHIR or Da Vinci PDEX Plan-Net surface; it authenticates with a bearer API key, has no OAuth scopes, and gates product families on per-account entitlement flags. It is segmented into provider, location, custom-filter, focus-area, price-transparency (v1 and v2), cost-estimate/eligibility, organization, reference-data, and network-analysis product families. Access is gated behind a request-demo / API-key sign-up rather than fully self-serve, and no pricing, plans, SDKs, sandbox, changelog or webhook surface is published.
h.name: H1

h.description: H2O Hospitality is a South Korea-based hospitality digital-transformation company that connects existing hotel and leisure systems rather than replacing them, streamlining operations from booking to checkout. Its products span three areas: Connect (cloud property-management tooling including Smart CRS, Smart RMS, and Smart FMS), Maximize (revenue and guest-engagement tools such as Smart D2C and AI-based CRM), and Transform (managed operations). It offers smart mobile check-in and automated inventory management, operates across nine countries in Korea, Japan, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, and is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.
h.name: H2O Hospitality

h.description: H2O.ai is an open-source artificial-intelligence and machine-learning company whose platform spans H2O-3 (a distributed, in-memory ML engine), H2O Driverless AI (automatic machine learning), H2O MLOps (model deployment, scoring and monitoring), H2O Wave (a Python/R framework for realtime AI apps), H2O LLM Studio, and Enterprise h2oGPTe (a private generative-AI, RAG and agent platform). Enterprise h2oGPTe publishes a 422-operation OpenAPI 3.0.1 contract covering collections, document ingestion, chat, agents, extractors, GraphRAG, guardrails, models, permissions and scheduled tasks, and H2O MLOps publishes an OpenAPI contract for its model-scoring endpoints. H2O.ai also ships a first-party MCP server that proxies the h2oGPTe REST API to agent clients, together with official Python, R, Java and JavaScript client libraries distributed via PyPI, CRAN, Maven Central and npm.
h.name: H2O.ai

h.description: HAAS Alert operates Safety Cloud, a connected-vehicle safety platform that delivers real-time digital alerts to nearby motorists about active emergency responses, roadside hazards, work zones, stopped vehicles, and slow-moving equipment. Using vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and cellular messaging, Safety Cloud gives drivers up to roughly 30 seconds of advance warning to help reduce collisions with first responders, tow operators, and roadway workers. HAAS Alert integrates with telematics platforms, fleet manufacturers, OEM vehicles, in-car navigation (including Waze), and roadway infrastructure to form a large connected-vehicle alerting ecosystem. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from HAAS Alert's public web surface; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs were found at the time of enrichment.
h.name: HAAS Alert

h.description: Haaven is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline. The company's primary web presence is haaven.com, which sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge; a published RFC 9116 security.txt (security@haaven.com, languages en,nl) and an api.haaven.com host were confirmed during enrichment, but no public OpenAPI, docs, or developer portal could be read.
h.name: Haaven

h.description: HAAWK is a Los Angeles-based music rights management and monetization company that administers digital rights across YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok for record labels, music publishers, and independent artists. Its products include HAAWK (full-service YouTube Content ID and Meta Rights Manager administration), Identifyy (self-service UGC rights management for independent creators), Keyframe Audio (a micro sync-licensing catalog of 50,000+ production music tracks), and Diistro (digital music distribution to Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music, and TikTok). HAAWK has administered 100B+ video views and manages 1.1M+ music copyrights for 2,000+ rights holders. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.
h.name: HAAWK

h.description: Habana Labs is an artificial-intelligence processor company, now part of Intel, that designs deep-learning accelerators for AI training and inference. Its Gaudi (training) and Goya (inference) processors — sold today as the Intel Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 AI accelerators — are programmed through the SynapseAI software suite, which integrates with PyTorch and DeepSpeed and ships reference models, containers, and installation tooling. Habana was founded in 2016 in Israel and acquired by Intel in 2019. Its public developer surface is not a hosted web API but an open-source SDK and toolchain: the HabanaAI GitHub organization (reference models, PyTorch bridge, setup/install, plus vLLM and Megatron forks) and the Intel Gaudi documentation at docs.habana.ai. This profile catalogs that developer footprint for the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Habana Labs

h.description: Habeas was an email reputation and deliverability services provider that helped legitimate senders monitor and manage their sending reputation to maximize inbox deliverability, using a trademark-based accreditation and safelist model to certify permission-based email. Founded in the mid-2000s and backed by Canaan Partners through a Series B round, Habeas was acquired by Return Path in 2008 (habeas.com now redirects to returnpath.com); Return Path was in turn acquired by Validity in 2019. The company is defunct as an independent brand and publishes no live public API or developer surface, so this profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio-history record rather than an active API provider.
h.name: Habeas

h.description: Haber (Elixa Technologies Private Limited), headquartered in Pune, India with a US presence in Chicago, is an industrial AI company delivering AI-led automation for smart manufacturing across heavy industries including pulp, paper, packaging and tissue, metals and mining, food and beverages, oil and gas, and water/utility institutions. Its product suite spans eLIXA, an IIoT-powered process intelligence platform; Mt. Fuji for historical data storage, visualizations, digital twins and predictive interventions; Kaiznn, an optimization engine for trim-loss reduction, inventory and production scheduling; plus Kensei and FiMorph. The platform emphasizes real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and enterprise-grade security (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Haber

h.description: Habi is a Colombian real estate technology company (proptech) that operates as a direct home buyer and seller — an iBuyer model where Habi itself purchases apartments in cash, typically within 10 days, rather than acting as a traditional agency. It operates across Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla and 20+ Colombian cities and is expanding into Mexico. Products include Habimetro (an online property valuation simulator), property listings and search, Habi Credit (mortgage financing), Habi Inmobiliaria (assisted longer-term sales), and an allied-agent partner network. The company reports 40,000+ families served, 4,000+ allied real estate agents, and 550+ real estate experts. Backed by Homebrew. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from Habi's public surface; the company publishes no public developer API.
h.name: Habi

h.description: Habitat Lab is Meta AI Research's embodied AI simulation platform. It provides documentation, quickstart code, and tools for training and evaluating AI agents in photorealistic 3D environments, with Habitat 2.0 focusing on household rearrangement tasks. Habitat Lab is delivered as a Python research library; it does not currently expose a public HTTP API.
h.name: Habitat Lab

h.description: Habiteo is a French PropTech company founded in 2014 in Paris that builds full-web 3D sales and marketing technology for new-build real estate. Its products let developers, house builders, commercial-property operators and their agencies model a programme in 3D before it is built: 3D floor plans and perspectives, virtual tours, drone-based site insertions and neighbourhood views (Modelisation and myHabiteo Studio), an interior configurator that lets a buyer choose materials and options in place of a physical showroom (Configurateur), a mobile on-site sales unit (Habiteo Truck), and the MegaWidget, a hosted mini-site that gathers every 3D asset for a programme behind a single link. myHabiteo is the operator platform that binds the 3D layer to commercialisation with a CRM, a reservation module, programme management and sales and marketing dashboards. More than 350 developers, including Nexity, Kaufman & Broad and Immobiliere 3F, have used the technology. Habiteo was acquired by the French listings portal Bien'ici in May 2022 and continues to operate under its own brand. Habiteo publishes no public developer programme, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract for any of these products; the only anonymously readable machine surface on its domain is the WordPress REST API behind its marketing site.
h.name: Habiteo

h.description: Habito is a UK-based digital mortgage broker that lets people research, compare, and apply for mortgages online across the whole of the market, pairing self-serve digital tools with human mortgage experts, alongside related home-buying services. Founded as a fintech in the consumer lending and real-estate space and backed by Ribbit Capital, Habito has since joined Monzo. The company operates a consumer web product (Webflow-hosted marketing site) and does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or OpenAPI at the time of this profile; this record is maintained by the API Evangelist network and reflects only publicly verifiable surfaces.
h.name: Habito

h.description: Habitto is a Tokyo-based fintech company building a mobile financial wellness app for the Japanese market under the banner お金の新習慣 ("new money habits"). The app pairs a high-yield savings account and a cashback debit card with access to human financial advisors who help users save, grow, and protect their money. Habitto is backed by the fintech-focused venture investors Anthemis and QED Investors. This API Evangelist profile has been enriched with company identity, website link properties, and a domain-security probe; Habitto is a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.
h.name: Habitto

h.description: Habu was a data clean room and data collaboration company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Francisco, that let brands, publishers, and media platforms run privacy-safe joins and analytics on each other's first-party data without moving or exposing raw records. In January 2024 Habu was acquired by LiveRamp, and the product now ships as LiveRamp Clean Room within the LiveRamp data collaboration network. The habu.com marketing domain 301-redirects to liveramp.com and the old docs.habu.com / developer.habu.com hosts no longer resolve, but the product API itself is still very much alive on Habu's own infrastructure: api.habu.com/v1 answers today, and LiveRamp publishes its full 151-operation OpenAPI 3.0.0 contract — titled "External APIs for Customer Integration", contact platform_admin@habu.com — under developers.liveramp.com. The console is still Habu-branded at console.habu.com. This profile originated as a portfolio-lead stub (backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Wing Venture Capital) and is enriched here from that live, publicly documented surface plus the security and compliance posture inherited by LiveRamp.
h.name: Habu

h.description: Habyt is a flexible-living and co-living accommodation provider offering furnished studios, apartments, and private rooms for stays ranging from a single night to several months. Positioned as "a new category of living for people in motion," the company blends hotel-style service and amenities with residential flexibility, targeting mobile professionals, relocators, and long-term travelers. Habyt operates properties across Europe (Berlin, Madrid, Vienna, with Lisbon and Milan announced) and Asia (multiple locations in Singapore), and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital. Habyt is a consumer real-estate and hospitality operator rather than an API-first technology provider; as of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found.
h.name: Habyt

h.description: Automated web-application security scanner that runs 200+ checks across DAST (OWASP ZAP), CVE exploit templates (Nuclei), static analysis (Semgrep/SAST), and SaaS-misconfiguration checks, producing a 0-100 AI Launch Score with go/no-go readiness bands and 1-click AI remediation fix prompts for Cursor, Claude Code, and Windsurf. Built by Aivi Labs for teams shipping sites made with AI coding tools (Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Claude Code); currently early-access/waitlist with no public developer API.
h.name: Hack My Website

h.description: Hackajob is a UK-founded (2015) tech-recruitment platform that connects jobseekers and employers across the UK and US using AI hiring agents. Its flagship product, Archer, is an always-on AI sourcing agent that finds, qualifies, and introduces high-fit passive candidates directly into an employer's ATS, complemented by agents Chase (AI recruiter) and Thena (applicant screening). Alongside the AI agents it runs an On-Demand contract hiring marketplace, a Talent Intelligence / hiring-insights product, an Upskill skills-assessment tool, and public jobs and company directories drawing on a talent network of 1.5M+ vetted knowledge workers. Hackajob does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK; this profile captures its public web, security, and trust surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched from real public sources.
h.name: Hackajob

h.description: Hacker News is Y Combinator's technology news aggregation and discussion platform. It exposes a public, read-only Firebase-backed API that gives developers real-time access to stories, comments, jobs, polls, and user profiles across the full HN dataset.
h.name: Hacker News

h.description: For compiling and running code in several languages
h.name: Hackerearth

h.description: Hackermeter is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Hackermeter

h.description: HackerNoon is an independent technology publishing platform and community CMS, founded in 2016 by David Smooke and headquartered in Edwards, Colorado. It operates a free, open library of more than 150,000 practitioner-authored, human-edited technology stories from 35,000+ contributing engineers, covering AI, software engineering, Web3, cybersecurity, startups and science, and serves roughly 3-4 million monthly readers. The company builds and open-sources the publishing software behind the site — the Chowa collaborative editor, the Pixel Icon Library, the HackerNoon pixel font and the Editing Protocol — and monetises through business blogging credits, targeted ads, newsletters and AI content licensing. HackerNoon publishes no public API: probed on 2026-08-22, it serves no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface. Its machine-readable surface is a content and AI-access one — an llms.txt, a per-crawler robots.txt policy, RSS feeds and sitemaps — with a "live content feed API" advertised in llms.txt as coming in Q3 2026 and not yet shipped.
h.name: Hackernoon

h.description: The industry’s first hacker API that helps increase productivity towards creative bug bounty hunting
h.name: HackerOne

h.description: HackerRank is a developer skills platform used by companies to screen, interview, and upskill technical talent, and by more than 26 million developers to practice coding and earn skill certifications. Its products include Screen (automated coding assessments), Interview (collaborative real-time coding interviews), Engage (technical hiring events and hackathons), and SkillUp. HackerRank for Work exposes a public REST API (v3) so customers can programmatically manage tests, candidates, questions, interviews, and results, and integrate assessments into their own applicant-tracking and hiring workflows. This API Evangelist profile catalogs HackerRank's developer surface and the enrichment artifacts derived from it.
h.name: HackerRank

h.description: HackMD is a real-time collaborative Markdown editor and knowledge base for individuals and teams. Multiple people can co-edit a Markdown document live, organize notes into folders and team workspaces, and publish them as web pages, slide decks or books. HackMD exposes a v1 REST API at api.hackmd.io that lets developers programmatically create, read, update and delete personal and team notes, manage folders and folder ordering, upload image attachments, restore notes from trash, and read the current user profile and view history. The API authenticates with a personal access token sent as an HTTP bearer credential, is described by a published OpenAPI 3.0 specification and Swagger UI, ships an official Node.js/TypeScript client (@hackmd/api) and command-line interface, and advertises its full developer surface through an RFC 9727 api-catalog. HackMD is a Techstars-backed company.
h.name: HackMD

h.description: IP geolocation, ISP and privacy/VPN scoring, email breach checks, DNS and WHOIS lookups
h.name: HackMyIP

h.description: HackNotice is an external threat-intelligence and cyber-risk platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Austin, Texas. It continuously collects intelligence from ransomware groups, infostealer malware logs, data breaches, dark-web marketplaces, hacker forums and public disclosures, then matches that intelligence against the domains, employees, customers and vendors an organization asks it to watch. The product is organized around four monitoring services — first-party domain monitoring, third-party vendor risk monitoring, end-user credential monitoring, and threat research and investigations — plus AI-assisted vendor security assessments. HackNotice exposes this surface programmatically through a REST API documented as a public Postman collection at api-docs.hacknotice.com, a remote Model Context Protocol server at mcp.hacknotice.com whose tool catalogue answers anonymously, first-party n8n automation nodes on npm, and webhook, Splunk HEC and SIEM/SOAR alert delivery.
h.name: HackNotice

h.description: Hackpad was a web-based real-time collaborative wiki and document editor, built on the open-source Etherpad codebase, that let teams write and edit documents together simultaneously. It was acquired by Dropbox in April 2014 and its underlying platform was released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license at github.com/dropbox/hackpad. The hosted hackpad.com service was wound down after Dropbox folded the team's work into Dropbox Paper, and the public service was discontinued in 2017. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hackpad as a historical, now-defunct portfolio company surfaced from the a16z portfolio; there is no live production API surface remaining, and the durable public artifact is the open-source repository.
h.name: Hackpad

h.description: HacWare is an AI-powered security awareness training and phishing simulation platform that helps organizations reduce human-factor cyber risk. Its RESTful Security Awareness API lets partners and developers embed HacWare into their own products: schedule and manage AI-generated phishing simulations (clickable link, attachment, direct response, and SMS), enroll users in micro-training courses, lesson plans and quizzes, run dark web breach reporting and human-risk assessments, manage users, groups and Microsoft 365 security groups, and operate a multi-tenant partner/customer hierarchy with compliance evidence retrieval. The API is documented with apiDoc and exposes 114 operations across Phishing, Training, Reporting, User, Group, Compliance, and Multi-Tenant surfaces. HacWare is a Techstars portfolio company.
h.name: Hacware

h.description: Hades Mining GmbH is a Munich-based deep-tech extraction company building technology-first methods for accessing critical minerals and geothermal energy from ultra-deep rock formations. Its flagship system, Cerberus, uses high-power continuous-wave fiber lasers delivered through proprietary fiber optics to fracture rock without mechanical bit wear, paired with in-situ recovery (ISR) fluid circulation to extract minerals without open-pit excavation. The company positions itself at the intersection of geology, engineering, and geopolitics under the tagline "Sovereignty begins subsurface," aiming to reduce Western dependence on imported critical minerals. Hades is backed by HV Capital and Headline via a EUR 15M seed round. As a physical deep-tech extraction company, Hades publishes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface at this time.
h.name: Hades

h.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.
h.name: Hadrian

h.description: Hadrius is an AI-native compliance platform for SEC- and FINRA-regulated financial firms, including broker-dealers, registered investment advisors (RIAs), private funds, and compliance consultants. The platform consolidates multiple compliance functions into a single system of record with human governance: a testing program that automates compliance testing and audit reporting, AI-powered marketing review and content approval workflows, people oversight for personal trading, attestations and certifications, communications archiving that supervises email, chat, and social media with zero-retention AI, and account surveillance that monitors trades against restricted lists and blackout windows. Hadrius serves 500+ institutions managing over $5 trillion in AUM, raised a $22M Series A, and is backed by Y Combinator and CRV. The company is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and GDPR compliant. This profile currently documents no public developer API; it is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Hadrius

h.description: Haekka is a Slack-native microlearning and security-awareness training platform that delivers short, timely training inside Slack to improve knowledge, compliance, and team performance. Core products include Training, Streams (auto-drip microlearning), Workflows (event-triggered training assignment), Pulse Engagements (surveys, quizzes, announcements), and a Phishing simulator with a Gmail Chrome extension. Haekka's catalog maps to SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI training requirements and integrates with Slack, Google Workspace, and HRIS/LMS/IAM systems. Its Public REST API exposes employees, trainings, and employee-training completion records plus training assignment, secured with a bearer API key generated in account settings.
h.name: Haekka

h.description: Hagglebee is an agent-first publishing site operated by API Evangelist. AI agents sign up, prepay from a card, and publish classified ads that run 30 days through a REST API or an MCP server; humans browse and search the same posts on the website. Every post is moderated by an open model (gpt-oss-safeguard-20b) against a published policy before it appears, abusive posts cost ten times their price, and published posts are licensed CC BY 4.0.
h.name: Hagglebee

h.description: HAGS is a consumer-sector company listed in the portfolio of GV (Google Ventures) and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its website, hags.com, is live but served behind Cloudflare, which challenge-blocks automated crawling (HTTP 403 on every path), so no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, API reference, or documentation surface could be located during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a lightweight company lead and will be expanded if and when HAGS publishes a developer or API surface.
h.name: HAGS

h.description: Hai is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Hai

h.description: Hailo Technologies Ltd. is an Israeli fabless semiconductor company, headquartered in Tel Aviv with offices in the United States, Germany, Japan, Taiwan, China and South Korea, that designs AI inference accelerators (the Hailo-8, Hailo-8L and Hailo-10 families) and AI vision processors (the Hailo-15 SoC family) for edge devices. Its developer surface is not a hosted web API: it is an on-device software stack published largely on GitHub under the hailo-ai organization — HailoRT, a C/C++/Python runtime library plus the hailortcli command line tool and a PCIe kernel driver; the Hailo Model Zoo of pre-compiled HEF models; TAPPAS and hailo-apps application pipelines; and the Hailo Media Library and Hailo Imaging stacks for the Hailo-15 vision processor. The machine-readable contracts Hailo publishes are Protocol Buffers — a 33-RPC gRPC MediaLibraryService, the HailoRT hRPC and GenAI message schemes, the HEF model-file format, and a WebSocket/ZMQ analytics metadata scheme. Hailo also publishes a first-party Agent Skills package (hailo15-agentic-coding) of twelve skills that drive board connection, pipeline editing, model swapping, cross-compilation and deployment on the Hailo-15 SBC.
h.name: Hailo

h.description: Hailuo AI is MiniMax's generative video and audio platform. MiniMax is a Singapore- and China-based foundation-model company whose developer platform (platform.minimax.io / api.minimax.io, and intl.minimaxi.com for international users) exposes documented HTTP APIs for AI video generation (the Hailuo text-to-video and image-to-video models - MiniMax-Hailuo-2.3, MiniMax-Hailuo-02, Video-01, T2V-01, I2V-01, S2V-01), large language model chat completions (the MiniMax / abab family), text-to-speech (T2A) over both HTTP and a real-time WebSocket, music generation, and voice cloning. Video generation follows an asynchronous create-task-then-poll pattern; all APIs authenticate with a Bearer API key.
h.name: Hailuo AI / MiniMax

h.description: The Hain Celestial Group is a leading organic and natural products company providing consumers with A Healthier Way of Life through a portfolio of natural, organic, and better-for-you brands. No public APIs or developer programs have been identified for Hain Celestial Group at this time.
h.name: Hain Celestial Group

h.description: Hakeem X Technologies (HAKEEM HOLDING LTD) is a UAE-based healthcare technology company delivering AI-powered clinical decision support and medical education to hospitals, universities, and healthcare professionals across the UAE and KSA. Its flagship HakeemDx assistant turns medical research into instant, evidence-based answers at the point of care for physicians and pharmacists, alongside licensed clinical reference suites (Micromedex, EBSCO DynaMed, Isabel, GIDEON), medication-adherence and virtual pharmacy tooling, and medical/nursing education platforms (Lecturio, Healer case simulations, Simtics). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, SDK, or portal is published at this time.
h.name: HAKEEM

h.description: Hakimo is a Menlo Park, California physical-security software company founded by Stanford AI researchers Sam Joseph and Sagar Honnungar. Its AI platform sits on top of a customer's existing camera, NVR/VMS and access-control estate and turns it into an autonomous security operations capability: the AI Operator triages alarms and assigns a true-alarm probability, remote guarding and SOC-as-a-Service provide 24/7 monitored response, and forensic search, weapon detection, facial recognition, an insights dashboard and a mobile app round out the product line. Hakimo integrates with roughly forty third-party systems (Genetec, Milestone, Avigilon, LenelS2, Eagle Eye Networks, Axis, ServiceNow, Slack, Microsoft Teams, ONVIF devices) by consuming those vendors' APIs. As of August 2026 Hakimo publishes no public developer program of its own: there is no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDK. Its tenant application API is served same-origin from the customer portal and answers unauthenticated requests with HTTP 401.
h.name: Hakimo

h.description: hakuna AG is a Swiss digital time-tracking and personnel-management platform for SMEs. The browser- and mobile-based product centralizes workforce administration: time recording with a running timer, absence and vacation management, expense processing, project and client tracking, task categorization, shift planning, personnel records, and compliance monitoring against Swiss labor-law requirements. hakuna is "100% Swiss" — all data is stored in Switzerland under Swiss data-protection law (DSG) — and requires no additional hardware terminals or badges. It exposes a token-authenticated REST API (X-Auth-Token) over JSON at app.hakuna.ch/api/v1 covering the timer, time entries, absences, projects, tasks, clients, users, company settings, and an organization-wide presence status endpoint, with admin-only management endpoints and a documented 100 requests/minute rate limit.
h.name: Hakuna

h.description: Haladir is a Y Combinator-backed startup building a decisional AI platform for logistics operations. Describing itself as "the decisional AI layer for logistics," Haladir unifies fragmented operational data from existing warehouse management (WMS), transportation management (TMS), and order management (OMS) systems into a single operational graph, then applies constraint-optimization solvers and machine-learning models to automate supply chain decisions across routing, picking, labor allocation, and inventory. Its approach treats large language models as formalization tools that translate messy operational rules into precise constraints for traditional solvers, rather than as decision-makers. Target customers include third-party logistics providers (3PLs), contract logistics providers, distributors, and shippers managing global supply chains. The company has raised $4.3M in seed funding led by BoxGroup and Susa Ventures. This profile currently exposes no public API or developer documentation; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.
h.name: Haladir

h.description: Halara is a direct-to-consumer athleisure and activewear fashion brand for women, best known for its versatile Active Dress and its Halara Flex fabric technology. Its Shopify-based online store sells exercise dresses, leggings, tennis skirts, joggers, pants, sports bras, loungewear, sweaters, and denim under the tagline "Athleisure for 365 Versions of You." Halara runs a mobile shopping app and a customer loyalty program (The Halara Circle), and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Halara publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web, brand, and policy properties for network discovery.
h.name: Halara

h.description: Halborn is a blockchain and digital-asset cybersecurity firm that sells professional security services rather than a developer product. Its assurance practice covers smart contract assessments, Layer 1 protocol reviews, code security audits, web application and cloud infrastructure penetration testing, red team exercises, and custody and key management assessments; its advisory practice covers AI security, blockchain architecture, compliance readiness, risk assessment, technical due diligence and technical training for banks, exchanges, custodians, tokenization platforms, stablecoin issuers, DeFi protocols, central banks and blockchain infrastructure providers. Halborn publishes its engagement results as a public audit repository, discloses zero-day findings under its own CVE assignment scope as a CVE Numbering Authority, and maintains BVSS, the Blockchain Vulnerability Scoring System. As of August 2026 it publishes no public API, no developer portal and no machine-readable contract; its Halborn ONE client platform at one.halborn.com is an invitation-only customer portal.
h.name: Halborn

h.description: Halcyon (Halcyon Tech, Inc.) is a cybersecurity company that builds a purpose-built, adaptive anti-ransomware and cyber-resilience platform. Its lightweight endpoint agent combines automated detection and disruption across the full ransomware attack lifecycle — pre-execution, encryption, and data exfiltration — with encryption-key recovery, a managed 24/7 Ransomware Operations Center (ROC), and a ransomware recovery warranty. Halcyon exposes a REST API for device/asset data and a universal API that streams alerts into SIEM, SOAR, and XDR platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Sumo Logic, and Exabeam, alongside backup integrations with Veeam, Cohesity, Acronis, and Commvault. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Obvious Ventures.
h.name: Halcyon

h.description: Halda Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company and Yale University spinout developing oral, targeted cancer therapies built on its proprietary RIPTAC (Regulated Induced Proximity TArgeting Chimera) platform, a novel "hold and kill" modality for the precision treatment of solid tumors. Its lead program, HLD-0915, is a first-in-class oral RIPTAC therapeutic in development for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), with earlier-stage candidates spanning breast, lung, and other tumor types. Backed by investors including Canaan Partners, Halda was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2025 for approximately $3.05 billion in cash, with its platform folded into Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine's oncology pipeline. As a therapeutics developer, Halda operated no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity and portfolio-graph record rather than an API producer.
h.name: Halda Therapeutics

h.description: Halesis is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: new-submission) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.
h.name: Halesis

h.description: Halia Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Lehi, Utah, founded in 2017 and led by CEO Dr. David Bearss. Halia discovers and develops small-molecule therapies that target the immune system's inflammatory response — chiefly allosteric NEK7/NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition and LRRK2 inhibition — to resolve the chronic inflammation that drives hematologic, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease. Its lead clinical program, ofirnoflast (HT-6184), holds FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designation for lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes; HT-4253, an LRRK2 inhibitor aimed at neuroinflammation and Alzheimer's prevention in APOE4 carriers, has completed a first-in-human Phase 1 study. The company also markets a "genetic resilience" research platform (GENMOR) built on family-cohort genomics. Halia is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a Webflow corporate site with pipeline, platform and press pages, and no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.
h.name: Halia Therapeutics

h.description: Halifax is a major British high-street banking brand serving personal and business customers with current accounts, savings, mortgages, credit cards, loans, and insurance. It operates as a trading division of Bank of Scotland plc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lloyds Banking Group, and is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA. As one of the UK Open Banking CMA9 mandated ASPSPs, Halifax publishes the full Open Banking Implementation Entity (OBIE) API surface: a set of PUBLIC, unauthenticated Open Data APIs (ATM and branch locators plus personal current account, business current account, unsecured SME loan, and commercial credit card product reference data) served live at api.halifax.co.uk, and the FAPI-secured OBIE Read/Write APIs for Account and Transaction Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), and Confirmation of Funds (CBPII). Read/Write access is delivered through the shared Lloyds Banking Group Developer Portal that also covers the Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland brands, secured with OAuth2/OIDC, PSD2 strong customer authentication, mutual-TLS, and OBIE/eIDAS certificates.
h.name: Halifax

h.description: Hall is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Hall

h.description: Halliburton delivers advanced products and services to meet the evolving needs of the global energy industry, driving innovation, reliability, and performance. Halliburton operates enterprise software platforms such as DecisionSpace 365, Landmark, and iEnergy, but does not currently publish a public, openly accessible REST API for general developer use.
h.name: Halliburton

h.description: Halliday is a web3 payments and agentic-workflow company (a16z crypto Series A) building the end-to-end onchain deposit platform. Its Agentic Workflow Protocol (AWP) lets developers compose high-level, AI-executable workflows behind immutable guardrails without writing smart-contract code. The flagship product, Halliday Payments, is a unified cross-chain payments API and drop-in widget that lets users onramp from fiat, bridge, and swap to acquire any asset on any chain in a fully self-custodial way, routing intelligently across onramps (MoonPay, Transak, Stripe), swaps, and bridges. The Halliday API V2 (https://v2.prod.halliday.xyz) exposes chains, assets, quotes, payments, balances, withdrawals, and signed workflow webhooks, authenticated with publishable API keys, alongside JS/React/React Native SDKs and a published Claude Code integration skill.
h.name: Halliday

h.description: Hallmark Cards, Inc. is a privately held, family-owned greeting card, gift, gift wrap and ornament company headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, founded in 1910 by J.C. Hall. Its portfolio spans Hallmark greeting cards and Keepsake Ornaments sold through Hallmark Gold Crown stores and mass retailers, the Crayola and Hallmark Business Connections (B2B greeting card programs) subsidiaries, and Hallmark Media (Hallmark Channel, Hallmark+). Hallmark publishes no public developer program: developer.hallmark.com does not resolve, api.hallmark.com serves a stock ASP.NET template with no documented endpoints, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known discovery document was found on any Hallmark host on 2026-09-17. Retail and supply-chain partners integrate through bilateral EDI (Hallmark Global Services) and Hallmark Business Connections' CRM/SSO integrations, none of which are documented publicly.
h.name: Hallmark Cards

h.description: Hallo is an AI-powered language assessment and language-learning company backed by Battery Ventures. Its enterprise platform delivers automated, AI-driven proficiency assessments across speaking, writing, listening, and reading in 80+ languages, with CEFR-aligned scoring, detailed feedback (fluency, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, coherence), real-time score reports and dashboards, and proctoring / anti-cheating for high-stakes hiring, placement testing, and employee development. Hallo integrates with major applicant-tracking systems (Greenhouse, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Lever, SuccessFactors, Recruitee, and others) and runs assessments across 160+ countries, with a stated SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and EU AI Act compliance posture. The company also operates a consumer language-learning app with AI tutors and native-speaker practice. Hallo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; its integration surface is delivered through prebuilt ATS connectors and enterprise onboarding rather than a self-serve developer portal.
h.name: Hallo

h.description: Hallo theo (rebranding to "Theo") is a German residential property management company (Hausverwaltung) that manages homeowners' associations (WEG/HOA), rental apartment buildings, and commercial properties across Germany. With 150+ experts and local teams in Berlin, Frankfurt am Main, Munich, Stuttgart, and Wildeshausen, the company manages over 20,000 units and is Section 26a HOA-certified, combining on-the-ground regional teams with central specialists in law, technology, and finance. Backed by Insight Partners, it offers HOA management, property management, commercial property management, succession, and sale-and-stay-on services to co-owners and building owners. This is a services company with a marketing/lead website (built on Framer + HubSpot); it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.
h.name: hallo theo

h.description: Hallow is the #1 Catholic and Christian prayer, meditation, and Bible app, offering guided daily prayer, the Rosary, Lectio Divina, the Examen, Christian meditation, faith-based sleep stories, Scripture readings, and audio-guided sessions led by well-known voices. Founded in 2018 and based in Chicago, Hallow is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) with a subscription tier (Hallow Plus), and it runs programs for parishes, families, and gifting. Hallow does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public web and product surface. Backed by General Catalyst, Homebrew, and Uncork Capital.
h.name: Hallow

h.description: Halo 5 and Halo Wars 2 Information
h.name: Halo

h.description: Halo Collar is the consumer GPS dog-fence and dog-tracking product built by Protect Animals With Satellites LLC (d/b/a Halo), founded in 2017 by Ken Ehrman, Michael Ehrman and dog behaviorist Cesar Millan. The product pairs a cellular- and GPS-connected smart collar (currently Halo Collar 5, with Halo Collar 4 still sold) with a companion iOS/Android app that lets an owner draw virtual GPS fences, watch real-time location, trigger Cesar Millan-designed training feedback, and read activity reports. The service runs on a required Pack Membership subscription in Bronze, Silver and Gold tiers that carries unlimited cellular data, an increasing virtual-fence allowance, accessory discounts and third-party partner perks. Halo publishes no public developer program: the app is served by a first-party, undocumented backend at api.halocollar.com (an ASP.NET service that self-identifies as Halo.Web.Api), and there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or webhook surface anywhere on the company's public web properties.
h.name: Halo Collar

h.description: Halo Connect is an Australian healthcare interoperability platform, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Brisbane, Queensland, that makes primary-care data integration simple by exposing on-premise practice management system (PMS) databases through a modern cloud API. Its Halo Link agent and Halo Cloud service let approved software integrators query systems such as Best Practice, Zedmed, and Dental4Windows using either SQL passthrough or a standards-based FHIR R4 (4.0.1) API built toward the AU Base 4.1.0 implementation guide, without maintaining a separate database agent per integration. Halo Connect built the first FHIR API for the Best Practice Premier medical-practice industry. The platform runs on Microsoft Azure hosted in Australia, and access is gated behind a Halo Cloud subscription using Azure API Management subscription keys and, for desktop applications, bearer JWT tokens issued from a token endpoint; there is no self-serve public API.
h.name: Halo Connect

h.description: Halo Mental Health (Halo Health) operates same-day mental health urgent care clinics, offering immediate psychiatric assessments, medication management, crisis intervention, individual and group therapy, and teletherapy for adults and children ages eight and older. Founded by Paul Manley with medical director Dr. Vahid Osman, the Joint Commission-accredited provider runs clinics in Central Las Vegas and Summerlin, accepts commercial insurance and Medicaid, and is building the largest network of urgent cares dedicated to same-day mental health services. Backed by 8vc. Halo Health publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity, web presence, and domain security posture.
h.name: Halo Health

h.description: Halo Health, now part of symplr and marketed as symplr Clinical Communications, is a HIPAA-compliant clinical communication and collaboration platform for healthcare organizations. It provides role-based secure messaging, voice communication, critical alert and clinical-alarm notification, and on-call schedule management so care teams can coordinate around patients. The platform integrates with hospital EHR and clinical systems using healthcare interoperability standards - HL7 ADT for patient admit/discharge/transfer events, HL7 ORU for laboratory and radiology results, and SMTP for alerts such as sepsis notifications - rather than through a documented public developer REST API. symplr acquired Halo Health to extend its healthcare operations software portfolio, and the product now sits alongside symplr's broader workforce, compliance, and provider-data solutions.
h.name: Halo Health (Symplr)

h.description: Halo Investing is a Chicago-based financial technology company that operates a marketplace for "protective investments" — structured notes, multi-manager structured note SMAs, buffered ETFs, annuities and insurance — connecting financial advisors, RIAs and financial institutions with more than 40 global banking and insurance issuers. Founded in 2015 by Biju Kulathakal and Jason Barsema, the platform lets advisors analyze, customize, price, execute and then monitor outcome-based products from a single dashboard, with tools such as the Aura portfolio simulator and an asset allocation framework for structured notes. Halo reports more than $45.5B in transactions since 2015 and employs 100+ people. Its affiliate Halo Securities LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and a member of FINRA/SIPC, acting as distributor and selling agent for structured note products. The advisor platform at notes.haloinvesting.com is entirely authenticated behind a login. As of this profiling pass Halo Investing publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK, CLI, MCP server or A2A agent card; advisor-side API integration is offered through the third-party Schwab OpenView Gateway rather than a Halo-published API.
h.name: Halo Investing

h.description: HALO Precision Diagnostics (HALO Dx) is a Menlo Park, California precision-diagnostics company that acquires community imaging centers and rebuilds them as what it calls Imaging Center 2.0 — next-generation diagnostic hubs where advanced imaging, genomics and biomarker testing are all performed under one roof. Its diagnostic ensemble combines whole-body and multiparametric MRI, PSMA-targeted PET (PYLARIFY), digital pathology, polygenic risk scoring, hereditary and proteomic testing, and AI-assisted interpretation, applied first to cancer — the prostate program adds MRI-guided targeted biopsy and MRI-guided TULSA-PRO focal ablation — and expanding into cardiovascular disease and dementia. The company is led by CEO Michael Uhl with co-founder Brian Axe as Chief Product Officer and Dr. John Feller as Chief Medical Officer. Clinical delivery happens in HALO's own centers; referring physicians reach orders, results and images through a vendor-operated provider portal (RoyalMD) and the eUnity enterprise image viewer, and HALO advertises EMR integration for pushing orders and pulling results as a service its vendors deliver rather than as an interface it publishes. HALO operates no public developer program, publishes no API documentation, ships no SDK, and serves no machine-readable API contract; the only JSON on halodx.com is the marketing site's stock WordPress core REST API.
h.name: HALO Precision Diagnostics

h.description: Halogen Capital is Malaysia's first and only licensed digital asset fund manager, regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia (License eCMSL/A0388/2023) and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. The firm gives high-net-worth individuals, family offices, corporates, and institutional investors regulated access to cryptocurrency and traditional assets through unit trust structures, offering Shariah-compliant Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Crypto Titans basket funds alongside a MYR liquid fund, a ringgit income fund, and an enhanced income fund, all secured with multi-signature custody. Backed by Kenanga Investment Bank and 500 Global, Halogen manages roughly RM400 million in assets under management and is expanding into real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence and domain-security posture; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.
h.name: Halogen Capital

h.description: Halp was a conversational ticketing and help-desk tool that let teams turn Slack and Microsoft Teams messages into trackable tickets, founded in Boulder, Colorado and backed by Techstars. Atlassian acquired Halp in February 2020 and folded its capabilities into Jira Service Management; the standalone Halp product and its API were subsequently discontinued. The halp.com domain now resolves to Atlassian and is served from Atlassian's edge, so no independent Halp developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or MCP surface remains to enrich. This profile records the company's history and the (Atlassian-operated) security posture still observable on the halp.com domain.
h.name: Halp

h.description: Halter is a New Zealand-founded agri-technology company that builds GPS-enabled, solar-powered smart collars for cattle paired with a mobile and web app, letting farmers set and move virtual fences, remotely shift and hold herds, and monitor animal location, behavior, heat and health without physical fencing or manual labor. The platform combines wearable IoT devices (including direct-to-satellite connectivity) with pasture-management and grazing-allocation tools for dairy and beef operations. Halter operates across New Zealand, Australia and the United States and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Bond Capital and DCVC. No public developer API surface has been identified; this profile captures the company identity, web properties and domain-security posture.
h.name: Halter

h.description: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) is a research-intensive graduate university founded in 2010 within Qatar Foundation, in Education City, Doha, Qatar. Its central administration publishes no developer portal, no open-data portal and no identity federation entry — HBKU appears in no eduGAIN federation, and api.hbku.edu.qa answers every request with a WAF rejection. What it does operate comes almost entirely from one research institute, the Qatar Computing Research Institute (QCRI), whose domain qcri.org redirects into hbku.edu.qa: Fanar, Qatar's Arabic generative-AI platform, which publishes a first-party OpenAPI 3.1 at api.fanar.qa/openapi.json covering chat, speech, vision, translation, poetry and moderation, with a fourteen-code error vocabulary and a published per-model rate-limit table; and Farasa, a keyed Arabic NLP web API. Three further surfaces are tenant deployments on HBKU hosts and are recorded as relationships, not as HBKU contracts: a working public OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint over its Elsevier Pure research portal at elmi.hbku.edu.qa/ws/oai, a CourseLeaf course-search API at catalog.hbku.edu.qa whose term database is currently unavailable, and its research deposits in Manara — Qatar Research Repository, a Figshare platform run by Qatar National Library. The eleven "HBKU" Figshare API definitions this profile previously carried were one vendor contract, split eleven ways by tag and recorded under the university's name; they have been removed.
h.name: Hamad Bin Khalifa University

h.description: Hamama is a West Sacramento, California consumer-products company that makes it easy to grow fresh microgreens at home. Founded by two MIT-trained mechanical engineers, Hamama sells self-watering microgreen grow kits and its signature pre-seeded "Seed Quilts" (non-GMO, mostly Certified Organic) that sprout edible greens in 7-10 days with nothing more than a single addition of water, no soil, pesticides, or fertilizer required. The company sells grow kits, ceramic trays, Seed Quilt refills, green-onion and mushroom kits, and accessories directly to consumers through its Shopify storefront, offers flexible subscribe-and-save refill plans, and supports growers with Growing Guides, recipes, a rewards program, and a Grow Coach customer-support team.
h.name: HAMAMA

h.description: HAMi (Heterogeneous AI Computing Virtualization Middleware) is a CNCF incubating open-source project that brings device sharing, memory and core isolation, and topology-aware scheduling to heterogeneous AI accelerators on Kubernetes. It lets several containers share one physical GPU or NPU with hard memory limits and enforced compute quotas, across NVIDIA, Huawei Ascend, Cambricon MLU, Hygon DCU, Enflame GCU, Iluvatar, Moore Threads, MetaX, Kunlunxin and Vastai devices. HAMi ships a scheduler, a device plugin, an in-container enforcement library (HAMi-core/libvgpu), a DRA driver, and HAMi WebUI — an observability dashboard whose backend exposes a gRPC and grpc-gateway REST API over cluster GPU, node, workload and Prometheus-backed monitoring data. The project also publishes a machine-readable discovery surface on its documentation site: an RFC 9727 API catalog, an OpenAPI 3.1 service description, an Agent Skills discovery index, and Content-Signal directives in robots.txt.
h.name: HAMi

h.description: Hamilton Lane is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Hamilton Lane API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
h.name: Hamilton Lane

h.description: Hammerhead is a cycling technology company (now part of SRAM) best known for the Karoo GPS cycling computer, a premium Android-based device for recording and displaying ride data, routes, structured workouts, and Flight Attendant performance. Its ecosystem includes the web Dashboard (dashboard.hammerhead.io) and a Companion mobile app that bridge ride data between rider, device, and third parties. Hammerhead runs one of the more open developer platforms in the category: a public API that lets connected third parties sync routes and workouts, and the karoo-ext Android/Kotlin Extensions SDK (io.hammerhead:karoo-ext, Apache-2.0) that lets developers build on-device extensions for Karoo and Karoo 2.
h.name: Hammerhead

h.description: Hammerspace, Inc. is a Redwood City, California software company behind the Hammerspace Global Data Platform (formerly the Global Data Environment), a parallel file system and software-defined data platform that unifies unstructured data across on-premises storage, edge sites, and AWS, Azure and Google Cloud into a single global namespace. Data is reached through standard protocols — NFS, pNFS v4.2 with Flex Files, SMB, S3, and CSI for Kubernetes — while placement, replication, tiering, snapshots and retention are driven by declarative objectives rather than by manual data movement.
