Haus reports running thousands of experiments annually across tens of billions of dollars in optimized ad spend for customers such as FanDuel, Intuit, Wayfair, and Coursera. Founded by former Google economists, Haus is backed by Insight Partners.
h.name: Haus

h.description: Haus Labs by Lady Gaga (formerly Haus Laboratories) is an American clean-beauty cosmetics brand founded by Lady Gaga. It first launched in September 2019 and relaunched in June 2022 with Sephora as its exclusive retail partner. The brand makes skincare-infused, high-performance color cosmetics and makeup — including its Triclone Skin Tech Foundation plus lip, eye, and complexion products — that are always vegan and cruelty-free. It sells direct-to-consumer through hauslabs.com and through Sephora. Haus Labs is a consumer packaged goods / beauty company with no public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio.
h.name: Haus Laboratories

h.description: HauteLook was a members-only, flash-sale e-commerce destination for fashion, beauty, and home goods, founded in 2007 in Los Angeles. It was acquired by Nordstrom in 2011 and operated as a standalone flash-sale brand before being folded into Nordstrom Rack; www.hautelook.com now redirects to the Nordstrom Rack Flash storefront. The provider publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so no API artifacts could be enriched during the pipeline pass.
h.name: HauteLook

h.description: Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) is a free service operated by Troy Hunt that lets individuals and organizations check whether their email addresses, phone numbers, passwords, or domains have appeared in known data breaches, pastes, or stealer logs. The service aggregates billions of compromised records and exposes both free and paid endpoints, including the k-anonymity Pwned Passwords API. The v3 REST API at haveibeenpwned.com requires an hibp-api-key header for breach, paste, domain, and stealer log endpoints and is offered across Core, Pro, and High RPM subscription tiers.
h.name: Have I Been Pwned

h.description: havekarma is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: havekarma

h.description: Haven, Inc. was an ocean freight technology company founded in 2014 that built software to automate quoting, booking, document management, and shipment management for commodity producers, traders, and freight forwarders moving international ocean cargo. Backed by DCVC, Haven was acquired by supply-chain visibility platform FourKites in April 2021, and its technology became the foundation of FourKites' Dynamic Ocean product for end-to-end international ocean shipment visibility. Haven no longer operates an independent public developer program or API; the Haven brand survives only as the "Haven Marketplace" login at app.haveninc.com, now operated as part of FourKites.
h.name: Haven

h.description: Haven Connect is an affordable-housing software company (founded 2014, San Jose, CA) that streamlines the affordable-housing application and waitlist process for both property managers and low-income applicants. Its web platform lets property managers publish waitlists, collect and screen online applications, and automate waitlist updates — eliminating paper forms and manual data entry — while giving applicants a single portal to find and apply for affordable housing. Haven Connect is a Techstars Impact portfolio company and has raised roughly $2.9M. It is a SaaS product company with no public developer API; this profile captures its public website, support, and commercial surfaces for the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Haven Connect

h.description: Haven Energy is an Austin, Texas based residential clean-energy company that sells, finances, installs and operates home battery storage and solar systems, and then aggregates those systems into one of the largest virtual power plant (VPP) networks in the United States. Homeowners get an instant online quote, a fixed monthly payment over a ten-year term, end-to-end permitting and certified installation through Haven's Channel Partner network of local electricians, and ongoing remote monitoring. Haven then enrolls the installed batteries into utility and grid programs - California SGIP, PG&E, and Massachusetts ConnectedSolutions among them - so customers can monetize grid participation while utilities and community choice aggregators gain flexible local capacity. Founded in 2022 by Jeff Chapin, Philip Krim and Vinnie Campos, the company raised a $40M Series B in December 2025 led by Giant Ventures. Haven operates as a direct-to-consumer and utility-partner business; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.
h.name: Haven Energy

h.description: Havenly is an online interior-design platform that connects clients with professional designers for virtual and in-person home-decorating services. Clients take a style quiz, match with a designer, collaborate on 3D room renderings, and shop curated furniture and decor from partner brands at exclusive prices. Havenly also offers AI-assisted design. The company exposes a REST API (documented publicly via Postman at api-docs.havenly.com) covering users and profiles, addresses, design boards and board products, a vendor product catalog (vendor variants), attribute types, board feedback, and user opinions/likes. Authentication is OAuth2 (password grant) returning a Bearer token; HAL+JSON responses use page/limit pagination and zf-doctrine-querybuilder query filters. Havenly is backed by 500 Global and Foundry Group.
h.name: Havenly

h.description: HavocAI (Havoc) is a Providence, Rhode Island-based defense technology company building all-domain collaborative autonomy software and autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army and allied militaries. Its software suite pairs Havoc OS, an edge autonomy operating system for heterogeneous platforms, with Havoc C2 for one-to-many operator control, Havoc Insights for real-time sensor and telemetry analytics, and Havoc Connect, a resilient peer-to-peer overlay network for degraded or GPS-denied environments. The company builds the Rampage, Seahound, Kiakoa and Atlas autonomous surface vessels and is partnered with Hanwha on 200-foot ASVs. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no public developer API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal or documentation, no published SDKs or packages, no MCP server, and no A2A agent card - the platform is delivered under defense contract rather than as a self-serve developer product.
h.name: HavocAI

h.description: Hawaii Open Data Portal is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 976 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
h.name: Hawaii Open Data Portal

h.description: Hawaiian Electric Industries (HEI) is a Honolulu-based holding company whose principal subsidiary, Hawaiian Electric, delivers electricity to roughly 95% of Hawaii's residents through three operating utilities — Hawaiian Electric (Oahu), Hawaii Electric Light (Hawaii Island) and Maui Electric (Maui County) — alongside Pacific Current, its clean-energy and sustainability investment arm. HEI runs no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server. It does serve one real, anonymously callable machine-readable surface: a public Esri ArcGIS REST feature-service catalog carrying the Locational Value Maps, published grid needs and EV charging locations that its own hawaiianelectric.com map applications consume.
h.name: Hawaiian Electric Industries

h.description: Hawaiian Holdings was the parent company of Hawaiian Airlines, the largest and longest-serving airline of Hawaii, providing scheduled passenger service to destinations across the Pacific. In 2024 the company combined with Alaska Air Group, and Hawaiian Holdings became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alaska Air Group. No public developer portal or production-facing APIs are advertised.
h.name: Hawaiian Holdings

h.description: Hawaya is a Muslim-focused online dating and matrimonial app that began as Harmonica, an Egyptian matchmaking startup backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), and was later acquired by Match Group and rebranded as Hawaya. The service emphasized serious, marriage-minded connections with privacy controls tailored to Muslim singles across the Middle East, North Africa, and international diaspora markets, offered as consumer iOS and Android mobile apps rather than a developer platform. Hawaya was discontinued in 2023 and no longer accepts new registrations; it exposes no public API, SDK, or developer program. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a company record with identity and legal links captured from the provider's own site.
h.name: Hawaya

h.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.
h.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations

h.description: HawkEye 360 is a Herndon, Virginia-based radio frequency (RF) data analytics and geospatial intelligence company that operates the first commercial satellite constellation purpose-built to identify, process, and geolocate a broad range of RF signals from space. Founded in 2015 by Chris DeMay, Charles Clancy, and Bob McGwier, the company flies clusters of three small satellites in formation that use time- and frequency-difference-of-arrival triangulation to pinpoint emitters across VHF through Ku-band. As of 2025, HawkEye 360 has placed 36 Hawk satellites on orbit across 12 operational clusters. Its core products include RFGeo (the underlying RF signal mapping and geolocation data product), RFIQ (its RF intelligence data product recently selected by NASA Commercial LEO programs), and Mission Space, a web-based RF geospatial intelligence analysis platform. The company also offers a Regional Awareness Subscription (RAS) service providing persistent monitoring of high-interest regions such as the Mediterranean, South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula. In December 2023 HawkEye 360 acquired Maxar Intelligence's RF Solutions business (formerly Aurora Insight), expanding its spectrum-mapping capabilities. Customers are concentrated in defense, intelligence, national security, and maritime domain awareness — including the US Government, allied partners, and foreign military sales (a 2025 FMS to India was approved by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency). HawkEye 360 has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO. There is no public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open-source release; data access is delivered through gated commercial and government contracts via the Mission Space platform and a customer-facing API for ordering and integration of RF analytics into customer systems.
h.name: HawkEye 360

h.description: HawkSoft is an insurance agency management system (AMS) for independent property and casualty agencies, covering client management, policy tracking, documentation, accounting, and workflow automation. HawkSoft operates a gated Partner API program that lets vetted third-party technology vendors and agencies read agency, office, client, contact, policy, coverage, vehicle, driver, and log data, and (with 2-way integration) write activities back into HawkSoft as log notes, attachments, and payment receipts. The Partner API documentation is publicly readable at partner.hawksoft.app, but credentials are issued only to approved API Partners, and an agency must opt in to share its data. Endpoints are versioned (V1.8 and V3.0, with V3.0 built on the HawkSoft 6 cloud data model).
h.name: HawkSoft

h.description: Hawthorne is an internet-first men's personal care and grooming brand founded in 2016 in New York City (a Techstars alum, later Series B). It sells personalized, long-lasting fragrance and grooming products — cologne, deodorant, body wash, face and hair care — tuned to a customer's body chemistry and lifestyle through an onboarding quiz and a smart-subscription model built around its "Surround Scent" technology. The direct-to-consumer storefront at hawthorne.co runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a published /llms.txt and /agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint so AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout.
h.name: Hawthorne

h.description: Hayden AI is a San Francisco based artificial intelligence and spatial analytics company that builds a mobile perception platform for public transit agencies and city governments. The company mounts a purpose-built AI camera and edge compute box on transit buses and other municipal fleet vehicles, then uses computer vision to detect bus lane, bus stop, bike lane, double parking and tram blocking violations in real time. Detections are reviewed by authorized agency staff in the Hayden AI Data Portal, which also carries traffic rule management, city asset monitoring and aggregated traffic analytics, and which hands verified evidence off to an agency's existing violations processing system for citation issuance. Hayden AI publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract; the platform is sold and integrated directly with transit agencies and municipalities.
h.name: Hayden AI

h.description: Hayneedle (formerly NetShops) was an online retailer of home goods, furniture, and outdoor products, founded as NetShops in Omaha, Nebraska in 2002 and rebranded to Hayneedle.com in 2009. It grew into a large specialty e-commerce operator running hundreds of niche home-and-lifestyle storefronts, and was acquired by Jet.com in 2016 for roughly $90 million, becoming a Walmart subsidiary after Walmart bought Jet.com. The standalone brand was subsequently wound down and hayneedle.com now redirects into walmart.com. It was listed as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no first-party public developer surface (no API docs, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or event surface); the only signal captured is honest DNS/TLS domain-security data for the still-resolving redirect domain.
h.name: hayneedle.com (formerly know as NetShops)

h.description: Haystack is deepset's open-source Python framework for building context-engineered, production-ready LLM applications - modular Pipelines and agent workflows assembled from 100+ Components and document stores for RAG, semantic search, and agents. Haystack pipelines deploy as REST services via Hayhooks, and the commercial deepset AI Platform (deepset Cloud) exposes a hosted REST API at api.cloud.deepset.ai for pipelines, search, files, and workspaces.
h.name: Haystack / deepset

h.description: Haz (operated by Vend Solutions Ltd) is a London-based AI social commerce mobile app that connects friends through the things they own and makes it easier to track, buy, and sell second-hand belongings. Its proprietary receipt-reading technology scans digital purchase receipts in a user's email inbox to automatically digitize owned items in real time, removing the manual listing, photography, and description work traditionally required for resale. Users get real-time valuations of everything they own and can offer items to their social circle in a live feed, increasing the liquidity of everyday goods such as clothing and electronics. Haz launched on iOS in March 2024 and raised a $1.4M pre-seed round led by Speedinvest. It is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.
h.name: Haz

h.description: Hazel Health is the nation's leading provider of school-based telehealth, delivering virtual physical and mental health care to K-12 students. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, Hazel partners directly with school districts and families to connect students with licensed, linguistically and culturally diverse clinicians and therapists — at school or at home — often within minutes for medical care and within days for teletherapy, at no cost to families. The company serves more than two million students across 100-plus districts nationwide, helping reduce chronic absenteeism and address gaps in access to care as an extension of the school health team. Hazel operates HIPAA- and FERPA-compliant systems with full encryption and secure access controls. It is a B2B/B2G healthcare provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
h.name: Hazel Health

h.description: Hazelcast is a real-time data platform that helps businesses accelerate their applications with data caching, data integration, and distributed computing. Hazelcast provides in-memory computing capabilities for high-performance, low-latency applications, exposing a REST API for managing maps, queues, cluster state, configuration, and health.
h.name: Hazelcast

h.description: Hazelight is a Swedish video game development studio founded in 2014, known for creating cooperative multiplayer games that emphasize narrative and emotional storytelling. Their flagship titles include "A Way Out" and "It Takes Two," both of which have received critical acclaim for innovative gameplay mechanics and award-winning design. Hazelight focuses on delivering high-quality, story-driven experiences that bring players together, fostering collaboration and shared adventure across platforms.
h.name: Hazelight

h.description: HCA Healthcare (formerly HCA Holdings) is one of the largest for-profit operators of healthcare facilities in the world, operating hospitals, surgery centers, freestanding emergency rooms, and urgent care centers. The company was named HCA Holdings until May 2017. No public developer portal or production APIs are advertised.
h.name: HCA Healthcare

h.description: HCA Holdings is an alias for HCA Healthcare, one of the largest for-profit operators of healthcare facilities in the world, operating hospitals, surgery centers, freestanding emergency rooms, and urgent care centers. The legal entity rebranded to HCA Healthcare; this index tracks the legacy name. No public developer portal or production APIs are advertised.
h.name: HCA Holdings

h.description: hCaptcha, operated by Intuition Machines, is a privacy-focused CAPTCHA and bot-defense platform used as a drop-in replacement for Google reCAPTCHA. The free Publisher and Pro tiers offer a JavaScript widget and a server-side /siteverify endpoint that issue and verify single-use tokens. The Enterprise tier (hCaptcha Enterprise) adds advanced bot detection, account defense, MFA, machine-learning fraud signals, and management APIs. hCaptcha is broadly integrated into web frameworks and CMS platforms (React, Vue, Angular, Node/Express, WordPress, Magento) and ships first-party mobile SDKs for iOS and Android.
h.name: hCaptcha

h.description: HCC Insurance Holdings was a leading specialty insurance group with offices in the United States, the United Kingdom, Spain, and Ireland. It was acquired by Tokio Marine in 2015 and now operates as Tokio Marine HCC, providing more than 100 classes of specialty insurance products in approximately 180 countries.
h.name: HCC Insurance Holdings

h.description: HCF — The Hospitals Contribution Fund of Australia Limited (ABN 68 000 026 746, AFSL 241 414), founded in 1932 and headquartered in Sydney — is Australia's largest not-for-profit health fund, covering over 2 million members. It underwrites private health insurance (hospital, extras and ambulance cover) and Overseas Visitors Health Cover, and distributes life and Recover Cover products (life protect, income protect, critical illness), travel, pet, home, car and landlord insurance, plus the Flip accidental-injury brand, alongside its own HCF dental and eyecare centres and the HCF Research Foundation. As a carrier in Australian private health insurance, HCF publishes NO public, self-serve developer API and no developer portal: probes of developer.hcf.com.au, developers.hcf.com.au and docs.hcf.com.au do not resolve, and /developers, /developer, /api-docs, /partners and /integrations on www.hcf.com.au all return 404. Member and provider integration runs through channels HCF does not itself expose as an API — point-of-service extras claiming over third-party HICAPS VX, HICAPS Trinity and CommBank Smart Health terminals, Medicare Benefit Statements for medical gap claims, the My Membership app and online member services behind an Okta-backed sign-in at id.hcf.com.au, and four login-gated ASP.NET provider portals (hospital, medical, dental and ancillary) at www.hcf.com.au/provider-portals which are web applications rather than machine interfaces. The only machine-readable surface HCF answers on is that Okta tenant's OIDC and RFC 8414 discovery metadata, captured in this record. No ACORD reference of any kind appears on the site, which is consistent with private health insurance sitting outside the general-insurance ACORD/AL3 world, and Australia's Consumer Data Right — designated for general insurance and then deferred — never reached health insurance at all. The record here is deliberately an honest stub: this is a partner-gated, no-public-API carrier.
h.name: HCF

h.description: HCLSoftware, part of HCLTech, delivers a broad portfolio of enterprise software solutions spanning AI-driven operations, cybersecurity, data analytics, and low-code development platforms. The company focuses on orchestrating experiences, data, and operations at scale for large organizations, offering products such as HCL BigFix, HCL Cloud, and HCL Volt MX. Through its extensive suite, HCLSoftware enables digital transformation, secure endpoint management, and intelligent automation across industries.
h.name: HCLSoftware

h.description: HD is an AI-native healthcare marketplace and patient-navigation platform for emerging Southeast Asia, headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand. Its consumer surface, HDmall, is a health, dental, aesthetics, and surgery marketplace that lets patients compare transparent pricing and book online across 30,000+ services from 3,000+ clinics and hospitals in Thailand (hdmall.co.th) and Indonesia (hdmall.id). AI-powered navigation turns patient symptoms into personalized, safety-checked care recommendations, and HDcare adds human-led, AI-assisted concierge support for complex surgical cases. The platform has navigated over 500,000 patients. HD is a consumer-facing healthtech operator with no public developer API or portal; the strongest machine-readable surface it publishes today is an llms.txt guiding LLMs to its canonical content. HD is a portfolio company of Partech, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.
h.name: HD

h.description: HD Supply is one of the largest industrial distributors in North America, providing maintenance, repair, and operations products and value-added services to multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, and government facilities. HD Supply operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Home Depot following its acquisition in 2020.
h.name: HD Supply Holdings

h.description: HData is the AI-native operating system for energy regulation. Founded in 2018 by Hudson Hollister, the platform turns disconnected federal and state regulatory filings, dockets, and proceedings from sources such as FERC, EIA, and state utility commissions into standardized, citable, machine-readable data. It combines centralized regulatory data, domain-specific AI trained on more than 20 million citable documents, and purpose-built tools — including HData Analytics, Regulatory Intelligence, Gateway for FERC data extraction, and Data Request Management — to help utilities, regulators, advocates, advisory firms, financial institutions, and large energy customers accelerate rate cases, resource planning, compliance reporting, and policy research.
h.name: HData

h.description: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance) is a Chicago-based commercial trucking insurance company delivering modern, data-driven coverage for small and mid-size fleet operators. Its flagship HDVI Shift product uses integrated telematics and safety data to dynamically price premiums, rewarding safe driving with monthly discounts of up to 20 percent, and its Fleet Portal gives fleets tools to improve safety, reduce risk, maintain compliance, and lower costs. HDVI was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it operates a customer-facing Fleet Portal and telematics/ELD/dash-cam partner integrations rather than an open developer program. This profile captures the company's real public identity, its published llms.txt, its SOC 2 Type 2 compliance posture, and domain-security posture.
h.name: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance)

h.description: Heabsy provides an OpenAI‑compatible inference API hosted in the European Economic Area, targeting regulated industries such as finance, insurance, and manufacturing. The platform offers sovereign AI models with zero data retention, compliance with EU AI regulations, and detailed security certifications. It includes a developer console for key management, pricing tiers, and extensive documentation for integration.
h.name: Heabsy

h.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.
h.name: Headgum

h.description: Headlight is a US mental health services company delivering teletherapy, in-person therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through a clinician-centered care model. Founded by Drs. Manish Sheth and Shashita Inamdar, it helps patients move from initial interest to a well-matched therapist or prescriber with less friction, treating conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, trauma, OCD, panic disorder, postpartum depression, and insomnia. Headlight is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Kaiser, Moda) and operates across Alaska, California, Colorado, Oregon, Texas, and Washington. The company raised $18M led by Matrix and EPIC Ventures. This is a consumer clinical services provider with no public developer API surface.
h.name: Headlight

h.description: Headnote is a legal payments and accounts-receivable platform built specifically for law firms. Founded in 2016 by attorney Sarah Schaaf, it lets firms accept trust-compliant credit card and eCheck (ACH) payments via shareable payment links and a hosted client payment portal, then automates collections, AR tracking, and client NPS/satisfaction reporting. Headnote is designed to be 100% compliant with IOLTA rules, the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct, and lawyer trust/operating account requirements across all 50 states, and integrates with existing billing and practice-management software by attaching a Headnote payment link to invoices. Card and bank data are tokenized with Stripe and Plaid and the platform runs on AWS with PCI-compliant, encrypted-at-rest-and-in-transit infrastructure. Headnote was acquired by ASG LegalTech (an Alpine Investors platform, alongside PracticePanther, Bill4Time, and MerusCase) in 2020. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. Headnote does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile is an identity record.
h.name: Headnote

h.description: Headout is a global experiences marketplace that curates and sells tickets to tours, attractions, events, shows and activities across major cities worldwide. For developers, Headout operates a public Partner API (github.com/headout/api-docs) that lets affiliates and resellers browse the catalog (products, categories, collections and subcategories by city and language), pull live inventory and per-person/per-group pricing for a variant, and place bookings through a two-step create-then-capture flow. The API is versioned by URI path (v1 and v2 under /api/public/), authenticates with a Headout-Auth API key (pk_ production / tk_ sandbox), paginates with offset/limit, and returns a structured error envelope. A registrable seatmap iframe component is offered for seat selection. Headout is backed by 500 Global and Version One Ventures.
h.name: HeadOut

h.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.
h.name: Headspace

h.description: HeadSpin is a real-device digital-experience, functional, and performance testing platform for mobile, web, and OTT applications. Teams test, monitor, and optimize app behavior on real devices and real SIMs across 60+ locations in 50+ countries, running manual and automated tests through frameworks such as Appium and Selenium while capturing 130+ performance KPIs across app, device, browser, audio-video, and network layers. HeadSpin exposes a v0 REST API (Bearer API-token auth) for authentication, device management, capture sessions, app instrumentation, biometrics, and audio/video capture, plus an official `hs` command-line interface and a family of open-source Appium drivers for Roku, LG WebOS, and Samsung Tizen TV.
h.name: HeadSpin

h.description: HeadsUp was an AI conversion engine for product-led growth (PLG) that helped go-to-market teams identify which product-qualified users to engage and when to engage them. It ingested product usage and analytics data (for example from Segment), applied feature engineering and machine-learning scoring to surface conversion, churn, and upsell signals, and synced those insights into sales tooling such as Salesforce so reps could act on in-product behavior without engineering, code, or SQL. Customers included Contentful, Dialpad, and Matillion. HeadsUp was backed by Wing Venture Capital and 645 Ventures and was acquired by composable-CDP company Hightouch in November 2023, after which its team joined Hightouch to work on Customer 360. The standalone headsup.ai product and developer surface have since been wound down; this profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.
h.name: HeadsUp

h.description: Headway operates a national mental-health care platform that connects patients, therapists and psychiatrists, and insurance companies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Headway builds the first asset-free national network of behavioral-health providers who accept insurance, handling insurance credentialing, claims management, payments, and scheduling for clinicians while letting patients search for in-network providers, book appointments online, and see costs up front. The company partners with 45+ major insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Oxford, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar) and, as of 2026, powers 600,000+ appointments per month across all 50 states. Headway is backed by a16z, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, and Forerunner. It maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Headway does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.
h.name: Headway

h.description: Heal (legally Get Heal, Inc.) was a Los Angeles based in-home primary care practice founded in 2014 that delivered on-demand doctor house calls, one-touch telemedicine, telepsychology and remote patient monitoring, aimed largely at Medicare Advantage members. Humana took a $100M stake in the company in July 2020 and then acquired it outright, folding the practice into its CenterWell primary care brand. Heal never ran a public developer program: it published no OpenAPI, no developer portal and no SDKs. As of this profile heal.com issues a 301 redirect to centerwell.com for every path, and the one surviving technical host, api.heal.com, answers every request with a blanket HTTP 401.
h.name: Heal

h.description: Healf (healf.mx) is a Mexico City-based InsurTech startup founded in 2022 that offers an AI-based SaaS platform to simplify, explain, and manage medical / health insurance policies. Using generative AI, natural language processing, and information-retrieval models, the platform automates repetitive inquiries, provides 24/7 conversational support to insurance brokers, and gives the insured comprehensive insight into their policy details for better-informed decisions. For brokers and doctors it streamlines communication and automates processes, improving transparency and traceability for insurers. Healf is a 500 Global portfolio company (Somos Lucha Batch 19), also backed by Blue Zone Ventures. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.
h.name: Healf

h.description: Healint is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company best known for Migraine Buddy, the world's largest migraine and headache tracking and research platform, used by more than three million people to log attacks, symptoms, triggers, medications, and treatment outcomes. The company applies machine learning, mobile sensor technologies, and analytics to help people manage migraine and other neurological conditions, and to generate real-world evidence for clinicians, researchers, and pharmaceutical partners. Healint and Migraine Buddy are now part of Aptar Digital Health, whose regulated companion apps, patient-support software, and drug-delivery platforms operate across more than 120 countries on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. Healint does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Healint

h.description: Health Co (Stealth) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Health Co (Stealth)

h.description: Health Connect is a Google-backed platform that enables Android apps to read and write a user's health and fitness data in a privacy-preserving way. It provides a unified API for accessing data such as steps, heart rate, sleep, nutrition, and more, allowing developers to build health-focused experiences while giving users granular control over data sharing. The service integrates with Google Fit and other health providers, offering standardized data models and secure permissions management.
h.name: Health Connect

h.description: Health Gorilla operates a national health-data interoperability network and a FHIR-first API suite for healthcare developers. Its HL7 FHIR R4 REST API provides access to patient records, person-authorized record retrieval across national exchange networks (QHIN / TEFCA), diagnostic (lab and radiology) ordering and results, clinical documents, and coverage/eligibility data under OAuth 2.0.
h.name: Health Gorilla

h.description: Health IQ was a venture-backed insurtech founded in 2013 in Mountain View, California that offered lower-cost life insurance to health-conscious individuals, later pivoting in 2019 to selling Medicare Advantage plans to seniors. Backed by a16z and others (~$200M raised), the company laid off staff in December 2022 and filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on August 30, 2023. As of this enrichment pass the healthiq.com domain resolves to a parked "domain may be for sale" page, and the company operates no public website, developer portal, or API. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.
h.name: Health IQ

h.description: Health Net is a managed care organization offering health benefits to individuals, families, businesses, and beneficiaries of government sponsored programs. Health Net is a wholly owned subsidiary of Centene Corporation, one of the largest managed care companies in the United States.
h.name: Health Net

h.description: The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) is the primary Federal agency for improving access to health care services for people who are uninsured, isolated, or medically vulnerable. HRSA provides data and web services for healthcare resources, facility locations, and program information.
h.name: Health Resources and Services Administration

h.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.
h.name: Health Scholars

h.description: Health Standards covers the collection of technical standards and specifications used in healthcare interoperability, including HL7 FHIR, HL7 v2, CDA, DICOM, IHE profiles, ICD codes, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, US Core, and other health data exchange and coding standards. This index curates the canonical specifications, reference implementations, registries, and developer resources for building interoperable healthcare applications.
h.name: Health Standards

h.description: Health Universe is an enterprise healthcare AI platform and compliant app cloud that lets clinical, research, and life-sciences teams build, deploy, govern, and monitor AI agents inside regulated environments. Developers package Python models as Streamlit, FastAPI, React, or Agent2Agent (A2A) apps and ship them with one click to a HIPAA-aligned, SOC 2 Type II, ONC-certified, TEFCA-connected workspace. The platform unifies patient records via TEFCA and SMART on FHIR, and provides Navigator, Explorer/Roster, and Observer surfaces for deploying agents, building cohorts, and monitoring cost, hallucination, and high-risk scenarios with human-in-the-loop review. Health Universe ships a first-party CLI (@health-universe/cli), a Python SDK, and an A2A agent SDK. Backed by Kleiner Perkins.
h.name: Health Universe

h.description: Healthcare.com (HealthCare, Inc.) is a privately held, non-government health insurance marketplace and distribution platform founded in 2014. Consumers use healthcare.com to find, compare and enroll in ACA/under-65 individual health plans, Medicare Advantage and Medicare Supplement plans, and specialty coverage; distributors, FMOs, MGAs and agents use its Autopilot machine-learning enrollment acquisition platform, which matches high-intent shoppers to distributor partners with predictive scoring and value-based lead pricing. Its Pivot Health subsidiary develops and markets proprietary short-term medical, fixed indemnity and supplemental gap products with A-rated carriers. Insurance is sold through Healthcare.com Insurance Services, LLC. As of this profiling pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition or SDKs.
h.name: Healthcare.com

h.description: Educational content about the US Health Insurance Marketplace
h.name: Healthcare.gov

h.description: HealthcareSource is a healthcare-focused talent management software provider whose recruiting, applicant tracking, onboarding, behavioral assessments, learning, and employee performance-management products are used across U.S. healthcare organizations. HealthcareSource was acquired by symplr in July 2021 (from Francisco Partners) and its products are now delivered as part of symplr's healthcare talent-management suite, including symplr Recruiting. No public developer program, API documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the brand at profiling time; the healthcaresource.com domain 301-redirects to symplr.com/healthcaresource.
h.name: Healthcaresource.com

h.description: Health Catalyst is a healthcare data, analytics, and AI company that helps healthcare organizations achieve measurable clinical, financial, and operational improvement. Its flagship platform, Health Catalyst Ignite, is a healthcare-specific data and analytics ecosystem built on Azure Databricks that natively integrates clinical, financial, and operational data and exposes pre-built standard APIs, healthcare data models, and self-service analytics tools. Health Catalyst serves more than 1,100 organizations and maintains a deep security and compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF, HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, TX-RAMP). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the pipeline.
h.name: Healthcatalyst

h.description: Healthchecks.io provides simple, effective cron job and background task monitoring. Users create unique ping URLs for each job, and Healthchecks.io tracks execution, sending alerts via email, Slack, webhooks, and many other integrations when jobs fail to run on schedule. The service offers a free tier for up to 20 checks, detailed dashboards, tagging, and configurable grace periods, supporting integrations with popular platforms like Prometheus, PagerDuty, and GitHub Actions.
h.name: Healthchecks.io

h.description: HealthData.gov is the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services open data platform providing public access to federal health datasets including Medicare claims, hospital quality ratings, drug utilization data, public health indicators, and data from agencies such as CMS, CDC, FDA, and NIH. The platform is powered by the Socrata Open Data API (SODA) and exposes every dataset through a consistent REST API using SoQL query language, enabling developers to build applications, conduct research, and create data visualizations from authoritative government health data.
h.name: HealthData.gov

h.description: Healthdirect Australia is a national, government-owned, not-for-profit organisation that operates core Australian digital-health infrastructure and consumer health services on behalf of the Commonwealth, states, and territories. It runs the free healthdirect symptom checker and health advice service and, most relevant to developers, delivers the National Health Services Directory (NHSD) — the authoritative national directory of health services and practitioners, covering more than 400,000 service and practitioner records. Healthdirect exposes the NHSD to government, commercial, and clinical software developers through standards-based HL7 FHIR APIs (aligned to the HL7 AU Provider Directory / AU-PD implementation guide, using SNOMED CT-AU terminology and G-NAF geocoded addresses), a FHIR bulk data export, a FHIR ingestion/data-acquisition hub for contributing sources, an embeddable NHSD search widget, and a Provider Appointments API that surfaces real-time appointment availability from certified booking platforms. Integration is gated behind a formal onboarding and test-environment registration process, and APIs are secured with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials plus an API key. Home market is Australia.
h.name: Healthdirect Australia

h.description: HealthEngine is Australia's largest consumer healthcare marketplace and patient-engagement platform, founded in 2006 and headquartered in Perth, Western Australia. Its consumer app and website let millions of Australians search a national directory of primary-care providers and book, manage, and attend appointments (including telehealth) across GP, dental, allied-health, and specialist practices. For practices, HealthEngine sells a SaaS suite - GP Complete, Patient Connect, Online Booking, Appointment Reminders and Recalls, Featured Listings, online payments, patient reviews, and Scripts - that plugs into the practice's existing software. It maintains private, real-time integrations into 25+ Australian practice management systems (Best Practice / Bp Premier, MedicalDirector Pracsoft, Zedmed, Cliniko, Genie, Gentu, Medtech, Nookal, PracSuite, Dental4Windows, and others) so appointment availability and bookings sync directly with the front desk. Home market is Australia. HealthEngine does NOT publish a public developer portal, REST OpenAPI, or HL7 FHIR endpoint - its API surface is a set of gated, partner-only PMS integrations rather than a self-serve developer program, so this profile is an honest identity stub with no public machine-readable contract to harvest.
h.name: HealthEngine

h.description: HealthEquity is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The HealthEquity API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
h.name: HealthEquity

h.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.
h.name: Healthera

h.description: HealthEx is a patient-centric health-data-rights platform that securely unifies an individual's medical records across places of care into one connected history, and lets them share that record — under explicit, patient-initiated consent — with providers, apps, and AI services. It operates as an Information Access Services (IAS) Provider on the TEFCA network, complies with HIPAA privacy rules, and reaches records across more than 80% of U.S. care providers. For developers HealthEx exposes a REST admin API (patient outreach, consent checking and auditing, record-location search, usage), a FHIR R4 server ($everything, USCDIv3), and a hosted Model Context Protocol server that gives AI agents governed, consent-scoped access to a patient's health record.
h.name: HealthEx

h.description: HealthGeneTech (HGT) is a genomics company focused on gene fragment analysis and the development of applications for genetic testing and diagnostics. It is a healthcare portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The public website healthgenetech.com redirects to www.hgt.cn. As of enrichment, no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification could be located, and the primary web host did not serve content to automated probes; this profile remains a lead awaiting a discoverable API surface.
h.name: healthgenetech

h.description: Healthie is a cloud, API-first EHR and practice management platform purpose-built for digital health startups, virtual care companies, and modern clinical practices. Healthie packages an EHR, scheduling, charting, telehealth, intake forms, care plans, online programs, messaging, billing, claims (CMS-1500 / ClaimMD), and patient portal behind a single GraphQL API and modular SDKs that power both the Healthie product UI and partner applications. Healthie targets the digital health ecosystem with a "buy the EHR, build the experience" model — the same API that backs the Healthie web and mobile apps is fully exposed to customers building branded patient and provider experiences on top of the platform.
h.name: Healthie

h.description: HealthJoy is a Chicago-based employee-benefits engagement, healthcare navigation, and cost-containment platform founded in 2014, which markets itself as a "Benefits Operating System" (BOS) for employers and benefit consultants. It unifies fragmented health benefits into a single member-facing app combining Joy AI — a 24/7 AI assistant trained on each client's benefits plan — with a licensed human healthcare concierge team, provider search with cost scores and quality ratings, prescription savings, medical bill review, and an intelligent steerage engine that routes members to high-value, fair-priced care. Employers and consultants get a client dashboard reporting engagement, utilization, savings, and ROI. HealthJoy reports 1,800+ client companies and 1.25M+ members. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract; integrations with benefits-administration and TPA vendors (e.g. Employee Navigator) are delivered as managed eligibility/census data feeds set up by its implementation team rather than as a self-serve API.
h.name: HealthJoy

h.description: HealthMode was a machine-learning digital medicine company, founded in 2017 in San Francisco by Bradford Cross and Dan Karlin, that developed AI-enabled digital measurement methods to increase the precision and speed of clinical research. Its techniques improved phenotype understanding, streamlined screening and eligibility, enabled early detection of adverse events, and provided objective, low-burden efficacy endpoints for next-generation clinical trials. HealthMode was acquired by MindMed in 2021 and folded into MindMed's digital-medicine division (Albert); it no longer operates as an independent company, maintains no standalone website or public developer/API surface, and none of its former domains resolve.
h.name: Healthmode

h.description: Healthpeak Properties (NYSE: DOC) is an S&P 500 healthcare real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops real estate for healthcare discovery and outpatient care — concentrated in lab/life-sciences, outpatient medical, and continuing care retirement community (CCRC) senior housing segments. The company tagline is "Where Discovery and Outpatient Care Thrive." Originally founded as HCP Inc. in 1985, the company rebranded to Healthpeak Properties in 2019. On March 1, 2024, Healthpeak completed an all-stock merger of equals with Physicians Realty Trust, combining two of the largest outpatient medical real estate platforms in the United States and adopting the new NYSE ticker DOC (previously PEAK). Healthpeak's portfolio spans roughly 700 properties nationwide, with lab concentrations in the South San Francisco, Boston, and San Diego clusters (including Torrey Pines Science Park and The Cove at Oyster Point) and outpatient medical assets clustered on or near top-ranked hospital campuses such as Medical City Dallas. The company reports that approximately 150,000 scientists, researchers, physicians, and healthcare professionals work in its buildings. As a healthcare REIT, Healthpeak does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or technical integration surface. Its public digital footprint is limited to corporate marketing, an investor relations site, SEC filings, ESG/sustainability reporting, and a press room. Tenant-facing operational systems (work orders, building access, energy reporting) are not exposed externally.
h.name: Healthpeak Properties

h.description: HealthSherpa is the leading ACA (Affordable Care Act) health insurance quoting and enrollment platform, and was the first company to partner with CMS to offer Enhanced Direct Enrollment (EDE) for agents. Its developer surface, HealthSherpa ONE (one.healthsherpa.com), exposes a public OpenAPI 3.1 REST API for on- and off-exchange ACA plan quoting, county/issuer/provider reference lookups, agent and self-service enrollment sessions, and an approval-gated direct enrollment API covering the full off-exchange (ICHRA) application lifecycle — create, update, submit, cancel, terminate, supporting-document upload, and payment redirect. Authentication is a single x-api-key header; enrollment writes support Idempotency-Key with 24-hour retention. Separate ICHRA and Medicare Partner APIs provide QuoteConnect/EnrollConnect, deeplinked enrollment, and webhooks. HealthSherpa publishes first-party Agent Skills, an llms.txt, and vibe-coding prompts for agents.
h.name: HealthSherpa

h.description: HealthSouth, rebranded as Encompass Health in 2018, is one of the largest providers of post-acute healthcare services in the United States, operating inpatient rehabilitation hospitals across the country. The company focuses on rehabilitation services for stroke, neurological conditions, spinal cord injuries, and orthopedic conditions. No public developer APIs have been identified.
h.name: HealthSouth (Encompass Health)

h.description: HealthTap is a United States virtual primary care medical group and telehealth technology company. It operates a nationwide network of board-certified, U.S.-licensed physicians covering all 50 states and Washington, D.C., and delivers video and phone visits for primary care, urgent care, chronic condition management and preventive care, plus 90-day follow-up text messaging with the treating doctor, prescription and lab ordering, and Dr. A.I. symptom triage. It sells direct to consumers on a monthly membership plus a per-visit fee, is in network with commercial and Medicare plans, and is deployed white-labeled or co-branded with employers, health plans, health systems and retailers. HealthTap previously operated a public developer platform, HealthTap Cloud (developers.healthtap.com, launched November 2016), which offered REST APIs and iOS/Android SDKs over its HOPES health operating system; that portal no longer resolves in DNS and HealthTap publishes no public API documentation, OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI or MCP surface today. Partner data exchange runs through contracted integrations such as Commure and Health Gorilla. Sector: healthtech.
h.name: HealthTap

h.description: HealthVerity is a United States life-sciences data platform, headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, that operates what it describes as the nation's largest real-world data (RWD) ecosystem - more than 150 billion de-identified transactions covering over 330 million U.S. patients across 75-plus data sources spanning medical and pharmacy claims, labs, and EHR (following its integration of Symphony Health). Its products are organized around the IPGE framework (Identity, Privacy, Governance, Exchange) and include HealthVerity Marketplace (verified RWD datasets), Identity Manager and Census (privacy-safe probabilistic identity resolution that replaces PII with a universal HealthVerity ID / HVID), Governance Manager, HealthVerity FLOW, and eXOs (an AI-native real-world-evidence agent). HealthVerity is a HIPAA-aligned, tokenization-and-de-identification company serving pharma, payers, and government - not a self-serve, standards-based clinical interoperability vendor. Unlike EHR and FHIR-network players, it exposes no public developer portal, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no downloadable OpenAPI; the only vendor-named programmatic surface is the gated, enterprise HealthVerity Identity API for real-time de-identification, described conceptually on the Identity Manager product page but without public reference documentation, base URL, or self-serve onboarding.
h.name: HealthVerity

h.description: Healthvision was a healthcare-IT software and services company based in Irving, Texas, that provided access to healthcare information to improve clinical and financial outcomes for public and private healthcare organizations. It was formed in 2007 through Battery Ventures' take-private acquisition of Quovadx (NASDAQ QVDX) and its Integration Solutions Division, and was subsequently acquired by Lawson Software (now part of Infor). The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.
h.name: Healthvision

h.description: Healthy Labs is a healthcare and insurance technology company that powers a portfolio of digital health brands driving membership growth for Medicare and ACA (Affordable Care Act) insurance providers. Its offerings center on consumer lead generation, compliance and operational analytics, and member acquisition and retention optimization for the health-insurance market. The company has since rebranded as MPA (mpa.com), positioning itself as an AI-powered platform for licensed insurance professionals and agencies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile is enriched from public sources; no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or API surface was found at the time of enrichment.
h.name: Healthy Labs

h.description: Healthy.io is a digital-health company that turns an ordinary smartphone camera into a clinical-grade measurement device, using colorimetric analysis, computer vision and machine learning trained on more than a million tagged color-spectrum images. Its Minuteful product line covers home urinalysis for chronic kidney disease (Minuteful Kidney, FDA 510(k) cleared and CE marked), urinary tract infection testing (Minuteful UTI), a ten-parameter urinalysis panel (Minuteful 10), and digitized chronic wound assessment (Minuteful for Wound). The company sells to health systems, provider groups and payers - including Medicare Advantage and nonprofit health plans - rather than to developers, and states that its technology integrates into most EMRs via SMART on FHIR. Healthy.io operates from Boston, London and Tel Aviv, and publishes a detailed public trust center covering security, privacy, availability and compliance, including a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy.
h.name: Healthy.io

h.description: Healx is a Cambridge, UK clinical-stage biotechnology company that uses artificial intelligence to discover and develop new treatments for rare diseases. Its Healnet platform pairs generative AI with drug-discovery and rare-disease expertise to build a biomedical knowledge graph from public and proprietary sources - biomedical literature, disease and biochemical datasets, clinical trials and patents - and to identify novel uses for known compounds. Founded by David Brown and Tim Guilliams, Healx advances its own therapeutic pipeline (including its NF1 lead candidate HLX-1502) and partners with pharma companies such as Sanofi. Healx does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.
h.name: Healx

h.description: Heap is a digital analytics platform that automatically captures every user interaction on web and mobile applications without requiring manual event tracking code. It provides product analytics, session replay, and behavioral data science capabilities to help teams understand user behavior and improve digital experiences.
h.name: Heap

h.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.
h.name: Heard

h.description: Hearst is a privately held, diversified American media, information, and services conglomerate headquartered in the Hearst Tower in New York City. Founded in 1887 by William Randolph Hearst, the company spans more than 360 businesses across magazines, newspapers, broadcast television, cable networks, business and financial information, healthcare information, automotive data, and venture investments. Hearst reported approximately US$13B in revenue (2024) with ~22,000 employees worldwide.
h.name: Hearst

h.description: Heart Aerospace is a hybrid-electric aircraft manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Torrance / Los Angeles, California, working to decarbonize and lower the cost of regional air travel. The company is developing the X1, a full-scale hybrid-electric technology demonstrator, and the ES-30, a 30-seat regional production aircraft, backed by strategic airline partners including United Airlines and Air Canada and investors such as Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, EQT Ventures, and Y Combinator. Heart Aerospace publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network entry in the sustainable-transport sector.
h.name: Heart Aerospace

h.description: Heartbeat Health is a New York-based modern cardiology practice delivering remote and virtual cardiovascular care. The company combines early detection, home-based cardiac diagnostics, remote patient monitoring, risk stratification and evidence-based care coordination to proactively identify, treat and manage moderate-to-high cardiovascular risk. It serves hospitals and health systems, payors and employer groups, providers and ACOs, and in-home care providers, reporting outcomes such as 90%+ of patients reaching target blood pressure and a 53% reduction in cardiac readmissions. Backed by Optum Ventures, DaVita Venture Group and Echo Health Ventures, it is a care-delivery organization rather than a public API provider; no developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface was found during enrichment.
h.name: Heartbeat Health

h.description: Heartbeat Medical is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of hv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Heartbeat Medical

h.description: Heartflow, Inc. (Nasdaq: HTFL) is a healthcare technology company founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its Heartflow One platform applies AI to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) to non-invasively diagnose and manage coronary artery disease, bundling Roadmap Analysis, FFRct Analysis, Plaque Analysis, Plaque Staging and the PCI Navigator, and delivering results back into hospital PACS and EMR systems. More than 650,000 patients have been analyzed across 1,800+ institutions. Heartflow runs a production REST API at api.heartflow.net and customer documentation at docs.heartflow.net, but both are authenticated: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and no self-serve signup.
h.name: HeartFlow

h.description: Hearth is a business-management platform for residential home-improvement contractors and trades professionals. It bundles customer financing (a marketplace of 18+ lenders with $0 dealer fees), quotes and estimates, digital contracts and e-signature, invoicing and payments, client management, and scheduling, together with Harper, a 24/7 AI receptionist that answers calls, handles follow-ups, and creates social content. Hearth serves 16+ residential contracting verticals including roofing, HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, fencing, and flooring, and is backed by 8vc.
h.name: Hearth

h.description: Hearthstone Cards Information
h.name: Hearthstone

h.description: Heartland Express is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Heartland Express API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.
h.name: Heartland Express

h.description: Heartland Financial USA, Inc. (HTLF) was a Denver, Colorado bank holding company — formerly headquartered in Dubuque, Iowa — that operated a multi-charter family of community banks across twelve states, including Dubuque Bank and Trust, Illinois Bank & Trust, Wisconsin Bank & Trust, New Mexico Bank & Trust, Arizona Bank & Trust, Rocky Mountain Bank, Citywide Banks, Minnesota Bank & Trust, Premier Valley Bank, First Bank & Trust, Bank of Blue Valley and Signature Bank of Arkansas. Its business was commercial and retail banking, treasury management, and wealth services delivered through branches and third-party core banking platforms rather than through a developer program. HTLF never published a developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind. UMB Financial Corporation completed its all-stock acquisition of HTLF on January 31, 2025 — the largest in UMB's history — and completed the systems and brand conversion of every former HTLF divisional bank in October 2025, at which point the HTLF brand ceased to exist. The htlf.com edge configuration has since been decommissioned. This profile is retained as a historical record; any banking API surface for these institutions now lives with UMB and is tracked separately under the UMB Bank profile.
h.name: Heartland Financial USA

h.description: Heartland Payment Systems is a payment processing company offering payroll, customer engagement, point-of-sale, and other business solutions to merchants across the United States. Heartland is now a brand of Global Payments, and developer resources for Heartland integrations are published through the Global Payments developer portal. The platform supports online and in-person payments, bill pay, IoT/connected device payments, gift and loyalty, payroll, and PCI-validated point-to-point encryption.
h.name: Heartland Payment Systems

h.description: Heartport is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Heartport

h.description: Heartstream is an emergency-care and defibrillation brand, now part of Philips, that makes automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and professional monitor/defibrillators for public-access, home, and EMS use. The company originated as a Mayfield-backed medical-device startup that pioneered automatic external defibrillators and was later acquired by Hewlett-Packard; today the Heartstream name lives on across the HeartStart AED and Tempus ALS product lines sold in more than 50 countries and regions. Its public site publishes product support, a document center (instructions for use), and a newsroom, but it exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.
h.name: Heartstream

h.description: HeartThis was a mobile fashion shopping and discovery app, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and GV and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company appears defunct/absorbed: heartthis.com and www.heartthis.com now return a 301 redirect to an OpenSky content page (www.opensky.com/content/general/heartthis), the host serves a long-expired stale wildcard TLS certificate (CN wildcard auctivacommerce.com, expired 2022-12-16), and no api, developer, or docs subdomains resolve (NXDOMAIN). No public developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be found, so no API artifacts could be enriched without fabrication.
h.name: HeartThis

h.description: Heartwork is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of cowboy-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: unknown. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: Heartwork

h.description: HeartyyFresh is a mobile-first Indian grocery delivery service that lets customers order fresh Indian groceries and household staples for home delivery through its iOS and Android apps. The consumer offering centers on convenience and quality, promoting a first-time incentive of 20% off the first five orders placed through the app. HeartyyFresh operates as a direct-to-consumer grocery app (published under the com.rahein.heartyyfresh Android package and the "HeartyyFresh - Indian Grocery" iOS listing) rather than a developer platform; it exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched for identity only.
h.name: HeartyyFresh

h.description: HEAT is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
h.name: HEAT

h.description: Heathrow Airport Limited operates London Heathrow (IATA LHR, ICAO EGLL), the United Kingdom's principal international hub and Europe's busiest airport by passenger numbers, under the ultimate ownership of FGP Topco Limited - whose largest shareholder since December 2024 is Ardian, alongside Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and a residual Ferrovial holding. In the travel distribution chain Heathrow is infrastructure, not an intermediary - it sells no seats, holds no bookable inventory, issues no PNRs or e-tickets, and sits entirely outside the GDS and IATA NDC value chain, earning aeronautical charges, retail concessions, car parking and property income instead. Its API posture is unusual for an airport - Heathrow does run a real, branded, publicly reachable developer portal at developer.heathrow.com, built on Microsoft Azure API Management, which publicly describes three products in prose - Flights, Flight Connections and Weather - but publishes no OpenAPI, no endpoint reference, no rate limits, no pricing and no SLA to anonymous visitors. The API catalogue and Products list return empty to unauthenticated callers, sign-in is via Azure Active Directory, and the portal's own How It Works page requires a prospective developer to email support@heathrow.com and be enrolled before any access is granted. The gateway at api.heathrow.com goes further and rejects requests with "400 No required SSL certificate was sent", meaning mutual TLS with a Heathrow-issued client certificate. So - public docs, gated contracts, no exit path beyond a UK GDPR data portability request to privacy@heathrow.com.
h.name: Heathrow Airport

h.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.
h.name: Heaviside Industries

h.description: HEAVY.AI is a GPU-accelerated analytics platform (formerly OmniSci / MapD, now part of NVIDIA) built to interactively query and visualize very large, often geospatial and time-series, datasets. It pairs an open-source, GPU-accelerated SQL database (HeavyDB) with a server-side rendering engine (HeavyRender) and a web-based visual analytics application (Heavy Immerse). Developers interact with the platform through native SQL, an Apache Thrift API, JDBC/ODBC drivers, the heavysql command-line console, a Python data-science client (heavyai) and a JavaScript connector (@heavyai/connector), plus a Vega-based rendering API. The documentation is published on the NVIDIA docs site and exposes an llms.txt index and a hosted MCP server for AI agents.
h.name: HEAVY.AI

h.description: HeavyConnect is a digital documentation and compliance platform purpose-built for agricultural operations, serving growers, harvesters, shippers, and processors. Its mobile-first, offline-capable modules cover food safety compliance, worker training and certification, time and productivity tracking, quality assurance inspections, end-to-end traceability, and supplier management. The platform replaces paper-based recordkeeping with audit-ready digital documentation and real-time analytics dashboards, helping food and agriculture operations stay inspection-ready. HeavyConnect reports 2,600+ active users across operations including Sysco, Naturipe, Talley, and Empire. It is offered as a month-to-month subscription with a request-a-demo onboarding path. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (500 Global, Techstars) and enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.
h.name: HeavyConnect

h.description: Hebbia provides institutional-grade AI for finance and high-stakes enterprise work, centered on its Matrix product that reasons across massive volumes of unstructured documents. The platform connects to enterprise data sources such as Snowflake, AWS S3, SharePoint, Box, Dropbox, and Egnyte, and financial data providers including FactSet, S&P Capital IQ, PitchBook, Guidepoint, and Thirdbridge. Hebbia is a sales-led enterprise product without a fully public developer portal; API and integration access is granted to customers through their account team.
h.name: Hebbia

h.description: Convert between Gregorian and Hebrew, fetch Shabbat and Holiday times, etc
h.name: Hebrew Calendar

h.description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem (HUJI, האוניברסיטה העברית בירושלים) is Israel's leading research university, founded in 1918 and operating campuses in Jerusalem, Rehovot and Eilat across the humanities, sciences, medicine, agriculture and law. It publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no API keys and no terms of use for machine access — api.huji.ac.il, developer.huji.ac.il and data.huji.ac.il do not resolve at all. What it does operate, on its own infrastructure and without anyone advertising it, are two genuinely institution-run programmable surfaces. The first is the JSON API behind Shnaton, the official course catalog at shnaton.huji.ac.il: fully public, entirely unauthenticated, bilingual Hebrew/English, covering faculties, degree programs, specializations, courses, timetabled study sessions and syllabi for academic years 2020 through 2027, with a single unauthenticated search call returning the whole 6,355-course catalog in one 14 MB response. The second is the university's own SAML 2.0 identity provider at idp.cc.huji.ac.il, which publishes live machine-readable metadata signed with a certificate the institution issued to itself. Both were confirmed institution-operated by IP ownership rather than hostname — they resolve inside the 128.139.0.0/16 ILAN allocation registered to IUCC and announced by AS378, behind the university's own load balancers. Beyond those two, the footprint is tenancy: the research portal at cris.huji.ac.il is Elsevier Pure (a CNAME to huji.elsevierpure.com) and its working OAI-PMH endpoint is Pure's engineering, and library discovery runs on Ex Libris Primo under institution code 972HUJI_INST. Those relationships are recorded here; their vendors' contracts deliberately are not.
h.name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem

h.description: Hedera is an enterprise-grade public distributed ledger platform built for the digital economy and governed by a council of leading global institutions. The Hedera Mirror Node REST API provides read-only access to historical network data including transactions, accounts, tokens, NFTs, smart contracts, consensus topics, blocks, schedules, and network-level information. The public API requires no authentication and supports mainnet, testnet, and previewnet environments.
h.name: Hedera

h.description: Hedge is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol built on the Solana blockchain that lets users mint USH, a stablecoin soft-pegged to the US dollar. Users deposit collateral into vaults to take out 0% interest loans for a one-time fee, maintaining a collateral-to-debt ratio above 110% to avoid liquidation. A stability pool absorbs liquidations and rewards depositors with discounted collateral, while a Peg Stability Module and a multi-source oracle (Pyth Network primary, Switchboard fallback) keep USH near its peg. Hedge is an on-chain protocol rather than a hosted REST API; its documentation, whitepaper, and audited Solana program are its public surface.
