k.description: The Kemper family of companies is one of the nation's leading insurers. With approximately $13 billion in assets, Kemper is improving the world of insurance by offering personalized solutions for individuals, families and businesses.
k.name: Kemper

k.description: Kenbi is a German healthcare organization focused on nursing education and workforce development, operating through two divisions. Kenbi Academy delivers continuing professional development for care workers with 100+ ZFU-certified courses recognized by all German health insurers and available nationwide, spanning nursing service management, quality assurance, wound care, and instructor training. Kenbi Campus runs vocational nursing programs in Berlin and Hamburg, including a three-year registered nurse generalist program and an 18-month nursing assistant curriculum. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found.
k.name: Kenbi

k.description: Kencko is a direct-to-consumer functional-food company that makes no-fuss instant smoothies and other whole-food products from 100% organic, vegan, freeze-dried fruits and vegetables with no added sugars. Customers subscribe and shop through a Shopify-hosted online store at kencko.com. Kencko is a Techstars-backed portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for the enrichment pipeline. It publishes no first-party developer API; the only machine-readable discovery surface on its domain is the Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth well-known configuration that backs storefront customer login.
k.name: Kencko Foods

k.description: Kendra Scott is an American jewelry and accessories retailer founded in 2002 in Austin, Texas, offering personalized jewelry, watches, home goods, and gifts through customization options such as initials, birthstones, and engraving. The brand operates a direct-to-consumer ecommerce storefront alongside a network of retail stores, and pairs its Color Bar customization experience with a philanthropic giving model tied to purchases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a consumer ecommerce site but no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile captures its public identity and web-property surface pending any future developer program.
k.name: Kendra Scott

k.description: Kenjo is an all-in-one human resources (HRIS) software platform for small and mid-sized companies, with a strong focus on deskless and shift-based teams. It covers the full employee lifecycle - employee database, attendance and time tracking, absence and time-off management, document management, payroll and compensation, shift planning, performance reviews, and recruiting. Kenjo exposes a documented REST API (base https://api.kenjo.io/api/v1, sandbox https://sandbox-api.kenjo.io/api/v1) that lets customers read and write employees, attendances, time-off requests, company documents, compensation, org structure, and recruiting data. API access is gated - it is available on Kenjo's top-tier Connect plan and must be activated by the Kenjo Customer Success team, then keys are generated in Settings > Integrations > API and exchanged for a bearer token.
k.name: Kenjo

k.description: Kenna Security is the risk-based vulnerability management platform now part of Cisco as Cisco Vulnerability Management. Founded in Chicago and acquired by Cisco in 2021, the platform ingests scanner, asset, and threat-intelligence data to prioritize vulnerabilities by real-world exploitability and business risk. It exposes a REST API (the Kenna / Cisco Vulnerability Management API) at api.kennasecurity.com covering assets, asset groups, applications, findings, fixes, vulnerabilities, vulnerability intelligence, connectors, data exports, dashboards, metrics, roles, and users. The API uses an X-Risk-Token API-key header over HTTPS, page-number pagination, and JSON payloads. Kenna also publishes a first-party open-source Scripting Toolkit on GitHub for building connectors and integrations. Sector: cybersecurity / vulnerability management.
k.name: Kenna Security

k.description: Kennametal is a leading provider of productivity solutions for metalworking, earth cutting, and wear components, coatings, and powders. Kennametal offers online integration services including Punch-Out / OCI (Open Catalog Interface), EDI, and a Product Data Portal for catalog and product information.
k.name: Kennametal

k.description: Kennek (Kennek Solutions Ltd) is a UK-based fintech providing all-in-one loan management software built for specialist bridge and development lenders. The platform lets lenders originate, manage, and service loans while monitoring funding lines in one place, automating manual workflows, covenant and eligibility calculations, portfolio risk visibility, and investor reporting so lending teams can scale without adding headcount. Founded by former lenders and backed by HV Capital, Kennek is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio-company profile; it publishes a marketing site and legal pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.
k.name: Kennek

k.description: Keno is an on-demand, doorstep car-wash and vehicle-care mobile application operating in the United Arab Emirates, billing itself as the "No.1 car wash app in the UAE". Customers download the iOS or Android app, add their vehicle, select from wash, maintenance, and detailing services (priced by vehicle class from bike to luxury SUV), and a mobile team of "ninjas" arrives at the customer's location to perform the work with a choice of payment methods. Keno is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.
k.name: Keno

k.description: Kensho Technologies is the AI innovation hub of S&P Global, building machine learning and AI systems that structure, connect, and extract meaning from the world's financial and business data. Kensho's developer platform exposes a suite of production APIs: Scribe for speech-to-text transcription of audio and video, Extract for turning PDF documents into structured JSON, NERD for named-entity recognition and disambiguation against Wikimedia and S&P Capital IQ knowledge bases, and the LLM-ready API (kfinance) that connects LLMs, agents, and AI applications to S&P Global's trusted data through Adaptive Retrieval and a hosted, OAuth-secured Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Authentication is bearer-token based, issued from Kensho's services platform via personal tokens or production key pairs, with OAuth 2.0 (authorization code, client credentials, and refresh token flows, PKCE, and dynamic client registration) for the MCP surface.
k.name: Kensho

k.description: Kentico is an enterprise .NET CMS and digital experience platform offering REST and GraphQL APIs for managing web content, e-commerce, digital marketing, and personalization. Xperience by Kentico provides headless channel GraphQL endpoints auto-generated per channel, a content item .NET API, file storage APIs supporting Azure Blob and Amazon S3, and a management REST service for CRUD operations on CMS objects. The platform supports ASP.NET Core with channel-based licensing covering website, email, and headless channels.
k.name: Kentico

k.description: Kentik is a network observability company whose SaaS platform (the Kentik Portal) unifies network flow records, BGP routing, SNMP and streaming telemetry, synthetic tests, and cloud VPC/flow logs into one analytics engine for network performance monitoring, capacity planning, DDoS detection and mitigation, cloud and container visibility, service-provider peering and OTT analytics, and AI-driven network intelligence. The Kentik V6 API is a gRPC-first platform with REST/JSON transcoding that exposes dozens of services — devices, sites, labels, users, alert policies, mitigations, synthetics, cloud export, notification channels, capacity plans, and an AI Advisor MCP server — authenticated with X-CH-Auth-Email plus X-CH-Auth-API-Token headers.
k.name: Kentik

k.description: Kenvue is the world's largest pure-play consumer health company by revenue, formed from the consumer health spin-off of Johnson & Johnson. Everyday care is a powerful catalyst in making you feel better, inside and out. Kenvue's iconic brands include Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, Aveeno, Band-Aid, and Johnson's.
k.name: Kenvue

k.description: Kenz is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Kenz

k.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.
k.name: Kepler Communications

k.description: Open-source, AI-native testing platform that captures real production API traffic with eBPF and replays it in CI as deterministic tests, auto-generated mocks, and production-like sandboxes with zero code changes. Publishes a first-party OpenAPI 3.0.3 for its Cloud REST API, a hosted MCP server with a 112-tool catalog, llms.txt, and a Kubernetes Proxy REST API for in-cluster recording and replay.
k.name: Keploy

k.description: Kerberos is a computer-network authentication protocol that works on the basis of tickets to allow nodes communicating over a non-secure network to prove their identity to one another in a secure manner. It is widely used in enterprise environments for single sign-on authentication.
k.name: Kerberos

k.description: Kernel is browser infrastructure for AI agents and automations. It runs sandboxed cloud Chromium browsers that spin up in under 30ms, with Playwright execution, computer-use controls, managed authentication into third-party sites, reusable browser profiles, proxies, pre-warmed browser pools, session replays, live telemetry, and a serverless App platform for deploying and invoking agent actions. Kernel exposes a REST API (OpenAPI 3.1, 135 operations across 22 tags), first-party TypeScript, Python and Go SDKs, a CLI, and a centrally hosted MCP server so agents can drive real browsers. Backed by General Catalyst.
k.name: Kernel

k.description: Kerning Cultures is a Middle East and North Africa media company producing narrative journalism and audio storytelling podcasts in Arabic and English. Based in Dubai, UAE and backed by 500 Global, the Kerning Cultures Network creates original shows, branded audio, and advertising for a regional listener audience. It operates as a consumer media and content brand and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future API surface.
k.name: Kerning Cultures

k.description: Kerros Health (Kerros) was a digital mental-health and wellness startup building clinically validated, mobile-based programs proven to improve mental health, positioned as an evidence-based consumer brand modernizing established treatments through mobile technology and design. The product began as a teen-created mental-health app (originating out of Scarsdale High School) and grew largely through word of mouth. Co-founded by Justin Ip and backed by Cowboy Ventures at the seed stage, the company has since exited. It was a consumer mobile app with no public developer/API surface; this API Evangelist profile is maintained as a portfolio-lead record and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation could be found during enrichment.
k.name: Kerros Health

k.description: Kerys Software is a European (Palaiseau, France) cybersecurity company behind YS::Desktop, a Type 1 hypervisor that runs multiple fully isolated environments on a single workstation. By preallocating dedicated CPU cores to the hypervisor versus VM workloads and adding hypervisor-level encryption, YS::Desktop closes VM escape and cross-VM attack vectors while sustaining roughly 92% native performance. It replaces dedicated admin machines, air-gapped OT laptops, and traditional VDI for regulated organizations in aerospace and defense, energy, finance, construction, and the public sector, with a mandatory Security Domain model (no unmanaged VMs) administered through the YAC console. The company positions around NIS2, IEC 62443, and ANSSI multi-environment workstation guidance and sells 100% through resellers. Kerys does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or pricing; it was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched here from its public site.
k.name: Kerys

k.description: Kespry was an industrial drone and aerial-intelligence company founded in the San Francisco Bay Area that paired automated fixed-perimeter drones with a cloud analytics platform to turn aerial imagery into measurable data. Its product was used for stockpile and inventory volumetrics in mining and aggregates, construction-site progress monitoring and earthworks, and insurance roof inspection. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Kespry was acquired by Firmatek in 2020 and the brand has since been retired; the former developer and marketing domain kespry.com now issues a 301 redirect to firmatek.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio mapping, but Kespry publishes no live, standalone developer surface, API, documentation, or client SDKs of its own.
k.name: Kespry

k.description: Kestra is a declarative workflow orchestration platform where pipelines are defined in YAML, combining visual and code-first approaches.
k.name: Kestra

k.description: Kestrel AI is a YC-backed startup building an AI-native cloud incident response platform. Founded by former Illumio Kubernetes Security engineers, Kestrel uses autonomous AI agents to detect, investigate, and remediate infrastructure incidents across Kubernetes and cloud environments. The platform provides continuous monitoring, root cause analysis, and automated remediation through GitOps workflows, integrating with Slack, PagerDuty, GitHub, GitLab, AWS, and major observability platforms.
k.name: Kestrel

k.description: Kestrl is a UK-based, FCA-regulated ethical fintech offering a values-aligned money app for Muslim and ethically-minded consumers. In partnership with Maybank Islamic, it provides interest-free (Sharia-compliant) banking, a Mastercard debit card with values filtering, goal-based sub-accounts, interest purification and Zakat calculation, transaction monitoring that alerts users to payments toward ethically questionable companies, and security features such as card freezing and biometric authentication. Kestrl is a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.
k.name: Kestrl: Muslim Money App

k.description: Ketch is a data permissioning and consent platform that helps enterprises keep customer data clean, permissioned, and AI-ready across web, mobile, and backend systems. Its products span consent management, data subject rights automation, AI-powered data mapping, marketing preference management, risk and reporting, a Data Sentry privacy pentest, and an AI governance layer. The Ketch Agent Network turns privacy program insights into agent-driven actions. Builders use a public REST API hosted at global.ketchapi.com, web and mobile SDKs published on GitHub, and Google Tag Manager templates to enforce consent at the source. Ketch advertises more than 1,000 pre-built API integrations with systems, apps, and AI models, with a free tier alongside enterprise and mid-market editions.
k.name: Ketch

k.description: Ketera is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Ketera

k.description: Ketryx is an AI-native application lifecycle management (ALM) and compliance platform for regulated medical-device and life-sciences software teams. It integrates with developer tools such as Jira and GitHub to automate the documentation, traceability, and quality-management work required by FDA, EU MDR, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, and IEC 62304, keeping teams continuously audit-ready. Capabilities include automated Design and Development File generation, requirement-risk-code-test traceability, agentic AI for repetitive compliance tasks, ISO 14971 risk management, software bill-of-materials (SBOM) and vulnerability tracking, QMS enforcement, and change-impact assessment. Ketryx exposes a public Build API that lets CI/CD pipelines report builds, JUnit / Cucumber test results, build artifacts, and CycloneDX / SPDX SBOM documents into a project, via a first-party GitHub Action and Python utility. The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.
k.name: Ketryx

k.description: KETS Quantum Security is a Bristol, UK deep-tech company (incorporated 2016) building chip-based quantum-safe encryption and networking hardware. Its product line spans Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG), and the KETS KORE sub-system, delivering security grounded in the laws of physics rather than computational complexity. KETS technology hardens telecommunications networks, satellite and aerospace communications (including Airbus collaborations), data-center backups, and critical infrastructure control systems against the emerging threat of quantum computing. Backed by European quantum-specialist venture investors including Speedinvest and supported by multiple UK government funding awards, KETS is a hardware and photonics company; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security signals.
k.name: Kets

k.description: Kettle is a reinsurance company that uses machine learning to model climate risk, according to the venture portfolio listings of its investors. Its focus is climate and catastrophe risk modeling applied to reinsurance underwriting. Kettle is backed by Anthemis, DCVC, Homebrew and True Ventures, and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for this provider yet; this profile remains a stub awaiting a successful enrichment run with network access.
k.name: Kettle

k.description: Dr Pepper Snapple Group was an integrated brand owner, manufacturer, and distributor of nonalcoholic beverages in the United States, Canada, Mexico, and the Caribbean. In 2018 the company merged with Keurig Green Mountain to form Keurig Dr Pepper, a leading beverage company in North America with a portfolio of more than 150 brands including Dr Pepper, 7UP, Snapple, Canada Dry, Keurig, and Peet's Coffee.
k.name: Keurig Dr Pepper (formerly Dr Pepper Snapple Group)

k.description: Keurig Green Mountain was a leader in specialty coffee and coffee makers, producing the Keurig single-serve brewing system and partnering with leading coffee brands. In 2018 Keurig Green Mountain merged with Dr Pepper Snapple Group to form Keurig Dr Pepper, a Fortune 500 beverage company. This repository preserves the historical API and developer footprint of Keurig Green Mountain prior to that merger.
k.name: Keurig Green Mountain

k.description: Kev is an open-source (Apache-2.0) family of small decision models built on Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 by Jared Palmer, released on GitHub and Hugging Face. Its self-hosted server exposes an HTTP API that, per the README, "matches TypeSafe's System One" (POST /v1/systemone with noul, choice and score questions). Not a Cognition product. No OpenAPI or JSON Schema file is published in the repository.
k.name: Kev

k.description: Kevala Inc. is a San Francisco based grid intelligence company, founded in 2014, that builds a cloud-based electric-grid data and analytics platform for utilities, regulators and government agencies, renewable energy developers, and transportation electrification planners. The platform merges address-specific geospatial data, utility network models and hyper-granular time-series data into map-based analytics for integrated grid planning, distributed energy resource (DER) adoption forecasting, project siting, power flow analysis, locational carbon accounting, production cost modeling, and predictive interconnection siting metrics, with exports compatible with CYME, Synergi, PSS/E and OpenDSS. Kevala licenses its data and analysis by subscription and operates an authenticated platform API at api.kevala.com; the DER metering surface publishes an OpenAPI document and a ReDoc reference, but both require platform credentials and no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is served anonymously.
k.name: Kevala

k.description: Kevel is an API-first ad serving platform that lets brands and publishers build unified, fully customized ad systems supporting any ad format, any creative, and multiple demand sources. Kevel exposes a Decision API for ad requests, a Management API for campaign and creative operations, a Reporting API for performance analytics, and a UserDB API for first-party audience and user data.
k.name: Kevel

k.description: kevin. was a Lithuanian account-to-account (A2A) payments infrastructure company providing PSD2 open-banking Payment Initiation and Account Information services to merchants across 28 European countries. Its platform API let businesses initiate bank (SEPA) and card (hybrid) payments, issue refunds, read account data, and receive signed payment webhooks through a single integration to hundreds of banks, supported by an official Node.js SDK, a CLI, and a React UI component library. Backed by Accel. The company has wound down its public web presence - kevin.eu no longer resolves as of 2026-07 - and this profile is enriched from kevin.'s published npm packages and archived developer reference.
k.name: Kevin.

k.description: Key AI is a professional networking platform that rebuilds business connection-making around AI and consent-based introductions. Its Kai AI agent surfaces the right people through warm paths in your existing network, while Handshake handles consent-first introductions (launching summer 2026). The platform also offers matched Opportunities (jobs, deals, and partnerships), branded Communities and directories for alumni groups and associations, event and calendar pre-matching, a searchable knowledge Library, and Connectors for Slack, WhatsApp, and LinkedIn. Founded by Google alumni behind the 35,000-member Xoogler community and backed by Felicis, Key AI is an end-user and community-operator product; as of July 2026 it publishes no public API, developer platform, or API documentation.
k.name: Key

k.description: Keybase is an end-to-end encrypted messaging, file-sharing, and key-directory platform built on public-key cryptography, founded by Chris Coyne and Max Krohn and acquired by Zoom in 2020. It maps human-readable usernames to public keys and cryptographically verifiable social-identity proofs (Twitter, GitHub, Reddit, Hacker News, personal domains, and cryptocurrency addresses), and provides encrypted chat, teams, KBFS encrypted filesystem, git, and a wallet. Keybase exposes a public read-oriented HTTP JSON API (version 1.0) at keybase.io/_/api/1.0 for user lookup, PGP key fetch, Merkle-tree verification, and session/signature auth, plus officially supported chat-bot SDKs for Node.js, Python, and Go that script the local keybase client and CLI.
k.name: Keybase

k.description: Keyboardio is a hardware company that designs and sells premium ergonomic mechanical keyboards, including the sculpted hardwood Model 100, the ultra- portable Atreus, and the upcoming Preonic. Its keyboards run fully open-source, reprogrammable firmware (Kaleidoscope) configured through the cross-platform Chrysalis GUI, both developed in the open on GitHub. Keyboardio sells direct through a Shopify storefront at shop.keyboard.io; customer login and account management use Shopify Customer Accounts (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0) bound to the keyboard.io domain. Keyboardio has no first-party public HTTP API — this profile captures the real developer, open-source, and identity surfaces the company publishes.
k.name: Keyboardio

k.description: KeyCare is a telehealth platform that connects health systems to a national network of independent, virtual-first care providers through deep Epic EHR integration. Built on Epic using CareEverywhere, MyChart, Telehealth Anywhere, and Book Anywhere workflows, KeyCare lets member health systems extend their own Epic instance to on-demand urgent care (24/7/365 across all 50 states), behavioral health, neurology, primary care, and expanding specialties such as rheumatology, cardiology, and maternal care. The company serves health systems including Allina Health, Memorial Healthcare, Ochsner Health, WellSpan, and Confluence Health. KeyCare is backed by 8VC. This profile has no public API or developer surface at the time of enrichment.
k.name: KeyCare

k.description: Get the IP geolocation data through the simple REST API. All the responses are JSON encoded
k.name: keycdn IP Location Finder

k.description: Keychain is an AI-powered operating system and network for the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry, connecting brands and retailers with the contract manufacturers, co-packers, and suppliers that make their products. The platform lets CPG brands discover and match with vetted manufacturing partners, manage sourcing and production relationships, and streamline the supplier-discovery workflow that has traditionally been manual and relationship-driven. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Keychain was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from the a16z venture portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Keychain publishes a marketing and product web presence at keychain.com but does not expose a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API discovery surface (no developer/API subdomain, no /.well-known catalog, no llms.txt).
k.name: Keychain

k.description: Keycloak is an open source identity and access management solution for modern applications and services, providing single sign-on, identity brokering, user federation, and fine-grained authorization using OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.
k.name: Keycloak

k.description: KeyCorp (KeyBank) is one of the nation's largest bank-based financial services companies and a super-regional commercial bank headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, providing deposit, lending, cash management, treasury, and investment services to individuals, small businesses, and middle-market companies. The KeyBank Developer Portal at developer.key.com publishes a self-service catalog of commercial and embedded-banking APIs covering account information reporting, ACH origination, RTP and wire payments, account validation, ACH/wire/RTP inquiry, check services, and payment event webhooks. Each product ships a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1 definition and is secured with OAuth2 bearer tokens, mutual TLS client certificates, and FAPI-style interaction-id headers.
k.name: KeyCorp

k.description: Keyfactor is a machine-identity and PKI (public key infrastructure) company that provides a control plane for digital trust — helping organizations discover, issue, automate, and govern cryptographic keys and certificates across enterprise, cloud, DevOps, and IoT environments. Its core products are Keyfactor Command (certificate lifecycle automation at scale), EJBCA Enterprise (modern, quantum-ready PKI and certificate authority), SignServer / Signum (code signing and verification), Cloud PKI-as-a-Service, and cryptographic discovery and inventory. Keyfactor Command and EJBCA expose REST APIs (self-hosted or cloud, per customer) with official Go, .NET, and CLI clients, and an experimental MCP server for agentic-AI integration. Keyfactor is trusted by roughly 40% of the Fortune 500 and is backed by Insight Partners.
k.name: Keyfactor

k.description: Keyfile is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Keyfile

k.description: Keyframe Labs builds real-time foundation models that turn AI voice and text agents into lifelike, emotionally expressive video calls. Its Persona-1.5-Live product lets developers add photoreal AI avatars ("personas") to their agents and applications with a few lines of embed code, at roughly 500ms latency and from $0.06 per minute. The platform exposes a REST Sessions API (create a live session, manage meeting bots for Zoom/Meet/Teams, and list voices and LLM models), JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, and embeddable UI elements, with hosted and self-managed integration paths that plug into agent frameworks such as LiveKit Agents, ElevenLabs Agents, and OpenAI Realtime. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), Keyframe Labs is based in San Francisco.
k.name: Keyframe Labs

k.description: Keygen is a software licensing, entitlements, and distribution API for desktop, on-prem, IoT, and other installed applications. It issues license keys, activates and tracks machines, enforces policy-based entitlements, and distributes releases and artifacts for auto-updates. Keygen ships as the source-available, self-hostable Keygen CE / EE and as the managed Keygen Cloud, exposing a JSON:API interface under api.keygen.sh.
k.name: Keygen

k.description: KeyMe is a nationwide locksmith and key-duplication company that pairs mobile locksmith technicians with a network of self-service key-copying kiosks located inside thousands of retail stores across the United States. Customers can copy residential, commercial, and automotive keys, RFID fobs and access cards at a kiosk, order duplicates online, or request 24/7 mobile locksmith help for home, auto, and business lockouts, transponder and ignition key programming, lock installation, re-keying, and access-control and master-key systems. KeyMe is backed by Battery Ventures. As of this profile the company operates as a consumer-facing locksmith and kiosk service and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network.
k.name: KeyMe

k.description: KeyNexus was an enterprise encryption key management company based in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, providing centralized key management, Bring Your Own Key (BYOK), and Key Management as a Service for cloud, on-premises, and hybrid deployments. Its platform helped enterprises generate, store, distribute, and control the lifecycle of encryption keys used to protect data across applications and infrastructure. KeyNexus was acquired by StorMagic in January 2021, and its technology was folded into the StorMagic SvKMS (Secure Virtual Key Management Service) product; the keynexus.com domain now redirects to StorMagic's encryption key management offering. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking. KeyNexus no longer operates as an independent developer platform.
k.name: Keynexus

k.description: Keynua is a Latin American digital identity and electronic signature platform that lets businesses design signing flows combining video, drawn, OTP, and digital signatures with biometric identity verification — liveness detection, facial matching, 3D and selfie identification, and geopositioning. Its REST API covers contracts, document templates, identity verification, OTP, and Deceval promissory notes, delivering requests to signers over WhatsApp, SMS, or email and emitting webhooks for asynchronous processing events. It supports 20+ Latin American identity documents across 20 countries and serves financial services, real estate, human resources, commercial contracts, and sports betting.
k.name: Keynua

k.description: Keyo is a palm-based biometric identification platform offering a complete suite of touchless identity SaaS for payments, access control, ticketing, and time & attendance. Its palm-print and palm-vein (near-infrared) technology lets people verify their identity with a wave of the hand. Keyo exposes a REST API (developers.keyo.co) for managing biometric Identities and driving palm enrollment on Keyo devices, secured with the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow, plus real-time webhooks for enrollment and identification events. Keyo is backed by 500 Global and Obvious Ventures.
k.name: Keyo

k.description: keyper is an Austrian technology company providing connected ticketing and digital access solutions. Its developer platform lets ticketing systems, resellers and access control systems (ACS) deliver e-tickets and exchange access data through the keyper Access API, Connect Provider / Reseller APIs, Ticket Delivery API, native Android and iOS SDKs, and embeddable web components (seatmaps and checkout). The Access API sends entry transactions for keys (ticket barcodes) and their permissions (events), and returns the Grant / Block permission whitelist an access control system enforces at the gate. keyper serves sports, arts and culture organisations across Austria and Central Europe and is backed by Speedinvest.
k.name: Keyper

k.description: Keyrock is a digital asset market maker and liquidity provider founded in Brussels in 2017 and now operating as a global crypto investment group. It runs in-house algorithmic and high-frequency trading infrastructure to supply market making, over-the-counter (OTC) trading, an options desk, onchain/DEX liquidity, validator services, ecosystem development and a Smart Beta fund to token issuers, exchanges, brokerages and institutional counterparties across 85+ centralised and decentralised venues. Keyrock also publishes proprietary crypto, FX, commodity and US equity pricing into the Pyth Network oracle. Its commercial surface is bilateral rather than self-serve: engagements are contracted, and clients receive execution analytics and PnL attribution through a credentialed dashboard. As of this profiling round Keyrock publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract of any kind. The group holds a MiCA licence through its French entity Keyrock FR SAS and has publicly announced SOC 2 Type II compliance.
k.name: Keyrock

k.description: KeyRunner is a local-first API platform combining a desktop API client, request monitor, mock server, and secret manager. It is delivered as desktop applications (Windows, macOS Intel, macOS Apple Silicon), a VS Code extension, and a CLI, with all requests and secrets kept inside the developer environment.
k.name: KeyRunner

k.description: Keys is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Keys

k.description: Profile for Keysight Technologies in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 617).
k.name: Keysight Technologies

k.description: keysino is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: keysino

k.description: Keystatic is an open source, Git-based content management system that stores content as Markdown, JSON, and YAML directly in a project's Git repository. The Keystatic Reader API is a Node.js library that lets applications read Keystatic content from any local directory or GitHub repository server-side, supporting frameworks like Next.js, Astro, Remix, and React Server Components.
k.name: Keystatic

k.description: KeystoneJS is an open-source headless CMS and GraphQL API platform for Node.js. It auto-generates a powerful GraphQL API and a beautiful management UI from schema definitions, enabling developers to manage content and user data without boilerplate. Built on TypeScript with Prisma for database migrations, it supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite and includes access control, session management, hooks, and rich document editing out of the box.
k.name: KeystoneJS

k.description: Keywords AI is an LLM observability and gateway platform. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible proxy (chat completions across 250+ models) plus REST APIs for request logging, prompt management, threads, evaluations, and traces - all under a single Bearer-authenticated API at https://api.keywordsai.co/api. (The company is rebranding to Respan; the keywordsai.co host and API remain active.)
k.name: Keywords AI

k.description: Kezaihui (再惠 / Zaihuihui (Shanghai) Network Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based Chinese SaaS platform for local-life-service commerce, providing offline merchants — primarily mid-tier restaurants plus entertainment, beauty, and hospitality businesses — with one-stop store-opening and digital-operations tooling. Founded around 2012, the company offers private-domain member and community management, trading-platform shop diagnostics and automated strategy recommendations, content-creator (influencer) marketing, multi-channel precision ad delivery, and the Hui Shenghuo (惠生活) rights-aggregation platform, helping merchants operate across Meituan, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and Taobao. It reports serving hundreds of thousands of merchants across dozens of Chinese cities with more than 1,000 employees. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment.
k.name: Kezaihui

k.description: KG-NINJA is the operator identity (GitHub user KG-NINJA, Osaka; Cloudflare Wallet handle @kgninja) behind Agent Verification Utility at agent-economy.kgninja.dev, a Cloudflare Workers service (v0.4.3) that runs bounded deterministic checks (SHA-256 equality, JSON Pointer existence/equality/type) over caller-supplied inline JSON and returns an Ed25519-signed execution record, sold to agents per call for 10000 atomic USDC ($0.01) on Base through x402 v2 with no account, API key or OAuth. One origin exposes the product three ways — a 44-operation OpenAPI 3.1.0 contract at /openapi.json, a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server at /mcp answering an anonymous tools/list (five tools, one paid), and an A2A 1.0 agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json with JSON-RPC at /a2a — plus an RFC 9727 API catalog, an MCP Registry server.json, a provider-published Agent Skill, a JWKS, an x402 manifest, llms.txt and Content-Signal. The apex kgninja.dev has no A record; the subdomain is its only web presence.
k.name: KG-NINJA

k.description: kgateway is the most widely deployed gateway in Kubernetes for microservices and AI agents. It is a feature-rich, fast, and flexible Kubernetes-native ingress controller and next-generation API gateway built on top of Envoy proxy and the Kubernetes Gateway API.
k.name: Kgateway

k.description: KGeN (Kratos Gamer Network) is a verified-human data network powering Physical AI and Large Language Models across the Global South, and the operator of the KGeN Economy Protocols — a suite of developer APIs (Esports and Loyalty) that let game studios add leaderboard-based competitions and customizable reward systems paid in KCash, redeemable for real-world items at the Kratos Store. Server-to-server and per-user (JWT/OTP) endpoints cover sessions, tournaments, wallets, rewards, and rewardable events. Company revenue feeds $KGEN tokenomics, where every AI-data contract permanently retires token supply on-chain. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures.
k.name: KGeN

k.description: Khalifa University of Science and Technology is a research-intensive public university in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (ROR 05hffr360), formed from the 2017 merger of KUSTAR, the Masdar Institute and the Petroleum Institute. Its programmable footprint is small, real, and almost entirely indirect. Two surfaces are genuinely institution-operated: an OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint for the Khazna research portal at khazna.ku.ac.ae/ws/oai, live and anonymous with an institution admin contact, and the university's own Microsoft Entra ID tenant for the ku.ac.ae namespace, which issues OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0 for institution systems. A third, partial surface is the WordPress REST API on www.ku.ac.ae, whose discovery root and a handful of routes answer publicly while the core collections are closed with HTTP 401. Everything else a search turns up is a vendor contract running under the university's name: Khazna itself is an Elsevier Pure tenant (khazna.ku.ac.ae CNAMEs to khalifauniversity.elsevierpure.com) and Elsevier's own Pure API spec is served from that host; the LMS is a Blackboard Learn tenant behind elearn.ku.ac.ae; discovery is Ex Libris Primo VE; the library web presence, calendar and ask-a-librarian service are Springshare; off-campus access is OCLC EZproxy. Those relationships are recorded here as tenancies. None of their contracts are catalogued as Khalifa's. There is no central developer portal, no published API program, no open-data portal, and no institution-operated API reference.
k.name: Khalifa University

k.description: Khan Academy is a non-profit providing free online educational content. The legacy Khan Academy API (v1) is deprecated/limited and the public api-explorer.khanacademy.org redirects to the main site. Some endpoints under www.khanacademy.org/api/v1/ remain in use for internal apps and historical integrations, but Khan Academy no longer maintains a publicly supported developer program.
k.name: Khan Academy

k.description: Khatabook is a Bengaluru, India-based fintech company building a mobile-first digital ledger ("bahi khata") and business management platform for India's 6.3 crore-strong MSME sector. Founded in 2018 by Ravish Naresh, Vaibhav Kalpe, Dhanesh Kumar, and Jaideep Poonia, its flagship Khatabook Android app lets shopkeepers and small merchants record credit transactions ("udhaar"), send free WhatsApp/SMS payment reminders, collect payments via UPI and QR codes, and generate ledger statements — replacing the paper notebook ("khata") historically used across Indian retail. The app has been downloaded over 50 million times and is offered in 13+ Indian languages. Khatabook's portfolio also includes Cashbook (cash-in/cash-out tracking), Pagarkhata/Pagarbook (staff attendance and salary management), Biz Analyst (Tally mobility for accountants, acquired in 2021 for ~$10M), and a suite of GST, EMI, income tax, payroll, and loan calculators. The company has raised roughly $190M across seed through Series C from Sequoia Capital, Tencent, DST Global, GGV Capital, Y Combinator, B Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, and angels including MS Dhoni, valuing it around $600M. Khatabook monetizes via SMB lending tie-ups, premium business tools, and adjacent fintech distribution. The Khatabook GitHub organization (verified, owns khatabook.com) exists but has no public repositories, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or partner program — its surface is a consumer/SMB mobile app rather than a developer platform.
k.name: Khatabook

k.description: Khazenly is a Cairo, Egypt based cloud order-fulfillment and e-commerce enablement platform that helps online merchants and brands manage the full post-checkout journey. Its stack combines an order management system, warehousing and pick-pack-ship fulfillment, last-mile delivery, and cash-on-delivery collection so sellers can outsource operations while retaining visibility. Khazenly connects to popular e-commerce storefronts and marketplaces to sync orders, inventory, and shipping status. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network; its public developer/API surface is not openly documented, so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signals rather than harvested API artifacts.
k.name: Khazenly

k.description: Khazna is Egypt's leading financial super app, a Cairo-based fintech building inclusive financial services for the country's underbanked payroll workers and their families. Through its consumer mobile app it offers earned-wage access and salary advances, bill and utility payments, savings, and everyday consumer lending, with the goal of extending affordable, digital financial services to people traditionally excluded from the formal banking system. Khazna is backed by Speedinvest and operates as a business-to-consumer application; it does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with verified public identity and domain-security signals.
k.name: Khazna

k.description: Kheiron Medical Technologies is a London-founded medical-imaging AI company best known for Mia (Mammography Intelligent Assessment), a deep-learning solution that supports radiologists in breast-cancer screening as an independent, concurrent, or triage reader. Founded in 2016 and backed by investors including Atomico, Kheiron now operates as part of RadNet's DeepHealth, whose portfolio spans breast, prostate, lung, brain, and thyroid imaging plus the Diagnostic, Operations, and TechLive suites. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kheiron/DeepHealth as a health-AI provider; the company exposes clinical products and enterprise integrations rather than a public self-serve developer API, so most machine-readable API artifacts are not applicable and this record captures its identity, security, and legal surface.
k.name: Kheiron Medical Technologies

k.description: Khmerhome (khmerhome.com) is Cambodia's real estate marketplace, based in Phnom Penh, connecting buyers, renters, and property owners across houses, apartments, condos, villas, boreys, land, warehouses, and commercial spaces. The platform offers property search and browsing, sales and rental listings with photos and agent details, property valuation and appraisal tools, an articles section covering Cambodian economic and property developments, and community events for real estate professionals and expats. Khmerhome ships native iOS and Android mobile apps and operates alongside sister sites khmerload.com and khmercars.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer/API surface, OpenAPI specification, or documentation portal has been found at this time.
k.name: Khmer Home

k.description: Khoros is the enterprise online-community and social-customer-engagement platform formed when Lithium Technologies merged with Spredfast in 2018; the combined company rebranded as Khoros in 2019 and is today operated by IgniteTech. This record was listed as Lithium until 2026-09-24, and it also carries the Spredfast product line (Khoros Marketing). The Lithium name is still load-bearing in the live platform: the Khoros Care APIs are served from *.response.lithium.com and api.app.lithium.com, the Community plugin SDK and CLI ship on npm as lithium-sdk (the `li` command), and the public GitHub organization is still github.com/lithiumtech. The platform exposes four public developer surfaces documented at developer.khoros.com — Khoros Care (agent, author, conversation, bot, work-queue, analytics and GDPR APIs on the Lithium hosts), Khoros Marketing (the Spredfast-lineage Conversations, CRM, Stream, label-set and notification APIs on api.spredfast.com), Khoros Flow (the flow.ai bot and messaging REST API), and Khoros Community (the LiQL-powered Community v2 API plus the legacy v1 REST API), with the newer Aurora community platform adding a GraphQL API behind a login.
k.name: Khoros

k.description: Khosla Ventures is a Menlo Park, California venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla. The firm backs bold, early, and impactful ventures, favoring contrarian deep-tech bets with world-class teams and a conviction-driven approach that deliberately accepts a high failure rate to capture transformative outcomes. Khosla invests across seed, early (Series A/B), and growth stages through its Seed Fund, Main Fund, and Opportunity (growth) Fund, writing checks that range from small seed positions to large growth rounds. Focus sectors span artificial intelligence, enterprise and consumer software, financial services and fintech, robotics and frontier/deep tech, aerospace and defense, climate and sustainability (clean energy, fusion, materials, agriculture), and digital health, medtech, diagnostics, and therapeutics. The firm manages roughly $16 billion in assets as of 2025 and is known for early investments in OpenAI, Stripe, Square/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Affirm, Impossible Foods, GitLab, Okta, Rocket Lab, and QuantumScape. Headquarters are at 2128 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA, with a primarily United States geographic focus and select global investments.
k.name: Khosla Ventures

k.description: Khush is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Khush

k.description: Ki is the first fully digital, algorithmically driven syndicate at Lloyd's of London, launched in 2020 out of Brit with Google Cloud and University College London and capitalised with US$500m from Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and Fairfax Financial. Operating from the United Kingdom as Lloyd's Syndicate 1618, Ki writes follow-only capacity across specialty lines — property, casualty and specialty — quoting risks that a lead underwriter has already priced, in seconds rather than days, through an algorithm rather than a face-to-face negotiation in the Room. Brokers reach Ki through app.ki-insurance.com, a partner-gated single-page platform behind an Auth0 authorization-code login, and Ki announced a "Broker API" in May 2021 that lets partner broking platforms request quotes directly from the algorithm. That API posture is entirely partner-gated: there is no developer portal, no public reference documentation, no self-serve signup, no provider-published OpenAPI or Postman collection, and no public webhook or event catalog. What is observable is the platform API itself — Ki's own broker client ships a complete endpoint registry in its public JavaScript bundle, exposing a same-origin REST surface of roughly a hundred JSON operations across quotes, quote lines, pricing, schedules of values, slip extraction, leads, pipeline, broking houses, nominated leads and Lloyd's risk codes, all authorised with an Auth0 bearer token. API Evangelist has derived an observed OpenAPI from that bundle. Ki remains the archetype of the United Kingdom's London-market pattern: genuinely advanced machine-to-machine insurance placement infrastructure, aimed at brokers and syndicates rather than at developers, and therefore effectively invisible from the outside.
k.name: Ki Insurance

k.description: Kia Corporation is a South Korean automaker. Through KIA Developers (developer.kia.com) it publishes a Korea-market connected-car data API: OAuth2 account APIs, personal-data consent APIs, and vehicle profile, status (odometer, range, EV battery/charging) and warning-lamp data for partner services.
k.name: Kia

k.description: Kiavi (formerly LendingHome) is a technology-driven private lender for residential real estate investors, providing fix-and-flip bridge loans, new-construction financing, and DSCR rental loans across 49 states plus Washington, D.C. The company has originated more than $30 billion in loans and funded over 100,000 investment properties, pairing a digital application and portfolio-management experience with institutional capital. Kiavi is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Kiavi publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, a real-estate-investing blog, legal/policy pages, and a HackerOne-based security vulnerability disclosure program.
k.name: Kiavi

k.description: Kibana is an open-source data visualization and exploration tool used for log and time-series analytics, application monitoring, and operational intelligence. Kibana provides histograms, line graphs, pie charts, heat maps, geospatial visualizations, dashboards, alerting, and management of saved objects across spaces, exposing a comprehensive REST API for programmatic configuration and automation.
k.name: Kibana

k.description: Kibin is a consumer study and academic-writing company operating at kibin.com, trusted by students since 2011. Its newest product is an AI-powered study partner (iOS app) that turns lectures, notes, PDFs, and YouTube videos into personalized study guides, quizzes, flashcards, transcripts, and explanations to help students learn faster and build mastery. Alongside the study app, Kibin also runs its long-standing academic-writing surface — professional essay editing, a paper grader, a thesis-statement generator, essay examples, and a writing blog. Kibin is a B2C, mobile- and web-delivered product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.
k.name: Kibin

k.description: Kick is a self-driving, agentic bookkeeping platform for business owners and accounting firms — "an agentic ledger that does your books with you." It auto-categorizes bank and card transactions in real time (via Plaid), surfaces commonly missed deductions, supports customizable categorization rules, classes, multi-entity journal entries, reconciliation, and tax-ready financials (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, tax package). Kick exposes a hosted, OAuth-secured Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at use.kick.co/mcp and a first-party CLI (@kickfinance/cli), letting AI agents in Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini query and safely write to the books with preview-first confirmation. Backed by Felicis and General Catalyst.
k.name: Kick

k.description: Kickbox is an email verification and list cleaning service that helps senders improve deliverability by detecting invalid, disposable, role-based, and risky email addresses before they enter mailing lists. The platform offers real-time single verification, bulk batch verification, and a deliverability monitoring suite. Kickbox provides a simple HTTPS REST API authenticated by API key returning structured verification results with reason codes.
k.name: Kickbox

k.description: Kickpay is an intelligent finance platform for e-commerce and hardware brands that unlocks capital tied up in inventory. It plugs into a company's data sources — fulfillment centers, e-commerce sales channels, and bank accounts — to see historic sales, then finances the manufacturing cost of each SKU it estimates will sell within a reasonable window (typically around 16 weeks). Kickpay can fund the brand directly or pay the manufacturer to purchase more inventory, and the brand only pays Kickpay back as units ship: when a unit ships from the fulfillment center, Kickpay activates an ACH payment for the manufacturing price plus a fixed fee. It provides smart daily servicing and reporting, distinguishes customer shipments from internal stock movements, and uses prediction tooling to forecast future sales and cash flow so it can underwrite startups with as little as three months of sales history. Kickpay was backed by Canaan Partners and DCVC. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Kickpay publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs, and the enrichment pipeline found no machine-readable API surface.
k.name: Kickpay

k.description: Kickstarter is a public-benefit crowdfunding platform where creators launch funding campaigns for creative projects — film, music, art, design, games, technology, publishing, and more — and backers pledge money to help bring them to life on an all-or-nothing funding model. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York, it has channeled billions of dollars in pledges to hundreds of thousands of successfully funded projects. Kickstarter does not currently operate a public developer API program or developer portal; its GraphQL and REST endpoints power its own web and mobile clients and are not documented for third-party integration. The company does maintain an active open-source GitHub organization (including its iOS and Android app source), a help center, and a company blog. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kickstarter's public developer, security, and platform surface for discovery and enrichment.
k.name: Kickstarter

k.description: Kidas is a Techstars-backed trust-and-safety company that builds white-label scam detection and online-protection solutions for enterprises and consumers. Its ProtectMe platform monitors PC gaming and Discord voice and text channels for cyberbullying, predators, phishing, and scams, and its broader suite adds SMS scam detection, email protection, a scam-screening chatbot, and deepfake/impersonation defense that integrate into existing customer channels. Kidas markets custom builds and lists Aura, Comcast, Overwolf, Razer, Walmart, Intel, and Best Buy among its customers. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published as of this profile.
k.name: Kidas

k.description: Kiddom is a K-12 curriculum management, instruction and assessment platform used by school districts to implement high-quality instructional materials (HQIM), plan and pace lessons, deliver digital assignments, administer standards-aligned assessments, and analyze student performance data. The product is sold to districts rather than to developers: there is no public developer program, API key, or published API reference. Kiddom's public machine-readable surface is its 1EdTech interoperability posture — it is certified as an LTI Advantage 1.3 Tool and as a OneRoster 1.1 REST Data Consumer, and it rosters from Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology and Microsoft Teams. The only publicly reachable API endpoints are the LTI 1.3 launch pair on api.kiddom.co; the API documentation at api.kiddom.co/docs sits behind Cloudflare Access.
k.name: Kiddom

k.description: KiddoWear (now operating as Kiddo Health) is a pediatric healthcare technology company that offers a connected care platform for capturing and sharing health data for children with physical and behavioral health challenges. The platform combines biometric tracking of 12+ biomarkers (respiration, heart rate, stress scores, and sleep), family journaling of behavior and health status between visits, educational family resources, care navigation that integrates with medical records and clinical workflows, and a provider dashboard that surfaces insights and real-time health trends. Kiddo Health serves behavioral health conditions such as ADHD and autism spectrum disorder and metabolic conditions such as childhood obesity and diabetes, bridging gaps between families, providers, and care teams across health plans, health systems, and employers. A Techstars-backed portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.
k.name: KiddoWear

k.description: Kigen is a security-focused eSIM and iSIM technology company, spun out of Arm in 2020 and headquartered in Cambridge, UK, backed by SoftBank. Kigen builds GSMA-compliant SIM operating systems, integrated SIM (iSIM) and embedded SIM (eSIM) technology, remote SIM provisioning (RSP), and In-Factory Profile Provisioning (IFPP), together with lifecycle and over-the-air (OTA) management for connected and IoT devices. Its eUICC security, SIM OS, and provisioning platform serve mobile network operators, device manufacturers, OEMs and ODMs, IoT service providers, and enterprises building connected products, enabling secure cellular connectivity at scale across the device lifecycle. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Kigen's public web surface.
k.name: Kigen

k.description: Kiira (Kiira Health) was a student-focused digital health / telehealth platform that partnered with colleges and universities to bridge the gap between students and clinicians, providing online visits with doctors, nurses, and therapists, primary care and gynecological consultations, mental health support, and health literacy workshops and education resources through a patient booking portal. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this pass the company operated a consumer/patient web app only and published no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so there is no API surface to enrich. Its recorded domain kiira.io is no longer controlled by the company — it now redirects to an unrelated third-party site — so this profile reflects the company's last-known (archived, Dec 2024) state and is treated as a defunct / lapsed lead.
k.name: Kiira

k.description: Kik (Kin) refers to the Kin cryptocurrency created by Kik Interactive, the messaging company, as a blockchain-based digital currency for use inside consumer applications. Kin originally launched on a fork of the Stellar network and later migrated to Solana, shipping first-party developer SDKs (JavaScript/Node and Python) under the kinecosystem GitHub organization and a developer program at developer.kin.org. The Kin project is now defunct: the developer surface no longer resolves, every kinecosystem repository is archived, the published SDKs are deprecated, and Kik itself was acquired by MediaLab AI Inc. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and is retained as a historical record of a wound-down crypto developer surface.
k.name: Kik (Kin)

k.description: Kiki (Kikihub) is a location-based social networking and chat mobile app that connects people nearby for local friendships, dating, networking, and community conversations. Users join local chat rooms to discover people around them and start real conversations, meeting new friends and matches in their area. The app is available for iOS and Android. Kiki publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed (500 Global, a16z) consumer social lead awaiting any future developer surface.
k.name: Kiki

k.description: Kiko Labs is a neuroscience-based early-learning company (a 500 Global portfolio company) that builds adaptive brain-training games for children ages 3-7. Its flagship product, Kiko's Thinking Time, is a voice-guided iOS app developed with Harvard and UC Berkeley neuroscientists with support from the US Department of Education and National Science Foundation. The program trains executive functions — working memory, inhibition, focus, and cognitive flexibility — through progressive games, and includes a parent and educator dashboard for tracking skill development. Kiko Labs is a consumer edtech company and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.
k.name: Kiko Labs

k.description: Kikoff is a San Francisco-based consumer fintech, founded in 2019, that helps people build and repair credit. Its products include a Credit Account that furnishes tradelines to all three bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion), rent and bill reporting, credit monitoring and disputes, an AI Debt Negotiator, the Fynn AI credit coach, and an invite-only secured credit card, sold across Basic, Premium, and Ultimate subscription tiers. Kikoff Enterprise exposes a unified REST API covering member enrollment, tradeline furnishing, and dispute status so businesses can embed credit-building infrastructure. Backed by GGV Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
k.name: Kikoff

k.description: Kildare County Council Open Data is a county government open-data portal for Ireland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 80 datasets.
k.name: Kildare County Council Open Data

k.description: Kili Technology is a training-data and data-labeling platform for building high-quality datasets for machine learning and LLMs. Its labeling application is fully programmable through a single GraphQL API (and a Python SDK) covering projects, assets, labels, issues, and users at https://cloud.kili-technology.com/api/label/v2/graphql.
k.name: Kili Technology

k.description: Kilo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
k.name: Kilo

k.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.
k.name: Kilsar

k.description: Kimba is an AI-powered sleep technology company building a bedside device that uses personalized scent therapy to improve sleep quality. The device reads biometric data from wearables (Oura, WHOOP, Apple Watch, Garmin), monitors sleep architecture, breathing, movement and disturbances, and releases natural, water-based scent formulations at precise moments in the sleep cycle to enhance rest, reduce nighttime disruptions and support cognitive performance. Kimba is a Techstars-backed direct-to-consumer hardware and subscription brand whose online store runs on Shopify; it exposes an agent-facing commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), a hosted MCP endpoint, and Shopify Customer Account API (OIDC) authentication rather than a traditional developer API.
k.name: Kimba

k.description: Kimberly-Clark is a global personal care and consumer tissue company with brands including Huggies, Kleenex, Scott, Kotex, Cottonelle, Poise, Depend, and Pull-Ups. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified for Kimberly-Clark; this repository tracks corporate, supplier, and integration surfaces for ongoing API discovery.
k.name: Kimberly-Clark

k.description: Kimetsu (kimetsu.dev) is Rodrigo Córdoba's open-source infrastructure for coding agents. Kimetsu itself is a local, model-free memory sidecar — one Rust binary and one SQLite brain per project — that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and OpenClaw load as a local-stdio MCP server (~28 kimetsu_* tools), with a CLI, npm/cargo/PyPI packages, a self-hostable Kimetsu Remote HTTP MCP server and published benchmark numbers. The domain also operates agents.kimetsu.dev, a credential-free, read-only Agent Gateway with a published OpenAPI 3.1.0 (15 operations), an A2A Agent Card served at the RFC 8615 path (0.3 by default, 1.0 negotiated with the A2A-Version header) and a live JSON-RPC guide for Sidequest Commons — the maintainer's daily public project-selection loop run through GitHub issues and reactions — plus llms.txt on two hosts, a /.well-known/kimetsu-agents.json discovery pointer and JSON Schemas for its discovery documents. Everything is MIT OR Apache-2.0. Seeded from the A2A Registry listing dev.kimetsu.sidequest_commons_guide under the harvest name "Sidequest Commons".
k.name: Kimetsu

k.description: Kimi is the long-context large language model family and assistant from Moonshot AI. This is a duplicate profile: Moonshot AI and the Kimi API platform are profiled in the moonshot-ai repository, which is canonical. Consolidated 2026-10-13, approved by Kin Lane.
k.name: Kimi (Moonshot AI)

k.description: Team radio and interview quotes by Finnish F1 legend Kimi Räikkönen
k.name: kimiquotes

k.description: Kimola is a market research automation platform that turns customer feedback into research insights. It tracks feedback from social media, reviews, and direct uploads; analyzes it with AI to detect themes, sentiment, and patterns across 30+ languages; and generates executive summaries, customer personas, pain points, and journey maps. Kimola exposes a public REST API for presets (pre-trained classification and entity-extraction models), reports, feedback feeds, query consumption, and subscription usage, plus the Kimola Cognitive API for running text through custom and pre-built classification models and returning tagged predictions with probabilities. Official Python, Node.js, and C# SDKs are published. Kimola is backed by 500 Global.
k.name: Kimola

k.description: Kimono Labs was a developer-tools startup that let users turn any website into a structured API without writing code, using a visual point-and-click tool to define data selectors that Kimono would crawl on a schedule and expose as JSON/CSV endpoints and RSS feeds. Founded in 2014 by Pratap Ranade and Ryan Rowe and backed by Cowboy Ventures, the company was acquired by Palantir Technologies in February 2016, after which the hosted cloud service at kimonolabs.com was shut down on 29 February 2016; a downloadable Kimono Desktop application was released as a farewell so existing scrapers could continue running locally. The company is defunct and operates no live API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.
k.name: Kimono Labs

k.description: Kimpton AI is an AI-native investment research platform for institutional portfolio managers at hedge funds, mutual funds, and sustainable equity funds. It ingests market data, SEC filings, 13F holdings, earnings, and a fund's own investment mandates and research documents, then generates daily trade proposals with citations grounded in the fund's actual holdings — keeping human managers in control of every final decision. The platform connects to custodians and OMS/portfolio systems (or accepts direct uploads) to sync positions and P&L, aggregates mandates and research in a document vault, and integrates market-data partners FactSet, Tiingo, Massive, and Plaid. It is a managed service for professional investors and does not currently expose a public developer API. Backed by Y Combinator.
k.name: Kimpton AI

k.description: Kin Euphorics is a non-alcoholic functional beverage company that makes "euphorics" — botanical drinks blending adaptogens, nootropics, and botanics formulated to lift mood, ease stress, and offer a social alternative to alcohol. Co-founded by Jen Batchelor and Bella Hadid, the brand sells ready-to-drink and mixable products such as Kin Spritz, Dream Light, Lightwave, and High Rhode direct to consumers through a Shopify storefront. That storefront exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) discovery document advertising an MCP shopping endpoint for catalog search, cart, and checkout, alongside Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect for authentication and Google Pay / Shop Pay payment handlers.
k.name: Kin Euphorics

k.description: Kin Insurance is a direct-to-consumer home insurance platform founded in 2016 that leverages data and artificial intelligence to provide homeowners insurance in high-risk coastal and weather-exposed markets. The platform uses thousands of property data points for automated underwriting, enabling online quote generation, policy binding, and claims management without the need for traditional agents. Kin offers homeowners, condo, flood, and auto insurance across multiple states with a focus on affordability and accessibility in markets traditionally underserved by major carriers.
k.name: Kin Insurance

k.description: Kinaset Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Medfield, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Robert Clarke (CEO), Roger Heerman (COO) and Frazer Morgan (CDO) to develop novel inhaled therapeutics for severe respiratory disease. Its lead candidate, frevecitinib (KN-002), is a dry-powder inhaled pan-JAK inhibitor — potent and balanced across JAK1, JAK2, JAK3 and TYK2 — designed as a non-invasive anti-inflammatory add-on to standard of care for all severe asthma patients regardless of the underlying cause of inflammation, and explored in COPD. The company completed a Phase 1/1b program (NCT05006521), received FDA IND clearance, and in July 2026 dosed the first patient in the Phase 2b PANAIRAMA trial (NCT07532265) after closing a $103M oversubscribed Series B in January 2026 led by RA Capital Management and Forge Life Science Partners, with EQT Life Sciences, Vivo Capital, Schroders Capital, Willett Advisors, Pictet Alternative Advisors, Sixty Degree Capital, Atlas Venture, 5AM Ventures and Gimv participating on roughly $143M raised to date. Kinaset is a drug developer, not a software company: its product is a clinical pipeline, and it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs, no webhooks and no machine-readable API contract. Its entire public surface is a 34-page Squarespace marketing and investor-news site whose robots.txt disallows every platform JSON view and blocks the major AI crawlers by user agent.
k.name: Kinaset Therapeutics

k.description: Kinaxis is a concurrent supply chain planning platform — branded Maestro (formerly RapidResponse) — that provides REST APIs for supply chain orchestration, scenario modeling, demand sensing, and supply planning across global manufacturing and distribution networks. The platform offers an AI-infused intelligence engine, digital twin simulation, and a Developer Studio for building custom applications and algorithms on top of the supply chain data fabric.
k.name: Kinaxis

k.description: Kindara is a fertility-awareness and reproductive-health company offering a digital fertility charting system across web (app.kindara.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps. It lets users track basal body temperature, cervical fluid, and menstrual cycle data to understand their fertility, time conception, or practice fertility-awareness-based birth control. Kindara pairs its charting app with the Wink basal thermometer and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing femtech product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.
k.name: Kindara

k.description: Kindbody is a national fertility and family-building clinic network and employer benefit provider. Services include IVF, egg freezing, embryo banking, male fertility care, LGBTQ+ family building, oncofertility, gestational surrogacy, and egg donation, plus a wellness layer (Kindbody360) and lab testing (Kindlabs). Kindbody operates a direct-to-employer fertility benefit and partners with payers; clinical workflows are exposed through a Patient Portal, an online scheduling system, and a Referring Provider Portal. No public developer or partner API has been identified - integration appears to be handled through gated employer and payer onboarding. This entry catalogs the company surface for the API Evangelist index.
k.name: Kindbody

k.description: Kinde is a developer-first authentication and customer identity platform that bundles authentication (passwords, passwordless, social, enterprise SSO), authorization (roles, permissions, scopes), B2B organizations, billing, and feature flags into a single integrated product. Founded in Australia, Kinde positions itself as "the fully integrated developer platform — secure and monetize your product from day one" and is used by over 70,000 developers. The platform exposes a Management API for tenant administration and an Account API for end-user self-service flows, both backed by published OpenAPI specs and a large open-source SDK ecosystem on GitHub (TypeScript, React, Next.js, Python, Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, Elixir, Flutter, iOS, Android, Expo, React Native, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Remix, TanStack Start) plus a Go-based CLI, a Terraform provider, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.
k.name: Kinde

k.description: Kinder Morgan is one of the largest energy infrastructure companies in North America, owning and operating pipelines and terminals that transport natural gas, refined petroleum products, crude oil, carbon dioxide, and other commodities. Kinder Morgan publishes pipeline informational postings and capacity data through Electronic Bulletin Board (EBB) portals; no public REST API or developer program has been identified at this time.
k.name: Kinder Morgan

k.description: Kindor is a performance-intelligence platform for technology teams that turns engineering, project-management, finance, and HR activity into automated metrics, reports, and smart notifications. It integrates with tools like GitHub, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Notion, Google Calendar, and Google Meet to track DORA delivery metrics, resource allocation across initiatives, AI-tool adoption and ROI, and productivity anomalies, giving technology leaders real-time visibility and AI-generated summaries so they can align tech investments with business goals without manual reporting. Kindor claims outcomes such as lower tech operating costs, faster delivery, and less time spent on reporting. It is a 500 Global portfolio company; the public website is a Wix site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access, but Kindor publishes no first-party product API or developer portal.
k.name: Kindor

k.description: Kindred is a members-only home exchange platform where verified members swap their real homes with one another instead of paying for traditional accommodation. The service runs on a credit economy — members earn one night of travel credit for every night they host, and new members start with five nights of credit. Kindred verifies every member and home, provides professional cleaning before and after each stay, and includes up to $100K in damage protection. There are no membership fees; travelers pay only a cleaning and service fee per trip. The platform operates across 190+ cities in North America and Europe and is backed by a16z, Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, Index Ventures, and NEA. Kindred is a consumer travel product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.
k.name: Kindred
