Playground concentrates on four pillars: next-gen compute (quantum computing, novel AI chip architectures, advanced interconnects, and semiconductors), automation (robotics, supply-chain and industrial automation with tangible ROI), energy transition and decarbonization, and engineered biology (AI-driven drug discovery, RNA editing, and next-generation therapies). It invests at the earliest stages, often at company formation, and operates Studio Palo Alto, a lab and prototyping environment for hardware and deep-science founders. Reported assets under management are over $1.2 billion across its funds. Notable portfolio companies include PsiQuantum, Relativity Space, Ultima Genomics, d-Matrix, Velo3D (NYSE), and MosaicML (acquired by Databricks).
p.name: Playground Global

p.description: Playground Pediatrics is a pediatric medical group and practice-support (management services) organization that partners with independent, community-based pediatric practices across North Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, and Pennsylvania. It provides partner practices with operational support (billing, payer contracting, HR, payroll, technology, compliance, and marketing), talent recruiting/development/retention, and infrastructure for long-term stability and value-based care participation, while letting each practice keep its local identity. Partner practices include Cobb Pediatrics, Cornerstone Medical Associates, and Rainbow Pediatrics. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or event surface was found as of this enrichment pass.
p.name: Playgroundpediatrics

p.description: Playhouse is a consumer real estate application that combines homes-for-sale listings with community polls and reactions. Home searchers, neighbors, homebuyers, investors, and real estate professionals browse luxury and residential listings and react to them, turning property discovery into a social, opinion-driven experience. The product ships as native iOS and Android apps backed by a private api.playhouse.so service; there is no publicly documented developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or API reference surface. Playhouse is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile was enriched from live probes of its Webflow marketing site, app-store listings, and DNS/TLS records.
p.name: playhouse

p.description: PlayHT, now operating as PlayAI, is a generative voice platform offering realistic text-to-speech models, AI voice agents, and a podcast generation tool called PlayNote. The platform centers on the PlayDialog and Play 3.0 Mini models, providing more than 200 prebuilt voices across multiple languages and accents with sub-second latency suited to conversational applications. PlayAI exposes REST and streaming endpoints for text-to-speech, voice listing, voice cloning, and voice agent management. It ships Python and Node.js SDKs and a hosted playground, and integrates with the major voice agent infrastructure stacks. The product is widely used to build voice assistants, IVRs, narration pipelines, and content production workflows.
p.name: PlayHT

p.description: PlayPlay is an online video and visual creation platform that lets business teams produce on-brand videos and images without prior editing experience. Through a drag-and-drop editor, AI-assisted tools (text-to-video, script and voice-over generation, automatic subtitles) and enterprise collaboration, brand-kit and review workflows, it serves marketing, communications and HR teams at large organizations. Founded in France and backed by Balderton Capital, Insight Partners and Point Nine, PlayPlay is a SaaS product without a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its published identity, legal and security surface (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR).
p.name: PlayPlay

p.description: PlayQ is a Los Angeles-based mobile game developer and publisher creating free-to-play games for a global audience, including titles such as Charm King and Treasure Party. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass PlayQ operates a consumer-facing marketing and game-support website with no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface; player support is routed through per-game Zendesk help centers.
p.name: PlayQ

p.description: Playraven is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Playraven

p.description: Playroll is a global HR platform providing Employer of Record (EOR), contractor management, and global payroll across 180+ countries. It runs local payroll, statutory benefits, and compliance for distributed teams, and offers a partner/enterprise integration surface - native HRIS connectors (HiBob, BambooHR), an "Open API" for bi-directional HR data sync, and custom/embedded integration builds. The developer API is partner- and enterprise-gated; sandbox access and documentation are provided to integration partners rather than published on a public developer portal.
p.name: Playroll

p.description: Playroom (Playroom Kit) is a client-side developer platform for building multiplayer apps and games in minutes. Its single JavaScript/TypeScript SDK (npm playroomkit) provides synchronized global and per-player state, an elected host model, remote procedure calls (RPCs), matchmaking and lobbies, on-screen joystick/gamepad controllers, bots, and turn-based helpers, with wrappers for Unity (C#) and Godot and support across React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Remix, Phaser, and React Three Fiber. Apps authenticate with a read-only gameId issued from the Dev Portal rather than a server API key, and Playroom hosts the realtime infrastructure. It also embeds into Discord Activities and TikTok Live. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.
p.name: Playroom

p.description: Playsome (Playsome Ltd. / Playsome Oy) is a Helsinki, Finland mobile game studio that builds free-to-play games combining deep gameplay with polished visuals under the philosophy of making "big games with a small team". Its flagship title is Friends & Dragons, a cooperative multiplayer puzzle-RPG for iOS and Android featuring 150+ collectible heroes and 700+ puzzles and dungeons. The company is backed by gaming-focused venture firms Play Ventures and EQT. Playsome does not publish a traditional developer API, but its Wix-hosted website exposes a live Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access, letting agents retrieve business details, search the site, and start bookings/purchases without scraping.
p.name: Playsome

p.description: PlayStation, a brand of Sony Interactive Entertainment, is a leading global provider of interactive entertainment hardware, software, and services. It offers the PlayStation consoles, a vast library of games, subscription services like PlayStation Plus, and a developer ecosystem. The company engages millions of players worldwide through innovative gaming experiences, community features, and a robust digital marketplace.
p.name: PlayStation

p.description: Playstream is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Playstream

p.description: PLAYSTUDIOS, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYPS) is a developer and publisher of free-to-play casual and casino-style mobile and social games, including myVEGAS Slots, POP! Slots, MGM Slots Live, myKONAMI, Tetris Block Puzzle, Solitaire, Bingo, and Mahjong titles. Its differentiating platform, playAWARDS, is a loyalty rewards engine that lets players earn real-world rewards from brand partners across gaming, hospitality, dining, and entertainment. The company is headquartered in Las Vegas and went public in 2021 via a business combination with Acies Acquisition Corp. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a dcm-ventures portfolio company; PLAYSTUDIOS publishes consumer-facing games and corporate/investor properties but no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.
p.name: PLAYSTUDIOS

p.description: Playtika Holding is an Israel-based mobile gaming company and Fortune 1000 firm that develops and publishes free-to-play casual and casino-themed games such as Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, and Caesars Slots. The company operates a portfolio of social and casual mobile gaming titles distributed through major app stores and uses data-driven engagement and live operations to monetize its global player base. Playtika does not publish a public developer portal or external API.
p.name: Playtika Holding

p.description: Please (Please Platforms) is an AI-powered "thinking" reminders application for iOS that lets people capture a thought, a link, or an image with zero effort, then automatically enriches each reminder with additional context and surfaces intelligent, connected suggestions so nothing gets missed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Please ships a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.
p.name: Please

p.description: Please Assist Me (PAM) is an apartment-amenity and home-management service that partners with residential buildings to handle cleaning, errands, groceries, laundry, dry-cleaning, package handling, and custom special requests for residents. Dedicated per-building teams deliver the service, backed by a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and a web app for booking and account management, a 24-hour satisfaction guarantee, and body-camera transparency. Backed by Techstars. The company operates a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.
p.name: Please Assist Me

p.description: PleasrDAO is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) formed in 2021 by a collective of digital artists, NFT collectors, and DeFi investors. It is known for acquiring and stewarding culturally significant digital and physical assets, including the sole copy of Wu-Tang Clan's album "Once Upon a Time in Shaolin," the original "Doge" meme image, and Edward Snowden's "Stay Free" NFT. The organization pioneers fractionalized, on-chain ownership of art and cultural artifacts. PleasrDAO operates as a community-governed collective rather than a conventional software or API company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation surface.
p.name: PleasrDAO

p.description: Plena Health is an AI operating system for specialty medical practices, founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch. Plena automates the complex administrative workflows a clinic's staff shouldn't have to do — referrals, fax intake, patient calls, scheduling, prior authorization, procedure compliance, and collections — end to end, running in the background across the EHRs, clearinghouses, and other systems a practice already uses, rather than requiring the practice to adopt new software. Founded by Eyad Abdalla (CEO) and Ahmed Al Mudarris (CTO) and based in San Francisco, the company reports operating across six specialties in eight states. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Plena publishes only a marketing site (a single-page React application) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.
p.name: Plena Health

p.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.
p.name: Plenful

p.description: Plenna is a women's healthcare provider operating a network of integrated medical clinics across Mexico City, redefining health for women across every life stage. Its services span gynecology, maternity and prenatal care, fertility, menopause, contraception, gynecological surgery, psychology, nutrition, laboratory studies, vaccines and lactation support, delivered across six physical clinics (Tlalpan, Coapa, Del Valle, Polanco, San Angel and Satelite) and through Portal Plenna, a patient portal and iOS/Android mobile app for scheduling appointments, virtual consultations, test results, prescriptions and pregnancy tracking. Plenna is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.
p.name: Plenna

p.description: Plenty is an American indoor vertical farming company that grows produce such as leafy greens and strawberries in controlled, climate-independent indoor facilities using proprietary vertical growing systems, automation, and robotics. Headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area and founded in 2014, Plenty is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund and DCM Ventures. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a frontier-tech portfolio-company profile; the public enrichment pass found no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.
p.name: Plenty

p.description: Pleo is a business spend management platform that issues smart company cards to employees, enabling real-time expense tracking, receipt capture, and automated bookkeeping. The Pleo REST API lets developers automate workflows, sync accounting data, manage users and cards, and build custom integrations against accounting systems. The API supports OAuth 2.0 (with PKCE) and API key authentication with a scopes-based permission model, and offers both a sandbox and production environment. Pleo also runs an App Marketplace where partners can publish integrations available to thousands of businesses across Europe.
p.name: Pleo

p.description: Plerion is an AI-powered cloud security platform that gives teams unified visibility and automated remediation across cloud, code, and AI. It covers Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) for AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes; Cloud Workload Protection (CWPP) with vulnerability and SBOM scanning; Code Security (IaC and SCA scanning for GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket); AI Security Posture Management (AI-SPM) for Bedrock, OpenAI, and Anthropic deployments; attack-path analysis, entitlements analysis, resource access grants, and compliance tracking against frameworks like ISO 27001, SOC 2, CIS, and ISMS-P. Plerion exposes a tenant-scoped REST API (Bearer API key, regional hosts) plus a cross-platform CLI so teams can query findings, assets, risks, vulnerabilities, and compliance posture programmatically.
p.name: Plerion

p.description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.
p.name: Plerk

p.description: Plex, Inc. is a personal-media and streaming company whose Plex Media Server organizes, transcodes and streams a user's own movies, TV, music and photos to Plex client apps on virtually every platform, alongside a free ad-supported live TV and on-demand catalog, Discover, Rentals, the Plexamp music player and the paid Plex Pass tier. In September 2025 Plex published official documentation for the Plex Media Server HTTP API for the first time — an OpenAPI 3.1 contract covering libraries, metadata, playlists, play queues, sessions, DVR/Live TV, transcoding and server administration — together with a new public-key JWT authentication flow on plex.tv, Plex Pass webhooks, and an OAuth-protected remote MCP server for agents.
p.name: Plex

p.description: Plex Systems provides the Plex Smart Manufacturing Platform, a cloud‑based, elastic Manufacturing Execution System (MES) that integrates people, processes, machines and supply chains. Hosted by Rockwell Automation, Plex delivers real‑time visibility, AI‑driven insights, and scalable SaaS tools for manufacturers to improve operations, quality, and agility across the enterprise.
p.name: Plex Systems

p.description: Plexistor was an enterprise storage startup that built Software-Defined Memory (SDM) - a converged memory-and-storage architecture delivering ultra-low latency and millions of IOPS on commodity servers by tiering across DRAM, NVDIMM-N, Intel/Micron 3D XPoint, flash, and spinning disk. It positioned SDM as a persistent-memory storage layer for big-data workloads such as Cassandra, Couchbase, and Spark, adding enterprise features like snapshots, clones, high availability, and clustering. The company was acquired by NetApp in 2017 and its technology was folded into NetApp's memory/storage roadmap. The plexistor.com site survives as a static legacy marketing page with no active product download, API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that Plexistor exposes no public API surface.
p.name: Plexistor

p.description: Plexium is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of crv, dcvc, lux-capital, softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Plexium

p.description: PlexTrac is a penetration test reporting and proactive exposure management platform that unifies offensive security data from pentests, vulnerability scanners, and bug bounty programs into a single system of record. It automates pentest report authoring (including AI-assisted findings), centralizes and prioritizes vulnerability data by business impact, and drives remediation through workflows integrated with tools such as Jira and ServiceNow. PlexTrac exposes a JWT-authenticated REST API (v1 and v2) for managing clients, reports, findings, assets, and content-library writeups, plus RBAC/tenant administration and outbound webhooks, letting security teams and MSSPs integrate reporting and remediation into their own pipelines.
p.name: PlexTrac

p.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.
p.name: Plexus

p.description: Plexus Computers is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Plexus Computers

p.description: Plexxi was a software-defined networking (SDN) startup building data-center fabric and network orchestration, backed by GV and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and folded into the Aruba Networks / HPE data-center portfolio; plexxi.com now 301-redirects to arubanetworks.com. As of this enrichment pass Plexxi has no independent, live developer surface: no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, SDKs, or other API artifacts remain reachable. This record is retained for network lineage and its venture-portfolio provenance rather than any active API.
p.name: Plexxi *

p.description: Pliant is a Berlin-based financial technology company offering a business credit card and spend-management platform, plus Cards-as-a-Service (CaaS) and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) infrastructure for banks and platforms. Its Pro API lets customers programmatically issue physical, virtual, single-use and specialized cards (travel, fleet, benefits, insurance-claim), apply card controls and advanced limits, retrieve transactions and accounting data, manage receipts, projects, teams and statements, and subscribe to real-time callbacks. Pliant is PCI DSS certified, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified and holds an EU e-money license, with customers including BMW, Decathlon, Deutsche Telekom and Commerzbank.
p.name: Pliant

p.description: Pliant Technology, Inc. was a data-center storage company that pioneered the introduction of high-performance enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) into mission-critical data-center environments. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by SanDisk in 2011 and its product line was folded into SanDisk's enterprise storage solutions. The company operated as a hardware/semiconductor storage vendor and published no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer surface; its former domain now redirects to SanDisk. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record with no API surface to enrich.
p.name: Pliant Technology

p.description: Pliant Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of integrin-based therapies for underserved areas of medical need. Leveraging a proprietary integrin drug discovery and delivery platform, its lead program PLN-101095 is a dual-selective avb8/avb1 integrin inhibitor being evaluated in the FORTIFY clinical trial for patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, alongside additional pipeline programs in fibrosis and oncology. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Pliant Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this profile captures corporate identity and web presence only.
p.name: Pliant Therapeutics

p.description: Plink is a personalized commerce and card-linking platform that turns everyday payment transactions into intelligent, permission-based savings and engagement experiences for banks, merchants, and consumers. Its technology enriches transactions in real time, applying business rules and automated actions across payments, digital banking, and customer engagement, and exposes an API that lets any payment network make its transactions "smart" while keeping consumers anonymous. Plink says it has personalized over 700 million transactions and reaches 350+ banks, hundreds of thousands of merchants, and 10+ million consumers through an invitation-only network. The company operates a merchant/business portal and a consumer savings program (Fancoins) built on a PCI-compliant, tokenized card-linking structure.
p.name: Plink

p.description: A JSON API over the entire US grantmaking universe — about 205,000 grantmaking foundations and 17.9 million grants, read from public IRS Form 990, 990-EZ and 990-PF e-file filings and the IRS Business Master File. The funder-grantee graph traverses in both directions: filter by funder_id for everything a foundation funded, or by recip_id for every funder behind a nonprofit. Offers REST endpoints for grants, organization profiles, an IRS compliance and OFAC screen, an ad-hoc read-only SQL endpoint over a 31-table warehouse, and a hosted OAuth 2.1 MCP connector for AI agents. Entity resolution is free and unmetered. Published by Plinth, trading name of Time to Spare Ltd (UK Companies House 11530023), which also operates plinth.org.uk in the UK.
p.name: Plinth US Grants Data

p.description: Pliops is an Israeli data-acceleration semiconductor company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Ramat Gan, that builds the Extreme Data Processor (XDP) — a low-profile PCIe accelerator card that offloads storage and key-value data-path work from server CPUs. Its software surface is delivered as host libraries rather than as a web API: XDP-AccelKV and XDP-Rocks expose a RocksDB-API-compatible key-value engine (the "storelib" shared library) used as a drop-in under MySQL/MyRocks, Redis, KVRocks, TiDB, Kafka and Spark, and XDP LightningAI extends the same acceleration to GenAI KV-cache offload for vLLM-based inference. Pliops raised roughly $205M from investors including Intel Capital, NVIDIA, AMD, SoftBank Ventures Asia and Western Digital, and was acquired by Astera Labs in February 2026, which took certain assets, IP and about half the staff into a new Israeli R&D center. Pliops has never operated a public developer program: there is no developer portal, no public API reference, no published OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no published SDK in any package registry — product and library access runs through a sales/evaluation conversation.
p.name: Pliops

p.description: Plivo is a global communications platform offering programmable Voice, Messaging (SMS/MMS/WhatsApp), SIP Trunking, Verify, and Lookup APIs, plus an AI Voice Agent platform. The HTTP API is available at https://api.plivo.com/v1/ with HTTP Basic Auth using Auth ID and Auth Token credentials.
p.name: Plivo

p.description: Plixer is a network observability and defense company whose platform combines network flow (NetFlow/IPFIX) data with AI-driven analysis to help IT and security teams investigate incidents, detect threats, and optimize performance across on-premises, cloud, and zero-trust environments. Its products include Plixer One (unified observability), Plixer Scrutinizer (flow-first visibility with a native MCP server), FlowPro (threat detection), Replicator (NetFlow distribution), Machine Learning behavioral analytics, Endpoint Analytics, and an AI Assistant for natural-language queries grounded in flow data. Plixer Scrutinizer exposes a REST API and, as of Plixer 19.8, a native Model Context Protocol server. Backed by Battery Ventures.
p.name: Plixer

p.description: Plixi is an AI-powered Instagram growth platform that helps influencers, businesses, e-commerce brands, and content creators gain authentic followers through organic automation rather than bots or fake accounts. The service combines paid advertising, micro-interactions, and niche audience-data clustering with a machine-learning targeting feature (AI-Match) that lets users train the algorithm by rating accounts. It provides a real-time analytics dashboard, optional expert account management (Plixi Experts), and a subscription model across Basic, Pro, and Experts tiers. Plixi is a consumer SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.
p.name: Plixi

p.description: Plobal Apps is a no-code mobile app builder for Shopify merchants that turns online stores into native iOS and Android shopping apps without engineering. The platform offers drag-and-drop app design with HTML/CSS/JavaScript code blocks, push-notification marketing campaigns, live selling, AI-powered product recommendations, advanced search and smart filtering, and real-time analytics tracking 60+ in-app actions, plus omnichannel flows such as in-app ordering with in-store pickup. It installs through the Shopify App Store and is used by direct-to-consumer brands to grow mobile commerce revenue and customer retention.
p.name: Plobal Apps

p.description: Ploid is an applied AI lab building a people search and intelligence platform: a living index of more than two billion people available through a web app, a REST API, a CLI, and a hosted MCP server. The Ploid Public API (OpenAPI 3.1, 31 operations on api.ploid.com) covers synchronous people search, person resolution and evidence-backed person research runs, contact and social enrichment, public LinkedIn reads, monitors, and account usage and credit budgets, metered in ACU credits.
p.name: Ploid

p.description: Plooto is a Toronto-based payments automation company (founded 2015 by Hamed Abbasi and Serguei Kloubkov) that helps small and medium businesses and accounting firms automate domestic and international accounts payable and accounts receivable. Its cloud platform unifies bill pay, approval workflows, supplier and customer payments, reconciliation, and reporting across Canadian EFT, US ACH, credit card, and cross-border rails, syncing two-way with QuickBooks Online, Xero, and NetSuite. Plooto is a licensed money services business in its home market of Canada, working with Tier 1 banks and processing partners. Its posture is integration-led rather than API-platform-led: money movement runs on a first-party backend gateway (api.plooto.com) that powers the app and its accounting connectors, but Plooto does not publish a public, self-serve developer portal, downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or public API reference. Partner and embedded access is arranged through a gated partner onboarding process, not open developer sign-up.
p.name: Plooto

p.description: These examples use the search API to search the PLOS corpus of scientific articles. These examples are not intended to be a full explanation on the use of Solr. A full Solr query language explanation can be found here and a tutorial here. The construction of PLOS search queries deviates from the standard Solr query URL by using search instead of select when making request to the end point. The primary endpoint is http://api.plos.org/search and supports parameters such as q, fl, wt, start, and rows for querying the PLOS Solr index.
p.name: PLOS

p.description: Automotive and property data API. The published surface covers US VIN histories and vehicle specifications, UK MOT records, auto parts fitment catalogues, vehicle valuations, and property listings for the UK and US markets, served as typed JSON over a single REST endpoint. Positioned for AI agents and for developers who would otherwise integrate several gated data sources separately. The product is real and live; what is not public is the interface — documentation, the API reference and key issuance all sit behind an account sign-in, and the machine-readable artifacts the site advertises are not currently served.
p.name: PlotAPI

p.description: PlotBox is a deathcare management platform for cemeteries, crematories, and funeral homes. Founded in Northern Ireland, its cloud SaaS combines records management, interactive digital cemetery mapping, financial and trust-fund management, work orders, scheduling, and family-facing records portals to help deathcare providers run compliant, efficient operations. PlotBox serves over 2,000 facilities globally, is hosted on Microsoft Azure, and holds ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.
p.name: PlotBox

p.description: Plotlogic is a mining technology company that builds AI-driven sensing systems for real-time ore and material characterisation. Its flagship product, OreSense, scans rock in open-pit, stockpile, and underground mining operations and delivers decision-ready quantitative mineralogy in under 15 minutes, compared with more than an hour for traditional laboratory assay methods. The hardware is engineered for harsh mining environments and integrates into existing operational workflows so mines can reduce waste, improve grade control, and make faster material-routing decisions. Plotlogic is headquartered in Zillmere, Queensland, Australia, and is backed by the deep-tech venture firm DCVC. Customer access is delivered through an enterprise client platform rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer program, SDK, or API documentation at this time.
p.name: Plotlogic

p.description: Plotly is a Montreal-based data visualization and analytics company behind the open-source Plotly graphing libraries (plotly.js, plotly.py, Plotly.R, Plotly.NET, plotly.rs, Dash.jl) and the Dash framework for building interactive analytical web applications in Python. Its commercial products are Plotly Studio, an AI-native desktop application that generates Dash data apps from a dataset; Plotly Cloud, the hosted publishing and sharing platform for Dash and Studio apps; and Dash Enterprise, the self-hosted data app platform used by financial services, healthcare and life sciences, energy, and retail organizations. Plotly's machine-readable surfaces are a remote Dash Docs MCP server, an OAuth 2.1/OIDC authorization server for Plotly Cloud, and a first-party GraphQL management API for Dash Enterprise. The legacy Chart Studio Cloud REST API was retired on 2025-10-31.
p.name: Plotly

p.description: Ploy is an AI-powered web marketing automation platform that turns a company's marketing website into a growth channel. Founded in 2025 by former Webflow CTO Bryant Chou, backed by Y Combinator and First Round Capital ($27M), Ploy runs AI agents that build and optimize Astro/Tailwind marketing sites, write copy, run technical SEO and answer-engine optimization, identify visiting companies without cookies, launch ad campaigns, and execute reusable multi-step workflows called Ploybooks. Its programmable surface is deliberately CLI-first rather than REST-first: Ploy publishes no OpenAPI and no public API reference, but it does ship a standalone `ploy` CLI binary (workspaces, sites, publishing, variables and secrets, documents, Ploybooks, databases, Code Sync, and design-system inspection) authenticated by workspace-scoped API tokens for headless CI and remote coding agents, an installable Agent Skills catalog (`ploy skills init`), and one public HTTP endpoint — an authenticated inbound webhook ingest at /api/v1/webhook/{endpointSlug} that stores arbitrary JSON and triggers a Ploybook.
p.name: Ploy

p.description: Pluang is an Indonesian multi-asset investment and trading platform that lets retail users invest across a single app in US stocks and ETFs (fractional from $1), Indonesian stocks, cryptocurrencies with staking, mutual funds (Reksa Dana), physical gold and silver, options, and leveraged crypto futures. Features include Auto Invest dollar-cost averaging, the Pocket portfolio bundling tool, TradingView-powered charting, USD yield products, and the Aura AI recommendation assistant. Pluang operates under OJK and Bappebti regulatory oversight across its subsidiaries and reports 12M+ users. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface. Surfaced as an accel portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
p.name: Pluang

p.description: PlugShare provides the most comprehensive map of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations worldwide. Users can find, filter, and navigate to charging locations, read reviews, see photos, and get real-time availability where supported. The platform also offers an embed map, permalinking, and API access for developers to integrate charging data into apps, services, and navigation solutions. PlugShare supports community contributions, charging tips, and detailed station information, helping EV drivers plan trips and locate reliable charging infrastructure.
p.name: PlugShare

p.description: Plugsurfing provides a seamless EV charging experience across Europe, offering drivers access to a large network of charging stations through its mobile app and white‑label solutions for businesses. The platform supports roaming via the OCPI 2.2.1 protocol, enabling operators to connect to the Plugsurfing network with real‑time charger data, tariffs, and availability. It also offers APIs for developers to embed charging functionality into apps, in‑car navigation, and other digital services, fostering a more integrated electric mobility ecosystem.
p.name: Plugsurfing

p.description: Plum is a UK-based personal finance "money app" that helps consumers save and invest automatically. Its mobile app pairs automated savings algorithms (eight saving automations) with a range of regulated products including Easy Access Savings, a Cash ISA, a 95-day Notice Account, a money-market Interest pocket, a Stocks & Shares ISA, a Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP), and access to thousands of stocks and funds. Plum operates under FCA oversight through multiple entities covering payment services, e-money, investment broking, and account information services, and monetizes via subscription tiers (Basic, Plus, Boost, Max). It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
p.name: Plum

p.description: Pluma is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pluma

p.description: Plume Design, Inc. is a SaaS platform for internet service providers, delivering managed WiFi, network intelligence, and cyber-security services to ISP subscribers at global scale. Its product suite includes Haystack (network intelligence and observability), Plume Home (residential WiFi and cyber protection), WorkPass (small-business connectivity), Uprise (multi-dwelling-unit WiFi management), and Sweepr (AI-orchestrated ISP customer support). Plume is the primary sponsor of OpenSync, an open-source software-defined-networking framework for CPE and consumer networking devices that exposes northbound cloud APIs. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.
p.name: Plume

p.description: Plume Health (Plume) is a telehealth company delivering gender-affirming care to transgender and gender non-conforming people across the United States. Through a mobile app and licensed clinicians, Plume provides gender-affirming hormone therapy (estrogen and testosterone), mental health support, medical letters for surgery and identification changes, and everyday clinical care, all on a monthly membership subscription. Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, Plume operates as a HIPAA-covered, LegitScript-certified consumer healthcare provider. It is a consumer-facing care service and does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.
p.name: Plume Health

p.description: Plumerai builds AI software for intelligent cameras that pairs tiny on-device edge AI models with cloud Vision Language Models (VLMs). Its Video Intelligence products cover detection of people, vehicles, animals and packages, Familiar Face Identification, cross-camera Re-Identification, noise-robust motion detection, VLM-based video search, and custom AI notifications. The Plumerai Inference Engine is a deep-learning model compiler and runtime optimized for CPU inference on Arm Cortex-M / Cortex-A, RISC-V and x86_64. Plumerai integrates via SDKs (C++, C, Python, Rust, Java) rather than a hosted REST API, with the same unified API running from microcontrollers to servers. Plumerai also maintains the open-source Larq ecosystem for training and running Binarized Neural Networks.
p.name: Plumerai

p.description: Plumery is an Amsterdam, Netherlands-based fintech that provides a headless, mobile-first digital banking engagement platform it markets as the "Digital Success Fabric" — a "Digital Engagement Platform for Banks." It lets banks, credit unions, and financial institutions build and launch branded mobile and web banking experiences on top of their existing core banking systems, delivered to engineering teams as an API-first, composable platform with SDKs and developer documentation (built on the Stainless docs/SDK toolchain). Plumery maintains a public GitHub organization of supporting engineering tooling and publishes a security & compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001). The company is backed by QED Investors and Seedcamp.
p.name: Plumery

p.description: Plumma SRL is an Italian software house (VAT IT04209450362, REA MO-451932) with its registered office at Via Corsini 21, Fellicarolo, Fanano (Modena) and an operational office at Via Provinciale 175/B, Crespellano, Valsamoggia (Bologna). Its own product, Plumma Connect, is an aggregation gateway in front of mobile network operators: it sells enterprises a single integration point for the operator-held identity, SIM and network-state signals that the GSMA Open Gateway programme exposes, instead of requiring the buyer to onboard operator-by-operator and country-by-country. Plumma states it is a GSMA Open Gateway channel partner and names GSMA, TIM, AWS and WaveMaker among its partners. Its architectural position is the notable part, and it is deliberate. Rather than mirroring the CAMARA one-endpoint-per-capability shape, Plumma Connect publishes a SINGLE OpenAPI 3.1 operation — POST /api on https://connect.plumma.it/services — that takes a phone number in E.164 form plus a list of named commands (sim_swap, kyc_match, age_verification, current_carrier, porting_logs, roaming_intel, churn_tracker, digital_footprint and others), so the CAMARA surface is an implementation detail behind an abstraction layer rather than the developer contract. The company is not, however, standard-averse underneath: its KYC request schema carries the CAMARA KnowYourCustomer Match attribute vocabulary verbatim (in snake_case), and every 4xx/5xx returns an RFC 7807 problem document with a correlation_id. The divergence is at the endpoint shape, not the data model. The product is positioned for fraud prevention and identity verification, with company-stated coverage of 17 live countries across Europe, the Americas, APAC and Africa and 75+ network connections. Documentation, the OpenAPI and a draft-07 request schema are public and ungated, and the JavaScript documentation portal is backed by an unauthenticated JSON content API at connect.ploomma.com that serves 72 documents including the billing guide, SLA, terms and full command reference. Billing is EUR 200/month plus a prepaid wallet charged per served command; published rate limits are 2/5 RPS and 180 commands/day. There is no MCP server, no agent card, no SDKs and no /.well-known documents — the provider marks SDKs and webhooks 'under construction'.
p.name: Plumma

p.description: Plunk is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) email platform for developers that unifies transactional email, marketing campaigns, contact segmentation and event-driven workflow automation behind a single REST API. It publishes its own OpenAPI 3.1.0 at docs.useplunk.com/openapi.json, declaring next-api.useplunk.com as the production base URL, and authenticates with a two-class Bearer API key where the prefix decides capability — sk_ for every endpoint and pk_ for the client-safe /v1/track tracking call. The API supports Idempotency-Key on both public write endpoints, cursor pagination, a structured error envelope carrying machine codes plus remediation hints, and a documented webhook event catalogue delivered as workflow steps. Every documentation page is also served as Markdown. The entire stack self-hosts with Docker Compose for full data ownership and no per-email costs.
p.name: Plunk

p.description: Plural is an AI platform built for private markets professionals across private debt, private equity, and banking. Its AI agents ingest and analyze complex financial documents and data-room sources (documents, SharePoint, data rooms) to generate auditable, fully-referenced outputs — deal screeners, investment committee (IC) memos, term-sheet drafts, portfolio reports, and compliance documentation. Plural emphasizes EU data residency, end-to-end encryption, ISO 27001-aligned controls, and GDPR/DORA readiness, with no training on customer data. The company is backed by Speedinvest, Creative Destruction Lab, AI SEED, Innovate UK, and the European Commission. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published; the product references MCP and agent integrations for private-markets workflows.
p.name: Plural Ai

p.description: Plural Finance is a financial operating system for infrastructure — a programmable execution layer that automates ownership, payments, compliance, and reporting across the lifecycle of infrastructure and energy assets. Its AssetOS platform tokenizes infrastructure assets such as distributed renewables, data centers, public-private partnerships, and electricity sales contracts, so institutional and individual investors can underwrite, monitor, and trade projects, with smart-contract execution of capital contributions and distributions and embedded regulatory controls. The company holds broker-dealer licensing and is backed by Paradigm. Plural currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is through its institutional web application.
p.name: Plural Finance

p.description: Pluralis Research is a decentralized AI lab pioneering Protocol Learning, a third path between closed proprietary models and open-weight models in which large transformer models are collaboratively pre-trained across many low-bandwidth, geographically distributed consumer GPUs without any single participant holding the full model weights. Its work spans communication-efficient model parallelism, asynchronous pipeline-parallel optimization, and community-owned training runs (Agora, node0), published as research papers at NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR and as open-source libraries. Pluralis is backed by Union Square Ventures. It exposes research libraries, a participation CLI, and live run dashboards rather than a conventional REST/GraphQL developer API.
p.name: Pluralis

p.description: APIs for the Pluralsight technology skills and engineering intelligence platform, providing access to courses, learning paths, assessments, user progress, channels, teams, and engineering metrics via GraphQL and REST APIs.
p.name: Pluralsight

p.description: Pluribus Networks was a software-defined networking (SDN) and open-networking vendor known for its NetVisor ONE network operating system (NVOS), the Adaptive Cloud Fabric controllerless SDN fabric, the UNUM management/analytics platform, and the Freedom 9000 series switches. The company was acquired by Arista Networks in 2022; the pluribusnetworks.com domain now redirects to Arista's Pluribus support resources, and the core Pluribus product line (NVOS, UNUM, Freedom 9000) has since been moved to End-of-Sale / End-of-Life. No independent Pluribus developer portal, public REST API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK is published; support and technical documentation are provided through the Arista customer portal. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Menlo Ventures.
p.name: Pluribus Networks

p.description: Pluro is India's fertility and IVF platform, built as a co-creation model with doctors for patients. It delivers personalised, evidence-based reproductive care through a growing network of 15+ clinics across India, combining advanced clinical science, AI-assisted embryology, standardised treatment protocols, and transparent pricing. Founded by Dr. Bhaskar Shah, Dr. Jaydeep Tank, and Dr. Parikshit Tank, Pluro raised a Rs 125 crore Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners in 2025. It offers IVF/ICSI, IUI, ovulation induction, and a range of diagnostic and surgical fertility treatments. Pluro publishes an llms.txt for AI agents but exposes no public developer API.
p.name: Pluro

p.description: Plus (PlusAI) develops AI-based autonomous driving technology for commercial trucks. Its flagship SuperDrive is an AI-powered Level 4 autonomous driving system, and HyperFoundry is an integrated development platform for Physical AI. Plus works through partnerships with truck OEMs including TRATON GROUP, Hyundai, and IVECO rather than shipping a public developer API. Backed by GGV Capital, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed it exposes no public API, SDK, or developer portal surface, and captured its domain-security posture.
p.name: Plus

p.description: Plus One Robotics is a San Antonio, Texas warehouse-automation company founded in 2016 by Erik Nieves and Shaun Edwards that builds AI-powered computer-vision software and robotic work cells for parcel handling, depalletizing, palletizing and induction. Its PickOne perception system tells a robot arm how to grasp each item and verifies placement, while Yonder provides supervised autonomy — remote human "Crew Chiefs" who take over when the robot hits an exception. Packaged work cells DepalOne and InductOne wrap that stack in deployable hardware. The company reports more than 1.5 billion lifetime picks across robots fielded in 15 countries, with additional offices in Eindhoven (Netherlands) and Boulder, Colorado. Plus One Robotics publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; product integration is handled through its partner channel and a login-gated partner portal.
p.name: Plus One Robotics

p.description: +Simple (Plus Simple) is a French digital insurance underwriting agency (agence de souscription) founded in 2015 and headquartered in Marseille. Operating as one of France's largest wholesale insurance brokers, it runs a fully digital extranet platform that lets partner insurance brokers prospect, price, underwrite, issue, and manage professional insurance contracts across more than 1,200 covered activities and 30+ niche product lines, including RC Décennale (ten-year construction liability) coverage. +Simple distributes on a 100% brokerage model in partnership with carriers such as Hiscox, Allianz, Wakam, QBE and Beazley, serving a network of 8,000+ partner brokers. The company is backed by Anthemis and Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; it publishes no public API or developer surface at this time (its broker and insured portals are authenticated web applications, not open APIs).
p.name: Plus Simple

p.description: PlusDental was a Berlin-based direct-to-consumer orthodontic company offering clear dental aligners ("Zahnschiene") for teeth straightening, backed by HV Capital. The brand has since been migrated to DR SMILE (operated by Sunshine Smile GmbH); plusdental.com now serves a handover notice redirecting customers to DR SMILE customer service. This is a consumer healthcare service with no public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical integration surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline confirmed no API artifacts exist.
p.name: PlusDental

p.description: Plusgrade provides ancillary revenue solutions for the travel industry, helping airlines, hotels, cruise lines, and rail operators increase revenue through flexible upgrade and add‑on offers. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Montreal, the company operates globally with offices in Toronto, New York, London, Dubai, Tel Aviv, and Singapore. Plusgrade’s platform enables travelers to customize their experience while delivering measurable incremental revenue for partners, serving over 250 companies worldwide.
p.name: Plusgrade

p.description: Plush is an AI-powered fashion discovery and shopping platform at plush.shop that lets shoppers describe what they want in natural language and returns curated results from trusted and emerging brands. Rather than rigid keyword search, Plush matches on mood, aesthetic, and intent, layering image search, smart real-time filters, influencer edit collections, and wishlists on top of its proprietary AI curation. Founded by Chang Liu (CEO) and Ying Zhu (CTO) — who met through Y Combinator's co-founder matching — Plush is backed by the Anthemis Female Innovators Lab Fund and the Oxford Seed Fund. It is a consumer-facing web application; no public developer API is published at this time.
p.name: Plush

p.description: PlushCare is a direct-to-consumer telehealth and virtual primary care service that connects patients with board-certified physicians for online doctor visits, available 24/7 across all 50 US states. Services include online prescriptions and refills, urgent care video visits, mental health care and therapy, weight-loss management including GLP-1 medications, chronic disease management, pediatric and preventive care, and sexual health. Founded in 2014 in San Francisco by Dr. James Wantuck and Ryan McQuaid, PlushCare accepts most major insurance and sells a $19.99/month patient membership. Ownership has changed three times: Accolade acquired PlushCare in 2021, Transcarent acquired Accolade in 2025, and effective 2026-07-31 PlushCare, Inc. became a subsidiary of Fabric Labs, Inc. As a consumer telehealth service, PlushCare publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API reference, SDK, MCP server or agent card; its one live API host, api.plushcare.com, is the patient app's own private Django REST Framework backend and returns 403 anonymously. This profile captures its public web, pricing, compliance and domain-security surface.
p.name: PlushCare

p.description: pluslife is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: pluslife

p.description: PlusMargin (Plus Margin) is a Bangkok, Thailand based digital marketing and business consulting practice operating under the tagline "Connect | Engage | Convert." The firm focuses on inbound marketing strategy, personalized and AI-assisted marketing, buyer-persona development, and customer-journey mapping for its clients, and publishes Thai-language editorial content across marketing, business, advertising, technology, learning, insurance, and lifestyle topics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global — where secondary sources describe an earlier Singapore-founded "predictive persuasion" e-commerce personalization product — but the domain today serves a four-page consulting and content site with no trace of that platform. Enrichment on 2026-08-12 confirmed no product API, no developer portal, no SDKs on any package registry, no /.well-known/ discovery surface, no llms.txt and no agent card. The one callable, machine-readable surface is the stock WordPress REST API the marketing site exposes at /wp-json — 237 routes across 11 namespaces, anonymously readable for content — which is WordPress core's API rather than a product PlusMargin designed, documents, or supports.
p.name: PlusMargin

p.description: PlusThis is an Arizona-based marketing automation add-on company, founded in 2011, that sells a toolkit of roughly seventy no-code "tools" which bolt extra behaviour onto a CRM a business already runs — Keap (Infusionsoft), ActiveCampaign, Ontraport, HubSpot, Drip and HighLevel (GHL). The tools cover action links and smart links, countdown and evergreen-date scarcity, webinar and meeting connections (Zoom, GoToWebinar, WebinarJam, EverWebinar), scheduling connections (Calendly, Acuity), SMS sequences, field math and text formatting, contact validation and deduplication, Google Sheets and Drive export, Slack and DocuSign connections, and a Webhook Catcher that writes inbound third-party webhook payloads onto a CRM contact record. PlusThis is metered commercially on Active Tools and monthly Tool Runs rather than API calls, and it publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no client SDKs — it is a consumer of other vendors' APIs rather than a producer of one.
p.name: PlusThis

p.description: Pluto (Pluto Health, trypluto.com now pluto.health) is an AI-powered clinical intelligence and care-delivery platform that unifies fragmented health data from roughly 90% of US health systems. It aggregates medical records, insurance data, and social determinants of health, then applies AI-driven clinical intelligence to surface care gaps, coordinate preventive care, screenings, vaccines and at-home lab testing, and match patients to clinical trials. Pluto offers turnkey, white-label, or API-based deployment of its clinical operations. It is backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation.
p.name: Pluto

p.description: Pluto AI is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pluto AI

p.description: Pluto (Plutopillow) is a Los Angeles-based direct-to-consumer sleep wellness brand best known for the Pluto Pillow, a made-to-order pillow custom-built around each customer's unique sleep profile via an online sleep quiz. The company also sells the PUFF body pillow, the POD travel pillow, and temperature-regulating bedding, and offers a 125-night risk-free trial with free shipping and returns. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Pluto is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or partner-integration surface at this time; this profile captures its public web properties for discovery.
p.name: Pluto Brand

p.description: Pluto Mobility is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: mobility. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pluto Mobility

p.description: Pluton Biosciences is a microbial discovery company that uses a proprietary Discovery Platform - high-throughput soil microbiome screening combined with computational analysis - to find naturally occurring microbial consortia for agriculture and carbon sequestration. Its lead product is a Biological Nitrogen System: photosynthetic microbial consortia that operate at the soil surface to fix atmospheric nitrogen and mobilize phosphorus. Pluton is a research-and-product company, not an API company; it has no public developer portal. Partnership and licensing inquiries are handled directly.
p.name: Pluton Biosciences

p.description: Plutus Labs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Plutus Labs

p.description: Plyrium is a contractor operating system for home-service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing) built in Coolidge, Arizona - AI phone answering, scheduling, quotes, invoicing with Stripe payments and Google Business Profile automation. Its public API surface is VouchSpec, an agent-only service on vouchspec.plyrium.com that sells fresh static validation and Ed25519-signed DSSE evidence for one exact public GitHub Agent Skill commit, paid per request in USDC over x402 on Base, and discoverable through an OpenAPI 3.1 contract, llms.txt, an A2A agent card, a remote MCP server, an installable Agent Skill and an ARD ai-catalog.
p.name: Plyrium

p.name: Pmcs

p.description: PNC Financial Services Group is a Pittsburgh-based money-center bank and Fortune 500 diversified financial services company offering retail banking, corporate and institutional banking, treasury management, asset management, and residential mortgage banking across the United States. PNC operates a real first-party developer portal at developer.pnc.com ("PNC Developer Tools: Open APIs for Banking & Payments") that publishes a catalog of treasury and payments API products — including Account Verification Services, ePayments, Real-Time Payments (RTP), Direct-to-Debit-Card (push-to-card) disbursement, and information reporting — surfaced through its PINACLE commercial banking platform and PINACLE Connect embedded-banking integrations. Full API reference documentation, sandbox/testing environments, and call codes are gated behind credentialed onboarding arranged through a PNC Relationship Manager or Treasury Management Officer; no OpenAPI/Swagger specifications are publicly downloadable. On the consumer open-finance side, PNC exposes account data through an Akoya-provided tokenized data-access API and signed a bilateral data-access agreement with Plaid in September 2024, positioning PNC ahead of CFPB Section 1033 personal-financial-data-rights requirements.
p.name: PNC

p.description: pnpm is a fast, disk space efficient package manager for JavaScript and Node.js projects. It uses a content-addressable store and a strict, symlinked node_modules layout so every version of every package is stored exactly once on disk and projects can only access dependencies they explicitly declare. pnpm provides first-class monorepo support via pnpm-workspace.yaml, the workspace protocol, Catalogs, package filtering, and a shared lockfile, and ships supply-chain safety features such as minimumReleaseAge, opt-in lifecycle scripts, dependency overrides, and a built-in patch workflow. Developed in the open under the MIT license on GitHub with an Open Collective sponsorship model, pnpm is used by major JavaScript projects including Next.js, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, Material UI, Prisma, Astro, and SvelteKit.
p.name: pnpm

p.description: Pocket Communications Northeast is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pocket Communications Northeast

p.description: Pocket FM is an audio entertainment platform offering long-form audio series, audiobooks, and serialized stories across genres such as romance, fantasy, thriller, and horror. Listeners stream free episodes and unlock premium content through an in-app coins/store model, while writers and voice creators publish original work through the Pocket FM Studio. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass, Pocket FM operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web product and does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.
p.name: Pocket Fm

p.description: Pocket Gems is a San Francisco mobile games and interactive entertainment studio founded in 2009, employing over 200 people and backed by Sequoia Capital and Tencent. It builds and operates the Episode interactive-storytelling network, Episode XOXO, and the 3D real-time strategy title War Dragons on its proprietary mobile-first Mantis Engine, with products downloaded more than 325 million times. Pocket Gems ships consumer mobile applications rather than a developer-facing API program: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification. Its public developer surface is a GitHub organization and four first-party Apache-2.0 Node.js libraries published to npm under the @pocketgems scope (the internal "Todea" service stack), plus an Episode Writer's Portal used by story authors.
p.name: Pocket Gems

p.description: Pocket Menu (Pocket Concierge / ポケットコンシェルジュ) is a Japanese fine-dining restaurant reservation and payment service that curates high-quality restaurants and lets diners book and pay for reservations online. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The public surface is a consumer web application (Ruby on Rails / React on Rails) at pocket-concierge.jp with no published developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or .well-known discovery documents detected during enrichment.
p.name: Pocket Menu

p.description: Pocket Network is the decentralized RPC layer of Web3 — a permissionless, fully open data delivery protocol built on Cosmos SDK and CometBFT (the Shannon upgrade, June 2025). 5,000+ independent supplier nodes serve relays across 60-69+ blockchains, metered in compute units at $1/billion and settled on-chain in POKT under deflationary tokenomics (PIP-41, 97.5% mint ratio). Grove (grove.city) is the for-profit infrastructure company that operates the largest gateway on the network — rpc.grove.city — and maintains PATH, the open-source Go gateway any operator can run to expose Pocket Network as a single HTTP endpoint. Grove offers free no-API-key per-IP public endpoints per chain (eth.rpc.grove.city, solana.rpc.grove.city, etc.) plus paid portal applications with relay analytics and SLAs. Together they form the canonical decentralized alternative to Alchemy / Infura / QuickNode for serving JSON-RPC, REST, and WebSocket traffic to any public blockchain.
p.name: Pocket Network

p.description: Pocket Network is a decentralized, permissionless RPC infrastructure network providing free public API access to 60+ blockchain chains including Ethereum, Avalanche, Polygon, Solana, and other EVM-compatible and non-EVM networks. The Shannon upgrade (June 2025) made Pocket the first open, permissionless API network where anyone can stake POKT tokens to deploy gateways and supply nodes without centralized approval.
p.name: Pocket Network

p.description: Pocket Protector is a consumer peer-to-peer trading application operated by Pocket Protector Inc. Under the tagline "Trade Better Together," it lets users trade items and assets with one another through an iOS app and an accompanying Telegram bot (@pocketprotectorbot). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Electric Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes a marketing site with privacy and terms pages but no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or OpenAPI surface.
p.name: Pocket Protector

p.description: PocketBase is an open-source backend-as-a-service delivered as a single executable, providing a REST API for managing collections, records, authentication, file uploads, real-time subscriptions via Server-Sent Events, and admin management through a built-in dashboard. It embeds SQLite for persistent storage and supports OAuth2, OTP, and password-based authentication out of the box. Developers can extend PocketBase with custom business logic using Go or JavaScript hooks and event handlers. Official SDKs for JavaScript and Dart make client integration straightforward across web, mobile, and desktop platforms.
p.name: PocketBase

p.description: PocketHealth is a patient-centric medical imaging platform that lets patients access, view, store, and share their diagnostic imaging (DICOM) and reports online, and lets healthcare providers exchange imaging across institutions and networks. PocketHealth also publishes an open, RESTful developer API aimed at RIS/PACS/VNA vendors, letting them embed PocketHealth's patient enrollment, electronic consent, and background record-delivery workflows natively into their own clinical software. The developer API is partner-gated - it is free forever for RIS/PACS vendors, healthcare providers, and physicians, but the full technical reference (base URL, endpoint paths, authentication) is not published on the open web; engaged vendors are assigned a dedicated integration rep who provides testing resources and detailed documentation. As a result the APIs below are modeled from PocketHealth's public developer-program descriptions rather than a public API reference or OpenAPI definition.
p.name: PocketHealth

p.description: Pocus is an AI sales intelligence and product-led sales platform that turns product usage, CRM and third-party buying signals into prioritized action for revenue teams. It ingests data from customer data warehouses (Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, Athena, Databricks) and CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), scores and enriches accounts and contacts, and surfaces recommendations to reps through an Intelligent Inbox, Playbooks, Lists, SmartMap and a Chrome extension, with write-back and sequencing into Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo, Gong and Slack. Its programmable surface is a GraphQL core API at api.pocus.com, an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server at auth.pocus.com, SCIM 2.0 user provisioning and SAML SSO, plus a Snowflake data share for warehouse-native delivery. Pocus was acquired by Apollo.io, announced 2026-03-19.
p.name: Pocus

p.description: Pod Point — trading as Pod since its February 2026 rebrand, with pod-point.com now 301-redirecting to podenergy.com — is a British electric vehicle charging company founded in London in 2009 and wholly owned by EDF since its delisting from the London Stock Exchange in August 2025. It sells and installs home, workplace and fleet chargers, operates the third-largest public charging network in the United Kingdom across Tesco and Lidl car parks, and acquired depot-charging specialist EO Charging in May 2026. It sits on the demand side of the UK electricity value chain, between the driver and the electricity supplier, as a Charge Point Operator rather than a metering, network or settlement body. Its API posture is narrow but real and honestly split: there is no developer portal, no OpenAPI, no Swagger and no consumer data API, yet a live OCPI 2.2.1 Charge Point Operator service runs at ocpi.podenergy.com whose version negotiation answers anonymously and enumerates a full module set, while every data module — locations, tariffs, sessions, CDRs — returns 401 Unauthorized without a bilaterally exchanged OCPI credentials token. Britain's Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 name OCPI 2.2.1 as the vehicle for open charge point data; the plumbing that regulation names is verifiably in place at Pod, but the open part of it is not obtainable anonymously from outside, and the company publishes no open data page, no OCPI token policy and no developer onboarding of any kind.
p.name: Pod Point

p.description: Podbean is a podcast hosting, distribution, and monetization platform for creators, businesses, and networks. Its public REST API (base https://api.podbean.com/v1) uses OAuth 2.0 and lets third-party apps and integrations manage a user's podcast programmatically - read podcast profiles, list and publish/update/delete episodes, authorize media file uploads, embed players via oEmbed, and pull download, engagement, and advertising analytics reports. Apps can act on behalf of a single podcast (Client Credentials) or across many podcasts (Multiple Podcasts tokens) for agencies and networks.
p.name: Podbean

p.description: An API for developers to get information on over 4 million podcasts, 180 million episodes, and 1.5 million transcripts. Powered by Taddy's GraphQL API, the Podcast API supports search across podcast series, episode details, transcripts, top charts, popularity data, and webhook subscriptions.
p.name: Podcast API

p.description: The Podcast Index (Podcast Index LLC) is a software developer focused partnership that provides tools and data to anyone who aspires to create new and exciting Podcast experiences without the heavy lifting of indexing, aggregation and data management.
p.name: PodcastIndex

p.description: Podcastle is an AI audio and podcast creation platform whose developer engine, Async, exposes a low-latency Voice API for human-like text-to-speech, a browsable voice library, and instant voice cloning from a short audio sample. The API is served from https://api.async.com and authenticated with an x-api-key header plus a version header. Transcription is a Podcastle platform feature; no standalone transcription endpoint is documented in the public Voice API.
p.name: Podcastle

p.description: Podcastpage.io was a podcast website builder that provided programmatic access for managing podcast websites and content. The product is now operating under the Beamly brand (beamly.com) following a rebrand. As of this entry the service does not publish a public OpenAPI specification or open developer documentation, and integration support is provided through customer support and Help Center articles.
p.name: Podcastpage

p.description: Podchaser provides one of the most comprehensive podcast databases, exposed through a GraphQL API designed to drive podcast discovery for listeners, podcasters, brands, and platform partners. The API surface is GraphQL-only and is therefore not represented as an OpenAPI specification in this index.
p.name: Podchaser

p.description: Podcorn is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Podcorn

p.description: Podfund provides startup and growth capital to podcast creators and audio-driven media companies, typically investing $25,000 to $150,000 based on stage, track record, traction, and revenue. Operated by TechNexus Venture Collaborative, which has backed 600+ startups since 2007, Podfund pairs funding with business planning, a peer community, mentor matching, a growth toolkit, and partner offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network. Podfund publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web presence for network discovery.
p.name: Podfund

p.description: Podia is an all-in-one creator platform for selling online courses, digital downloads, coaching, webinars, and memberships, with a website builder, blog, communities, and built-in email marketing. As of this review, Podia does NOT offer a public or partner developer API and does not expose webhooks. The company's own help center states plainly that "Podia does not offer a public API or webhooks," and directs builders to Zapier as the only supported integration path. The logical resources below (products, customers/audience, community, and sales) are therefore documented as endpointsModeled - they reflect the objects and events Podia surfaces through its Zapier app, not a first-party REST API. There is no published base URL, authentication scheme, or OpenAPI description to catalog. What Podia does publish, and what this profile captures, is a real client-side surface: an Advanced JavaScript tracking API exposing Podia.Customer and Podia.Conversion objects plus three DOM CustomEvents on every storefront page, an embeddable email-capture form that POSTs to a per-creator subscriptions endpoint, and a 509-link llms.txt at help.podia.com that renders every help article as markdown. Podia also runs a public Atlassian status page and a Beamer changelog, and allows GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot in robots.txt - the missing agent surface here is a missing API product, not an anti-AI posture.
p.name: Podia

p.description: Podio is a flexible work management and collaboration platform (originally acquired by Citrix in 2012, and now part of Progress Software following the October 2024 acquisition of ShareFile and Podio) that lets teams build custom apps, workspaces, and workflows for project management, CRM, and internal operations. The Podio API offers a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality including apps, items, tasks, workspaces, users, files, and webhooks, with official client libraries available for PHP, .NET, Ruby, Java, Python, Android, and Objective-C.
p.name: Podio

p.description: Podium is a customer communication platform providing a REST API for local businesses to manage text-based conversations, reviews, payment requests, lead capture forms, webchat, and AI-driven lead conversion. The API is organized around REST with predictable resource-oriented URLs, JSON-encoded responses, and OAuth 2.0 authentication.
p.name: Podium

p.description: Podium Education is an Austin, Texas experiential-learning and career platform founded in 2018 that partners with colleges, universities and employers to close the college-to-career gap. Its flagship program, The Global Career Accelerator, is a credit-bearing, financial-aid and Pell-eligible online field experience in which undergraduates work on real brand projects in data analytics, web development, digital marketing and tech operations alongside peers in other countries, earning certificates and minors through their own institution. Podium delivers the program on its own platform stack — a hosted Canvas LMS estate and a student application at globalcareeraccelerator.org — sold to universities as a partnership rather than as software, and it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.
p.name: Podium Education

p.description: Podman is a daemonless, open-source container engine for developing, managing, and running OCI containers on Linux, supporting both rootful and rootless operation as a drop-in replacement for Docker. The Podman REST API exposes a Docker-compatible surface alongside Libpod-specific endpoints for pods, volumes, networks, secrets, generators, and system management.
p.name: Podman

p.description: Podqi is an AI-native intellectual property and brand protection platform that automatically detects and removes brand infringements across digital platforms. It scans major marketplaces, storefronts, and domains for counterfeit listings, stolen imagery, fake products, and copycat sites, then packages evidence and files takedowns at scale with minimal human intervention. The company reports roughly 95% AI automation with same-day detection and an average resolution time of about 1.2 days, and also operates Brandsweep.ai, a free public brand-protection scanning tool. Podqi serves brand owners, entertainment and creative companies, e-commerce sellers, and law firms. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Podqi publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.
p.name: Podqi

p.description: Podz is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Podz

p.description: Poetic is an enterprise AI automation company whose platform learns an organization's rules and procedures and then executes end-to-end business processes with high precision and compliance. Marketed as "turn your business into software," Poetic ingests procedures, training materials, and expert feedback to build self-healing automations that adapt when underlying systems change, targeting long, multi-step workflows such as fraud detection, KYC, and dispute resolution. The company emphasizes enterprise-grade security with zero data retention (processing data in-transit only) and states SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, and cites customers including AIG, SoFi, and Chime. Poetic is an early-stage, Kleiner Perkins-backed AI company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.
p.name: Poetic

p.description: PoetryDB is a public REST API providing programmatic access to a database of English-language poems.
