Developers can search the collection by author name, poem title, line content, and line count. The API requires no authentication or API key, returns JSON or plain text responses, and supports CORS. It is built on Ruby and Sinatra with a MongoDB datastore and is maintained as a free open-source resource for poets and developers.
p.name: PoetryDB

p.description: Poggio (Poggio Labs) is an AI revenue intelligence platform for enterprise sales teams — a "Revenue Superagent" that unlocks Salesforce investment by combining deep-research AI agents with a unified context engine connecting CRM, call recordings (Gong), documents, and real-time web intelligence to arm sellers with always-current account knowledge, prioritization, relationship maps, and automated account plans. Poggio exposes its intelligence programmatically through a versioned REST API (v2) and a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, both secured with OAuth 2.0 (authorization code, client credentials, refresh token) and dynamic client registration, plus native Slack, Salesforce/Agentforce, Highspot, and Gong integrations. Poggio Labs also ships Goalkeeper, an Apache-2.0 self-hosted "durable goals" service for teams of people and AI agents, with its own OpenAPI 3.1 REST API and a stateless Streamable HTTP MCP server distributed as container images. Backed by Accel.
p.name: Poggio Labs

p.description: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) is a private research university in Pohang, North Gyeongsang, South Korea, founded in 1986 by the steelmaker POSCO and consistently ranked inside the QS world top 100. POSTECH operates no developer portal, no open-data program and no API it authored itself — but it is not empty, and three genuinely institution-operated machine-readable surfaces were verified live on 2026-08-30, all of them on POSTECH's own network (141.223.0.0/16). The OASIS institutional repository serves a fully anonymous OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting endpoint over a corpus of 106,805 records in twelve metadata formats across 163 sets, reaching back to 2014. POSTECH runs its own SAML 2.0 identity provider at idpass.postech.ac.kr, registered in the KAFE federation since 2017 and resolvable through eduGAIN, supporting the REFEDS Research and Scholarship entity category and asserting SIRTFI — machine-readable institutional infrastructure that almost nothing in this cohort catalogues. And POSTECH's LMS publishes a live, public LTI 1.3 Advantage platform keyset and OAuth 2.0 token endpoint, which most institution-hosted Moodles keep unreachable. Everything else is a login wall or someone else's platform: the PODIUM portal, admissions and certificate systems are gated; the DSpace REST interface sits behind a JavaScript bot challenge that returns 200 with a challenge shell; and the thesis pipeline runs through postech.dcollection.net, a tenancy on the KERIS-operated national dCollection platform, recorded here as a relationship rather than as POSTECH's engineering.
p.name: Pohang University of Science and Technology

p.description: Point (Point Digital Finance, Inc.) is a San Francisco fintech founded in 2015 by Eddie Lim, Eoin Matthews, and Alex Rampell that gives homeowners access to their home equity without monthly payments or income requirements. Its flagship Home Equity Investment (HEI) provides lump sums up to $600,000 in exchange for a share of a home's future appreciation over a 30-year term, alongside a HELOC product offering lines up to $750,000. Point has served more than 25,000 homeowners and facilitated over $2 billion in home equity investments, and is backed by a16z, Bloomberg Beta, and Ribbit Capital. Point is a consumer-facing platform with no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline (identity + domain-security probe only — no API surface found).
p.name: Point

p.description: Point Nine Capital is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Berlin, Germany. It is one of Europe's best-known seed investors, specializing in B2B SaaS, B2B marketplaces, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health, and increasingly AI across digital, physical, and biological domains. Point Nine typically writes initial checks of roughly $1M-$10M (EUR 0.5M-5M) and aims to be the first institutional investor for "v0.9" founders graduating from friends-and-family capital. The firm runs a deliberately small, equal partnership in which each partner works closely with only 6-8 companies at a time to provide deep operational support. Since inception it has backed more than 160 startups across 30+ countries, including early bets on Algolia, Chainalysis, Clio, Contentful, Delivery Hero, Docplanner, Factorial, Front, Loom, Mambu, NexHealth, Revolut, Typeform, Zendesk, and Westwing, with 11+ companies reaching unicorn status.
p.name: Point Nine Capital

p.description: Point One Navigation operates Polaris, a GNSS RTK corrections network delivering 1-3 cm (True RTK) and sub-10 cm (Virtual RTK) positioning across North America, Europe, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea, alongside FusionEngine, its GNSS/INS sensor-fusion positioning engine, and the Atlas and Standard Dev Kit hardware platforms. Developers reach the network three ways: a standards-based NTRIP interface that streams RTCM v3.2 MSM4 corrections to any compatible receiver, a native Polaris protocol with an API-key-to-bearer-token exchange, and a Personal Access Token-authenticated GraphQL platform API for device, tag, license, device-profile and reference station management with real-time subscriptions.
p.name: Point One Navigation

p.description: point.me is an award-travel company that operates a real-time award flight search engine for consumers and, through point.me Gateway, an API-first embedded loyalty-travel platform that banks and loyalty programs run inside their own branded apps. The consumer product searches award availability across 150+ airline and hotel loyalty programs on Basic/Standard/Premium annual subscriptions, and adds paid concierge booking. Gateway sells award search, point transfers and booking as an embedded integration to financial institutions (Amex among its named partners) and to loyalty programs. The API host api.point.me is live and identifies itself as "Flight Search APIs", but every path on it answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, and Gateway is sold through a demo form rather than a public developer portal, so no machine-readable contract is published.
p.name: POINT.ME

p.description: PointCheckout is a MENA-region payments and rewards platform, backed by 500 Global, that lets shoppers pay online with reward points and miles and lets merchants accept card and rewards payments. Its developer-facing Merchant API (powered by paymennt.com) exposes hosted web, payment-link, QR, and mobile checkouts, recurring subscriptions, merchant branches, and HMAC-signed webhooks. The API is RESTful JSON, versioned in the URI path (v2.0), secured with an API key and secret header pair, and ships with a separate test environment plus iOS/Android SDKs and e-commerce plugins for Magento 2, WooCommerce, OpenCart, and Shopify.
p.name: PointCheckout

p.description: PointClickCare is the leading cloud-based software platform for the senior care and post-acute care industry, providing electronic health records (EHR), care coordination, financial management, and clinical decision support to skilled nursing facilities, senior living communities, and home health agencies. PointClickCare publishes both a partner EHR API and a HL7 FHIR API for clinical interoperability across the long-term and post-acute care (LTPAC) ecosystem.
p.name: PointClickCare

p.description: Pointee is an agentic automation platform for enterprise business process automation, guiding organizations through the full automation journey from discovery to running AI at scale. Its Process Discovery maps how work actually runs to surface automation potential and ROI, Workflow Automation orchestrates people, bots, and AI agents in unified workflows, and Guardian Agents continuously monitor automation to detect quality drops, automate incident response, and prevent cost overruns and security threats. Pointee also offers a dedicated offering to maximize existing RPA investments. The product is operated by Pointee Interactive s.r.o. (Liberec, Czech Republic) and is a portfolio company of Earlybird; customers include KBC, Intel, Deloitte, AXA, Microsoft, and Mutual of Omaha.
p.name: Pointee

p.description: PointFive is the AI Efficiency Operating System for FinOps, platform, and engineering teams. It detects 500+ types of cloud, Kubernetes, and AI-infrastructure waste that traditional cost dashboards miss, then converts findings into auditable remediation — drafting pull requests and Jira tickets — and tracks realized savings back to actual budget impact. Marquee capabilities include DeepWaste Detection, DeepWaste for AI (model/GPU/data-platform spend), TokenShift (coding-agent token governance), and Agentic Remediation. Its public programmatic surface is an OAuth 2.1 Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings cost intelligence into AI tools like Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT. Surfaced as an Accel / Index Ventures portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
p.name: Pointfive

p.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.
p.name: Pointone

p.description: Point One Navigation provides precision location technology for autonomous systems and vehicles, delivering centimeter-level accuracy even in challenging environments. Its core offerings are the Polaris RTK/SSR corrections network — a globally distributed network of thousands of base stations across the US, UK, EU, Korea, Australia, New Zealand, and Japan with 99% uptime — and the FusionEngine sensor-fusion positioning software for dead reckoning where open-sky GNSS is unavailable. Developers integrate via a GraphQL API for workflow and data management, an NTRIP/RTCM corrections stream, and open-source FusionEngine and Polaris client libraries. Point One is a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures.
p.name: Pointonenav

p.description: Pointy was an Irish retail-technology startup (pointy.com), founded by Mark Cummins and Charles Bibby and backed by Seedcamp, that helped independent brick-and-mortar retailers put their in-store inventory online by connecting a simple barcode-scanning device or point-of-sale integration to a searchable online product page. Google acquired Pointy in 2020 and has since fully folded the product into Google's own tooling: pointy.com now redirects to Google Business Profile support, and the former Pointy app is now Google's Local Inventory app, which syncs in-store products to Google Search and Maps via POS systems such as Clover, Square, and Lightspeed. Pointy no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this API Evangelist profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record and historical marker rather than an active API provider.
p.name: Pointy

p.description: Poka is a manufacturing-focused connected worker platform that helps industrial and frontline teams standardize work execution across learning, daily management, and operations. It combines digital work instructions, on-the-job training, skills management, and factory-floor knowledge sharing with embedded Industrial AI. Poka exposes a RESTful Poka API for building integrations with third-party systems (MES, CMMS, LMS, QMS, ERP, BI), SCIM for automated user provisioning from identity providers, the Poka Automate iPaaS, and a Poka Data Lake for BI/reporting. Poka is part of IFS and runs regionally in the US, Canada, and EU.
p.name: Poka

p.description: Pokelabo (ポケラボ) is a Japanese mobile game development studio founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tokyo. Originally an independent social-game maker, it became a subsidiary of GREE and, as of January 1, 2025, was integrated into WFS (Wright Flyer Studios) under the GREE group. The studio develops and operates smartphone games built on licensed and original intellectual properties, including titles such as SINoALICE and Magia Exedra (Puella Magi Madoka Magica). Pokelabo is a consumer entertainment company and does not expose a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.
p.name: Pokelabo

p.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.
p.name: Poker Skill

p.description: Pokkt is a mobile-first advertising and app monetization platform, part of AnyMind Group, serving app publishers and game developers with SDK-based ad monetization (rewarded video, interstitial, and video advertising) and serving advertisers with performance campaigns, remarketing, and connected-TV (CTV) inventory across India, Southeast Asia, and MENA. Its public API surface is entirely ad-tech: a supply-side Ad Server API at vdo.pokkt.com serving JSON, HTML and VAST responses, a mobile-web rewarded video surface, a server-to-server rewarded-video gratification callback, and a demand-side OpenRTB 2.5/2.6 bid endpoint with global, APAC and US regional hosts. Pokkt publishes an llms.txt-indexed developer wiki and an IAB Tech Lab sellers.json, but no OpenAPI, no OAuth, and no public pricing; the console GraphQL API at api.pokkt.com is authentication-gated and its client SDKs have not been republished since October 2021.
p.name: Pokkt

p.description: Poko was a Singapore-based fintech that built a fiat-to-crypto on-ramp aggregator for Web3 businesses — wallets, wallet-as-a-service providers, marketplaces, dApps, and games. Its product connected 100+ local and international payment methods with local KYC and smart routing so global users could buy crypto or pay for NFTs with familiar local payment rails, exposed to developers via SDKs (including a React Native SDK) and a Dashboard API. Backed by 500 Global, ADB Ventures, Amasia, CE Innovation Capital, and CreditEase, Poko was acquired by Web3Auth (Torus Labs) in October 2023 and its on-ramp aggregator continues under the Web3Auth brand. The original Poko developer surface is no longer operational: the pokoapp.xyz domain is now parked/for sale and the docs.pokoapp.xyz documentation host has been deprovisioned.
p.name: Poko

p.description: PokéAPI (pokeapi.co) is a free, open-source RESTful and GraphQL API serving comprehensive Pokémon data — including Pokémon species, abilities, moves, items, types, locations, evolution chains, encounters, berries, contests, games, and machines. Built as an educational tool licensed under BSD-3-Clause, it is community-funded via Open Collective and GitHub Sponsors, requires no authentication, and is hosted with a fair-use policy encouraging clients to cache responses locally. The API powers tutorials, fan apps, machine-learning experiments, and game tooling worldwide and consistently serves one billion-plus requests per month.
p.name: PokéAPI

p.description: The Unofficial GraphQL for PokeAPI
p.name: PokéAPI (GraphQL)

p.description: GraphQL beta endpoint for PokéAPI providing Hasura-powered queries over the complete Pokémon database including species, moves, abilities, items, evolutions, and game version data.
p.name: PokéAPI GraphQL

p.description: The Pokémon TCG API is a free, community-run REST API created and maintained by Andrew Backes that serves Pokémon Trading Card Game data - more than 20,000 cards across 170+ sets, from Base Set onward. Every card carries full gameplay data (attacks, abilities, weaknesses, resistances, retreat costs), format legalities, high-resolution card images, and daily-updated market prices from TCGplayer and Cardmarket. A Lucene-like query syntax supports keyword, phrase, wildcard, exact, range, and nested-field searches across every field. The API works without authentication at a reduced rate limit; a free API key from the developer portal, sent in the X-Api-Key header, raises the limits. Official SDKs cover Python, Ruby, JavaScript, TypeScript, C#, Kotlin, PHP, Go, Dart, and Elixir.
p.name: Pokémon TCG API

p.description: Polar Electro Oy (operating as Polar Global) is a Finnish sports and fitness technology company founded in 1977 and headquartered in Kempele, Finland. Polar invented the first wireless wearable heart rate monitor — the Sport Tester PE 2000 in 1982 — and remains one of the longest-standing brands in consumer heart rate sensing, GPS sports watches, and fitness wearables. The Polar device portfolio includes the H10 and H9 chest straps, the Verity Sense and OH1 optical sensors, the Polar 360 and Loop fitness bands, and the Vantage, Grit X, Pacer, Ignite, and Unite watch lines, along with a dedicated equine sensor line. Developers access Polar data through the Polar AccessLink API for consumer Polar Flow data, the Polar TeamPro API for team and player training sessions, and the open-source Polar BLE SDK for iOS and Android applications that stream live sensor data over Bluetooth Low Energy.
p.name: Polar

p.description: Polar is an open-source, developer-first monetization platform that acts as a Merchant of Record (MoR), handling billing, payments, and global sales tax so software teams can sell digital products, subscriptions, usage-based billing, and license keys. The Polar API (https://api.polar.sh/v1) exposes products, prices, checkouts, customers, subscriptions, orders, benefits, license keys, a customer portal, usage meters/events, and webhooks behind Bearer organization access tokens. Not affiliated with Polar Electro (fitness wearables) or the Polaris design system.
p.name: Polar

p.description: Polar Analytics is an all-in-one data analytics and AI platform purpose-built for Shopify-based ecommerce and DTC brands. It consolidates data from 45+ sources into a dedicated Snowflake warehouse, ships 400+ pre-built ecommerce metrics with a semantic layer, and adds a first-party pixel with lifetime ID, incrementality testing, Klaviyo audience enrichment, and advertising conversion signals for Meta and Google. Its AI layer includes agents for data analysis, media buying, email marketing, and inventory planning, all exposed to LLM clients through the hosted Polar Headless MCP server at api.polaranalytics.com/mcp with Bearer API-key and OAuth 2.0 access. Backed by point-nine.
p.name: Polar Analytics

p.description: Polar Signals is a continuous profiling company built by the team behind the open-source Parca project. Its Polar Signals Cloud product uses eBPF to continuously profile CPU, memory, and NVIDIA GPU workloads across Kubernetes, Docker, ECS, and bare metal with under 1% overhead and no code changes, storing profiles in the open-source FrostDB columnar database and querying them with Prometheus-style label selectors and PromQL. It exposes a gRPC/Connect API (published at buf.build/polarsignals/api) for managing organizations, projects, service accounts, roles, RBAC, and billing; a Parca-compatible profiling data plane at grpc.polarsignals.com; a hosted MCP server for AI-assisted performance analysis; language agents and SDKs for Go, Rust, Python, Node.js, JVM, .NET, PHP, Ruby and more; and the psctl CLI.
p.name: Polar Signals

p.description: Profile for Polaris in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F500 (rank 424).
p.name: Polaris

p.description: Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII), long known as Polaris Industries, is a Minnesota-based global manufacturer of powersports and off-road vehicles. Its portfolio spans RANGER, RZR, Polaris XPEDITION and GENERAL side-by-sides, Sportsman ATVs, snowmobiles, Slingshot moto-roadsters, military and commercial off-road vehicles, Aixam quadricycles, Goupil electric utility vehicles, and Bennington and Godfrey pontoon and deck boats. Its connected-vehicle platform, RIDE COMMAND, ships in-dash navigation and vehicle telematics to riders as an end-user product. Polaris completed the separation of Indian Motorcycle and the sale of a majority stake to Carolwood LP on 2 February 2026. Polaris publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; the only credentialed integration surface a member of the public can find is the dealer portal at polarisportal.com, which authenticates against an Auth0 tenant.
p.name: Polaris Industries

p.description: Polaron is a London-based AI software company that builds "the intelligence layer for materials science." Its platform applies machine learning to microscopy and image data to automate microstructure analysis, connecting process, structure, and performance so materials engineering teams can characterise, design, and manufacture materials faster and with less uncertainty. The platform centers on three core model families: Segmentation (identifying and measuring microstructural features), Reconstruction (converting 2D micrographs into 3D representations), and Design (optimising microstructural parameters). It is applied across batteries, metals and alloys, composites, ceramics, additive manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals, spanning R&D, quality and qualification, and modelling and simulation workflows. Polaron is backed by Speedinvest and research institutions including Imperial College London, Manchester, Oxford, and Cambridge.
p.name: Polaron

p.description: Polars is a blazingly fast, open-source DataFrame library and query engine written in Rust, with first-party bindings for Python, Rust, Node.js, and R. It provides lazy and eager execution, streaming for larger-than-memory datasets, automatic query optimization, multi-threading, and the Apache Arrow columnar memory format. Polars Cloud extends the same DataFrame API to managed and on-premise distributed compute with zero code changes. The project is developed by pola-rs and backed by Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.
p.name: Polars

p.description: Polestar is a Swedish premium electric performance car brand, originally spun out of Volvo Cars' Polestar Performance racing arm and now jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.
p.name: Polestar

p.description: Police Bank is a mutual, member-owned Australian bank (ABN 95 087 650 799, ACN 087 650 799, AFSL / Australian Credit Licence No. 240018) founded to serve the New South Wales police community and their families and now open to the wider public. As an Authorised Deposit-taking Institution it participates in Australia's Consumer Data Right (Open Banking) regime as an active data holder - it publishes an unauthenticated Product Reference Data (PRD) API conforming to the Consumer Data Standards, and lets members share their banking data with ACCC-accredited data recipients. Police Bank states it is in the process of gaining ACCC accreditation to also receive data as an Accredited Data Recipient.
p.name: Police Bank

p.description: POLICYANDPLAY LTD (England & Wales, company no. 17253846) operates fetch-price, a UK product and price search API built for AI agents: one POST to api.fetch-price.com returns live eBay UK listings (via the official Browse API; Amazon UK rolling out) as normalised JSON with GBP prices, condition and an affiliate-tracked purchase URL. The free tier needs no API key (50 lookups/month, 30 requests/minute); Pro (GBP 29) and Scale/Trade (GBP 99) plans raise quotas and let customers route affiliate commission to their own eBay Partner Network account. The same API is exposed as a conformant A2A 1.0.0 agent card with a live JSON-RPC message/send binding, a stdio MCP server listed in the official MCP registry, a provider-authored SKILL.md, llms.txt, and npm/PyPI SDKs. No OpenAPI is published; the profile's spec was generated by API Evangelist from the provider's own reference and checked against the live host.
p.name: POLICYANDPLAY LTD

p.description: Policybazaar is India's largest online insurance aggregator and digital marketplace, operated by PB Fintech Ltd. It lets consumers compare, buy and manage insurance across health, term life, motor, travel, investment and corporate lines from a wide panel of insurers, providing quotes, policy issuance, renewals, claims assistance and advisory. Surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Policybazaar publishes a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (no developer/API subdomain, no /.well-known documents, no llms.txt).
p.name: Policybazaar

p.description: PolicyCheck (formerly LegalEasy) is a seller-policy risk intelligence service built for AI purchasing agents. Given a store URL or raw policy text it extracts structured facts from return, shipping, warranty, terms and privacy policies — return window, restocking fees, binding arbitration, class-action waivers, data selling — scores them deterministically into a 0-10 risk score and a 0-100 buyer protection score, labels standard boilerplate separately from unusual restrictions, and can return the result as an Ed25519-signed assessment an agent presents at checkout and a merchant verifies against a public JWKS. The surface is anonymous REST at policycheck.tools/api/check, an A2A JSON-RPC agent with a published agent card, a stdio MCP server on npm, an x402 pay-per-analysis endpoint settled in USDC on Base, a versioned clause registry, and a keyed audit log and compliance report. The published OpenAPI covers only the two legacy ChatGPT-plugin operations.
p.name: PolicyCheck

p.description: Policygenius is an independent online insurance marketplace and licensed brokerage founded in 2014 by Jennifer Fitzgerald and Francois de Lame and headquartered in New York City. The platform lets consumers compare quotes, get unbiased expert advice, and buy life, disability, homeowners, auto, and renters insurance across dozens of carriers, and it operates Policygenius Pro, a turnkey life-insurance fulfillment platform for financial advisors, agents, banks, and credit unions. Policygenius was acquired by Zinnia (an Eldridge company) in 2023. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Policygenius publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and forks only.
p.name: Policygenius

p.description: PolicyPal is a Singapore-based InsurTech and digital insurance broker founded in 2016 by Val Yap that lets consumers buy, understand, and organize their insurance policies from a mobile app using OCR and rule-based policy digitization. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), PayPal Incubation, and Startupbootcamp FinTech, it was the first startup to graduate from the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox and was acquired by Hong Kong's AMTD Digital in 2020. As of 2025 PolicyPal Pte. Ltd. and its entities (including PolicyPal Tech Pte. Ltd., Baoxianbaobao Pte. Ltd. and the ValueChampion brand) are no longer regulated by MAS, and the consumer website is undergoing a revamp. PolicyPal does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.
p.name: PolicyPal

p.description: Polimorphic is a New York-based government technology company building a complete AI platform for local, county, state, and federal government service delivery. Its product suite pairs a Constituent Relationship Manager (CRM) with an AI Chatbot & Search, a Voice Agent (VoiceAI), and Workflows so public agencies can answer residents 24/7 in 75+ languages and guide them through permits, licenses, applications, and payments from intake to resolution. Polimorphic connects to existing government systems of record (ArcGIS, Tyler, Accela, Salesforce, Laserfiche, Stripe, and more) and is used by 200+ public-sector departments serving tens of millions of residents. Founded by Parth Shah (CEO) and Daniel Smith (CTO), the company is backed by General Catalyst, M13, and Shine.
p.name: Polimorphic

p.description: Polisen is Sweden’s national police authority, responsible for law enforcement, public safety, and crime prevention across the country. The agency provides public information, services, and resources through its website, including crime statistics, reporting tools, and guidance for citizens. While primarily a governmental organization, its digital platforms expose various APIs for data access, service integration, and public engagement, making it a relevant entity for API profiling and integration efforts.
p.name: Polisen

p.description: Politecnico di Milano is Italy's largest technical university — engineering, architecture and design — and a public research institution in Milan, ROR 01nffqt88. Like almost every university it is a federation of buyers rather than an API producer: there is no developer portal, no public API key, no status page and no changelog anywhere on polimi.it. What it does operate itself is real and was verified live on 2026-09-01. An open data portal at www.opendata.polimi.it publishes a DCAT-AP_IT catalogue in RDF Turtle describing 25 datasets, each with a CSV and a JSON distribution at a stable unauthenticated URL — all 25 returned 200 and 38,255 rows on probe, covering the course catalogue, enrolments, graduates, mobility, internships, grade distributions and research output under CC BY 4.0. Two separate OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoints are served from its own hosts: Re.Public@Polimi for research products and POLITESI for theses, the latter also harvestable in the DataCite kernel-4 metadata schema. It runs its own Shibboleth identity provider, shibidp.polimi.it, whose SAML 2.0 metadata is public and whose entityID is registered in the Italian IDEM GARR federation. Against that, the surfaces it does NOT own are recorded as such: the authenticated IRIS REST API on its repository host is CINECA's product contract, not the university's, and api.polimi.it is a live Kong gateway with no publicly routable endpoint behind it. This profile saves contracts only for the surfaces the institution itself operates.
p.name: Politecnico di Milano

p.description: Politecnico di Torino (PoliTO) is Italy's oldest technical university, founded in Turin in 1859, with roughly 38,000 students across engineering, architecture and design. Unusually for this cohort, its programmable footprint is genuinely its own rather than a vendor's: the university publishes the OpenAPI definition of the REST API behind its official student and faculty mobile applications in the verified @polito GitHub organisation (polito/api-spec, authored in TypeSpec and emitted as two client contracts, Polito Faculty API and Polito Students API), and the React Native apps that consume it are open-sourced under EUPL-1.2 in polito/rn-apps and polito/students-app. That API runs on the university's own host, app.didattica.polito.it, and covers announcements, authentication with MFA, room and slot bookings, courses, lectures, news, people, places, exams, grades, degree offering, job offers, surveys, support tickets and the European Student Card. It is not a self-service developer programme: the production base path returns 403 to an anonymous caller, every operation is bearer authenticated against a PoliTO account, and no key can be requested by an outsider. Two further institution-operated machine-readable surfaces exist and are recorded here for the first time — a Shibboleth SAML 2.0 identity provider registered in IDEM GARR and eduGAIN since 2020, and an OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting service over the IRIS research repository, the latter a CINECA tenant deployment rather than PoliTO engineering. A fourth institution-operated surface was found on 2026-08-30 and is the only one an outsider can actually call: four keyless JSON web services behind the polito.it site search — staff, departments and teachings at mypoli.polito.it/dotnet/ws_anagrafe and a campus room locator at legacyprod.polito.it — all returning HTTP 200 and real data with no credential, on hosts inside the university's own GARR address space. They are undocumented and unversioned, PoliTO does not present them as a developer product, and the OpenAPI held here is derived from probing rather than published. The university also runs HPC@PoliTO, an academic computing service managed in-house, whose allocation process is entirely by email with no programmatic surface. The institutional open-data portal publishes downloadable datasets only, with no API behind it, and there is no data.polito.it or api.polito.it host in service.
p.name: Politecnico di Torino

p.description: Politico illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow’s headlines, not reports on yesterday’s news. Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across key democratic capitals provide premier politics and policy newsroom, offering analysis for leaders and decision‑makers.
p.name: Politico

p.description: Polkadot is a multi-chain blockchain network that enables interoperability between specialized blockchains called parachains. Developer APIs are provided through Subscan (a multi-chain block explorer with a hosted HTTP API) and the Substrate API Sidecar (a REST interface for Polkadot SDK-based chains), enabling queries against extrinsics, events, accounts, blocks, staking data, and parachain state on Polkadot, Kusama, and related networks.
p.name: Polkadot

p.description: Pollen Technologies is a London-based, FCA-authorised white-label fintech platform that lets any business launch its own banking and payments product with no code and a fully managed back office. The platform delivers programmatic payment delivery, instant named IBAN account opening, third-party bank account linking for real-time balances and transaction data, multi-currency payments across 148 currencies into more than 160 countries, local payment schemes, and virtual and physical cards. A managed compliance layer covers KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, client fund safeguarding and help-desk support under SLAs. Pollen Technologies Ltd is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (firm reference 768011), founded in 2015 and backed by Seedcamp, Level39 and Q-Advisers. Access to the underlying payments and banking APIs is delivered as a managed, partner-only service rather than a public self-serve developer program, so no public API specifications, SDKs or developer portal are currently published.
p.name: Pollen

p.description: Pollfish is a mobile-first survey and market research platform, owned by Prodege LLC. It lets researchers reach real respondents inside mobile apps and websites and lets app publishers monetize their audience by serving Pollfish (and mediated third-party) surveys as rewarded ads or an offerwall. Pollfish exposes a REST Dashboard API on https://www.pollfish.com for managing publisher apps and pulling performance, revenue, demographic, and user-log analytics (HTTP Basic Auth), plus a survey-serving / offerwall API on https://wss.pollfish.com for requesting and rendering surveys, and server-to-server postback callbacks for survey-completion and eligibility events. Survey creation and audience targeting for researchers are done through the Pollfish dashboard and are not exposed as a documented public REST API.
p.name: Pollfish

p.description: Pollinate is a London-headquartered financial technology company that builds a cloud-based, bank-grade digital experience platform helping banks and payment processors reinvent merchant acquiring and value-added services for their small and medium business (SMB) customers. The platform wraps around a bank's legacy payment systems to deliver dynamic merchant onboarding, a bank-branded Merchant Command Center dashboard (transaction reconciliation, dispute management, statements, service discovery), integrated merchant services inside online banking, and ISV enablement. Built on Microsoft Azure and open-banking ready, it powers live bank deployments including Tyl by NatWest (UK), NAB Hive (Australia), and Tyl by CIBC (Canada), with clients including Truist and partners including Fiserv, Endava, and Dun & Bradstreet. Pollinate's APIs are private and partner-facing; it does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.
p.name: Pollinate

p.description: Polly is a .NET resilience and transient-fault-handling library that allows developers to express resilience strategies such as Retry, Circuit Breaker, Hedging, Timeout, Rate Limiter, and Fallback in a fluent and thread-safe manner. A .NET Foundation member project.
p.name: Polly

p.description: Polly is an AI-native capital markets operating system launched in October 2026. It provides a unified platform for mortgage pricing, risk management, loan-level attribution, and investor discovery. The platform offers transparent pricing, intelligent execution at scale, and an API suite ready for integration, aiming to streamline end‑to‑end capital markets processes for lenders and investors.
p.name: Polly

p.description: US based digital asset exchange
p.name: Poloniex

p.description: Polsia is an autonomous AI business-management platform marketed as "AI that runs your company while you sleep." It deploys a set of specialized AI agents — business planning, competitor research, social media, ads, email outreach, customer support, code generation, finance, and deployment — coordinated by an orchestrator to run a company's daily operations on recurring schedules for a monthly subscription plus a share of revenue generated on the platform. Founded by Ben Sera and backed by True Ventures and Sound Ventures (raised $30M at a $250M valuation in 2026), Polsia is a hosted consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server.
p.name: Polsia

p.description: Poly is an AI-powered intelligent cloud file browser that syncs a user's local files to the cloud and layers an AI agent over them, letting people search by image, concept, phrase, color or face and ask natural-language questions about their documents, images, video and audio to get summaries, transcriptions, tags and generated content such as podcasts and presentations. Founded by CEO Abhay Agarwal, Poly (formerly reached at withpoly.com, now poly.app) emerged from stealth in November 2025 with $8M in seed funding led by Felicis with participation from Bloomberg Beta, NextView, Figma Ventures, AI Grant, Wing Ventures and MVP Ventures. It is currently in waitlist/beta on web and Mac, with a Windows version planned, and as of this enrichment pass publishes no public developer API, SDKs, CLI, or MCP server.
p.name: Poly

p.description: PolyAI builds enterprise-grade voice and chat AI agents that handle real customer service conversations across 24+ languages, with 99.994% production uptime. The PolyAI Platform exposes three REST API families — an Agents API to create, branch, configure and deploy agents through environments; a Conversations API to retrieve transcripts, audio, metrics and session data; and a Webhooks & Alerts surface for real-time event notifications — plus Chat, SMS, Outbound Calling, Handoff, DNI, External Events, Messaging (WebSocket) and a WebRTC Gateway. Authentication is header-based (x-api-key) with region-scoped keys, and a Python Agent Development Kit (ADK) offers a Git-like local build-pull-push workflow. Backed by Khosla Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.
p.name: Polyai

p.description: Poly, built using cutting-edge AI and Kubernetes-native technology, accelerates development and simplifies the operation of integrations, orchestrations, and microservices with TypeScript, Python, Java, and C.
p.name: PolyAPI

p.description: Polycam is a cross-platform 3D scanning and capture company building consumer and professional tools for turning the physical world into high-fidelity 3D content. Its iOS, Android, and web apps support LiDAR-based space capture, photogrammetry, photosphere capture, AI-generated 3D models, and Gaussian Splat reconstructions, with export formats including glTF/GLB, OBJ, FBX, DAE, STL, USDZ, point clouds, and CAD-friendly files. Polycam serves freelancers, AEC and real-estate teams, VFX and game studios, e-commerce sellers, and enterprise operators with 2D/3D floor plans, measurement tools, shared team libraries, virtual walkthroughs, AI reports, custom branding, SSO, and TransformEngine for custom 3D file creation. Revenue is subscription based across Free, Basic ($30/mo or $150/yr), Business ($400/yr per user), and Enterprise tiers, with sales-led pricing for organizations at scale. Polycam exposes a developer mode in the iOS app that unlocks a raw-data export bundle (raw.glb mesh, keyframes, images, cameras, depth maps, confidence data, mesh_info.json) used by partners such as Vuforia, Immersal, and Unity/Unreal workflows, and ships an open-source Python toolkit (polyform) for converting raw captures to NeRF and other research formats. As of this profile there is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal — integrations happen through raw exports, partner pipelines, and the Polycam app surface itself.
p.name: Polycam

p.description: Polychain Capital is a San Francisco-based investment firm founded in 2016 by Olaf Carlson-Wee, the first employee and former Head of Risk at Coinbase. The firm is dedicated exclusively to blockchain and cryptocurrency, investing in protocols, digital tokens, and early-stage crypto companies through both a liquid token hedge fund and dedicated venture capital vehicles. Polychain's thesis centers on digital assets whose scarcity derives from mathematical and cryptographic properties, and its portfolio spans layer-1 and layer-2 networks, DeFi, developer and cryptographic infrastructure, custody, exchanges, zero-knowledge and privacy technology, AI-native crypto, and stablecoins. The firm has led notable rounds including Uniswap, dYdX, Yellow Card, Arbitrum (Offchain Labs), Scroll, and EigenLayer, and its venture funds are backed by LPs including Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Founders Fund. Reported assets under management have ranged from roughly $2.6B to about $5B across its funds; Polychain closed a $200M fourth venture fund in 2023 and employs a team of roughly 32 people from its San Francisco headquarters.
p.name: Polychain Capital

p.description: Polycode Limited is a UK information-technology consultancy (Companies House 10172940, Leeds, incorporated 2016) that operates marginalia, a small public chat experiment built on a shared, provenance-tracked memory graph: a language model synthesises conversations into an OWL-typed graph and questions are answered by narrowing that graph with SPARQL. marginalia publishes a public REST API (OpenAPI 3.0.3, 50 operations at https://marginalia.polycode.co.uk/api — async chat with task polling, session search and history, insights, projects, usage and budget, key-authed private graphs; no key for reads and chat), an A2A 0.3.0 agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json with a live JSON-RPC endpoint (message/send, message/stream, tasks/get) advertising chat, recall-memory and research-projects skills, an OpenAI-shaped zero-token completion shim, a first-party CLI and the AGPL-3.0 source on GitLab. Visitor contributions are PII-redacted at ingest and republished under CC-BY-SA 4.0; a volatile flag keeps a turn out of shared memory. The corporate apex polycode.co.uk did not resolve when profiled; the product host is the live web presence.
p.name: Polycode

p.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.
p.name: Polycom

p.description: Polygon ID (now operating as Privado ID) is a self-sovereign identity platform that enables issuers to create and manage decentralized identifiers (DIDs) and verifiable credentials (VCs) using zero-knowledge proof cryptography. Built on the iden3 protocol and the Polygon blockchain, it allows organizations to issue privacy-preserving credentials — such as KYC attestations, age proofs, and reputation signals — while giving users full control over their identity data. Verifiers can authenticate users and gate access using ZK queries without learning underlying personal information.
p.name: Polygon ID

p.description: Polygon Labs builds the Open Money Stack, a suite of APIs enabling programmable stablecoin payments, cross‑chain transfers, wallet services, and on‑chain settlement. The platform offers pay‑ins, payouts, virtual accounts, orchestration, and developer tools for global money movement, serving enterprises and fintechs worldwide.
p.name: Polygon Labs

p.description: PolygonScan is the leading blockchain explorer, search, API, and analytics platform for the Polygon PoS network. It provides a REST API for querying transactions, token transfers, smart contract source code, ERC-20/ERC-721/ERC-1155 balances, gas prices, and network statistics on the Polygon blockchain (Chain ID 137). API access is unified under Etherscan API V2, enabling access with a single API key across 60+ EVM-compatible chains.
p.name: PolygonScan

p.description: Polymarket is a decentralized prediction-market platform built on Polygon where users buy and sell binary outcome shares in real-world events. Settlement is on-chain via the UMA optimistic oracle, while order matching runs through a hybrid central-limit order book (CLOB). Developer surface includes the CLOB API for order placement and market data, the Gamma API for market and event metadata, a Data API for historical and analytical reads, a WebSocket stream, and official CLOB client SDKs in TypeScript, Python, and Rust.
p.name: Polymarket

p.description: Polymateria Ltd is a British materials-science company, based at the Imperial College I-HUB on the White City Campus in London, that develops Biotransformation — a masterbatch additive blended into polyethylene and polypropylene at roughly 2% by weight so that plastic which escapes a waste stream weathers into a bioavailable wax and fully biodegrades in the open environment without leaving microplastics behind. The company co-authored BSI PAS 9017, the first standard for measuring the biodegradability of polyolefins, is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and a Terra Carta signatory, and sells to converters, brand owners and packaging manufacturers rather than to developers. Its product is a chemical additive, not software: the public website is a WordPress marketing and media site, and the only credentialed surface it operates is a customer portal that serves third-party test datasets as documents. No developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind was found in this pass.
p.name: Polymateria

p.description: Polymath Robotics builds general autonomy and safety software for off-highway and industrial vehicles such as tractors, loaders, dozers, and mining trucks. Its Synapse REST API lets developers command a real or simulated Polymath-powered vehicle: sending GPS and relative waypoints, issuing motion and vehicle commands, reading combined autonomy, navigation, and vehicle feedback, managing exclusive teleoperation control leases, and streaming media over LiveKit. Caladan, its browser-based simulation environment, lets teams build and test autonomous behaviors in Python without ROS, Gazebo, or Linux before deploying to physical machines. Founded in 2021 (YC S22), San Francisco.
p.name: Polymath Robotics

p.description: Polymathic Technologies Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Polymathic Technologies

p.description: Polymer (Polymer Search) is an AI-driven embedded analytics and business intelligence platform that lets teams and product developers turn raw spreadsheet, database, and SaaS data into interactive dashboards, charts, and visualizations without a data analyst. Its REST API lets developers create workspaces, connect data sources (Snowflake, BigQuery, CSV/JSON uploads), build boards composed of visualization blocks, and embed white-labeled, permission-scoped dashboards directly into their own applications with a few lines of code. Authentication is via API key, with short-lived embed tokens for end-user access. Polymer is backed by Sierra Ventures and 500 Global.
p.name: Polymer

p.description: Polymorph is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building adaptive consumer internet infrastructure that personalizes user experiences with AI agents. Founded in San Francisco by Andrew Sy, the platform runs thousands of continuous product and lifecycle-engagement experiments for its customers, each carrying the craft of that product's direction and brand, so consumer teams can scale experimentation in product surfaces without being bottlenecked by headcount or design capacity. Its stated vision is to make the consumer internet polymorphic — one that adapts to each user and optimizes for delightful experiences. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site only; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or developer portal.
p.name: Polymorph

p.description: PolyOne Corporation was a specialty polymer materials and services company formed in 2000 through the merger of M.A. Hanna Company and The Geon Company. In 2020, after acquiring a division from Clariant, the company rebranded as Avient Corporation. No public developer APIs are documented.
p.name: Polyone

p.description: PolySign, Inc. is an Oakland / San Francisco / New York financial technology company building blockchain-enabled infrastructure for institutional digital asset capital markets and payments. Founded by Arthur Britto, David Schwartz and Jack McDonald, PolySign operates a third-generation permissioned blockchain and the AtomicNet settlement network, and was the parent of Standard Custody & Trust Company, the NYDFS-regulated digital asset custody, trading and settlement platform acquired by Ripple in 2024. PolySign publishes three OpenAPI 3.0.3 contracts for AtomicNet — the AtomicNet API Server (node interface for assets, orders, escrow and beneficiary authorizations, settlements, settlement confirmations, book transfers, partners and investors), the AtomicNet Merchant Gate Node, and the AtomicNet ABC Proxy Service (account registration, digest memorialization, signing and testnet faucet) — all authenticated with OAuth 2.0 client credentials issued by a PolySign-hosted token endpoint.
p.name: PolySign

p.description: Polyteia is a Berlin-based govtech company offering a data platform for the German and European public sector. It lets public administrations connect existing systems, harmonize fragmented data, and use it in AI-supported workflows for forms, case processing, statistical evaluation, and reporting. The platform ships pre-built Solutions for common public-sector use cases (social-service planning, budget controlling, crisis response, kindergarten demand forecasting) plus a no-code/low-code Studio. It serves 80+ government entities in Germany, including the states of Schleswig-Holstein and Saarland. The platform is fully driveable through an RPC-style API (command/query over a single POST endpoint) authenticated with Personal Access Keys, backed by a Trust Center and GDPR/BSI/C5 compliance. Founded by Faruk Tuncer, Taisia Antonova, and Lukas Rambold; backed by HV Capital and DvH Ventures.
p.name: Polyteia

p.description: Polytomic is a data integration platform providing no-code data syncing between databases, data warehouses, and SaaS applications. The Polytomic REST API exposes connections, syncs, models, bulk syncs, identity, schemas, and webhooks for programmatic management of data movement.
p.name: Polytomic

p.description: Let'sMOD (formerly Polyup) is a Sunnyvale, California company founded in 2015 that builds a consumer platform where users aged 8 and up can play, modify, remix, and share short 3D microgames and AI-powered interactive memes. Originally a computational-thinking and math learning tool under the Polyup brand, the product has evolved into a generative-AI-driven microgame and viral-content community at letsmod.com. Let'sMOD is a 500 Global portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its public GitHub organization contains only internal CLI tooling and configuration. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via live domain-security probing.
p.name: Polyup

p.description: Polyvore was a community-powered fashion and lifestyle social-commerce website where members created and shared outfit "sets" by clipping product images into collages. Founded in 2007 and backed by Matrix Partners, it was acquired by Yahoo in 2015 (~$200M), passed to Verizon/Oath, and its assets were acquired by Canadian e-commerce retailer SSENSE in April 2018, which shut the site down immediately. The polyvore.com domain now 301-redirects to ssense.com; there is no live product, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.
p.name: Polyvore

p.description: Polywork is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Polywork

p.description: PolyXLabs is a Techstars-backed biotechnology and sustainable-materials company developing biodegradable plastic alternatives from lignocellulose-based biomass, including food waste such as spent coffee grounds. The company produces customized, toxin-free, microplastic-free polymers designed to be lightweight and durable as drop-in replacements for conventional plastics in consumer goods and packaging, with operations across the United States and Europe and headquarters in Martonvasar, Hungary. PolyXLabs currently publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.
p.name: PolyXLabs

p.description: Pomelo (pomelo.la) is a Latin American card-issuing and embedded-finance platform. Its REST API lets fintechs and enterprises onboard users (KYC/KYB), issue physical and virtual cards, manage card accounts and balances, process and query transactions, move money with transfers and settlements, and authorize transactions in real time over a synchronous authorization webhook.
p.name: Pomelo

p.description: Pomelo Care is a value-based virtual healthcare company delivering 24/7 clinician-led care for women and children across fertility and preconception, prenatal and postpartum, pediatric and NICU, and midlife and menopause health. Operating as a telehealth platform contracted with employers and health plans, Pomelo pairs licensed clinicians, doulas, and care teams with remote monitoring to close the gaps between doctor visits, reduce NICU admissions, and improve maternal and infant outcomes. The company reports covering 25 million lives across all 50 states and raised a $92M Series C at a $1.7B valuation. Pomelo Care is a patient-, employer-, and payer-facing platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and First Round Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and monitoring.
p.name: Pomelo Care

p.description: Pomelo Fashion is an omnichannel fashion retailer headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, selling women's apparel and accessories across Southeast Asia through its website and mobile app. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront (pomelofashion.com, served via CloudFront) but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface (all probed paths returned HTTP 405). This profile therefore carries only probed domain-security signal; it remains a lead for revisiting should a developer program launch.
p.name: Pomelo fashion

p.description: Pomelo Health (formerly Chronometriq, founded 2012, headquartered in Montreal with offices in Boston and Toronto) is a Canadian patient-engagement software company operating within the TELUS Health ecosystem. Its cloud platform helps medical clinics reduce no-shows and modernize the front-desk experience with online booking/e-booking, automated SMS/voice/email appointment reminders, digital intake eForms, telemedicine, secure two-way messaging, patient broadcasts, and a patient portal. Pomelo ships as an EMR add-on that syncs with TELUS Health EMRs — Accuro, Medesync, and TELUS CHR — rather than as an open integration platform. As of this review Pomelo Health publishes NO public developer portal, NO documented REST/OpenAPI, and NO public HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement or SMART-on-FHIR surface; third-party connectivity is achieved through the underlying EMR partner APIs, so this profile is an honest identity stub for a company with a gated, partner-only integration model. Home market: Canada.
p.name: Pomelo Health

p.description: Pomerium is an identity-aware reverse proxy that enables secure, zero-trust access to internal applications without a VPN.
p.name: Pomerium

p.description: Pomo is an AI marketing platform that runs an always-on AI marketing team, turning continuous market, competitor, brand, and trend intelligence into strategy, creative direction, ad-placement planning, and launch-ready campaign workflows for lean growth, brand, and performance teams. It monitors signals daily, surfaces opportunity and whitespace, drafts approval-ready campaigns, briefs, and creatives, and supports AEO/GEO AI-search visibility and Marketing Mix Modeling. Pomo is also offered as a managed service where in-house marketing experts operate the platform on a customer's behalf. The platform runs on a public FastAPI backend at api.usepomo.ai that publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 contract covering 924 paths and 994 operations across campaigns, competitor tracking, market intelligence, earned media, influencer discovery, a unified data model, and connectors to Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn, Shopify, Square, Stripe, QuickBooks, Klaviyo, HubSpot, and Slack, plus a bearer-gated programmatic API with self-service API keys and an internal MCP tool broker. The legal entity is MachFlow, Inc. dba Pomo. Founded in 2025 and based in Palo Alto, California, Pomo raised a $4.5M seed round led by Kindred Ventures with Databricks Ventures, SV Angel, and angel investors.
p.name: Pomo

p.description: POMS Corporation develops POMSnet Aquila, a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) purpose-built for pharmaceutical, biotech, cell and gene therapy, and medical device manufacturers. The platform delivers FDA-compliant electronic batch records (EBR), production execution, review-by-exception, and plant-floor integration with ERP and equipment systems, deployed on-premise or in the cloud. POMS also offers the POMSnet Falcon EBR analytics dashboards. Founded around its first MES implementation in 1988 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, POMS sells enterprise software to regulated life-sciences manufacturers rather than publishing a public developer API. Surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, this profile is enriched from the company's public web presence; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found.
p.name: POMS

p.description: Poncho was a consumer weather service founded in 2013 in New York City by Kuan Huang and Paul Murphy that delivered a personalized, personality-driven daily forecast through the messaging layer — Facebook Messenger, SMS, email, and Amazon Alexa — rather than a traditional weather app. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Comcast Ventures, and Lerer Hippeau, the company was acquired by Dirty Lemon and is no longer independently operating. It never published a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile carries identity metadata only.
p.name: Poncho

p.description: Pond5 is a royalty-free stock media marketplace where creators buy and sell video footage, music tracks, sound effects, motion graphics, images, and other digital assets. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile has been through a local enrichment pass: the public web presence sits behind DataDome bot protection with no discoverable public API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or security.txt at the time of the pass. Only live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security posture could be probed. Sector: media.
p.name: Pond5

p.description: Ponder was a data-science software company founded by UC Berkeley RISELab researchers (Doris Lee, Devin Petersohn, and Prof. Aditya Parameswaran) to commercialize the popular open-source Python libraries Modin (a drop-in pandas replacement that scales dataframe workflows with a single line of code) and Lux (automated visualization and intelligent data discovery inside notebooks). Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, 8VC, Intel Capital, and The House Fund via a $7M seed in March 2022, Ponder was acquired by Snowflake in October 2023. The ponder.io domain is now parked and no longer serves a live product, developer portal, or API; the open-source libraries remain the durable public surface.
p.name: Ponder

p.description: Pongalo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pongalo

p.description: Pontem is a Web3 product development studio building with the Move language on Aptos and other Layer 1 blockchains, in partnership with Aptos Labs. Its product portfolio spans the Pontem Wallet (a browser-extension and mobile crypto wallet for APT, MOVE, ETH, SOL and more), the Liquidswap decentralized exchange and AMM, the Lumio L2 VM-abstraction framework, and a Move developer tooling suite that includes the Move Code Playground, the IntelliJ Move IDE plugin, the ByteBabel Solidity-to-Move bytecode translator, and the Dove Move package manager. Pontem publishes first-party TypeScript SDKs, an embeddable Liquidswap web-component widget, wallet adapters, and CLIs. Backed by Pantera Capital, Animoca Brands, and Aptos Labs.
p.name: Pontem

p.description: Pontera (formerly FeeX; legal entity Pontera Solutions Inc.) is a wealthtech platform that lets financial advisors securely manage, rebalance, and report on clients' held-away workplace-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 401(a), 403(b), 457, TSP, and certain 529 plans — without a rollover. Accounts connect through a client-permissioned, credential-free workflow designed to avoid triggering custody under SEC Rule 206(4)-2, with an un-editable audit log for supervision. Pontera integrates with portfolio-management, reporting, billing, and supervision systems (Orion, Addepar, Black Diamond, Morningstar and others) but publishes no public developer API. Backed by ICONIQ Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
p.name: Pontera

p.description: Pontis is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: Pontis

p.description: Ponto is a crypto banking and payments infrastructure company in the fintech sector, surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and Polychain and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be located for the company - the previously associated ponto.io domain now redirects to an unrelated party and no other candidate domain resolved to a live crypto-banking product. This profile remains a thin lead pending discovery of a verified developer/API surface, at which point the pipeline can harvest and enrich real artifacts.
p.name: Ponto

p.description: Brazilian address/location-intelligence API mapping CEP (postal code) or address to IBGE CNEFE census points with latitude/longitude, joined with Receita Federal business establishments. Offers proximity/radius search, full-text street search, and companies-at-location lookups. Agent-first provider with a hosted MCP server and llms.txt.
p.name: PontoFato

p.description: Pony.ai is a global autonomous-mobility company founded in Silicon Valley in 2016 and dual-headquartered in Guangzhou and Fremont. Its core technology is the Pony "virtual driver", a Level 4 autonomous driving stack deployed across three business lines: Robotaxi (PonyPilot+ ride-hailing service operating in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, plus pilots in California and Arizona), Robotruck (autonomous heavy-duty trucking in China), and Personally Owned Vehicle (POV) intelligent driving software for production passenger cars. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ under PONY and reports more than 32 million kilometres of autonomous road testing. Pony.ai does not publish a traditional public developer API; its public GitHub presence includes infrastructure tooling such as pony_aim (experiment tracker) and bazel-buildfarm rather than the AV stack itself. This profile captures the company surface and any developer-relevant artifacts.
p.name: Pony.ai

p.description: Pool.com is a Web3 domain service provider offering Infinity Domains, enabling ICANN-accredited registrars and other partners to mint and distribute Second Level Domains and integrate Web3 naming into their services through Pool's registrar API.
p.name: Pool

p.description: PoolParty is a founder-led (Adam Byrne) broadcast-style media platform in pilot: a "programmable airtime network" where humans and AI agents submit short media blocks — launch videos, demos, proof assets — into a moderated public queue on the Main Stage (channel "main", a.k.a. PP0), watch the queue become the show, and read back proof of what aired. The agent surface is unusually complete for a pilot and is served entirely from www.poolparty.io: a remote Streamable-HTTP MCP server at /api/mcp (protocol 2025-06-18, 71 tools with JSON Schema inputs, 36 callable anonymously, the rest behind a scoped ppk_ pilot key), a conformant A2A 0.3.0 agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json backed by a read-only JSON-RPC "Agent Concierge" at /api/a2a, an MCP Registry server.json, llms.txt, AGENTS.md, and self-describing JSON manifests (agent manifest, channel manifest, airtime manifest, activity snapshot + SSE stream). Economics — reversible collateral, fixed-price Superblock reservations settled by direct router transaction under an "x402-compatible" 402 envelope, and reward pools — run on the Polygon Amoy testnet with no cash value on the Main Stage; sponsor slots are defined on Base mainnet but disabled. No OpenAPI is published for the REST manifest routes.
p.name: PoolParty

p.description: Poolside is an AI foundation model lab (founded 2023 by former GitHub CTO Jason Warner and Eiso Kant) building open-weight foundation models - the Laguna family - purpose-built for agentic software engineering. Poolside does not run a shared public SaaS API the way OpenAI or Groq do. Instead it publishes a full, public API reference (docs.poolside.ai) for an OpenAI-compatible inference API plus an admin/identity API, but the API itself only comes alive once a customer has a provisioned Poolside deployment - into their own AWS/Azure/Google Cloud VPC, on customer-owned NVIDIA GPU clusters via Helm, or fully air-gapped on-prem. There is no public signup page, free tier, or published pricing; access is arranged directly with Poolside's sales team. Separately, Poolside's smaller open-weight model, Laguna XS 2.1, can be called by anyone through third-party inference hosts such as OpenRouter, which is the closest thing to a public, self-serve way to hit a Poolside model over HTTP.
p.name: Poolside

p.description: Pop Mart International Group is a Chinese pop-culture and designer-toy company best known for its blind-box collectibles and character IP such as Labubu (The Monsters), Molly, Skullpanda and Dimoo. Headquartered in Beijing and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, it operates retail stores, robot-shop vending machines, and a consumer e-commerce presence across China and international markets. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan/Sequoia China). Consumer sector; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment (no developer portal, /.well-known documents, or llms.txt).
p.name: Pop Mart

p.description: Pop Up Archive was a startup that provided audio and podcast transcription, speech-to-text, and searchable spoken-word archiving tools, making audio content discoverable and machine-readable. It was acquired by Apple in 2017 and its independent products, developer surface, and popuparchive.com domain were retired. The domain now resolves to Apple nameservers with no active host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API to enrich. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Bloomberg Beta and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; no live API surface remains.
p.name: Pop Up Archive

p.description: Pop-Up Magazine is a live magazine created for a stage, a screen, and a live audience, produced by the team behind The California Sunday Magazine. Each production combines original nonfiction storytelling, live music, illustration, animation, and photography performed on tour in theaters across the United States. The company also operates Pop-Up Magazine Brand Studio, producing custom live and multimedia storytelling for brand partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Pop-Up Magazine is a consumer media and live-events brand; it publishes a public promotional website but exposes no developer program, public API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.
p.name: Pop-Up Magazine

p.description: Pop.in is a consumer social gaming platform that connects people through real-time multiplayer games including Spades, Hearts, Dominoes, Liar's Dice, crosswords, Pop Quiz trivia, and Just Chatting. Delivered as iOS and Android apps plus a web play surface at play.pop.in, the service reports over 100M downloads and 20M active users with a 4.75+ average rating. The company is backed by 500 Global and was surfaced through its portfolio; it operates a purely consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.
p.name: Pop.in

p.description: PopApp is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
p.name: PopApp

p.description: PopChill is Taiwan's largest secondhand luxury fashion trading platform, operating as a mobile marketplace app for buying and selling authenticated pre-owned designer goods including handbags, watches, jewelry, apparel, and footwear from Chanel, Hermes, Louis Vuitton, Dior, Gucci, Prada, and 40+ other brands. The company provides item authentication, secure transactions, and seller support to a consumer audience. PopChill is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or technical integration surface; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network pending any future API program.
p.name: PopChill

p.description: PopCom is an AI-powered automated retail technology company founded by e-commerce entrepreneur Dawn Dickson. Its flagship product, the PopShop, is a robotic self-service kiosk that dispenses physical and digital products while capturing customer data through computer vision, facial recognition, and real-time analytics. The platform gives brands and entrepreneurs the kind of sales metrics, inventory monitoring, targeted advertising, and customer-sentiment insight that online retailers enjoy, but for physical, unattended retail. PopCom sells its hardware on an annual lease with a monthly software subscription. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass PopCom publishes no public developer platform, API, or specification.
p.name: PopCom

p.description: Poplin (formerly SudShare) is a nationwide on-demand laundry pickup and delivery marketplace connecting customers with independent, work-from-home "Laundry Pros" who wash, dry, and fold laundry, serving 500+ cities and 150,000+ customers. Poplin operates two consumer-facing mobile apps - the customer app and the Laundry Pro app - plus a Laundry Pro web portal (laundry-pro.poplin.co), but it does not expose a public or partner developer API. No developer portal or API reference was found at poplin.co, and the api.poplin.co subdomain resolves but returns a bare 404 with no documentation, indicating internal-only use. Business/SMB accounts (property managers, hospitality) are onboarded through sales and an account manager rather than through self-service API keys.
p.name: Poplin

p.description: Popmeals (Pop Meals, operated by Farm To Fork Sdn Bhd) is a Malaysian food-delivery and cloud-kitchen brand offering popular meals at affordable prices through a central-kitchen model and a network of outlets across Malaysia and Southeast Asia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a consumer brand with a public ordering and support surface but no published developer/API program: domain-security posture was probed live, and no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal was found.
p.name: Popmeals

p.description: Popmenu is a restaurant technology platform offering websites, interactive and dynamic menus, online ordering, marketing automation, and menu management designed to turn a restaurant's web presence into a customer conversion engine. Popmenu promotes a Developer API that gives partners access to data on menus, guests, orders, and more for custom integrations, and it connects to applications such as Square, Toast, Google Analytics, Mailchimp, OpenTable, Resy, DoorDash, and Yelp, plus hundreds of others through partner integrations. That API is GraphQL rather than REST: a live single endpoint was verified at https://api.popmenu.com/graphql on 2026-08-13, mirrored at https://my.popmenu.com/graphql, returning HTTP 200 with vendor popmenu-ratelimit-* headers — but introspection and every query answer "unauthorized" without partner credentials, so the schema cannot be discovered publicly. No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, webhook catalog, MCP server, agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known/ document exists on any Popmenu host. Authentication, scopes, error codes and rate limits are undocumented, and get.popmenu.com/developer-api is a lead-capture form rather than a reference. Popmenu's engineering stack is Ruby on Rails with a React front end, and its entire marketing estate returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients.
p.name: Popmenu

p.description: Popp (Popp AI) is an API-first conversation engine for staffing and recruitment firms. It automates high-volume candidate interactions — screening tens of thousands of applicants, collecting and validating right-to-work and certification documents, running AI candidate analysis, auto-scheduling interviews with calendar sync, and re-qualifying dormant candidate databases — through a drag-and-drop workflow builder and a REST API. The platform exposes conversations, campaigns, documents, analysis, scheduling, and multi-step workflows over https://api.joinpopp.com/v1 with API-key authentication, SHA256-signed webhooks across four event categories, and a published remote MCP server for agent access. Backed by Techstars.
p.name: Popp

p.description: Poppi is an American prebiotic soda brand founded in Austin, Texas by Stephen and Allison Ellsworth, originally as Mother Beverage, rebranded to poppi in 2020 after a Shark Tank investment and acquired by PepsiCo in May 2025. Poppi sells direct to consumers from drinkpoppi.com, a Shopify storefront, and that storefront is where its machine-readable surface lives: poppi publishes agent instructions at /agents.md and /llms.txt, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and an anonymous remote MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp exposing 13 catalog, cart, checkout and order tools with full JSON Schema input contracts.
