s.description: Scanner is a cloud-native security data platform that indexes security logs directly in Amazon S3 to deliver full-text search across petabytes, continuous streaming threat detection, and programmatic and agent-native access to security data — an alternative to traditional SIEMs and data lakes. Its REST API (v1) covers searchable indexes, detection rules, event sinks, lookup tables, ad hoc queries, and query-capacity info, and it ships a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server plus a detection-rules-as-code CLI (scanner-cli). Authentication is a Scanner API key presented as an HTTP Bearer token; console SSO is brokered by Stytch (Okta, Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra, SCIM). SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant. Backed by CRV.
s.name: Scanner

s.description: ScanSource is an international technology distributor specializing in point-of-sale (POS), payments, barcode, physical security, unified communications, collaboration, telecom, and cloud services. Founded in 1992 in Greenville, South Carolina, ScanSource provides APIs that give partners real-time access to inventory, pricing, order management, and product information to automate the sales cycle and integrate with backend ERP systems and customer portals.
s.name: ScanSource

s.description: An independent Polymarket intelligence platform, operated by KotIQ OÜ, providing resolution-risk assessments on prediction markets through a documented OpenAPI 3.1 REST API. Resolution risk is the chance a market settles in a way its title does not lead a reader to expect — ambiguous rule language, an unverifiable resolution source, or a title that diverges from the rules. The API is an async create-and-poll surface with signed webhooks, a deterministic sandbox fixture catalog, a reconciled usage ledger, four deny-by-default token scopes and a required Idempotency-Key on its only billable write. The contract, an APIs.json index and an RFC 9727 api-catalog are all publicly retrievable; runtime access is private beta and feature-gated, so live calls require an entitled, allowlisted account. Read-only research only — no order placement, no custody, no trading advice.
s.name: Scanverity Resolution API

s.description: Scanwell was surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probing (2026-07-21) found no live API surface — the scanwellhealth.com domain associated with the Version One Ventures portfolio company (Scanwell Health, an at-home smartphone diagnostic-testing startup) now 301-redirects to an unrelated site, indicating the company is defunct, and the scanwell.com domain belongs to an unrelated freight-forwarding firm (Scanwell Logistics) that publishes no developer program.
s.name: Scanwell

s.description: Scape (Scape Wellness) is an on-demand wellness technology platform in Latin America that lets customers book professional spa experiences delivered to their home, apartment, hotel, Airbnb, office, or corporate event. Certified, identity-verified therapists arrive with all required equipment — professional massage table, towels, oils, and materials. The catalog spans relaxing, deep tissue, sports, prenatal, lymphatic drainage, reflexology, and couples massages; facials; body treatments; and combined facial-plus-massage experiences, alongside personal and corporate gift cards and workplace wellness programs. Scape operates in Mexico, Colombia, Chile, and the Dominican Republic via iOS and Android apps, with payments through MercadoPago and PayPal. It is a consumer booking platform and does not publish a public developer API or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.
s.name: Scape

s.description: Scarlet is Europe's only Notified Body specialised in software and AI-based medical devices. Operating at scarlet.cc, Scarlet certifies Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and AI as a Medical Device (AIaMD) under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), streamlining conformity assessment, CE marking, and certificate transfers for manufacturers who ship iteratively and release frequently. Backed by Creandum, Scarlet was built to bring modern, fast-moving regulatory certification to AI and software medical-technology companies. Scarlet is a regulatory and certification services provider; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.
s.name: Scarlet

s.description: SCB Statistics Sweden is Sweden’s official statistical agency, providing comprehensive data on the country’s demographics, economy, labor market, and more. It offers public access to a wide range of statistical datasets and APIs for developers to integrate official statistics into applications, research, and analysis. The agency ensures high-quality, up-to-date information for policymakers, businesses, and the public.
s.name: SCB Statistics Sweden

s.description: Scenario is a Paris- and San Francisco-headquartered AI platform for game asset generation founded in 2021 by Emmanuel de Maistre and Hervé Nivon. The Scenario REST API lets game studios and creative teams generate consistent, on-brand images, video, audio, and 3D assets, train custom LoRA models on their own reference art, automate batch asset pipelines, and integrate AI-generated visuals into production tools like Unity. Scenario aggregates 500+ AI models from 50+ providers behind a single workspace and API, with full commercial licensing for generated assets and enterprise SSO, SOC 2 Type II, and governance controls.
s.name: Scenario

s.description: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD. (Scenario X) is a financial-technology company building an AI- and quantum-computing-powered platform for financial risk analysis, stress testing, and regulatory reporting. The integrated platform is organized into four modules — Scenario (adverse market-condition design), PPNR (Pre-Provision Net Revenue projection), Risk (market, counterparty, credit, and operational risk), and Console (financial-data aggregation) — plus a quantum-computing offering for predictive financial modeling. It serves banks, insurers, family offices, independent wealth managers, and commodity traders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been found to date.
s.name: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING

s.description: Scene Health (formerly emocha Mobile Health, founded 2008 out of Johns Hopkins and rebranded in 2022) is a Maryland-based digital health company tackling medication nonadherence. Its MedEngagement platform pairs a patient mobile app with a human care team of pharmacists, nurses and health coaches: members record daily video check-ins of themselves taking their medication — a scaled, asynchronous form of Directly Observed Therapy — and the care team reviews each dose, captures side effects and symptoms, and works barriers such as cost, transportation and social determinants of health. Scene sells to health plans and Medicaid MCOs, health systems, public health departments, employers, and research and clinical-trial organizations, with programs covering hypertension, diabetes, asthma, tuberculosis, HIV, hepatitis C, sickle cell disease, opioid use disorder and transplant care. The company raised a $17.7M Series B in March 2023 led by ABS Capital Partners. Scene operates as a HIPAA Business Associate and maintains a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation audited by A-LIGN across all five trust services criteria. It publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; its software surface is the member and care-team application at app.emocha.com.
s.name: Scene Health

s.description: Scene Infrastructure Company is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
s.name: Scene Infrastructure Company

s.description: SceneRay Medical Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. is a Chinese medical-device and brain-computer-interface company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Suzhou Industrial Park. It designs and manufactures implantable neuromodulation systems, focusing on Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) devices and "brain-machine control chip" technology used to treat Parkinson's disease, movement disorders, epilepsy, and treatment-resistant psychiatric conditions. Its product line spans implantable pulse generators, programmable external controllers, and clinician programming systems. SceneRay reports over 100 international patents and 700+ total patent applications, with devices used across 18+ countries. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. As a medical hardware manufacturer, SceneRay publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or other machine-readable technical surface at the time of this enrichment pass.
s.name: SceneRay

s.description: Scentbird is a New York City-based monthly fragrance subscription service, founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator. Members receive a travel-size (8ml) designer fragrance each month for a flat subscription fee, selecting from a rotating catalog of hundreds of designer and niche perfume and cologne brands, and can also purchase full-size bottles, candles, and beauty products through the direct-to-consumer storefront. Scentbird operates as a consumer e-commerce and subscription brand; its public engineering presence is a GitHub organization of internal tooling and open-source forks (data-integration taps, shipping-API clients, Grails plugins), and it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.
s.name: ScentBird

s.description: SCG Cell Therapy Pte. Ltd. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Singapore, with operations across Singapore, China and Germany, developing novel immunotherapies for infectious diseases and the cancers they cause. The company targets the most common cancer-causing infections — Helicobacter pylori, human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) — and is advancing a pipeline of TCR-engineered T cell therapies, antibodies and therapeutic vaccines built on its proprietary GianTCR platform. Lead programs include SCG101, a first-in-class autologous HBV-specific TCR-T therapy targeting hepatitis B surface antigen in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma, and SCG142, a next-generation HPV E7-specific TCR-T therapy for HPV-associated solid tumors that received FDA IND clearance. SCG covers the full value chain from drug discovery and manufacturing through clinical development and commercialization. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract.
s.name: SCG Cell Therapy

s.description: Schaeffler Group is a German global Tier 1 automotive and industrial supplier headquartered in Herzogenaurach. Schaeffler designs and manufactures precision bearings, powertrain components, chassis applications, and e-mobility systems for the automotive and industrial sectors.
s.name: Schaeffler

s.description: Schedex is a workforce management platform built for food and beverage businesses, consolidating staff scheduling, shift management, attendance tracking, and payroll into a single mobile-first application. It offers mobile clock in/out with location technology, schedule optimization across multiple locations, real-time labor-cost tracking and reporting, automated wage and payroll calculation, leave requests and shift exchange, and a multilingual branded app, with the goal of reducing labor costs by up to 15 percent. Schedex was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.
s.name: Schedex

s.description: Scheduling Wizard is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
s.name: Scheduling Wizard

s.description: Schema Design is the practice of defining the structure, constraints, and semantics of data models used in APIs, databases, and data exchange formats. It encompasses schema-first API design approaches, data modeling methodologies, type systems, and tooling for creating, validating, and evolving data schemas. Key formats include JSON Schema, OpenAPI components/schemas, GraphQL types, Protocol Buffers, Apache Avro, and database DDL. Good schema design improves API consistency, enables automated validation, supports code generation, and facilitates interoperability between systems.
s.name: Schema Design

s.description: Schema Evolution is the practice of managing changes to data schemas over time while preserving compatibility between producers and consumers. It covers backward compatibility, forward compatibility, full compatibility, breaking change detection, schema migration strategies, and versioning patterns for REST APIs, event streaming (Kafka/Avro), GraphQL, database schemas, and Protocol Buffers. Effective schema evolution is critical for maintaining API contracts and enabling independent deployment of distributed system components.
s.name: Schema Evolution

s.description: Schema Free (schemaless) databases and APIs allow data to be stored and retrieved without a predefined fixed schema. Rather than enforcing structure at the database level, schema-free systems delegate schema management to the application layer. This enables rapid prototyping, flexible document storage, and agile development workflows. Key schema-free technologies include MongoDB (document store), Redis (key-value store), Apache Cassandra (wide-column store), Amazon DynamoDB (managed NoSQL), Elasticsearch (search/document store), and Apache CouchDB. While called "schemaless," these systems typically have implicit application-level schemas that must be managed carefully.
s.name: Schema Free

s.description: Schema validation is the practice of verifying that data structures conform to a defined schema, contract, or specification. In API development, schema validation ensures API requests and responses match declared OpenAPI, JSON Schema, AsyncAPI, or GraphQL specifications, enabling contract testing, governance, and runtime integrity. Key tools include AJV, Hyperjump JSON Schema, Spectral, and Schemathesis, each addressing different validation contexts from CLI pipelines to runtime API testing.
s.name: Schema Validation

s.description: Schema.org is a collaborative, community-driven project that creates and maintains a shared vocabulary for structured data on the web. Founded by Google, Microsoft, Yahoo, and Yandex in 2011, it provides types and properties that developers and webmasters use to annotate content in formats like JSON-LD, RDFa, and Microdata, enabling search engines and applications to better understand web content. The vocabulary currently consists of 800+ Types, 1500+ Properties, and covers domains including commerce, healthcare, organizations, events, creative works, and more. The Schema.org WebAPI type provides a standardized vocabulary for describing APIs in structured data.
s.name: Schema.org

s.description: A document-to-JSON extraction service. Upload a PDF or image, pick a preset or paste a JSON schema, and get typed fields back — vendor, totals, line items, packages, containers. Supports invoice, packing list, bank statement, and bill of lading presets plus custom schemas.
s.name: SchemaExtract

s.description: Structured data extraction API that converts unstructured text or HTML into JSON guaranteed to validate against a caller-supplied JSON Schema, or returns a typed error at no charge. Access is gated by x402 pay-per-call micropayments (USDC on Base), with no accounts or API keys.
s.name: SchemaSure

s.description: Schemathesis is a property-based API testing tool that automatically generates test cases from OpenAPI and GraphQL schemas to find bugs and specification violations. It uses the Hypothesis property-based testing framework to generate diverse, edge-case-covering test inputs from schema constraints, detecting server crashes, response schema violations, validation bypasses, and stateful bugs in multi-step workflows. Used by Netflix, SAP, Red Hat, IBM, and JetBrains.
s.name: Schemathesis

s.description: Schematic is a monetization platform that lets developers implement pricing once so that go-to-market teams can control pricing, packaging and entitlements without code changes. It decouples pricing from code: engineering integrates the entitlement and metering layer, and product, sales and finance then define plans, feature access and usage limits without shipping a release. The platform covers feature flags and entitlement checks, plan and package definition, usage metering and billing integration, with an official Stripe App for entitlement management. Schematic raised $6.5M in April 2026.
s.name: Schematic

s.description: Schematic Labs was a San Francisco consumer music startup founded in 2010, best known as the maker of SoundTracking, an "Instagram for songs" mobile app for sharing the music you are listening to. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), Accel Partners, and SoftBank Capital with roughly $5.9M raised, it was acquired by Rhapsody in August 2014 and wound down as a standalone company. Today soundtracking.com redirects to napster.com (Rhapsody's successor brand) and schematiclabs.com is a parked domain. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this profile records the company's place in the GV portfolio graph.
s.name: Schematic Labs

s.description: Schneider Electric Exchange is a developer platform providing APIs for EcoStruxure energy management, building automation, industrial IoT, and commerce partner integrations. The Exchange platform enables partners and developers to build integrations with Schneider Electric products and services. APIs span EcoStruxure data services (IT Expert, Facility Expert, Transformer Expert, Energy Contextualized Data) and Partner Commerce APIs for product catalog, inventory, pricing, orders, quotes, and marketplace integrations. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 with client credentials for Partner APIs and subscription-based API keys for EcoStruxure data APIs.

s.name: Schneider National

s.description: Schnitzer Steel Industries, now rebranded as Radius Recycling (acquired by Toyota Tsusho in 2025), is one of the largest manufacturers and exporters of recycled metal products in North America. The company processes scrap metal from automotive and industrial sources for use in steelmaking, operating 103 recycling facilities including the Pick-n-Pull auto parts chain and Cascade Steel Rolling Mills in McMinnville, Oregon. Schnitzer/Radius Recycling does not expose a public developer API or developer portal.
s.name: Schnitzer Steel Industries

s.description: SchoolAI is an AI platform built specifically for K-12 and higher education that helps teachers personalize learning, monitor student progress in real time, and provide timely interventions while keeping educators in control of student safety. Its core surfaces include Spaces (teacher-designed AI learning environments), Mission Control (a live dashboard of student engagement and where learners are struggling), PowerUps (focused AI activities for creation, practice, and exploration), a browser extension, and professional-learning programs. The platform integrates with LMS and identity systems via Canvas LTI, Google Classroom, and Google Workspace, and is FERPA, COPPA, SOC 2 Type 2, 1EdTech TrustEd Apps, FIPPA, and ESSA Tier 3 validated. Backed by Homebrew; surfaced as a portfolio-lead company in the API Evangelist network.
s.name: SchoolAI

s.description: SchoolCare provides a unified Student Health Record Platform for K‑12 schools, parents, and healthcare providers. It enables secure digital charting of student health information, immunizations, medications, and care coordination, complying with HIPAA and FERPA. The solution connects families and school staff to streamline health data management and improve student wellbeing across districts.
s.name: SchoolCare

s.description: Schoology (a PowerSchool company) is a K-12 LMS. The Schoology REST API exposes districts, schools, buildings, users, groups, courses, sections, enrollments, events, blog posts, discussions, updates, media albums, documents, assignments, grades, grading scales, rubrics, attendance, submissions, pages, SCORM packages, friend requests, invites, networks, grading periods, roles, private messaging, search, and resource collections.
s.name: Schoology

s.description: SchoolsFirst Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Tustin, California, serving educators and their families. Founded in 1934 as Orange County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in California and one of the largest in the United States, with roughly $31.9 billion in assets, over 1.4 million members, and about 70 branches. It offers savings, checking, loans, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services. Like most US credit unions, SchoolsFirst runs no first-party public developer program: probes of developer.schoolsfirstfcu.org fail to resolve and /developers returns 404, and its api.schoolsfirstfcu.org host is the member online-banking login backend, not a documented API. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity, MX, Akoya) rather than a direct API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented at this time.
s.name: SchoolsFirst FCU

s.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.
s.name: Schrödinger

s.description: Schuettflix is a German digital logistics platform for the construction industry, founded in 2018 in Guetersloh. It operates a neutral B2B marketplace that connects construction companies, bulk-material suppliers, freight forwarders and waste-disposal firms in a single fully digital workflow. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers order sand, gravel and crushed stone with transparent real-time pricing, coordinate dispatch and transport, capture delivery documentation, manage routes, and handle mineral-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling of construction materials. The company digitizes the traditionally analog and fragmented process of procuring and delivering bulk goods, earning a commission on the transactions facilitated through its platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.
s.name: Schuettflix

s.description: Schwarz Charite Health Data GmbH is a German health-data joint venture announced on 2026-03-20 by Charite - Universitaetsmedizin Berlin and Schwarz Digits, the IT and digital arm of the Schwarz Group (Lidl, Kaufland, STACKIT). Schwarz Digits holds 75 percent and Charite 25 percent. The venture takes the HIVEPRO platform to market: a clinical data platform whose core is an openEHR-based Clinical Data Repository queried with Archetype Query Language (AQL), able to exchange data over HL7 FHIR - including the German Medical Informatics Initiative (MII) core dataset - and to feed OMOP-compliant analytics. HIVEPRO harmonises and networks records that are otherwise trapped in incompatible hospital source systems, and is delivered as a managed cloud service running on STACKIT's sovereign cloud so that data residency and control stay in Germany under European data-protection rules. The technical lineage comes from the BMBF-funded HiGHmed consortium, active since 2016. openEHR International lists the company as an industry partner. As of this pass the company has no website, developer portal, documentation host or public API of its own; every public surface it has is a press page on its parent's site.
s.name: Schwarz Charite Health Data

s.description: Schwarz IT (Schwarz IT KG, Neckarsulm, Germany) is the IT service company of the Schwarz Group (Lidl, Kaufland), describing itself on GitHub as "the technological heartbeat of the companies of Schwarz Group". It is listed as an affiliated company of Schwarz Digits, the group's IT and digital division, and hosts the Schwarz Digits website. Its public GitHub organization publishes the Schwarz API rule definitions for the Spectral API linter (api-linter-rules), a Spectral IntelliJ plugin, an API-linting-as-a-service project, a Kotlin RFC 9457 problem-details library, community STACKIT Go client and Terraform provider, and SAP/ABAP open-source components.
s.name: Schwarz IT

s.description: Science 37 operates a decentralized, direct-to-patient clinical research platform — the first and only FDA-inspected direct-to-patient site — that delivers clinical trials to participants wherever they are. Its Metasite and Agile Clinical Trial operating model combine patient recruitment, research-grade nursing, telemedicine, eConsent, ePRO, wearable/device integration, and EHR data capture into a single end-to-end SaaS platform used by sponsors and CROs. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company has supported 200+ trials across many therapeutic areas. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment (developer./api.science37.com do not resolve); this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.
s.name: Science 37 *

s.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.
s.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)

s.description: Science Corporation is a neurotechnology company founded in 2021 by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, developing brain-computer interfaces and implantable neural devices to restore vision, cognition, and mobility (its PRIMA retinal implant and biohybrid BCI are its marquee programs). Its developer-facing surface is the Synapse Protocol, a flexible gRPC / Protocol Buffers standard API — paired with the Neural Data Transport Protocol (NDTP) — for discovering neural interface devices on a local network, configuring on-device signal chains (broadband source, spike detector, electrical/optical stimulation, disk writer, camera nodes), and streaming high-throughput neural data over UDP. Official client libraries ship for Python (science-synapse, including the synapsectl CLI), TypeScript, and C++, all generated from the open protobuf definitions in the sciencecorp GitHub org.
s.name: Science Corporation

s.description: Science Exchange is an R&D supplier orchestration and procurement platform for life-sciences organizations. It runs a marketplace of 3,800+ pre-qualified scientific service providers under a single master service agreement, and streamlines supplier sourcing, onboarding, contracting, compliance, and payment. The platform integrates with ERP (SAP, Oracle, Workday), P2P (Ariba, Coupa), and SSO/SAML identity systems, and exposes a read-only Providers REST API (v1) that lets scientific-service suppliers pull their RFQs, quotes, services, facilities, line items, ratings, tags, and users. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California; backed by a16z, Index Ventures, and Union Square Ventures.
s.name: Science Exchange

s.description: The Science Museum Group operates five UK science and technology museums: the Science Museum (London), the Science and Industry Museum (Manchester), the National Railway Museum (York), the National Science and Media Museum (Bradford), and Locomotion (Shildon). The group provides an open Collection API giving developers programmatic access to over 7 million objects, people, and documents in the museum collections via a JSONAPI-compliant REST interface. The API is free to use and supports searching, filtering, and retrieval of collection items with rich metadata, images, and curatorial notes.
s.name: Science Museum Group

s.description: Science On Call provides 24/7 AI-powered technology support built specifically for restaurants. Combining intelligent automation with human experts, the service helps restaurant staff triage and resolve operational technology issues across point-of-sale (POS) systems, kitchen display systems (KDS), loyalty programs, staff scheduling, online ordering, training platforms, phones, internet, and Wi-Fi. Staff reach support anytime via text, email, or phone with no app or login required, and issues are typically resolved in about 25 minutes. Science On Call is a Techstars-backed company; billing is handled through a hosted customer portal. This profile currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine- readable specification surface.
s.name: Science On Call

s.description: ScienceLogic is an AIOps and IT operations company whose ScienceLogic AI Platform — rebranded in 2026 as the Skylar family — covers infrastructure and application observability, network configuration and compliance, and workflow automation. Skylar One (formerly SL1) is the observability platform, with a REST API and a GraphQL API served from the customer's own Administration Portal, All-In-One Appliance or Database Server; ScienceLogic states that GraphQL is the forward path and that the REST API is now limited to bug fixes. Skylar Compliance (formerly Restorepoint, acquired by ScienceLogic) publishes a 314-operation OpenAPI 3.0 contract for configuration backup, change detection, compliance policy testing and device restore. Skylar Automation (formerly PowerFlow) handles ITSM and CMDB integration, and Skylar AI adds Advisor and Analytics on top. The ScienceLogic GitHub organization also publishes an MCP server that exposes read-only Skylar One and Skylar Compliance tools to AI agents. Products are deployed on customer appliances, SaaS, or private/public cloud, and are licensed per managed device per month.
s.name: ScienceLogic

s.description: Scientific Games is the global lottery company serving government-sponsored lotteries on six continents in 50+ countries with instant scratch games, draw-based and terminal-generated games, iLottery and mobile platforms, Central Gaming Systems (CGS), retail point-of-sale technology, sports betting solutions, loyalty/CRM, analytics, and managed/partner services. The company traces to Scientific Games Holdings (founded 1973) and was merged into Scientific Games Corporation in 2001 alongside the WMS, Bally and NYX/OpenBet acquisitions. In April 2022 the lottery business was carved out and sold to Brookfield Business Partners for $6.05 billion, taking Scientific Games private; the residual gaming and digital businesses were renamed Light & Wonder (NASDAQ/ASX: LNW), and the social casino subsidiary SciPlay (spun off via IPO in 2019) was reabsorbed and later sits within Light & Wonder. Today Scientific Games operates as an independent, Brookfield-owned, pure-play lottery technology and services company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with instant ticket manufacturing in Alpharetta and Montreal. Scientific Games does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, or public SDKs; customer integrations are delivered under direct contract with government lottery operators.
s.name: Scientific Games

s.description: Scientist.com provides a digital backbone for life science research, offering a unified platform that supports the full drug development lifecycle—from discovery and preclinical studies through clinical trials, manufacturing, and commercial operations. The platform integrates vendor networks, guided buying, workflow automation, regulatory compliance, and AI-driven insights, enabling organizations to source, manage, and scale external research efficiently.
s.name: Scientist.com

s.description: SCiFi Foods was a San Francisco Bay Area food-technology startup, founded in 2019 by Joshua March (CEO) and Kasia Gora (CTO), that developed cultivated (cell-cultured) beef blended with plant-based ingredients to make burgers close to the taste of conventional meat. The company used a proprietary platform built on gene-editing tools such as CRISPR to create and screen hundreds of animal cell lines each month. Backed by a16z among others, SCiFi Foods raised roughly $40M before ceasing operations in June 2024; its cell lines were later released to academia via the Good Food Institute. The company is defunct and exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface.
s.name: SCiFi Foods

s.description: Sciket (科研市集, operated by STAREK Scientific / 勢得科研股份有限公司) is Taiwan's specialized online marketplace for scientific research and technology procurement. The platform integrates thousands of global suppliers and millions of products — laboratory consumables and glassware, instruments and equipment, chemical reagents and materials, and industrial tools and hardware — into a single digitized purchasing, sourcing, and fast-shipment service for research labs, academic institutions, quality-control teams, and manufacturers. It offers enterprise purchasing, global sourcing, PunchOut system integration, monthly invoicing, and laboratory-construction services. Sciket runs an internal storefront/API host (api.sciket.com) but does not publish a public developer API program, documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with verified identity and domain-security data.
s.name: Sciket

s.description: Scimar (Scimar Ltd., formerly styled SciMar) is a privately held Canadian life-sciences company founded in 2009 with its head office in Dauphin, Manitoba and research laboratories in Winnipeg. It commercializes the work of co-founder and Chief Scientific Officer Dr. W. Wayne Lautt, who in 1996 identified hepatalin — known in the literature as hepatic insulin-sensitizing substance, or HISS — a liver hormone Scimar describes as the missing link in nutrient partitioning, prediabetes and type 2 diabetes. Its pipeline pairs diagnostics with therapeutics: SciMar NuPa Test, a diagnostic test meal that measures hepatalin production and is in Phase 2 clinical trials in Canada; SciMar NuPa Renew, a pre-meal pharmaceutical preparing for Phase 2B; SciMar NuPa Daily, an antioxidant supplement intended to protect hepatalin production; and Hepatalin-S, a synthetic hepatalin for advanced-stage disease. Alongside the science the company runs the Wellness Transformation Network, a community outreach program with nonprofits, Indigenous communities and Manitoba businesses, and produces the Webby-nominated science podcast Inside the Breakthrough hosted by Dan Riskin. Scimar publishes no product or developer API and operates no developer program. The machine-readable surface on scimar.ca is CMS-provided: a served llms.txt generated by All in One SEO, the anonymously readable WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that returns news stories, pages, team profiles, media and site search as JSON, and a WordPress MCP Adapter that advertises two Model Context Protocol endpoints plus RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 OAuth discovery documents — all of which are authentication-gated.
s.name: Scimar

s.description: Scimplify is a Bengaluru-based advanced specialty chemicals company that combines deep chemical expertise, software, and global manufacturing capacity to make complex chemical supply predictable at scale. Founded in 2023, it operates as a contract research (CRO) and contract manufacturing (CMO) organization across the specialty-chemicals lifecycle, serving pharmaceutical, agrochemical, flavors & fragrances, industrial, beauty & personal care, food & nutrition, dyes & pigments, oleochemicals, flame retardants, and critical-metals industries. Its integrated Scinode platform, IONS R&D and ATOMS manufacturing ecosystems, and Scira AI agentic layer coordinate discovery, sourcing, and production. Scimplify publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its web, content, and domain-security surface.
s.name: Scimplify

s.description: SciQuest was a spend-management and e-procurement software company founded in 1995 that grew into a source-to-settle suite spanning e-procurement, sourcing, contract lifecycle management, spend analytics, accounts payable and supplier management. In 2017 SciQuest rebranded as JAGGAER and consolidated its products into the JAGGAER One source-to-pay platform. JAGGAER exposes REST/JSON public APIs (request/response and event-driven push), cXML transactional messaging, an OAuth 2.0-secured Advanced Sourcing Optimizer (ASO) API, and 40+ prebuilt ERP connectors (SAP, Oracle, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite, Ellucian). This profile enriches the SciQuest lead against its live successor developer surface.
s.name: SciQuest

s.description: Scispot is a cloud-native laboratory data platform and operating system for modern life science labs. It provides an API-first architecture combining Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) and Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) capabilities with over 250 pre-built instrument connectors and 7,000+ application integrations via its GLUE layer. Labs use Scispot to centralize and activate their data, automate experiment workflows, manage samples, sequences, and chemical structures programmatically, and integrate with clinical data standards including HL7 FHIR, HL7 v2, and ASTM protocols.
s.name: Scispot

s.description: Sciwind Biosciences (Hangzhou Sciwind Biosciences Co., Ltd.) is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Hangzhou, China, with a US office in San Ramon, California, focused on discovering, developing, and delivering innovative therapeutics for weight management and metabolic disease. Its pipeline spans obesity, type 2 diabetes, and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), led by the GLP-1 receptor agonist Ecnoglutide (advancing through Phase III trials). The company operates proprietary drug-discovery platforms including BiasVantage (biased agonist discovery), OralVantage (oral peptide delivery), and HaleVantage (half-life extension), with 14+ pipeline programs, 120+ researchers, and 110+ patents. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public API or developer platform surface.
s.name: SCIWIND

s.description: Scodix is a digital print enhancement (embellishment) technology company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Rosh HaAyin, Israel. It manufactures the Scodix Ultra series of digital embellishment presses and the Scodix Studio web-to-print software, enabling decorative effects across 17 applications including Spot UV, foil, glitter, metallic, cast-and-cure, braille and variable data. Scodix serves commercial print, folding-carton packaging, publishing and web-to-print markets with over 400 installations worldwide, and went public on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) in 2021. Scodix Studio exposes integration APIs for connecting embellishment workflows to MIS and web-to-print storefronts, but Scodix does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve API documentation.
s.name: Scodix

s.description: Scondoo is a German consumer cashback and coupon platform, operated by acardo group AG, that lets shoppers earn money back on everyday grocery and drugstore purchases. Users browse exclusive cashback deals in the scondoo iOS and Android apps, buy the qualifying products at any supermarket or drugstore (Kaufland, REWE, EDEKA, Netto, Aldi, Lidl, dm, Rossmann and many more), then snap a photo of the receipt to have the cashback credited to their balance and paid out via bank transfer or PayPal. The service is consumer-facing and mobile-only; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or partner integration surface.
s.name: Scondoo

s.description: Scoop (Scoop Technologies, Inc.) is a San Francisco based future-of-work company backed by Index Ventures whose Scoop for Work product is a hybrid-work scheduling assistant. It plugs into employees existing calendar and Slack so teams can coordinate great in-office days, sync schedules, and see who will be in, while giving HR and workplace leaders analytics on office usage and hybrid work trends. Originally launched in 2015 as a carpool/commute service (takescoop.com), the company pivoted to hybrid workplace coordination. Note: as of this enrichment pass the product domain scoopforwork.com returns HTTP 410 Gone with a broken TLS certificate, and the legacy takescoop.com domain is parked for sale; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface could be found.
s.name: Scoop

s.description: Content Curation Service
s.name: Scoop.it

s.description: Scoopola was an early-stage consumer startup backed by 500 Startups (Batch 2, June 2011), pitched as "the HotelTonight for live music and theater" — a mobile app for discovering and buying last-minute, discounted tickets to local live-music and theater events. The company appears defunct; its associated web domains (getwillcall.com and scoopola.com) no longer resolve, and there is no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline found no live API to catalog.
s.name: Scoopola

s.description: Scope (Scope Inspection Ltd, London) is an AI-native inspection platform for the Testing, Inspection, and Certification (TIC) industry and heavy-asset operators. It captures field data through voice, video, and forms (offline-capable), extracts structured data from P&IDs, ASME forms, and inspection drawings, surfaces historical inspection context, and automates report generation in Word, Excel, and PDF. The product pushes results into enterprise CMMS/EAM systems via webhooks and prebuilt connectors, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time. Backed by Index Ventures and Y Combinator; raised a ~$18-20M round led by Index Ventures in 2026.
s.name: Scope

s.description: Scope3 is the source of truth for greenhouse-gas emissions data in media and advertising, and operates Scope3 Interchange, an agentic advertising platform where buyer agents and seller storefronts transact on the open Ad Context Protocol (AdCP). Its APIs let buyers, publishers and platforms measure the carbon footprint of every ad impression and creative across channels, benchmark against country/channel percentiles, and run AI-driven programmatic advertising end to end. Scope3 publishes four OpenAPI documents across three surfaces: the Carbon Calculator (Measurement) API at api.scope3.com/v2, the AI Impact Measurement API at aiapi.scope3.com (energy, gCO2e and water per inference), and the Interchange Buyer and Storefront v2 APIs at api.interchange.io with 481 operations between them. Interchange is built for AI agents as primary callers: hosted remote MCP endpoints with OAuth (RFC 8414 metadata, dynamic client registration, PKCE), an A2A agent card, three published Agent Skills, a documented error envelope, IETF draft-7 rate-limit headers and a published IU pricing model. Backed by GV.
s.name: Scope3

s.description: Scopely is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures, bessemer-venture-partners, felicis, techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
s.name: Scopely

s.description: Scopio (Scopio LLC) is a New York-based global visual-content marketplace and creative-talent platform, founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global. It connects businesses with a network of 25,000+ vetted photographers and visual artists across 172 countries and a library of more than three million authentic, diverse stock images that can be licensed under standard, extended, and editorial licenses. Brands including Disney, Microsoft, and Meta use Scopio to hire creative talent and source unique imagery, with AI used to sort, tag, title, and feature contributed work. Scopio operates as a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile marketplace (Shopify-hosted storefront plus iOS/Android artist apps); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
s.name: Scopio

s.description: Scorce is a Mexico-based API aggregation platform that gives businesses a single integration point to connect to multiple Latin American and global identity APIs for customer authentication, KYC (Know Your Customer), digital identity verification, and fraud prevention. The platform lets teams connect in under 24 hours, obtain provider trials, and monitor API performance across providers from one unified dashboard. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Puebla, Mexico, Scorce is backed by 500 Global, Finnovista, and Tenity.
s.name: Scorce

s.description: Score is an open-source, platform-agnostic workload specification developed under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox program. It provides a developer-centric YAML specification that enables teams to define application workloads once and deploy them across multiple container platforms including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and cloud runtimes without environment-specific configuration drift. The score-spec organization provides reference CLI implementations (score-compose and score-k8s) that translate Score YAML into platform-specific manifests, eliminating YAML bloat and reducing cognitive load for platform engineering teams.
s.name: Score

s.description: ScoreBig is an online event-ticket resale marketplace owned by TicketNetwork, selling tickets to live sports, concert, and theater events with an emphasis on transparent, all-in pricing (no extra fees or hidden costs) and a money-back guarantee. Its parent, TicketNetwork, operates the Mercury Web Services API and Mercury Retail integration platform, an API-driven, real-time ticket-inventory feed offered to partners under contract. ScoreBig itself is a consumer storefront and does not publish a public developer API; Mercury is partner-gated behind a sales/onboarding contact form with a sandbox provided to approved integrators. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.
s.name: ScoreBig (TicketNetwork)

s.description: Scorecard is a simulation and evaluation platform for building, testing, and deploying frontier AI agents. Teams run their agents through thousands of realistic scenarios, judge outputs with configurable AI, human, and heuristic metrics, and ship new capabilities with confidence. The platform organizes work into Projects, Testsets, Testcases, Metrics, Runs, Records, Scores, and Systems, and exposes a REST API (bearer API keys prefixed ak_) plus official Python, TypeScript/Node, and Go SDKs, a hosted MCP server, tracing integrations for LangChain, the Vercel AI SDK, and the Claude Agent SDK, and a GitHub Actions integration for evals in CI. Scorecard was founded to solve AI agent evaluation at scale and is backed by Kindred Ventures.
s.name: Scorecard

s.description: ScoreData Corporation is a Palo Alto based predictive-analytics and AI/ML platform company founded in 2014 by Danny Yang, Vas Bhandarkar, Mudit Chandra and Prasanta Behera. Its flagship ScoreFast platform, paired with iMaaS (intelligent Models as a Service), lets cross-functional AI teams develop, deploy, monitor, manage and govern machine-learning models in production across Banking, Insurance and Healthcare. ScoreFast uses patented dynamic machine learning that learns continuously, removing the need to manually regenerate predictive models, and its applications can be deployed across in-store, mobile, web, kiosk, chatbot and cloud contact-center touchpoints. ScoreData is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company awaiting a public developer/API surface.
s.name: ScoreData

s.description: Scoreloop was a Munich, Germany based mobile social gaming company that provided a cross-platform SDK adding social features to mobile games - online leaderboards, achievements, player challenges, friend invites, and in-game virtual currency and monetization. The Scoreloop SDK supported Android, iOS, Windows Phone, Samsung Bada, Marmalade/AirPlay, and Unity 3D, and at its peak was used by more than 3,000 game developers. The company was backed by earlybird and was acquired by Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 2011; the standalone Scoreloop platform and its developer service were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead - there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remaining (the scoreloop.com domain now serves a suspended page and no developer host resolves), so no API artifacts are available to harvest.
s.name: Scoreloop

s.description: SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) is a set of technical standards for e-learning software products. Originally developed by the Advanced Distributed Learning (ADL) Initiative, SCORM defines how online learning content and Learning Management Systems (LMS) communicate with each other, enabling interoperability between authoring tools, content packages, and LMS platforms. Key versions include SCORM 1.2 and SCORM 2004, with xAPI (Tin Can) as a modern successor.
s.name: SCORM

s.description: Scorpion is an American marketing technology company that provides revenue-focused advertising, marketing, and software services to local and multi-location businesses in home services, legal, franchise, and healthcare verticals. Founded in 2001 by Rustin Kretz and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah (with major operations in Valencia, California), Scorpion pairs done-for-you digital advertising and SEO with its own AI-driven platform. In 2024 it launched RevenueMAX, an AI marketing platform built on Scorpion AI that aligns marketing spend, intake, and long-term revenue, and in 2025 it introduced Scorpion Convert, an AI intake-and-conversion product that automates response, scheduling, and voice/messaging engagement for missed leads. Scorpion is a services-and-platform provider; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.
s.name: Scorpion

s.description: Scorpion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision oncology biotechnology company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It pursued what it called Precision Oncology 2.0 — integrating target discovery, medicinal chemistry and translational medicine to produce mutant-selective small-molecule cancer drugs — led by STX-478, an oral mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor in Phase 1/2 trials for breast cancer and other advanced solid tumors, and STX-721, a covalent EGFR/HER2 exon 20 inhibitor. In January 2025 Eli Lilly agreed to acquire Scorpion and its PI3K-alpha program in a transaction valued at up to $2.5 billion, with the non-PI3K-alpha pipeline and staff spun into a separate independent company. Scorpion is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and its own domain now redirects to the acquirer's announcement.
s.name: Scorpion Therapeutics

s.description: Scotiabank is one of Canada's leading financial institutions and a major international bank. Through its Scotia TranXact developer portal, Scotiabank provides APIs for corporate and commercial customers to integrate banking capabilities into their treasury management, ERP, and CRM systems. APIs cover wire payments, real-time payments via INTERAC e-Transfer, EFT payments, account balance and transaction data, account validation, and payment track and trace.
s.name: Scotiabank

s.description: Scott (by Juno Labs Inc.) is a Y Combinator (F25) planning workspace for engineering teams that build with coding agents. Teams sync recent local agent sessions, push a coding-agent thread into a shareable "planspace", align on design intent through Sync Chat, comments, reviews and approvals, then pull the reviewed context back into execution. Scott ships a first-party CLI/plugin (curl-installed) that wires a Scott skill, rule, and hosted MCP server into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini, plus a GitHub App that reviews pull requests against planspace design intent. This profile enriches the provider from its public REST API (api.tryscott.ai, 139 operations), docs, CLI, MCP surface, and security posture.
s.name: Scott Ai

s.description: Scott Foresman was a leading elementary educational publisher for PreK through Grade 6 across all subject areas. Founded in 1896, the company became part of Pearson PLC in 1996. In 2019, Pearson spun off its U.S.-based K-12 courseware business, which was rebranded as Savvas Learning Company in 2020. Scott Foresman's iconic educational content — including the "Dick and Jane" reading series and basal reading programs — now lives under the Savvas Learning brand. No public developer API is currently available.
s.name: Scott Foresman

s.description: Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks (SSEN) is the SSE plc electricity networks business in the United Kingdom, operating the poles-and-wires layer rather than selling energy. SSEN Distribution is the licensed Distribution Network Operator for two GB licence areas — Scottish Hydro Electric Power Distribution (SHEPD) in the north of Scotland and Southern Electric Power Distribution (SEPD) in central southern England — serving over 3.9 million homes and businesses, while SSEN Transmission owns and operates the high-voltage transmission system for the north of Scotland. Its API posture is the classic network-distributor split — grid and market data are genuinely open, consumer data is not offered at all. SSEN runs a CKAN open data portal whose anonymous Action API serves 45 datasets, an anonymous real-time outage API behind Power Track, a key-gated near-real-time power-flow API (NeRDA) covering EHV/HV/LV networks, and an Opendatasoft Explore API over 60 transmission datasets. There is no consumer data-portability mandate in Great Britain equivalent to the Australian Consumer Data Right or Ontario's Green Button regulation, and SSEN publishes no API through which a third party can obtain an individual customer's usage or billing data. What Britain mandated instead is infrastructure and disclosure — smart meter traffic runs through the licensed Smart DCC monopoly, and Ofgem's Data Best Practice licence condition under RIIO-ED2 obliges network licensees to treat data assets as Presumed Open subject to Open Data Triage. SSEN implements that obligation visibly — it became the first DNO to publish full smart meter half-hourly consumption data, aggregated to no fewer than five properties per LV feeder, and attaches published Open Data Triage records to its datasets.
s.name: Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks

s.description: ScottishPower (Scottish Power Limited, Glasgow) is one of the "Big Six" British energy companies and has been wholly owned by Spain's Iberdrola since 2007. It is unusual in the post-liberalisation UK market for still spanning three regulated roles at once: ScottishPower Energy Retail supplies electricity and gas to millions of British homes and businesses; SP Energy Networks is the licensed distribution network operator for central and southern Scotland (SP Distribution), Merseyside, Cheshire and North Wales (SP Manweb), plus the transmission owner for southern Scotland (SP Transmission); and ScottishPower Renewables develops and operates onshore and offshore wind. That structure produces the sharpest possible version of this sector's split, and the split is the finding. On the consumer side there is nothing — Britain has no Consumer Data Right, no Green Button mandate and no consumer energy data-portability obligation of any kind, and ScottishPower publishes no developer portal, no self-serve API programme and no documented way for a third party to obtain an individual customer's usage or billing data. developer.scottishpower.co.uk, developers.scottishpower.co.uk, data.scottishpower.co.uk and docs.scottishpower.co.uk do not resolve at all, api.scottishpower.co.uk exists in DNS but returns HTTP 403, and www.scottishpower.co.uk returns HTTP 403 to every anonymous client on every path including /robots.txt. The only public account of ScottishPower's API programme is a WSO2 customer story describing an API Manager deployment used to expose services to commercial partners — an internal, partner-gated estate, not a developer programme. On the network side the picture inverts completely. Ofgem's Data Best Practice Guidance, made a licence condition under the RIIO-ED2 price control (Special Licence Condition 9.5), obliges electricity network licensees to treat their data as "presumed open", and SP Energy Networks has actually built that: the SP Energy Networks Open Data Portal at spenergynetworks.opendatasoft.com serves 150 datasets — embedded capacity register, network flow, historic substation demand, LV monitoring, smart-meter penetration, generation heat maps, flexibility and connections data — through a live, fully anonymous Opendatasoft Explore API v2.1 with a real OpenAPI 3.0.3 contract, CORS wide open, a 5,000 request/day anonymous quota, a DCAT-AP catalogue export, and an SP Energy Networks Open Data Licence based on Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Britain mandated the infrastructure and the network data, not the data right — ScottishPower is the proof. Its smart-meter obligation runs through the Smart DCC and the Smart Energy Code, which is an infrastructure monopoly for licensed parties rather than a consumer data right, and no public register entry or endpoint for that obligation could be verified from outside.
s.name: ScottishPower

s.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.
s.name: Scout

s.description: Scout RFP is a strategic sourcing and supplier engagement platform founded in 2014 and acquired by Workday in 2019, where it now ships as Workday Strategic Sourcing. The product covers sourcing events (RFPs/RFIs/RFQs and auctions), supplier management, contracts, projects, spend categories, awards, and supplier payments. Its public developer platform exposes a JSON:API-conformant REST API across eleven versioned services — Suppliers, Events, Reports, Contracts, Projects, Payments, Fields, Awards, Attachments, and Spend Categories — plus a SCIM 2.0 user-provisioning API. Authentication is by company API key plus a per-user personal token, all calls are HTTPS/JSON:API, cursor paginated, and rate limited to five requests per second. The legacy v3 API on api.scoutrfp.com was sunset April 18, 2025 in favor of the versioned services on api.us.workdayspend.com (with EU and CA regional hosts).
s.name: Scout RFP (Workday Strategic Sourcing)

s.description: Scout.fm (Scout FM) was a podcast-curation startup whose iOS, Android, Alexa and CarPlay apps turned podcasts into personalized, radio-like stations using AI-driven recommendations across genres such as news, sports and true crime. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Precursor Ventures, Advancit Capital and Samsung NEXT (roughly $1.4M raised), the company was acquired by Apple in September 2020 and subsequently shut down, with its apps pulled from every platform. The scout.fm domain no longer resolves and the company publishes no developer, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is nothing left to enrich.
s.name: Scout.fm

s.description: Scoutbee is an AI-powered supplier discovery and procurement intelligence platform that helps enterprise buyers instantly find, vet, and connect with trusted suppliers. Founded in 2015 in Berlin, Germany, Scoutbee uses large language models, knowledge-graph technology, and a global supplier network to power supplier discovery, sourcing project execution (Streamline), and a centralized supplier data foundation (DeepSee), surfaced through the Scoutbee Intelligence Platform. Its AI gives procurement, sourcing, and category-management teams recommendations for suppliers matched on qualifications, risk, certifications, sustainability, diversity, cost, and experience. Scoutbee integrates with SAP Ariba guided sourcing and, following its October 2025 acquisition by Coupa, is being embedded into the Coupa Supplier Portal. Scoutbee does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile captures its public identity and web surface.
s.name: Scoutbee

s.description: Scouter is a Mexican online marketplace, founded in 2021 in Guadalajara, for discovering and booking unique locations — houses, mansions, studios, terraces, haciendas, rooftops and more — for audiovisual productions, events, photo shoots and workshops across Mexico. It connects brands, agencies and production companies with the owners of over 1,500 spaces, handling quotes and reservations directly via WhatsApp (no public list prices, 8-hour minimum booking). Clients have included Netflix, HBO, Puma, Nike and Grupo Modelo. Backed by 500 Global (500 LatAm "Somos Lucha" Batch 16). The public product is a consumer/host web app at wearescouter.com; it exposes no public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched.
s.name: Scouter

s.description: Scoutzie is a Y Combinator-founded company (2012) led by Kirill Zubovsky. It launched as a curated marketplace connecting startups with top mobile designers and developers, operating from 2012 to 2020, and has since transformed into an AI-powered MVP (minimum viable product) development agency that builds and ships startup products in roughly two weeks. Today Scoutzie sells product-development services, an MVP Agent, founder training, and SEO consulting rather than a public developer API. It was surfaced through the a16z portfolio graph and enriched here as an API Evangelist network company profile.
s.name: Scoutzie

s.name: Scoville

s.description: Scrapfly is a web scraping API platform that enables effortless collection of web data with battle-tested APIs that scale. It provides capabilities for scraping web pages, capturing screenshots, and extracting structured data with AI assistance to handle anti-bot measures and JavaScript rendering. One API key unlocks five APIs: Web Scraping (anti-bot unblocker), Cloud Browser (CDP), Screenshot, Extraction, and Crawler. Scrapfly operates globally with proxies across 190+ countries.
s.name: Scrapfly

s.description: ScrapingAnt is a web-data infrastructure platform operated by DATAANT that puts headless Chrome rendering, a rotating pool of 3M+ residential and datacenter proxies, CAPTCHA avoidance and AI-powered extraction behind a single HTTP API. One request returns a fully JavaScript-rendered page as raw HTML, as LLM-ready Markdown, as an extended JSON envelope carrying cookies, headers, XHRs and iframes, or as structured JSON described in plain English. A hosted, remote MCP server exposes three of those formats as native tools to Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline and VS Code, so an AI agent gets live web access without running a browser locally. Billing is metered in API credits with a permanently free 10,000-credit monthly tier; standalone rotating proxies are sold separately by bandwidth.
s.name: ScrapingAnt

s.description: ScrapingBee is a France-based web scraping API that handles headless browsers, proxy rotation, anti-bot defenses, and CAPTCHA solving so developers can extract data from any website with a single API call. The platform exposes a unified HTML scraping endpoint alongside dedicated APIs for Google Search, Amazon, Walmart, YouTube, and ChatGPT, with JavaScript rendering, AI-powered data extraction, screenshots, and an MCP server for agentic workflows.
s.name: ScrapingBee

s.description: Proxy API for Web scraping
s.name: ScrapingDog

s.description: Scrapy is an open-source Python web crawling framework for extracting structured data from websites using spiders and built-in data pipelines.
s.name: Scrapy

s.description: Scrapybara provides virtual desktops for AI agents - remote Ubuntu, browser, and Windows instances that computer-use models can see and control. A single x-api-key REST API starts and manages cloud instances, streams the desktop, runs computer / keyboard / mouse actions, drives Chromium over Playwright CDP, executes bash and code, manages the filesystem and Jupyter notebooks, and saves reusable browser auth states.
s.name: Scrapybara

s.description: Scratchpad is an AI-powered workspace for sales teams that sits on top of Salesforce, reducing the friction of keeping the CRM up to date. Reps manage notes, opportunities, tasks, and pipeline from a fast, lightweight interface that syncs everything back to Salesforce, with AI-native sheets and Kanban boards, an AI notetaker and call recorder, automated field updates, executive summaries, and CRM hygiene monitoring. The product connects to Salesforce via API and inherits its permissions and guardrails, and integrates with Slack, Zoom, and Gong. Founded in 2019 by Pouyan Salehi and Cyrus Karbassiyoon in San Francisco, and backed by Accel and Craft Ventures. Scratchpad publishes no REST API for its own Salesforce-native workspace, but the same company ships Clearskies (clearskies.cc), a Customer Context Graph delivered as a single remote MCP server at https://mcp.clearskies.cc/mcp, OAuth-protected with dynamic client registration and PKCE, that unifies Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Scratchpad, Gmail/Outlook, calendars, Slack, Linear, Jira and Pylon behind one endpoint for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, n8n and Retool. This profile captures Scratchpad identity, its commercial surface, its agent surface, and its security posture.
s.name: Scratchpad

s.description: Scratchpay (Scratch Financial, Inc., NMLS ID 1582666) is a digital payment and financing platform for veterinary and human healthcare. Practices offer borrowers Scratch Pay installment plans ($200-$10,000 over 12-24 months, 0-36% APR) with no hidden fees and a soft credit check, plus Scratch Checkout payment processing and Scratch Comms patient communications. Over 12,000 veterinary hospitals across the U.S. and Canada integrate Scratch, which pays practices up front and collects from borrowers. Scratchpay exposes a partner/borrower API (published as archived OpenAPI on GitHub) for submitting loan applications and receiving an asynchronous approve/decline decision via a partner callback. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners.
s.name: Scratchpay

s.description: Screaming Frog is a UK-based SEO software company and search marketing agency, best known for the SEO Spider website crawler tool used by SEO professionals worldwide to perform technical SEO audits, crawl analysis, and integrations with third-party APIs. The SEO Spider integrates with Google Analytics (GA4), Google Search Console, PageSpeed Insights, Ahrefs, Majestic, Moz, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, and Anthropic. Screaming Frog also offers a free Log File Analyser for analyzing server log files to understand search bot behavior. Screaming Frog operates no public web API. Its machine-callable surfaces are the SEO Spider command line interface, which runs the product fully headless, and — since version 24.0, released 19 May 2026 — a first-party Model Context Protocol server built into the desktop application, exposing 29 tools for crawl control, reports, bulk exports, URL inspection, screenshots, embeddings, Node scripting and sandboxed file access. The MCP server is a paid licence feature and runs inside the user's own installation over stdio or a loopback HTTP transport; there is no hosted endpoint.
s.name: Screaming Frog

s.description: ScreenCloud is a cloud digital signage platform that turns any screen into a managed display for content, dashboards, and apps. Its developer surface is the ScreenCloud Studio API - a single public GraphQL endpoint (bearer-token authenticated, region-specific, copied from the DEVELOPER tab in Studio) that lets you automate anything you can do in Studio by hand - pairing and managing screens, building playlists and channels, uploading media and files, casting content, installing and configuring signage apps, and exporting playback logs and QR metrics. ScreenCloud also runs a Developer Platform / App framework for building custom HTML/JavaScript signage apps that can be published (with approval) to the App Store. There is no documented public WebSocket API - the Studio API is request/response GraphQL over HTTPS.
s.name: ScreenCloud

s.description: Screenhero was a Y Combinator (W13) startup that built interactive screen sharing with voice and video, letting remote users share and control any application together. It was acquired by Slack in January 2015; the six-person team joined Slack and the standalone Screenhero product was discontinued, with its screen-sharing, voice, and video capabilities folded into Slack (today surfaced as Slack Huddles). The screenhero.com domain now 301-redirects to slack.com/features/huddles. No independent Screenhero developer portal, API, or SDK exists; this record is retained as a historical a16z portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network.
s.name: Screenhero

s.description: Screenleap is a screen sharing and online meeting service that lets anyone share their screen instantly from a browser with no software install required for viewers. Beyond the consumer product, Screenleap offers a REST-style developer API (api.screenleap.com/v2) that lets businesses embed live interaction — screen sharing, video conferencing, audio conferencing, chat and cloud recording — directly into their own websites and online services. The API creates and manages screen share sessions, returns a viewer URL and the screenShareData used by the screenleap.js JavaScript library to start sharing, and reports session usage and participant detail. Authentication uses an account id and auth token passed as request headers over SSL. Screenleap is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).
s.name: Screenleap

s.description: Screenpipe is a local-first, source-available desktop application (by Mediar AI, Y Combinator S26) that continuously captures everything you see, say, and hear on your computer, reads on-screen text through OS accessibility APIs with an OCR fallback, transcribes system and microphone audio with local Whisper by default (or, when the user selects one in settings, with a cloud engine such as Deepgram or screenpipe-cloud, or an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint; audio leaves the device only when a remote engine is selected), and stores it all in a local SQLite database as a private, searchable memory. It exposes a full local REST API at http://localhost:3030 (71 operations across search, frames, audio, meetings, memories, speakers, tags, vault, cloud sync, cloud archive, and data retention) and ships as an MCP server so agents like Claude, Cursor, Codex, and Cline can query screen history and meeting transcripts. Automations are built as "pipes" — scheduled AI agents written in plain markdown. It is positioned as a local-first alternative to Rewind.ai, Microsoft Recall, and cloud meeting bots.
s.name: Screenpipe

s.description: ScreenPoint Medical is a Netherlands-based healthcare AI company, founded in 2014 by Professor Nico Karssemeijer and Professor Sir Michael Brady, that develops Transpara Breast AI for earlier detection of breast cancer in 2D (FFDM) and 3D (DBT) mammography. Transpara is vendor-agnostic, integrates into PACS and reading workflows via medical-imaging (DICOM) pipelines rather than a public developer API, and is FDA cleared (K241831, K232096) and CE marked (0344). The product is used in over 200 clinics across 25+ countries and is backed by three randomized controlled trials (including MASAI in The Lancet). The company is backed by Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: no public developer/API surface exists, but real security-disclosure and compliance posture were captured.
s.name: ScreenPoint Medical

s.description: ScreenshotAPI (screenshotapi.to) is a hosted screenshot and PDF capture API — send a URL or raw HTML, get back a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF without running browser infrastructure. The contract is deliberately small: one screenshot resource answering both GET and POST, plus a health check. What sets it apart from its size is the agent-readable surface around it — an llms.txt on the root, a 302KB llms-full.txt, a separate docs llms.txt, an agent install guide, a dedicated AI-agents page, and per-page markdown by appending .md to any /docs/ URL. An MCP server exists but runs locally over stdio and is not yet published to npm, so it is described here rather than advertised as a hosted endpoint. Not to be confused with ScreenshotAPI.net, a different company in the same category — see the screenshotapi-net entry.
s.name: ScreenshotAPI

The API supports GET and POST requests over HTTPS and enables capture of screenshots in PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF and other formats with customizable rendering options including screen size, dark mode, ad blocking, and metadata extraction.

s.description: Scribd Inc. is an American digital-content media company founded in 2007 by Trip Adler, Jared Friedman and Tikhon Bernstam and headquartered in San Francisco, California. It operates four consumer platforms: Scribd (a document-sharing library), Everand (a subscription service for ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, podcasts and sheet music, formerly the flagship Scribd subscription), SlideShare (presentation hosting) and Fable (a social reading app). Scribd was an early Y Combinator company. Its historical public "Platform" API for uploading, converting and displaying documents is now legacy — the official Ruby client (scribd/rscribd) was archived in 2019, Scribd no longer accepts new API accounts, and the SlideShare developer portal has been retired — so this profile documents the company's identity and the remaining first-party developer artifacts rather than a live API surface.
s.name: Scribd

s.description: Scribe (scribehow) is an AI workflow-documentation platform founded in 2019 that automatically turns any process or software walkthrough into a step-by-step guide. Its products — Scribe Capture, the knowledge base, and the newer Scribe Optimize workflow-mapping platform — are used by more than five million people across a large share of the Fortune 500. For developers, Scribe publishes a read-only Search & Retrieval API (OpenAPI 3.1) that searches, lists, and retrieves an organization's Scribe Documents and Knowledge Pages for integration into custom applications and AI agents. Public API access is an Enterprise-plan feature authenticated with a static API key sent in the X-API-Key header. The company is backed by Amplify Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Tiger Global, StepStone, Morado Ventures, and New York Life Ventures, and reached a $1.3B valuation with its 2025 Series C.
s.name: Scribe

s.description: Scribe Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Alameda, California, engineering CRISPR-based genetic medicines through its proprietary "CRISPR by Design" platform. Co-founded by molecular engineers Benjamin Oakes, Brett Staahl, and David Savage alongside CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, the company builds highly engineered CasX-derived enzymes — including its X-Editing (XE) molecules for precise gene editing and ELXR epigenetic long-term X-repressor technology for durable gene silencing without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Scribe focuses initially on cardiometabolic disease, the leading cause of death globally, and expands into areas such as sickle cell disease and neurological conditions through strategic pharmaceutical partnerships. The company is backed by a16z and Menlo Ventures and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a venture portfolio company. Scribe Therapeutics is a therapeutics and drug-discovery company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface.
s.name: Scribe Therapeutics

s.description: Scripbox is an Indian direct-to-consumer wealth management and mutual fund investment platform operated by Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited. It helps families pursue financial freedom through personalized mutual fund recommendations shaped by expert advisors and data-backed algorithms, offering both regular (commission-based, zero monthly fee) and direct (advisory-fee) plans. The platform bundles portfolio construction and monitoring, financial planning, goal-based investing, tax-saving tools such as its Smart Withdraw algorithm, and multi-channel support.
