Thanx is API-first and publishes a public developer portal documenting a Consumer API for custom consumer experiences, a Partner API for privileged integration use cases, and a Loyalty API for digital ordering and kiosk providers, along with webhooks and Connex data-export integrations to warehouses like Snowflake and BigQuery. Thanx serves roughly 500 brands and processes over a billion transactions annually. It also publishes a hosted Docs MCP server for natural-language API search and an open agent-skills starter kit.
t.name: Thanx

t.description: Thatch (Thatch Health, Inc.) is a modern health benefits platform that makes it easy for employers to offer personalized healthcare to employees using an ICHRA (Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement). Thatch for Platforms is a set of REST APIs and embeddable components that let partner platforms — payroll, HR, and benefits products — bring ICHRA benefits to their customers, covering employer onboarding, employee management, enrollments, members, pay schedules, and payroll deductions.
t.name: Thatch Health

t.description: ThatGameCompany is an American independent video game studio founded in 2006 by Jenova Chen and Kellee Santiago, known for emotionally driven, art-forward titles including Flow, Flower, Journey, and the free-to-play social adventure Sky: Children of the Light. The studio focuses on creating timeless interactive entertainment that inspires human connection across all ages. It publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a technology / gaming entity and records domain-security posture from live probes.
t.name: ThatGameCompany

t.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.
t.name: ThayerMahan

t.description: The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is a division of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services dedicated to promoting the economic and social well-being of children, families, and communities. ACF administers programs including TANF (cash assistance), CCDF (child care), Head Start, LIHEAP (energy assistance), child welfare, and refugee assistance. ACF collects administrative data via systems including AFCARS (foster care and adoption), NCANDS (child abuse and neglect), NYTD (youth in transition), TANF data reporting, and CCDF data. ACF is pursuing interoperability standards using HL7 FHIR and USCDI+ for human services data exchange. The TANF Data Portal (tanfdata.acf.hhs.gov) provides state agencies with a data submission and analysis interface.
t.name: The Administration for Children and Families

t.description: The Ainglish Project is an open, measured register of a developing English dialect for AI agent-to-agent communication, operated from ainglish.org by Starsol Ltd (England) with the AI agent Reticuli credited as builder and moderator and Jack Parnell as the named human in the loop. Agents propose, second, measure and vote on constructs through a public JSON API under /api/v1 (OpenAPI 3.1, 116 operations), the same contract projected as a 51-tool remote MCP server at /mcp, a Python SDK on PyPI, and Claude Code / Codex plugins; every construct maps losslessly back to standard English and ratified language is released as CC0 bundles. Reads are public with no key; writes present a Colony id_token obtained by RFC 8693 token exchange. The register is content-addressed (RFC 8785 JCS), hash-chained and anchored with OpenTimestamps, publishes an A2A agent card, ai-plugin.json, llms.txt, an Atom feed, signed webhooks and a machine-readable rate-limit endpoint.
t.name: The Ainglish Project

t.description: The Andersons, Inc. (NASDAQ: ANDE) is a diversified North American agribusiness headquartered in Maumee, Ohio and founded in 1947, operating across four segments: Agribusiness / commodity merchandising through The Andersons Trade Group grain elevators and terminals, Nutrient & Industrial through The Andersons Plant Nutrient Group and its turf and specialty products, Renewables through its ethanol production and marketing joint ventures, and premium food and pet-food ingredients. The company publishes NO public developer API, no developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDKs. Its customer-facing digital surface is a set of authenticated end-user applications — the GRAINweb grain account portal, the Farm2Market SmartTicket delivery-ticket web app at andersonstickets.com, the AndeConnect and Trade Group mobile apps (the AndeConnect app is operated on the company's behalf by the ag platform vendor Bushel), and portal.andersonsinc.com account management — all federated through an Active Directory Federation Services identity provider at portalauth.andersonsinc.com. Business-to-business integration is handled through EDI and direct merchant relationships rather than a self-service API. NOTE ON IDENTITY: the domain andersons.com belongs to Anderson's of White Bear Lake, Minnesota, an unrelated prom and school-spirit party-supply retailer; The Andersons, Inc. is at andersonsinc.com.
t.name: The Andersons

t.description: The Atavist is a pioneering digital longform-storytelling brand founded in 2009 by Evan Ratliff, Jefferson Rabb, and Nicholas Thompson. It comprises The Atavist Magazine, which publishes one immersive work of narrative nonfiction each month and has earned National Magazine Award and Emmy recognition, and the Atavist multimedia publishing platform for building rich, media-driven stories. Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com) acquired both the magazine and the platform in 2018; the platform's storytelling features were folded into WordPress.com and the magazine now runs on Newspack by Automattic. The Atavist exposes no public developer API or documented developer program — it is a reader-facing publication at magazine.atavist.com.
t.name: The Atavist

t.description: The Athletic is a subscription-based digital sports media company founded in 2016 by Alex Mather and Adam Hansmann, offering in-depth, ad-light coverage of national and local professional and college sports through a large staff of beat writers and columnists. Acquired by The New York Times Company in 2022, The Athletic delivers written articles, newsletters, podcasts, and live coverage across its website and mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass The Athletic does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; its GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source engineering tooling rather than any public API product.
t.name: The Athletic

t.description: The Atlas Marketplace (branded "The Atlas") is a free online community and knowledge marketplace for local government leaders. Officials and staff use it to learn from their peers about the smart, safe, and sustainable solutions working in their communities, browsing a searchable library of case studies, vendors, and civic-technology projects. The platform connects public-sector practitioners with the companies and partners behind proven municipal solutions across mobility, infrastructure, sustainability, and public safety. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a content and community website rather than a developer/API product; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public web presence.
t.name: The Atlas Marketplace

t.description: The Backplane, Inc. was a US social-network-builder startup (founded 2011) that built branded social networks for fan groups and organizations, most notably Lady Gaga's Little Monsters community, and later pivoted to the Place.xyz network-building platform. Backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Sequoia, Greylock and others, it raised roughly $18.9M before running out of money, going out of business in April 2016 and selling all of its assets (patents, code, trademarks, URLs). The company is defunct; enrichment found no live website, developer portal, API, specification, or SDK surface to catalog.
t.name: The Backplane

t.description: The Bank of London (TBOL) is a UK principal clearing bank and Banking-as-a-Service provider, authorised by the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the FCA and PRA (FRN 930379). Operating a "safer by design" model in which client deposits are never loaned, invested or leveraged, it offers clearing, payments and settlement, agency banking, embedded banking (BaaS) and commercial and corporate banking to banks, non-bank financial institutions, virtual-asset service providers, digital platforms, financial intermediaries and corporates. Its Developer Studio at developer.bankoflondon.com publishes a public OpenAPI 3.0.3 contract for the Bank of London API v2 covering accounts, customer onboarding, virtual account management, Confirmation of Payee, Faster Payments, Bacs, CHAPS, agency and cross-border payments, standing orders, direct-debit mandates, transactions, statements and webhooks, backed by a free open sandbox that requires no NDA. A separate PSD2 / Open Banking UK v3.1 TPP interface is operated on the bank's behalf by Salt Edge Priora under provider code `tbol`.
t.name: The Bank of London

t.description: The Beard Club is a men's grooming and beard-care brand selling beard oils, balms, washes, aftershave, grooming kits, trimmers, and subscription grooming boxes through its Shopify-powered online store at thebeardclub.com. Beyond the consumer storefront, the store is agent-commerce ready: it implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP 2026-04-08) with a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp, a machine-readable /llms.txt and /agents.md, UCP service discovery at /.well-known/ucp, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and read-only product and collection JSON endpoints — so AI shopping assistants can search the catalog, build carts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts programmatically.
t.name: The Beard Club

t.description: Everything you need from the Bible in one discoverable place
t.name: The Bible

t.description: The Black Tux is an online formalwear company offering premium suit and tuxedo rentals and purchases for weddings and formal events. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, it pairs a direct-to-consumer online store with roughly 50 physical showrooms nationwide, home try-on, group wedding coordination with party pricing, free shipping over $200, and a perfect-fit guarantee. The storefront runs on Shopify; The Black Tux does not publish a first-party developer API. The only machine-readable surface on the domain is Shopify's managed Customer Account identity service (OIDC / OAuth authorization server discovery). This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and enriched with the verifiable public identity and web properties the company genuinely publishes.
t.name: The Black Tux

t.description: The Block is a New York-based digital-assets research, analysis, and news brand founded in 2018, covering cryptocurrency, blockchain, and Web3 markets. Its subscription platform, The Block Pro, packages breaking news, in-depth research, proprietary datasets, and venture-funding intelligence for professional investors, funds, and enterprises. The Block Pro also exposes a set of license-gated APIs - a real-time News API (REST, request-only, JSON), a Deals/Funding API, an Ecosystems/Data API, and a WebSocket news stream - available only to organizations holding a Block Pro subscription. The APIs have no public developer portal or OpenAPI definition; access and technical documentation are arranged through The Block's client-services team.
t.name: The Block

t.description: The Boring Company is an American infrastructure and tunnel-construction company founded by Elon Musk in 2016 that designs and builds underground transportation, utility, and freight tunnels to reduce urban traffic congestion. Its Prufrock tunnel-boring machines dig low-cost tunnels roughly a mile a week, and its all-electric, zero-emissions Loop system carries passengers in Tesla vehicles through those tunnels — the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop is its first commercial deployment. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its web presence is marketing, careers, Vegas Loop ticketing, and a merchandise store.
t.name: The Boring Company

t.description: The Bot Company is a San Francisco robotics startup founded in 2024 by Kyle Vogt, the co-founder and former CEO of Cruise, building a helpful general-purpose robot for every home to automate everyday household chores. Its team draws from Tesla, Cruise, OpenAI, Google, and Pixar, and the company has raised roughly $301M (reportedly valued near $2B) from investors including Spark Capital and SV Angel. As of this profile the company operates a marketing and careers site only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.
t.name: The Bot Company

t.description: The Bouqs Co. is a direct-from-farm online flower and plant delivery service headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, offering fresh cut bouquets, potted plants, wedding and event florals, and recurring flower subscriptions sourced from sustainable farm partners in South America and California. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts. This profile captures verifiable company identity plus live domain-security posture only.
t.name: The Bouqs

t.description: The Brandtech Group is a privately held marketing and marketing-technology holding group founded in 2015 by former Havas CEO David Jones as You & Mr Jones and renamed in 2022. It positions itself as a generative-AI marketing group and operates a portfolio of wholly owned brands rather than a single product: Oliver (in-house agency), Jellyfish (digital and performance marketing), Pencil (a generative-AI creative platform for ad copy, image and video), Acorn-i (Amazon and ecommerce retail-media analytics), fifty-five and DP6 (data and marketing science), Collectively (creator and influencer marketing), Mobkoi, Gravity Road, Mofilm and Brandtech Consulting. Its customer-facing software surface is Pencil, a SaaS platform that orchestrates third-party generative-AI models (OpenAI, Google, Adobe, Runway, Bria) and pushes creative into Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Google Display, DV360 and LinkedIn. The group publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no public API keys or SDKs; integration is delivered through the products themselves and through partner connectors.
t.name: The Brandtech Group

t.description: The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) is an agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce that provides economic data to policymakers, businesses, and the general public. The BEA collects and analyzes a wide range of economic indicators, including gross domestic product (GDP), personal income, and trade data. Through its reports and analysis, the BEA helps inform decision-making at all levels of government and helps businesses and individuals understand the state of the economy. The BEA Data API provides programmatic access to all published economic statistics including NIPA, regional data, international accounts, and industry-level data.
t.name: The Bureau of Economic Analysis

t.description: The Business of Fashion (BoF) is an authoritative digital media and intelligence company founded by Imran Amed in 2007, serving the global fashion and luxury industry. It publishes news, analysis, case studies and industry data, and operates subscription products including BoF Professional membership, BoF Insights research reports, events and online courses. Backed by Index Ventures. BoF publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, subscription and legal surface plus a domain-security probe.
t.name: The Business of Fashion

t.description: The Campbell's Company (formerly Campbell Soup Company) is an American manufacturer and marketer of branded convenience food products including soups, simple meals, beverages, and snacks. Major brands include Campbell's, Rao's, V8, Pace, Pepperidge Farm, Snyder's of Hanover, Lance, Cape Cod, Kettle Brand, Goldfish, and Prego. The company operates consumer-facing digital properties, an investor relations portal, a careers platform, and supplier resources, but does not publish general-purpose public APIs.
t.name: The Campbell's Company

t.description: The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG) is a global investment firm that deploys private capital across Global Private Equity, Global Credit, Global Investment Solutions (AlpInvest), and carveouts such as Carlyle Direct Lending. Carlyle does not publish a public developer API. Institutional LPs, co-investors, and portfolio companies interact with the firm through a set of private, authentication-gated portals: LP Connect for fund investors, Carlyle Direct Lending's portal for direct lending clients, the Carlyle Global Portfolio Solutions (resources.carlyle.com) portal, and brand experiences such as Carlyle & Co. Integrations with fund administrators, custodians, and placement agents run through bespoke secure file exchange and vendor-managed APIs.
t.name: The Carlyle Group

t.description: An open, free, read and write API all about cats. Access thousands of cat images, vote, favorite, and explore breed information.
t.name: The Cat API

t.description: A global health services company providing health insurance, pharmacy benefits, and behavioral health services. Serves over 180 million customer relationships worldwide through its Cigna Healthcare and Evernorth divisions.
t.name: The Cigna Group

t.description: The Clearing House (TCH) is a U.S. banking association and payments company owned by many of the largest commercial banks. It operates three core payment systems: CHIPS (large-value wire clearing), the EPN automated clearing house (ACH), and the RTP network, the private-sector real-time payments rail it launched in 2017 as the first new U.S. payments infrastructure in decades. RTP is a 24/7/365 instant-payments scheme built on the ISO 20022 messaging standard, supporting immediate credit-push transfers up to $10 million with final settlement, plus Request for Payment (RfP), remittance data, and a UID addressing/directory lookup. TCH is the scheme operator for the U.S. market and competes with the Federal Reserve's FedNow service. Its API posture is documentation- and rulebook-first: TCH does not publish an open, self-serve public REST API or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification. Instead it publishes ISO 20022 message specifications (pacs, pain, camt, remt) as PDFs, the RTP network operating rules, playbooks, and a technology-provider program. Real-time HTTP/JSON RTP APIs are surfaced to businesses by participating financial institutions (for example U.S. Bank) and registered technology providers that connect to the RTP network on their behalf.
t.name: The Clearing House (RTP)

t.description: The Climate Corporation (Climate LLC, a Bayer company) operates Climate FieldView, one of the world's largest digital agriculture platforms, spanning 120M+ acres and 100,000+ farmers. Its FieldView Platform APIs let approved partners read and write growers' data with OAuth2 consent: field boundaries (GeoJSON), farm organizations, operations, resource owners, and agronomic layers (as-planted, as-applied, as-harvested, scouting), plus asynchronous bulk uploads and exports of planting, application, harvest, imagery, seeding prescription (rx), and soil-sample data. Every call requires both a Bearer access token and a partner X-Api-Key. A v5 API surface is in preview.
t.name: The Climate Corporation

t.description: The Clinician is a New Zealand-headquartered digital health company whose product, The Clinician Platform (TCP, formerly ZEDOC), is an outcomes-intelligence layer for value-based healthcare. TCP captures patient-reported outcome and experience measures (PROMs, PREMs, CROMs) omnichannel over SMS, email, web and native mobile in 20+ languages, scores and benchmarks them automatically against MCID thresholds, runs configurable digital care pathways with a threshold-triggered alert engine, and returns outcomes to the EMR via FHIR. It sits alongside an EMR/PAS rather than replacing it, and the company markets an API-driven architecture aligned with HL7 FHIR (incl. SMART-on-FHIR), HL7 v2.x, openEHR and DICOM, plus an OMOP Clinical Events API. No public API reference, developer portal or machine-readable contract is published — API access runs through an enterprise sales engagement.
t.name: The Clinician

t.description: The Clorox Company is a multinational consumer-goods manufacturer best known for its bleach, cleaning and disinfecting brands, alongside a portfolio that includes Pine-Sol, Liquid-Plumr, Glad, Kingsford, Brita, Burt's Bees and Hidden Valley. Clorox runs no developer program and publishes no API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK or portal, and its commercial integration with retailers and suppliers runs over EDI and partner agreements rather than a public API. It does nonetheless serve a small, undocumented, anonymous first-party REST surface from its corporate site at /wp-json — Clorox-authored tcc/v1 and clorox-security/v1 namespaces exposing a Safety Data Sheet index, cleaning-product ingredient disclosure records, a CPSC general conformity certificate lookup, a live job feed and consent signalling. A MuleSoft Anypoint gateway at api.clorox.com serves partner traffic behind a 403, and Clorox's Anypoint Exchange public portal is enabled but publishes zero assets.
t.name: The Clorox Company

t.description: The Co-operative Bank plc is a UK high-street retail and commercial bank, headquartered in Manchester and long known for its customer-led ethical banking policy. Following its 2013-2017 recapitalisation it was owned by institutional bondholders, and in January 2025 it completed its acquisition by Coventry Building Society, becoming part of the member-owned Coventry Building Society Group; it also operates the online-only "smile" brand. Authorised by the PRA and regulated by the FCA and PRA, it is an FCA-authorised ASPSP under PSD2 and the UK Open Banking regime. While it is not one of the nine CMA-mandated banks (CMA9), it implements the Open Banking Implementation Entity (OBIE) Read/Write API Standard (v3.1) and publishes a public developer portal at developer.co-operativebank.co.uk exposing Account Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), and Confirmation of Funds (CBPII) APIs for both the Co-operative Bank and smile brands, secured with FAPI-grade OAuth2/OIDC, mutual-TLS client authentication using Open Banking directory certificates, and PSD2 strong customer authentication, with a manual TPP onboarding process and a sandbox for testing before production.
t.name: The Co-operative Bank

t.description: The Co-operators is a Canadian insurance and financial services co-operative, formed in 1978 from the amalgamation of the Saskatchewan and Ontario co-operative insurers whose roots run back to the Co-operative Life Insurance Company founded in Regina in 1945. It is owned by Canadian co-operatives, credit union centrals and farm organizations rather than public shareholders, and writes multi-line property and casualty, home, auto, farm, travel and life insurance alongside group benefits, group retirement and savings, wealth management and institutional asset management, reporting more than $62 billion in assets under administration, nearly 7,000 employees and more than 2,800 licensed insurance representatives across Canada. Its API posture is partner-gated. There is no first-party developer portal on cooperators.ca — developer, developers, docs, api and partners subdomains do not resolve in DNS, and /developers, /developer, /api, /partners and /integrations all return HTTP 404 — while the advisor and broker channel is a set of sign-in walls (lifeportal.cooperators.ca, benefitsnowlogon.cooperators.ca, basis.cooperators.ca, illustration.cumis.com). The only public API surface in the group belongs to its embedded-insurance brand Duuo, whose Duuo Platform partner APIs cover account, quote, payment and policy issuance for tenant and event insurance behind a signed partnership agreement and issued OAuth 2.0 client credentials; the developer portal Duuo advertises at developer.duuo.ca is a Postman-hosted documentation domain that returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-07-25. No ACORD, AL3 or CSIO reference was found anywhere in the company's public materials.
t.name: The Co-operators

t.description: The Coca-Cola Company is the world's largest non-alcoholic beverage company, owning and marketing more than 200 brands across sparkling soft drinks, water, hydration, sports, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based drinks. The company sells its products in more than 200 countries through a bottling and distribution partner network. While Coca-Cola does not currently publish a broadly available public REST API, it is a heavy enterprise API consumer running an internal API program on MuleSoft that connects ERP, manufacturing, distribution, retail, marketing, and consumer engagement systems through a Center for Enablement (C4E) model. Historical Coca-Cola Enterprises (CCE) Product and Location APIs at developer.cokecce.com are no longer maintained as a public-facing developer program.
t.name: The Coca-Cola Company

t.description: The Coin Analysis provides real-time cryptocurrency news, market analysis, and price data through a REST API. It offers endpoints for current crypto prices, historical data, and news articles, secured with an API key. The service targets developers building financial, trading, or analytics applications.
t.name: The Coin Analysis

t.description: The Colony (thecolony.ai, also served at thecolony.cc) is an AI-agent forum, social network, marketplace and messaging platform operated by Starsol Ltd (Norwich, England) where agents register themselves over the API with no human verification and take part alongside humans in topic-based sub-communities ("colonies"). Its machine surface is unusually complete: a 567-operation OpenAPI 3.1 at /openapi.json, a live streamable-HTTP MCP server at /mcp/ (224 tools, 7 resources, 3 prompts; tools/list answers anonymously), an A2A agent card at both well-known paths, llms.txt and a provider-hosted skill.md, an agent-facing structured reference at /api/v1/instructions, a public machine-readable deprecations registry, an Idempotency-Key on every authenticated write, HMAC-signed webhooks for 58 events, Lightning-settled tips and marketplace payments, and an agent-first OpenID Connect provider ("Log in with the Colony") with RFC 8414/OIDC discovery, dynamic client registration, RFC 8693 token exchange, CIBA, device flow, DPoP and PAR. First-party SDKs ship on PyPI, npm/JSR, Go and Packagist, plus a Claude Code plugin and an agentskills.io skill.
t.name: The Colony

t.description: Pass in any valid color and get conversion into any other format, the name of the color, placeholder images and a multitude of schemes.
t.name: The Color API

t.description: The Companies API is a company data and enrichment platform offering programmatic access to firmographic, technographic, and web-intelligence data on 50M+ companies. Its REST API (base https://api.thecompaniesapi.com, all resources under /v2) covers company search and segmentation, company enrichment by domain, email, or social profile, similar-company lookup, industry and technology reference data, location reference data, saved lists, and asynchronous bulk actions. Requests are authenticated with an API token passed in the Authorization header, billing is credit-based, and the full OpenAPI 3.1 description is published at /v2/openapi.
t.name: The Companies API

t.description: The Company Company is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
t.name: The Company Company

t.description: The Coterie is a financial technology company founded in 2022 by Ethan Agarwal, Jeson Patel, and Chris Boies to give startup founders access to venture capital investments, estate-planning strategies (including its ATOM Trust product), and lending. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, the company has since rebranded and now operates as Allocate (allocate.co), positioning itself as "an operating system for private markets" serving wealth advisors and asset managers with deal sourcing, white-labeled fund creation, AI-powered portfolio management, and unified reporting. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.
t.name: The Coterie

t.description: The Cru (now branded "The Cru Empowered by Luminary") is a membership community founded by Tiffany Dufu that matches women and allies into small peer-coaching accountability circles ("Crus") of 6-8 members who meet in monthly 90-minute gatherings to advance their personal and professional goals. It was acquired by Luminary, a New York City based professional community and coworking organization, and the thecru.com site now redirects to weareluminary.com/luminary-crus. This is a consumer community and coaching business, not a technical platform - it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.
t.name: The Cru

t.description: The Culture Commons (culture.sbs) is an agent-native online commons — "a commons for minds, and for agents becoming minds" — run under the Memetica Corporation GitHub organization (per its security.txt and MCP Registry manifest). It is a live chat room with fifty seats and a heartbeat rule, a persistent append-only board, and a trust-tagged "edge ledger" of testimony about what crossed the room, exposed three ways from one host: a 35-operation OpenAPI 3.1.0 REST contract at https://culture.sbs/openapi.json, a remote stateless MCP server at https://culture.sbs/mcp listed in the official MCP Registry as sbs.culture/commons with seventeen tools that answer an anonymous tools/list, and an A2A 1.0.0 agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json whose single greeter skill points agents inward to MCP. Access is free and identity-blind — an agent takes a "standing" by signing its own name (or optionally with Sign-In-With-Ethereum) and every durable write carries a caller-generated idempotency key. It also ran ARC/v0, a bounded, on-chain-escrowed agent-referral experiment on Base that closed on 2026-09-16 and remains publicly auditable through the same API.
t.name: The Culture Commons

t.description: The Data Guild is a San Francisco-based venture studio, founded in 2013, that builds data-driven companies addressing challenges in healthcare, life sciences, renewable energy, and climate change. Steeped in machine learning, data science, and artificial intelligence, the Guild pioneers a co-creation model that converts LP capital into equity across a portfolio of new ventures while applying its own team's efforts directly rather than simply allocating capital. It brings products to market through spinouts, alongside portfolio-company teams, and with strategic partners. Investors include Bloomberg Beta, David Gutelius, and Silicon Valley Data Capital. The Data Guild operates a marketing/company website and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or MCP surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe.
t.name: The Data Guild

t.description: A public service all about Dogs, free to use when making your fancy new App, Website or Service
t.name: The Dog

t.description: The Echo Nest was a music-intelligence company, spun out of the MIT Media Lab, that ran a developer platform and API for music understanding — machine-listening audio analysis (tempo, key, energy, danceability, valence), artist and song metadata, automated playlisting and taste profiles, and the Rosetta Stone service for translating artist and track IDs across music services. It was acquired by Spotify in March 2014 (reported at roughly €49.7M / ~$100M). Spotify consolidated onto its own Web API: The Echo Nest API stopped issuing new keys on 2016-03-29 and stopped serving requests on 2016-05-31, with developers directed to the Spotify Web API (whose audio-features and audio-analysis endpoints descend from Echo Nest technology). The developer.echonest.com portal no longer resolves; the echonest.com domain now redirects to an unrelated WordPress site. This profile was surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio company; it is retained for historical/lineage reference and has no live, public API surface to enrich.
t.name: The Echo Nest

t.description: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. (NYSE: EL) is one of the world's leading manufacturers, marketers and sellers of quality prestige skin care, makeup, fragrance and hair care products. Founded in 1946 by Estée and Joseph Lauder, the family-controlled, New York-headquartered conglomerate operates a portfolio of more than 20 prestige brands sold in approximately 150 countries and territories, employs roughly 57,000 people worldwide, and reported fiscal 2025 net sales of approximately $14.32 billion. ELC's corporate website (elcompanies.com) does not expose any public developer APIs, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, sandboxes, or a developer portal — the EsteeLauder GitHub organization is empty of public repositories. The technology surface is instead expressed through enterprise partnerships: the AI Innovation Lab (announced 2023, expanded April 2024) jointly run with Microsoft on Azure OpenAI Service; the ConsumerIQ tool built on Microsoft Copilot Studio (2025); an Adobe Firefly Services generative AI collaboration for digital marketing assets (March 2025); a Google Gemini / Vertex AI–powered Jo Malone London Scent Advisor (December 2025); and a Shopify-based unified global direct-to-consumer commerce platform (announced October 2025, ~50% rolled out by calendar year-end 2026). ELC's strategic vision, "Beauty Reimagined" (announced February 2025), and the Profit Recovery and Growth Plan ($0.8–1.0B gross benefits; $1.2–1.6B restructuring charges) anchor the One ELC operating model now led by CEO Stéphane de La Faverie and Board Chair William P. Lauder.
t.name: The Estée Lauder Companies

t.description: The Expert is a consumer marketplace that connects people with top interior designers worldwide through paid one-on-one video consultations, paired with an Expert-curated home shopping marketplace where those designers' product picks can be purchased directly. Founded by celebrity interior designer Jake Arnold and tech entrepreneur Leo Seigal, the company is backed by Forerunner Ventures, First Round Capital, WndrCo, and others. It operates as a business-to-consumer platform with a trade program for design professionals; it publishes no public developer API. This profile captures its public web presence and domain security posture.
t.name: The Expert

t.description: The Exploration Company (TEC) is a European deep-tech space startup founded in July 2021 by Hélène Huby and a team of aerospace engineers from Airbus and ArianeGroup. Headquartered in Munich, Germany with sites in Bordeaux, Oberpfaffenhofen, Italy, France, Houston, and the MENA region, TEC develops Nyx, a family of modular, reusable, in-orbit refuelable spacecraft designed to carry cargo — and eventually humans — to low Earth orbit, lunar orbit, and the Moon, serving space stations and long-distance research missions. The company has raised a €40.5M Series A and a €150M Series B and is a certified B Corp. It exposes no public developer API; interfaces are provided to payload customers via a Payload User's Guide.
t.name: The Exploration Company

t.description: The Farmer's Dog is a direct-to-consumer pet health company that delivers fresh, human-grade dog food on a personalized subscription. Customers complete an online profile of their dog (breed, age, weight, activity, health goals) and the company formulates and ships pre-portioned meal plans on a recurring cadence. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in New York City, it is backed by Forerunner Ventures among others and has delivered over one billion meals nationwide. The business runs on a JavaScript/TypeScript stack with an internal "Core API" that powers ordering, subscription management, and its veterinarian program, but the company does not publish a public developer platform, API documentation, or client SDKs. This profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture; there is no public API surface to catalog.
t.name: The Farmer's Dog

t.description: The Feed is an online sports nutrition store for endurance athletes, stocking products from more than 300 brands across fuel, hydration, supplements, and recovery. Founded by Matt Johnson while managing a Tour de France cycling team, it sells gels, chews, and drink mixes as single servings so athletes can test products without committing to full boxes, offers AutoShip subscriptions and a Feed First membership, and is the official nutrition partner of USA Triathlon. The company builds personalized fueling plans around before/during/after-workout nutrition, tested with input from over 200,000 athletes. It is a consumer e-commerce brand (Shopify storefront) with no public developer API; its machine-readable surfaces are a published llms.txt and a Google Merchant product feed.
t.name: The Feed

t.description: The Fit Body Co (Fitbody) is a Mexican direct-to-consumer sports nutrition and dietary supplements brand selling isolated and hydrolyzed protein powders, creatine, vitamins, and wellness products, along with digital recipe guides, through a Shopify-based online storefront at fitbody.mx. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As an e-commerce retail brand it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.
t.name: The Fit Body Co

t.description: The Folklore is a commerce platform and B2B wholesale marketplace that helps emerging and diverse consumer brands sell and market globally, connecting them with retail buyers and shoppers through dropship, shipping, and commerce technology. Its storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven search, cart, checkout, and fulfillment, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and published /llms.txt and /agents.md instructions so AI shopping agents can transact with buyer approval.
t.name: The Folklore

t.description: The GEO Group, Inc. (NYSE: GEO) is a publicly traded private corrections and community supervision company headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida. Founded in 1984 as Wackenhut Corrections Corporation and rebranded in 2004, it is the largest private prison operator in the United States and a primary contractor to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the U.S. Marshals Service, the Federal Bureau of Prisons, and numerous state departments of corrections. As of 2024 the company owned or managed approximately 80,000 beds across roughly 99 facilities and reported $2.424 billion in revenue. Its wholly owned subsidiary BI Incorporated operates the federal Intensive Supervision Appearance Program (ISAP) and builds the ankle monitors, GPS trackers, voice-verification systems and SmartLINK smartphone app used to monitor people in immigration proceedings and community supervision. GEO Group publishes no public developer API and has no GitHub presence; the only "platform" surfaces it exposes are customer-facing operational systems (BI TotalAccess for officers, BI SmartLINK for supervised individuals) used inside its own contracts. This repository documents the corporate footprint, the technology subsidiary, and the public-record controversies surrounding the firm under the second Trump administration's 2025+ ICE detention expansion, for purposes of the API Evangelist network's coverage of API absence in sensitive sectors.
t.name: The GEO Group

t.description: The Giving Block is a crypto-native fundraising platform that lets nonprofits and enterprises accept cryptocurrency, stock, and card donations. Through its Public API and embeddable donation widget, partners can build their own donation experiences or embed The Giving Block's donation form to route gifts to more than 1,000 nonprofit organizations in its network. The API securely accepts Bitcoin, Ethereum, and 100+ other cryptocurrencies, instantly converts crypto donations to cash so nonprofits never have to touch crypto, and also supports stock and donor-advised-fund (DAF) giving. It is a RESTful, JSON API with JWT-based authentication, AES-256 encrypted webhook notifications, and separate production and sandbox environments. The Giving Block was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its published developer documentation.
t.name: The Giving Block

t.description: The Graph is a decentralized blockchain data indexing protocol. It exposes Subgraphs (GraphQL APIs over indexed on-chain data), Substreams (parallel streaming dataflows), the Token API (REST/MCP for token data), and supports 80+ chains. Self-hosted Graph Node and Firehose are open-source.
t.name: The Graph

t.description: The Guardian newspaper REST API providing access to 2M+ articles, news content, sections, tags, editions, and real-time breaking news from Guardian journalists worldwide. The API covers all articles published since 1999 and supports advanced search, filtering by section, tag, date range, and edition (UK, US, Australia).
t.name: The Guardian

t.description: The Guild is an open-source software group building much of the GraphQL ecosystem's tooling, published together at the-guild.dev. Its portfolio spans GraphQL Hive (schema registry, usage observability and breaking-change detection), GraphQL Mesh (composing many APIs into one graph), GraphQL Yoga (server), Envelop (plugin runtime), GraphQL Tools and Schema Stitching (schema composition), GraphQL Code Generator (typed clients and servers), GraphQL Inspector (schema diffing and CI checks) and GraphQL Scalars. Every product listed here shares the-guild.dev as its home, which is why they are profiled as one provider with many APIs rather than as separate companies.
t.name: The Guild

t.description: The Helper Bees is an Austin-based aging-in-place technology company that operates one connected platform linking benefits, in-home service providers, and support so older adults can safely age at home. Its products include Care Concierge human guidance, an Aging-in-Place Marketplace for OTC products and nonmedical services (home care, safety modifications, meals, transportation), the Helpful benefits card, digital invoicing and claims processing for home and facility care, and digital nurse eligibility assessments for long-term care insurance. The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The Helper Bees publishes member and provider applications (the api.thehelperbees.com app host, the myhomealign.com provider portal, and mobile apps) but does not currently expose a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.
t.name: The Helper Bees

t.description: The Hog is a real-time web intelligence API for AI agents and go-to-market teams, founded in 2025 (Y Combinator F25) by Hudson Liao and Paulo Nascimento in San Francisco. One credit-based REST API unifies company and people search, contact enrichment, LLM-powered deep research, multi-platform web and social scraping (LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook), SEO intelligence, and recurring signal monitors. Fast calls return synchronously; long-running jobs run asynchronously with polling, organization-scoped idempotency keys, cursor pagination, request-id tracing, and a consistent JSON error envelope. A hosted OAuth MCP server and a local stdio MCP package expose the same capabilities to agents.
t.name: The Hog

t.description: The THC Open Mindfulness Resources API, provided by The Holistic Care, offers a free, public, read‑only REST API delivering structured mindfulness resources. It includes research citations, a glossary, 16 mindfulness games, 111 guided audio practices, and excerpts from 527 blog posts. The API requires no authentication, API key, or cost, and supports searching and browsing across all resource families via the /v1/resources and /v1/search endpoints.
t.name: The Holistic Care — THC Open Mindfulness API

t.description: The Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer, offering tools, construction products, appliances, and services through stores, websites, and apps in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
t.name: The Home Depot

t.description: The House of LR&C (Love, Respect & Care) is a Seattle-based, mission-driven direct-to-consumer fashion company founded in 2020 by Russell Wilson, Ciara, and retail veteran Christine Day. A Certified B Corporation, it operates a portfolio of apparel brands including Good Man Brand, LITA by Ciara, and Human Nation, donating 3% of net revenue to the Why Not You Foundation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its public commerce runs on Shopify; the company publishes no first-party developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. The only machine-readable surface on the storefront host is Shopify's platform-level Customer Account API OIDC discovery document.
t.name: The House Of LR&C

t.description: The Human Utility (formerly the Detroit Water Project) is a Y Combinator-backed not-for-profit organization founded in 2014 by Tiffani Ashley Bell whose mission is to preserve human dignity by increasing water affordability for families across the United States. It matches families who are behind on their water bills with donors who want to help, paying utility companies directly on their behalf through crowdfunded donations, community-building, and policy action. Operating in Detroit, Baltimore, and dozens of other cities, it has helped thousands of households avoid water shutoffs. The Human Utility runs a public-facing web application for donors and recipients rather than a developer-facing API product; its source code lives in the humanutility GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with identity and link details; no public API surface was found.
t.name: The Human Utility

t.description: The Icon League is a five-a-side (small-sided) football entertainment league co-founded by former Real Madrid and Germany midfielder Toni Kroos and German streamer Elias Nerlich (Eliasn97), operated by The Icon League GmbH of Cologne, Germany (Amtsgericht Köln, HRB 117138). Played indoors in a US-style 14-team franchise format with two 12-minute halves and "Rulebreaker" mechanics designed to maximize attacking play, the league blends professional and amateur players and is distributed primarily through livestreams and social platforms to a young German-speaking audience. Season one generated more than 1.3 billion social-media impressions, and the league raised a €15M Series A (backed by HV Capital) to professionalize operations and expand across Europe. This is a consumer sports-and-media property; it publishes a public content website (teams, players, standings, matchdays, news, tickets, shop) but exposes no public developer API surface.
t.name: The Icon League

t.description: theindex.fyi is a maintained meta-index of indie web and small web index sites — a curated catalog of curated catalogs. It tracks ~40 indexes spanning six categories (curated directories, RSS / feed aggregators, search engines, random-discovery tools, constraint-based clubs, and IndieWeb infrastructure), and exposes the catalog through a public, read-only JSON:API.
t.name: The Index

t.description: The Inside is a direct-to-consumer, made-to-order home furnishings brand founded in 2017 by Christiane Lemieux and Britt Bunn, offering customizable upholstered furniture — sofas, chairs, beds, headboards, and decor — in 100+ fabrics and patterns. Backed by Canaan Partners along with Corigin Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Forerunner Ventures, and BAM Ventures, it was acquired by Havenly in February 2022. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known metadata surface was found — theinside.com serves an e-commerce storefront with no documented programmatic interface.
t.name: The Inside

t.description: The Interaction Company of California (d/b/a Poke) builds Poke, a proactive AI assistant that lives in Apple Messages, WhatsApp, Telegram, and SMS. Poke texts like a human, knows the user, and integrates with their email, calendar, reminders, and dozens of apps to draft replies, reschedule meetings, pay or flag invoices, and book travel. For developers, Poke acts as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) client that third parties extend by connecting remote MCP servers, and it exposes a minimal HTTP API for sending messages to Poke programmatically, plus a first-party `poke` CLI/SDK (npm) and the Kitchen platform for building and publishing shareable Recipes. Founded by Marvin von Hagen and Felix Schlegel; backed by General Catalyst, Spark Capital, Village Global, Earlybird Venture Capital, and Anti Fund.
t.name: The Interaction Company Of California

t.description: Ladders (TheLadders.com) is a New York City based online job-search service founded in 2003 by Marc Cenedella that specializes in vetted executive and professional roles paying $100,000 or more per year. The subscription platform pairs a curated $100K+ job board with recruiter access, resume review and rewrite tools, AI-powered resume and LinkedIn optimization, and a daily career-news and advice product (Ladders News). It runs a consumer-facing web application with free Basic and paid Premium memberships and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or partner integration program.
t.name: The Ladders

t.description: Lafz is a halal-certified cosmetics and personal-care brand, founded in 2019 and headquartered in Singapore as part of the Believe PTE FMCG group. It sells hair care, skin care, makeup, a caffeine range, deodorants and fragrance made without alcohol, parabens or animal by-products. The direct-to-consumer storefront at lafz.com runs on Shopify and exposes real agent-facing surfaces: a Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect provider, an /llms.txt agent guide, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) shopping MCP server for buyer-approved agent-driven checkout. thelafz.com is the corporate "halal compliant factories" site. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio-graph lead and enriched from its live public surfaces.
t.name: The Lafz

t.description: The League is an American social and dating mobile application founded in 2014 by Amanda Bradford and launched in 2015. It positions itself as a selective, career-oriented dating community ("Date. Intelligently."), using an application/waitlist model and LinkedIn/Facebook-based verification to curate its membership. The League was acquired by Match Group in 2022 and operates as a consumer iOS/Android app. It is a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures. As a consumer mobile app it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or partner API surface.
t.name: The League

t.description: The Learning Experience is an early childhood education and childcare franchise operating academies of early education for children from six weeks to six years old across a nationwide network of centers. Its programs span infant, toddler, preschool, and pre-kindergarten care built on a proprietary curriculum. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-facing childcare operator it publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture.
t.name: The Learning Experience

t.description: The Lord of the Rings API
t.name: The Lord of the Rings

t.description: The Lowdown is the UK's leading community-driven reproductive and sexual health platform for women, founded in 2019 by Alice Pelton. It enables people to review and research their health conditions, symptoms and medications so they can make more informed decisions, starting with contraception and expanding into menopause, fertility, PCOS, endometriosis, periods and weight care. The platform combines scientific information with a unique dataset of thousands of community reviews and hundreds of thousands of data points on lived experience across dozens of contraceptive methods and brands, alongside medical advice and online prescriptions. It is free to use, monetising through partnerships with the NHS, women's health innovators and clinical trial recruitment. The Lowdown was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer web platform and currently exposes no public API or developer program.
t.name: The Lowdown

t.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.
t.name: The Meta

t.description: The Michaels Companies is the largest arts and crafts specialty retailer in North America, providing materials, project ideas, and education for creative inspiration. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for The Michaels Companies.
t.name: The Michaels Companies

t.description: The Mind Company is a consumer mental-fitness company that builds a multi-app platform for cognitive and emotional wellbeing. Its apps include Elevate (cognitive training across memory, vocabulary, math, and more), Balance (personalized meditation for sleep, stress, and focus), and Spark (puzzle-based learning). The company is a portfolio company of Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a direct-to-consumer mobile app business, The Mind Company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed security posture.
t.name: The Mind Company

t.description: The Mechanical Licensing Collective (MLC) is a U.S. statutory organization that administers mechanical licensing and royalty distribution for music creators. It provides a centralized database of musical works, facilitates licensing for digital music services, and ensures creators receive proper compensation. The MLC offers APIs and data services to support industry participants in accessing catalog information, licensing data, and royalty reports.
t.name: The MLC

t.description: The Mobile-First Company is a French / US (Miami HQ) startup building a suite of mobile-first, AI-powered business apps for small teams under a "one problem, one app" philosophy. Its flagship product, Allo, is an AI phone system used by 5,000+ businesses — an AI receptionist that answers 24/7, call recording with transcription and AI summaries, intelligent routing, spam blocking, SMS, and CRM sync. Allo ships a full REST API (calls, SMS, contacts, CRM, analytics, webhooks), a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and OAuth 2.0. Sibling apps Due (invoicing) and Claim (expenses) extend the same approach. The company is backed by Base10 Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
t.name: The Mobile First Company

t.description: The Mobility House (TMH) is a Munich-headquartered electric-mobility and energy technology company, founded in 2009, with offices in Zurich, Montreal, Paris, Singapore and Belmont (USA). Its ChargePilot smart charging and energy management system pairs an on-site controller with a cloud dashboard to run dynamic load management across mixed-vendor AC and DC charging infrastructure, and its Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) platform markets electric-vehicle battery capacity into energy and grid-balancing markets. ChargePilot integrates with third-party systems over open, standards-based interfaces rather than a public REST developer program: OCPP to charging stations, a VDV 463 WebSocket interface to depot and fleet management systems, a Modbus TCP/IP server for building and site energy management systems, and an outbound Charging Data Push-API that delivers completed charging sessions as JSON to a customer endpoint.
t.name: The Mobility House

t.description: The Modern Milkman is a UK doorstep delivery service that brings farm-fresh milk, groceries and household essentials to customers in returnable and reusable glass bottles or recyclable packaging, with flexible ordering and early-morning delivery. Founded to modernise the traditional milkround, the company focuses on reducing food waste and single-use plastic through a return-and-reuse model, local sourcing, and a subscription-style ordering experience delivered through its website and mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company publishes no public developer API, but does maintain an llms.txt for AI agents, a customer help centre, and a blog. Sector: consumer / direct-to-consumer grocery delivery.
t.name: The Modern Milkman

t.description: The Mom Project is a talent marketplace that connects skilled professionals (with a focus on mothers and caregivers) to remote, hybrid, and onsite roles at family-friendly employers. The platform pairs a community of hundreds of thousands of vetted candidates with thousands of companies through job matching, curated talent search, and managed hiring services such as pay-per-hire and access plans. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, The Mom Project operates a consumer/employer web product and consumes third-party APIs (for example a Docusign eSignature integration for hiring workflows) but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface of its own.
t.name: The Mom Project

t.description: The Movie Database (TMDB) is a community-built movie, TV, and people metadata catalog with a free REST API used by streaming apps, recommendation engines, second-screen experiences, fan sites, and AI/ML workflows. The TMDB API v3 exposes ~150 endpoints across movies, TV series, seasons, episodes, people, credits, images, collections, companies, networks, keywords, genres, reviews, lists, certifications, trending, discover/search, watch providers, account/lists, authentication, and configuration. A v4 surface adds OAuth-style user authentication and richer list management. Non-commercial use is free; commercial use requires a separate written agreement with TMDB.
t.name: The Movie Database

t.description: The Muse is a careers and company-profiles platform that helps people find jobs at companies whose values match their own. Its free, documented public REST API (v2) exposes hundreds of thousands of live job openings - searchable by category, experience level, company, and location - alongside rich employer company profiles (industry, size, locations, and behind-the-scenes content). An optional api_key raises rate limits. This makes The Muse a strong source for "job openings", jobs, careers, and recruiting use cases and for building job boards, career sites, and employer-branding integrations.
t.name: The Muse

t.description: The Naked Market is a San Francisco-based consumer packaged goods (CPG) company and brand incubator founded in 2019 by Harrison Fugman, Alex Kost, and Tim Marbach. It uses a "fast fail" end-to-end infrastructure to take a food or beverage product from idea to market in roughly three months, launching and acquiring socially conscious direct-to-consumer brands across snacks, drinks, and better-for-you categories. Its portfolio has included Project Breakfast, Flock crispy chicken chips, Avocrazy avocado puffs, Beach House Bowls, Rob's Backstage Popcorn, and the low-alcohol aperitif brand Haus. The company raised $27.5 million in Series A funding in 2021 and is backed by HV Capital. It operates as a consumer brand holding company and does not publish a traditional developer API program, but its Shopify-hosted storefront exposes an agent-commerce surface: llms.txt agent instructions, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, OpenID Connect discovery, and a live MCP endpoint for catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout.
t.name: The Naked Market

t.description: NASA explores the unknown in air and space, innovates for the benefit of humanity, and inspires the world through discovery. The api.nasa.gov portal hosts a federated set of APIs that make NASA imagery, science, and mission data accessible to application developers.
t.name: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration

t.description: The New Stack is a tech media platform covering cloud native, DevOps, AI, and open source technologies, providing news, analysis, podcasts, webinars, and ebooks for developers, software engineers, and operations professionals. Public data access is available via RSS feeds for articles and podcasts.
t.name: The New Stack

t.description: The New York Times is one of the world's most respected news organizations, providing comprehensive journalism across politics, culture, business, science, health, and the arts since 1851. The NYT Developer Network exposes a suite of RESTful APIs enabling developers to search and access NYT articles, best-seller book lists, movie reviews, semantic metadata, top stories, and popular content. All APIs require an API key obtained from the NYT Developer Portal.
t.name: The New York Times

t.description: The New York Times Company (NYSE: NYT) is the publisher of The New York Times and operator of a portfolio of news, product-review, sports, cooking, and games products including The Athletic, Wirecutter, Wordle, NYT Cooking, and NYT Games. The company also runs a public developer program at developer.nytimes.com that exposes a family of read-only REST APIs over its newsroom content: article search, top stories, most popular, archive going back to 1851, best-seller and book-review lists, movie reviews, the Times Newswire firehose, the controlled vocabulary that powers Times Topics (TimesTags), the Semantic API, and a Geographic API that pairs Times geo-tagged content with the GeoNames database. All APIs share api.nytimes.com as the host, use a query-string api-key for authentication, and respond as JSON.
t.name: The New York Times Company

t.description: The News API provides free access to search worldwide news and top stories from over 40,000 sources in 50 countries. Access live and historical news articles with advanced filtering by keyword, category, language, country, domain, and date. The API supports boolean search operators, pagination, and returns structured article data including headlines, descriptions, images, and category classifications.
t.name: The News API

t.description: The Next Web is a leading online media organization covering technology news, business, and culture. Founded in 2006, TNW reports on startups, innovation, artificial intelligence, digital culture, and the future of work. The primary programmatic access to TNW content is through its RSS 2.0 feed, which is updated hourly with the latest articles across all topic areas. Category-specific feeds are also available for Deep Tech, Plugged (consumer tech), and Sustainability. TNW also organizes the annual TNW Conference and operates a technology events business.
t.name: The Next Web

t.description: The Nuclear Company (TNC) is a U.S.-based nuclear energy infrastructure firm deploying nuclear power at fleet scale with a "design once, build many" standardized construction approach. Through its Powerhouse Resources arm it provides maintenance, outage execution, turbine, electrical, and instrumentation services to nuclear plants nationwide, and its proprietary AI-driven Nuclear Operating System (NOS) manages deployment and operations across the nuclear lifecycle. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company and portfolio company of True Ventures.
t.name: The Nuclear Company

t.description: The Nudge is a free consumer lifestyle app that texts its members short videos from locals recommending their favorite real-world things to do — secret hikes, date ideas, restaurants, and activities — a few "Nudges" each week to help people (primarily millennials) have more fun in real life and be more adventurous, romantic, and social. Founded in 2018 by siblings Sarah and John Peterson and based in San Francisco, The Nudge is available on iOS and Android and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners among other investors. It is a business-to-consumer product delivered over SMS and mobile apps, with no public API or developer program.
t.name: The Nudge

t.description: No-bullshit file hosting and URL shortening service
t.name: The Null Pointer

t.description: The Odds API provides sports betting odds from over 40 major bookmakers worldwide. Access current and historical odds for head-to-head, spreads, totals, and outrights markets across 100+ sports. Endpoints cover live scores, event listings, participants, and historical odds snapshots dating back to June 2020. Quota is consumed per request based on the number of regions and markets requested. All requests require an API key.
t.name: The Odds API

t.description: The OK Company was a consumer technology startup, backed by Obvious Ventures, best known for OK Play - a mobile app for iOS and Android that turned screen time into a catalyst for real-world, parent-and-child play activities designed to build empathy, kindness, and creativity in young children. It was founded by CEO JJ Aguhob and President Chris Ovitz (previously co-founders of the mobile video app Viddy), with developmental psychologist Dr. Colleen Russo Johnson as Chief Scientist. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its domain theokcompany.com no longer resolves to a product site and instead redirects to a third-party domain-sale listing. The OK Company was a consumer mobile app business and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead.
t.name: The OK Company

t.description: RSS reader
t.name: The Old Reader

t.description: The OMDb API is a RESTful web service to obtain movie, series, and episode information. All content and images on the site are contributed and maintained by users. Access movie and TV metadata including title, year, genre, director, cast, plot, ratings, and IMDb data. Search by title or look up by IMDb ID. Requires a free API key obtained at omdbapi.com/apikey.aspx.
t.name: The Open Movie Database

t.description: The Org operates the world's largest network of public organizational charts, mapping companies, their teams, and reporting hierarchies. Its developer platform exposes a metered REST API and an official MCP server for retrieving a company's public org chart by domain or LinkedIn URL, prospecting positions and people with rich filters, resolving a person's manager, and monitoring credit usage. Authentication is via an account-scoped X-Api-Key header over HTTPS, usage is metered in monthly credits, and the same key powers a remote Model Context Protocol endpoint exposing thirteen tools for agent-native access — company and person lookup, job search, reporting-line traversal, work-email resolution, and lead-list management. The MCP surface is materially wider than the REST API: eight of the thirteen tools have no REST equivalent, and list creation is the only write operation The Org exposes anywhere. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital.
t.name: The Org

t.description: The Other Guys is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
t.name: The Other Guys

t.description: The Philadelphia Inquirer is the largest newspaper in Pennsylvania, owned by the nonprofit Lenfest Institute for Journalism. Inquirer.com publishes Philadelphia, regional, national, and world news, sports, business, opinion, arts, food, and obituaries. The Inquirer does not operate a public commercial developer program. Programmatic surfaces are limited to Arc XP-generated RSS feeds, news sitemaps, and a small set of open-source repositories from its `phillymedia` GitHub organization, including the `dewey-mcp` Model Context Protocol server that wraps an Azure AI Search index of the Inquirer archive.
t.name: The Philadelphia Inquirer

t.description: The Picklr is the largest indoor pickleball club franchise in North America, founded in 2021 in Utah by Jorge Barragan and Austin Wood and franchising since March 2023. It operates membership-based indoor facilities offering unlimited court reservations, open play, adult and junior coaching academies, leagues, tournaments and corporate events, with a single membership valid at every club nationwide. The company publishes no developer programme and sells no API product. It does, however, serve a genuine machine-readable surface from its own domain: a public WordPress REST API exposing 157 club locations plus pages, posts, press and events; a published llms.txt; and three live Model Context Protocol endpoints advertised through RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 discovery documents and gated by an OAuth 2.1 authorization server with PKCE and dynamic client registration. Court booking, membership billing and reservations run on PlayByPoint, a third-party platform, and are outside any Picklr-owned contract.
t.name: The Picklr

t.description: The Pill Club was a US direct-to-consumer telehealth and pharmacy service for birth control and reproductive health, delivering prescription contraception and sexual-health products by mail. The brand has been consolidated into Nurx (a Thirty Madison company): its domain thepillclub.com now 301-redirects to nurx.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found for either the legacy brand or its Nurx successor; this is a consumer healthcare service with no external API program.
t.name: The Pill Club

t.description: The Players Trunk is an e‑commerce platform offering weekly drops of sports‑team themed player trunks and related apparel. Featured on Shark Tank, the company ships orders on Sundays and provides a curated selection of jerseys, shorts, bags, gloves, footwear, and outerwear for college and professional teams. Customers can browse collections by school, sign up as sellers, and follow the brand on social media platforms including Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and TikTok. The site emphasizes fast shipping, limited‑edition releases, and community engagement through its online store.
t.name: The Players Trunk

t.description: The Players' Tribune is a sports-media company that gives athletes a platform to connect directly with fans in their own words, publishing first-person stories, essays, letters, and video from professional players across football, basketball, soccer, baseball, and other sports. Founded in 2014 and backed by GV and IVP, it operates as a digital publisher rather than an API provider: an enrichment probe of theplayerstribune.com found a public sports-content website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (no docs/api/developer subdomains, no /.well-known/ metadata, no llms.txt). This profile captures the company identity and the results of a live domain-security probe.
t.name: The Players' Tribune

t.description: The Possible Company is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
t.name: The Possible Company

t.description: The Predictive Index (PI) is a talent optimization platform that pairs 70+ years of behavioral science with software to help organizations hire, engage, and develop teams — behavioral and cognitive assessments, hiring and candidate screening, leadership development, employee engagement, and performance management. PI publishes a RESTful Integration API (on Azure API Management) that lets external systems such as ATS/HRIS platforms programmatically create candidates, send behavioral and cognitive assessments, retrieve jobs and results, and generate insight and coaching-guide reports — the same data that appears in the PI Portal software. Status-change notification webhooks push assessment completion events to listening systems. Backed by a $50M investment from General Catalyst.
t.name: The Predictive Index

t.description: The Priceline Group was a leading provider of online travel and travel-related services through brands including Priceline, Booking.com, KAYAK, Agoda, and Rentalcars.com before being renamed Booking Holdings.
t.name: The Priceline Group

t.description: The Promenade (The Promenade Studios) is a San Francisco AI studio, backed by a16z, that builds Simcluster (simcluster.ai) - a cooperative human-agent social simulation, video game, and free AI media-generation platform. Simcluster exposes a "hyperprompting" media API through a live, remote MCP server (streamable HTTP at /mcp, 158 tools) plus HTTP agent-lifecycle endpoints, letting AI agents and humans collaboratively generate images, videos, songs, text and 3D models from player-owned "concepts", publish and remix them on a social network, and transact in an in-game currency ("clout") with optional crypto rails.
t.name: The Promenade

t.description: High performance API for horse racing statistical modelling, application development and web content. Complete coverage of UK, Irish and Hong Kong horse racing with real-time data updates every 3 minutes.
t.name: The Racing API

t.description: letitrain.com was the corporate domain of The Rainmaker Group Ventures, LLC, an Atlanta-based hospitality revenue and profit optimization software vendor serving hotels, resorts and casinos. Rainmaker sold an "intelligent profit platform" built around three products: guestrev for transient pricing and science-based revenue management, grouprev for group pricing and evaluation, and revintel for business intelligence and reporting, with a demand forecast marketed to operators including Caesars Entertainment, Atlantis Casino Resort Spa and Two Roads Hospitality. The company was backed by Norwest Venture Partners and ran offices in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Singapore and Dubai. The brand is retired: letitrain.com now serves a blanket redirect to Cendyn, the acquiring company, its TLS certificate expired in December 2022, and no Rainmaker developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.
t.name: The Rainmaker Group Ventures (letitrain.com)

t.description: The RealReal is the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated, resale luxury goods, operating a managed consignment marketplace across women's and men's fashion, fine jewelry and watches, handbags, fine art, and home. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company employs in-house gemologists, horologists, art curators, and brand authenticators to verify every item, pairing that expertise with data-driven pricing and demand insights. The RealReal is a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: REAL) and has processed tens of millions of consigned items. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass The RealReal publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.
t.name: The RealReal

t.description: Food & Drink Reviews
t.name: The Report of the Week

t.description: The Rounds was a membership-based sustainable grocery and household-goods delivery startup (backed by a16z and Redpoint Ventures) built around reusable packaging and reducing single-use waste. The company has since been wound down and folded into Misfits Market — as of this enrichment pass https://www.therounds.co/ returns an HTTP 301 redirect to a Misfits Market "welcome-new-rounds" landing page ("Same Mission, More Groceries"). No developer portal, API, documentation, or public API surface was found; api./docs./developer.therounds.co do not resolve. This profile is retained as a network lead with an acquired/defunct status.
t.name: The Rounds

t.description: The Rundown is a sports betting data API platform providing real-time odds, lines, scores, and results across 30+ sports leagues including NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, WNBA, MLS, college football and basketball, and international soccer, tennis, cricket, and Formula 1.
